grammar.title: The Alphabet & Sounds
grammar.lead: English uses the Latin alphabet: 26 letters that combine to spell every word. Knowing the letter names and their basic sounds lets you spell your name, read new words, and follow spelling out loud.

leadTr.uz: Ingliz tili lotin alifbosidan foydalanadi: har bir soʻzni hijjalaydigan 26 ta harf. Harf nomlari va ularning tovushlarini bilish ismingizni hijjalash, yangi soʻzlarni oʻqish va ovozli hijjalashni tushunish imkonini beradi.
leadTr.ru: Английский использует латинский алфавит: 26 букв, из которых складывается каждое слово. Знание названий букв и их звуков помогает произносить по буквам своё имя, читать новые слова и понимать устное написание.

grammar.situation: You meet someone new: “What’s your name?” — “Anna.” — “How do you spell it?” — “A-N-N-A.” We spell words and names letter by letter, so knowing the letter names is the first step in English.

p: There are 26 letters. Five of them are vowels: A, E, I, O, U. The other 21 are consonants (B, C, D, F, G, …).
Sometimes Y acts like a vowel, as in happy or my.
ex: Vowels: A E I O U
Consonants: B C D F G H J K L M N P Q R S T V W X Y Z

p: Every letter has a name (how you say the letter) and a sound (how it works inside a word).
For example, the letter B is called “bee”, but its sound is /b/ as in book.
ex: C = “see” → sound /k/ in cat
H = “aitch” → sound /h/ in hat

p: We spell a word by saying each letter. Two of the same letter together are called “double”.
‘Hello’ = H – E – double L – O.
ex: “How do you spell cat?” — “C–A–T.”
‘Coffee’ = C–O–double F–double E… (F–F, E–E)

p: Each letter has a capital (A, B, C) and a small form (a, b, c).
We use capitals to start a sentence, for names, for the word I, and for countries, days and months.
ex: I live in Tashkent.
Monday, July, Anna

grammar.tip: Be careful with vowels — the same vowel can sound different: the a in cat is not the a in car. Listen and repeat new words to learn their real sound.
examples: My name is Anna — names start with a capital letter.
‘Hour’ begins with a silent H, so we say it like ‘our’.
The vowels in ‘education’ are e, a, i and o.
We say the letter W as ‘double-u’.
"‘Coffee’ has double F and double E."
"The vowels are a, e, i, o, u."
"Please write your surname in capital letters."

mistakes.x: My name is spelt with double “n”: N-N. (said as “en en”)
mistakes.v: Say each letter clearly: “double N”. English speakers often say “double” for two of the same letter.

mistakes.x: The letter “i” sounds like Uzbek/Russian “и”.
mistakes.v: In English the letter “i” is named /aɪ/ (“eye”), not /iː/.

quiz.q: Which of these is a vowel?
quiz.e: The vowels are A, E, I, O, U — so E is a vowel.

quiz.q: How many letters are in the English alphabet?
quiz.e: The alphabet has 26 letters.

quiz.q: How do you spell 'dog'?
quiz.e: ‘Dog’ is spelled D-O-G.

quiz.q: Which letter is a consonant?
quiz.e: M is a consonant; A, O and U are vowels.

quiz.q: The word 'sun' has how many letters?
quiz.e: S-U-N = three letters.

quiz.q: The 'LL' in 'ball' is called ___.
quiz.e: Two of the same letter together are called ‘double’.

quiz.q: Which word begins with a vowel sound?
quiz.e: ‘Apple’ begins with the vowel A.

quiz.q: Choose the correct spelling.
quiz.e: ‘Happy’ has a double P: H-A-P-P-Y.

quiz.q: Which word must start with a capital letter?
quiz.e: Names of cities (Tashkent) always take a capital letter.

quiz.q: 'Coffee' is spelled with ___.
quiz.e: C-O-F-F-E-E has double F and double E.

quiz.q: Which letter can act as a vowel in 'my'?
quiz.e: In ‘my’, Y works as a vowel.

quiz.q: How do you spell 'school'?
quiz.e: ‘School’ is S-C-H-O-O-L, with a silent H and double O.

quiz.q: Which sentence uses capitals correctly?
quiz.e: Capital I, capital for the city London, and a capital to start the sentence.

quiz.q: The name of the letter 'H' is ___.
quiz.e: The letter H is called ‘aitch’.

quiz.q: Which word has a silent letter?
quiz.e: In ‘know’, the K is silent — we say /noʊ/.

situation.uz: Siz yangi odam bilan tanishasiz: “What’s your name?” — “Anna.” — “How do you spell it?” — “A-N-N-A.” Soʻz va ismlarni harfma-harf hijjalaymiz, shuning uchun harf nomlarini bilish — ingliz tilidagi birinchi qadam.
situation.ru: Вы знакомитесь: «What’s your name?» — «Anna.» — «How do you spell it?» — «A-N-N-A.» Слова и имена произносят по буквам, поэтому знание названий букв — первый шаг в английском.

tip.uz: Unlilarga eʼtibor bering — bir xil unli har xil eshitilishi mumkin: ‘cat’dagi a ‘car’dagi a emas. Yangi soʻzlarni tinglang va takrorlang.
tip.ru: Будьте внимательны с гласными — одна и та же гласная может звучать по-разному: a в ‘cat’ не то же, что в ‘car’. Слушайте и повторяйте новые слова.

p.uz: Jami 26 ta harf bor. Ulardan beshtasi unli: A, E, I, O, U. Qolgan 21 tasi undosh (B, C, D, F, G, …).
p.ru: Всего 26 букв. Пять из них — гласные: A, E, I, O, U. Остальные 21 — согласные (B, C, D, F, G, …).

p.uz: Baʼzan Y unli kabi ishlaydi, masalan happy yoki myda.
p.ru: Иногда Y ведёт себя как гласная, как в happy или my.

p.uz: Har bir harfning nomi (harfni qanday aytishingiz) va tovushi (soʻz ichida qanday ishlashi) bor.
p.ru: У каждой буквы есть название (как вы её называете) и звук (как она работает в слове).

p.uz: Masalan, B harfi “bee” deb ataladi, lekin uning tovushi /b/, bookdagidek.
p.ru: Например, букву B называют “bee”, но её звук — /b/, как в book.

p.uz: Soʻzni har bir harfini aytib hijjalaymiz. Yonma-yon kelgan bir xil ikki harf “double” deyiladi.
p.ru: Слово произносят по буквам, называя каждую. Две одинаковые буквы подряд называют “double”.

p.uz: ‘Hello’ = H – E – double L – O.
p.ru: ‘Hello’ = H – E – double L – O.

p.uz: Har bir harfning bosh (A, B, C) va kichik (a, b, c) shakli bor.
p.ru: У каждой буквы есть заглавная (A, B, C) и строчная (a, b, c) форма.

p.uz: Bosh harflarni gap boshlash uchun, ismlar uchun, I soʻzi uchun, hamda davlat, kun va oylar uchun ishlatamiz.
p.ru: Заглавные используем, чтобы начать предложение, для имён, для слова I, а также для стран, дней и месяцев.

quiz.uz: Unlilar: A, E, I, O, U — demak E unli.
quiz.ru: Гласные — A, E, I, O, U, поэтому E — гласная.

quiz.uz: M — undosh; A, O va U — unlilar.
quiz.ru: M — согласная; A, O и U — гласные.

quiz.uz: Yonma-yon kelgan bir xil ikki harf ‘double’ deyiladi.
Shahar nomlari (Tashkent) doim bosh harf bilan yoziladi.
quiz.ru: Названия городов (Tashkent) всегда пишутся с заглавной буквы.

quiz.uz: C-O-F-F-E-Eda double F va double E bor.
quiz.ru: В C-O-F-F-E-E двойная F и двойная E.

quiz.uz: ‘School’ — S-C-H-O-O-L, jim H va double O bilan.
quiz.ru: ‘School’ — S-C-H-O-O-L, с немой H и двойной O.

quiz.uz: Bosh harf I, London shahri uchun bosh harf va gap boshida bosh harf.
quiz.ru: Заглавная I, заглавная для города London и заглавная в начале предложения.

grammar.title: Verb to be
grammar.lead: ‘Be’ is the most important verb in English. We use it to say who we are, how we feel, where things are, and to describe people and objects. It has three present forms: am, is, are.

leadTr.uz: ‘Be’ — ingliz tilidagi eng muhim feʼl. U kimligimizni, qanday his qilishimizni, narsalar qayerdaligini aytadi va taʼriflaydi. Hozirgi zamonda uch shakli bor: am, is, are.
leadTr.ru: ‘Be’ — важнейший глагол в английском. Им говорят, кто мы, как себя чувствуем, где находятся вещи, и описывают людей и предметы. В настоящем времени три формы: am, is, are.

grammar.situation: “I am a teacher. My sister is a doctor. We are from Tashkent.” The verb be connects a person to a job, a place or a description.

ex: I am (I’m)
you are (you’re)
he / she / it is (he’s)
we are (we’re)
you are
they are (they’re)

p: Use am with I, is with he / she / it, and are with you / we / they.
ex: I am a student. · She is happy. · They are at home.

p: In speaking and informal writing we join the pronoun and ‘be’: I’m, you’re, he’s, she’s, it’s, we’re, they’re.
ex: I’m tired. · He’s from Italy. · They’re teachers.

p: Add not after ‘be’. Short forms: isn’t (= is not), aren’t (= are not). ‘am not’ has no short form.
ex: She is not / isn’t here. · We are not / aren’t ready. · I am not cold.

p: To make a question, put ‘be’ before the subject. For wh‑questions, the wh‑word goes first.
ex: Are you a student? — Yes, I am. / No, I’m not.
Where is she? — She’s at school.

grammar.tip: Don’t confuse it’s (= it is) with its (possessive). ‘It’s cold’ = it is cold. ‘The dog likes its food’ = the food belonging to it.
examples: I am from Spain. (I’m from Spain.)
She is a nurse. (She’s a nurse.)
They are in the garden. (They’re in the garden.)
Is he your brother? — Yes, he is.

mistakes.x: I student. / She doctor.
mistakes.v: I am a student. / She is a doctor. (don’t drop “be”)

mistakes.x: He are happy.
mistakes.v: He is happy. (he/she/it → is)

mistakes.x: I’m agree with you.
mistakes.v: I agree with you. (“agree” is a verb — no “be”)

quiz.q: I ___ a student.
quiz.e: With ‘I’ we use ‘am’.

quiz.q: She ___ from Tashkent.
quiz.e: With he/she/it we use ‘is’.

quiz.q: We ___ friends.
quiz.e: With we/you/they we use ‘are’.

quiz.q: The short form of 'he is' is ___.
quiz.e: ‘he is’ = ‘he’s’.

quiz.q: They ___ at home.
quiz.e: With ‘they’ we use ‘are’.

quiz.q: ___ you a teacher?
quiz.e: With ‘you’ we use ‘are’, and it comes first in a question.

quiz.q: He ___ happy today.
quiz.e: ‘is not’ = ‘isn’t’.

quiz.q: Choose the correct negative: 'We ___ ready.'
quiz.e: With ‘we’ the negative is ‘aren’t’.

quiz.q: '___ she your sister?' — 'Yes, she ___.'
quiz.e: Question ‘Is she…?’ and short answer ‘Yes, she is.’

quiz.q: It ___ a beautiful day.
quiz.e: With ‘it’ we use ‘is’.

quiz.q: Which sentence is correct?
quiz.e: ‘am not’ has no contraction; we say ‘I’m not’.

quiz.q: 'Where ___ your parents?'
quiz.e: ‘parents’ is plural → ‘are’.

quiz.q: Complete: 'My name ___ Anna and I ___ ten.'
quiz.e: ‘name is’ (it) and ‘I am’.

quiz.q: Choose the correct short answer: 'Are they students?'
quiz.e: In short answers we don’t contract: ‘Yes, they are.’

quiz.q: Find the mistake: 'She are my best friend.'
quiz.e: With ‘she’ we use ‘is’: She is my best friend.

situation.uz: “I am a teacher. My sister is a doctor. We are from Tashkent.” ‘Be’ feʼli odamni kasb, joy yoki taʼrif bilan bogʻlaydi.
situation.ru: «I am a teacher. My sister is a doctor. We are from Tashkent.» Глагол ‘be’ связывает человека с профессией, местом или описанием.

tip.uz: it’s (= it is) va its (egalik)ni adashtirmang. ‘It’s cold’ = sovuq. ‘The dog likes its food’ = unga tegishli ovqat.
tip.ru: Не путайте it’s (= it is) и its (принадлежность). ‘It’s cold’ = холодно. ‘The dog likes its food’ = его еда.

p.uz: I bilan am, he / she / it bilan is, you / we / they bilan are ishlating.
p.ru: С I — am, с he / she / it — is, с you / we / they — are.

p.uz: Nutqda va norasmiy yozuvda olmosh bilan ‘be’ni qoʻshamiz: I’m, you’re, he’s, she’s, it’s, we’re, they’re.
p.ru: В речи и неформальном письме местоимение и ‘be’ объединяют: I’m, you’re, he’s, she’s, it’s, we’re, they’re.

p.uz: ‘be’dan keyin not qoʻshing. Qisqa shakllar: isn’t (= is not), aren’t (= are not). ‘am not’ qisqa shaklga ega emas.
p.ru: После ‘be’ добавьте not. Краткие формы: isn’t (= is not), aren’t (= are not). У ‘am not’ нет краткой формы.

p.uz: Savol yasash uchun ‘be’ni ega oldidan qoʻying. wh-savollarda wh-soʻz birinchi keladi.
p.ru: Чтобы задать вопрос, поставьте ‘be’ перед подлежащим. В wh-вопросах wh-слово идёт первым.

quiz.uz: ‘you’ bilan ‘are’, savolda esa u birinchi keladi.
quiz.ru: С ‘you’ — ‘are’, и в вопросе оно идёт первым.

quiz.uz: Savol ‘Is she…?’ va qisqa javob ‘Yes, she is.’
quiz.ru: Вопрос ‘Is she…?’ и краткий ответ ‘Yes, she is.’
В кратких ответах не сокращаем: ‘Yes, they are.’

quiz.uz: ‘she’ bilan ‘is’: She is my best friend.
quiz.ru: С ‘she’ — ‘is’: She is my best friend.

grammar.title: Pronouns & possessives
grammar.lead: Pronouns replace nouns so we don’t repeat names. Possessive words show who something belongs to. Getting these right makes your English sound natural.

leadTr.uz: Olmoshlar otlar oʻrnini bosadi, shunda ismlarni takrorlamaymiz. Egalik soʻzlari nimanidir kimga tegishliligini koʻrsatadi. Ularni toʻgʻri ishlatish nutqingizni tabiiy qiladi.
leadTr.ru: Местоимения заменяют существительные, чтобы не повторять имена. Притяжательные слова показывают принадлежность. Их правильное употребление делает речь естественной.

ex: I work here.
He is tall.
They are friends.
This is my bag.
His car is red.
Their house is big.

p: These do the action and usually come before the verb: I, you, he, she, it, we, they.
ex: He plays football. · We live here.

p: These receive the action and come after the verb or a preposition: me, you, him, her, it, us, them.
ex: She loves me. · Give the book to him. · I can see them.

p: These go before a noun to show owner: my, your, his, her, its, our, their.
ex: This is my bag. · Their house is big.

p: Possessive pronouns stand alone: mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs. We also add ’s to a name to show belonging.
ex: This book is mine. · That’s Anna’s pen (= the pen of Anna).

grammar.tip: ‘Their’ (owner), ‘there’ (place) and ‘they’re’ (= they are) sound the same but are different words. ‘Their car is over there, and they’re late.’
examples: This is my book and that one is yours.
We like them, and they like us.
Her bag is blue; his is black.
That car is ours, not theirs.
This is Tom’s pen (the pen of Tom).

mistakes.x: Me like coffee.
mistakes.v: I like coffee. (subject = I)

mistakes.x: This is me book.
mistakes.v: This is my book. (possessive = my)

mistakes.x: Her is my sister.
mistakes.v: She is my sister. (subject = she)

quiz.q: ___ play tennis every Sunday. (the speaker + friends)
quiz.e: Subject pronoun for the group with the speaker is ‘We’.

quiz.q: This is ___ book. (it belongs to me)
quiz.e: Before a noun we use the possessive adjective ‘my’.

quiz.q: I can see ___. (he)
quiz.e: After the verb we use the object pronoun ‘him’.

quiz.q: That car is ___. (it belongs to us)
quiz.e: Standing alone, we use the possessive pronoun ‘ours’.

quiz.q: ___ is a doctor. (female)
quiz.e: Subject pronoun for a female is ‘She’.

quiz.q: The dog likes ___ food. (belonging to the dog)
quiz.e: ‘Its’ (no apostrophe) shows possession.

quiz.q: Give the keys to ___. (we)
quiz.e: After a preposition we use the object pronoun ‘us’.

quiz.q: This pen is ___. (it belongs to you)
quiz.e: Standing alone we use the possessive pronoun ‘yours’.

quiz.q: ___ parents are very kind. (they)
quiz.e: Before a noun we use ‘their’.

quiz.q: Whose bag is this? It's ___.
quiz.e: We add ’s to show possession: Anna’s.

quiz.q: Choose the correct sentence.
quiz.e: The subject is ‘I’: I like coffee.

quiz.q: Complete: 'She gave ___ book to ___.'
quiz.e: ‘her book’ (possessive adjective) and ‘to me’ (object pronoun).

quiz.q: Which uses 'theirs' correctly?
quiz.e: ‘theirs’ stands alone: This house is theirs.

quiz.q: Find the mistake: 'Its a beautiful day.'
quiz.e: Here we need ‘It’s’ (= it is), not the possessive ‘its’.

quiz.q: Complete: 'My brother and ___ are at school.' (I)
quiz.e: As part of the subject we use ‘I’: My brother and I.

tip.uz: ‘Their’ (egasi), ‘there’ (joy) va ‘they’re’ (= they are) bir xil eshitiladi, lekin har xil soʻzlar. ‘Their car is over there, and they’re late.’
tip.ru: ‘Their’ (владелец), ‘there’ (место) и ‘they’re’ (= they are) звучат одинаково, но это разные слова.

p.uz: Ular harakatni bajaradi va odatda feʼldan oldin keladi: I, you, he, she, it, we, they.
p.ru: Они выполняют действие и обычно стоят перед глаголом: I, you, he, she, it, we, they.

p.uz: Ular harakatni qabul qiladi va feʼl yoki predlogdan keyin keladi: me, you, him, her, it, us, them.
p.ru: Они принимают действие и стоят после глагола или предлога: me, you, him, her, it, us, them.

p.uz: Ular egasini koʻrsatish uchun ot oldidan keladi: my, your, his, her, its, our, their.
p.ru: Они стоят перед существительным и показывают владельца: my, your, his, her, its, our, their.

p.uz: Egalik olmoshlari yakka turadi: mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs. Shuningdek, egalikni koʻrsatish uchun ismga ’s qoʻshamiz.
p.ru: Притяжательные местоимения стоят самостоятельно: mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs. Также к имени добавляем ’s для принадлежности.

quiz.uz: Soʻzlovchi bilan birga guruh uchun ega olmoshi ‘We’.
‘theirs’ yakka turadi: This house is theirs.
quiz.ru: ‘theirs’ стоит самостоятельно: This house is theirs.

quiz.uz: Bu yerda ‘It’s’ (= it is) kerak, egalik ‘its’ emas.
quiz.ru: Здесь нужно ‘It’s’ (= it is), а не притяжательное ‘its’.

quiz.uz: Eganing bir qismi sifatida ‘I’: My brother and I.
quiz.ru: Как часть подлежащего — ‘I’: My brother and I.

grammar.title: Articles & nouns
grammar.lead: Articles (a, an, the) are small words before nouns. Choosing the right one — and knowing how to make plurals — is essential for clear, correct English.

leadTr.uz: Artikllar (a, an, the) ot oldidagi kichik soʻzlar. Toʻgʻrisini tanlash va koʻplik yasashni bilish aniq va toʻgʻri ingliz tili uchun zarur.
leadTr.ru: Артикли (a, an, the) — маленькие слова перед существительным. Правильный выбор и умение образовывать множественное число важны для грамотного английского.

ex: a book
a car
a university (“yoo-”)
an apple
an egg
an hour (silent h)

p: Use a before a consonant sound and an before a vowel sound. We use them for singular things mentioned for the first time.
ex: a book · a university (‘yoo’ sound)
an apple · an hour (silent h)

p: Use the when both speaker and listener know which one, or there is only one.
ex: I bought a cake. The cake is delicious.
The sun is hot.

p: Most nouns add -s. After -s, -ss, -ch, -sh, -x we add -es. A consonant + y becomes -ies.
ex: book → books · box → boxes · baby → babies

p: Some plurals are irregular. Some nouns are uncountable (no plural, no a/an): water, rice, money, information.
ex: man → men · woman → women · child → children · foot → feet
I need some water (not ‘a water’).

grammar.tip: Choose a/an by the sound, not the letter. ‘an MP’ (em-sound) is correct; ‘a university’ (yoo-sound) is correct even though it starts with a vowel.
examples: I ate an apple and a banana.
There is a dog in the garden. The dog is friendly.
one box → two boxes; one baby → two babies.
The moon is bright tonight. (only one moon)
I need some water — not ‘a water’.
"I have a brother and a sister."
"There are three boxes on the table."

mistakes.x: a apple / a hour
mistakes.v: an apple / an hour (vowel sound)

mistakes.x: I need a informations.
mistakes.v: I need information. (uncountable — no “a”, no “-s”)

mistakes.x: She is teacher.
mistakes.v: She is a teacher. (jobs take “a/an”)

quiz.q: I have ___ apple.
quiz.e: ‘Apple’ starts with a vowel sound, so ‘an’.

quiz.q: She is reading ___ book.
quiz.e: ‘Book’ starts with a consonant sound, so ‘a’.

quiz.q: The plural of 'cat' is ___.
quiz.e: Most nouns just add -s: cats.

quiz.q: The plural of 'box' is ___.
quiz.e: After -x we add -es: boxes.

quiz.q: ___ sun is very bright today.
quiz.e: There is only one sun, so we use ‘the’.

quiz.q: The plural of 'baby' is ___.
quiz.e: Consonant + y → -ies: babies.

quiz.q: I'd like ___ orange and ___ banana.
quiz.e: ‘an orange’ (vowel sound), ‘a banana’ (consonant sound).

quiz.q: Which noun is uncountable?
quiz.e: ‘Water’ is uncountable — no plural, no a/an.

quiz.q: The plural of 'man' is ___.
quiz.e: ‘man’ is irregular: men.

quiz.q: I saw a film. ___ film was great.
quiz.e: The film is now known, so we use ‘the’.

quiz.q: Choose the correct article: '___ hour.'
quiz.e: ‘Hour’ has a silent h (vowel sound), so ‘an hour’.

quiz.q: Which is correct?
quiz.e: ‘University’ starts with a ‘yoo’ sound, so ‘a university’.

quiz.q: The plural of 'child' is ___.
quiz.e: ‘child’ is irregular: children.

quiz.q: Find the mistake: 'I need a money.'
quiz.e: ‘Money’ is uncountable: ‘I need money / some money.’

quiz.q: Complete: 'There is ___ egg and ___ spoon on ___ table.'
quiz.e: ‘an egg’ (vowel), ‘a spoon’ (consonant), ‘the table’ (specific).

tip.uz: a/an’ni harf emas, tovushga qarab tanlang. ‘an MP’ (em-tovush) toʻgʻri; ‘a university’ (yoo-tovush) ham toʻgʻri.
tip.ru: Выбирайте a/an по звуку, а не по букве. ‘an MP’ (звук «эм») верно; ‘a university’ (звук «ю») тоже верно.

p.uz: Undosh tovush oldidan a, unli tovush oldidan an ishlating. Ularni birinchi marta tilga olingan birlik narsalar uchun ishlatamiz.
p.ru: Перед согласным звуком — a, перед гласным звуком — an. Используем для единичных предметов, упомянутых впервые.

p.uz: Soʻzlovchi va tinglovchi qaysi biri ekanini bilsa yoki bitta boʻlsa, the ishlating.
p.ru: Используйте the, когда и говорящий, и слушающий знают, о ком речь, или предмет один.

p.uz: Koʻp otlar -s qoʻshadi. -s, -ss, -ch, -sh, -x dan keyin -es qoʻshamiz. Undosh + y → -ies.
p.ru: Большинство существительных добавляют -s. После -s, -ss, -ch, -sh, -x — -es. Согласная + y → -ies.

p.uz: Baʼzi koʻpliklar tartibsiz. Baʼzi otlar sanoqsiz (koʻplik yoʻq, a/an yoʻq): water, rice, money, information.
p.ru: Некоторые формы множественного неправильные. Некоторые существительные неисчисляемые (нет множественного, нет a/an): water, rice, money, information.

quiz.uz: ‘Apple’ unli tovush bilan boshlanadi, shuning uchun ‘an’.
‘Book’ undosh tovush bilan boshlanadi, shuning uchun ‘a’.
‘Hour’da jim h (unli tovush), shuning uchun ‘an hour’.
quiz.ru: В ‘hour’ немая h (гласный звук), поэтому ‘an hour’.

quiz.uz: ‘University’ ‘yoo’ tovushi bilan boshlanadi, shuning uchun ‘a university’.

grammar.title: Demonstratives
grammar.lead: This, that, these and those point to people or things. They tell us about number (one or many) and distance (near or far).

leadTr.uz: This, that, these va those odam yoki narsalarga ishora qiladi. Ular son (bitta yoki koʻp) va masofani (yaqin yoki uzoq) bildiradi.
leadTr.ru: This, that, these и those указывают на людей или предметы. Они показывают число (один или много) и расстояние (близко или далеко).

ex: this book (one)
these books (more)
that house (one)
those houses (more)

p: Use this/these for things near you, and that/those for things far from you.
ex: This is my phone (in my hand). · That is your car (over there).

p: This and that are singular (one). These and those are plural (more than one).
ex: this book → these books
that shoe → those shoes

p: They can stand alone (a pronoun) or come before a noun (an adjective).
ex: This is delicious. (alone)
This cake is delicious. (+ noun)

p: We use them on the phone and to introduce people.
ex: Hello, this is Anna. (on the phone)
These are my friends, Tom and Sam.

grammar.tip: Match number carefully: ‘these book’ is wrong. Say this book (one) or these books (many).
examples: This phone (in my hand) is new.
These shoes are mine; those are yours.
Hello, this is Sara speaking. (on the phone)
These are my friends, Tom and Lucy.

mistakes.x: this books / these book
mistakes.v: this book (one) · these books (more than one)

mistakes.x: I like these. (pointing far away)
mistakes.v: I like those. (far = that/those)

quiz.q: ___ is my pen. (in my hand)
quiz.e: Near + singular = ‘This’.

quiz.q: ___ are my shoes. (near me)
quiz.e: Near + plural = ‘These’.

quiz.q: Look at ___ bird in the sky. (far)
quiz.e: Far + singular = ‘that’.

quiz.q: ___ houses over there are new. (far)
quiz.e: Far + plural = ‘Those’.

quiz.q: The plural of 'this' is ___.
quiz.e: this → these.

quiz.q: ___ apples here are fresh.
quiz.e: Near + plural ‘apples’ = ‘These’.

quiz.q: Choose: 'Is ___ your bag?' (the one near you)
quiz.e: Near + singular = ‘this’.

quiz.q: On the phone: 'Hello, ___ is Sara.'
quiz.e: We say ‘this is …’ to introduce ourselves on the phone.

quiz.q: The plural of 'that' is ___.
quiz.e: that → those.

quiz.q: ___ are my parents. (introducing them)
quiz.e: Introducing two people (plural) = ‘These’.

quiz.q: Which sentence is correct?
quiz.e: Plural ‘books’ needs ‘These … are’.

quiz.q: Complete: '___ shoes are nicer than ___ ones over there.'
quiz.e: Near plural ‘These’ vs. far plural ‘those’.

quiz.q: Find the mistake: 'Look at those car near us.'
quiz.e: ‘car’ is singular and near, so ‘this car’ (or far ‘that car’).

quiz.q: Choose the natural sentence.
quiz.e: Plural ‘friends’ → ‘Those are’ (or ‘These are’).

quiz.q: '___ is delicious!' (the cake you are eating now)
quiz.e: One thing, near/now = ‘This’.

tip.uz: Sonni diqqat bilan moslang: ‘these book’ notoʻgʻri. this book (bitta) yoki these books (koʻp) deng.
tip.ru: Внимательно согласуйте число: ‘these book’ неверно. Говорите this book (один) или these books (много).

p.uz: Sizga yaqin narsalar uchun this/these, sizdan uzoq narsalar uchun that/those ishlating.
p.ru: Для предметов близко — this/these, для предметов далеко — that/those.

p.uz: This va that — birlik (bitta). These va those — koʻplik (bittadan koʻp).
p.ru: This и that — единственное (один). These и those — множественное (больше одного).

p.uz: Ular yakka turishi (olmosh) yoki ot oldidan kelishi (sifat) mumkin.
p.ru: Они могут стоять самостоятельно (местоимение) или перед существительным (прилагательное).

p.uz: Ularni telefonda va odamlarni tanishtirishda ishlatamiz.
p.ru: Их используют по телефону и при знакомстве людей.

quiz.uz: ‘car’ birlik va yaqin, shuning uchun ‘this car’ (yoki uzoq ‘that car’).
quiz.ru: ‘car’ единственное и близко, поэтому ‘this car’ (или далёкое ‘that car’).

grammar.title: Present simple
grammar.lead: The present simple is the tense for facts, routines and habits — things that are generally true or happen regularly. It is the most common tense in everyday English.

leadTr.uz: Hozirgi oddiy zamon — faktlar, kundalik ishlar va odatlar uchun. U kundalik ingliz tilidagi eng koʻp ishlatiladigan zamon.
leadTr.ru: Present simple — для фактов, распорядка и привычек, того, что обычно верно или происходит регулярно. Это самое частое время в повседневном английском.

grammar.situation: Tom is a nurse. He works at a hospital. He starts at 8 and finishes at 4. He doesn’t work on Sundays. — Use the present simple for habits, routines and things that are generally true.

timeline.note: A repeated action / general fact — true in the past, now and the future.

p: For routines (every day), facts (always true) and habits.
ex: I get up at seven every day.
Water boils at 100°C.

p: With he, she, it we add -s to the verb. After -o, -ss, -ch, -sh, -x we add -es; consonant + y → -ies.
ex: I work → she works · go → goes · study → studies

p: Use don’t (I/you/we/they) and doesn’t (he/she/it) + the base verb (no -s).
ex: They don’t eat meat. · He doesn’t like tea.

p: Use Do/Does + subject + base verb. Adverbs of frequency (always, usually, often, sometimes, never) go before the main verb.
ex: Do you play chess? · Does she work here?
I always brush my teeth.

grammar.tip: After does/doesn’t, the verb has no -s: ‘She doesn’t likes’ is wrong → ‘She doesn’t like.’ The -s is already in ‘does’.
examples: I get up at seven every day.
She goes to work by bus. (he/she/it + -s)
Do you play tennis? — Yes, I do.
We always have dinner at eight.
"I get up at seven every day."

mistakes.x: He work in a bank.
mistakes.v: He works in a bank. (he/she/it → add -s)

mistakes.x: She don’t like tea.
mistakes.v: She doesn’t like tea. (he/she/it → doesn’t)

mistakes.x: Do you likes football?
mistakes.v: Do you like football? (after do/does, no -s)

quiz.q: He ___ to school every day.
quiz.e: With ‘he’ we add -s: goes.

quiz.q: I ___ coffee every morning.
quiz.e: With ‘I’ we use the base verb: drink.

quiz.q: They ___ football on Sundays.
quiz.e: With ‘they’ we use the base verb: play.

quiz.q: She ___ English very well.
quiz.e: With ‘she’ we add -s: speaks.

quiz.q: We ___ in Tashkent.
quiz.e: With ‘we’ we use the base verb: live.

quiz.q: She ___ like fish.
quiz.e: With ‘she’ the negative is ‘doesn’t’.

quiz.q: The third-person form of 'study' is ___.
quiz.e: Consonant + y → -ies: studies.

quiz.q: ___ you like music?
quiz.e: With ‘you’ we use ‘Do’.

quiz.q: Choose the correct sentence.
quiz.e: The frequency adverb goes before the verb: I always eat.

quiz.q: ___ she work on Saturdays?
quiz.e: With ‘she’ we use ‘Does’.

quiz.q: Negative of 'He plays tennis': ___
quiz.e: doesn’t + base verb (no -s): He doesn’t play.

quiz.q: The third-person form of 'go' is ___.
quiz.e: After -o we add -es: goes.

quiz.q: Find the mistake: 'Does she likes pizza?'
quiz.e: After ‘does’ the verb has no -s: ‘Does she like pizza?’

quiz.q: Complete: 'My father ___ to work by bus, but I ___ to walk.'
quiz.e: ‘father goes’ (he) and ‘I prefer’.

quiz.q: Which is correct?
quiz.e: ‘never’ is already negative and goes before the verb: He never eats meat.

situation.uz: Tom is a nurse. He works at a hospital. He starts at 8 and finishes at 4. He doesn’t work on Sundays. — Odat, kundalik ish va umumiy faktlar uchun present simple ishlatamiz.
situation.ru: Tom is a nurse. He works at a hospital. He starts at 8 and finishes at 4. He doesn’t work on Sundays. — Present simple используем для привычек, распорядка и общих фактов.

tip.uz: does/doesn’t dan keyin feʼlda -s boʻlmaydi: ‘She doesn’t likes’ notoʻgʻri → ‘She doesn’t like.’ -s allaqachon ‘does’da bor.
tip.ru: После does/doesn’t у глагола нет -s: ‘She doesn’t likes’ неверно → ‘She doesn’t like.’ -s уже в ‘does’.

p.uz: Kundalik ishlar (har kuni), faktlar (doim toʻgʻri) va odatlar uchun.
p.ru: Для распорядка (каждый день), фактов (всегда верно) и привычек.

p.uz: he, she, it bilan feʼlga -s qoʻshamiz. -o, -ss, -ch, -sh, -x dan keyin -es; undosh + y → -ies.
p.ru: С he, she, it к глаголу добавляем -s. После -o, -ss, -ch, -sh, -x — -es; согласная + y → -ies.

p.uz: don’t (I/you/we/they) va doesn’t (he/she/it) + asosiy feʼl (-s yoʻq) ishlating.
p.ru: Используйте don’t (I/you/we/they) и doesn’t (he/she/it) + базовый глагол (без -s).

p.uz: Do/Does + ega + asosiy feʼl ishlating. Takror ravishlari (always, usually, often, sometimes, never) asosiy feʼldan oldin keladi.
p.ru: Используйте Do/Does + подлежащее + базовый глагол. Наречия частотности (always, usually, often, sometimes, never) стоят перед главным глаголом.

quiz.uz: Takror ravishi feʼldan oldin keladi: I always eat.
quiz.ru: Наречие частотности идёт перед глаголом: I always eat.

quiz.uz: doesn’t + asosiy feʼl (-s yoʻq): He doesn’t play.
quiz.ru: doesn’t + базовый глагол (без -s): He doesn’t play.

quiz.uz: ‘does’ dan keyin feʼlda -s yoʻq: ‘Does she like pizza?’
quiz.ru: После ‘does’ у глагола нет -s: ‘Does she like pizza?’

quiz.uz: ‘never’ allaqachon inkor va feʼldan oldin keladi: He never eats meat.
quiz.ru: ‘never’ уже отрицательное и идёт перед глаголом: He never eats meat.

grammar.title: Present continuous
grammar.lead: The present continuous describes actions happening now, at this moment, or around now (a temporary situation). It is formed with ‘be’ + verb-ing.

leadTr.uz: Hozirgi davom zamoni hozir, shu daqiqada yoki shu atrofda (vaqtinchalik holat) sodir boʻlayotgan ishni bildiradi. ‘be’ + feʼl-ing bilan yasaladi.
leadTr.ru: Present continuous описывает действие, происходящее сейчас, в этот момент или в этот период (временно). Образуется ‘be’ + глагол-ing.

grammar.situation: Look! It is raining and the children are playing inside. — Use the present continuous for an action happening now, at the moment of speaking.

timeline.note: The action is happening right now and is not finished.

ex: I work every day.
She drinks coffee.
I am working now.
She is drinking coffee.

p: Use the right form of ‘be’ and add -ing to the main verb.
ex: I am reading. · She is sleeping. · They are playing.

p: Drop a final silent -e (make → making). Double the final consonant after a short stressed vowel (run → running). ‘ie’ → ‘y’ (lie → lying).
ex: write → writing · sit → sitting · die → dying

p: Present simple = routines/facts. Present continuous = happening now or temporary.
ex: I work in a bank. (job) — I’m working from home today. (now)

p: Negative: add not after ‘be’. Question: put ‘be’ first.
ex: She isn’t listening. · Are you working?

grammar.tip: Some verbs (like, want, know, love, need, understand) describe states, not actions. We don’t usually use them in the continuous: say ‘I want tea’, not ‘I am wanting tea’.
examples: I ’m reading a book right now.
They are playing in the park at the moment.
write → writing; run → running; lie → lying.

mistakes.x: I am go to school now.
mistakes.v: I am going to school now. (be + -ing)

mistakes.x: She cooking dinner.
mistakes.v: She is cooking dinner. (don’t drop “is”)

mistakes.x: I am knowing the answer.
mistakes.v: I know the answer. (state verbs: no -ing)

quiz.q: Look! The baby ___ now.
quiz.e: ‘now’ → present continuous: is crying.

quiz.q: They ___ in the garden at the moment.
quiz.e: ‘at the moment’ → are playing.

quiz.q: I ___ a book right now.
quiz.e: ‘right now’ → am reading.

quiz.q: The -ing form of 'make' is ___.
quiz.e: Drop the silent -e: making.

quiz.q: She ___ to music now.
quiz.e: ‘now’ → is listening.

quiz.q: The -ing form of 'run' is ___.
quiz.e: Short stressed vowel → double the consonant: running.

quiz.q: We ___ dinner at the moment.
quiz.e: ‘at the moment’ → are having.

quiz.q: Choose the 'now' sentence.
quiz.e: ‘right now’ needs the continuous form.

quiz.q: Negative: 'He ___ TV now.'
quiz.e: Present continuous negative: isn’t watching.

quiz.q: The -ing form of 'sit' is ___.
quiz.e: Short stressed vowel → double: sitting.

quiz.q: Which sentence is correct?
quiz.e: ‘want’ is a state verb — not used in the continuous: I want a coffee.

quiz.q: Complete: 'Be quiet! The students ___ a test.'
quiz.e: Action happening now → are taking.

quiz.q: The -ing form of 'lie' is ___.
quiz.e: ‘ie’ → ‘y’: lying.

quiz.q: Choose the correct question.
quiz.e: Continuous question: Are you doing…?

quiz.q: Find the mistake: 'She is read a book now.'
quiz.e: After ‘is’ we need the -ing form: She is reading.

situation.uz: Look! It is raining and the children are playing inside. — Hozir, gapirayotgan paytda sodir boʻlayotgan ish uchun present continuous ishlatamiz.
situation.ru: Look! It is raining and the children are playing inside. — Present continuous используем для действия, происходящего сейчас, в момент речи.

tip.uz: Baʼzi feʼllar (like, want, know, love, need, understand) holatni bildiradi, harakatni emas. Ularni odatda davom shaklida ishlatmaymiz: ‘I want tea’, ‘I am wanting tea’ emas.
tip.ru: Некоторые глаголы (like, want, know, love, need, understand) выражают состояние, а не действие. Их обычно не ставят в continuous: ‘I want tea’, а не ‘I am wanting tea’.

p.uz: ‘be’ning toʻgʻri shaklini ishlating va asosiy feʼlga -ing qoʻshing.
p.ru: Используйте нужную форму ‘be’ и добавьте -ing к главному глаголу.

p.uz: Oxiridagi jim -eni tushiring (make → making). Qisqa urgʻuli unlidan keyin oxirgi undoshni ikkilantiring (run → running). ‘ie’ → ‘y’ (lie → lying).
p.ru: Опускайте конечную немую -e (make → making). Удваивайте конечную согласную после краткого ударного гласного (run → running). ‘ie’ → ‘y’ (lie → lying).

p.uz: Present simple = kundalik ishlar/faktlar. Present continuous = hozir sodir boʻlayotgan yoki vaqtinchalik.
p.ru: Present simple = распорядок/факты. Present continuous = происходит сейчас или временно.

p.uz: Inkor: ‘be’dan keyin not qoʻshing. Savol: ‘be’ni birinchi qoʻying.
p.ru: Отрицание: после ‘be’ добавьте not. Вопрос: поставьте ‘be’ первым.

quiz.uz: Qisqa urgʻuli unli → undoshni ikkilantiramiz: running.
quiz.ru: Краткий ударный гласный → удваиваем согласную: running.

quiz.uz: ‘want’ — holat feʼli, davomda ishlatilmaydi: I want a coffee.
quiz.ru: ‘want’ — глагол состояния, не в continuous: I want a coffee.

quiz.uz: Hozir sodir boʻlayotgan harakat → are taking.

quiz.ru: Вопрос в continuous: Are you doing…?

quiz.uz: ‘is’ dan keyin -ing shakli kerak: She is reading.
quiz.ru: После ‘is’ нужна форма -ing: She is reading.

grammar.title: Have got · there is/are
grammar.lead: ‘Have got’ talks about possession, family and features. ‘There is / there are’ says that something exists or is present. Both are very common in everyday speech.

leadTr.uz: ‘Have got’ egalik, oila va xususiyatlar haqida. ‘There is / there are’ nimadir mavjudligini yoki borligini bildiradi. Ikkalasi ham kundalik nutqda juda koʻp uchraydi.
leadTr.ru: ‘Have got’ — о принадлежности, семье и признаках. ‘There is / there are’ — о существовании или наличии. Оба очень частотны в речи.

ex: There is a book on the table.
Is there a problem?
There are three books.
There aren’t any chairs.

p: Use have got (I/you/we/they) and has got (he/she/it). Short forms: I’ve got, she’s got.
ex: I’ve got two brothers. · She’s got a new phone.

p: Negative: haven’t/hasn’t got. Question: Have/Has + subject + got?
ex: We haven’t got a car. · Has he got a sister?

p: Use there is (+ singular / uncountable) and there are (+ plural) to say something exists.
ex: There is a book on the table. · There are five chairs.

p: Negative: there isn’t / there aren’t. Question: Is there…? / Are there…?
ex: There isn’t any milk. · Are there any shops near here?

grammar.tip: Don’t mix them up: use have got for an owner (‘I have got a dog’) and there is/are for existence (‘There is a dog in the garden’).
examples: There is a book on the desk.
There are five chairs in the room.

mistakes.x: There is three rooms.
mistakes.v: There are three rooms. (plural → there are)

mistakes.x: She have got a car.
mistakes.v: She has got a car. (he/she/it → has got)

mistakes.x: I have got not a pen.
mistakes.v: I haven’t got a pen.

quiz.q: I ___ a new bag.
quiz.e: With ‘I’ we use ‘have got’.

quiz.q: She ___ two cats.
quiz.e: With ‘she’ we use ‘has got’.

quiz.q: ___ a pen on the desk.
quiz.e: Singular ‘a pen’ → There is.

quiz.q: ___ three windows in the room.
quiz.e: Plural ‘windows’ → There are.

quiz.q: Short form of 'I have got' is ___.
quiz.e: ‘I have’ = ‘I’ve’ → I’ve got.

quiz.q: We ___ a garden.
quiz.e: With ‘we’ the negative is ‘haven’t got’.

quiz.q: ___ any milk in the fridge?
quiz.e: ‘milk’ is uncountable (singular) → Is there.

quiz.q: ___ he got a bicycle?
quiz.e: With ‘he’ the question is ‘Has he got…?’.

quiz.q: There ___ a lot of people here.
quiz.e: ‘people’ is plural → are.

quiz.q: Choose the correct negative: 'There ___ any chairs.'
quiz.e: Plural ‘chairs’ → There aren’t.

quiz.q: Which sentence is correct?
quiz.e: With ‘she’: She has got a dog.

quiz.q: Complete: '___ a problem, but ___ no easy answers.'
quiz.e: ‘a problem’ (singular) → there is; ‘answers’ (plural) → there are.

quiz.q: Find the mistake: 'There is five students in the class.'
quiz.e: Plural ‘five students’ needs ‘There are’.

quiz.q: Which question is correct?
quiz.e: With ‘you’: Have you got a car?

quiz.q: Complete: 'My sister ___ long hair, and ___ a beautiful park near her house.'
quiz.e: ‘sister has got’ (possession) + ‘there is a park’ (existence, singular).

tip.uz: Ularni aralashtirmang: egasi uchun have got (‘I have got a dog’), mavjudlik uchun there is/are (‘There is a dog in the garden’).
tip.ru: Не путайте: для владельца — have got (‘I have got a dog’), для существования — there is/are (‘There is a dog in the garden’).

p.uz: have got (I/you/we/they) va has got (he/she/it) ishlating. Qisqa shakllar: I’ve got, she’s got.
p.ru: Используйте have got (I/you/we/they) и has got (he/she/it). Краткие формы: I’ve got, she’s got.

h.uz: have got bilan inkor va savollar
h.ru: Отрицания и вопросы с have got

p.uz: Inkor: haven’t/hasn’t got. Savol: Have/Has + ega + got?
p.ru: Отрицание: haven’t/hasn’t got. Вопрос: Have/Has + подлежащее + got?

p.uz: Nimadir mavjudligini aytish uchun there is (+ birlik / sanoqsiz) va there are (+ koʻplik) ishlating.
p.ru: Чтобы сказать о существовании, используйте there is (+ ед./неисчисляемое) и there are (+ мн.).

p.uz: Inkor: there isn’t / there aren’t. Savol: Is there…? / Are there…?
p.ru: Отрицание: there isn’t / there aren’t. Вопрос: Is there…? / Are there…?

quiz.uz: ‘she’ bilan: She has got a dog.
quiz.ru: С ‘she’: She has got a dog.

quiz.uz: ‘you’ bilan: Have you got a car?
quiz.ru: С ‘you’: Have you got a car?

quiz.uz: ‘sister has got’ (egalik) + ‘there is a park’ (mavjudlik, birlik).
quiz.ru: ‘sister has got’ (принадлежность) + ‘there is a park’ (существование, ед.).

grammar.title: Modals: can/can't · imperatives
grammar.lead: ‘Can’ expresses ability, possibility and permission. ‘Can’t’ is its negative. The imperative gives instructions, orders and advice. Both are short and very useful.

leadTr.uz: ‘Can’ qobiliyat, imkoniyat va ruxsatni bildiradi. ‘Can’t’ uning inkori. Buyruq mayli koʻrsatma, buyruq va maslahat beradi. Ikkalasi ham qisqa va juda foydali.
leadTr.ru: ‘Can’ выражает способность, возможность и разрешение. ‘Can’t’ — его отрицание. Повелительное наклонение даёт указания, приказы и советы. Оба коротки и полезны.

grammar.situation: “Can you swim?” — “Yes, I can, but I can’t dive.” Can shows ability and possibility, and it never changes form.

p: Can + base verb means ‘is able to’. It never changes form (no -s, no ‘to’).
ex: I can swim. · She can speak three languages.

p: We also use can to ask for and give permission.
ex: Can I open the window? · You can go now.

p: The negative is can’t (cannot). Same form for all subjects.
ex: He can’t drive. · We can’t hear you.

p: Use the base verb to give an instruction. Add don’t for negative imperatives. We often add ‘please’ to be polite.
ex: Open your books. · Don’t run! · Please sit down.

grammar.tip: After ‘can’ never use ‘to’: ‘I can to swim’ is wrong → ‘I can swim.’ And ‘can’ has no -s with he/she/it: ‘She can swim’, not ‘She cans’.
examples: I can swim, but I can’t drive.
Can I open the window, please?

mistakes.x: I can to swim.
mistakes.v: I can swim. (can + base verb, no “to”)

mistakes.x: He cans drive.
mistakes.v: He can drive. (no -s on modals)

mistakes.x: Please to sit down.
mistakes.v: Please sit down. (imperative = base verb)

quiz.q: I ___ swim very well.
quiz.e: ‘can’ + base verb, no -s, no ‘to’.

quiz.q: He ___ drive. He has no licence.
quiz.e: Negative ability = can’t.

quiz.q: ___ I borrow your pen?
quiz.e: Request for permission: ‘Can I…?’

quiz.q: ___ your books, please. (instruction)
quiz.e: Imperative uses the base verb: Open.

quiz.q: She ___ speak French.
quiz.e: ‘can’ never changes: She can speak.

quiz.q: Negative imperative: '___ late!'
quiz.e: Negative imperative: Don’t be late!

quiz.q: We ___ hear the teacher. It's too noisy.
quiz.e: Negative ability: can’t hear.

quiz.q: Choose the correct sentence.
quiz.e: can + base verb: I can play.

quiz.q: '___ quiet, please.' (instruction)
quiz.e: Imperative of ‘be’ is just ‘Be’.

quiz.q: They ___ come to the party. They're busy.
quiz.e: Negative ability/possibility: can’t come.

quiz.q: Which is correct?
quiz.e: ‘can’ takes no -s and the verb stays base: She can cook.

quiz.q: Make it negative: 'Touch the wall.'
quiz.e: Negative imperative: Don’t + base verb.

quiz.q: Find the mistake: 'Can you to help me?'
quiz.e: After ‘can’ we don’t use ‘to’: Can you help me?

quiz.q: Complete: 'You ___ smoke here, but you ___ sit outside.'
quiz.e: No permission inside (can’t), permission outside (can).

quiz.q: Which gives polite advice correctly?
quiz.e: Imperative + please: ‘Sit down, please.’

situation.uz: “Can you swim?” — “Yes, I can, but I can’t dive.” Can qobiliyat va imkoniyatni bildiradi va shakli oʻzgarmaydi.
situation.ru: «Can you swim?» — «Yes, I can, but I can’t dive.» Can выражает способность и возможность и не меняет форму.

tip.uz: ‘can’ dan keyin hech qachon ‘to’ ishlatmang: ‘I can to swim’ notoʻgʻri → ‘I can swim.’ Va ‘can’ he/she/it bilan -s olmaydi: ‘She can swim’, ‘She cans’ emas.
tip.ru: После ‘can’ никогда не ставьте ‘to’: ‘I can to swim’ неверно → ‘I can swim.’ И ‘can’ не получает -s с he/she/it: ‘She can swim’, а не ‘She cans’.

p.uz: Can + asosiy feʼl ‘qodir’ degani. U shaklini hech qachon oʻzgartirmaydi (-s yoʻq, ‘to’ yoʻq).
p.ru: Can + базовый глагол значит ‘уметь/мочь’. Форма никогда не меняется (без -s, без ‘to’).

p.uz: Shuningdek, ruxsat soʻrash va berish uchun can ishlatamiz.
p.ru: Также can используют, чтобы просить и давать разрешение.

p.uz: Inkor shakli can’t (cannot). Barcha egalar uchun bir xil.
p.ru: Отрицание — can’t (cannot). Одна форма для всех подлежащих.

p.uz: Koʻrsatma berish uchun asosiy feʼl ishlating. Inkor buyruq uchun don’t qoʻshing. Muloyimlik uchun koʻpincha ‘please’ qoʻshamiz.
p.ru: Для указания используйте базовый глагол. Для отрицательного повеления добавьте don’t. Для вежливости часто добавляем ‘please’.

quiz.uz: Buyruq mayli asosiy feʼl bilan: Open.
can + asosiy feʼl: I can play.
quiz.ru: can + базовый глагол: I can play.

quiz.uz: ‘can’ -s olmaydi va feʼl asosiy qoladi: She can cook.
quiz.ru: ‘can’ без -s, глагол в базовой форме: She can cook.

quiz.uz: ‘can’ dan keyin ‘to’ ishlatmaymiz: Can you help me?
quiz.ru: После ‘can’ не ставим ‘to’: Can you help me?

grammar.title: Adjectives
grammar.lead: Adjectives describe nouns — they tell us what people, places and things are like. Knowing where to put them and learning common opposites makes your descriptions clear.

leadTr.uz: Sifatlar otlarni taʼriflaydi — odam, joy va narsalar qanaqaligini aytadi. Ularning oʻrnini va keng tarqalgan qarama-qarshilarini bilish taʼrifni aniq qiladi.
leadTr.ru: Прилагательные описывают существительные — какими являются люди, места и вещи. Знание их места и распространённых антонимов делает описание ясным.

ex: a red car
an old house
The car is red.
They are old.

p: An adjective usually goes before the noun, or after the verb ‘be’. It never changes for plural.
ex: a red car · The car is red. · two red cars (not ‘reds’)

p: Learn adjectives in pairs.
ex: big ↔ small · hot ↔ cold · old ↔ new/young · happy ↔ sad · easy ↔ difficult

p: When two adjectives describe a noun, opinion comes before fact: a nice big house (opinion + size).
ex: a beautiful old city · a small black bag

p: Use very or really before an adjective to make it stronger.
ex: It’s very cold. · She’s really kind.

grammar.tip: Adjectives never take a plural -s in English: say ‘three big dogs’, not ‘three bigs dogs’.
examples: a red car → two red cars (never ‘reds’)
big ↔ small · hot ↔ cold · easy ↔ difficult
a small black bag (size before colour)
a nice big house (opinion before size)

mistakes.x: a car red
mistakes.v: a red car (adjective before the noun)

mistakes.x: They are happys.
mistakes.v: They are happy. (adjectives have no plural -s)

quiz.q: Choose the correct order.
quiz.e: Adjective before noun: a red car.

quiz.q: The opposite of 'big' is ___.
quiz.e: big ↔ small.

quiz.q: The flowers are ___.
quiz.e: Adjective after ‘be’, no plural -s: are beautiful.

quiz.q: The opposite of 'hot' is ___.
quiz.e: hot ↔ cold.

quiz.q: It's a ___ day.
quiz.e: We need an adjective before ‘day’: a sunny day.

quiz.q: Choose the correct sentence.
quiz.e: Adjective after ‘be’, no -s: are happy.

quiz.q: The opposite of 'difficult' is ___.
quiz.e: difficult ↔ easy.

quiz.q: Which order is correct?
quiz.e: Size before colour: a small black bag.

quiz.q: She has ___ eyes.
quiz.e: Adjective stays singular: blue eyes.

quiz.q: Make it stronger: 'The film was ___ good.'
quiz.e: ‘very’ + adjective: very good.

quiz.q: Find the mistake: 'I have two reds pens.'
quiz.e: Adjectives don’t take -s: two red pens.

quiz.q: Choose the natural order.
quiz.e: Opinion (nice) before size (big): a nice big house.

quiz.q: Complete: 'My grandfather is ___, but he feels ___.'
quiz.e: old ↔ young; adjectives stay singular.

quiz.q: Which sentence is correct?
quiz.e: ‘interesting’ starts with a vowel sound → ‘an’, and the adjective goes before the noun.

quiz.q: Choose the correct description.
quiz.e: ‘an’ (vowel sound) + opinion/fact order: an expensive new phone.

tip.uz: Ingliz tilida sifatlar hech qachon koʻplik -s olmaydi: ‘three big dogs’ deng, ‘three bigs dogs’ emas.
tip.ru: В английском прилагательные никогда не получают -s множественного: ‘three big dogs’, а не ‘three bigs dogs’.

p.uz: Sifat odatda ot oldidan yoki ‘be’ feʼlidan keyin keladi. U koʻplik uchun oʻzgarmaydi.
p.ru: Прилагательное обычно стоит перед существительным или после глагола ‘be’. Во множественном не меняется.

p.uz: Sifatlarni juftlikda oʻrganing.
p.ru: Учите прилагательные парами.

p.uz: Ikki sifat otni taʼriflasa, fikr faktdan oldin keladi: a nice big house (fikr + oʻlcham).
p.ru: Когда два прилагательных описывают существительное, мнение идёт перед фактом: a nice big house (мнение + размер).

p.uz: Sifatni kuchaytirish uchun undan oldin very yoki really ishlating.
p.ru: Чтобы усилить прилагательное, ставьте перед ним very или really.

quiz.uz: Sifat ot oldidan: a red car.
quiz.ru: Прилагательное перед существительным: a red car.

quiz.uz: Sifat ‘be’ dan keyin, koʻplik -s yoʻq: are beautiful.
‘day’ oldidan sifat kerak: a sunny day.
quiz.ru: Перед ‘day’ нужно прилагательное: a sunny day.

quiz.uz: Sifat ‘be’ dan keyin, -s yoʻq: are happy.
Oʻlcham rangdan oldin: a small black bag.
quiz.ru: Размер перед цветом: a small black bag.

quiz.uz: Fikr (nice) oʻlchamdan (big) oldin: a nice big house.
quiz.ru: Мнение (nice) перед размером (big): a nice big house.

quiz.uz: ‘interesting’ unli tovush bilan boshlanadi → ‘an’, va sifat ot oldidan keladi.
quiz.ru: ‘interesting’ начинается с гласного → ‘an’, и прилагательное перед существительным.

quiz.uz: ‘an’ (unli tovush) + fikr/fakt tartibi: an expensive new phone.
quiz.ru: ‘an’ (гласный) + порядок мнение/факт: an expensive new phone.

grammar.title: Quantity: some / any
grammar.lead: ‘Some’ and ‘any’ talk about an amount that isn’t exact. Choosing between them depends on whether the sentence is positive, negative or a question — and on whether the noun can be counted.

leadTr.uz: ‘Some’ va ‘any’ aniq boʻlmagan miqdor haqida. Ular orasida tanlash gap tasdiq, inkor yoki savol ekanligiga va ot sanaladimi-yoʻqligiga bogʻliq.
leadTr.ru: ‘Some’ и ‘any’ говорят о неточном количестве. Выбор зависит от того, утверждение это, отрицание или вопрос, и можно ли сосчитать существительное.

ex: I have some money.
There are some apples.
I don’t have any money.
Are there any apples?

p: Countable nouns have a plural (apple → apples). Uncountable nouns don’t (water, rice, money, bread).
ex: three apples (countable) · some water (uncountable)

p: Use some in affirmative sentences with plural and uncountable nouns.
ex: I have some friends here. · There is some milk in the cup.

p: Use any in negatives and most questions.
ex: I don’t have any money. · Is there any sugar?

p: We use some (not any) in polite offers and requests, even though they are questions.
ex: Would you like some tea? · Can I have some water, please?

grammar.tip: With uncountable nouns, don’t use a/an or a plural: say ‘some bread’, not ‘a bread’ or ‘breads’.
examples: We have some rice but we don’t have any eggs.
"There are some apples in the bag."

mistakes.x: I don’t have some sugar.
mistakes.v: I don’t have any sugar. (negative → any)

mistakes.x: Do you have some questions?
mistakes.v: Do you have any questions? (question → any)

quiz.q: I have ___ apples.
quiz.e: Positive sentence → some.

quiz.q: There isn't ___ juice.
quiz.e: Negative sentence → any.

quiz.q: Is there ___ bread?
quiz.e: Question → any.

quiz.q: Which noun is uncountable?
quiz.e: ‘Rice’ is uncountable.

quiz.q: We have ___ eggs in the fridge.
quiz.e: Positive + plural → some.

quiz.q: Would you like ___ coffee?
quiz.e: Polite offer uses ‘some’.

quiz.q: He doesn't have ___ brothers.
quiz.e: Negative → any.

quiz.q: Can I have ___ water, please?
quiz.e: Polite request uses ‘some’.

quiz.q: Choose the correct sentence.
quiz.e: ‘Bread’ is uncountable → some bread.

quiz.q: There are ___ books on the shelf.
quiz.e: Positive + plural → some.

quiz.q: Find the mistake: 'Do you have some questions?'
quiz.e: In a normal question we use ‘any’: Do you have any questions?

quiz.q: Complete: 'We have ___ rice but we don't have ___ vegetables.'
quiz.e: Positive → some rice; negative → any vegetables.

quiz.q: Which is correct?
quiz.e: Negative + plural → aren’t any.

quiz.q: Choose the natural offer.
o: Do you want some help — yes or no?
quiz.e: Offers use ‘some’: Would you like some cake?

quiz.q: Complete: 'Is there ___ milk? — Yes, there's ___.'
quiz.e: Question → any; positive answer → some.

tip.uz: Sanoqsiz otlar bilan a/an yoki koʻplik ishlatmang: ‘some bread’ deng, ‘a bread’ yoki ‘breads’ emas.
tip.ru: С неисчисляемыми не используйте a/an или множественное: ‘some bread’, а не ‘a bread’ или ‘breads’.

p.uz: Sanaladigan otlarning koʻpligi bor (apple → apples). Sanoqsizlarda yoʻq (water, rice, money, bread).
p.ru: У исчисляемых есть множественное (apple → apples). У неисчисляемых нет (water, rice, money, bread).

p.uz: Koʻplik va sanoqsiz otlar bilan tasdiq gaplarda some ishlating.
p.ru: В утвердительных предложениях с множественными и неисчисляемыми используйте some.

p.uz: Inkor va koʻp savollarda any ishlating.
p.ru: В отрицаниях и большинстве вопросов используйте any.

p.uz: Muloyim takliflar va soʻrovlarda, savol boʻlsa ham, some (any emas) ishlatamiz.
p.ru: В вежливых предложениях и просьбах, хотя это вопросы, используем some (не any).

quiz.uz: Oddiy savolda ‘any’ ishlatamiz: Do you have any questions?
quiz.ru: В обычном вопросе используем ‘any’: Do you have any questions?

quiz.uz: Tasdiq → some rice; inkor → any vegetables.
quiz.ru: Утверждение → some rice; отрицание → any vegetables.

quiz.uz: Takliflar ‘some’ ishlatadi: Would you like some cake?
quiz.ru: Предложения используют ‘some’: Would you like some cake?

grammar.title: Prepositions
grammar.lead: Prepositions are small words that show relationships of place and time. The most common are in, on, at, and a few movement words. Learn them in fixed phrases.

leadTr.uz: Predloglar joy va vaqt munosabatlarini koʻrsatadigan kichik soʻzlar. Eng koʻp uchraydiganlari in, on, at va bir nechta harakat soʻzlari. Ularni tayyor iboralarda oʻrganing.
leadTr.ru: Предлоги — маленькие слова, показывающие отношения места и времени. Самые частые — in, on, at и несколько слов движения. Учите их в устойчивых выражениях.

ex: at 7 o’clock
on Monday
on 5 May
in the morning
in July

p: in = inside / areas (in a box, in Tashkent). on = a surface (on the table, on the wall). at = a point/place (at the door, at school).
ex: The keys are in my bag. · The photo is on the wall. · I’m at home.

p: under (below), next to (beside), between (in the middle of two), behind, in front of, near.
ex: The cat is under the chair. · The bank is next to the school.

p: at + clock time/night (at 7, at night). on + days/dates (on Monday). in + months/years/parts of day (in July, in the morning).
ex: at 6 o’clock · on Friday · in 2026 · in the evening

p: Some phrases must be memorised.
ex: at home · at school · at work · in bed · on time · at the weekend

grammar.tip: Time prepositions follow a pattern: at = small (clock time), on = medium (a day), in = large (month/year). Think small → big.
examples: The book is on the table.
The cat is under the chair.
We meet on Monday at 8 o’clock.
The shop is between the bank and the café.

mistakes.x: I get up in 7 o’clock.
mistakes.v: I get up at 7 o’clock. (clock time → at)

mistakes.x: See you in Monday.
mistakes.v: See you on Monday. (days → on)

quiz.q: The book is ___ the table.
quiz.e: A surface → on the table.

quiz.q: I live ___ Tashkent.
quiz.e: Cities use ‘in’.

quiz.q: The cat is ___ the chair. (below it)
quiz.e: Below = under.

quiz.q: We meet ___ Monday.
quiz.e: Days use ‘on’: on Monday.

quiz.q: School starts ___ 8 o'clock.
quiz.e: Clock time uses ‘at’.

quiz.q: The shop is ___ the bank and the café.
quiz.e: In the middle of two things = between.

quiz.q: My birthday is ___ July.
quiz.e: Months use ‘in’: in July.

quiz.q: She is ___ home now.
quiz.e: Fixed phrase: at home.

quiz.q: The picture is ___ the wall.
quiz.e: A surface (wall) → on.

quiz.q: The dog is ___ the door, waiting.
quiz.e: A point/place → at the door.

quiz.q: Complete: 'I get up ___ 7 ___ the morning.'
quiz.e: Clock time ‘at 7’, part of day ‘in the morning’.

quiz.q: Which is correct?
quiz.e: Fixed phrase: in bed.

quiz.q: Find the mistake: 'The bank is in front the school.'
o: in front the → in front of the
quiz.e: The phrase is ‘in front of’: in front of the school.

quiz.q: Complete: 'See you ___ the weekend, ___ Saturday ___ 5 pm.'
quiz.e: ‘at the weekend’, ‘on Saturday’, ‘at 5 pm’.

quiz.q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: The ball is on the box. (inside it)
The keys are in the table.
The lamp is between two windows.
quiz.e: ‘between two windows’ is correct; the others mix up in/on/at.

tip.uz: Vaqt predloglari naqsh boʻyicha: at = kichik (soat vaqti), on = oʻrta (kun), in = katta (oy/yil). Kichik → katta deb oʻylang.
tip.ru: Предлоги времени по схеме: at = малое (часы), on = среднее (день), in = большое (месяц/год). Думайте малое → большое.

p.uz: in = ichida / hududlar (in a box, in Tashkent). on = yuza (on the table, on the wall). at = nuqta/joy (at the door, at school).
p.ru: in = внутри / области (in a box, in Tashkent). on = поверхность (on the table, on the wall). at = точка/место (at the door, at school).

p.uz: under (ostida), next to (yonida), between (ikkitasi orasida), behind (orqasida), in front of (oldida), near (yaqinida).
p.ru: under (под), next to (рядом), between (между двумя), behind (за), in front of (перед), near (около).

p.uz: at + soat vaqti/tun (at 7, at night). on + kunlar/sanalar (on Monday). in + oylar/yillar/kun qismlari (in July, in the morning).
p.ru: at + время на часах/ночь (at 7, at night). on + дни/даты (on Monday). in + месяцы/годы/части суток (in July, in the morning).

p.uz: Baʼzi iboralarni yodlash kerak.
p.ru: Некоторые выражения нужно запомнить.

quiz.uz: Soat vaqti ‘at 7’, kun qismi ‘in the morning’.
Ibora ‘in front of’: in front of the school.
quiz.ru: Выражение ‘in front of’: in front of the school.

quiz.uz: ‘between two windows’ toʻgʻri; qolganlari in/on/at’ni adashtiradi.
quiz.ru: ‘between two windows’ верно; остальные путают in/on/at.

grammar.title: Question words
grammar.lead: Question words (wh- words) ask for information. Each one asks about something different — a person, a place, a time, a reason. Knowing them lets you ask about everything around you.

leadTr.uz: Savol soʻzlari (wh- soʻzlar) maʼlumot soʻraydi. Har biri boshqa narsani soʻraydi — odam, joy, vaqt, sabab. Ularni bilish atrofingizdagi hamma narsani soʻrash imkonini beradi.
leadTr.ru: Вопросительные слова (wh-) запрашивают информацию. Каждое спрашивает о своём — о человеке, месте, времени, причине. Зная их, вы можете спросить обо всём.

grammar.situation: “Where do you live?” “What do you do?” “When does the film start?” — Question words go first, then we use do / does + subject + verb.

p: What (thing), Who (person), Where (place), When (time), Why (reason), How (way/manner).
ex: What is this? · Who is she? · Where do you live? · Why are you late?

p: How many + countable (how many books). How much + uncountable / price (how much water, how much is it).
ex: How many students are there? · How much is this jacket?

p: wh- word + be + subject.
ex: Where is the station? · Who are they?

p: wh- word + do/does + subject + base verb.
ex: What do you want? · Where does she work?

grammar.tip: Use how many for things you can count and how much for things you can’t (and for prices): ‘How many apples?’ but ‘How much money?’

mistakes.x: Where you live?
mistakes.v: Where do you live? (add do/does)

mistakes.x: What you are doing?
mistakes.v: What are you doing? (be questions: be + subject)

mistakes.x: How much costs it?
mistakes.v: How much does it cost?

quiz.q: ___ is your name?
quiz.e: We ask about a name (thing) with ‘What’.

quiz.q: ___ do you live?
quiz.e: Place → Where.

quiz.q: ___ is your teacher?
quiz.e: Person → Who.

quiz.q: ___ is your birthday?
quiz.e: Time/date → When.

quiz.q: ___ are you sad?
quiz.e: Reason → Why.

quiz.q: ___ apples are there?
quiz.e: Countable ‘apples’ → How many.

quiz.q: ___ is this bag?
quiz.e: Price → How much.

quiz.q: ___ do you go to school?
quiz.e: Place → Where.

quiz.q: ___ old are you?
quiz.e: Age uses ‘How old’.

quiz.q: ___ does she work?
quiz.e: Place of work → Where.

quiz.q: Which question is correct?
quiz.e: wh- + be + subject: Where are you from?

quiz.q: Complete: '___ time ___ the film start?'
quiz.e: ‘What time’ + does (it) start.

quiz.q: Find the mistake: 'How much books do you have?'
quiz.e: Countable ‘books’ needs ‘How many’.

quiz.q: Choose the correct order.
quiz.e: wh- + do + subject + base verb: What do you want?

quiz.q: Complete: '___ is the weather today?'
quiz.e: We ask about weather with ‘How is the weather?’

situation.uz: “Where do you live?” “What do you do?” “When does the film start?” — Savol soʻzlari birinchi keladi, soʻng do / does + ega + feʼl ishlatamiz.
situation.ru: «Where do you live?» «What do you do?» «When does the film start?» — Вопросительные слова идут первыми, затем do / does + подлежащее + глагол.

tip.uz: Sanaladigan narsalar uchun how many, sanalmaydigan (va narx) uchun how much: ‘How many apples?’ lekin ‘How much money?’
tip.ru: Для исчисляемого — how many, для неисчисляемого (и цены) — how much: ‘How many apples?’, но ‘How much money?’

p.uz: What (narsa), Who (odam), Where (joy), When (vaqt), Why (sabab), How (usul/tarz).
p.ru: What (предмет), Who (человек), Where (место), When (время), Why (причина), How (способ).

p.uz: How many + sanaladigan (how many books). How much + sanoqsiz / narx (how much water, how much is it).
p.ru: How many + исчисляемое (how many books). How much + неисчисляемое / цена (how much water, how much is it).

p.uz: wh- soʻz + be + ega.
p.ru: wh-слово + be + подлежащее.

p.uz: wh- soʻz + do/does + ega + asosiy feʼl.
p.ru: wh-слово + do/does + подлежащее + базовый глагол.

quiz.uz: wh- + be + ega: Where are you from?
quiz.ru: wh- + be + подлежащее: Where are you from?

quiz.uz: wh- + do + ega + asosiy feʼl: What do you want?
quiz.ru: wh- + do + подлежащее + базовый глагол: What do you want?

quiz.uz: Ob-havoni ‘How is the weather?’ bilan soʻraymiz.
quiz.ru: О погоде спрашиваем ‘How is the weather?’

grammar.title: Verb patterns: like + -ing
grammar.lead: To talk about activities you enjoy or dislike, English often uses a verb of feeling (like, love, hate, enjoy) followed by the -ing form. This is a key A1 pattern.

leadTr.uz: Yoqtirgan yoki yoqtirmagan mashgʻulotlar haqida gapirish uchun ingliz tili koʻpincha his feʼli (like, love, hate, enjoy) + -ing shaklini ishlatadi. Bu muhim A1 naqsh.
leadTr.ru: Чтобы говорить о занятиях, которые нравятся или нет, английский часто использует глагол чувства (like, love, hate, enjoy) + форму -ing. Это важная модель уровня A1.

ex: I like swimming.
She loves cooking.
good at drawing
before going out

p: After these verbs, an activity usually takes the -ing form.
ex: I like swimming. · She loves dancing. · They hate getting up early.

p: These verbs can also be followed directly by a noun.
ex: I like music. · She loves chocolate.

p: Use don’t/doesn’t + like/enjoy + -ing.
ex: I don’t like cooking. · He doesn’t enjoy running.

p: would like is different: it means ‘want’ and is followed by to + base verb or a noun.
ex: I’d like to go home. · I’d like a coffee.

grammar.tip: Don’t confuse like + -ing (enjoy an activity) with would like + to (want something now): ‘I like swimming’ vs. ‘I’d like to swim now.’
examples: I’d like to go home now. (= want)

mistakes.x: I like swim.
mistakes.v: I like swimming. (like + -ing)

mistakes.x: I enjoy to read.
mistakes.v: I enjoy reading. (enjoy + -ing)

quiz.q: I like ___ books.
quiz.e: After ‘like’ we use -ing: reading.

quiz.q: She loves ___.
quiz.e: love + -ing: dancing.

quiz.q: They hate ___ up early.
quiz.e: hate + -ing: getting.

quiz.q: I like ___. (a noun)
quiz.e: like + noun: music.

quiz.q: We enjoy ___ football.
quiz.e: enjoy + -ing: playing.

quiz.q: He doesn't like ___.
quiz.e: don’t/doesn’t like + -ing: cooking.

quiz.q: Choose the correct sentence.
quiz.e: like + -ing: I like swimming.

quiz.q: She loves ___ to music.
quiz.e: love + -ing: listening.

quiz.q: I'd like ___ a sandwich, please.
quiz.e: would like + to + base verb: to have.

quiz.q: They don't enjoy ___ in winter.
quiz.e: enjoy + -ing: running.

quiz.q: Which sentence is correct?
quiz.e: would like + to + base verb: I’d like to swim.

quiz.q: Complete: 'She likes ___ but she'd like ___ a new hobby.'
quiz.e: like + -ing (painting); would like + to (to find).

quiz.q: Find the mistake: 'I love to cooking.'
quiz.e: After ‘love’ use -ing without ‘to’: I love cooking.

quiz.q: Choose the natural request.
o: I like to a tea, please.
quiz.e: Polite request: I’d like a tea, please.

quiz.q: Complete: 'Do you like ___? — Yes, but I'd like ___ a film tonight.'
quiz.e: like + -ing (reading); would like + to (to watch).

tip.uz: like + -ing (mashgʻulotdan zavq) va would like + to (hozir biror narsani xohlash)ni adashtirmang: ‘I like swimming’ vs ‘I’d like to swim now.’
tip.ru: Не путайте like + -ing (нравится занятие) и would like + to (хотеть сейчас): ‘I like swimming’ vs ‘I’d like to swim now.’

p.uz: Bu feʼllardan keyin mashgʻulot odatda -ing shaklini oladi.
p.ru: После этих глаголов занятие обычно стоит в форме -ing.

p.uz: Bu feʼllardan keyin toʻgʻridan-toʻgʻri ot ham kelishi mumkin.
p.ru: После этих глаголов может идти и прямо существительное.

p.uz: don’t/doesn’t + like/enjoy + -ing ishlating.
p.ru: Используйте don’t/doesn’t + like/enjoy + -ing.

p.uz: would like boshqacha: u ‘xohlamoq’ degani va undan keyin to + asosiy feʼl yoki ot keladi.
p.ru: would like — другое: значит ‘хотеть’, и за ним следует to + базовый глагол или существительное.

quiz.uz: would like + to + asosiy feʼl: to have.
quiz.ru: would like + to + базовый глагол: to have.

quiz.uz: would like + to + asosiy feʼl: I’d like to swim.
quiz.ru: would like + to + базовый глагол: I’d like to swim.

quiz.uz: ‘love’ dan keyin ‘to’siz -ing ishlating: I love cooking.
Muloyim soʻrov: I’d like a tea, please.
quiz.ru: Вежливая просьба: I’d like a tea, please.

grammar.title: Numbers & measures
grammar.lead: Numbers are everywhere — ages, prices, dates and the time. This lesson covers cardinal and ordinal numbers, and how to say dates, prices and the clock.

leadTr.uz: Sonlar hamma joyda — yosh, narx, sana va vaqt. Bu dars sanoq va tartib sonlarni, hamda sana, narx va soatni qanday aytishni oʻrgatadi.
leadTr.ru: Числа повсюду — возраст, цены, даты и время. Этот урок охватывает количественные и порядковые числительные, а также как называть даты, цены и время.

p: These count: one, two, three… Note the tricky ‘teens’ and ‘tens’: thirteen vs. thirty, fifteen vs. fifty.
ex: 13 = thirteen · 30 = thirty · 15 = fifteen · 50 = fifty

p: These show order: first (1st), second (2nd), third (3rd), fourth (4th)… We use them for dates and floors.
ex: the first of May · the third floor

p: Say the day as an ordinal: ‘the 5th of June’ or ‘June the 5th’. Years: 2026 = ‘twenty twenty-six’.
ex: My birthday is the 12th of July.

p: Prices: $5.50 = ‘five fifty’ / ‘five dollars fifty’. Time: 9:00 = ‘nine o’clock’, 9:15 = ‘quarter past nine’, 9:30 = ‘half past nine’, 9:45 = ‘quarter to ten’.
ex: It’s half past six. · It costs twenty euros.

grammar.tip: Listen for the stress to tell teens from tens: thirTEEN (stress at the end) vs. THIRty (stress at the start).
examples: the first of May; the third floor.
6:30 = half past six; 7:45 = quarter to eight.
My exam is on the 12th of June.
"There are twenty students in my class."
"I need three hundred grams of sugar."

mistakes.x: two hundreds people
mistakes.v: two hundred people (no -s after a number)

mistakes.x: I am twenty years.
mistakes.v: I am twenty years old.

mistakes.x: It costs five dollar.
mistakes.v: It costs five dollars. (plural after numbers > 1)

quiz.q: How do you write the number 15?
quiz.e: 15 = fifteen.

quiz.q: The ordinal form of 'two' is ___.
quiz.e: two → second (2nd).

quiz.q: Which is a month?
quiz.e: August is a month.
A full hour → o’clock.

quiz.q: Which number comes after nineteen?
quiz.e: After 19 comes 20 (twenty).

quiz.q: 30 is written ___.
quiz.e: 30 = thirty (note: not thirteen).

quiz.q: The 3rd of May means the ___ day of May.
quiz.e: 3rd = third.
6:30 = half past six.

quiz.q: The ordinal of 'five' is ___.
quiz.e: five → fifth.
Prices: ‘ten twenty’.

quiz.q: Which is correct for 13 vs 30?
quiz.e: thirteen = 13; thirty = 30.
7:45 = quarter to eight.

quiz.q: How do you say the year 2026?
quiz.e: 2026 is usually ‘twenty twenty-six’.

quiz.q: Complete the date: 'My exam is on the ___ of March.' (1)
quiz.e: Dates use ordinals: the first of March.

quiz.q: It's 8:15. The correct phrase is ___.
quiz.e: 8:15 = quarter past eight.

tip.uz: Oʻn va oʻnlikni urgʻudan farqlang: thirTEEN (oxirida urgʻu) vs THIRty (boshida urgʻu).
tip.ru: Различайте «-надцать» и десятки по ударению: thirTEEN (ударение в конце) vs THIRty (ударение в начале).

p.uz: Ular sanaydi: one, two, three… ‘teens’ va ‘tens’ chalkash: thirteen vs thirty, fifteen vs fifty.
p.ru: Они считают: one, two, three… Внимание к ‘teens’ и ‘tens’: thirteen vs thirty, fifteen vs fifty.

p.uz: Ular tartibni koʻrsatadi: first (1st), second (2nd), third (3rd), fourth (4th)… Ularni sana va qavatlar uchun ishlatamiz.
p.ru: Они показывают порядок: first (1st), second (2nd), third (3rd), fourth (4th)… Используем для дат и этажей.

p.uz: Kunni tartib son bilan ayting: ‘the 5th of June’ yoki ‘June the 5th’. Yillar: 2026 = ‘twenty twenty-six’.
p.ru: День называйте порядковым: ‘the 5th of June’ или ‘June the 5th’. Годы: 2026 = ‘twenty twenty-six’.

p.uz: Narxlar: $5.50 = ‘five fifty’ / ‘five dollars fifty’. Vaqt: 9:00 = ‘nine o’clock’, 9:15 = ‘quarter past nine’, 9:30 = ‘half past nine’, 9:45 = ‘quarter to ten’.
p.ru: Цены: $5.50 = ‘five fifty’ / ‘five dollars fifty’. Время: 9:00 = ‘nine o’clock’, 9:15 = ‘quarter past nine’, 9:30 = ‘half past nine’, 9:45 = ‘quarter to ten’.

quiz.uz: Sanalar tartib sonni ishlatadi: the first of March.
quiz.ru: Даты используют порядковые: the first of March.

grammar.title: Adverbs of frequency
grammar.lead: Words like always, usually, often, sometimes and never tell us how often something happens. In this lesson you learn where to put them in a sentence.

leadTr.uz: always, usually, often, sometimes va never so'zlari ish-harakat qanchalik tez-tez bo'lishini bildiradi. Bu darsda ularni gapda qayerga qo'yishni o'rganasiz.
leadTr.ru: Слова always, usually, often, sometimes и never показывают, как часто что-то происходит. В этом уроке вы узнаете, куда ставить их в предложении.

grammar.situation: Aziz: "Do you eat plov every day?" Lola: "No! I usually eat plov on Thursdays. I never cook it at home — my mother always makes it."

p: Adverbs of frequency make a scale: always (100%), usually, often, sometimes, rarely, never (0%).
They answer the question "How often?"
ex: I always drink tea in the morning.
She sometimes walks to school.
We never watch TV at breakfast.

p: With normal verbs (eat, go, play…), the adverb goes BEFORE the verb: subject + adverb + verb.
ex: Aziz often plays football on Sundays.
They usually go to the bazaar on Saturday.

p: With am / is / are, the adverb goes AFTER the verb be, not before it.
ex: Lola is always happy in the morning.
The buses are often late in Tashkent.
I am never tired on holiday.

p: To ask about frequency, use How often…? You can answer with phrases like every day, once a week, twice a month. These phrases go at the END of the sentence.
ex: How often do you visit your grandmother? — Once a week.
I clean my room every day.

grammar.tip: Remember the rule in three words: BEFORE normal verbs, AFTER be. "I often read" but "I am often busy".
examples: My father always drinks green tea after lunch.
We sometimes have dinner at my uncle's house.
Lola is usually at home in the evening.
How often do you play chess? — Twice a week.

mistakes.x: I go always to school by bus.
mistakes.v: I always go to school by bus. — the adverb goes before a normal verb.

mistakes.x: She always is late.
mistakes.v: She is always late. — with be, the adverb comes after it.

mistakes.x: I every day eat breakfast.
mistakes.v: I eat breakfast every day. — time phrases like every day go at the end.

quiz.q: Which word means 100% of the time?
quiz.e: always = 100%, never = 0%.

quiz.q: I ___ drink coffee at night. (0%)
quiz.e: 0% of the time = never.

quiz.q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: Often she visits always her aunt.
quiz.e: The adverb goes before a normal verb: often visits.

quiz.q: Aziz ___ late for class. He is a good student.
quiz.e: With be, the adverb comes after it: is never.

quiz.q: Put the words in order: usually / we / at home / have lunch
o: We have usually lunch at home.
Usually we have at home lunch.
We usually have lunch at home.
We have lunch usually at home.
quiz.e: Subject + adverb + verb: We usually have…

quiz.q: ___ do you go to the bazaar?
quiz.e: We ask about frequency with How often…?

quiz.q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: I am sometimes tired after work.
I sometimes am tired after work.
I am tired sometimes am after work.
Sometimes am I tired after work.
quiz.e: After be: am sometimes tired.

quiz.q: They play football ___.
quiz.e: The correct phrase is twice a week.

quiz.q: Which sentence is correct?
o: My mother cooks every day plov.
My mother every day cooks plov.
Every day cooks my mother plov.
My mother cooks plov every day.
quiz.e: Time phrases like every day go at the end of the sentence.

quiz.q: Choose the sentence with the correct word order.
o: The metro always is busy, and I often take it.
The metro is always busy, and I often take it.
The metro is always busy, and I take often it.
Always the metro is busy, and often I take.
quiz.e: After be (is always busy) but before a normal verb (often take).

situation.uz: Aziz: "Do you eat plov every day?" Lola: "No! I usually eat plov on Thursdays." — usually va never fe'ldan oldin, always ham shunday: my mother always makes it.
situation.ru: Азиз спрашивает, ест ли Лола плов каждый день. В ответе usually, never и always стоят перед смысловым глаголом: I usually eat, I never cook, my mother always makes.

tip.uz: Qoidani uch so'zda eslang: oddiy fe'ldan OLDIN, be dan KEYIN. "I often read", lekin "I am often busy".
tip.ru: Запомните правило: ПЕРЕД обычным глаголом, ПОСЛЕ be. "I often read", но "I am often busy".

p.uz: Takrorlanish ravishlari shkala hosil qiladi: always (100%), usually, often, sometimes, rarely, never (0%).
p.ru: Наречия частотности образуют шкалу: always (100%), usually, often, sometimes, rarely, never (0%).

p.uz: Ular "How often?" (qanchalik tez-tez?) savoliga javob beradi.
p.ru: Они отвечают на вопрос "How often?" (как часто?).

p.uz: Oddiy fe'llar (eat, go, play…) bilan ravish fe'ldan OLDIN keladi: ega + ravish + fe'l.
p.ru: С обычными глаголами (eat, go, play…) наречие стоит ПЕРЕД глаголом: подлежащее + наречие + глагол.

p.uz: am / is / are bilan ravish be dan KEYIN keladi, oldin emas.
p.ru: С am / is / are наречие стоит ПОСЛЕ be, а не перед ним.

p.uz: Tezlik haqida so'rash uchun How often…? ishlatiladi. Javobda every day, once a week, twice a month kabi iboralar bo'lishi mumkin — ular gap OXIRIDA keladi.
p.ru: Чтобы спросить о частоте, используйте How often…? Отвечать можно фразами every day, once a week, twice a month — они ставятся в КОНЦЕ предложения.

quiz.uz: Ravish oddiy fe'ldan oldin: often visits.
quiz.ru: Наречие перед обычным глаголом: often visits.

quiz.uz: be bilan ravish undan keyin keladi: is never.
quiz.ru: С be наречие идёт после него: is never.

quiz.uz: Ega + ravish + fe'l: We usually have…
quiz.ru: Подлежащее + наречие + глагол: We usually have…
О частоте спрашиваем с How often…?

quiz.uz: be dan keyin: am sometimes tired.
every day kabi iboralar gap oxirida keladi.
quiz.ru: Фразы типа every day ставятся в конце предложения.

quiz.uz: be dan keyin (is always busy), oddiy fe'ldan oldin (often take).
quiz.ru: После be (is always busy), но перед обычным глаголом (often take).

grammar.title: Object pronouns
grammar.lead: Me, you, him, her, it, us and them are object pronouns. We use them after verbs and prepositions instead of repeating a noun.

leadTr.uz: Me, you, him, her, it, us va them — vositali (obyekt) olmoshlar. Ularni otni takrorlamaslik uchun fe'l va predloglardan keyin ishlatamiz.
leadTr.ru: Me, you, him, her, it, us и them — объектные местоимения. Мы используем их после глаголов и предлогов, чтобы не повторять существительное.

grammar.situation: Lola: "Do you know Aziz?" Karim: "Yes, I know him well. I play football with him every week. He often helps me with English."

p: Every subject pronoun has an object partner: I → me, you → you, he → him, she → her, it → it, we → us, they → them.
The subject does the action; the object receives it.
ex: I like her. She likes me.
We help them. They help us.

p: The object pronoun comes after the verb: verb + object pronoun.
ex: Aziz has a new phone. He bought it yesterday.
Where is Lola? I can't see her.
Call me tonight, please.

p: After words like with, for, to, at, about, we also use object pronouns, never subject pronouns.
ex: This present is for you.
Come with us to the bazaar!
She is talking about him.

p: Use the pronoun instead of the noun — do not say the noun and the pronoun together in one place.
ex: I love plov. I eat it every Thursday.
My grandparents live in Samarkand. We visit them in summer.

grammar.tip: After a preposition, always use the object form: "with me", "for him", "to us" — never "with I" or "for he".
examples: This is my sister. Do you know her?
The teacher gave us a lot of homework.
I like these shoes. Can I try them on?
Wait for me at the metro station!

mistakes.x: I saw she at the market.
mistakes.v: I saw her at the market. — after a verb we need the object form.

mistakes.x: Come with I.
mistakes.v: Come with me. — after a preposition, use the object pronoun.

mistakes.x: I like Aziz. I like he very much.
mistakes.v: I like him very much. — he is a subject form; after a verb use him.

quiz.q: What is the object pronoun for "he"?
quiz.e: he → him. (his is possessive.)

quiz.q: I have a dog. I walk ___ every morning.
quiz.e: A dog is it → object form it.

quiz.q: Where is Lola? I want to talk to ___.
quiz.e: After the preposition to → her.

quiz.q: My parents are at home. I am cooking dinner for ___.
quiz.e: they → them after the preposition for.

quiz.q: Can you help ___? We don't understand this exercise.
quiz.e: we → us after the verb help.

quiz.q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: I saw they at the bazaar.
I saw them at the bazaar.
I saw their at the bazaar.
I saw themselves at the bazaar.
quiz.e: After the verb saw → object form them.

quiz.q: This is a photo of my brother. Do you know ___?
quiz.e: my brother = he → object form him.

quiz.q: Lola and I are going to the park. Come with ___!
quiz.e: Lola and I = we → with us.

quiz.q: Which sentence is correct?
quiz.e: Give + object pronoun + thing: Give her the book.

quiz.q: I bought apples at the bazaar and gave ___ to my neighbour.
quiz.e: apples (plural) → them.

situation.uz: "Do you know Aziz?" "Yes, I know him well." — Aziz o'rniga him ishlatiladi: fe'ldan keyin (know him) va predlogdan keyin (with him).
situation.ru: «Ты знаешь Азиза?» «Да, я хорошо его знаю.» — Вместо имени используется him: после глагола (know him) и после предлога (with him).

tip.uz: Predlogdan keyin doim obyekt shaklini ishlating: "with me", "for him", "to us" — hech qachon "with I" yoki "for he" emas.
tip.ru: После предлога всегда объектная форма: "with me", "for him", "to us" — никогда "with I" или "for he".

p.uz: Har bir ega olmoshining obyekt jufti bor: I → me, you → you, he → him, she → her, it → it, we → us, they → them.
p.ru: У каждого личного местоимения есть объектная пара: I → me, you → you, he → him, she → her, it → it, we → us, they → them.

p.uz: Ega ish-harakatni bajaradi; obyekt uni qabul qiladi.
