p.ru: Подлежащее выполняет действие; дополнение его получает.

p.uz: Obyekt olmoshi fe'ldan keyin keladi: fe'l + obyekt olmoshi.
p.ru: Объектное местоимение стоит после глагола: глагол + объектное местоимение.

p.uz: with, for, to, at, about kabi so'zlardan keyin ham obyekt olmoshlari ishlatiladi, ega olmoshlari emas.
p.ru: После слов with, for, to, at, about тоже используются объектные местоимения, а не именительные.

p.uz: Ot o'rniga olmosh ishlating — bitta joyda otni ham, olmoshni ham birga aytmang.
p.ru: Используйте местоимение вместо существительного — не называйте их вместе в одном месте.

quiz.uz: Hayvon it deyiladi → obyekt shakli it.
quiz.ru: Собака — это it → объектная форма it.

quiz.uz: saw fe'lidan keyin → obyekt shakli them.
quiz.ru: После глагола saw → объектная форма them.

quiz.uz: my brother = he → obyekt shakli him.
quiz.ru: my brother = he → объектная форма him.

quiz.uz: Lola and I = we → with us.
quiz.ru: Lola and I = we → with us.

quiz.uz: Give + obyekt olmoshi + narsa: Give her the book.
quiz.ru: Give + объектное местоимение + предмет: Give her the book.

grammar.title: Possessive 's & whose
grammar.lead: To say that something belongs to a person, add 's to their name: Aziz's car. To ask who the owner is, use whose.

leadTr.uz: Biror narsa kimgadir tegishli ekanini aytish uchun ismga 's qo'shiladi: Aziz's car. Egasi kimligini so'rash uchun whose ishlatiladi.
leadTr.ru: Чтобы сказать, что вещь принадлежит человеку, добавьте 's к имени: Aziz's car. Чтобы спросить, чья это вещь, используйте whose.

grammar.situation: Teacher: "Whose bag is this?" Lola: "It's Aziz's bag. And this phone is my sister's — she left it here."

p: For one person or animal, add 's after the name or noun: Aziz's, my mother's, the cat's.
ex: This is Lola's book.
My father's car is white.
The cat's bowl is empty.

p: If a plural noun already ends in -s, add only an apostrophe after it: my parents' house.
Irregular plurals without -s take 's: the children's room.
ex: My grandparents' garden is beautiful.
The children's toys are on the floor.

p: Whose asks about the owner: Whose + noun + is/are…? You can answer with a name + 's or a possessive like mine, hers, theirs.
ex: Whose phone is this? — It's Karim's.
Whose shoes are these? — They're mine.

p: 's can also be the short form of is: Aziz's tired = Aziz is tired. Look at the next word: if a noun follows, it is usually possession; if an adjective or -ing verb follows, it is is.
ex: Aziz's bike is new. ('s = possession)
Aziz's riding his bike now. ('s = is)

grammar.tip: Word order is different from Uzbek: in English the OWNER comes first — "Aziz's car", not "car of Aziz's". For things, use of: "the door of the house".
examples: Whose keys are on the table? — They're my father's.
The students' books are in the classroom.

mistakes.x: This is the car of Aziz.
mistakes.v: This is Aziz's car. — for people, use name + 's, not of.

mistakes.x: My parent's are doctors.
mistakes.v: My parents are doctors. — no apostrophe in a simple plural; 's is only for possession.

mistakes.x: Who's bag is this?
mistakes.v: Whose bag is this? — whose asks about the owner; who's = who is.

quiz.q: Choose the correct form: This is ___ phone.
quiz.e: One owner → name + 's: Lola's phone.

quiz.q: ___ book is this? — It's mine.
quiz.e: Whose asks about the owner.

quiz.q: My ___ house is near the bazaar. (two grandparents)
quiz.e: Plural noun ending in -s → only an apostrophe: grandparents'.

quiz.q: The ___ room is upstairs. (the children)
quiz.e: Irregular plural without -s → children's.

quiz.q: Whose pen is this? — It's ___.
quiz.e: Answer with name + 's: It's Karim's.

quiz.q: Which sentence uses 's for possession?
quiz.e: A noun (jacket) follows, so 's shows possession; the others mean Aziz is.

quiz.q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: This is the bag of my sister.
quiz.e: For a person: my sister's bag, owner first.

quiz.q: The door ___ is broken.
quiz.e: For things we normally use of: the door of the house.

quiz.q: ___ shoes are these? — They're my brother's.
quiz.e: Whose + noun asks about the owner; who's = who is.

quiz.q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: My two brothers' names are Aziz and Karim.
My two brother's names are Aziz and Karim.
My two brothers names' are Aziz and Karim.
My two brothers's names are Aziz and Karim.
quiz.e: Two brothers = plural in -s → brothers'.

situation.uz: O'qituvchi: "Whose bag is this?" (Bu kimning sumkasi?) Lola: "It's Aziz's bag." — Egasi ism + 's bilan ko'rsatiladi: Aziz's, my sister's.
situation.ru: Учитель: "Whose bag is this?" (Чья это сумка?) Лола: "It's Aziz's bag." — Владелец обозначается именем + 's: Aziz's, my sister's.

tip.uz: So'z tartibi o'zbekchaga o'xshaydi: EGASI oldin keladi — "Aziz's car" (Azizning mashinasi). Narsalar uchun of ishlatiladi: "the door of the house".
tip.ru: В английском ВЛАДЕЛЕЦ идёт первым: "Aziz's car", а не "car of Aziz's". Для предметов используйте of: "the door of the house".

p.uz: Bitta odam yoki hayvon uchun ism yoki otdan keyin 's qo'shiladi: Aziz's, my mother's, the cat's.
p.ru: Для одного человека или животного добавьте 's после имени или существительного: Aziz's, my mother's, the cat's.

p.uz: Ko'plikdagi ot -s bilan tugasa, faqat apostrof qo'shiladi: my parents' house.
p.ru: Если существительное во множественном числе уже оканчивается на -s, добавьте только апостроф: my parents' house.

p.uz: -s siz tuzilgan noodatiy ko'pliklar 's oladi: the children's room.
p.ru: Нерегулярные формы без -s получают 's: the children's room.

p.uz: Whose egasini so'raydi: Whose + ot + is/are…? Javobda ism + 's yoki mine, hers, theirs kabi egalik olmoshi bo'ladi.
p.ru: Whose спрашивает о владельце: Whose + существительное + is/are…? Отвечают именем + 's или формами mine, hers, theirs.

p.uz: 's shuningdek is ning qisqa shakli bo'lishi mumkin: Aziz's tired = Aziz is tired. Keyingi so'zga qarang: ot kelsa — odatda egalik; sifat yoki -ing fe'l kelsa — bu is.
p.ru: 's может быть и краткой формой is: Aziz's tired = Aziz is tired. Смотрите на следующее слово: существительное — обычно принадлежность; прилагательное или глагол на -ing — это is.

quiz.uz: -s bilan tugagan ko'plik → faqat apostrof: grandparents'.
Keyin ot (jacket) kelgan, demak 's — egalik; qolganlari Aziz is degani.
quiz.ru: Дальше идёт существительное (jacket), значит 's — принадлежность; остальные значат Aziz is.

quiz.uz: Odam uchun: my sister's bag — egasi oldin.
quiz.ru: Для человека: my sister's bag — владелец первым.

quiz.uz: Narsalar uchun odatda of: the door of the house.
quiz.ru: Для предметов обычно of: the door of the house.

quiz.uz: Whose + ot egasini so'raydi; who's = who is.
quiz.ru: Whose + существительное спрашивает о владельце; who's = who is.

reading.title: My Family
reading.text:
Hello! My name is Jack. I am eleven years old. I live in Manchester with my family.
I have one brother and one sister. My brother is fourteen and my sister is seven. My mother is a doctor and my father is a teacher.
We have a small dog. Its name is Bobby. Bobby is brown and very friendly. I love my family very much.

quiz.e: The text says ‘I am eleven years old.’

quiz.e: He lives in Manchester.

quiz.e: His mother is a doctor.

quiz.q: How many brothers and sisters does Jack have?
quiz.e: He has one brother and one sister.

reading.title: Emily's Day
reading.text:
Emily is a student in Leeds. From Monday to Friday she gets up at seven o'clock. She has breakfast with her family and then goes to school by bus.
School starts at half past eight. Emily likes English and art, but she doesn't like maths.
In the afternoon she does her homework. In the evening she watches TV or reads a book. She goes to bed at ten o'clock.
At the weekend Emily doesn't go to school. She plays with her friends in the park.

quiz.e: She gets up at seven o’clock.

quiz.e: She doesn’t like maths.

quiz.e: In the evening she watches TV or reads.

quiz.e: At the weekend she plays with friends in the park.

reading.title: At the Market
reading.text:
On Saturday morning, Tom and his mother go to the market in Oxford. The market is big and busy. There are many people and lots of fruit and vegetables.
Tom's mother wants to buy apples, bread and some milk. The apples are red and fresh. They cost two pounds for one kilo. Tom likes the oranges, so his mother buys four oranges too.
They don't buy any meat today because they have meat at home. After shopping, they are tired and thirsty, so they drink some water and go home by taxi.

quiz.e: They go to the market in Oxford.

quiz.e: The apples cost two pounds for one kilo.

quiz.q: Why don't they buy meat?
quiz.e: They have meat at home.

quiz.q: How do they go home?
quiz.e: They go home by taxi.

reading.title: My Town
reading.text:
I live in a small town near Bath, in the west of England. It is a quiet place, but there is a lot to do.
In the centre there is a big park with tall trees and a small lake. Next to the park there is a library where I borrow books every week. There are two schools, a hospital and many shops.
My favourite place is the café on Green Street. It is between the post office and the bank. The coffee there is cheap and the people are friendly.
The town is not perfect — there isn't a cinema, and the buses are sometimes late. But I am happy here because my friends and family are close.

quiz.q: Where is the town?
quiz.e: It is a small town near Bath, in the west of England.

quiz.e: Next to the park there is a library.

quiz.e: The café is between the post office and the bank.

quiz.q: What does the town NOT have?
quiz.e: There isn’t a cinema.

quiz.q: Why is the writer happy in the town?

quiz.e: He is happy because his friends and family are close.

reading.title: A Letter from Sophie
reading.text:
Dear Grace,

Thank you for your letter. I am very happy to hear from you. How are you and your family?

I am writing to you from my new home in Bristol. Last month we moved here from London because my father has a new job. At first I was sad because I missed my old friends, but now I feel better.

My new school is bigger than my old one. I am learning French and Spanish, and I really enjoy art. French is difficult, but my teacher is patient and I am getting better every day. After school I usually play netball with new friends.

Please write soon and tell me your news. Maybe you can visit me in the summer holidays!

Love,
Sophie

quiz.e: French is difficult, but she is getting better, and her teacher is patient.

quiz.e: She suggests Grace visit her in the summer holidays.

reading.title: Aziz's Morning
reading.text: Aziz lives in Tashkent with his family. Every morning he gets up at seven o'clock. His mother makes fresh non and green tea for breakfast. Aziz eats breakfast with his little sister, Madina. At eight o'clock he takes the metro to school. The metro station is beautiful — it has big lamps and pictures on the walls. School starts at nine o'clock. Aziz likes Mondays because he has an English lesson. His English teacher is from India, and her lessons are fun. After school, Aziz plays football with his friends in the yard.

reading.title: A Postcard from Bukhara
reading.text:
Dear Tom,

Hello from Bukhara! I am here with my parents for three days. Bukhara is a very old city in Uzbekistan. Today we visited the Ark fortress — it is very big and very old. Then we drank tea near a small lake called Lyabi-Hauz. The weather is sunny and warm. In the evening we eat shashlik and watch the lights on the old buildings. Tomorrow we want to buy presents at the market. I love this city!

See you soon,
Lola

listening.script: Seller: Good morning! Welcome! What would you like? — Customer: Good morning. How much are the tomatoes? — Seller: They are eight thousand som for one kilo. The red ones are sweet. — Customer: Two kilos of red apples, please. How much is that together? — Seller: Tomatoes and apples… twenty-four thousand som. — Customer: Here you are. Thank you! — Seller: Thank you! Come again!

quiz.q: How much are the tomatoes for one kilo?
quiz.e: The seller says: eight thousand som for one kilo.

quiz.q: Where are the tomatoes from?
quiz.e: Very fresh, from Fergana!

quiz.q: Which apples does the customer buy?
quiz.e: The customer asks for two kilos of red apples.

quiz.q: How much does the customer pay in total?
quiz.e: Tomatoes and apples together cost twenty-four thousand som.

quizTr.uz: Sotuvchi aytadi: bir kilosi sakkiz ming so'm.
quizTr.ru: Продавец говорит: восемь тысяч сумов за кило.

quizTr.uz: Juda yangi, Farg'onadan!
quizTr.ru: Очень свежие, из Ферганы!

quizTr.uz: Xaridor ikki kilo qizil olma so'raydi.

quizTr.uz: Pomidor va olma birgalikda yigirma to'rt ming so'm turadi.

listening.title: Dilshod's Week
listening.script: Hello! My name is Dilshod. I am a student, and my week is very busy. From Monday to Friday I have classes at university. My favourite day is Wednesday, because we have English in the morning and sport in the afternoon. On Saturday I work in my uncle's shop. I help him from nine to five. It is hard work, but I like talking to people. Sunday is my free day. In the morning I play football with my friends, and in the evening we all have dinner at my grandmother's house. She makes the best plov in our city!

quiz.q: What is Dilshod's favourite day?
quiz.e: His favourite day is Wednesday — English in the morning, sport in the afternoon.

quiz.q: What does he do on Saturday?
quiz.e: On Saturday he works in his uncle's shop from nine to five.

quiz.q: When does he play football?
quiz.e: On Sunday morning he plays football with his friends.

quiz.q: Who makes the best plov?
quiz.e: She makes the best plov in our city — his grandmother.

quizTr.uz: Uning sevimli kuni — chorshanba: ertalab ingliz tili, tushdan keyin sport.
quizTr.ru: Его любимый день — среда: утром английский, днём спорт.

quizTr.uz: Shanba kuni u amakisining do'konida to'qqizdan beshgacha ishlaydi.
quizTr.ru: В субботу он работает в магазине дяди с девяти до пяти.

quizTr.uz: Yakshanba ertalab u do'stlari bilan futbol o'ynaydi.
quizTr.ru: В воскресенье утром он играет в футбол с друзьями.

quizTr.uz: Shahrimizdagi eng zo'r oshni buvisi tayyorlaydi.
quizTr.ru: Лучший плов в городе готовит его бабушка.

grammar.title: Past simple
grammar.lead: The past simple describes finished actions and states at a definite time in the past. It is the main tense for telling stories and talking about yesterday, last week, or years ago.

leadTr.uz: O'tgan zamon (past simple) aniq vaqtda tugagan ish-harakatlarni bildiradi. Bu hikoya qilish hamda 'kecha', 'o'tgan yili' haqida gapirishning asosiy zamoni.
leadTr.ru: Past simple описывает завершённые действия в определённый момент прошлого. Это основное время для рассказов и разговоров о «вчера» и «в прошлом году».

grammar.situation: “What did you do yesterday?” “I watched a film and went to bed early.” — Use the past simple for finished actions at a definite past time.

timeline.note: A completed action at a known time in the past.

p: Most verbs add -ed. Verbs ending in -e add only -d; a consonant + y becomes -ied; a short stressed vowel doubles the final consonant.
ex: work → worked · live → lived · study → studied · stop → stopped

p: Many common verbs are irregular and must be learned.
ex: go → went · have → had · see → saw · make → made · buy → bought

p: Use didn’t + base verb for negatives, and Did + subject + base verb for questions. The main verb returns to its base form.
ex: I didn’t go out. · Did you see the film?

p: Past simple often appears with: yesterday, last night/week, two days ago, in 2010, when I was young.
ex: We arrived two hours ago. · She was born in 2009.

grammar.tip: After didn’t and did, never use the past form: ‘I didn’t went’ is wrong → ‘I didn’t go.’ The past is already shown by ‘did’.
examples: "Yesterday I watched a film and cooked dinner."
"Did you finish your homework? — Yes, I did."
"He bought a new bike two weeks ago."
"We were very tired after the trip."
"We went to the cinema on Friday."
"I didn’t have time to call you."

mistakes.x: I goed home. / She buyed it.
mistakes.v: I went home. / She bought it. (irregular verbs)

mistakes.x: Did you went there?
mistakes.v: Did you go there? (after did → base verb)

mistakes.x: I didn’t saw him.
mistakes.v: I didn’t see him.

quiz.q: Yesterday I ___ football with my friends.
quiz.e: Regular verb + -ed: played.

quiz.q: The past simple of 'go' is ___.
quiz.e: ‘go’ is irregular: went.

quiz.q: She ___ a sandwich for lunch.
quiz.e: Irregular: eat → ate.

quiz.q: We ___ to the cinema last night.
quiz.e: go → went.

quiz.q: The past simple of 'study' is ___.
quiz.e: Consonant + y → -ied: studied.

quiz.q: I ___ TV yesterday evening.
quiz.e: Regular past: watched.

quiz.q: They ___ come to school yesterday.
quiz.e: Past negative: didn’t come.

quiz.q: ___ you see Tom last week?
quiz.e: Past question: Did you see…?

quiz.q: The past simple of 'buy' is ___.
quiz.e: Irregular: buy → bought.

quiz.q: He ___ his keys this morning.
quiz.e: Irregular: lose → lost.

quiz.q: Find the mistake: 'I didn't went home.'
quiz.e: After ‘didn’t’ use the base verb: I didn’t go home.

quiz.q: Complete: 'She ___ a letter and ___ it to her friend.'
quiz.e: Irregular: write → wrote; send → sent.

quiz.q: Which question is correct?
quiz.e: Did + base verb: Did you go out?

quiz.q: Complete: 'We ___ tired, so we ___ early.'
quiz.e: ‘we were’ (plural) and irregular leave → left.

quiz.q: The past simple of 'can' is ___.
quiz.e: can → could.

situation.uz: “Kecha nima qilding?” “Film ko'rdim va erta uxladim.” — Aniq o'tgan vaqtda tugagan ish-harakatlar uchun past simple ishlatiladi.
situation.ru: «Что ты делал вчера?» «Посмотрел фильм и рано лёг спать.» — Past simple используется для завершённых действий в определённое время в прошлом.

tip.uz: didn't va did dan keyin hech qachon o'tgan zamon shaklini ishlatmang: 'I didn't went' — xato → 'I didn't go'. O'tgan zamonni 'did' o'zi ko'rsatib turibdi.
tip.ru: После didn't и did никогда не используйте форму прошедшего времени: 'I didn't went' — ошибка → 'I didn't go'. Прошедшее время уже показано словом did.

p.uz: Ko'p fe'llarga -ed qo'shiladi. -e bilan tugaganlarga faqat -d; undosh + y → -ied; qisqa urg'uli unlidan keyin oxirgi undosh ikkilanadi.
p.ru: Большинство глаголов получают -ed. Оканчивающиеся на -e добавляют только -d; согласная + y → -ied; после краткой ударной гласной конечная согласная удваивается.

p.uz: Ko'p ishlatiladigan fe'llarning aksariyati noto'g'ri — ularni yodlash kerak.
p.ru: Многие частые глаголы — неправильные, их нужно выучить.

p.uz: Inkor uchun didn't + fe'lning asosiy shakli, savol uchun Did + ega + asosiy shakl. Asosiy fe'l boshlang'ich shakliga qaytadi.
p.ru: Для отрицания: didn't + начальная форма; для вопроса: Did + подлежащее + начальная форма. Основной глагол возвращается к начальной форме.

p.uz: Past simple ko'pincha shu so'zlar bilan keladi: yesterday, last night/week, two days ago, in 2010, when I was young.
p.ru: Past simple часто идёт со словами: yesterday, last night/week, two days ago, in 2010, when I was young.

quiz.uz: O'tgan zamon savoli: Did you see…?
quiz.ru: Вопрос в прошедшем: Did you see…?

quiz.uz: 'didn't' dan keyin asosiy shakl: I didn't go home.
quiz.ru: После didn't — начальная форма: I didn't go home.

quiz.uz: Did + asosiy shakl: Did you go out?
quiz.ru: Did + начальная форма: Did you go out?
'we were' (мн. число) и неправильный leave → left.

grammar.title: Past continuous
grammar.lead: The past continuous describes an action in progress at a moment in the past. It is often used to set the scene in a story, or for an action interrupted by another.

leadTr.uz: Past continuous o'tmishdagi muayyan paytda davom etayotgan ish-harakatni bildiradi. U ko'pincha hikoyada vaziyatni tasvirlash yoki boshqa harakat tomonidan bo'lingan harakat uchun ishlatiladi.
leadTr.ru: Past continuous описывает действие, длившееся в определённый момент прошлого. Часто используется для описания обстановки или прерванного действия.

grammar.situation: “At 8 o’clock last night I was watching TV when the phone rang.” — The past continuous sets the longer background; the past simple is the shorter action that interrupts it.

timeline.note: Long action in progress (was -ing) interrupted by a short one (past simple).

ex: I was cooking at 6.
They were sleeping.
…when she called.
…when it started to rain.

p: Use was (I/he/she/it) or were (you/we/they) + verb-ing.
ex: I was reading. · They were playing outside.

p: Use past continuous for the longer action and past simple for the shorter one that interrupts it, often joined by when or while.
ex: I was sleeping when the phone rang.
While she was cooking, he arrived.

p: Use past continuous for two longer actions happening at the same time.
ex: I was reading while my brother was watching TV.

p: Negative: wasn’t/weren’t + -ing. Question: Was/Were + subject + -ing?
ex: She wasn’t listening. · Were you working at 8 pm?

grammar.tip: Use the past simple for the short, completed action and the past continuous for the longer background action: ‘I was walking home when it started to rain.’
examples: "At 8 o’clock last night I was studying."
"They were watching TV when I came in."
"While we were having dinner, the lights went out."
"We were waiting when the bus came."
"While I was cooking, the phone rang."

mistakes.x: I was watch TV.
mistakes.v: I was watching TV. (was/were + -ing)

mistakes.x: While I cooked, he arrived.
mistakes.v: While I was cooking, he arrived.

quiz.q: At 7 pm yesterday I ___ dinner.
quiz.e: Action in progress (I) → was having.

quiz.q: They ___ football when it started to rain.
quiz.e: Background action (they) → were playing.

quiz.q: She ___ a book at 9 o'clock.
quiz.e: In progress (she) → was reading.

quiz.q: We ___ TV all evening.
quiz.e: With ‘we’ → were watching.

quiz.q: The past continuous of 'he sleeps' is ___.
quiz.e: he + was + -ing.

quiz.q: I ___ when the phone rang.
quiz.e: Longer action → was showering.

quiz.q: While she ___, he arrived.
quiz.e: Background action (she) → was cooking.

quiz.q: They ___ when I called.
quiz.e: Negative (they) → weren’t working.

quiz.q: ___ you sleeping at midnight?
quiz.e: Question (you) → Were you sleeping?

quiz.q: Choose: 'I was walking home ___ it started to snow.'
quiz.e: A sudden interrupting action uses ‘when’.

quiz.q: Find the mistake: 'They was playing in the garden.'
quiz.e: With ‘they’ use ‘were’: They were playing.

quiz.q: Complete: 'While I ___ TV, my sister ___ her homework.'
quiz.e: Two parallel past actions → both continuous.

quiz.q: Which sentence is correct?
o: When I arrived, she was cooking.
When I was arriving, she cooked.
When I arrive, she was cooking.
quiz.e: Short action ‘arrived’ + longer background ‘was cooking’.

quiz.q: Complete: 'What ___ you ___ at 10 pm?'
quiz.e: Question (you) → Were you doing?

quiz.q: Choose the correct pair.
o: I was reading when he was calling.
I read when he was calling.
I was reading when he called.
I was read when he called.
quiz.e: Longer action ‘was reading’ + interrupting ‘called’.

situation.uz: “Kecha soat 8da televizor ko'rayotgan edim, birdan telefon jiringladi.” — Past continuous uzunroq fon harakatini, past simple esa uni bo'lgan qisqa harakatni bildiradi.
situation.ru: «Вчера в 8 я смотрел телевизор, когда зазвонил телефон.» — Past continuous задаёт длительный фон, past simple — короткое действие, которое его прерывает.

tip.uz: Qisqa, tugagan harakat uchun past simple, uzun fon harakati uchun past continuous: 'I was walking home when it started to rain.'
tip.ru: Для короткого завершённого действия — past simple, для длительного фона — past continuous: 'I was walking home when it started to rain.'

p.uz: was (I/he/she/it) yoki were (you/we/they) + fe'l-ing.
p.ru: was (I/he/she/it) или were (you/we/they) + глагол-ing.

p.uz: Uzun harakat — past continuous, uni bo'lgan qisqa harakat — past simple; ko'pincha when yoki while bilan bog'lanadi.
p.ru: Длинное действие — past continuous, прерывающее короткое — past simple; часто соединяются when или while.

p.uz: Bir vaqtda davom etgan ikkita uzun harakat uchun ikkalasida ham past continuous.
p.ru: Для двух длительных одновременных действий — оба в past continuous.

p.uz: Inkor: wasn't/weren't + -ing. Savol: Was/Were + ega + -ing?
p.ru: Отрицание: wasn't/weren't + -ing. Вопрос: Was/Were + подлежащее + -ing?

quiz.uz: Ikkita parallel o'tgan harakat → ikkalasi continuous.
quiz.ru: Два параллельных действия в прошлом → оба continuous.

grammar.title: Present perfect
grammar.lead: The present perfect links the past and the present. We use it for life experiences (without saying exactly when), recent actions with a present result, and situations that started in the past and continue now.

leadTr.uz: Present perfect o'tmish bilan hozirgi zamonni bog'laydi: hayotiy tajriba (qachonligini aytmasdan), natijasi hozir sezilib turgan yaqin voqealar uchun ishlatiladi.
leadTr.ru: Present perfect связывает прошлое с настоящим: жизненный опыт (без указания времени) и недавние действия с результатом в настоящем.

grammar.situation: “I have visited London twice.” We don’t say when — the experience matters now, not the exact time.

timeline.note: A past action connected to now — no definite time.

p: Use have (I/you/we/they) or has (he/she/it) + the past participle (the 3rd form: done, gone, seen, been).
ex: I have seen that film. · She has finished her work.

p: Use ever in questions and never in negatives to talk about experiences at any time in your life.
ex: Have you ever been to London? · I have never eaten sushi.

p: just = a very short time ago; already = sooner than expected; yet = used in questions and negatives at the end.
ex: I’ve just arrived. · She’s already left. · Have you finished yet?

p: Use for + a period of time and since + a point in time for situations continuing now.
ex: We’ve lived here for five years. · I’ve known him since 2018.

grammar.tip: Don’t use the present perfect with a finished past time. Say ‘I saw her yesterday’ (past simple), not ‘I have seen her yesterday’. Use the present perfect when the time is unfinished or unstated.

mistakes.x: I have seen him yesterday.
mistakes.v: I saw him yesterday. (definite time → past simple)

mistakes.x: She has went home.
mistakes.v: She has gone home. (past participle)

mistakes.x: I am here since Monday.
mistakes.v: I have been here since Monday.

quiz.q: I ___ my homework. (it's finished now)
quiz.e: Present perfect: have finished.

quiz.q: She ___ to Paris. (experience)
quiz.e: With ‘she’: has been.

quiz.q: The past participle of 'see' is ___.
quiz.e: see → saw → seen.

quiz.q: We ___ this film before.
quiz.e: have + past participle: have seen.

quiz.q: They ___ just arrived.
quiz.e: With ‘they’: have just arrived.

quiz.q: Have you ___ been to Spain?
quiz.e: In questions about experience we use ‘ever’.

quiz.q: I've ___ eaten octopus. (not in my life)
quiz.e: Negative experience: never.

quiz.q: Has she finished ___?
quiz.e: In questions, ‘yet’ goes at the end.

quiz.q: We've lived here ___ 2015.
quiz.e: A point in time → since 2015.

quiz.q: I've known him ___ ten years.
quiz.e: A period of time → for ten years.

quiz.q: Find the mistake: 'I have seen her yesterday.'
quiz.e: With ‘yesterday’ (finished time) use past simple: I saw her yesterday.

quiz.q: Complete: 'She ___ already ___ the email.'
quiz.e: has + past participle (send → sent).

quiz.q: Which is correct?
quiz.e: ‘yet’ goes at the end of the question.

quiz.q: Complete: 'I ___ this book ___ three days, but I haven't finished it.'
quiz.e: ‘for three days’ + present perfect ‘have had’.

quiz.q: The past participle of 'go' (experience: visit and return) is ___.
quiz.e: For an experience there and back we use ‘been’: I have been to Rome.

situation.uz: “I have visited London twice.” Qachonligini aytmaymiz — muhimi hozirgi tajriba, aniq vaqt emas.
situation.ru: «I have visited London twice.» Мы не говорим когда — важен опыт сейчас, а не точное время.

tip.uz: Present perfect'ni tugagan o'tgan vaqt bilan ishlatmang: 'I saw her yesterday' (past simple) to'g'ri, 'I have seen her yesterday' — xato. Vaqt tugamagan yoki aytilmagan bo'lsa — present perfect.
tip.ru: Не используйте present perfect с законченным временем: 'I saw her yesterday' (past simple), а не 'I have seen her yesterday'. Present perfect — когда время не закончено или не указано.

p.uz: have (I/you/we/they) yoki has (he/she/it) + fe'lning 3-shakli (done, gone, seen, been).
p.ru: have (I/you/we/they) или has (he/she/it) + 3-я форма глагола (done, gone, seen, been).

p.uz: Hayotdagi tajriba haqida: savollarda ever, inkorda never.
p.ru: Об опыте в жизни: в вопросах ever, в отрицаниях never.

p.uz: just = hozirgina; already = kutilganidan erta; yet = savol va inkorlarda, gap oxirida.
p.ru: just = только что; already = раньше ожидаемого; yet = в вопросах и отрицаниях, в конце предложения.

p.uz: for + davr (muddat), since + boshlanish nuqtasi — hozirgacha davom etayotgan holatlar uchun.
p.ru: for + период, since + точка отсчёта — для ситуаций, продолжающихся до сих пор.

quiz.uz: 'yesterday' (tugagan vaqt) bilan past simple: I saw her yesterday.
quiz.ru: С 'yesterday' (законченное время) — past simple: I saw her yesterday.

quiz.uz: Borib qaytilgan tajriba uchun 'been': I have been to Rome.
quiz.ru: Об опыте «съездил и вернулся» — 'been': I have been to Rome.

grammar.title: Future: will & going to
grammar.lead: English has several ways to talk about the future. The two most common at A2 are ‘will’ and ‘be going to’. Each fits different situations — predictions, decisions, plans and intentions.

leadTr.uz: Ingliz tilida kelasi zamonni aytishning bir necha yo'li bor. A2 darajasida eng muhimlari — 'will' va 'be going to'; biri bashorat va qarorlar, ikkinchisi rejalar uchun.
leadTr.ru: В английском несколько способов говорить о будущем. На A2 главные — will и be going to: предсказания и решения против планов.

ex: (phone rings) I’ll get it.
I think it ’ll rain.
We’re going to move house.
Look — it’s going to rain!

p: Use will + base verb for instant decisions, offers, promises and general predictions. Short form: ’ll; negative: won’t.
ex: I’ll help you. · It will rain tomorrow. · I won’t be late.

p: Use be going to + base verb for plans you have already decided and for predictions based on what you can see now.
ex: We’re going to visit Rome. · Look at the sky — it’s going to rain.

p: A decision made now = will; a plan decided before = going to.
ex: (phone rings) I’ll get it! · I’m going to study tonight. (already planned)

p: For fixed arrangements with a time, the present continuous is also common.
ex: I’m meeting Sara at six. · We’re flying on Monday.

grammar.tip: For a decision you make while speaking, use will: ‘I’ll have the chicken, please.’ For something you already planned, use going to: ‘I’m going to start a new job.’
examples: "I think it will be sunny tomorrow."
"Don’t worry, I ’ll carry that bag for you."
"We ’re going to buy a new car next month."
"Look out — you ’re going to drop it!"
"We are going to buy a house."
"Look at the clouds — it ’s going to snow."
"They are going to visit us soon."

mistakes.x: I will to call you.
mistakes.v: I will call you. (will + base verb)

mistakes.x: Look at the clouds — it will rain.
mistakes.v: …it’s going to rain. (evidence now → going to)

quiz.q: I think it ___ rain tomorrow.
quiz.e: A prediction → will rain.

quiz.q: We ___ visit our grandparents next week. (a plan)
quiz.e: A decided plan → are going to visit.

quiz.q: The negative of 'will' is ___.
quiz.e: will not = won’t.

quiz.q: (The phone rings.) I ___ answer it!
quiz.e: An instant decision → I’ll answer it.

quiz.q: Look at those clouds! It ___ rain.
quiz.e: Prediction from evidence → is going to rain.

quiz.q: She ___ be twelve next month.
quiz.e: A future fact → will be.

quiz.q: They ___ move to a new house. (already decided)
quiz.e: A plan → are going to move.

quiz.q: I promise I ___ tell anyone.
quiz.e: A promise (negative) → won’t tell.

quiz.q: What ___ you ___ do at the weekend? (plans)
quiz.e: Asking about plans → are you going to do?

quiz.q: Choose the instant decision.
quiz.e: Deciding now → I’ll help you.

quiz.q: Find the mistake: 'I will to call you later.'
quiz.e: After ‘will’ use the base verb: I will call you.

quiz.q: Complete: 'A: I'm cold. B: I ___ close the window.'
quiz.e: Reacting now (offer) → I’ll close the window.

quiz.q: Which shows a fixed arrangement?
quiz.e: Arrangement with a time → present continuous.

quiz.q: Complete: 'We ___ (plan) start a business, and we hope it ___ (prediction) succeed.'
o: are going to / are going to
quiz.e: Plan → going to start; prediction → will succeed.

quiz.q: Choose the correct prediction from evidence.
o: She will have a baby — look!
She's going to have a baby — look!
She will to have a baby.
quiz.e: Evidence-based prediction → is going to have.

tip.uz: Gapirayotib qabul qilingan qaror — will: 'I'll have the chicken, please.' Oldindan rejalashtirilgan ish — going to: 'I'm going to start a new job.'
tip.ru: Решение, принятое в момент речи — will: 'I'll have the chicken, please.' Заранее запланированное — going to: 'I'm going to start a new job.'

p.uz: will + asosiy fe'l: oniy qarorlar, takliflar, va'dalar va umumiy bashoratlar uchun. Qisqa shakl: 'll; inkor: won't.
p.ru: will + начальная форма: мгновенные решения, предложения, обещания и общие предсказания. Краткая форма: 'll; отрицание: won't.

h.uz: be going to — rejalar va niyatlar
h.ru: be going to — планы и намерения

p.uz: be going to + fe'l: oldindan qabul qilingan rejalar va ko'rinib turgan dalilga asoslangan bashoratlar uchun.
p.ru: be going to + глагол: для уже принятых планов и предсказаний на основе видимых признаков.

p.uz: Hozir qabul qilingan qaror = will; oldin qabul qilingan reja = going to.
p.ru: Решение сейчас = will; план, принятый раньше = going to.

p.uz: Aniq vaqti bor kelishuvlar uchun present continuous ham keng ishlatiladi.
p.ru: Для договорённостей с точным временем также обычен present continuous.

quiz.uz: Qabul qilingan reja → are going to visit.
quiz.ru: Принятый план → are going to visit.

quiz.uz: Dalilga asoslangan bashorat → is going to rain.
quiz.ru: Предсказание по признакам → is going to rain.

quiz.uz: Rejalar haqida savol → are you going to do?
quiz.ru: Вопрос о планах → are you going to do?

quiz.uz: 'will' dan keyin asosiy shakl: I will call you.
quiz.ru: После 'will' — начальная форма: I will call you.

quiz.uz: Hozirgi taklif → I'll close the window.
quiz.ru: Предложение сейчас → I'll close the window.

quiz.uz: Reja → going to start; bashorat → will succeed.
quiz.ru: План → going to start; предсказание → will succeed.

quiz.uz: Dalilga asoslangan → is going to have.
quiz.ru: По признакам → is going to have.

grammar.title: Comparatives & superlatives
grammar.lead: We use comparatives to compare two things and superlatives to compare one thing with all the others in a group. The form depends on the length of the adjective.

leadTr.uz: Comparative ikki narsani, superlative esa bir narsani guruhdagi barcha narsalar bilan solishtiradi. Shakl sifatning uzunligiga bog'liq: -er/-est yoki more/most.
leadTr.ru: Сравнительная степень сравнивает два предмета, превосходная — один предмет со всеми. Форма зависит от длины прилагательного: -er/-est или more/most.

ex: taller than
more expensive than
better than
the tallest
the most expensive
the best

p: One-syllable adjectives: add -er (comparative) and -est (superlative). Double a final consonant after a short vowel; -y becomes -ier/-iest.
ex: tall → taller → the tallest · big → bigger · happy → happier

p: Two or more syllables: use more (comparative) and the most (superlative).
ex: expensive → more expensive → the most expensive

p: Use than after a comparative, and the before a superlative.
ex: She is taller than me. · It’s the biggest city in the country.

p: A few adjectives are irregular.
ex: good → better → the best · bad → worse → the worst · far → further

grammar.tip: Don’t mix the two forms: ‘more taller’ and ‘most biggest’ are wrong. Use either -er/-est or more/most, never both.
examples: "This is the cheapest phone in the shop."
"Maths is more difficult than art for me."
"She is the most intelligent student in the class."
"My new car is better than my old one."
"It was the worst film I’ve ever seen."
"This box is heavier than that one."
"She is the tallest in the class."
"My phone is more expensive than yours."
"Today is the hottest day of the year."
"This test was easier than the last one."

mistakes.x: She is more taller than me.
mistakes.v: She is taller than me. (don’t use “more” with -er)

mistakes.x: It is the most big.
mistakes.v: It is the biggest. (short adjective → -est)

mistakes.x: He is more good.
mistakes.v: He is better. (irregular)

quiz.q: This box is ___ than that one.
quiz.e: Short adjective + -er: heavier.

quiz.q: He is the ___ boy in the class.
quiz.e: Superlative of a short adjective: the tallest.

quiz.q: A car is ___ than a bicycle.
quiz.e: faster than.

quiz.q: The comparative of 'big' is ___.
quiz.e: Double the consonant: bigger.

quiz.q: Gold is ___ than silver.
quiz.e: Long adjective → more expensive.

quiz.q: This is the ___ restaurant in town.
quiz.e: Irregular superlative: the best.

quiz.q: Today is ___ than yesterday.
quiz.e: Irregular comparative: worse.

quiz.q: The superlative of 'happy' is ___.
quiz.e: -y → -iest: happiest.

quiz.q: She is ___ student in the school.
quiz.e: Long adjective superlative: the most intelligent.

quiz.q: My bag is ___ than yours.
quiz.e: heavier than.

quiz.q: Find the mistake: 'This is more cheaper than that.'
quiz.e: Don’t use ‘more’ with -er: cheaper than.

quiz.q: Complete: 'It is ___ city ___ the country.'
quiz.e: Superlative: the biggest city in the country.

quiz.q: Which is correct?
quiz.e: Use ‘the tallest’ (no ‘most’ with short adjectives).

quiz.q: Complete: 'This exam was ___ than the last one, but not ___ I've ever taken.'
quiz.e: more difficult than … the most difficult.

quiz.q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: My results are gooder than his.
My results are better than his.
My results are more good than his.
My results are best than his.
quiz.e: good → better (irregular).

tip.uz: Ikki shaklni aralashtirmang: 'more taller' va 'most biggest' — xato. Yoki -er/-est, yoki more/most — hech qachon ikkalasi birga emas.
tip.ru: Не смешивайте формы: 'more taller' и 'most biggest' — ошибка. Либо -er/-est, либо more/most, но никогда вместе.

p.uz: Bir bo'g'inli sifatlar: -er (qiyosiy) va -est (orttirma). Qisqa unlidan keyin undosh ikkilanadi; -y → -ier/-iest.
p.ru: Односложные: -er (сравнительная) и -est (превосходная). После краткой гласной согласная удваивается; -y → -ier/-iest.

p.uz: Ikki va undan ko'p bo'g'in: more (qiyosiy) va the most (orttirma).
p.ru: Два и более слога: more (сравнительная) и the most (превосходная).

p.uz: Qiyosiy shakldan keyin than, orttirma shakldan oldin the.
p.ru: После сравнительной — than, перед превосходной — the.

p.uz: Ba'zi sifatlar noto'g'ri o'zgaradi: good → better → the best.
p.ru: Некоторые прилагательные изменяются нестандартно: good → better → the best.

quiz.uz: Uzun sifat orttirmasi: the most intelligent.
Orttirma: the biggest city in the country.
quiz.ru: Превосходная: the biggest city in the country.

quiz.uz: more difficult than … the most difficult.
quiz.ru: more difficult than … the most difficult.

grammar.title: Adverbs of manner
grammar.lead: Adverbs of manner tell us how an action is done. They usually describe a verb and most are formed from adjectives.

leadTr.uz: Ravish (adverb of manner) ish-harakat qanday bajarilishini bildiradi. Ko'pchiligi sifatga -ly qo'shib yasaladi: slow → slowly.
leadTr.ru: Наречия образа действия говорят, как совершается действие. Большинство образуется от прилагательных с -ly: slow → slowly.

ex: a quick runner
She is careful.
He runs quickly.
She drives carefully.

p: Most adverbs add -ly to the adjective. Adjectives ending in -y change to -ily; -le changes to -ly.
ex: slow → slowly · happy → happily · simple → simply

p: Some adverbs are irregular or the same as the adjective.
ex: good → well · fast → fast · hard → hard · early → early

p: The adverb usually goes after the verb (or after the object).
ex: She sings beautifully. · He drives the car carefully.

p: An adjective describes a noun; an adverb describes a verb.
ex: He is a careful driver. (adjective) · He drives carefully. (adverb)

grammar.tip: ‘Good’ is an adjective; its adverb is well: ‘She is a good singer’ but ‘She sings well.’ ‘She sings good’ is wrong.
examples: "The children played happily in the garden."

mistakes.x: He speaks very good English.
mistakes.v: He speaks English very well. (good → well)

mistakes.x: She sings beautiful.
mistakes.v: She sings beautifully. (verb → adverb)

quiz.q: She sings ___.
quiz.e: Adverb of manner: beautifully.

quiz.q: The adverb of 'quick' is ___.
quiz.e: quick → quickly.

quiz.q: He runs very ___.
quiz.e: ‘fast’ is the same as adverb and adjective.

quiz.q: Please speak ___.
quiz.e: Adverb: slowly.

quiz.q: The adverb of 'good' is ___.
quiz.e: good → well (irregular).

quiz.q: They worked ___ all day.
quiz.e: ‘hard’ (= with effort) is the adverb; ‘hardly’ means ‘almost not’.

quiz.q: She plays the violin ___.
quiz.e: Use ‘well’, the adverb of ‘good’.

quiz.q: The adverb of 'happy' is ___.
quiz.e: -y → -ily: happily.

quiz.q: He drives ___.
quiz.e: Adverb: carefully.

quiz.q: Choose the adverb sentence.
quiz.e: ‘speaks quietly’ uses the adverb.

quiz.q: Find the mistake: 'He sings very good.'
quiz.e: Use the adverb ‘well’: He sings very well.

quiz.q: Complete: 'She is a ___ worker and she works ___.'
quiz.e: Adjective ‘careful’ (worker) + adverb ‘carefully’ (works).

quiz.q: Which is correct?
quiz.e: Adverb after the object: answered the question correctly.

quiz.q: Complete: 'The test was ___, so she finished it ___.'
quiz.e: Adjective ‘easy’ (test) + adverb ‘easily’ (finished).

quiz.q: Choose the correct adverb form.
quiz.e: angry → angrily.

tip.uz: 'Good' — sifat, uning ravishi well: 'She is a good singer', lekin 'She sings well.' 'She sings good' — xato.
tip.ru: 'Good' — прилагательное, его наречие — well: 'She is a good singer', но 'She sings well.' 'She sings good' — ошибка.

p.uz: Ko'p ravishlar sifatga -ly qo'shib yasaladi. -y → -ily; -le → -ly.
p.ru: Большинство наречий: прилагательное + -ly. -y → -ily; -le → -ly.

p.uz: Ba'zi ravishlar noto'g'ri yoki sifat bilan bir xil: fast, hard, well.
p.ru: Некоторые наречия нестандартны или совпадают с прилагательным: fast, hard, well.

p.uz: Ravish odatda fe'ldan (yoki to'ldiruvchidan) keyin keladi.
p.ru: Наречие обычно стоит после глагола (или после дополнения).

p.uz: Sifat otni, ravish fe'lni izohlaydi.
p.ru: Прилагательное описывает существительное, наречие — глагол.

quiz.uz: 'fast' ravish va sifat sifatida bir xil.
Ravish to'ldiruvchidan keyin: answered the question correctly.
quiz.ru: Наречие после дополнения: answered the question correctly.

grammar.title: Quantifiers: much, many, a lot of
grammar.lead: Quantifiers say how much or how many. The right one depends on whether the noun is countable or uncountable, and whether the sentence is positive, negative or a question.

leadTr.uz: Miqdor so'zlari (much, many, a lot of) qancha ekanini bildiradi. To'g'ri tanlov ot sanaladigan yoki sanalmaydigan ekaniga bog'liq.
leadTr.ru: Кванторы (much, many, a lot of) выражают количество. Правильный выбор зависит от того, исчисляемое существительное или нет.

ex: How many books?
not many people
a lot of friends
How much water?
not much time
a lot of money

p: Use many with countable nouns and much with uncountable nouns, mostly in questions and negatives.
ex: How many apples? · How much water? · I don’t have much time.

p: Use a lot of (or lots of) with both countable and uncountable nouns, usually in positive sentences.
ex: She has a lot of friends. · We have a lot of homework.

p: Use a few with countable nouns and a little with uncountable nouns to mean ‘a small amount’.
ex: I have a few questions. · Add a little salt.

p: too much/many = more than you want; enough = the right amount.
ex: There are too many cars. · We don’t have enough chairs.

grammar.tip: In positive sentences, a lot of usually sounds better than ‘much’ or ‘many’: say ‘I have a lot of work’, not ‘I have much work’.
examples: "How many students are in your class?"
"We have a lot of homework today."
"Add a little sugar to the tea."

mistakes.x: How much books?
mistakes.v: How many books? (countable → many)

mistakes.x: I have many money.
mistakes.v: I have a lot of money. (uncountable, positive → a lot of)

quiz.q: How ___ apples do you want?
quiz.e: Countable ‘apples’ → many.

quiz.q: How ___ water is there?
quiz.e: Uncountable ‘water’ → much.

quiz.q: She has ___ friends.
quiz.e: Positive sentence → a lot of.

quiz.q: I have ___ books on this subject.
quiz.e: Countable, small number → a few.

quiz.q: Add ___ salt to the soup.
quiz.e: Uncountable, small amount → a little.

quiz.q: There isn't ___ time left.
quiz.e: Uncountable + negative → much.

quiz.q: We don't have ___ chairs.
quiz.e: Countable + negative → many.

quiz.q: There are ___ people in the room. (more than we want)
quiz.e: Countable, excess → too many.

quiz.q: I'd like ___ sugar in my coffee.
quiz.e: Uncountable, small amount → a little.

quiz.q: We have ___ homework tonight.
quiz.e: Uncountable positive → a lot of.

quiz.q: Find the mistake: 'I have much friends.'
quiz.e: Countable positive → ‘many’ or ‘a lot of’ friends.

quiz.q: Complete: 'There isn't ___ juice, but there are ___ apples.'
quiz.e: Uncountable ‘much juice’ + countable ‘a few apples’.

quiz.q: Which is correct?
o: We don't have a enough chairs.
quiz.e: ‘enough’ goes before the noun: enough chairs.

quiz.q: Complete: 'How ___ money do you need? Only ___.'
quiz.e: Uncountable ‘much money’ + ‘a little’.

quiz.q: Choose the natural sentence.
o: He drinks a lot of coffee.
quiz.e: Positive + uncountable → a lot of coffee.

tip.uz: Darak gaplarda 'much'/'many' o'rniga a lot of tabiiyroq: 'I have a lot of work', 'I have much work' emas.
tip.ru: В утвердительных предложениях a lot of звучит естественнее, чем much/many: 'I have a lot of work', а не 'I have much work'.

p.uz: many — sanaladigan otlar bilan, much — sanalmaydigan otlar bilan; asosan savol va inkorlarda.
p.ru: many — с исчисляемыми, much — с неисчисляемыми; в основном в вопросах и отрицаниях.

p.uz: a lot of (yoki lots of) — ikkala tur ot bilan, odatda darak gaplarda.
p.ru: a lot of (или lots of) — с обоими типами, обычно в утверждениях.

p.uz: a few — sanaladigan, a little — sanalmaydigan otlar bilan: 'ozgina' ma'nosida.
p.ru: a few — с исчисляемыми, a little — с неисчисляемыми: «немного».

p.uz: too much/many = keragidan ortiq; enough = yetarli.
p.ru: too much/many = больше, чем нужно; enough = достаточно.

quiz.uz: Sanaladigan darak → 'many' yoki 'a lot of' friends.
quiz.ru: Исчисляемое утверждение → 'many' или 'a lot of' friends.

quiz.uz: Darak + sanalmaydigan → a lot of coffee.
quiz.ru: Утверждение + неисчисляемое → a lot of coffee.

grammar.title: Verb + infinitive or -ing
grammar.lead: After certain verbs we use the infinitive (to + verb); after others we use the -ing form. Learning which verbs take which form is an important A2 skill.

leadTr.uz: Ba'zi fe'llardan keyin infinitiv (to + fe'l), boshqalaridan keyin -ing shakli keladi: want to go, lekin enjoy going. Qaysi fe'l qaysi shaklni olishini yodlash kerak.
leadTr.ru: После одних глаголов идёт инфинитив (to + глагол), после других — форма -ing: want to go, но enjoy going. Какой глагол что требует — нужно запомнить.

ex: want to go
decide to leave
hope to win
enjoy reading
finish working
avoid driving

p: These verbs are followed by to + base verb: want, would like, need, decide, hope, plan, promise, learn, try.
ex: I want to go home. · She decided to stay. · We hope to win.

p: These verbs are followed by the -ing form: like, love, enjoy, hate, finish, stop, mind, suggest, practise.
ex: I enjoy reading. · They finished eating. · Do you mind waiting?

p: Use to + verb to explain why you do something (the purpose).
ex: I went to the shop to buy milk.

p: like + -ing = enjoy in general; would like + to = want now.
ex: I like swimming. · I’d like to swim now.

grammar.tip: Memorise verbs in short phrases: ‘want to go’, ‘enjoy going’. When unsure, remember that want, need, hope and decide take to, while enjoy, finish and stop take -ing.
examples: "They decided to move to a new city."
"We went out to celebrate her birthday."

mistakes.x: I want going home.
mistakes.v: I want to go home. (want + to)

mistakes.x: I enjoy to swim.
mistakes.v: I enjoy swimming. (enjoy + -ing)

quiz.q: I want ___ home.
quiz.e: want + to: to go.

quiz.q: She enjoys ___.
quiz.e: enjoy + -ing: dancing.

quiz.q: We hope ___ the match.
quiz.e: hope + to: to win.

quiz.q: They finished ___ dinner.
quiz.e: finish + -ing: eating.

quiz.q: I need ___ a doctor.
quiz.e: need + to: to see.

quiz.q: He decided ___ at home.
quiz.e: decide + to: to stay.

quiz.q: Do you mind ___ the door?
quiz.e: mind + -ing: closing.

quiz.q: I went to the library ___ a book.
quiz.e: Purpose → to borrow.

quiz.q: She stopped ___ because she was tired.
quiz.e: stop + -ing: working.

quiz.q: We learned ___ in summer.
quiz.e: learn + to: to swim.

quiz.q: Find the mistake: 'I enjoy to read books.'
quiz.e: enjoy + -ing: I enjoy reading books.

quiz.q: Complete: 'She wants ___ a teacher, so she's learning ___ children.'
quiz.e: want + to (to become); learn + to (but here ‘teaching’ as a noun-like activity she practises) → best: to teach. (to become / to teach)

quiz.q: Which is correct?
quiz.e: would like + to: I’d like to swim.

quiz.q: Complete: 'He finished ___ and then decided ___ for a walk.'
quiz.e: finish + -ing (working) + decide + to (to go).

quiz.q: Choose the purpose sentence.
o: I study to passing the exam.
I study to pass the exam.
I study for pass the exam.
quiz.e: Purpose uses to + base verb: to pass.

tip.uz: Fe'llarni qisqa iboralar bilan yodlang: 'want to go', 'enjoy going'. Ikkilansangiz: want, need, hope, decide → to; enjoy, finish, stop → -ing.
tip.ru: Учите глаголы короткими фразами: 'want to go', 'enjoy going'. Если сомневаетесь: want, need, hope, decide → to; enjoy, finish, stop → -ing.

p.uz: Bu fe'llardan keyin to + asosiy shakl: want, would like, need, decide, hope, plan, promise, learn, try.
p.ru: После этих глаголов to + начальная форма: want, would like, need, decide, hope, plan, promise, learn, try.

p.uz: Bu fe'llardan keyin -ing shakli: like, love, enjoy, hate, finish, stop, mind, suggest, practise.
p.ru: После этих глаголов форма -ing: like, love, enjoy, hate, finish, stop, mind, suggest, practise.

p.uz: Nega qilishingizni tushuntirish uchun to + fe'l (maqsad).
p.ru: Чтобы объяснить зачем — to + глагол (цель).

p.uz: like + -ing = umuman yoqtirish; would like + to = hozir istayman.
p.ru: like + -ing = нравится вообще; would like + to = хочу сейчас.

quiz.uz: want + to (to become); o'rgatish uchun → to teach.
quiz.ru: want + to (to become); учить → to teach.

quiz.uz: would like + to: I'd like to swim.
quiz.ru: would like + to: I'd like to swim.

quiz.uz: Maqsad: to + asosiy shakl → to pass.
quiz.ru: Цель: to + начальная форма → to pass.

grammar.title: Present perfect vs past simple
grammar.lead: These two tenses both talk about the past, but they are used differently. The past simple is for a finished time; the present perfect connects the past to now.

leadTr.uz: Ikkala zamon ham o'tmish haqida, lekin: past simple — tugagan vaqt uchun (yesterday, in 2020), present perfect esa o'tmishni hozir bilan bog'laydi.
leadTr.ru: Оба времени о прошлом, но past simple — для законченного времени (yesterday, in 2020), а present perfect связывает прошлое с настоящим.

ex: I have seen that film.
She has just left.
I saw it last week.
She left at 6.

p: Use the past simple with a finished time word (yesterday, last week, in 2010). Use the present perfect when the time is unstated or unfinished (today, this week, ever).
ex: I saw her yesterday. · I have seen that film. (when? not important)

p: Present perfect = experience at any time. Past simple = a specific completed event.
ex: Have you ever been to Rome? — Yes, I went there in 2019.

p: Present perfect shows a present result; past simple just reports a finished action.
ex: I’ve lost my keys. (I can’t find them now) · I lost my keys yesterday.

p: Past simple: yesterday, ago, last…, in 2015. Present perfect: ever, never, just, already, yet, recently, since, for.
ex: She moved here two years ago. · She has lived here for two years.

grammar.tip: A finished time word forces the past simple. ‘I have finished it yesterday’ is wrong → ‘I finished it yesterday.’
examples: "I have visited Paris, but I visited it last spring."
"Have you ever eaten sushi? — Yes, I tried it in Tokyo."

mistakes.x: I have finished it yesterday.
mistakes.v: I finished it yesterday. (yesterday = finished time)

mistakes.x: Did you ever eat sushi?
mistakes.v: Have you ever eaten sushi? (life experience → present perfect)

quiz.q: I ___ my homework yesterday.
quiz.e: ‘yesterday’ → past simple: finished.

quiz.q: She ___ to Japan. (experience)
quiz.e: Experience → present perfect: has been.

quiz.q: We ___ a great film last night.
quiz.e: ‘last night’ → past simple: saw.

quiz.q: He ___ his keys. (he can't find them now)
quiz.e: Present result → has lost.

quiz.q: They ___ here in 2015.
quiz.e: ‘in 2015’ → past simple: moved.

quiz.q: ___ you ever ___ a horse?
quiz.e: Experience question → Have you ever ridden?

quiz.q: I ___ him two days ago.
quiz.e: ‘two days ago’ → past simple: met.

quiz.q: She's not here; she ___ already ___.
quiz.e: ‘already’ + result now → has left.

quiz.q: We ___ in this town for ten years.
quiz.e: ‘for ten years’ continuing → present perfect: have lived.

quiz.q: What time ___ you ___ home last night?
quiz.e: ‘last night’ → past simple: did you arrive?

quiz.q: Find the mistake: 'I have seen her last week.'
quiz.e: ‘last week’ forces past simple: I saw her last week.

quiz.q: Complete: 'I ___ Tom for years. We ___ at school in 2010.'
quiz.e: Continuing ‘have known’ + finished event ‘met’ (in 2010).

quiz.q: Which is correct?
o: Did you ever go to Spain?
Have you ever been to Spain?
Have you ever went to Spain?
Did you ever been to Spain?
quiz.e: Experience → Have you ever been…?

quiz.q: Complete: 'She ___ three books this year, and she ___ this one last weekend.'
quiz.e: ‘this year’ (unfinished) → has read; ‘last weekend’ → read.

quiz.q: Choose the sentence with a present result.
o: I've broken my arm — it hurts!
quiz.e: Present perfect shows the result now: I’ve broken my arm.

tip.uz: Tugagan vaqt so'zi past simple'ni talab qiladi. 'I have finished it yesterday' — xato → 'I finished it yesterday.'
tip.ru: Слово законченного времени требует past simple. 'I have finished it yesterday' — ошибка → 'I finished it yesterday.'

p.uz: Tugagan vaqt so'zi bilan (yesterday, last week, in 2010) — past simple. Vaqt aytilmagan yoki tugamagan bo'lsa (today, this week, ever) — present perfect.
p.ru: Со словом законченного времени (yesterday, last week, in 2010) — past simple. Если время не указано или не закончено (today, this week, ever) — present perfect.

p.uz: Present perfect = istalgan vaqtdagi tajriba. Past simple = aniq tugallangan voqea.
p.ru: Present perfect = опыт в любое время. Past simple = конкретное завершённое событие.

p.uz: Present perfect hozirgi natijani ko'rsatadi; past simple faqat tugagan ishni xabar qiladi.
p.ru: Present perfect показывает результат сейчас; past simple просто сообщает о завершённом действии.

p.uz: Past simple: yesterday, ago, last…, in 2015. Present perfect: ever, never, just, already, yet, recently, since, for.
p.ru: Past simple: yesterday, ago, last…, in 2015. Present perfect: ever, never, just, already, yet, recently, since, for.

quiz.uz: Tajriba savoli → Have you ever ridden?
quiz.ru: Вопрос об опыте → Have you ever ridden?

quiz.uz: 'for ten years' davom etyapti → have lived.
'last night' → past simple: did you arrive?
quiz.ru: 'last night' → past simple: did you arrive?

quiz.uz: 'last week' past simple'ni talab qiladi: I saw her last week.
quiz.ru: 'last week' требует past simple: I saw her last week.
'this year' (не закончен) → has read; 'last weekend' → read.

quiz.uz: Present perfect hozirgi natijani ko'rsatadi: I've broken my arm.
quiz.ru: Present perfect показывает результат сейчас: I've broken my arm.

grammar.title: used to
grammar.lead: We use ‘used to’ to talk about past habits and states that are no longer true. It is a simple way to contrast the past with the present.

leadTr.uz: 'Used to' endi mavjud bo'lmagan o'tmishdagi odat va holatlarni bildiradi: I used to play football — ilgari o'ynardim (hozir yo'q).
leadTr.ru: Used to описывает прошлые привычки и состояния, которых больше нет: I used to play football — раньше играл (теперь нет).

grammar.situation: “I used to play tennis, but I stopped years ago.” — used to describes a past habit or state that is no longer true.

p: used to + base verb describes something that happened regularly in the past, or a state that was true before but isn’t now.
ex: I used to play football every day. · She used to live in Leeds.

p: Negative: didn’t use to (no -d). Question: Did … use to…?
ex: He didn’t use to like coffee. · Did you use to have long hair?

p: ‘used to’ always contrasts the past with now.
ex: I used to smoke, but now I don’t. · We didn’t use to have a car, but now we do.

p: For present habits, use the present simple, not ‘used to’.
ex: Now I go to the gym every day. (not ‘I use to go’)

grammar.tip: In negatives and questions the ‘-d’ disappears: ‘didn’t use to’ and ‘Did you use to…?’, never ‘didn’t used to’.
examples: "I used to live in a small village."
"We didn’t use to watch much TV."
"Did you use to walk to school?"
"He used to be shy, but now he’s very confident."
"They used to play outside every afternoon."
"We used to live in a village."
"There used to be a cinema here."

mistakes.x: I use to live here.
mistakes.v: I used to live here. (affirmative: used)

mistakes.x: I didn’t used to smoke.
mistakes.v: I didn’t use to smoke. (after did → use, no -d)

quiz.q: I ___ play tennis when I was young.
quiz.e: Past habit: used to play.

quiz.q: She ___ live in London.
quiz.e: Past state: used to live.

quiz.q: We ___ have a dog.
quiz.e: Past state: used to have.

quiz.q: They ___ go to the beach every summer.
quiz.e: Past habit: used to go.

quiz.q: He ___ be very thin.
quiz.e: Past state: used to be.

quiz.q: Negative: 'I ___ like vegetables.'
quiz.e: Negative drops the -d: didn’t use to.

quiz.q: ___ you use to have long hair?
quiz.e: Question: Did you use to…?

quiz.q: She ___ like coffee, but now she loves it.
quiz.e: Negative past habit: didn’t use to.

quiz.q: We ___ play outside, but now we stay in.
quiz.e: Past habit: used to play.

quiz.q: Choose the correct question.
quiz.e: Did + use to (no -d): Did you use to smoke?

quiz.q: Find the mistake: 'He didn't used to study hard.'
o: didn't used to → didn't use to
quiz.e: Drop the -d after didn’t: didn’t use to study.

quiz.q: Complete: 'I ___ be afraid of dogs, but now I ___ them.'
quiz.e: Past state ‘used to be’ + present ‘love’.

quiz.q: Which sentence is correct for a present habit?
o: Now I use to run daily.
Now I used to run daily.
Now I am use to run daily.
quiz.e: For present habits use the present simple: I run daily.

quiz.q: Complete: '___ they ___ live near here?'
quiz.e: Did + use to: Did they use to live…?

quiz.q: Choose the natural contrast.
o: I used to play piano, and I still do every day exactly the same.
I used to play piano, but I stopped years ago.
I use to play piano now.
I am used to play piano before.
quiz.e: ‘used to’ contrasts a past habit with the present (now stopped).

situation.uz: “Men tennis o'ynardim, lekin yillar oldin tashladim.” — used to endi mavjud bo'lmagan o'tmish odati yoki holatini bildiradi.
situation.ru: «Я раньше играл в теннис, но бросил много лет назад.» — used to описывает прошлую привычку или состояние, которых больше нет.

tip.uz: Inkor va savollarda '-d' tushib qoladi: 'didn't use to' va 'Did you use to…?', hech qachon 'didn't used to' emas.
tip.ru: В отрицаниях и вопросах '-d' исчезает: 'didn't use to' и 'Did you use to…?', никогда 'didn't used to'.

p.uz: used to + asosiy fe'l: o'tmishda muntazam bo'lgan ish yoki avval to'g'ri bo'lib, endi bo'lmagan holat.
p.ru: used to + начальная форма: регулярное действие в прошлом или состояние, которое было, а теперь нет.

p.uz: Inkor: didn't use to (-d siz). Savol: Did … use to…?
p.ru: Отрицание: didn't use to (без -d). Вопрос: Did … use to…?

p.uz: 'used to' doim o'tmishni hozir bilan qarama-qarshi qo'yadi.
p.ru: 'used to' всегда противопоставляет прошлое настоящему.

p.uz: Hozirgi odatlar uchun present simple ishlatiladi, 'used to' emas.
p.ru: Для нынешних привычек — present simple, а не 'used to'.

quiz.ru: В отрицании -d исчезает: didn't use to.

quiz.uz: Did + use to (-d siz): Did you use to smoke?
quiz.ru: Did + use to (без -d): Did you use to smoke?

quiz.uz: didn't dan keyin -d siz: didn't use to study.
quiz.ru: После didn't — без -d: didn't use to study.

quiz.uz: Hozirgi odat uchun present simple: I run daily.
quiz.ru: Для нынешней привычки — present simple: I run daily.

quiz.uz: Did + use to: Did they use to live…?
quiz.ru: Did + use to: Did they use to live…?

quiz.uz: 'used to' o'tmish odatini hozir bilan solishtiradi (endi yo'q).
quiz.ru: 'used to' противопоставляет прошлую привычку настоящему (теперь нет).

grammar.title: Obligation: must, have to, should
grammar.lead: These modal verbs talk about rules, necessity and advice. ‘Must’ and ‘have to’ express obligation; ‘should’ gives advice; their negatives have different meanings.

leadTr.uz: Bu modal fe'llar qoida, zarurat va maslahatni bildiradi: 'must' va 'have to' — majburiyat, 'should' — maslahat. Inkor shakllari esa turlicha ma'no beradi.
leadTr.ru: Эти модальные глаголы выражают правила, необходимость и совет: must и have to — обязанность, should — совет. Их отрицания означают разное.

ex: You must stop here.
I have to work.
You mustn’t smoke. (forbidden)
You don’t have to come. (not necessary)

p: must and have to + base verb both mean something is necessary. ‘Must’ often comes from the speaker; ‘have to’ often comes from outside rules.
ex: You must wear a seatbelt. · I have to work on Saturday.

p: should + base verb gives advice or an opinion about the best thing to do.
ex: You should see a doctor. · We shouldn’t waste food.

p: mustn’t = it is prohibited (don’t do it!). don’t have to = it isn’t necessary (but you can).
ex: You mustn’t smoke here. (forbidden) · You don’t have to come. (optional)

p: The past of both ‘must’ and ‘have to’ is had to.
ex: Yesterday I had to stay late at work.

grammar.tip: Be careful: mustn’t and don’t have to are very different. ‘You mustn’t go’ = do NOT go. ‘You don’t have to go’ = you can stay if you like.
examples: "You must stop at a red light."
"I have to get up early tomorrow."
"You mustn’t use your phone in the exam."
"We don’t have to pay — it’s free."
"She had to wait an hour for the bus."
"You don’t have to pay — it’s free."

mistakes.x: You mustn’t pay — it’s free, so it’s OK not to.
mistakes.v: You don’t have to pay. (no obligation ≠ mustn’t)

mistakes.x: He must to go.
mistakes.v: He must go. (must + base verb)

quiz.q: You ___ wear a uniform at this school. (rule)
quiz.e: Obligation/rule → have to.

quiz.q: You look tired. You ___ go to bed.
quiz.e: Advice → should.

quiz.q: You ___ smoke here. It's forbidden.
quiz.e: Prohibition → mustn’t.

quiz.q: I ___ get up early tomorrow.
quiz.e: Necessity → have to.

quiz.q: We ___ waste water.
quiz.e: Advice not to do → shouldn’t.

quiz.q: It's free, so you ___ pay.
quiz.e: Not necessary → don’t have to.

quiz.q: Students ___ be quiet in the library. (rule)
quiz.e: Strong rule → must.

quiz.q: The past of 'I must leave' is ___.
quiz.e: Past of must/have to → had to leave.

quiz.q: You're ill. You ___ see a doctor.
quiz.e: Advice → should.

quiz.q: You ___ touch that — it's dangerous!
quiz.e: Prohibition → mustn’t.

quiz.q: Find the difference: 'You don't have to come.' means ___.
quiz.e: don’t have to = not necessary (optional).

quiz.q: Complete: 'You ___ be late, but you ___ come if you're busy.'
quiz.e: ‘mustn’t be late’ (forbidden) + ‘don’t have to come’ (optional).

quiz.q: Which gives advice correctly?
quiz.e: should + base verb: You should study more.

quiz.q: Complete: 'Yesterday I ___ work late, so I ___ cancel my plans.'
quiz.e: Past obligation → had to (twice).

quiz.q: Choose the prohibition.
o: You don't have to park here.
quiz.e: Prohibition → mustn’t park here.

tip.uz: Ehtiyot bo'ling: mustn't va don't have to butunlay boshqa. 'You mustn't go' = borish TAQIQLANGAN. 'You don't have to go' = xohlasangiz qolishingiz mumkin.
tip.ru: Осторожно: mustn't и don't have to — совершенно разное. 'You mustn't go' = идти ЗАПРЕЩЕНО. 'You don't have to go' = можно остаться, если хотите.

p.uz: must va have to + asosiy fe'l — zarurat. 'Must' ko'proq so'zlovchidan, 'have to' tashqi qoidalardan kelib chiqadi.
p.ru: must и have to + начальная форма — необходимость. 'Must' чаще от говорящего, 'have to' — от внешних правил.

p.uz: should + asosiy fe'l maslahat yoki eng to'g'ri ish haqidagi fikrni bildiradi.
p.ru: should + начальная форма — совет или мнение о лучшем действии.

p.uz: mustn't = taqiqlangan (qilmang!). don't have to = shart emas (lekin mumkin).
p.ru: mustn't = запрещено (не делайте!). don't have to = не обязательно (но можно).

p.uz: 'must' va 'have to'ning o'tmishi — had to.
p.ru: Прошедшее от 'must' и 'have to' — had to.

quiz.ru: don't have to = не обязательно (по желанию).
'mustn't be late' (запрет) + 'don't have to come' (по желанию).

quiz.uz: should + asosiy fe'l: You should study more.
quiz.ru: should + начальная форма: You should study more.

grammar.title: First conditional
grammar.lead: The first conditional talks about a real or likely situation in the future and its result. It uses ‘if’ + present simple for the condition and ‘will’ for the result.

leadTr.uz: Birinchi shart gapi (first conditional) kelajakdagi real vaziyat va uning natijasini bildiradi: If + present simple, natijada esa 'will'.
leadTr.ru: Первый кондиционал описывает реальную будущую ситуацию и её результат: if + present simple, а в результате — will.

grammar.situation: “If it rains tomorrow, we ’ll stay at home.” — The first conditional talks about a real, likely future result.

p: The if-clause uses the present simple; the result clause uses will + base verb.
ex: If it rains, we will stay home.
I will call you if I have time.

p: You can start with either clause. Use a comma only when the if-clause comes first.
ex: If you study, you’ll pass. · You’ll pass if you study.

p: unless means ‘if … not’.
ex: You’ll be late unless you hurry. (= if you don’t hurry)

blocks.h: may / might / can in the result
p: Instead of ‘will’, you can use may, might (possible) or can (ability) in the result.
ex: If it’s sunny, we might go to the beach.

grammar.tip: Don’t use ‘will’ in the if-clause: ‘If it will rain’ is wrong → ‘If it rains, we will stay home.’ The condition is in the present simple.
examples: "If it rains, we will stay at home."
"I’ll help you if you ask me."
"You’ll miss the bus unless you run."
"If she studies hard, she will pass."
"If we leave now, we might catch the train."
"If I have time, I ’ll call you."
"We ’ll miss the bus if we don’t hurry."
"What will you do if it snows?"
"If you heat the soup, it ’ll be nicer."

mistakes.x: If it will rain, I will stay in.
mistakes.v: If it rains, I will stay in. (no “will” after if)

mistakes.x: If you study, you passed.
mistakes.v: If you study, you ’ll pass.

quiz.q: If it rains, we ___ at home.
quiz.e: Result clause → will stay.

quiz.q: If you ___ hard, you'll pass.
quiz.e: If-clause → present simple: study.

quiz.q: I'll call you if I ___ time.
quiz.e: If-clause → present simple: have.

quiz.q: If she runs, she ___ the bus.
quiz.e: Result → will catch.

quiz.q: We'll have a picnic if the weather ___ nice.
quiz.e: If-clause → present: is.

quiz.q: If you ___ now, you'll arrive on time.
quiz.e: If + present: leave.

quiz.q: You'll be tired ___ you sleep more.
quiz.e: ‘unless’ = if … not.

quiz.q: If I ___ the exam, my parents will be happy.
quiz.e: If + present: pass.

quiz.q: If it's sunny, we ___ go to the park.
quiz.e: Possible result → might go.

quiz.q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: If it will rain, I'll stay.
quiz.e: If + present, will + base.

quiz.q: Find the mistake: 'If you will help me, I'll finish faster.'
quiz.e: No ‘will’ in the if-clause: If you help me…

quiz.q: Complete: 'You ___ pass ___ you study harder.'
quiz.e: ‘won’t pass unless you study’ = if you don’t study.

quiz.q: Which is correct?
o: If we leave now, we catch the train.
If we leave now, we'll catch the train.
If we will leave now, we'll catch.
If we leave now, we caught the train.
quiz.e: If + present, will + base verb.

quiz.q: Complete: 'If it ___ tomorrow, the match ___ cancelled.'
quiz.e: If + present (snows) + will + base (will be).

quiz.q: Choose the sentence with correct punctuation.
o: You'll be fine, if you relax.
If you relax you'll be fine.
If you relax, you'll be fine.
If, you relax you'll be fine.
quiz.e: Comma after the if-clause when it comes first.

situation.uz: “Agar ertaga yomg'ir yog'sa, uyda qolamiz.” — Birinchi shart gapi real, ehtimoliy kelajak natijasi haqida.
situation.ru: «Если завтра пойдёт дождь, мы останемся дома.» — Первый кондиционал о реальном, вероятном будущем результате.

tip.uz: If qismida 'will' ishlatmang: 'If it will rain' — xato → 'If it rains, we will stay home.' Shart present simple'da bo'ladi.
tip.ru: Не используйте 'will' в if-части: 'If it will rain' — ошибка → 'If it rains, we will stay home.' Условие — в present simple.

p.uz: If qismi present simple'da; natija qismi will + asosiy fe'l.
p.ru: If-часть в present simple; часть результата — will + начальная форма.

p.uz: Istalgan qismdan boshlash mumkin. Vergul faqat if qismi birinchi kelganda qo'yiladi.
p.ru: Можно начать с любой части. Запятая — только когда if-часть первая.

p.uz: unless = 'agar … bo'lmasa'.
p.ru: unless = «если … не».

p.uz: 'will' o'rniga may, might (ehtimol) yoki can (imkoniyat) ishlatish mumkin.
p.ru: Вместо 'will' можно may, might (возможно) или can (возможность).

quiz.uz: If qismida 'will' yo'q: If you help me…
quiz.ru: В if-части нет 'will': If you help me…

quiz.uz: 'won't pass unless you study' = agar o'qimasangiz.
quiz.ru: 'won't pass unless you study' = если не будете заниматься.

quiz.uz: If qismi birinchi kelsa, undan keyin vergul.
quiz.ru: Если if-часть первая — после неё запятая.

grammar.title: Relative clauses
grammar.lead: Relative clauses give extra information about a noun. They begin with a relative pronoun — who, which, that, where — and help you build longer, more natural sentences.

leadTr.uz: Nisbiy ergash gaplar (relative clauses) ot haqida qo'shimcha ma'lumot beradi. Ular who, which, that, where bilan boshlanadi va uzunroq, tabiiyroq gaplar qurishga yordam beradi.
leadTr.ru: Относительные придаточные дают дополнительную информацию о существительном. Они начинаются с who, which, that, where и делают речь естественнее.

ex: the man who called
the book which I read
the town where I live

p: Use who for people and which for things and animals.
ex: The man who lives next door is a doctor.
I bought a phone which takes great photos.

p: that can replace who or which in many sentences, especially in speaking.
ex: The book that I read was excellent.

p: Use where to talk about a place.
ex: This is the café where we first met.

p: Use whose to show that something belongs to someone.
ex: That’s the girl whose brother is a singer.

grammar.tip: Use who for people, which for things; that can replace either. Don’t add an extra pronoun: ‘The man who he lives next door’ is wrong — drop ‘he’.
examples: "The woman who teaches us is very kind."
"This is the laptop which I bought yesterday."
"He’s the player that scored the goal."
"That’s the town where I was born."
"She’s the friend whose car we borrowed."
"The film that we saw was boring."
"The woman who called is my boss."
"This is the book which I told you about."
"That’s the house where I grew up."
"He’s the man whose car was stolen."
"The film that we saw was great."
"It’s a phone which takes good photos."
"This is the café where we met."

mistakes.x: The man which called…
mistakes.v: The man who called… (people → who)

mistakes.x: That’s the house which I live.
mistakes.v: That’s the house where I live. (place → where)

quiz.q: The man ___ lives here is my uncle.
quiz.e: People → who.

quiz.q: I have a watch ___ was very expensive.
quiz.e: Things → which.

quiz.q: This is the school ___ I study.
quiz.e: Place → where.

quiz.q: She's the woman ___ son is a doctor.
quiz.e: Possession → whose.

quiz.q: The book ___ I read was great.
quiz.e: Things → that (or which).

quiz.q: The teacher ___ teaches English is new.
quiz.e: People → who.

quiz.q: That's the restaurant ___ we had dinner.
quiz.e: Place → where.

quiz.q: I like the shoes ___ you're wearing.
quiz.e: Things → which (or that).

quiz.q: He's the boy ___ won the competition.
quiz.e: People → who (or that).

quiz.q: Choose the correct relative pronoun: 'a person ___ helps others.'
quiz.e: People → who.

quiz.q: Find the mistake: 'The man who he lives next door is friendly.'
quiz.e: Don’t add an extra subject: The man who lives next door…

quiz.q: Complete: 'That's the girl ___ bag was stolen and ___ called the police.'
quiz.e: ‘whose bag’ (possession) + ‘who called’ (subject).

quiz.q: Which is correct?
o: The film who we saw was good.
The film which we saw was good.
The film where we saw was good.
The film whose we saw was good.
quiz.e: Things → which (or that).

quiz.q: Complete: 'This is the hospital ___ I was born, near the park ___ is now closed.'
quiz.e: Place ‘where I was born’ + thing ‘which is now closed’.

quiz.q: Choose the natural sentence.
o: I know a place that sells great coffee.
I know a place who sells great coffee.
I know a place whose sells great coffee.
I know a place where sells great coffee.
quiz.e: Things → that (here ‘a place that sells…’).

tip.uz: Odamlar uchun who, narsalar uchun which; that ikkalasini almashtira oladi. Ortiqcha olmosh qo'shmang: 'The man who he lives next door' — xato, 'he' olib tashlanadi.
tip.ru: Для людей — who, для предметов — which; that заменяет оба. Не добавляйте лишнее местоимение: 'The man who he lives next door' — ошибка, 'he' убирается.

p.uz: Odamlar uchun who, narsalar va hayvonlar uchun which.
p.ru: Для людей — who, для предметов и животных — which.

p.uz: that ko'p gaplarda who yoki which o'rnini bosadi, ayniqsa og'zaki nutqda.
p.ru: that заменяет who или which во многих предложениях, особенно в речи.

p.uz: Joy haqida gapirganda where ishlatiladi.
p.ru: О месте — where.

p.uz: Biror narsa kimgadir tegishli ekanini ko'rsatish uchun whose.
p.ru: Чтобы показать принадлежность — whose.

quiz.uz: Ortiqcha ega qo'shilmaydi: The man who lives next door…
quiz.ru: Лишнее подлежащее не добавляется: The man who lives next door…

quiz.uz: Joy 'where I was born' + narsa 'which is now closed'.
quiz.ru: Место 'where I was born' + предмет 'which is now closed'.

grammar.title: Linking words: because, so, but, although
grammar.lead: Linking words join ideas to make your writing and speaking flow. They show reasons, results, contrasts and additions between two parts of a sentence.

leadTr.uz: Bog'lovchi so'zlar (because, so, but, although) fikrlarni bir-biriga bog'laydi: sabab, natija, qarama-qarshilik va qo'shimchani ko'rsatadi.
leadTr.ru: Союзы because, so, but, although связывают идеи: причина, следствие, контраст и дополнение между частями предложения.

ex: I stayed in because it rained.
It rained, so I stayed in.
It rained, but we went out.
Although it rained, we went out.

p: because introduces a reason; so introduces a result.
ex: I stayed home because I was ill. · I was ill, so I stayed home.

p: but joins two contrasting ideas in one sentence; however often starts a new sentence.
ex: It was cold, but we went out. · It was cold. However, we went out.

p: although introduces a surprising contrast within a sentence.
ex: Although it was raining, we played football.

p: and adds; or gives a choice; also adds extra information.
ex: We had tea and cake. · Tea or coffee? · She sings; she also dances.

grammar.tip: ‘because’ is followed by a reason and ‘so’ by a result. ‘I was tired because I worked late’ = the reason; ‘I worked late, so I was tired’ = the result.
examples: "I was hungry, so I made a sandwich."
"Although she was tired, she finished the work."
"It rained all day, so we stayed inside."
"I stayed home because I was tired."
"I wanted to come, but I couldn’t."
"Although it was raining, we went out."
"He was ill, so he stayed in bed."
"Although he is rich, he isn’t happy."

mistakes.x: Because it was late, so we left.
mistakes.v: Use one linker: Because it was late, we left. (not both)

mistakes.x: Although it was hard but he tried.
mistakes.v: Although it was hard, he tried. (no “but” with “although”)

quiz.q: I was tired, ___ I went to bed.
quiz.e: Result → so.

quiz.q: She was happy ___ she passed the exam.
quiz.e: Reason → because.

quiz.q: It was raining, ___ we went out.
quiz.e: Contrast → but.

quiz.q: Would you like tea ___ coffee?
quiz.e: Choice → or.

quiz.q: We had cake ___ ice cream.
quiz.e: Addition → and.

quiz.q: ___ it was cold, we went swimming.
quiz.e: Surprising contrast → Although.

quiz.q: He didn't study, ___ he failed.
quiz.e: Result → so.

quiz.q: I like coffee ___ I don't drink it at night.
quiz.e: Contrast → but.

quiz.q: They stayed home ___ the bad weather.
quiz.e: ‘because of’ + noun (the bad weather).

quiz.q: Choose the reason: 'We left early ___ the film was boring.'
quiz.e: Reason → because.

quiz.q: Find the mistake: 'Although it was late, but we kept working.'
quiz.e: Don’t use ‘although’ and ‘but’ together: Although it was late, we kept working.

quiz.q: Complete: 'I was ill, ___ I missed school ___ I'm fine now.'
quiz.e: Result ‘so I missed school’ + contrast ‘but I’m fine now’.

quiz.q: Which sentence shows a contrast correctly?
o: Because it was hot, we wore coats.
Although it was hot, we wore coats.
So it was hot, we wore coats.
And it was hot, we wore coats.
quiz.e: Surprising contrast → Although.

quiz.q: Complete: 'She studied medicine ___ she wanted to help people, ___ now she's a doctor.'
quiz.e: Reason ‘because’ + addition ‘and now she’s a doctor’.

quiz.q: Choose the correct linker for a result.
o: It snowed heavily because the roads closed.
It snowed heavily, so the roads closed.
It snowed heavily although the roads closed.
It snowed heavily but the roads closed.
quiz.e: Result → so the roads closed.

tip.uz: 'because'dan keyin sabab, 'so'dan keyin natija keladi. 'I was tired because I worked late' = sabab; 'I worked late, so I was tired' = natija.
tip.ru: После 'because' — причина, после 'so' — следствие. 'I was tired because I worked late' = причина; 'I worked late, so I was tired' = следствие.

p.uz: because sababni, so natijani kiritadi.
p.ru: because вводит причину; so — следствие.

p.uz: but bitta gapda ikki zid fikrni bog'laydi; however ko'pincha yangi gapni boshlaydi.
p.ru: but соединяет два контраста в одном предложении; however часто начинает новое.

p.uz: although gap ichida kutilmagan qarama-qarshilikni kiritadi.
p.ru: although вводит неожиданный контраст внутри предложения.
