p.uz: and qo'shadi; or tanlov beradi; also qo'shimcha ma'lumot kiritadi.
p.ru: and добавляет; or даёт выбор; also вводит дополнительное.

quiz.uz: 'although' va 'but' birga ishlatilmaydi: Although it was late, we kept working.
quiz.ru: 'although' и 'but' вместе не используются: Although it was late, we kept working.

quiz.uz: Natija 'so I missed school' + qarama-qarshilik 'but I'm fine now'.
quiz.ru: Следствие 'so I missed school' + контраст 'but I'm fine now'.

quiz.uz: Sabab 'because' + qo'shish 'and now she's a doctor'.
quiz.ru: Причина 'because' + добавление 'and now she's a doctor'.

grammar.title: Question tags
grammar.lead: Question tags are short questions added to the end of a statement, used to check information or invite agreement. The tag matches the tense and reverses the verb.

leadTr.uz: Question tags — gap oxiriga qo'shiladigan qisqa savollar: ma'lumotni tekshirish yoki rozilik so'rash uchun. Tag zamonga mos keladi va fe'lni teskarisiga aylantiradi.
leadTr.ru: Разделительные вопросы — короткие вопросы в конце утверждения для проверки информации. Хвостик повторяет время и меняет утверждение на отрицание.

ex: You’re tired, aren’t you?
He likes it, doesn’t he?
You aren’t tired, are you?
He doesn’t like it, does he?

p: After a positive statement, the tag is negative, using the same auxiliary verb.
ex: You’re from Spain, aren’t you? · She likes tea, doesn’t she?

p: After a negative statement, the tag is positive.
ex: You aren’t tired, are you? · He didn’t call, did he?

p: Use ‘be’ with ‘be’; with other verbs use do/does/did; with the present perfect use have/has; with modals repeat the modal.
ex: They can swim, can’t they? · You’ve finished, haven’t you?

p: ‘I am’ → tag is aren’t I. ‘Let’s…’ → tag is shall we.
ex: I’m next, aren’t I? · Let’s go, shall we?

grammar.tip: The tag repeats the auxiliary verb and reverses positive/negative. Statement positive → tag negative, and the other way round: ‘He’s here, isn’t he?’ / ‘He isn’t here, is he?’

mistakes.x: You’re ready, isn’t it?
mistakes.v: You’re ready, aren’t you? (match the verb & subject)

mistakes.x: She can swim, can she?
mistakes.v: She can swim, can’t she? (positive → negative tag)

quiz.q: You're from Italy, ___?
quiz.e: Positive statement → negative tag: aren’t you?

quiz.q: She likes coffee, ___?
quiz.e: Present simple positive → doesn’t she?

quiz.q: They aren't here, ___?
quiz.e: Negative statement → positive tag: are they?

quiz.q: He can swim, ___?
quiz.e: Modal ‘can’ → can’t he?

quiz.q: You don't like fish, ___?
quiz.e: Negative → positive tag: do you?

quiz.q: She's a teacher, ___?
quiz.e: ‘be’ positive → isn’t she?

quiz.q: They went home, ___?
quiz.e: Past simple positive → didn’t they?

quiz.q: You've finished, ___?
quiz.e: Present perfect positive → haven’t you?

quiz.q: He won't come, ___?
quiz.e: Negative ‘won’t’ → positive tag: will he?

quiz.q: Let's go to the park, ___?
quiz.e: ‘Let’s…’ → shall we?

quiz.q: Complete: 'I'm late, ___?'
quiz.e: ‘I am’ takes the special tag ‘aren’t I?’

quiz.q: Choose the correct tag: 'She didn't call you, ___?'
quiz.e: Negative past → positive tag: did she?

quiz.q: Which sentence is correct?
quiz.e: Positive modal → negative tag: can’t you?

quiz.q: Complete: 'They've been to Paris, ___?'
quiz.e: Present perfect positive → haven’t they?

quiz.q: Choose the correct tag: 'There's a problem, ___?'
quiz.e: With ‘there is’ the tag is ‘isn’t there?’

tip.uz: Tag yordamchi fe'lni takrorlaydi va musbat/manfiyni teskarisiga aylantiradi: 'He's here, isn't he?' / 'He isn't here, is he?'
tip.ru: Хвостик повторяет вспомогательный глагол и меняет знак: 'He's here, isn't he?' / 'He isn't here, is he?'

p.uz: Musbat gapdan keyin tag manfiy bo'ladi, o'sha yordamchi fe'l bilan.
p.ru: После утверждения хвостик отрицательный, с тем же вспомогательным глаголом.

p.uz: Manfiy gapdan keyin tag musbat bo'ladi.
p.ru: После отрицания хвостик положительный.

p.uz: 'be' bilan 'be'; boshqa fe'llar bilan do/does/did; present perfect bilan have/has; modal bilan o'sha modal.
p.ru: С 'be' — 'be'; с другими глаголами do/does/did; с present perfect — have/has; с модальными — тот же модальный.

p.uz: 'I am' → tag: aren't I. 'Let's…' → tag: shall we.
p.ru: 'I am' → хвостик aren't I. 'Let's…' → хвостик shall we.

quiz.uz: Musbat gap → manfiy tag: aren't you?
Manfiy gap → musbat tag: are they?
Manfiy o'tmish → musbat tag: did she?
quiz.ru: Отрицание в прошлом → положительный: did she?

quiz.uz: Musbat modal → manfiy tag: can't you?
quiz.ru: Утверждение с модальным → отрицательный: can't you?

grammar.title: Present perfect with just, already & yet
grammar.lead: Just, already and yet make the present perfect more exact: just = a very short time ago, already = sooner than expected, yet = until now (in questions and negatives).

leadTr.uz: Just, already va yet present perfect ni aniqroq qiladi: just = hozirgina, already = kutilganidan erta, yet = hozirgacha (savol va inkorlarda).
leadTr.ru: Just, already и yet уточняют present perfect: just = только что, already = раньше, чем ожидалось, yet = ещё / уже (в вопросах и отрицаниях).

grammar.situation: Lola: "Have you finished your homework yet?" Aziz: "Yes, I've already finished it. And I've just made some tea — do you want a cup?"

p: Use just for something that happened a very short time ago. It goes between have/has and the past participle.
ex: I've just seen Karim at the metro.
The bus has just left — we're too late!

p: Use already in positive sentences when something happened earlier than expected. It also goes between have/has and the past participle.
ex: She's already bought the tickets.
It's only 10 a.m., but I've already drunk three cups of tea.

p: Use yet in questions and negative sentences about something we expect to happen. It goes at the END of the sentence.
ex: Have you tried Lola's plov yet?
I haven't called my grandmother yet.

p: just and already go in the middle (have + just/already + participle); yet goes at the end of questions and negatives.
A typical mini-conversation: "Have you done it yet?" "Yes, I've already done it." / "No, not yet."
ex: "Has the film started yet?" "Yes, it's just started."
"Have you packed yet?" "No, I haven't packed yet."

grammar.tip: yet almost always stands at the end of the sentence, and only in questions and negatives. If the sentence is positive, you probably need already or just instead.
examples: I've just come back from the bazaar.
Aziz hasn't found a job yet.
Have you seen the new film yet?

mistakes.x: I have finished just my work.
mistakes.v: I have just finished my work. — just goes between have and the participle.

mistakes.x: I haven't eaten already.
mistakes.v: I haven't eaten yet. — in negatives use yet, not already.

mistakes.x: Have you yet washed the dishes?
mistakes.v: Have you washed the dishes yet? — yet goes at the end.

quiz.q: The train has ___ left. It left one minute ago!
quiz.e: A very short time ago → just.

quiz.q: Have you finished the report ___?
quiz.e: In questions, yet goes at the end.

quiz.q: I've ___ seen this film twice, so let's watch another one.
quiz.e: Positive sentence, earlier than expected → already.

quiz.q: She hasn't answered my message ___.
quiz.e: Negative sentence → yet at the end.

quiz.q: Choose the correct sentence.
quiz.e: just goes between have and the past participle.

quiz.q: "Is Lola here?" "No, she's ___ left."
quiz.e: She left a moment ago → just.

quiz.q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: Have you already been to Bukhara yet?
Haven't you been yet already to Bukhara?
Have you been to Bukhara yet?
Have you been yet to Bukhara?
quiz.e: Question + yet at the end; don't mix already and yet.

quiz.q: "Have you done the shopping?" "No, not ___."
quiz.e: The short answer is "Not yet."

quiz.q: It's only Tuesday, but they ___ finished the project.
quiz.e: Sooner than expected, positive → have already finished.

quiz.q: Which sentence is wrong?
quiz.e: already and yet cannot be used together like this.

situation.uz: "Have you finished your homework yet?" "Yes, I've already finished it. And I've just made some tea." — yet savolda oxirida, already va just have bilan fe'l orasida keladi.
situation.ru: «Ты уже закончил домашнее задание?» «Да, уже закончил. И я только что заварил чай.» — yet стоит в конце вопроса, already и just — между have и глаголом.

tip.uz: yet deyarli har doim gap oxirida turadi va faqat savol hamda inkorlarda ishlatiladi. Gap tasdiq bo'lsa, sizga already yoki just kerak.
tip.ru: yet почти всегда стоит в конце предложения и только в вопросах и отрицаниях. В утвердительном предложении нужны already или just.

p.uz: Juda yaqinda bo'lgan ish uchun just ishlating. U have/has va past participle orasida keladi.
p.ru: Используйте just для действия, которое произошло совсем недавно. Оно ставится между have/has и причастием.

p.uz: Biror ish kutilganidan erta bo'lganida tasdiq gaplarda already ishlating. U ham have/has va past participle orasida keladi.
p.ru: Используйте already в утвердительных предложениях, когда что-то произошло раньше, чем ожидалось. Оно тоже стоит между have/has и причастием.

p.uz: Bo'lishini kutayotgan ish haqidagi savol va inkor gaplarda yet ishlating. U gap OXIRIDA keladi.
p.ru: Используйте yet в вопросах и отрицаниях о том, что мы ожидаем. Оно ставится в КОНЦЕ предложения.

p.uz: just va already o'rtada keladi (have + just/already + participle); yet savol va inkorlarning oxirida turadi.
p.ru: just и already стоят в середине (have + just/already + причастие); yet — в конце вопросов и отрицаний.

p.uz: Odatiy mini-suhbat: "Have you done it yet?" "Yes, I've already done it." / "No, not yet."
p.ru: Типичный мини-диалог: "Have you done it yet?" "Yes, I've already done it." / "No, not yet."

quiz.ru: В вопросах yet ставится в конце.

quiz.uz: just have va past participle orasida keladi.
quiz.ru: just стоит между have и причастием.

quiz.uz: Savol + oxirida yet; already va yet ni aralashtirmang.
quiz.ru: Вопрос + yet в конце; не смешивайте already и yet.

quiz.uz: Kutilganidan erta, tasdiq → have already finished.
quiz.ru: Раньше ожидаемого, утверждение → have already finished.

quiz.uz: already va yet bunday birga ishlatilmaydi.
quiz.ru: already и yet так вместе не используются.

grammar.title: Phrasal verbs: basics
grammar.lead: A phrasal verb is a verb + a small word (up, on, off, after…) with a new meaning: get up, turn on, look after. This lesson shows you the most useful ones and how to use them.

leadTr.uz: Phrasal verb — bu fe'l + kichik so'z (up, on, off, after…) va yangi ma'no: get up, turn on, look after. Bu darsda eng kerakli phrasal verb lar va ulardan foydalanishni ko'rasiz.
leadTr.ru: Фразовый глагол — это глагол + частица (up, on, off, after…) с новым значением: get up, turn on, look after. В уроке — самые полезные из них и как их употреблять.

grammar.situation: Mother: "Aziz, wake up! Get up and turn off your alarm!" Aziz: "Five more minutes… OK, OK, I'm getting up. Can you turn on the light, please?"

p: A phrasal verb = verb + particle (up, on, off, out, after…). Together they often have a meaning you cannot guess from the two words alone.
ex: I get up at 6 o'clock. (= leave my bed)
The plane took off on time. (= left the ground)

p: Learn these common ones first: wake up, get up, turn on/off, put on, take off (clothes), go out, come back, look for.
ex: Put on your coat — it's cold outside.
I'm looking for my keys. Have you seen them?
We went out for dinner and came back at ten.

p: With many phrasal verbs, a noun can go after the particle or between: turn on the TV / turn the TV on.
But a pronoun (it, them, him…) MUST go in the middle: turn it on — never "turn on it".
ex: Take off your shoes. = Take your shoes off.
These are new words. Write them down, please.

p: Some phrasal verbs never split. The noun or pronoun always comes after the particle: look after, look for, get on/off (a bus).
ex: Lola looks after her little brother on Sundays.
We got on the bus near the bazaar.

grammar.tip: When you learn a new phrasal verb, learn it in a full sentence — "I turned off the light" — not as a lonely pair of words. The sentence shows you where the object goes.
examples: I wake up at seven and get up at ten past seven.
Can you turn the music down? The baby is sleeping.
He took off his shoes at the door.
She is looking for a new job in Tashkent.

mistakes.x: Please turn on it.
mistakes.v: Please turn it on. — a pronoun goes between the verb and the particle.

mistakes.x: She looks her grandmother after.
mistakes.v: She looks after her grandmother. — look after never splits.

mistakes.x: I look forward my holiday.
mistakes.v: I'm looking for / I look after… — check the particle: every phrasal verb has its own.

quiz.q: I ___ at 6:30 every morning, but I stay in bed until 7.
quiz.e: wake up = stop sleeping; get up = leave the bed.

quiz.q: It's dark in here. Can you ___ the light?
quiz.e: turn on = start a light or machine.

quiz.q: It's cold. ___ your jacket.
quiz.e: put on = start wearing clothes.

quiz.q: The TV is too loud. Please turn ___.
quiz.e: A pronoun goes in the middle: turn it off.

quiz.q: Who ___ your children when you are at work?
quiz.e: look after = take care of someone.

quiz.q: I can't find my phone. I've been ___ it all morning.
quiz.e: look for = try to find.

quiz.q: Choose the correct sentence.
quiz.e: Pronoun between verb and particle: took them off.

quiz.q: We ___ the bus at the last stop.
quiz.e: get off a bus/train = leave it.

quiz.q: Which phrasal verb CANNOT be separated?
quiz.e: look after is inseparable: look after him, never "look him after".

quiz.q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: Please write down them in your notebook.
Please write them down in your notebook.
Please write down they in your notebook.
Please them write down in your notebook.
quiz.e: write down is separable, and a pronoun must go in the middle.

situation.uz: Ona: "Aziz, wake up! Get up and turn off your alarm!" — Bir sahnada to'rtta phrasal verb: wake up (uyg'onmoq), get up (turmoq), turn off (o'chirmoq), turn on (yoqmoq).
situation.ru: Мама: "Aziz, wake up! Get up and turn off your alarm!" — В одной сцене четыре фразовых глагола: wake up (проснуться), get up (встать), turn off (выключить), turn on (включить).

tip.uz: Yangi phrasal verb ni to'liq gap ichida yodlang — "I turned off the light" — ikki so'zni alohida emas. Gap obyekt qayerga qo'yilishini ko'rsatadi.
tip.ru: Учите новый фразовый глагол в полном предложении — "I turned off the light", а не как пару слов. Предложение показывает, куда ставить дополнение.

p.uz: Phrasal verb = fe'l + yuklama (up, on, off, out, after…). Birgalikda ular ko'pincha ikki so'zdan taxmin qilib bo'lmaydigan yangi ma'no beradi.
p.ru: Фразовый глагол = глагол + частица (up, on, off, out, after…). Вместе они часто имеют значение, которое нельзя угадать по отдельным словам.

p.uz: Avvalo shu keng tarqalganlarini o'rganing: wake up, get up, turn on/off, put on, take off (kiyim), go out, come back, look for.
p.ru: Сначала выучите самые частые: wake up, get up, turn on/off, put on, take off (одежда), go out, come back, look for.

p.uz: Ko'p phrasal verb larda ot yuklamadan keyin ham, o'rtada ham kela oladi: turn on the TV / turn the TV on.
p.ru: У многих фразовых глаголов существительное может стоять после частицы или между: turn on the TV / turn the TV on.

p.uz: Lekin olmosh (it, them, him…) ALBATTA o'rtada keladi: turn it on — hech qachon "turn on it" emas.
p.ru: Но местоимение (it, them, him…) ОБЯЗАТЕЛЬНО стоит в середине: turn it on — никогда "turn on it".

p.uz: Ba'zi phrasal verb lar hech qachon ajralmaydi. Ot yoki olmosh doim yuklamadan keyin keladi: look after, look for, get on/off (avtobus).
p.ru: Некоторые фразовые глаголы никогда не разделяются. Существительное или местоимение всегда идёт после частицы: look after, look for, get on/off (автобус).

quiz.uz: wake up = uyg'onmoq; get up = o'rindan turmoq.
quiz.ru: wake up = проснуться; get up = встать с кровати.

quiz.uz: turn on = chiroq yoki asbobni yoqmoq.
quiz.ru: turn on = включить свет или прибор.

quiz.uz: Olmosh o'rtada keladi: turn it off.
quiz.ru: Местоимение стоит в середине: turn it off.

quiz.uz: Olmosh fe'l va yuklama orasida: took them off.
quiz.ru: Местоимение между глаголом и частицей: took them off.

quiz.uz: look after ajralmaydi: look after him, hech qachon "look him after" emas.
quiz.ru: look after не разделяется: look after him, никогда "look him after".

quiz.uz: write down ajraladi, olmosh esa o'rtada bo'lishi shart.
quiz.ru: write down разделяется, а местоимение обязано стоять в середине.

grammar.title: Infinitive of purpose
grammar.lead: To explain WHY we do something, we use to + verb: "I went to the bazaar to buy fruit." This is called the infinitive of purpose.

leadTr.uz: Nima UCHUN qilishimizni tushuntirish uchun to + fe'l ishlatamiz: "I went to the bazaar to buy fruit." Bu infinitive of purpose (maqsad infinitivi) deyiladi.
leadTr.ru: Чтобы объяснить, ЗАЧЕМ мы что-то делаем, используем to + глагол: "I went to the bazaar to buy fruit." Это называется инфинитивом цели.

grammar.situation: Karim: "Why are you learning English?" Lola: "To get a better job. And I'm saving money to travel to London one day."

p: Use to + the base verb to give a reason or purpose. It can answer a Why…? question alone.
ex: I went to the market to buy vegetables.
She called me to ask about the homework.
"Why did you go to the bank?" "To open an account."

p: In many languages purpose is said with "for", but in English we do NOT say "for buy" or "for to buy". Use to + verb.
ex: I came here to see you. (NOT: for see you)
He is studying hard to pass the exam.

p: for is correct before a NOUN: for bread, for a walk, for lunch. Compare: to buy bread (verb) / for bread (noun).
ex: I went out for bread. = I went out to buy bread.
We stopped at a choyxona for tea.

p: In order to + verb means the same as to + verb but sounds more formal. In everyday speech, simple to is more common.
ex: In order to improve your English, practise every day.
He moved to Tashkent in order to find work.

grammar.tip: If the next word is a verb, use to: "to buy milk". If the next word is a noun, use for: "for milk". Never "for buy milk".
examples: Aziz went online to check the football results.
I'm learning English to talk with tourists at the bazaar.
She got up early to catch the first train to Samarkand.
We stopped for lunch on the way home.

mistakes.x: I went to the shop for buy milk.
mistakes.v: I went to the shop to buy milk. — before a verb, use to, not for.

mistakes.x: She is saving money for to travel.
mistakes.v: She is saving money to travel. — never combine for and to before a verb.

mistakes.x: I went out to bread.

quiz.q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: I'm saving money for to buy a car.
I'm saving money to buy a car.
I'm saving money for buy a car.
I'm saving money buy a car.
quiz.e: Purpose = to + verb, never for to / for + verb.

quiz.q: He is learning Russian ___ with his colleagues in Moscow.

quiz.q: ___ pass the IELTS exam, you need to practise writing.
quiz.e: In order to + verb = formal purpose.

quiz.q: "Why are you going to the bazaar?" — Choose the best short answer.

quiz.q: Which sentence is wrong?
o: I went out to buy bread.
I went out for to buy bread.

quiz.e: for to + verb is never correct in English.

quiz.q: She turned on her laptop ___ her emails before the meeting.

situation.uz: "Why are you learning English?" "To get a better job." — Maqsad to + fe'l bilan aytiladi: to get, to travel. U yolg'iz o'zi ham Why…? savoliga javob bo'la oladi.
situation.ru: «Зачем ты учишь английский?» «Чтобы получить работу получше.» — Цель выражается через to + глагол: to get, to travel. Такой ответ может стоять и отдельно.

tip.uz: Keyingi so'z fe'l bo'lsa — to: "to buy milk". Keyingi so'z ot bo'lsa — for: "for milk". Hech qachon "for buy milk" emas.
tip.ru: Если дальше глагол — to: "to buy milk". Если существительное — for: "for milk". Никогда "for buy milk".

p.uz: Sabab yoki maqsadni aytish uchun to + fe'lning asosiy shakli ishlatiladi. U Why…? savoliga yolg'iz o'zi ham javob bo'la oladi.
p.ru: Чтобы назвать причину или цель, используйте to + начальную форму глагола. Он может сам по себе отвечать на вопрос Why…?

p.uz: Ko'p tillarda maqsad "uchun" bilan aytiladi, lekin inglizchada "for buy" yoki "for to buy" deyilmaydi. to + fe'l ishlating.
p.ru: Во многих языках цель выражается через «для», но по-английски нельзя сказать "for buy" или "for to buy". Используйте to + глагол.

p.uz: for OTdan oldin to'g'ri: for bread, for a walk, for lunch. Solishtiring: to buy bread (fe'l) / for bread (ot).
p.ru: for правильно перед СУЩЕСТВИТЕЛЬНЫМ: for bread, for a walk, for lunch. Сравните: to buy bread (глагол) / for bread (существительное).

p.uz: In order to + fe'l to + fe'l bilan bir xil ma'noni beradi, lekin rasmiyroq eshitiladi. Kundalik nutqda oddiy to ko'proq ishlatiladi.
p.ru: In order to + глагол значит то же, что to + глагол, но звучит формальнее. В повседневной речи чаще простое to.

quiz.uz: to + asosiy fe'l Why…? ga javob beradi.
quiz.ru: to + начальная форма отвечает на Why…?

quiz.uz: Maqsad = to + fe'l, hech qachon for to / for + fe'l emas.
quiz.ru: Цель = to + глагол, никогда for to / for + глагол.

quiz.uz: In order to + fe'l = rasmiy maqsad.
quiz.ru: In order to + глагол = формальная цель.

quiz.uz: for to + fe'l inglizchada hech qachon to'g'ri emas.

reading.title: A Trip to London
reading.text:
Last summer, Daniel and his sister Olivia travelled to London for the first time. They took an early train from Manchester and arrived at about ten o'clock.
First, they visited the British Museum, which was free and very interesting. After that, they had lunch in a small café near the river. In the afternoon, they went on a boat trip and saw many famous buildings.
The weather was warm and sunny all day. In the evening, they were tired but happy. They bought some souvenirs and took lots of photos before they caught the last train home.

reading.title: My First Job
reading.text:
My name is Sophie and I'm nineteen. Last year, I got my first job in a small bookshop in Bristol. At first, I was nervous because I didn't have any experience.
My manager, Mr Clarke, was very kind and patient. He showed me how to use the till and how to help customers find books. The other staff were friendly too, so I soon felt comfortable.
I worked part-time, three days a week, and the salary wasn't very high. But I learned a lot, and I really enjoyed talking to customers about books. Now I want to study literature at university.

reading.title: An Email about a Holiday
reading.text:
Hi Grace,

How are you? I'm writing from a small hotel in Brighton, where I've been since Monday. I'm having a wonderful time!

I've already done so many things. I've walked along the beach, eaten fresh fish, and visited the famous pier. Yesterday I went swimming in the sea, although the water was quite cold. I haven't been shopping yet, but I'm planning to go tomorrow.

The weather has been mostly sunny, but it rained a little this morning. The people here are very friendly, and the food is delicious.

I'll be home on Saturday. Let's meet next week — I'll show you my photos!

Love,
Jack

reading.title: Town or City?
reading.text:
Many people argue about whether it is better to live in a big city or a small town. Both have advantages and disadvantages.
Big cities, like London or Birmingham, are more exciting. There are more jobs, better shops, and lots of things to do in the evening. However, cities are usually more expensive and more crowded, and the air is often more polluted.
Small towns are quieter and cheaper. People are often friendlier and know their neighbours. On the other hand, there are fewer jobs, and young people sometimes find life a little boring.
In my opinion, the best choice depends on your age and your needs. When I was younger, I loved the city, but now I prefer the peace of a small town.

quiz.e: Now the writer prefers the peace of a small town.

reading.title: The Lost Phone
reading.text:
It was a cold Friday evening, and Emily was hurrying home from work. While she was waiting at the bus stop, she took out her phone to check the time. The bus arrived, and in the rush to get on, she didn't notice that her phone had fallen onto the seat next to her.
When she got home, she realised her phone was missing. She felt terrible — all her photos and messages were on it. She borrowed her flatmate's phone and called her own number, but nobody answered.
The next morning, however, she received an email. A kind passenger named Harry had found the phone and seen her details on the screen. They arranged to meet at a café in the city centre, and Harry returned the phone. Emily was so grateful that she bought him a coffee. Now they are good friends.

quiz.e: It fell onto the seat as she rushed onto the bus.

quiz.e: Her photos and messages were on the phone.

o: He sent an email after seeing her details.
quiz.e: He emailed her after seeing her details on the screen.

quiz.q: What happened in the end?

quiz.e: Harry returned it and now they are good friends.

reading.title: Navruz in Our Mahalla
reading.text: Last March our mahalla celebrated Navruz, and it was the best day of spring. The women started cooking sumalak the night before. Sumalak is a sweet dish made from young wheat, and it must cook slowly for almost twenty-four hours. People took turns stirring the big pot and made wishes. In the morning, the men set up long tables in the yard, and every family brought a plate of food. There was plov, somsa, fresh salads and a lot of sweets. Children ran everywhere, and my grandfather told old stories about his childhood. In the afternoon there was a small concert: our neighbours sang songs and one boy played the doira. When the sumalak was finally ready, everyone got a small bowl to take home. I was tired at the end of the day, but very happy.

reading.title: The Tashkent Metro
reading.text: The Tashkent metro opened in 1977, and it was the first metro in Central Asia. Today it has more than fifty stations, and many of them look like small museums. Kosmonavtlar station, for example, is decorated with pictures of famous astronauts, and Alisher Navoiy station has beautiful blue domes like an old madrasah. For many years it was forbidden to take photos in the metro, because it was also a bomb shelter. The rule changed in 2018, and now tourists come with their cameras every day. The metro is cheap and fast. Trains come every four or five minutes, and you can cross the whole city in half an hour. Many people say it is the most beautiful way to travel in Tashkent — and the coolest place in the hot summer!

listening.title: Ordering a Taxi
listening.script: Operator: City Taxi, good evening. How can I help you? — Caller: Good evening. I need a taxi to the airport, please. — Operator: Of course. Where are you now? — Caller: I'm at the Grand Hotel on Amir Temur Street. — Operator: And what time is your flight? — Caller: At eleven thirty tonight. I want to leave at eight thirty, to be safe. — Operator: Good idea. The evening traffic is heavy. A white car will come at eight thirty. The driver's name is Rustam. — Caller: How much will it cost? — Operator: About sixty thousand som. You can pay by card or cash. — Caller: Perfect, thank you very much. — Operator: Thank you for calling. Have a good flight!

listening.title: A School Trip to Samarkand
listening.script: Teacher: Good morning, everyone! Listen carefully, please. Tomorrow is our trip to Samarkand. The bus leaves at six o'clock in the morning, so don't be late! The journey takes about four hours. First we will visit Registan Square, and a guide will tell us about its history. After that, we will have lunch at a café near the square. In the afternoon we will see Ulugbek's observatory — he was a great astronomer, and he built it almost six hundred years ago. Please bring water, a hat and comfortable shoes, because we will walk a lot. And don't forget your student cards — the tickets are cheaper with them. Any questions?

grammar.title: Present perfect continuous
grammar.lead: The present perfect continuous links the past to the present and emphasises the duration or repetition of an activity, especially one that is still going on or has only just stopped.

leadTr.uz: Present perfect continuous o'tmishni hozir bilan bog'lab, harakatning davomiyligini ta'kidlaydi — ayniqsa hali davom etayotgan yoki endigina tugagan faoliyat uchun.
leadTr.ru: Present perfect continuous связывает прошлое с настоящим и подчёркивает длительность действия — особенно продолжающегося или только что закончившегося.

grammar.situation: “You look exhausted!” “Yes, I ’ve been working in the garden all day.” — The present perfect continuous focuses on an activity that has been going on and explains a present result.

timeline.note: An activity continuing up to now (and maybe still going on).

ex: I’ve been reading all day.
It’s been raining.
I’ve read three books.
It’s rained twice.

p: Use have/has been + verb-ing. It focuses on the activity itself rather than the finished result.
ex: I have been working all day. · She has been studying since nine.

p: Use for + a period and since + a starting point to show how long the activity has lasted.
ex: We’ve been waiting for two hours. · He’s been living here since 2019.

p: The continuous stresses how long / how active; the simple stresses the completed result.
ex: I’ve been reading this book. (still reading) · I’ve read this book. (finished)

p: It can explain a present situation caused by a recent activity.
ex: You look tired. — Yes, I’ve been running.

grammar.tip: Don’t use the continuous with state verbs (know, like, be, have = possess): say ‘I have known her for years’, not ‘I have been knowing’.
examples: "I ’ve been learning English for five years."
"They ’ve been working on the project since Monday."
"Why are you so dirty? — I ’ve been gardening."
"How long have you been learning English?"
"We ’ve been living abroad for two years."

mistakes.x: I have been knowing her for years.
mistakes.v: I have known her for years. (state verb → simple)

mistakes.x: I am working here since May.
mistakes.v: I ’ve been working here since May.

quiz.q: I ___ for two hours and I'm still not finished.
quiz.e: Ongoing activity + duration → have been working.

quiz.q: She ___ since this morning.
quiz.e: Still going → has been studying.

quiz.q: How long ___ you ___ here?
quiz.e: Duration of an ongoing situation → have you been living.

quiz.q: It ___ all day; the streets are wet.
quiz.e: Activity with present result → has been raining.

quiz.q: They ___ football for an hour.
quiz.e: Duration of activity → have been playing.

quiz.q: Choose the duration form: 'We ___ for ages.'
quiz.e: Emphasis on how long → have been waiting.

quiz.q: You're out of breath. What ___ you ___?
quiz.e: Recent activity explaining a state → have you been doing.

quiz.q: He ___ here since 2018.
quiz.e: Both are possible, but with ‘since’ + ongoing the continuous is natural: has been living.

quiz.q: Which verb is wrong in the continuous?
quiz.e: ‘know’ is a state verb → not used in the continuous.

quiz.q: Complete: 'My eyes hurt because I ___ at the screen.'
quiz.e: Recent ongoing activity → have been staring.

quiz.q: Find the mistake: 'I have been knowing him for years.'
quiz.e: State verb: I have known him for years.

quiz.q: Complete: 'She ___ all morning, so the cake is ready.'
quiz.e: Activity over a period explaining a result → has been baking.

quiz.q: Which sentence stresses the finished result?
quiz.e: Completed result with a number → present perfect simple: I’ve written three emails.

quiz.q: Complete: 'They ___ in this town ___ ten years and they love it.'
quiz.e: Ongoing + period → have been living for ten years.

quiz.q: Choose the natural sentence.
o: How long have you been waiting?
How long have you waited continuously?
quiz.e: Duration of an ongoing wait → have you been waiting.

tip.uz: Holat fe'llari (know, like, be, have = egalik) bilan continuous ishlatmang: 'I have known her for years' deyiladi, 'I have been knowing' emas.
tip.ru: Не используйте continuous с глаголами состояния (know, like, be, have = владеть): «I have known her for years», а не «I have been knowing».

p.uz: have/has been + fe'l-ing ishlatiladi. U tugallangan natijaga emas, harakat jarayonining o'ziga urg'u beradi.
p.ru: have/has been + глагол-ing. Акцент на самом процессе, а не на завершённом результате.

p.uz: for + davr va since + boshlanish nuqtasi — harakat qancha vaqt davom etganini ko'rsatadi.
p.ru: for + период и since + точка отсчёта показывают, как долго длится действие.

p.uz: Continuous qancha vaqt / qanchalik faol bo'lganini ta'kidlaydi; simple esa tugallangan natijani.
p.ru: Continuous подчёркивает длительность и активность; simple — завершённый результат.

p.uz: U yaqinda bo'lgan harakat keltirib chiqargan hozirgi vaziyatni tushuntirishi mumkin.
p.ru: Может объяснять текущую ситуацию, вызванную недавней активностью.

quiz.uz: Davom etayotgan harakat + muddat → have been working.
quiz.ru: Длящееся действие + срок → have been working.

quiz.uz: Hali davom etmoqda → has been studying.
quiz.ru: Всё ещё продолжается → has been studying.

quiz.uz: Davom etayotgan holatning muddati → have you been living.
quiz.ru: Длительность продолжающейся ситуации → have you been living.

quiz.uz: Hozirgi natijaga ega harakat → has been raining.
quiz.ru: Действие с результатом сейчас → has been raining.

quiz.uz: Qancha davom etganiga urg'u → have been waiting.
quiz.ru: Акцент на длительности → have been waiting.

quiz.uz: Holatni tushuntiruvchi yaqindagi harakat → have you been doing.
quiz.ru: Недавняя активность объясняет состояние → have you been doing.

quiz.uz: Ikkalasi ham mumkin, lekin 'since' + davom etayotgan holat bilan continuous tabiiyroq: has been living.
quiz.ru: Оба возможны, но с «since» + продолжающейся ситуацией естественнее continuous: has been living.
«know» — глагол состояния → не употребляется в continuous.

quiz.uz: Yaqinda davom etgan harakat → have been staring.
quiz.ru: Недавнее длящееся действие → have been staring.

quiz.uz: Holat fe'li: I have known him for years.
quiz.ru: Глагол состояния: I have known him for years.

quiz.uz: Natijani tushuntiruvchi davomli harakat → has been baking.
quiz.ru: Длительное действие, объясняющее результат → has been baking.

quiz.uz: Son bilan tugallangan natija → present perfect simple: I've written three emails.
quiz.ru: Завершённый результат с числом → present perfect simple: I've written three emails.

quiz.uz: Davom etayotgan holat + davr → have been living for ten years.
quiz.ru: Продолжается + период → have been living for ten years.

quiz.uz: Davom etayotgan kutish muddati → have you been waiting.
quiz.ru: Длительность продолжающегося ожидания → have you been waiting.

grammar.title: Past perfect
grammar.lead: The past perfect shows that one past action happened before another past action. It helps to make the order of events in a story clear.

leadTr.uz: Past perfect bir o'tmishdagi harakat boshqa o'tmishdagi harakatdan OLDIN bo'lganini ko'rsatadi. U hikoyada voqealar tartibini aniq qiladi.
leadTr.ru: Past perfect показывает, что одно прошлое действие произошло РАНЬШЕ другого. Он делает порядок событий в рассказе ясным.

grammar.situation: “When I got to the station, the train had already left.” — The past perfect shows the train left before I arrived. It puts two past events in order.

timeline.note: The “had” action happens first; the past simple action happens second.

p: Use had + past participle for the earlier of two past actions.
ex: When I arrived, the train had already left.

p: Often used with the past simple: the past perfect = the earlier action; the past simple = the later one.
ex: She had finished dinner before he came home.

blocks.h: after, before, when, by the time
p: Common with these time linkers to show sequence.
ex: By the time we got there, the film had started.

p: Negative: hadn’t + past participle. Question: Had + subject + past participle?
ex: I hadn’t seen her before. · Had you eaten when they called?

grammar.tip: Use the past perfect only when you need to show one past event happened before another. For a simple sequence (first… then…), the past simple alone is enough.
examples: "When we arrived, the party had already started."
"She had never flown before that day."
"They had finished the work before the boss returned."
"By the time I woke up, he had left."
"I knew I had met him somewhere."
"Had you booked the room before you arrived?"
"When we arrived, the film had already started."
"She had finished dinner before he came."
"They had never flown before that day."
"By the time help came, he had recovered."
"The thief had escaped before the police arrived."
"We were late because we had missed the train."

mistakes.x: After I had ate, I went out.
mistakes.v: After I had eaten, I went out. (past participle)

mistakes.x: When I arrived, the film already started.
mistakes.v: …the film had already started.

quiz.q: When I arrived, the train ___.
quiz.e: Earlier past action → had already left.

quiz.q: She ___ dinner before he came home.
quiz.e: Earlier action → had finished.

quiz.q: The past perfect of 'see' is ___.
quiz.e: had + past participle: had seen.

quiz.q: By the time we got there, the film ___.
quiz.e: Earlier action → had started.

quiz.q: They ___ never ___ sushi before that trip.
quiz.e: had + past participle: had eaten.

quiz.q: I recognised her because I ___ her before.
quiz.e: Earlier action → had met.

quiz.q: After he ___ the letter, he posted it.
quiz.e: First action → had written.

quiz.q: We were late; the meeting ___ already ___.
quiz.e: had + past participle: had begun.

quiz.q: ___ you ever ___ abroad before that holiday?
quiz.e: Past perfect question: Had you been?

quiz.q: Choose the earlier action: 'When I phoned, she ___.'
quiz.e: Before the phone call → had gone out.

quiz.q: Find the mistake: 'After I had ate, I went out.'
quiz.e: Past participle of eat is eaten: had eaten.

quiz.q: Complete: 'By the time the police arrived, the thief ___.'
quiz.e: Earlier action → had escaped.

quiz.q: Which order is correct?
o: He had left before I arrived.
He left before I had arrived.
He had left before I had arrived.
quiz.e: Earlier action ‘had left’ + later ‘arrived’.

quiz.q: Complete: 'I didn't recognise the town because it ___ so much.'
quiz.e: Change happened before → had changed.

quiz.q: Choose the natural sentence.
o: When the guests arrived, she had cooked dinner.
When the guests arrived, she has cooked dinner.
When the guests arrived, she cooks dinner.
When the guests had arrived, she has cooked.
quiz.e: Dinner cooked before guests arrived → had cooked.

tip.uz: Past perfect faqat bir o'tgan voqea boshqasidan oldin bo'lganini ko'rsatish kerak bo'lganda ishlatiladi. Oddiy ketma-ketlik uchun (avval… keyin…) past simple ning o'zi yetarli.
tip.ru: Past perfect нужен только чтобы показать, что одно событие в прошлом произошло раньше другого. Для простой последовательности (сначала… потом…) достаточно past simple.

p.uz: Ikki o'tgan harakatdan oldingisi uchun had + fe'lning 3-shakli ishlatiladi.
p.ru: Для более раннего из двух прошлых действий: had + 3-я форма глагола.

p.uz: Ko'pincha past simple bilan birga keladi: past perfect — oldingi harakat, past simple — keyingisi.
p.ru: Часто идёт вместе с past simple: past perfect — более раннее действие, past simple — более позднее.

h.uz: after, before, when, by the time
h.ru: after, before, when, by the time

p.uz: Ketma-ketlikni ko'rsatish uchun shu vaqt bog'lovchilari bilan ko'p ishlatiladi.
p.ru: Часто употребляется с этими временными союзами для показа последовательности.

p.uz: Inkor: hadn't + sifatdosh. Savol: Had + ega + sifatdosh?
p.ru: Отрицание: hadn't + причастие. Вопрос: Had + подлежащее + причастие?

quiz.uz: Oldinroq bo'lgan harakat → had already left.
quiz.ru: Более раннее действие → had already left.

quiz.uz: Past perfect savoli: Had you been?
quiz.ru: Вопрос в past perfect: Had you been?

quiz.uz: eat fe'lining sifatdoshi — eaten: had eaten.
quiz.ru: Причастие от eat — eaten: had eaten.

quiz.uz: Ovqat mehmonlar kelishidan oldin pishgan → had cooked.
quiz.ru: Ужин был готов до прихода гостей → had cooked.

grammar.title: Future forms
grammar.lead: English uses several forms to talk about the future. Choosing the right one depends on whether you mean a prediction, a plan, an arrangement, a timetable or an instant decision.

leadTr.uz: Kelasi zamonning bir necha shakli bor. To'g'ri tanlov nimani nazarda tutishingizga bog'liq: bashorat, reja, kelishuv, jadval yoki hozirgi qaror.
leadTr.ru: У будущего времени несколько форм. Выбор зависит от смысла: предсказание, план, договорённость, расписание или спонтанное решение.

ex: We’re going to paint it. (intention)
I’m meeting Sam at six. (arrangement)
It ’ll snow tonight. (prediction)
The train leaves at 9. (timetable)

p: will = predictions, instant decisions, offers, promises. be going to = plans/intentions and predictions from evidence.
ex: It will snow tonight. · We’re going to paint the house.

p: Use the present continuous for fixed arrangements, usually with a time and another person.
ex: I’m meeting Sara at six. · They’re flying to Rome on Friday.

p: Use the present simple for timetabled events (transport, programmes, schedules).
ex: The train leaves at 9:15. · The film starts at eight.

p: Use may/might for things that are possible but not certain.
ex: It might rain later. · I may go to the party.

grammar.tip: For a plan use ‘going to’; for an arrangement with a time use the present continuous; for a timetable use the present simple; for an instant decision use ‘will’.
examples: "Look at the clouds — it ’s going to rain."
"The bus leaves at half past seven."
"I might visit my cousin at the weekend."
"Don’t worry, I ’ll carry that for you."

mistakes.x: The plane will arrive at 6 — it’s the timetable.
mistakes.v: The plane arrives at 6. (timetable → present simple)

mistakes.x: I think I’m passing the exam.
mistakes.v: I think I’ll pass. (prediction → will)

quiz.q: Look at that car! It ___ crash.
quiz.e: Prediction from evidence → is going to crash.

quiz.q: The train ___ at 10:30.
quiz.e: Timetable → present simple: leaves.

quiz.q: I ___ Tom for coffee at four. (arrangement)
quiz.e: Fixed arrangement → present continuous.

quiz.q: (phone rings) I ___ get it.
quiz.e: Instant decision → will.

quiz.q: It ___ rain later, but I'm not sure.
quiz.e: Possibility → might.

quiz.q: We ___ visit Spain next summer. (plan)
quiz.e: Plan → are going to visit.

quiz.q: The match ___ at 8 pm tonight.
quiz.e: Scheduled → present simple: starts.

quiz.q: She ___ to the dentist tomorrow at nine. (arrangement)
quiz.e: Arrangement with time → present continuous.

quiz.q: I'm cold. — I ___ close the window.
quiz.e: Offer/instant decision → will.

quiz.q: Choose the evidence-based prediction.
o: She will have a baby — look!
She's going to have a baby — look!
She might to have a baby.
quiz.e: Evidence now → is going to.

quiz.q: Find the mistake: 'The plane will arrive at 6, it's the timetable.'
quiz.e: Timetable → present simple: arrives.

quiz.q: Complete: 'We ___ (plan) move house, and I think it ___ (prediction) be stressful.'
o: are going to / are going to
quiz.e: Plan → going to; prediction → will.

quiz.q: Which shows a possibility?
quiz.e: Uncertain future → might go.

quiz.q: Complete: 'Hurry! The film ___ at eight and we ___ Jack there.'
quiz.e: Timetable ‘starts’ + arrangement ‘are meeting’.

quiz.q: Choose the natural arrangement sentence.
o: I have dinner with them tonight.
I'm having dinner with them tonight.
I will have dinner with them, it's arranged.
I might have dinner tonight, it's arranged.
quiz.e: Fixed arrangement → present continuous.

tip.uz: Reja uchun 'going to'; vaqti belgilangan kelishuv uchun present continuous; jadval uchun present simple; shu zahoti qabul qilingan qaror uchun 'will'.
tip.ru: Для плана — «going to»; для договорённости со временем — present continuous; для расписания — present simple; для мгновенного решения — «will».

p.uz: will = bashorat, shu zahoti qaror, taklif, va'da. be going to = reja/niyat va dalilga asoslangan bashorat.
p.ru: will = предсказания, мгновенные решения, предложения, обещания. be going to = планы/намерения и предсказания по признакам.

p.uz: Qat'iy kelishuvlar uchun present continuous ishlatiladi, odatda vaqt va boshqa odam bilan.
p.ru: Present continuous — для твёрдых договорённостей, обычно с указанием времени и другого человека.

p.uz: Jadval bo'yicha voqealar uchun (transport, dasturlar, jadvallar) present simple ishlatiladi.
p.ru: Present simple — для событий по расписанию (транспорт, программы, графики).

p.uz: Mumkin, lekin aniq bo'lmagan narsalar uchun may/might ishlatiladi.
p.ru: may/might — для возможных, но не точных событий.

quiz.uz: Dalilga asoslangan bashorat → is going to crash.
quiz.ru: Предсказание по признакам → is going to crash.

grammar.title: Second conditional
grammar.lead: The second conditional talks about imaginary, unlikely or unreal present and future situations. It uses the past simple in the if-clause and ‘would’ in the result clause.

leadTr.uz: Ikkinchi shart gapi xayoliy yoki ehtimoli past hozirgi/kelajak vaziyatlar uchun: If + past simple, natijada 'would'. If I had time, I would travel.
leadTr.ru: Второй кондиционал — для воображаемых или маловероятных ситуаций: if + past simple, в результате — would. If I had time, I would travel.

grammar.situation: “If I won the lottery, I ’d travel the world.” — The situation is imaginary and unlikely, so we use the past simple + would, not present + will.

ex: If it rains, I’ll stay in.
If it snowed in July, I’d be amazed.

blocks.h: Form: if + past simple, would + base
p: The past tense here doesn’t mean past time — it shows the situation is hypothetical.
ex: If I had more money, I would travel.

p: With ‘be’, we often use were for all persons, especially in advice with ‘If I were you’.
ex: If I were you, I’d apologise. · If she were here, she’d help.

p: Use could (ability/possibility) or might (possible result) instead of ‘would’.
ex: If I had a car, I could drive you. · We might win if we tried.

p: First conditional = real/likely; second conditional = unlikely/unreal.
ex: If it rains, I’ll stay in. (likely) · If it snowed in July, I’d be shocked. (unreal)

grammar.tip: For advice, ‘If I were you, I’d…’ is the natural phrase. Don’t mix forms: ‘If I would have money’ is wrong → ‘If I had money, I would…’.
examples: "If I won the lottery, I would buy a house."
"If I were you, I ’d see a doctor."
"She would travel more if she had time."
"If we lived by the sea, we could swim every day."
"What would you do if you lost your job?"
"If he spoke French, he might get the job."
"If I won the lottery, I ’d travel the world."
"She ’d be happier if she had a job."
"If we lived by the sea, we could swim daily."
"What would you do if you lost your phone?"
"I wouldn’t buy it if it weren’t so cheap."
"If they tried harder, they could win."

mistakes.x: If I would have money, I would travel.
mistakes.v: If I had money, I would travel. (no “would” after if)

mistakes.x: If I was you, I will help.
mistakes.v: If I were you, I ’d help.

quiz.q: If I ___ rich, I would buy a yacht.
quiz.e: Second conditional: if + past (were).

quiz.q: If I had time, I ___ help you.
quiz.e: Result → would help.

quiz.q: If I ___ you, I'd apologise.
quiz.e: Advice → If I were you.

quiz.q: She would travel if she ___ more money.
quiz.e: if + past simple: had.

quiz.q: If we lived nearer, we ___ visit more often.
quiz.e: Result → would visit.

quiz.q: What ___ you do if you won a million?
quiz.e: Hypothetical → would you do.

quiz.q: If he ___ harder, he'd pass.
quiz.e: if + past simple: studied.

quiz.q: I ___ buy it if it weren't so expensive.
quiz.e: Result → would buy.

quiz.q: If I had a car, I ___ drive you home.
quiz.e: Ability in result → could drive.

quiz.q: Choose the unreal situation.
o: If it rains, I'll stay in.
If it snowed in summer, I'd be amazed.
If I have time, I'll call.
If you heat ice, it melts.
quiz.e: Unlikely/unreal → second conditional.

quiz.q: Find the mistake: 'If I would have money, I would travel.'
quiz.e: No ‘would’ in the if-clause: If I had money…

quiz.q: Complete: 'If she ___ here, she ___ what to do.'
quiz.e: were (be) + would know.

quiz.q: Which is correct?
o: If I was you, I will help.
If I were you, I would help.
If I am you, I would help.
If I were you, I will help.
quiz.e: If I were you, I would help.

quiz.q: Complete: 'We ___ win the match if we ___ as a team.'
quiz.e: would win + played (past).

quiz.q: Choose the natural advice.
o: If I were you, I'd take the job.
If I am you, I take the job.
If I would be you, I take the job.
If I was you, I'll take the job.
quiz.e: If I were you, I’d take the job.

tip.uz: Maslahat uchun 'If I were you, I'd…' — eng tabiiy ibora. Shakllarni aralashtirmang: 'If I would have money' — xato → 'If I had money, I would…'.
tip.ru: Для совета естественна фраза «If I were you, I'd…». Не смешивайте формы: «If I would have money» — ошибка → «If I had money, I would…».

h.uz: Shakl: if + past simple, would + asosiy shakl
h.ru: Форма: if + past simple, would + начальная форма

p.uz: Bu yerdagi o'tgan zamon o'tgan vaqtni bildirmaydi — u vaziyat faraziy ekanini ko'rsatadi.
p.ru: Прошедшее время здесь не означает прошлое — оно показывает, что ситуация гипотетическая.

p.uz: 'be' bilan ko'pincha hamma shaxslarda were ishlatiladi, ayniqsa 'If I were you' maslahatida.
p.ru: С «be» часто используется were для всех лиц, особенно в совете «If I were you».

p.uz: 'would' o'rniga could (qobiliyat/imkoniyat) yoki might (ehtimoliy natija) ishlatish mumkin.
p.ru: Вместо «would» можно использовать could (способность/возможность) или might (возможный результат).

p.uz: First conditional = real/ehtimoli katta; second conditional = ehtimoli kam/noreal.
p.ru: First conditional = реальное/вероятное; second conditional = маловероятное/нереальное.

quiz.uz: If qismida 'would' bo'lmaydi: If I had money…
quiz.ru: В if-части нет «would»: If I had money…

quiz.uz: If I were you, I would help.
quiz.ru: If I were you, I would help.

quiz.uz: If I were you, I'd take the job.
quiz.ru: If I were you, I'd take the job.

grammar.title: Modals of deduction (present)
grammar.lead: We use modal verbs to say how certain we are about a present situation. ‘Must’ shows we are almost sure something is true; ‘can’t’ that it is impossible; ‘might/may/could’ that it is possible.

leadTr.uz: Hozirgi vaziyat haqidagi taxminlarda modal fe'llar ishonch darajasini ko'rsatadi: 'must' — deyarli aniq, 'can't' — bo'lishi mumkin emas, 'might' — balki.
leadTr.ru: В догадках о настоящем модальные глаголы показывают степень уверенности: must — почти наверняка, can't — невозможно, might — возможно.

ex: She must be home — the light’s on.
He can’t be hungry; he just ate.
She might be at work.
They could be lost.

p: Use must + base verb when you are sure something is true based on evidence.
ex: The light’s on — she must be home.

p: Use can’t (not ‘mustn’t’) when you are sure something is not true.
ex: He can’t be hungry; he’s just eaten.

p: Use these for things that are possible but uncertain.
ex: She might be at work. · They could be lost.

p: Use modal + be + -ing for an action happening now.
ex: He’s not answering — he must be sleeping.

grammar.tip: The opposite of ‘must be’ (sure it is) is ‘can’t be’ (sure it isn’t), not ‘mustn’t be’. ‘Mustn’t’ means prohibition, not deduction.
examples: "You’ve worked all day — you must be tired."
"That can’t be John; he’s in Spain."
"They must be having dinner; the lights are on."
"It could be true, but I’m not sure."
"The light’s on — she must be home."
"He can’t be hungry; he’s just eaten."
"You must be tired after that journey."

mistakes.x: He isn’t home — he mustn’t be at work.
mistakes.v: …he must be at work. (mustn’t ≠ deduction)

mistakes.x: She must works late.
mistakes.v: She must be working late. (modal + be + -ing)

quiz.q: The lights are on, so she ___ be home.
quiz.e: Sure it’s true → must be.

quiz.q: He's just eaten, so he ___ be hungry.
quiz.e: Sure it’s not true → can’t be.

quiz.q: I'm not sure, but she ___ be at work.
quiz.e: Possible → might be.

quiz.q: That ___ be true — it's impossible!
quiz.e: Impossible → can’t be.

quiz.q: They aren't answering. They ___ be out.
quiz.e: Possible explanation → might be out.

quiz.q: He's wearing a coat, so it ___ be cold.
quiz.e: Evidence → must be cold.

quiz.q: She speaks five languages — she ___ be clever.
quiz.e: Strong deduction → must be.

quiz.q: The phone is off. He ___ be sleeping.
quiz.e: Likely explanation → must be sleeping.

quiz.q: This ___ be the right address; the numbers don't match.
quiz.e: Sure it’s wrong → can’t be.

quiz.q: Choose the 'possible' modal.
quiz.e: ‘could’ = possible.

quiz.q: Find the mistake: 'He's not at home, he mustn't be at work.'
quiz.e: For a likely explanation use ‘must be at work’ (mustn’t is prohibition).

quiz.q: Complete: 'She ___ be ill — she ___ be at the gym; her bag is here.'
quiz.e: ‘might be ill’ (possible) + ‘can’t be at the gym’ (impossible — bag is here).

quiz.q: Which is correct?
quiz.e: Sure it isn’t → can’t be.

quiz.q: Complete: 'No one's answering. They ___ out, or they ___ be sleeping.'
quiz.e: Both uncertain → might be / might be.

quiz.q: Choose the present-continuous deduction.
quiz.e: modal + be + -ing: must be working.

tip.uz: 'must be' (aniq shunday) ning teskarisi — 'can't be' (aniq unday emas), 'mustn't be' emas. 'Mustn't' taqiqni bildiradi, xulosani emas.
tip.ru: Противоположность «must be» (точно так) — «can't be» (точно не так), а не «mustn't be». «Mustn't» — это запрет, а не вывод.

p.uz: Dalilga asoslanib biror narsa rost ekaniga ishonchingiz komil bo'lsa, must + asosiy shakl ishlatiladi.
p.ru: must + начальная форма — когда вы уверены, что это правда, на основе фактов.

p.uz: Biror narsa rost emasligiga ishonchingiz komil bo'lsa, can't ishlatiladi ('mustn't' emas).
p.ru: can't (а не «mustn't») — когда вы уверены, что это неправда.

p.uz: Mumkin, lekin aniq bo'lmagan narsalar uchun ishlatiladi.
p.ru: Для возможных, но неопределённых вещей.

p.uz: Hozir sodir bo'layotgan harakat uchun modal + be + -ing ishlatiladi.
p.ru: Для действия, происходящего сейчас: модальный глагол + be + -ing.

quiz.ru: Уверенность, что не так → can't be.

quiz.uz: Ehtimoli katta izoh → must be sleeping.
Ehtimoliy izoh uchun 'must be at work' (mustn't — taqiq).
quiz.ru: Для вероятного вывода — «must be at work» (mustn't — запрет).

quiz.uz: 'might be ill' (mumkin) + 'can't be at the gym' (imkonsiz — sumkasi shu yerda).
quiz.ru: «might be ill» (возможно) + «can't be at the gym» (невозможно — сумка здесь).
Уверенность, что не так → can't be.

quiz.uz: Ikkalasi ham noaniq → might be / might be.
quiz.ru: Оба неопределённы → might be / might be.

grammar.title: The passive
grammar.lead: We use the passive when the action is more important than the person who does it, or when we don’t know who did it. The object of the active sentence becomes the subject of the passive.

leadTr.uz: Majhul nisbat (passive) harakat bajaruvchidan muhimroq bo'lganda ishlatiladi: The bridge was built in 1905. Faol gapning to'ldiruvchisi egaga aylanadi.
leadTr.ru: Пассив используется, когда действие важнее исполнителя: The bridge was built in 1905. Дополнение активного предложения становится подлежащим.

grammar.situation: “This bridge was built in 1890.” — We use the passive when the action matters more than who did it (or we don’t know who did it).

ex: Orwell wrote the book.
Someone has cleaned the room.
The book was written by Orwell.
The room has been cleaned.

p: Use the right tense of be + the past participle. Present: am/is/are + pp. Past: was/were + pp.
ex: English is spoken here. · The window was broken yesterday.

p: Use by to say who or what does the action, but only when it is important.
ex: The book was written by Orwell. · He was bitten by a dog.

p: Use it when the doer is unknown, obvious or unimportant, or in formal/scientific writing.
ex: My car was stolen. (we don’t know who) · The results were analysed.

p: Present perfect: has/have been + pp. Future: will be + pp. Modal: can/must be + pp.
ex: The job has been done. · It will be finished soon. · It must be paid today.

grammar.tip: Only verbs with an object (transitive) can be made passive. ‘happen’, ‘arrive’ and ‘sleep’ have no object, so they cannot be passive.
examples: "Millions of phones are made in China."
"This letter was written by my grandmother."
"The thieves were caught by the police."
"English is spoken all over the world."

mistakes.x: The letter was wrote by John.
mistakes.v: The letter was written by John. (past participle)

mistakes.x: The accident was happened.
mistakes.v: The accident happened. (“happen” has no object → no passive)

quiz.q: English ___ in many countries.
quiz.e: Present passive: is spoken.

quiz.q: The window ___ yesterday.
quiz.e: Past passive: was broken.

quiz.q: The passive of 'They make cars here' is 'Cars ___ here.'
quiz.e: Plural subject → are made.

quiz.q: This book ___ by Dickens.
quiz.e: Past passive: was written.

quiz.q: The rooms ___ every day.
quiz.e: Plural present passive: are cleaned.

quiz.q: My bike ___ last week.
quiz.e: Past passive: was stolen.

quiz.q: Choose the agent: 'The house was designed ___ a famous architect.'
quiz.e: Agent → by.

quiz.q: The present perfect passive of 'do' is 'It ___.'
quiz.e: has/have been + pp: has been done.

quiz.q: Which verb CANNOT be passive?
quiz.e: ‘arrive’ has no object → not passive.

quiz.q: The future passive of 'finish' is 'It ___ tomorrow.'
quiz.e: will be + pp: will be finished.

quiz.q: Find the mistake: 'The letter was wrote by John.'
quiz.e: Past participle: was written.

quiz.q: Make passive: 'Somebody has cleaned the room.'
quiz.e: Present perfect passive: has been cleaned.

quiz.q: Which sentence is correct?
o: The thief was caught by police.
The thief was catch by police.
The thief is catch by police.
quiz.e: was + past participle: was caught.

quiz.q: Complete (modal passive): 'These forms ___ in pen.'
quiz.e: modal + be + pp: must be completed.

quiz.q: Make passive: 'They are building a new school.'
o: A new school is being built.
quiz.e: Present continuous passive: is being built.

tip.uz: Faqat to'ldiruvchisi bor (o'timli) fe'llar passiv bo'la oladi. 'happen', 'arrive' va 'sleep' to'ldiruvchi olmaydi, shuning uchun passiv bo'lmaydi.
tip.ru: В пассив можно поставить только переходные глаголы (с дополнением). У «happen», «arrive» и «sleep» нет дополнения, поэтому они не бывают в пассиве.

p.uz: be ning kerakli zamoni + fe'lning 3-shakli. Hozirgi: am/is/are + pp. O'tgan: was/were + pp.
p.ru: Нужное время be + причастие. Настоящее: am/is/are + pp. Прошедшее: was/were + pp.

p.uz: Harakatni kim yoki nima bajarganini aytish uchun by ishlatiladi, lekin faqat bu muhim bo'lganda.
p.ru: by показывает, кто или что совершает действие, но только когда это важно.

p.uz: Bajaruvchi noma'lum, ravshan yoki muhim bo'lmaganda, hamda rasmiy/ilmiy matnlarda ishlatiladi.
p.ru: Когда деятель неизвестен, очевиден или неважен, а также в официальных/научных текстах.

p.uz: Present perfect: has/have been + pp. Kelasi: will be + pp. Modal: can/must be + pp.
p.ru: Present perfect: has/have been + pp. Будущее: will be + pp. Модальные: can/must be + pp.

quiz.ru: Подлежащее во мн. числе → are made.
Мн. число, настоящий пассив: are cleaned.

quiz.uz: has/have been + pp: has been done.
quiz.ru: has/have been + pp: has been done.
У «arrive» нет дополнения → не бывает в пассиве.

quiz.uz: will be + pp: will be finished.
quiz.ru: will be + pp: will be finished.

quiz.uz: Present perfect passivi: has been cleaned.
quiz.ru: Пассив в present perfect: has been cleaned.

quiz.uz: Modal + be + pp: must be completed.
quiz.ru: Модальный + be + pp: must be completed.

quiz.uz: Present continuous passivi: is being built.
quiz.ru: Пассив в present continuous: is being built.

grammar.title: Reported speech: statements
grammar.lead: Reported (indirect) speech tells what someone said without using their exact words. Tenses usually move one step back, and pronouns and time words often change.

leadTr.uz: Ko'chirma gap (reported speech) birovning so'zini aynan keltirmasdan yetkazadi. Zamonlar odatda bir qadam orqaga suriladi, olmosh va vaqt so'zlari o'zgaradi.
leadTr.ru: Косвенная речь передаёт слова без цитирования. Времена обычно сдвигаются на шаг назад, местоимения и слова времени меняются.

ex: “I am tired.”
“I will call.”
“I can swim.”
He said he was tired.
She said she would call.
He said he could swim.

p: Move the tense back one step: present simple → past simple; present continuous → past continuous; will → would; can → could.
ex: “I am tired.” → He said he was tired.
“I will call.” → She said she would call.

p: Use tell + a person; use say without a person (or with ‘to’).
ex: She told me she was busy. · She said she was busy.

p: Change pronouns to fit the new speaker, and words like today→that day, tomorrow→the next day, now→then.
ex: “I’ll see you tomorrow.” → He said he’d see me the next day.

p: You can include or leave out that after say/tell.
ex: She said (that) she liked it.

grammar.tip: After tell you must name the listener (tell me/him/us); after say you don’t. ‘He said me’ is wrong → ‘He told me’ or ‘He said’.
examples: "“I’m hungry.” → She said she was hungry."
"“We live in Leeds.” → They said they lived in Leeds."
"“I’ll help you.” → He said he would help me."
"“I can swim.” → She told me she could swim."
"“I’m working now.” → He said he was working then."
"“I bought a car.” → She said she had bought a car."
"She said she had bought a car."
"She told us she didn’t like it."
"They said they had finished the work."

mistakes.x: He said me that he was late.
mistakes.v: He told me… / He said (that)… (tell + person, say + no person)

mistakes.x: She said she will come.
mistakes.v: She said she would come. (will → would)

quiz.q: "I am tired." → He said he ___ tired.
quiz.e: present → past: was.

quiz.q: "I will call." → She said she ___ call.
quiz.e: will → would.

quiz.q: "I live here." → He said he ___ there.
quiz.e: present → past: lived.

quiz.q: Choose the correct verb: 'She ___ me she was busy.'
quiz.e: + person → told me.

quiz.q: "I can swim." → He said he ___ swim.
quiz.e: can → could.

quiz.q: "We are eating." → They said they ___ eating.
quiz.e: present continuous → past continuous: were eating.

quiz.q: "I bought a car." → She said she ___ a car.
quiz.e: past → past perfect: had bought.

quiz.q: Choose say/tell: 'He ___ that he was sorry.'
quiz.e: No person → said.

quiz.q: "I'll see you tomorrow." → He said he'd see me ___.
quiz.e: tomorrow → the next day.

quiz.q: "I don't like it." → She said she ___ it.
quiz.e: present → past: didn’t like.

quiz.q: Find the mistake: 'He said me that he was late.'
quiz.e: After ‘said’ no person; use ‘told me’.

quiz.q: Report: "I have finished my homework."
o: She said she finished her homework.
She said she had finished her homework.
She said she has finished her homework.
She said she finishes her homework.
quiz.e: present perfect → past perfect: had finished.

quiz.q: Which is correct?
o: He told me he was tired.
He said me he was tired.
He say me he was tired.
quiz.e: tell + person: told me.

quiz.q: Report: "We are leaving now."
o: They said they are leaving now.
They said they were leaving then.
They said they will leave now.
quiz.e: present continuous → past continuous; now → then.

quiz.q: Report: "I can't come tomorrow."
o: He said he can't come tomorrow.
He said he couldn't come the next day.
He said he couldn't come tomorrow.
quiz.e: can’t → couldn’t; tomorrow → the next day.

tip.uz: 'tell' dan keyin tinglovchini aytish shart (tell me/him/us); 'say' dan keyin esa shart emas. 'He said me' — xato → 'He told me' yoki 'He said'.
tip.ru: После «tell» обязательно называем слушателя (tell me/him/us); после «say» — нет. «He said me» — ошибка → «He told me» или «He said».

p.uz: Zamon bir qadam orqaga suriladi: present simple → past simple; present continuous → past continuous; will → would; can → could.
p.ru: Время сдвигается на шаг назад: present simple → past simple; present continuous → past continuous; will → would; can → could.

p.uz: tell + shaxs bilan; say esa shaxssiz (yoki 'to' bilan) ishlatiladi.
p.ru: tell — с указанием лица; say — без лица (или с «to»).

p.uz: Olmoshlar yangi so'zlovchiga moslanadi; today→that day, tomorrow→the next day, now→then kabi so'zlar o'zgaradi.
p.ru: Местоимения меняются под нового говорящего; today→that day, tomorrow→the next day, now→then.

p.uz: say/tell dan keyin that ni qo'shish ham, tushirib qoldirish ham mumkin.
p.ru: После say/tell «that» можно ставить или опускать.

quiz.uz: Present continuous → past continuous: were eating.
quiz.ru: Present continuous → past continuous: were eating.

quiz.uz: 'said' dan keyin shaxs bo'lmaydi; 'told me' ishlatiladi.
Present perfect → past perfect: had finished.
quiz.ru: Present perfect → past perfect: had finished.

quiz.uz: Present continuous → past continuous; now → then.
quiz.ru: Present continuous → past continuous; now → then.

quiz.uz: can't → couldn't; tomorrow → the next day.
quiz.ru: can't → couldn't; tomorrow → the next day.

grammar.title: Reported questions & commands
grammar.lead: When we report questions and orders, the structure changes. Reported questions use statement word order, and reported commands use ‘to’ + verb.

leadTr.uz: Savol va buyruqlarni ko'chirishda tuzilish o'zgaradi: ko'chirilgan savolda darak gap tartibi, buyruqda esa 'to' + fe'l ishlatiladi.
leadTr.ru: При передаче вопросов и приказов структура меняется: в косвенном вопросе — прямой порядок слов, в приказе — to + глагол.

ex: He asked where I lived.
She asked if I was ready.
She told me to sit down.
He told me not to move.

p: Keep the question word, then use statement order (subject + verb) with no auxiliary do/does/did.
ex: “Where do you live?” → She asked where I lived.

p: Use if or whether, then statement order.
ex: “Are you ready?” → He asked if I was ready.

p: Use told/asked + person + to + verb. For negatives, use not to.
ex: “Sit down.” → She told me to sit down. · “Don’t move.” → He told me not to move.

p: Reported questions are statements, so they don’t end with a question mark.
ex: He asked where the station was.

grammar.tip: In reported questions, don’t keep the question word order or ‘do/did’: ‘She asked where did I live’ is wrong → ‘She asked where I lived.’
examples: "“What time is it?” → He asked what time it was."
"“Do you like tea?” → She asked if I liked tea."
"“Where are you going?” → He asked where I was going."
"“Close the door.” → She told me to close the door."
"“Please help me.” → He asked me to help him."
"“Don’t be late.” → She told me not to be late."
"She told me not to be late."

mistakes.x: She asked me what time was it.
mistakes.v: She asked what time it was. (statement word order)

mistakes.x: He told me to don’t go.
mistakes.v: He told me not to go.

quiz.q: "Where do you live?" → She asked where I ___.
quiz.e: Statement order, backshift: where I lived.

quiz.q: "Are you ready?" → He asked ___ I was ready.
quiz.e: Yes/No → if.

quiz.q: "Sit down." → She told me ___ down.
quiz.e: Command → to sit.

quiz.q: "Don't run." → He told me ___ run.
quiz.e: Negative command → not to run.

quiz.q: "What is your name?" → She asked what my name ___.
quiz.e: Backshift: what my name was.

quiz.q: "Do you like coffee?" → He asked if I ___ coffee.
quiz.e: if + statement order, backshift: liked.

quiz.q: "Open the window." → She asked me ___ the window.
quiz.e: Request → to open.

quiz.q: "Where are you going?" → He asked where I ___.
quiz.e: present cont. → past cont.: was going.

quiz.q: "Can you swim?" → She asked if I ___ swim.
quiz.e: can → could.

quiz.q: Choose the correct word order.
o: He asked where did I live.
He asked did where I live.
quiz.e: Statement order: where I lived.

quiz.q: Find the mistake: 'She asked me what time was it.'
quiz.e: Statement order: what time it was.

quiz.q: Report: "Please don't tell anyone."
o: He asked me not to tell anyone.
He asked me to don't tell anyone.
He asked me don't tell anyone.
He told to not tell anyone.
quiz.e: Negative request → asked me not to tell.

quiz.q: Report: "Have you finished?"
o: She asked if I had finished.
She asked if I have finished.
She asked if had I finished.
quiz.e: Yes/No + present perfect → if I had finished.

quiz.q: Report: "Why are you late?"
o: He asked why was I late.
He asked why I was late.
He asked why I am late.
He asked me why late I was.
quiz.e: Statement order, backshift: why I was late.

quiz.q: Report: "Wait here."
o: She told me to wait there.
She told me to wait here now.
She said me to wait there.
quiz.e: Command → to wait; here → there.

tip.uz: Ko'chirilgan savollarda savol tartibi va 'do/did' saqlanmaydi: 'She asked where did I live' — xato → 'She asked where I lived.'
tip.ru: В косвенных вопросах не сохраняются вопросительный порядок слов и «do/did»: «She asked where did I live» — ошибка → «She asked where I lived».

p.uz: Savol so'zi saqlanadi, keyin darak gap tartibi (ega + fe'l) keladi, do/does/did ishlatilmaydi.
p.ru: Сохраняется вопросительное слово, затем прямой порядок слов (подлежащее + глагол), без do/does/did.

p.uz: if yoki whether ishlatiladi, keyin darak gap tartibi.
p.ru: Используются if или whether, затем прямой порядок слов.

p.uz: told/asked + shaxs + to + fe'l ishlatiladi. Inkorda not to.
p.ru: told/asked + лицо + to + глагол. В отрицании — not to.

p.uz: Ko'chirilgan savollar darak gap, shuning uchun so'roq belgisi bilan tugamaydi.
p.ru: Косвенные вопросы — это утверждения, поэтому не оканчиваются вопросительным знаком.

quiz.uz: Darak tartibi, zamon orqaga: where I lived.
quiz.ru: Прямой порядок, сдвиг времени: where I lived.

quiz.uz: Zamon orqaga: what my name was.
quiz.ru: Сдвиг времени: what my name was.

quiz.uz: if + darak tartibi, zamon orqaga: liked.
Present continuous → past continuous: was going.
quiz.ru: Present continuous → past continuous: was going.

quiz.uz: Darak tartibi: what time it was.
quiz.ru: Прямой порядок: what time it was.

quiz.uz: Inkor iltimos → asked me not to tell.
quiz.ru: Отрицательная просьба → asked me not to tell.

quiz.uz: Ha/Yo'q + present perfect → if I had finished.
quiz.ru: Да/нет + present perfect → if I had finished.

quiz.uz: Darak tartibi, zamon orqaga: why I was late.
quiz.ru: Прямой порядок, сдвиг: why I was late.

grammar.title: Relative clauses (defining & non-defining)
grammar.lead: Relative clauses add information about a noun. Defining clauses give essential information; non-defining clauses give extra information and are separated by commas.

leadTr.uz: Aniqlovchi (defining) nisbiy gap zaruriy ma'lumot beradi; izohlovchi (non-defining) esa qo'shimcha ma'lumot bo'lib, vergul bilan ajratiladi.
leadTr.ru: Определительные придаточные дают необходимую информацию; распространительные — дополнительную и выделяются запятыми.

ex: The man who lives here is a doctor.
The book (that) I read was great.
My dad, who is 60, still works.
Paris, which I love, is busy.

p: Give essential information (you need it to know which person or thing). Use who, which, that, where, whose. No commas.
ex: The man who lives next door is a doctor.

p: Give extra, non-essential information, set off by commas. Don’t use ‘that’; don’t omit the pronoun.
ex: My brother, who lives in Leeds, is a teacher.

p: In defining clauses, you can omit who/which/that when it is the object.
ex: The book (that) I read was great.

p: whose shows possession; where refers to a place.
ex: She’s the woman whose car was stolen. · That’s the town where I grew up.

grammar.tip: Use commas only for extra information (non-defining). With commas, never use ‘that’ and never drop the pronoun. Without commas (defining), you can use ‘that’ and may drop an object pronoun.
examples: "The keys that were on the table have gone."
"Paris, which is the capital of France, is beautiful."
"My uncle, who is a pilot, travels a lot."
"That’s the house where I was born."
"He’s the boy whose dog bit me."
"The man who lives next door is a doctor."
"This is the phone that I bought."
"My brother, who lives in Leeds, is a teacher."
"Paris, which I love, is always busy."
"That’s the town where I grew up."
"She’s the woman whose car was stolen."

mistakes.x: My car, that is red, is fast.
mistakes.v: My car, which is red, is fast. (non-defining → which)

mistakes.x: The man which called…
mistakes.v: The man who called… (people → who)

quiz.q: The woman ___ teaches us is very kind.
quiz.e: People → who.

quiz.q: I bought a phone ___ takes great photos.
quiz.e: Things → which/that.

quiz.q: That's the café ___ we first met.
quiz.e: Place → where.

quiz.q: She's the girl ___ brother is famous.
quiz.e: Possession → whose.

quiz.q: Which clause has extra information (needs commas)?
o: The man who called is here.
My dad, who is 60, still works.
quiz.e: Non-defining → commas.

quiz.q: In which sentence can we omit the pronoun?
quiz.e: Object pronoun in a defining clause can be dropped: the book I read.

quiz.q: Non-defining: 'London, ___ is the capital, is huge.'
quiz.e: Non-defining things → which (never ‘that’).

quiz.q: The keys ___ were on the table are gone.
quiz.e: Things → which/that.

quiz.q: My sister, ___ lives in Bristol, is a nurse.
quiz.e: Non-defining people → who.

quiz.q: Choose the defining clause.
o: The man who called is my boss.
Paris, which I love, is busy.
Tom, whose car broke, is late.
quiz.e: Defining = essential, no commas.

quiz.q: Find the mistake: 'My car, that is red, is fast.'
quiz.e: Non-defining clauses use ‘which’, not ‘that’.

quiz.q: Complete: 'The hotel ___ we stayed, ___ was by the sea, was lovely.'
quiz.e: Place ‘where we stayed’ + non-defining ‘which was by the sea’.

quiz.q: Which sentence omits the pronoun correctly?
o: The film we saw was good.
The man lives here is nice.
The city is big I visited.
quiz.e: Object pronoun dropped: the film (that) we saw.

quiz.q: Complete: 'He's the player ___ goal won the match, ___ made him famous.'
quiz.e: ‘whose goal’ (possession) + non-defining ‘which made him famous’.

quiz.q: Choose the correct non-defining sentence.
o: My teacher who is French is kind.
My teacher, who is French, is kind.
My teacher, that is French, is kind.
My teacher which is French is kind.
quiz.e: Extra info → commas + who.

tip.uz: Vergul faqat qo'shimcha ma'lumot (non-defining) uchun qo'yiladi. Vergul bilan hech qachon 'that' ishlatmang va olmoshni tushirib qoldirmang. Vergulsiz (defining) 'that' ishlatish va to'ldiruvchi olmoshini tushirish mumkin.
tip.ru: Запятые ставятся только при дополнительной информации (non-defining). С запятыми нельзя «that» и нельзя опускать местоимение. Без запятых (defining) можно «that» и можно опустить местоимение-дополнение.

p.uz: Zaruriy ma'lumot beradi (qaysi odam yoki narsa ekanini bilish uchun kerak). who, which, that, where, whose ishlatiladi. Vergul yo'q.
p.ru: Дают необходимую информацию (без неё не ясно, о ком или о чём речь). Используются who, which, that, where, whose. Без запятых.

p.uz: Qo'shimcha, zaruriy bo'lmagan ma'lumot beradi, vergul bilan ajratiladi. 'that' ishlatilmaydi; olmosh tushirilmaydi.
p.ru: Дают дополнительную, необязательную информацию, выделяются запятыми. Нельзя «that»; нельзя опускать местоимение.

p.uz: Defining gaplarda who/which/that to'ldiruvchi bo'lsa, uni tushirib qoldirish mumkin.
p.ru: В defining-придаточных who/which/that можно опустить, если это дополнение.

p.uz: whose egalikni bildiradi; where joyga ishora qiladi.
p.ru: whose показывает принадлежность; where относится к месту.

quiz.uz: Defining gapdagi to'ldiruvchi olmoshi tushiriladi: the book I read.
quiz.ru: Местоимение-дополнение в defining можно опустить: the book I read.

quiz.uz: Joy 'where we stayed' + non-defining 'which was by the sea'.
quiz.ru: Место «where we stayed» + non-defining «which was by the sea».

quiz.uz: To'ldiruvchi olmoshi tushirilgan: the film (that) we saw.
quiz.ru: Опущено местоимение-дополнение: the film (that) we saw.

grammar.title: Past habits: used to & would
grammar.lead: To describe the past we can use ‘used to’ and ‘would’ for repeated habits, but only ‘used to’ works for past states. Both contrast the past with the present.

leadTr.uz: O'tmishdagi takrorlangan odatlar uchun 'used to' ham, 'would' ham bo'ladi, lekin o'tmishdagi HOLATLAR uchun faqat 'used to' ishlaydi: I used to live in Samarkand.
leadTr.ru: Для повторявшихся привычек подходят и used to, и would, но для прошлых СОСТОЯНИЙ — только used to: I used to live in Samarkand.

ex: I used to play tennis.
She used to have long hair.
Every summer we would visit them.
✗ I would have a bike.

p: used to + base verb describes past habits and past states that are no longer true.
ex: I used to play tennis. · She used to have long hair.

p: would + base verb describes repeated past actions, but not states. It is common in stories.
ex: Every summer we would visit my grandparents.

blocks.h: would vs. used to with states
p: Don’t use ‘would’ with state verbs (be, have, like, know). Use ‘used to’.
ex: ✓ I used to be shy. · ✗ I would be shy.

p: For ‘used to’: didn’t use to / Did … use to? (no -d).
ex: He didn’t use to like coffee. · Did you use to live here?

grammar.tip: Use ‘would’ only for repeated actions. For past states (be, have, like, know), you must use ‘used to’: ‘I used to have a bike’, not ‘I would have a bike’.
examples: "We used to live by the sea."
"On Sundays, my dad would cook a big breakfast."
"He didn’t use to exercise, but now he runs daily."
"As children, we would play outside all day."
"Did you use to have a dog?"
"I used to play tennis every weekend."
"On Sundays, my dad would cook breakfast."
"We would visit our grandparents each summer."
"There used to be a shop on this corner."

mistakes.x: I would have a red car when I was young.
mistakes.v: I used to have a red car. (state → used to)

mistakes.x: Did you used to live here?
mistakes.v: Did you use to live here? (after did → no -d)

quiz.q: I ___ play football every day as a child.
quiz.e: Past habit: used to play.

quiz.q: Every winter, we ___ go skiing.
quiz.e: Repeated action → would go.

quiz.q: She ___ have long hair.
quiz.e: Past state → used to have.

quiz.q: They ___ visit us every summer.
quiz.e: Repeated action → would visit.

quiz.q: He ___ be very thin.
quiz.e: Past state → used to be.

quiz.q: Which sentence is WRONG?
quiz.e: ‘would’ can’t be used with the state ‘be’.

quiz.q: Negative: 'I ___ like vegetables.'
quiz.e: didn’t use to (no -d).

quiz.q: On holiday, we ___ swim in the sea every morning.
quiz.e: Repeated action → would swim.

quiz.q: ___ you use to have a bike?
quiz.e: Did you use to…?

quiz.q: Choose the state-verb sentence (only 'used to').
o: I used to have a cat.
quiz.e: ‘have’ is a state → used to have.

quiz.q: Find the mistake: 'I would have a red car when I was young.'
quiz.e: State ‘have’ → used to have (not would).

quiz.q: Complete: 'My grandmother ___ tell us stories, and she ___ a wonderful voice.'
quiz.e: Repeated action ‘would tell’ + state ‘used to have’.

quiz.q: Which is correct for a past habit and a past state?
o: I would be a teacher and would smoke.
I used to be a teacher and would smoke.
I would be a teacher and used to smoke.
I use to be a teacher and would smoke.
quiz.e: State ‘used to be’ + repeated action ‘would smoke’.

quiz.q: Complete: '___ they ___ live in the countryside?'
quiz.e: Did + use to: Did they use to live…?

quiz.q: Choose the natural sentence.
o: When I was a kid, I would have a dog.
When I was a kid, I used to have a dog.
