When I was a kid, I use to have a dog.
When I was a kid, I am used to have a dog.
quiz.e: State ‘have’ → used to have.

tip.uz: 'would' faqat takrorlangan harakatlar uchun. O'tgan holatlar (be, have, like, know) uchun faqat 'used to': 'I used to have a bike', 'I would have a bike' emas.
tip.ru: «would» — только для повторявшихся действий. Для состояний в прошлом (be, have, like, know) нужно «used to»: «I used to have a bike», а не «I would have a bike».

p.uz: used to + asosiy shakl — endi mavjud bo'lmagan o'tgan odatlar va holatlarni bildiradi.
p.ru: used to + начальная форма описывает прошлые привычки и состояния, которых больше нет.

p.uz: would + asosiy shakl — takrorlangan o'tgan harakatlarni bildiradi, holatlarni emas. Hikoyalarda ko'p uchraydi.
p.ru: would + начальная форма описывает повторявшиеся действия в прошлом, но не состояния. Часто в рассказах.

h.uz: Holatlar bilan would va used to
h.ru: would и used to с состояниями

p.uz: Holat fe'llari (be, have, like, know) bilan 'would' ishlatmang. 'used to' ishlating.
p.ru: С глаголами состояния (be, have, like, know) нельзя «would». Используйте «used to».

p.uz: 'used to' uchun: didn't use to / Did … use to? (-d siz).
p.ru: Для «used to»: didn't use to / Did … use to? (без -d).

quiz.uz: Takroriy harakat 'would tell' + holat 'used to have'.
quiz.ru: Повторявшееся действие «would tell» + состояние «used to have».

quiz.uz: Holat 'used to be' + takroriy harakat 'would smoke'.
quiz.ru: Состояние «used to be» + повторявшееся действие «would smoke».

quiz.uz: Did + use to: Did they use to live…?
quiz.ru: Did + use to: Did they use to live…?

grammar.title: Gerunds & infinitives
grammar.lead: Many verbs are followed by a gerund (-ing) and others by an infinitive (to + verb). Some verbs take either form, and a few change meaning depending on which you choose.

leadTr.uz: Ko'p fe'llardan keyin gerund (-ing), boshqalaridan keyin infinitiv keladi. Ba'zilari ikkala shaklni oladi, ayrimlarida esa ma'no o'zgaradi: stop doing / stop to do.
leadTr.ru: После многих глаголов идёт герундий, после других — инфинитив. Некоторые принимают обе формы, а у части меняется смысл: stop doing / stop to do.

ex: decide to leave
refuse to help
manage to do
enjoy cooking
good at drawing
before going

p: After enjoy, finish, avoid, suggest, mind, keep, practise, can’t stand, look forward to, and after prepositions, use the -ing form.
ex: I enjoy cooking. · She’s good at drawing. · I look forward to seeing you.

p: After want, decide, hope, plan, promise, agree, offer, refuse, manage, learn, would like, use to + verb.
ex: We decided to leave. · He refused to help.

p: Some verbs take an object then to-infinitive: want, ask, tell, allow, advise, expect.
ex: She asked me to wait. · They allowed us to stay.

p: A few verbs change meaning: stop, remember, try, forget.
ex: I stopped smoking. (gave it up) · I stopped to smoke. (paused in order to)

grammar.tip: After prepositions (about, of, at, in, before, after, without), always use the -ing form: ‘I’m interested in learning’, ‘before going out’.
examples: "We can’t afford to travel this year."

mistakes.x: I’m interested in to learn Spanish.
mistakes.v: I’m interested in learning Spanish. (preposition + -ing)

mistakes.x: They allowed us stay.
mistakes.v: They allowed us to stay.

quiz.q: I enjoy ___ to music.
quiz.e: enjoy + -ing: listening.

quiz.q: We decided ___ early.
quiz.e: decide + to: to leave.

quiz.q: She's good at ___.
quiz.e: Preposition ‘at’ + -ing: drawing.

quiz.q: He refused ___ the question.
quiz.e: refuse + to: to answer.

quiz.q: Do you mind ___ the window?
quiz.e: mind + -ing: opening.

quiz.q: They asked me ___ them.
quiz.e: ask + object + to: to help.

quiz.q: I'm thinking about ___ a new car.
quiz.e: Preposition ‘about’ + -ing: buying.

quiz.q: She managed ___ the problem.
quiz.e: manage + to: to solve.

quiz.q: We're looking forward to ___ you.
quiz.e: ‘look forward to’ + -ing: seeing.

quiz.q: He suggested ___ a taxi.
quiz.e: suggest + -ing: taking.

quiz.q: Find the mistake: 'I'm interested in to learn Spanish.'
quiz.e: Preposition ‘in’ + -ing: learning.

quiz.q: Choose the correct meaning: 'He stopped to smoke' means ___.
o: he paused in order to smoke
quiz.e: stop + to = pause in order to do something.

quiz.q: Complete: 'Please remember ___ the door, and I'll never forget ___ here as a child.'
quiz.e: remember to do (duty) + forget doing (memory).

quiz.q: Which is correct?
quiz.e: allow + object + to: allowed us to stay.

quiz.q: Complete: 'I tried ___ the box, but it was locked, so I tried ___ a knife.'
quiz.e: try to do (attempt) + try doing (experiment): to open / using.

tip.uz: Predloglardan keyin (about, of, at, in, before, after, without) doim -ing shakli: 'I'm interested in learning', 'before going out'.
tip.ru: После предлогов (about, of, at, in, before, after, without) всегда форма -ing: «I'm interested in learning», «before going out».

p.uz: enjoy, finish, avoid, suggest, mind, keep, practise, can't stand, look forward to dan keyin va predloglardan keyin -ing shakli ishlatiladi.
p.ru: После enjoy, finish, avoid, suggest, mind, keep, practise, can't stand, look forward to и после предлогов — форма -ing.

p.uz: want, decide, hope, plan, promise, agree, offer, refuse, manage, learn, would like dan keyin to + fe'l ishlatiladi.
p.ru: После want, decide, hope, plan, promise, agree, offer, refuse, manage, learn, would like — to + глагол.

p.uz: Ba'zi fe'llar to'ldiruvchi, keyin to-infinitiv oladi: want, ask, tell, allow, advise, expect.
p.ru: Некоторые глаголы берут дополнение, затем to-инфинитив: want, ask, tell, allow, advise, expect.

p.uz: Ayrim fe'llarda ma'no o'zgaradi: stop, remember, try, forget.
p.ru: У нескольких глаголов значение меняется: stop, remember, try, forget.

quiz.uz: stop + to = biror ish qilish uchun to'xtamoq.
quiz.ru: stop + to = остановиться, чтобы что-то сделать.

quiz.uz: allow + to'ldiruvchi + to: allowed us to stay.
quiz.ru: allow + дополнение + to: allowed us to stay.

quiz.uz: try to do (urinish) + try doing (tajriba): to open / using.
quiz.ru: try to do (попытка) + try doing (эксперимент): to open / using.

grammar.title: Comparing: as…as, less, modifiers
grammar.lead: Beyond basic comparatives, we can show that two things are equal, that one is inferior, or how big the difference is. These patterns make comparisons more precise.

leadTr.uz: Oddiy qiyoslashdan tashqari tenglikni (as…as), kamlikni (less) va farq hajmini (much bigger, a bit smaller) ifodalash mumkin — bu qiyoslashni aniqroq qiladi.
leadTr.ru: Помимо простого сравнения можно выразить равенство (as…as), меньшую степень (less) и размер разницы (much bigger, a bit smaller).

ex: She’s as tall as him.
not as cold as yesterday
less interesting than
much better · a bit warmer

p: Use as + adjective + as to say two things are the same, and not as … as for inequality.
ex: She’s as tall as her brother. · It’s not as cold as yesterday.

p: Use less + adjective + than (the opposite of ‘more … than’), usually with longer adjectives.
ex: This film is less interesting than the book.

p: Make comparatives stronger or weaker with much, far, a lot, a bit, slightly.
ex: He’s much taller than me. · It’s a bit warmer today.

p: Use ‘the + comparative … the + comparative’ to show that two things change together.
ex: The more you practise, the better you get.

grammar.tip: To strengthen a comparative, use much or far (much/far better), not ‘very’. ‘Very better’ is wrong; ‘much better’ is correct.
examples: "Maths is as difficult as physics for me."
"This phone is not as expensive as that one."
"The book is less exciting than the film."
"He runs a bit faster than me."
"The harder you work, the more you earn."
"The more you practise, the better you get."
"This phone is just as good as that one."

mistakes.x: This car is very better than mine.
mistakes.v: …is much better than mine. (much/far, not very)

mistakes.x: She is as tall than him.
mistakes.v: She is as tall as him.

quiz.q: She is ___ tall ___ her sister.
quiz.e: Equality: as tall as.

quiz.q: It isn't ___ cold ___ yesterday.
quiz.e: not as cold as.

quiz.q: This book is ___ interesting than that one.
quiz.e: less interesting than.

quiz.q: He's ___ taller than me.
quiz.e: Modifier → much taller.

quiz.q: Today is ___ a bit warmer than yesterday.
quiz.e: ‘just a bit warmer’ — slightly (just/a bit) modifies the comparative.

quiz.q: My phone is ___ expensive ___ yours.
quiz.e: Equality: as expensive as.

quiz.q: The film was ___ exciting than the book.
quiz.e: less exciting than.

quiz.q: He's ___ better at chess than I am.
quiz.e: Modifier → far better.

quiz.q: Complete: '___ you practise, ___ you become.'
quiz.e: the more … the better.

quiz.q: Choose the equality sentence.
o: She is as tall as him.
She is more tall than him.
quiz.e: Equality → as tall as.

quiz.q: Find the mistake: 'This car is very better than mine.'
quiz.e: Use ‘much better’, not ‘very better’.

quiz.q: Complete: 'It's ___ as difficult ___ I expected — much easier, in fact.'
quiz.e: not as difficult as.

quiz.q: Which means 'they are equal'?
o: A is less good than B.
A is much better than B.
A is as good as B.
A isn't as good as B.
quiz.e: as good as = equal.

quiz.q: Complete: 'The ___ we leave, the ___ we'll arrive.'
quiz.e: the sooner … the earlier.

quiz.q: Choose the correctly modified comparative.
quiz.e: far cheaper (much/far + comparative).

tip.uz: Qiyosiy darajani kuchaytirish uchun much yoki far ishlatiladi (much/far better), 'very' emas. 'Very better' — xato; 'much better' — to'g'ri.
tip.ru: Чтобы усилить сравнительную степень, используйте much или far (much/far better), а не «very». «Very better» — ошибка; «much better» — верно.

p.uz: Ikki narsa bir xil ekanini aytish uchun as + sifat + as, tengsizlik uchun not as … as ishlatiladi.
p.ru: as + прилагательное + as — когда две вещи одинаковы; not as … as — при неравенстве.

p.uz: less + sifat + than ('more … than' ning teskarisi), odatda uzun sifatlar bilan ishlatiladi.
p.ru: less + прилагательное + than (противоположность «more … than»), обычно с длинными прилагательными.

p.uz: Qiyosiy darajani much, far, a lot, a bit, slightly bilan kuchaytirish yoki yumshatish mumkin.
p.ru: Сравнительную степень усиливают или смягчают: much, far, a lot, a bit, slightly.

p.uz: Ikki narsa birga o'zgarishini ko'rsatish uchun 'the + qiyosiy … the + qiyosiy' ishlatiladi.
p.ru: «the + сравнительная … the + сравнительная» показывает, что две вещи меняются вместе.

quiz.uz: 'just a bit warmer' — just/a bit qiyosiy darajani yumshatadi.
quiz.ru: «just a bit warmer» — just/a bit смягчают сравнение.

grammar.title: Quantifiers
grammar.lead: Quantifiers tell us about amount and number. At B1 we extend beyond some/any to all, most, both, neither, none, each and every, and learn how they combine with nouns and ‘of’.

leadTr.uz: B1 darajasida some/any dan tashqari all, most, both, neither, none, each va every so'zlarini hamda ularning ot bilan qanday birikishini o'rganamiz.
leadTr.ru: На B1 мы выходим за пределы some/any: all, most, both, neither, none, each, every и их сочетания с существительными.

ex: Most people like music.
Every student has a book.
Most of the students passed.
None of the answers were right.

p: Use these for general amounts. With ‘the/my/these’ + noun, add of: most of the students.
ex: Most people like music. · None of the answers were right.

p: both = the two together; neither = not one and not the other; either = one or the other.
ex: Both films are good. · Neither answer is correct. · Either day is fine.

p: Both mean ‘all, seen individually’, and take a singular verb. ‘every’ for the whole group; ‘each’ for the individuals.
ex: Every student has a book. · Each answer is different.

p: a few + countable, a little + uncountable, several = more than a few (countable).
ex: A few people came. · A little milk. · Several students passed.

grammar.tip: every and each are followed by a singular noun and verb: ‘Every student is here’, not ‘every students are here’.

mistakes.x: Every students are present.
mistakes.v: Every student is present. (every + singular)

mistakes.x: Most of people are kind.
mistakes.v: Most people are kind. (no “of” without the/my)

quiz.q: ___ people enjoy music.
quiz.e: General → Most people.

quiz.q: ___ of the students passed.
quiz.e: With ‘the’ → Most of the students.

quiz.q: ___ answers are correct — well done!
quiz.e: The two together → Both answers.

quiz.q: ___ student has a textbook.
quiz.e: + singular noun → Every student.

quiz.q: I have ___ money, just a little.
quiz.e: Uncountable → a little.

quiz.q: ___ of the answers was right; they were all wrong.
quiz.e: Zero → None of the answers.

quiz.q: ___ of us wants to leave; we're both happy.
quiz.e: Not one and not the other → Neither.

quiz.q: ___ child in the class is different.
quiz.e: Individuals + singular → Each child.

quiz.q: ___ students complained about the test.
quiz.e: More than a few, countable → Several.

quiz.q: Choose the correct verb: 'Every student ___ here.'
quiz.e: ‘every’ → singular: is.

quiz.q: Find the mistake: 'Every students are present.'
quiz.e: every + singular: Every student is present.

quiz.q: Complete: '___ of the two options is fine; choose ___ you like.'
quiz.e: Either of the two is fine; choose either.

quiz.q: Which is correct?
quiz.e: General statement → Most people (no ‘of’ without the/my/these).

quiz.q: Complete: '___ of my friends came, but ___ stayed late.'
quiz.e: All of my friends came, but none stayed late.

quiz.q: Choose the sentence with correct agreement.
o: Each of the rooms have a bed.
Each of the rooms has a bed.
Each of the room have a bed.
quiz.e: ‘each’ → singular verb: has.

tip.uz: every va each dan keyin birlikdagi ot va fe'l keladi: 'Every student is here', 'every students are here' emas.
tip.ru: После every и each — существительное и глагол в единственном числе: «Every student is here», а не «every students are here».

p.uz: Umumiy miqdorlar uchun ishlatiladi. 'the/my/these' + ot bilan of qo'shiladi: most of the students.
p.ru: Для общих количеств. С «the/my/these» + существительное добавляется of: most of the students.

p.uz: both = ikkalasi birga; neither = na u, na bu; either = u yoki bu.
p.ru: both = оба вместе; neither = ни тот, ни другой; either = тот или другой.

p.uz: Ikkalasi ham 'hammasi, alohida-alohida' ma'nosini beradi va birlikdagi fe'l oladi. 'every' — butun guruh uchun; 'each' — har biri uchun.
p.ru: Оба означают «все, по отдельности» и требуют глагол в единственном числе. «every» — о группе целиком; «each» — о каждом в отдельности.

p.uz: a few + sanaladigan, a little + sanalmaydigan, several = bir nechtadan ko'proq (sanaladigan).
p.ru: a few + исчисляемые, a little + неисчисляемые, several = больше, чем несколько (исчисляемые).

quiz.ru: + существительное в ед. числе → Every student.

quiz.uz: every + birlik: Every student is present.
quiz.ru: every + ед. число: Every student is present.

quiz.uz: Either of the two is fine; choose either.
quiz.ru: Either of the two is fine; choose either.

quiz.uz: Umumiy gap → Most people (the/my/these siz 'of' yo'q).
quiz.ru: Общее утверждение → Most people (без «of», если нет the/my/these).

quiz.uz: All of my friends came, but none stayed late.
quiz.ru: All of my friends came, but none stayed late.

grammar.title: Conditionals: zero, first & linkers
grammar.lead: Conditionals describe results that follow from conditions. The zero conditional states facts; the first conditional describes likely future situations. Linkers like unless and as long as add precision.

leadTr.uz: Shart gaplar natija va shartni bog'laydi: zero conditional — faktlar, first conditional — ehtimoliy kelajak. Unless, as long as, in case kabi bog'lovchilar ma'noni boyitadi.
leadTr.ru: Кондиционалы связывают условие и результат: zero — факты, first — вероятное будущее. Unless, as long as, in case обогащают смысл.

ex: If you heat ice, it melts.
If it rains, we’ll stay in.

p: Use if/when + present, present for things that are always true.
ex: If you heat water, it boils.

p: Use if + present, will + base for real, likely future situations.
ex: If it rains, we’ll stay in.

p: unless = if … not. It introduces the only condition that changes the result.
ex: I won’t go unless you come too. (= if you don’t come)

blocks.h: as long as / provided that / in case
p: as long as / provided that = on condition that; in case = as a precaution.
ex: You can stay as long as you’re quiet. · Take an umbrella in case it rains.

grammar.tip: Don’t use ‘will’ after if/unless/as long as/in case in the condition: ‘If it will rain’ is wrong → ‘If it rains, we’ll stay in.’
examples: "If you mix blue and yellow, you get green."
"You can borrow it as long as you return it."
"I’ll take my phone in case you call."
"Provided that you pay, you can join."
"You can stay as long as you’re quiet."
"Take an umbrella in case it rains."
"I won’t go unless you come too."

mistakes.x: I’ll help you as long as you will ask.
mistakes.v: …as long as you ask. (no “will” in the condition)

mistakes.x: Unless you don’t hurry, we’ll be late.
mistakes.v: Unless you hurry… (unless already = if not)

quiz.q: If you heat ice, it ___.
quiz.e: Zero conditional → present: melts.

quiz.q: If it rains, we ___ inside.
quiz.e: First conditional → will stay.

quiz.q: You'll be late ___ you hurry.
quiz.e: unless = if … not.

quiz.q: If you ___ water to 100°C, it boils.
quiz.e: Zero conditional → present: heat.

quiz.q: I'll call you ___ I arrive.
quiz.e: ‘when I arrive’ (it will happen).

quiz.q: Take a coat ___ it gets cold.
quiz.e: Precaution → in case it gets cold.

quiz.q: You can stay ___ you keep quiet.
quiz.e: Condition → as long as.

quiz.q: If you ___ now, you'll catch the bus.
quiz.e: First conditional → leave (present).

quiz.q: We won't win ___ we play better.
quiz.e: unless = if … not.

quiz.q: Choose the zero conditional.
o: If you drop glass, it breaks.
If I were rich, I'd travel.
quiz.e: General fact → zero conditional.

quiz.q: Find the mistake: 'I'll help you as long as you will ask.'
quiz.e: No ‘will’ in the condition: as long as you ask.

quiz.q: Complete: 'I'll lend it to you ___ you ___ it back.'
quiz.e: Condition → provided that you give it back.

quiz.q: Which is correct?
o: Unless you don't hurry, we'll be late.
Unless you hurry, we'll be late.
If you hurry, we'll be late.
Unless you will hurry, we'll be late.
quiz.e: unless already means ‘if not’: Unless you hurry…

quiz.q: Complete: 'Take the map ___ you ___ lost.'
quiz.e: Precaution → in case you get lost.

quiz.q: Choose the correct first conditional.
o: If it will snow, school closes.
If it snows, school will close.
If it snows, school closes always.
If it would snow, school will close.
quiz.e: If + present, will + base.

tip.uz: if/unless/as long as/in case dan keyin shart qismida 'will' ishlatmang: 'If it will rain' — xato → 'If it rains, we'll stay in.'
tip.ru: Не используйте «will» в условии после if/unless/as long as/in case: «If it will rain» — ошибка → «If it rains, we'll stay in».

p.uz: Doim to'g'ri bo'lgan narsalar uchun if/when + hozirgi, hozirgi zamon ishlatiladi.
p.ru: Для всегда верных вещей: if/when + настоящее, настоящее.

p.uz: Real, ehtimoli katta kelajak vaziyatlar uchun if + hozirgi, will + asosiy shakl.
p.ru: Для реальных, вероятных будущих ситуаций: if + настоящее, will + начальная форма.

p.uz: unless = if … not. U natijani o'zgartiradigan yagona shartni kiritadi.
p.ru: unless = if … not. Вводит единственное условие, меняющее результат.

h.uz: as long as / provided that / in case
h.ru: as long as / provided that / in case

p.uz: as long as / provided that = shu shart bilan; in case = ehtiyot chorasi sifatida.
p.ru: as long as / provided that = при условии, что; in case = на всякий случай.

quiz.uz: Ehtiyot chorasi → in case it gets cold.
quiz.ru: Предосторожность → in case it gets cold.

quiz.uz: Shart qismida 'will' bo'lmaydi: as long as you ask.
quiz.ru: В условии нет «will»: as long as you ask.

quiz.uz: Shart → provided that you give it back.
quiz.ru: Условие → provided that you give it back.

quiz.uz: unless o'zi 'if not' ma'nosini beradi: Unless you hurry…
quiz.ru: unless уже означает «если не»: Unless you hurry…

quiz.uz: Ehtiyot chorasi → in case you get lost.
quiz.ru: Предосторожность → in case you get lost.

quiz.uz: If + hozirgi zamon, will + asosiy shakl.

grammar.title: Articles: a / an / the / zero
grammar.lead: Articles are small but tricky. ‘A/an’ introduces something new or one of many; ‘the’ points to something specific or already known; and we use no article (zero) for general ideas and most plurals/uncountables.

leadTr.uz: Artikllar kichik, lekin murakkab: 'a/an' — yangi yoki noaniq narsa, 'the' — aniq yoki ma'lum narsa, ba'zi hollarda esa artikl umuman ishlatilmaydi.
leadTr.ru: Артикли малы, но коварны: a/an — новое или неопределённое, the — конкретное или известное, а иногда артикль не нужен вовсе.

ex: I saw a dog. The dog was big.
She’s the best.
Dogs are loyal.
I like music.
go to school

p: Use a/an with singular countable nouns mentioned for the first time or as examples. ‘an’ before a vowel sound.
ex: I saw a dog. · She’s an engineer. · It takes an hour. (silent h)

p: Use the when both speaker and listener know which one, for unique things, and when mentioned again.
ex: The sun is hot. · I bought a book; the book was great.

p: Use no article for plural and uncountable nouns in general, and most names, meals, and many places.
ex: Dogs are loyal. · I like music. · We have lunch at one.

p: Some places take ‘the’ or zero by convention.
ex: go to school/work/bed (zero) · play the piano · in the morning

grammar.tip: Use ‘a/an’ when it’s new or one of many, and ‘the’ when it’s specific or already known. For general statements with plurals/uncountables, use no article: ‘Books are useful’, not ‘The books are useful’.
examples: "It takes an hour to get there."

mistakes.x: I love the nature.
mistakes.v: I love nature. (general uncountable → no article)

mistakes.x: She is best doctor in town.
mistakes.v: She is the best doctor in town. (superlative → the)

quiz.q: I saw ___ cat in the garden.
quiz.e: New, singular countable → a cat.

quiz.q: She is ___ honest person.
quiz.e: Silent h, vowel sound → an honest.

quiz.q: ___ sun rises in the east.
quiz.e: Unique object → The sun.

quiz.q: I like ___ music.
quiz.e: General uncountable → no article.

quiz.q: He's ___ engineer.
quiz.e: Vowel sound → an engineer.

quiz.q: We go to ___ bed at ten.
quiz.e: Fixed expression → go to bed (zero).

quiz.q: I bought a phone. ___ phone was cheap.
quiz.e: Mentioned again → The phone.

quiz.q: ___ dogs are friendly animals. (in general)
quiz.e: General plural → no article.

quiz.q: She plays ___ violin.
quiz.e: Instruments → play the violin.

quiz.q: It takes ___ hour to get there.
quiz.e: Silent h → an hour.

quiz.q: Find the mistake: 'I love the nature.'
quiz.e: General uncountable → no article: I love nature.

quiz.q: Complete: 'We had ___ breakfast, then went to ___ work.'
quiz.e: Meals and ‘go to work’ → zero article.

quiz.q: Which is correct?
quiz.e: General abstract noun → no article: Life is hard.

quiz.q: Complete: 'I saw ___ film last night. ___ film was about ___ space.'
quiz.e: a film (new) / The film (known) / space (general, zero).

quiz.q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: She is best doctor in the town.
She is the best doctor in the town.
She is a best doctor in the town.
She is best doctor in town a.
quiz.e: Superlative needs ‘the’: the best doctor.

tip.uz: Yangi yoki ko'pdan biri bo'lsa — a/an; aniq yoki ma'lum bo'lsa — the. Ko'plik/sanalmaydigan otlar bilan umumiy gaplarda artikl ishlatilmaydi: 'Books are useful', 'The books are useful' emas.
tip.ru: Новое или одно из многих — a/an; конкретное или известное — the. В общих утверждениях с множественным числом и неисчисляемыми — без артикля: «Books are useful», а не «The books are useful».

p.uz: Birinchi marta tilga olingan yoki misol sifatida keltirilgan birlikdagi sanaladigan otlar bilan a/an ishlatiladi. Unli tovushdan oldin 'an'.
p.ru: a/an — с исчисляемыми существительными в ед. числе, упомянутыми впервые или как пример. Перед гласным звуком — «an».

p.uz: So'zlovchi ham, tinglovchi ham qaysi biri ekanini bilsa, yagona narsalar uchun va qayta tilga olinganda the ishlatiladi.
p.ru: the — когда и говорящий, и слушатель знают, о чём речь, для уникальных вещей и при повторном упоминании.

p.uz: Umumiy ma'nodagi ko'plik va sanalmaydigan otlar bilan, ko'pchilik nomlar, taomlar va ko'p joylar bilan artikl ishlatilmaydi.
p.ru: Без артикля — множественное число и неисчисляемые в общем значении, большинство имён, приёмы пищи и многие места.

p.uz: Ba'zi joylar an'anaga ko'ra 'the' yoki nol artikl oladi.
p.ru: Некоторые места по традиции берут «the» или нулевой артикль.

quiz.ru: Новое, ед. число, исчисляемое → a cat.

quiz.uz: h talaffuz qilinmaydi, unli tovush → an honest.
quiz.ru: Немая h, гласный звук → an honest.

quiz.uz: Turg'un ibora → go to bed (nol artikl).
quiz.ru: Устойчивое выражение → go to bed (нулевой артикль).

quiz.uz: Umumiy sanalmaydigan → artiklsiz: I love nature.
quiz.ru: Общее неисчисляемое → без артикля: I love nature.

quiz.uz: Taomlar va 'go to work' → nol artikl.
quiz.ru: Приёмы пищи и «go to work» → нулевой артикль.

quiz.uz: Umumiy mavhum ot → artiklsiz: Life is hard.
quiz.ru: Общее абстрактное существительное → без артикля: Life is hard.

quiz.uz: a film (yangi) / The film (ma'lum) / space (umumiy, nol artikl).
quiz.ru: a film (новое) / The film (известное) / space (общее, нулевой артикль).

quiz.uz: Orttirma daraja 'the' talab qiladi: the best doctor.
quiz.ru: Превосходная степень требует «the»: the best doctor.

grammar.title: Agreeing: so do I / neither do I
grammar.lead: Learn to agree quickly and naturally with 'So do I' and 'Neither do I' — the short echo responses English speakers use all the time.

leadTr.uz: 'So do I' va 'Neither do I' bilan tez va tabiiy rozilik bildirishni o'rganing — ingliz tilida doim ishlatiladigan qisqa javoblar.
leadTr.ru: Научитесь быстро и естественно соглашаться с помощью 'So do I' и 'Neither do I' — коротких ответов-эхо, которые англичане используют постоянно.

grammar.situation: Kamola: "I love green tea." Rustam: "So do I. But I can't drink it late at night." Kamola: "Neither can I — I don't sleep well after it."

blocks.h: Agreeing with a positive statement: So + auxiliary + subject
p: To say that the same positive thing is true for you, use So + auxiliary verb + subject. Notice the inverted word order: the auxiliary comes before the subject, like in a question.
The auxiliary must match the verb in the first sentence: be stays be, a modal stays the same modal, and present or past simple use do/does/did.
ex: "I'm from Tashkent." "So am I."
"Kamola works in IT Park." "So does her brother."
"We went to Samarkand last spring." "So did we."

blocks.h: Agreeing with a negative statement: Neither / Nor + auxiliary + subject
p: When the first statement is negative, agree with Neither (or Nor) + auxiliary + subject. The auxiliary is positive — the negative idea is already inside 'neither', so never say 'Neither can't I'.
ex: "I don't eat meat." "Neither do I."
"Rustam hasn't seen that film." "Neither has Kamola."
"I can't drive." "Nor can I."

p: Copy the auxiliary that is already in the sentence: am/is/are, was/were, have/has, will, would, can, could, must. If there is no auxiliary — that is, present simple or past simple — borrow do, does or did.
This is the same trick you use for question tags, so if you know 'She has finished, hasn't she?', you also know 'So have I.'
ex: "I'd love to visit Bukhara." "So would I." (would → would)
"She speaks three languages." "So does he." (present simple → does)
"They were late." "So were we." (were → were)

blocks.h: Disagreeing, and the informal 'Me too / Me neither'
p: To say the opposite is true for you, use subject + auxiliary in normal order: "I love winter." "Really? I don't." / "I can't cook." "Oh, I can."
In informal speech you can simply say 'Me too' after a positive statement and 'Me neither' after a negative one. Both are very common in conversation but too casual for formal writing.
ex: "I hate queues." "Me too."
"I've never been to London." "Me neither."
"I'm staying home tonight." "I'm not — I'm meeting friends."

grammar.tip: Word order is the trap: after 'so' and 'neither' the auxiliary jumps in front of the subject — So do I, Neither can I — never 'So I do' for agreement.
examples: "Rustam doesn't like horror films." "Neither does Kamola."

mistakes.x: "I like plov." "So I do."
mistakes.v: "So do I." — after 'so', put the auxiliary before the subject

mistakes.x: "I can't swim." "Neither can't I."
mistakes.v: "Neither can I." — 'neither' is already negative, so the auxiliary stays positive

mistakes.x: "She went home early." "So does I."
mistakes.v: "So did I." — match the tense (past simple → did) and the subject

quiz.q: "I love green tea." "___"
quiz.e: 'love' is present simple, so the auxiliary is 'do': So do I.

quiz.q: "I'm really tired today." "___"
quiz.e: 'am' is the verb be, so it repeats: So am I.

quiz.q: "I can't swim very well." "___"
quiz.e: Negative statement with 'can' → Neither can I.

quiz.q: "We went to Samarkand last week." "___"
quiz.e: Past simple has no auxiliary, so borrow 'did': So did I.

quiz.q: "I've never tried sushi." "___"
quiz.e: 'never' makes it negative; the perfect auxiliary is 'have': Neither have I.

quiz.q: Kamola doesn't like horror films. Neither ___ Rustam.
quiz.e: Present simple with a third-person subject → does.

quiz.q: "I won't be at the meeting tomorrow." "___"
quiz.e: 'won't' is negative → Neither will I (positive auxiliary after 'neither').

quiz.q: "I love cold winters." "Really? I ___ — I prefer summer."
quiz.e: To disagree with a positive statement, use normal order: I don't.

quiz.q: You can reply 'Me neither' after…
quiz.e: 'Me neither' agrees with a negative statement; 'Me too' agrees with a positive one.

quiz.q: Which reply correctly agrees with "She has already finished the report"?
quiz.e: Invert after 'so' and match 'has/have' to the new subject 'I': So have I.

situation.uz: Kamola: "I love green tea." Rustam: "So do I. But I can't drink it late at night." Kamola: "Neither can I." — qisqa javoblar suhbatda roziligimizni takrorlamasdan bildiradi.
situation.ru: Kamola: «I love green tea.» Rustam: «So do I. But I can't drink it late at night.» Kamola: «Neither can I.» — короткие ответы выражают согласие без повторения всей фразы.

tip.uz: So'z tartibi — asosiy tuzoq: 'so' va 'neither' dan keyin yordamchi fe'l egadan oldin keladi — So do I, Neither can I. Rozilik uchun 'So I do' demang.
tip.ru: Главная ловушка — порядок слов: после 'so' и 'neither' вспомогательный глагол ставится перед подлежащим — So do I, Neither can I. Для согласия не говорите 'So I do'.

h.uz: Ijobiy gapga qo'shilish: So + yordamchi fe'l + ega
h.ru: Согласие с утверждением: So + вспомогательный глагол + подлежащее

p.uz: Xuddi shu ijobiy narsa sizga ham tegishli ekanini aytish uchun So + yordamchi fe'l + ega ishlatiladi. So'z tartibi teskari: yordamchi fe'l xuddi savoldagidek egadan oldin keladi.
p.ru: Чтобы сказать, что то же положительное верно и для вас, используйте So + вспомогательный глагол + подлежащее. Порядок слов инвертирован: вспомогательный глагол стоит перед подлежащим, как в вопросе.

p.uz: Yordamchi fe'l birinchi gapdagi fe'lga mos bo'lishi kerak: be — be bo'lib qoladi, modal fe'l o'sha modal bo'lib qoladi, present yoki past simple esa do/does/did oladi.
p.ru: Вспомогательный глагол должен совпадать с глаголом первого предложения: be остаётся be, модальный глагол — тем же модальным, а present и past simple берут do/does/did.

h.uz: Inkor gapga qo'shilish: Neither / Nor + yordamchi fe'l + ega
h.ru: Согласие с отрицанием: Neither / Nor + вспомогательный глагол + подлежащее

p.uz: Birinchi gap inkor bo'lsa, Neither (yoki Nor) + yordamchi fe'l + ega bilan qo'shiling. Yordamchi fe'l ijobiy shaklda — inkor ma'nosi 'neither' ichida bor, shuning uchun hech qachon 'Neither can't I' demang.
p.ru: Если первое высказывание отрицательное, соглашайтесь через Neither (или Nor) + вспомогательный глагол + подлежащее. Глагол стоит в положительной форме — отрицание уже заложено в 'neither', поэтому никогда не говорите 'Neither can't I'.

p.uz: Gapda bor yordamchi fe'lni takrorlang: am/is/are, was/were, have/has, will, would, can, could, must. Yordamchi fe'l bo'lmasa — ya'ni present yoki past simple bo'lsa — do, does yoki did oling.
p.ru: Повторяйте тот вспомогательный глагол, который уже есть в предложении: am/is/are, was/were, have/has, will, would, can, could, must. Если его нет — то есть в present или past simple — берите do, does или did.

p.uz: Bu question tags dagi usulning o'zi: 'She has finished, hasn't she?' ni bilsangiz, 'So have I.' ni ham bilasiz.
p.ru: Это тот же приём, что и в question tags: если вы знаете 'She has finished, hasn't she?', то знаете и 'So have I.'

h.uz: Qo'shilmaslik va norasmiy 'Me too / Me neither'
h.ru: Несогласие и разговорные 'Me too / Me neither'

p.uz: Sizda aksincha ekanini aytish uchun oddiy tartibda ega + yordamchi fe'l ishlating: "I love winter." "Really? I don't." / "I can't cook." "Oh, I can."
p.ru: Чтобы сказать, что у вас наоборот, используйте обычный порядок: подлежащее + вспомогательный глагол: «I love winter.» «Really? I don't.» / «I can't cook.» «Oh, I can.»

p.uz: Og'zaki nutqda ijobiy gapdan keyin shunchaki 'Me too', inkor gapdan keyin 'Me neither' deyish mumkin. Ikkalasi ham suhbatda juda keng tarqalgan, lekin rasmiy yozuv uchun juda erkin.
p.ru: В устной речи после утверждения можно просто сказать 'Me too', после отрицания — 'Me neither'. Оба варианта очень частотны в разговоре, но слишком неформальны для официального письма.

quiz.uz: 'love' — present simple, yordamchi fe'l 'do': So do I.
quiz.ru: 'love' — present simple, вспомогательный глагол 'do': So do I.

quiz.uz: 'am' — be fe'li, u takrorlanadi: So am I.
quiz.ru: 'am' — глагол be, он повторяется: So am I.

quiz.uz: 'can' bilan inkor gap → Neither can I.
Past simple da yordamchi fe'l yo'q, 'did' olinadi: So did I.
quiz.ru: В past simple нет вспомогательного глагола, берём 'did': So did I.

quiz.uz: 'never' gapni inkor qiladi; perfect'ning yordamchisi 'have': Neither have I.
quiz.ru: 'never' делает фразу отрицательной; вспомогательный глагол перфекта — 'have': Neither have I.

quiz.uz: 'won't' — inkor → Neither will I ('neither' dan keyin fe'l ijobiy).
quiz.ru: 'won't' — отрицание → Neither will I (после 'neither' глагол положительный).

quiz.uz: Ijobiy gapga qo'shilmaslik uchun oddiy tartib: I don't.
quiz.ru: Чтобы не согласиться с утверждением — обычный порядок: I don't.

quiz.uz: 'Me neither' inkor gapga qo'shiladi; 'Me too' — ijobiy gapga.
quiz.ru: 'Me neither' — согласие с отрицанием; 'Me too' — с утверждением.

quiz.uz: 'so' dan keyin inversiya va yangi ega 'I' ga mos 'have': So have I.
quiz.ru: После 'so' — инверсия, и 'has/have' согласуется с новым подлежащим 'I': So have I.

grammar.title: Phrasal verbs: separable & inseparable
grammar.lead: Turn off, look after, give up — phrasal verbs are everywhere in real English. Learn which ones you can split and where the object goes.

leadTr.uz: Turn off, look after, give up — phrasal verbs jonli ingliz tilida hamma joyda. Qaysilarini bo'lish mumkinligini va to'ldiruvchi qayerga qo'yilishini o'rganing.
leadTr.ru: Turn off, look after, give up — фразовые глаголы встречаются в живом английском повсюду. Узнайте, какие из них можно разделять и куда ставить дополнение.

grammar.situation: Rustam is leaving the office in IT Park: "Can you turn off the lights? And don't forget to hand the report in — Kamola is waiting for it. If any problem comes up, call me."

p: A phrasal verb is a verb plus one or two small words (particles like up, off, on, after) that together create a new meaning. 'Give up' means 'stop trying' — the meaning is not simply 'give' + 'up'.
Because the meaning is often idiomatic, learn each phrasal verb as one piece of vocabulary, with an example sentence.
ex: The meeting was called off. (= cancelled)
Kamola takes after her mother. (= is similar to)
I need to look up this word. (= find in a dictionary)

p: With separable phrasal verbs, a noun object can go after the particle or between the verb and the particle: 'turn off the light' or 'turn the light off' — both are correct.
But when the object is a pronoun (it, them, her…), it MUST go in the middle: 'turn it off', never 'turn off it'. This is the most important rule of the lesson.
ex: Please fill in this form. / Please fill this form in.
She picked up the keys. → She picked them up.
Turn the music down — the baby is sleeping. → Turn it down.

p: Inseparable phrasal verbs never split: the object — noun or pronoun — always comes after the particle. Many verbs of this type describe relationships and situations: look after, get on with, run into, deal with.
ex: Who looks after your little brother? → Who looks after him?
I ran into an old classmate at Chorsu bazaar.
Rustam gets on well with his colleagues.

blocks.h: Three-word phrasal verbs and how to learn them
p: Some phrasal verbs have two particles: look forward to, run out of, put up with, get away with. These are always inseparable — the object follows the whole chain: 'I'm looking forward to the holidays.'
A good dictionary shows separability: 'turn sth off' (separable, sth can move) versus 'look after sb' (inseparable). Record phrasal verbs in that format in your notebook.
ex: We've run out of sugar — can you buy some?
I'm looking forward to your visit. → I'm looking forward to it.
How do you put up with the noise? (= tolerate)

grammar.tip: The pronoun test: if you can say 'verb + it + particle' (turn it off), the verb is separable. If the pronoun must follow the particle (look after it), it is inseparable.
examples: Can you turn the TV off? I'm trying to study.
My grandmother looked after me when I was small.
We're looking forward to the Navruz holidays.

mistakes.x: Please turn off it.
mistakes.v: Please turn it off. — with separable verbs a pronoun object must go between verb and particle

mistakes.x: She looks her nephew after.
mistakes.v: She looks after her nephew. — 'look after' is inseparable and never splits

mistakes.x: I'm looking forward to see you.
mistakes.v: I'm looking forward to seeing you. — here 'to' is a preposition, so the verb takes -ing

quiz.q: Which sentence is correct?
quiz.e: With separable phrasal verbs, a pronoun object goes between the verb and the particle.

quiz.q: 'The concert was called off.' What does 'called off' mean?
quiz.e: 'Call off' means 'cancel'.

quiz.q: Choose the correct sentence with 'look after'.
quiz.e: 'Look after' is inseparable: the object always follows the particle.

quiz.q: We've run ___ milk — I'll buy some on the way home.
quiz.e: 'Run out of something' = have none left.

quiz.q: Which sentence is NOT possible?
quiz.e: 'Fill in' is separable, so a pronoun must go in the middle: fill it in.

quiz.q: I ___ an old friend at the airport yesterday. (= met by chance)
quiz.e: 'Run into somebody' = meet by chance; it is inseparable.

quiz.q: I'm looking forward ___ you again.
quiz.e: In 'look forward to', 'to' is a preposition, so it is followed by -ing.

quiz.q: Kamola ___ her mother — they have the same smile.
quiz.e: 'Take after somebody' = look or behave like an older relative; inseparable.

quiz.q: The music is too loud. Turn ___, please.
quiz.e: 'Turn down' is separable: with a pronoun, say 'turn it down'.

quiz.q: Which shows that 'put up with' cannot be separated?
o: I can't put up with it.
I can't put it up with.
I can't put up it with.
I can't put with it up.
quiz.e: Three-word phrasal verbs are always inseparable: put up with + object.

situation.uz: Rustam IT Parkdagi ofisdan chiqmoqda: "Can you turn off the lights? And don't forget to hand the report in." — phrasal verbs kundalik ish nutqining ajralmas qismi.
situation.ru: Rustam уходит из офиса в IT Park: «Can you turn off the lights? And don't forget to hand the report in.» — фразовые глаголы — неотъемлемая часть повседневной речи.

tip.uz: Olmosh testi: 'verb + it + particle' deb ayta olsangiz (turn it off) — fe'l bo'linadigan (separable). Olmosh particle'dan keyin kelishi shart bo'lsa (look after it) — bo'linmaydigan (inseparable).
tip.ru: Тест с местоимением: если можно сказать 'verb + it + particle' (turn it off) — глагол разделяемый (separable). Если местоимение обязано стоять после частицы (look after it) — неразделяемый (inseparable).

p.uz: Phrasal verb — fe'l va bir yoki ikki kichik so'z (up, off, on, after kabi particle'lar) birikib, yangi ma'no hosil qiladi. 'Give up' — 'urinishni to'xtatish' degani; ma'no oddiygina 'give' + 'up' emas.
p.ru: Фразовый глагол — это глагол плюс одно-два коротких слова (частицы up, off, on, after и т.п.), вместе создающие новое значение. 'Give up' значит 'перестать пытаться' — это не просто 'give' + 'up'.

p.uz: Ma'no ko'pincha idiomatik bo'lgani uchun har bir phrasal verb'ni misol gap bilan alohida lug'at birligi sifatida yodlang.
p.ru: Поскольку значение часто идиоматично, учите каждый фразовый глагол как отдельную лексическую единицу, с примером.

p.uz: Bo'linadigan phrasal verb'larda ot bo'lgan to'ldiruvchi particle'dan keyin ham, fe'l bilan particle orasida ham kela oladi: 'turn off the light' yoki 'turn the light off' — ikkalasi ham to'g'ri.
p.ru: У разделяемых глаголов дополнение-существительное может стоять после частицы или между глаголом и частицей: 'turn off the light' и 'turn the light off' — оба варианта верны.

p.uz: Lekin to'ldiruvchi olmosh bo'lsa (it, them, her…), u ALBATTA o'rtada turadi: 'turn it off', hech qachon 'turn off it' emas. Bu darsning eng muhim qoidasi.
p.ru: Но если дополнение — местоимение (it, them, her…), оно ОБЯЗАНО стоять в середине: 'turn it off', и никогда 'turn off it'. Это главное правило урока.

p.uz: Bo'linmaydigan phrasal verb'lar hech qachon ajralmaydi: to'ldiruvchi — ot ham, olmosh ham — doim particle'dan keyin keladi. Bu turdagi ko'p fe'llar munosabat va vaziyatlarni bildiradi: look after, get on with, run into, deal with.
p.ru: Неразделяемые глаголы никогда не расщепляются: дополнение — и существительное, и местоимение — всегда идёт после частицы. Многие такие глаголы описывают отношения и ситуации: look after, get on with, run into, deal with.

h.uz: Uch so'zli phrasal verbs va ularni o'rganish
h.ru: Трёхсловные фразовые глаголы и как их учить

p.uz: Ba'zi phrasal verb'larda ikkita particle bor: look forward to, run out of, put up with, get away with. Ular doim bo'linmaydi — to'ldiruvchi butun zanjirdan keyin keladi: 'I'm looking forward to the holidays.'
p.ru: У некоторых глаголов две частицы: look forward to, run out of, put up with, get away with. Они всегда неразделяемы — дополнение идёт после всей цепочки: 'I'm looking forward to the holidays.'

p.uz: Yaxshi lug'at bo'linishni ko'rsatadi: 'turn sth off' (bo'linadigan, sth joyini o'zgartira oladi) va 'look after sb' (bo'linmaydigan). Daftaringizga phrasal verb'larni shu formatda yozing.
p.ru: Хороший словарь показывает разделяемость: 'turn sth off' (разделяемый, sth может перемещаться) против 'look after sb' (неразделяемый). Записывайте фразовые глаголы в тетрадь именно в этом формате.

quiz.uz: Bo'linadigan phrasal verb'da olmosh fe'l bilan particle orasida turadi: turn it off.
quiz.ru: У разделяемого глагола местоимение стоит между глаголом и частицей: turn it off.

quiz.uz: 'Look after' bo'linmaydi: to'ldiruvchi doim particle'dan keyin.
quiz.ru: 'Look after' неразделяем: дополнение всегда после частицы.

quiz.uz: 'Fill in' bo'linadigan, shuning uchun olmosh o'rtada bo'lishi kerak: fill it in.
quiz.ru: 'Fill in' разделяемый, поэтому местоимение должно стоять в середине: fill it in.

quiz.uz: 'Look forward to' dagi 'to' — predlog, undan keyin -ing keladi.
quiz.ru: В 'look forward to' 'to' — предлог, после него идёт -ing.

quiz.uz: 'Take after somebody' — kattaroq qarindoshga o'xshamoq; bo'linmaydi.
quiz.ru: 'Take after somebody' — быть похожим на старшего родственника; неразделяемый.

quiz.uz: 'Turn down' bo'linadigan: olmosh bilan 'turn it down'.
quiz.ru: 'Turn down' разделяемый: с местоимением — 'turn it down'.

quiz.uz: Uch so'zli phrasal verb'lar doim bo'linmaydi: put up with + to'ldiruvchi.
quiz.ru: Трёхсловные фразовые глаголы всегда неразделяемы: put up with + дополнение.

grammar.title: Indirect questions
grammar.lead: 'Could you tell me where the station is?' Indirect questions make you sound polite and professional — but they follow surprising word-order rules.

leadTr.uz: 'Could you tell me where the station is?' Bilvosita savollar sizni muloyim va professional qilib ko'rsatadi — lekin ularda kutilmagan so'z tartibi qoidalari bor.
leadTr.ru: 'Could you tell me where the station is?' Косвенные вопросы делают речь вежливой и профессиональной — но в них действуют неожиданные правила порядка слов.

grammar.situation: A tourist in Tashkent: "Excuse me, could you tell me where the metro station is?" Kamola: "Of course — it's just around the corner. Do you know which line you need?"

p: A direct question — 'Where is the bank?' — can sound abrupt, especially with strangers. Wrapping it in a polite opener softens it: 'Could you tell me where the bank is?', 'Do you know what time the museum opens?'
Common openers: Could you tell me…, Do you know…, I wonder…, I'd like to know…, Can you remember…, Have you any idea….
ex: Could you tell me where the ticket office is?
Do you know when the next train to Samarkand leaves?
I wonder why the flight was delayed.

blocks.h: The key rule: statement word order
p: Inside an indirect question, use statement order — subject before verb — and drop the auxiliary do/does/did completely. Direct: 'Where does Rustam work?' → Indirect: 'Do you know where Rustam works?'
With the verb be, the subject moves in front of it: 'Where is the station?' → '…where the station is.'
ex: What time does the shop close? → Could you tell me what time the shop closes?
Why did she leave? → I don't know why she left.
How much is this carpet? → Can you tell me how much this carpet is?

p: When the direct question has no question word (Is it…? Does he…? Did they…?), introduce the indirect version with if or whether. 'Does this bus go to Chilonzor?' → 'Do you know if this bus goes to Chilonzor?'
'Whether' is slightly more formal and is preferred before 'or not': 'I don't know whether or not to apply.'
ex: Is the office open on Saturdays? → Do you know if the office is open on Saturdays?
Did Kamola get the job? → I wonder whether Kamola got the job.
Can I pay by card? → Could you tell me if I can pay by card?

p: If the opener itself is a question (Could you tell me…? Do you know…?), the whole sentence ends with a question mark. If the opener is a statement (I wonder…, I don't know…, I'd like to know…), it ends with a full stop, even though a question hides inside.
ex: Do you know where he lives?
I don't know where he lives.
I wonder if the report is ready.

grammar.tip: One change, one rule: after the opener, turn the question back into a statement — subject + verb, no do/does/did. 'Where does she live?' → '…where she lives.'
examples: Could you tell me how I can get to Registan Square?
Do you know if the IT Park cafeteria is still open?
I'd like to know why the meeting was cancelled.

mistakes.x: Could you tell me where is the station?
mistakes.v: Could you tell me where the station is? — statement order after the question word

mistakes.x: Do you know what time does the bank open?
mistakes.v: Do you know what time the bank opens? — drop 'does' and add -s to the verb

mistakes.x: I wonder that he is at home.
mistakes.v: I wonder if/whether he is at home. — yes/no questions need if or whether, not 'that'

quiz.q: Could you tell me where ___?
quiz.e: Indirect questions use statement order: subject + verb.

quiz.q: Do you know what time ___?
quiz.e: Drop 'does' and put the verb after the subject: the shop closes.

quiz.q: Direct: 'Does this bus go to the airport?' → Do you know ___ this bus goes to the airport?
quiz.e: Yes/no questions become indirect with if or whether.

quiz.q: I wonder why ___ the meeting.
quiz.e: No 'did' inside an indirect question — the verb takes the past form: she missed.

quiz.q: Which sentence is correct?
o: Do you know where does Rustam work?
Do you know where Rustam works?
Do you know where works Rustam?
Do you know where Rustam does work?
quiz.e: Statement order and no 'does': where Rustam works.

quiz.q: Which opener needs a full stop, not a question mark?
quiz.e: 'I'd like to know…' is a statement, so the sentence ends with a full stop.

quiz.q: 'Is Kamola at the office?' → I'm not sure ___ at the office.
quiz.e: Yes/no question → if/whether + statement order: whether Kamola is.

quiz.q: Choose the most natural polite question to a stranger.
o: Tell me where the metro is.
Could you tell me where the metro is?
You know where is the metro?
quiz.e: 'Could you tell me…?' plus statement order is the polite pattern.

quiz.q: 'How much did the tickets cost?' → Can you remember how much ___?
quiz.e: Remove 'did'; past simple stays on the main verb: the tickets cost (past).

quiz.q: I don't know whether ___ to accept the offer.
quiz.e: 'Whether or not' is the standard combination; 'if or not' is not used directly like this.

situation.uz: Toshkentdagi sayyoh: "Excuse me, could you tell me where the metro station is?" — bilvosita savol notanish kishiga murojaatni muloyim qiladi.
situation.ru: Турист в Ташкенте: «Excuse me, could you tell me where the metro station is?» — косвенный вопрос делает обращение к незнакомцу вежливым.

tip.uz: Bitta o'zgarish, bitta qoida: kirish iboradan keyin savolni yana darak gapga aylantiring — ega + fe'l, do/does/did yo'q. 'Where does she live?' → '…where she lives.'
tip.ru: Одно изменение, одно правило: после вводной фразы превратите вопрос обратно в утверждение — подлежащее + глагол, без do/does/did. 'Where does she live?' → '…where she lives.'

p.uz: To'g'ridan-to'g'ri savol — 'Where is the bank?' — ayniqsa notanishlarga qo'pol eshitilishi mumkin. Muloyim kirish ibora uni yumshatadi: 'Could you tell me where the bank is?', 'Do you know what time the museum opens?'
p.ru: Прямой вопрос — 'Where is the bank?' — может звучать резко, особенно с незнакомыми людьми. Вежливая вводная фраза смягчает его: 'Could you tell me where the bank is?', 'Do you know what time the museum opens?'

p.uz: Keng tarqalgan kirish iboralar: Could you tell me…, Do you know…, I wonder…, I'd like to know…, Can you remember…, Have you any idea….
p.ru: Частые вводные фразы: Could you tell me…, Do you know…, I wonder…, I'd like to know…, Can you remember…, Have you any idea….

p.uz: Bilvosita savol ichida darak gap tartibi ishlatiladi — ega fe'ldan oldin — va do/does/did butunlay tushib qoladi. To'g'ridan-to'g'ri: 'Where does Rustam work?' → Bilvosita: 'Do you know where Rustam works?'
p.ru: Внутри косвенного вопроса используется порядок утверждения — подлежащее перед глаголом — а do/does/did полностью исчезает. Прямой: 'Where does Rustam work?' → Косвенный: 'Do you know where Rustam works?'

p.uz: Be fe'li bilan ega uning oldiga o'tadi: 'Where is the station?' → '…where the station is.'
p.ru: С глаголом be подлежащее ставится перед ним: 'Where is the station?' → '…where the station is.'

p.uz: To'g'ridan-to'g'ri savolda so'roq so'zi bo'lmasa (Is it…? Does he…? Did they…?), bilvosita variant if yoki whether bilan boshlanadi. 'Does this bus go to Chilonzor?' → 'Do you know if this bus goes to Chilonzor?'
p.ru: Если в прямом вопросе нет вопросительного слова (Is it…? Does he…? Did they…?), косвенный вариант вводится через if или whether. 'Does this bus go to Chilonzor?' → 'Do you know if this bus goes to Chilonzor?'

p.uz: 'Whether' biroz rasmiyroq va 'or not' oldidan afzal ko'riladi: 'I don't know whether or not to apply.'
p.ru: 'Whether' чуть формальнее и предпочтителен перед 'or not': 'I don't know whether or not to apply.'

p.uz: Kirish iboraning o'zi savol bo'lsa (Could you tell me…? Do you know…?), butun gap so'roq belgisi bilan tugaydi. Kirish ibora darak gap bo'lsa (I wonder…, I don't know…, I'd like to know…), ichida savol yashiringan bo'lsa ham, gap nuqta bilan tugaydi.
p.ru: Если вводная фраза сама — вопрос (Could you tell me…? Do you know…?), всё предложение заканчивается вопросительным знаком. Если вводная фраза — утверждение (I wonder…, I don't know…, I'd like to know…), предложение заканчивается точкой, хотя внутри спрятан вопрос.

quiz.uz: Bilvosita savolda darak gap tartibi: ega + fe'l.
quiz.ru: В косвенном вопросе — порядок утверждения: подлежащее + глагол.

quiz.uz: 'does' tushib qoladi, fe'l egadan keyin keladi: the shop closes.
quiz.ru: 'does' убирается, глагол идёт после подлежащего: the shop closes.

quiz.uz: Ha/yo'q savollari bilvosita shaklda if yoki whether oladi.
quiz.ru: Вопросы да/нет в косвенной форме вводятся через if или whether.

quiz.uz: Bilvosita savol ichida 'did' yo'q — fe'l o'tgan zamon shaklini oladi: she missed.
quiz.ru: Внутри косвенного вопроса нет 'did' — глагол в прошедшей форме: she missed.

quiz.uz: Darak tartibi va 'does'siz: where Rustam works.
quiz.ru: Порядок утверждения и без 'does': where Rustam works.

quiz.uz: 'I'd like to know…' — darak gap, shuning uchun gap nuqta bilan tugaydi.

reading.title: A Change of Career
reading.text:
For ten years, Daniel had worked as an accountant in a busy office in Birmingham. The salary was good, but he had never really enjoyed the job. He often felt bored, and by the end of each week he was exhausted.
Last year, everything changed. While he was helping a friend repair an old house, he realised how much he loved working with his hands. After a few months, he made a brave decision: he resigned from his job and started training as a carpenter.
Now Daniel earns less money than before, but he is much happier. He says he should have changed careers years ago. 'If I had known how good it would feel,' he says, 'I would have done it sooner.'

quiz.q: What was Daniel's first job?
quiz.e: He had worked as an accountant.

quiz.q: How did he usually feel at work?
quiz.e: He felt bored and exhausted.

quiz.q: What made him realise he wanted a change?
o: helping a friend repair a house
quiz.e: He discovered he loved working with his hands.

quiz.q: How does his salary now compare?
quiz.e: He earns less money than before.

quiz.q: How does Daniel feel about the change?
quiz.e: He is much happier and wishes he'd done it sooner.

reading.title: Living Abroad
reading.text:
When Sophie moved from Bristol to Spain, she expected the first few months to be easy. She had visited the country several times on holiday and had always loved the weather and the food. However, living abroad turned out to be very different from visiting.
At first, she found everyday tasks difficult. Simple things, such as opening a bank account or going to the doctor, were stressful because of the language. She often felt lonely and missed her family.
Gradually, things improved. She joined a local Spanish class, where she met other newcomers, and slowly she began to make friends. After a year, she felt completely at home. 'Moving abroad was the hardest thing I have ever done,' she says, 'but also the best.'

quiz.q: Why did Sophie think living in Spain would be easy?
o: She had visited on holiday and loved it.
quiz.e: She had visited and loved the weather and food.

quiz.q: What made everyday tasks hard at first?
quiz.e: The language made simple tasks stressful.

quiz.q: How did she feel in the early months?
quiz.e: She felt lonely and missed her family.

quiz.q: How did she start to make friends?
quiz.e: She met newcomers at a local Spanish class.

quiz.q: What is her overall opinion of moving abroad?
o: It was the hardest but best thing.
quiz.e: The hardest thing she'd done, but also the best.

quizTr.uz: Bu u qilgan eng qiyin, lekin eng yaxshi ish edi.

reading.title: The Power of Habit
reading.text:
Most of us would like to change something about our lives — to exercise more, eat better, or waste less time. Yet good intentions are rarely enough. Research suggests that the secret to lasting change is not willpower, but habit.
A habit is an action we repeat so often that it becomes automatic. Once a behaviour becomes a habit, we no longer have to think about it or force ourselves to do it. The difficulty, of course, is building the habit in the first place.
Experts recommend starting small. Instead of promising to run for an hour every day, you might begin with just ten minutes. It is also helpful to attach a new habit to an existing one — for example, doing a few exercises straight after brushing your teeth. If you keep the goal small and repeat it daily, it will eventually feel natural.

quiz.q: According to the text, what is the secret to lasting change?
quiz.e: The text says habit, not willpower.

quiz.q: What is a habit?
quiz.e: A habit is a repeated, automatic action.

quiz.q: Why are habits useful?
o: We no longer have to force ourselves.
quiz.e: Once automatic, no effort is needed.

quiz.q: What do experts recommend?
quiz.e: Start small, e.g. ten minutes.

quiz.q: What trick helps build a new habit?
o: attaching it to an existing habit
quiz.e: Attach the new habit to an existing one.

reading.title: A Letter of Complaint
reading.text:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to complain about a jacket I bought from your online shop on 3 May (order number 4471).

When the jacket arrived, I was very disappointed. Although the website described it as dark blue, the jacket I received was clearly black. Furthermore, there was a small hole in one of the pockets, which suggests it had not been checked properly before being sent.

I have been a regular customer for several years and have never had a problem before. However, on this occasion I am not satisfied with the quality of the product or the service.

I would therefore like a full refund. I have attached a photograph of the jacket as evidence. I look forward to hearing from you within seven days.

Yours faithfully,
J. Harris

quiz.e: It is a letter of complaint about a jacket.

o: It was black, not dark blue.
quiz.e: It was black instead of dark blue.

quiz.q: What does the customer want?
quiz.e: They request a full refund.

quiz.q: What did the customer attach as evidence?
quiz.e: A photograph of the jacket.

reading.title: The Interview
reading.text:
Emily had prepared for weeks. She had researched the company, practised her answers, and chosen her clothes carefully the night before. By the time the morning arrived, she felt ready — or so she thought.
The trouble began on the way there. Her train was cancelled, and by the time she found another, she was already running late. When she finally reached the office in Manchester, she was twenty minutes behind and out of breath.
To her surprise, the manager was understanding. He explained that one of his own interviews, years earlier, had gone badly for similar reasons, and he had still been offered the job. The interview went well, and Emily relaxed.
A week later, an email arrived. She had got the job. Looking back, she realised that the disaster on the way had actually helped: it had shown the manager how she behaved under pressure.

quiz.q: How had Emily prepared for the interview?
o: She researched, practised and chose clothes.
quiz.e: She researched, practised answers and chose clothes.

quiz.q: Why was she late?
quiz.e: Her train was cancelled.

quiz.q: How did the manager react to her lateness?
quiz.e: He was understanding and shared his own story.

quiz.q: What was the result?
quiz.e: A week later she got the job.

quiz.q: Why does she think the difficult journey helped?
o: It showed how she behaves under pressure.
quiz.e: It showed the manager how she handled pressure.
