reading.title: The Silk Road, Then and Now
reading.text:
For almost two thousand years, the cities of Samarkand, Bukhara and Khiva stood at the heart of the Silk Road — the network of trade routes that connected China with Europe. Caravans carried silk, paper, spices and glass, but historians argue that the most valuable cargo was invisible: ideas. Mathematics, medicine, religions and even recipes travelled with the merchants, which is why the region produced scholars like Al-Khwarizmi, whose name gave us the word 'algorithm'.

The caravans disappeared centuries ago, yet the idea of the Silk Road is having a second life. High-speed trains now link Tashkent and Samarkand in just over two hours, and container trains from China cross Central Asia on their way to European markets. Tourism is growing even faster: visitors who once knew Uzbekistan only from history books now walk through Registan Square with audio guides in a dozen languages. The challenge, locals say, is to welcome the world without turning living cities into museums. A trader from the old bazaar put it simply: 'Our ancestors sold silk to strangers. We sell them memories — but we still live here.'

quiz.q: According to historians, what was the most valuable cargo on the Silk Road?
quiz.e: Historians argue the most valuable cargo was invisible: ideas.

quiz.q: Why is Al-Khwarizmi mentioned?
o: He shows how the region produced great scholars
quiz.e: He is an example of the scholars the region produced — his name gave us 'algorithm'.

quiz.q: What does 'a second life' refer to?
o: The modern revival of Silk Road connections
A famous book about the region
The reopening of the old bazaar
quiz.e: Modern trains, trade and tourism are reviving the idea of the Silk Road.

quiz.q: What is the locals' main concern about tourism?
o: Cities could become museums instead of living places
quiz.e: The challenge is to welcome the world without turning living cities into museums.

quizTr.uz: Tarixchilar fikricha, eng qimmatli yuk ko'rinmas edi: g'oyalar.
quizTr.ru: По мнению историков, самым ценным грузом были невидимые вещи: идеи.

quizTr.uz: U mintaqa yetishtirgan olimlarga misol — uning nomidan 'algoritm' so'zi kelib chiqqan.
quizTr.ru: Он пример учёных региона — от его имени произошло слово «алгоритм».

quizTr.uz: Zamonaviy poyezdlar, savdo va turizm Ipak yo'li g'oyasini qayta jonlantirmoqda.
quizTr.ru: Современные поезда, торговля и туризм возрождают идею Шёлкового пути.

quizTr.uz: Muammo — dunyoni kutib olishda jonli shaharlarni muzeyga aylantirib qo'ymaslik.
quizTr.ru: Задача — принимать мир, не превращая живые города в музеи.

reading.title: Main Idea & Central Claim
reading.text:
The MAIN IDEA is the most important argument the author makes — not just a topic, but a CLAIM about that topic. Exam questions ask: 'Which choice best states the main idea?' or 'Which most accurately states the central claim?' The correct answer must cover the ENTIRE passage, not just one part of it.

Three wrong-answer traps: (1) TOO NARROW — mentions one specific detail but misses the bigger point. (2) TOO BROAD — goes beyond what the passage actually says. (3) DISTORTED — uses passage words but changes or reverses the meaning. After reading, ask: 'What is the author arguing about this topic from start to finish?'

For CENTRAL CLAIM questions the correct answer is almost always a complete argument: [Topic] + [What the author says about it]. Practice converting each passage into a one-sentence argument before looking at the choices. This prevents the common error of choosing an answer that is true but partial.

Key points:
• Main idea = Topic + Claim (not just the topic alone)
• Correct answer covers the WHOLE passage
• Too narrow = only mentions one detail from the passage
• Too broad = adds information not in the passage
• Distorted = changes or reverses the author's meaning
• Test: 'Would the author agree with this statement throughout the text?'
• Eliminate: any answer requiring information NOT stated in the passage

quiz.q:
Passage: 'Recent studies on urban green spaces reveal a striking pattern: cities with more parks and tree cover show measurably lower rates of anxiety and depression among residents. Researchers attribute this not to physical activity alone, but to the restorative psychological effects of encountering natural environments within urban settings.'

Which choice best states the main idea?
o: Urban parks are increasingly popular in modern cities
Studies show urban green spaces reduce anxiety and depression by providing psychological restoration, not just physical activity
Cities with more trees are better places to live than cities with fewer trees
Researchers are currently studying the mental health effects of urban environments
quiz.e: B captures both elements. A is just a topic. C overstates. D only describes what researchers are doing.

quiz.q:
Passage: 'Factory farming enables low meat prices but imposes heavy costs: antibiotic overuse accelerates drug resistance, concentrated waste contaminates waterways, and the conditions of confinement have been linked to increased disease transmission risk. These costs are largely externalized — borne by the public rather than the industry — which means market prices dramatically understate the true social cost of cheap meat.'

Which best states the central claim?
o: Factory farming uses antibiotics that contribute to drug-resistant bacteria
Factory farming's low prices hide substantial social and environmental costs that are not reflected in market prices
Factory farming is the primary cause of waterway contamination in rural areas
The conditions of factory farms increase the risk of disease outbreaks
quiz.e: A, C, and D are each one specific detail used as supporting evidence — all three are too narrow. The passage's main claim is the externalization point, not any single harm.

quiz.q:
Passage: 'Psychologist Carol Dweck's research on 'growth mindset' has been widely adopted in education. However, subsequent attempts to replicate her foundational studies have produced mixed results, and large-scale interventions based on her work have shown smaller effects in real classrooms than in laboratory conditions. The gap between a compelling psychological idea and a reliable educational intervention is wider than early enthusiasm suggested.'

Which choice best states the central claim?
o: Carol Dweck's growth mindset research has been completely debunked by subsequent studies
Growth mindset theory, while influential, has not translated into reliably large educational effects in real-world applications
The growth mindset approach should be abandoned in favor of more evidence-based educational methods
Large-scale educational interventions are generally ineffective compared to laboratory studies
quiz.e: A is a distortion (the passage says 'mixed results,' not 'completely debunked'). C is a recommendation not stated. D overgeneralizes beyond the scope of the passage.

quiz.q:
Passage: 'The human microbiome — the community of microorganisms living in and on the body — contains roughly as many cells as the human body itself. For decades, these microbes were regarded as passengers with minimal impact. Research over the past twenty years has overturned this view: gut bacteria regulate immune function, influence mood through the gut-brain axis, and may determine susceptibility to conditions ranging from obesity to depression.'

Which best states the main idea?
o: The human body contains a large number of microorganisms
Recent research has transformed our understanding of the microbiome from a passive presence to an active regulator of multiple body systems
Gut bacteria affect mood through a connection between the gut and the brain
Scientists have studied microorganisms in the human body for over twenty years
quiz.e: A is too broad (just says microbes exist). C is one specific finding. D misrepresents the timing (20 years of new research, not study of microbiomes).

quiz.q:
Passage: 'Most people assume that eyewitness testimony is highly reliable — after all, the witness was there. Decades of cognitive psychology research tells a different story. Human memory is reconstructive rather than reproductive: each retrieval of a memory rebuilds it from partial information, making it susceptible to distortion by subsequent events, leading questions, and unconscious expectation. These findings have led to documented wrongful convictions and major reforms in how law enforcement conducts witness interviews.'

Which best states the central claim?
o: Most people incorrectly believe that eyewitness testimony is reliable
Cognitive psychology research has demonstrated that memory's reconstructive nature makes eyewitness testimony less reliable than commonly assumed, with serious legal consequences
Leading questions during police interviews are the main cause of wrongful convictions
Human memory works differently than most people assume, which creates problems in daily life
quiz.e: A only states the assumption. C is one specific mechanism. D is too vague about what the 'problems' are.

quizTr.uz: B ikkala elementni ham qamrab oladi: A shunchaki mavzu, C bo'rttiradi, D esa faqat tadqiqotchilar nima qilayotganini tasvirlaydi.
quizTr.ru: B охватывает оба элемента: A — лишь тема, C преувеличивает, D лишь описывает работу исследователей.

quizTr.uz: A, C va D — dalil sifatida keltirilgan alohida detallar bo'lib, juda tor; asosiy da'vo xarajatlarning jamiyatga yuklanishi haqida.
quizTr.ru: A, C и D — отдельные детали-доказательства и слишком узки; главный тезис — о перекладывании издержек на общество.

quizTr.uz: A buzib talqin qiladi (matnda 'mixed results', butunlay rad etilgani emas), C matnda yo'q tavsiya, D esa haddan tashqari umumlashtiradi.
quizTr.ru: A искажает (в тексте «mixed results», а не полное опровержение), C — не заявленная рекомендация, D чрезмерно обобщает.

quizTr.uz: A juda keng (mikroblar borligini aytadi xolos), C bitta aniq topilma, D esa vaqtni noto'g'ri talqin qiladi.
quizTr.ru: A слишком широк (лишь констатирует существование микробов), C — одна конкретная находка, D неверно передаёт сроки.

quizTr.uz: A faqat taxminni bayon qiladi, C bitta aniq mexanizm, D esa 'muammolar' nimadaligini juda noaniq qoldiradi.
quizTr.ru: A лишь называет допущение, C — один конкретный механизм, D слишком расплывчато говорит о «проблемах».

reading.title: Purpose of Sentences & Textual Evidence
reading.text:
PURPOSE questions ask WHY the author includes something — a sentence, detail, or example. The stem is: 'What function does the underlined sentence serve?' or 'Why does the author include the example of X?' These require thinking about structure and argumentation, not just content.

Four common purposes: (1) INTRODUCE — sets up the main argument. (2) SUPPORT — provides evidence for a claim already made. (3) COUNTER — presents an opposing view the author will or has refuted. (4) CONCLUDE — synthesizes the argument. The sentence's position in the paragraph is a strong clue: first = often introduce; last = often conclude; middle = usually support or counter.

TEXTUAL EVIDENCE questions give you a claim and ask which quote from the passage best supports it. The key technique: the evidence must DIRECTLY support the specific claim stated — not just be on the same topic. Wrong answers are often on the correct topic but support a slightly different claim.

Key points:
• Purpose = WHY the author includes it (not WHAT it says)
• First sentence of paragraph → often introduces the topic/claim
• Last sentence → often concludes or extends the argument
• Middle sentences → often support or present counterarguments
• Counter-argument signals: however, although, despite, yet, while
• Evidence must DIRECTLY support the specific claim given
• Wrong answer trap: correct topic, wrong specific claim

quiz.q:
Passage: '[Sentence A: Between 2000 and 2020, more languages became extinct than in any comparable period in recorded history.] Most of these disappearances occurred without documentation, meaning the grammatical structures, vocabulary, and embedded cultural knowledge those languages contained vanished entirely. Linguists now regard language death as a crisis comparable in magnitude to biodiversity loss.'

What function does Sentence A serve?
o: It introduces the topic of extinct languages
It provides a statistic that establishes the urgency and scale of language extinction to motivate the argument that follows
It counters the claim that language extinction is a natural process
It concludes the argument by showing the historical scale of the problem
quiz.e: B is correct. A is vague (all sentences 'introduce' something). C inverts the function. D is wrong — it's the opening, not conclusion.

quiz.q:
Passage: 'Defenders of social media argue that it has democratized public discourse by giving ordinary people a platform previously available only to those with access to established media. [Sentence X: A 2023 study found that 95% of viral political content on one major platform was produced by accounts with fewer than 1,000 followers.] However, critics note that amplification algorithms primarily boost emotionally provocative content regardless of accuracy.'

Sentence X primarily functions to
o: Introduce a new argument about the dangers of social media algorithms
Provide evidence supporting the democratization argument made before it
Counter the critics' argument about algorithm-driven amplification
Conclude the passage by showing that ordinary users dominate political content
quiz.e: B correctly identifies this supporting function. A is wrong — the sentence doesn't introduce a new argument. C is wrong — the 'however' and critics' argument come after Sentence X. D is wrong — it's not a conclusion.

quiz.q:
Passage: 'In 1847, Ignaz Semmelweis demonstrated that handwashing by doctors dramatically reduced maternal deaths from childbed fever. His evidence was statistically compelling, yet his colleagues dismissed his findings and continued practices that killed patients. Semmelweis was eventually committed to an asylum, where he died — ironically, from an infection. [Final sentence: His story remains a cautionary example of how institutional resistance can delay the adoption of lifesaving knowledge even when the evidence is clear.]'

What function does the final sentence serve?
o: It provides a biographical detail about Semmelweis's death
It introduces a new argument about medical institutions
It extends the historical example into a general principle about the relationship between evidence and institutional adoption
It contradicts the claim that Semmelweis's findings were dismissed by colleagues
quiz.e: C captures this 'specific to general' concluding function. A only describes part of the final sentence's content. B is wrong — no new argument is introduced. D contradicts the passage.

quizTr.uz: B to'g'ri: A juda noaniq (har qanday jumla nimanidir 'kiritadi'), C funksiyani teskari talqin qiladi, D xato — bu xulosa emas, kirish jumlasi.
quizTr.ru: B верен: A расплывчат (любое предложение что-то «вводит»), C переворачивает функцию, D неверен — это начало, а не вывод.

quizTr.uz: B qo'llab-quvvatlash funksiyasini to'g'ri aniqlaydi: jumla yangi argument kiritmaydi, tanqid undan keyin keladi va u xulosa ham emas.
quizTr.ru: B верно определяет поддерживающую функцию: предложение не вводит новый аргумент, возражение идёт после него, и это не вывод.

quizTr.uz: C 'xususiydan umumiyga' yakunlovchi funksiyani ifodalaydi: A faqat bir qismini tasvirlaydi, B da yangi argument yo'q, D matnga zid.
quizTr.ru: C передаёт заключительный ход «от частного к общему»: A описывает лишь часть, B — новый аргумент не вводится, D противоречит тексту.

reading.title: Evaluating Relevance & Completing the Study
reading.text:
A specialized exam question type presents a student's research claim and a table or description of data, then asks which additional piece of information the student would need to COMPLETE or SUPPORT their argument. These questions test your ability to identify what is MISSING from an argument — what logical gap needs to be filled. The key skill: identify exactly what the claim is saying and determine which piece of evidence addresses the specific gap.

For COMPLETING THE RESEARCH questions: (1) Read the student's claim carefully and identify the exact assertion being made. (2) Ask: 'What would I need to KNOW to be convinced this claim is true?' (3) Look for the answer choice that provides exactly that missing information. Common wrong answers: information that CONFIRMS something already established rather than something missing; information about a RELATED topic that doesn't address the gap; information that would UNDERMINE the claim rather than support it.

For EVALUATING RELEVANCE: every supporting detail in a passage must connect to the main argument being made. When you are asked which detail is LEAST relevant or which detail does NOT support the argument, look for the answer choice that introduces a fact that, even if true, does not logically contribute to the author's main point. The irrelevant detail is often interesting and true — its irrelevance is logical, not factual.

Key points:
• Completing research: find what is MISSING from the argument
• Ask: 'What would I need to know to be convinced this claim is true?'
• Wrong answer: confirms something ALREADY established
• Wrong answer: related topic that doesn't fill the specific gap
• Evaluating relevance: irrelevant = logically unconnected to main argument
• True and interesting ≠ relevant (exam tests logical connection, not interestingness)
• The missing piece must address the EXACT assertion in the claim

quiz.q:
A student claims: 'The ancient city of Pompeii was not unique in being buried by a volcanic eruption — other Roman cities were similarly affected by the 79 CE eruption of Vesuvius.'

The student has documented that Pompeii was buried by ash in 79 CE. What evidence most directly supports the broader claim about other cities?
o: Historical records documenting that the cities of Herculaneum and Stabiae were also buried or damaged by the same 79 CE eruption
Archaeological evidence of the artistic and architectural features of Pompeii before the eruption
Scientific data on the temperature and composition of pyroclastic flows from the 79 CE eruption
Records of Pliny the Younger's eyewitness account of the eruption
quiz.e: The student has Pompeii data but lacks evidence about OTHER cities. A provides exactly this: Herculaneum and Stabiae (other cities) were also buried. B is about Pompeii's features (already documented). C is about the eruption's physics (not about other cities). D is an eyewitness account (doesn't prove other cities were buried).

quiz.q:
A researcher claims: 'Students who take handwritten notes learn material more deeply than those who type notes.' The researcher has data showing handwriters score higher on exams.

Which concern most undermines the causal claim?
o: The study did not specify what subject matter students were tested on
Students who choose to handwrite may already be more academically motivated, making it unclear whether handwriting itself caused the higher scores
The study did not measure how long students spent reviewing their notes
The exams used multiple-choice questions rather than essay questions
quiz.e: Students who choose handwriting may differ from typers in motivation, learning style, or prior academic performance — making it unclear whether handwriting CAUSED the higher scores or whether more motivated students happen to handwrite. B identifies this critical confound. A, C, and D are methodological concerns but not the fundamental confound.

quiz.q:
A student writes: 'The decline of coral reefs is not uniform — some regions are experiencing faster loss than others, which has important implications for conservation priorities.'

The student has data on reef health in the Caribbean and Indo-Pacific. What additional data most directly strengthens the argument about conservation prioritization?
o: Data on the total area of coral reefs globally
Evidence showing which reefs have the highest biodiversity and the slowest current decline rate, suggesting they are most worth protecting
Historical records of reef health from the 19th century
Data on the economic value of reef tourism in different regions
quiz.e: The student needs to know not just WHERE decline is fastest but which reefs have the most to save (high biodiversity) and the best chance of surviving (slowest decline). B directly provides the basis for prioritization. A is about total area. C is historical baseline (useful but doesn't help prioritize current action). D is about economic value (relevant but less directly tied to conservation biology priorities).

quizTr.uz: Talabada Pompeii ma'lumotlari bor, lekin BOSHQA shaharlar haqida dalil yo'q — A aynan shuni beradi: Herculaneum va Stabiae ham ko'milgan.
quizTr.ru: У студента есть данные о Pompeii, но нет о ДРУГИХ городах — A даёт именно это: Herculaneum и Stabiae тоже были погребены.

quizTr.uz: Qo'lda yozishni tanlagan o'quvchilar motivatsiyasi bilan farq qilishi mumkin, shuning uchun sabab noaniq — B aynan shu asosiy chalkashtiruvchi omilni ko'rsatadi.
quizTr.ru: Выбравшие рукописный конспект могут изначально отличаться мотивацией, поэтому причина неясна — B указывает именно на этот ключевой искажающий фактор.

quizTr.uz: Ustuvorlik uchun qaysi riflar eng boy (yuqori bioxilma-xillik) va omon qolish imkoni eng katta (eng sekin yemirilish) ekanini bilish kerak — B aynan shu asosni beradi.
quizTr.ru: Для приоритизации нужно знать, какие рифы самые богатые (биоразнообразие) и с лучшими шансами выжить (медленный спад) — B даёт именно эту основу.

Could you let me know by Friday if you accept? Yes, of course. Thank you so much. Great. We'll send you the contract by email. Goodbye.

listening.title: A Volunteer's Story
listening.script: Today on the programme we're talking to Tom, who volunteers at a city food bank. Tom, how did you start? Well, I lost my own job two years ago and a charity helped me through a hard time. When I got back on my feet, I wanted to give something back, so I started volunteering. What do you actually do? I help collect food from supermarkets and pack it for families in need. I work about two days a week. Is it rewarding? Absolutely. The best part is meeting people and knowing you've made a real difference. I'd encourage anyone with free time to try it.

quiz.q: Where does Tom volunteer?
quiz.e: He volunteers at a city food bank.

quiz.q: Why did he start volunteering?
quiz.e: A charity helped him, so he wanted to give back.

listening.title: A Local News Report
listening.script: And now the local news. The city council has announced that the old library in Oxford Street will be turned into a community centre. The building, which has been closed for three years, will reopen next spring after major repairs. The centre will offer free classes, a café, and a space for local groups to meet. The project will cost around two million pounds, most of which has come from the government. Not everyone is happy, however. Some residents argue that the money should have been spent on the city's schools instead. A public meeting will be held next Tuesday for people to share their views.

listening.title: Podcast: How I Finally Learned English
listening.script: Welcome back to Language Stories. Today's guest is Kamola, a designer from Tashkent. — Kamola: Thanks for having me. So, I studied English at school for seven years, and honestly, I couldn't order a coffee. I knew grammar rules, but speaking felt impossible. — Host: What changed? — Kamola: Two things. First, I stopped studying and started using the language. I changed my phone to English, I watched series with subtitles, and I joined a speaking club near Amir Temur square. The first meeting was terrifying — I forgot the word 'window'! But nobody laughed. Everyone there was making mistakes, and that's exactly why it worked. — Host: And the second thing? — Kamola: I made English part of my job. I started reading design articles in English, then writing short posts. When something is useful, you don't need motivation. My advice? Stop waiting until you're ready. You learn to speak by speaking badly first.

quiz.q: What was Kamola's problem after seven years of school English?
o: She knew rules but couldn't speak
quiz.e: She knew grammar rules, but speaking felt impossible — she couldn't even order a coffee.

quiz.q: Why did the speaking club work for her?
o: Everyone made mistakes, so she felt safe
quiz.e: Everyone was making mistakes, 'and that's exactly why it worked'.

quiz.q: How did she connect English to her job?
o: She read design articles and wrote posts
quiz.e: She started reading design articles in English, then writing short posts.

quiz.q: What is her main advice?
o: Start speaking before you feel ready
quiz.e: Stop waiting until you're ready — you learn to speak by speaking badly first.

quizTr.uz: U grammatika qoidalarini bilardi, lekin gapirish imkonsiz tuyulardi — hatto kofe ham buyurtma qila olmasdi.
quizTr.ru: Она знала правила грамматики, но говорить не могла — даже кофе заказать.

quizTr.uz: Hamma xato qilardi, 'aynan shuning uchun bu ish berdi'.
quizTr.ru: Все ошибались, «именно поэтому это сработало».

quizTr.uz: U ingliz tilida dizayn maqolalarini o'qib, keyin qisqa postlar yoza boshladi.
quizTr.ru: Она начала читать статьи о дизайне на английском и писать короткие посты.

quizTr.uz: Tayyor bo'lishni kutmang — avval xato qilib gapirish orqali gapirishni o'rganasiz.
quizTr.ru: Не ждите готовности — говорить учатся, сначала говоря с ошибками.

listening.title: Interview with a Plov Master
listening.script: Host: I'm standing in the Central Asian Plov Centre, and next to me is usta Karim, who has been making plov for thirty years. Usta, what's the secret? — Karim: People think the secret is a recipe. It isn't. It's attention. The rice, the carrots, the oil — they are a little different every day, and you must feel it. — Host: You cook in a kazan for two hundred people. Isn't that difficult? — Karim: The big kazan is actually more forgiving than a small pot. But you cannot leave it. Plov punishes impatient people. If you stir too early, you break the rice. If you're late with the fire, it burns. — Host: You trained your son as well? — Karim: Five years he only watched and prepared ingredients. People called me cruel! But when he finally cooked alone, his first plov was better than my first one. Watching is also learning. — Host: And your dream? — Karim: Simple. That my grandchildren eat plov made by their father, not bought in a package.

quiz.q: According to Karim, what is the real secret of plov?
quiz.e: People think the secret is a recipe. It isn't. It's attention.

quiz.q: What does 'plov punishes impatient people' mean?
o: Cooking too fast ruins the dish
quiz.e: Stirring too early breaks the rice; being late with the fire burns it — impatience ruins it.

quiz.q: How did Karim train his son at first?
o: He sent him to a school
The son only watched and prepared ingredients
quiz.e: For five years his son only watched and prepared ingredients.

quiz.q: What is Karim's dream?
o: That his family keeps cooking plov themselves
To cook for a thousand people
quiz.e: That his grandchildren eat plov made by their father, not bought in a package.

quizTr.uz: Odamlar siri retseptda deb o'ylaydi. Yo'q. Siri — e'tibor.
quizTr.ru: Люди думают, что секрет в рецепте. Нет. Секрет — внимание.

quizTr.uz: Erta aralashtirsangiz guruch sinadi; olovga kechiksangiz kuyadi — sabrsizlik oshni buzadi.
quizTr.ru: Помешаешь рано — сломаешь рис; опоздаешь с огнём — подгорит: нетерпение губит плов.

quizTr.uz: Besh yil o'g'li faqat kuzatdi va masalliqlarni tayyorladi.
quizTr.ru: Пять лет сын только наблюдал и готовил ингредиенты.

quizTr.uz: Nabiralari paketdan emas, otasi pishirgan oshni yeyishini orzu qiladi.
quizTr.ru: Он мечтает, чтобы внуки ели плов, приготовленный их отцом, а не купленный в упаковке.

grammar.title: Third conditional
grammar.lead: The third conditional talks about unreal situations in the past — things that did not happen — and their imagined results. We use it to express regret, criticism or relief about the past.

leadTr.uz: Uchinchi shart gapi o'tmishdagi bo'lmagan voqealar va ularning xayoliy natijalari haqida: afsus, tanqid va tahlil uchun ishlatiladi. If + past perfect, would have + V3.
leadTr.ru: Третий кондиционал — о несостоявшемся прошлом и его воображаемых результатах: сожаление, критика, анализ. If + past perfect, would have + V3.

grammar.situation: “If I had studied medicine, I would have become a doctor.” — But I didn’t study medicine, so I’m not a doctor. The third conditional imagines a different past.

timeline.note: Both clauses are unreal — the past cannot be changed.

blocks.h: Form: if + past perfect, would have + past participle
p: Both clauses refer to an imagined past that is now impossible to change.
ex: If I had studied, I would have passed.

p: Use could have (ability/possibility) or might have (possible result) instead of ‘would have’.
ex: If we’d left earlier, we could have caught the train. · She might have won if she’d tried.

p: ‘I’d’ can mean ‘I had’ or ‘I would’. In the if-clause it is ‘had’; in the result it is ‘would’.
ex: If I’d known (had), I’d have told you (would).

p: Express regret, criticism, or relief about a finished situation.
ex: If you’d listened, this wouldn’t have happened.

grammar.tip: Never use ‘would have’ in the if-clause: ‘If I would have known’ is wrong → ‘If I had known, I would have…’.
examples: "If I had known, I would have helped."
"She would have passed if she had revised."
"If we’d left earlier, we could have caught the bus."
"They might have won if they had played better."
"If it hadn’t rained, we would have gone out."
"You wouldn’t have got lost if you’d used a map."
"If we ’d left earlier, we could have caught the bus."
"You wouldn’t have got lost if you ’d used a map."
"If he had asked, I would have said yes."
"We would have missed it if you hadn’t called."

mistakes.x: If I would have known, I’d have called.
mistakes.v: If I had known, I’d have called. (no “would” after if)

mistakes.x: If you’d asked, I would helped.
mistakes.v: …I would have helped. (would + have + pp)

quiz.q: If I had studied, I ___ the exam.
quiz.e: Third conditional result: would have passed.

quiz.q: She would have come if you ___ her.
quiz.e: if + past perfect: had invited.

quiz.q: If we hadn't missed the train, we ___ on time.
quiz.e: Result: would have arrived.

quiz.q: If it ___ rained, we'd have gone to the beach.
quiz.e: if + past perfect negative: hadn't rained.

quiz.q: They ___ won if they'd trained harder.
quiz.e: Result: would have won.

quiz.q: If I'd had more time, I ___ you.
quiz.e: Result: would have helped.

quiz.q: We ___ caught the bus if we'd run.
quiz.e: Ability in the past → could have caught.

quiz.q: If she ___ harder, she might have got the job.
quiz.e: if + past perfect: had tried.

quiz.q: What ___ you ___ if you'd won the prize?
quiz.e: would have done.

quiz.q: Choose the past possibility.
quiz.e: Past unreal → might have won.

quiz.q: Find the mistake: 'If I would have known, I'd have called.'
quiz.e: No ‘would have’ in the if-clause: had known.

quiz.q: Complete: 'If they ___ a map, they ___ lost.'
quiz.e: had used + wouldn't have got.

quiz.q: Which expresses regret about the past?
o: If I had studied, I'd have passed.
quiz.e: Third conditional = past regret.

quiz.q: Complete: 'She ___ the train if she ___ ten minutes earlier.'
quiz.e: would have caught + had left.

quiz.q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: If you'd asked, I would have helped.
If you'd asked, I would helped.
If you asked, I would have helped.
If you had ask, I would have helped.
quiz.e: had asked + would have helped.

tip.uz: If qismida hech qachon 'would have' ishlatmang: 'If I would have known' — xato → 'If I had known, I would have…'.
tip.ru: Никогда не используйте 'would have' в if-части: 'If I would have known' — ошибка → 'If I had known, I would have…'.

h.uz: Shakl: if + past perfect, would have + sifatdosh
h.ru: Форма: if + past perfect, would have + причастие

p.uz: Ikkala qism ham endi o'zgartirib bo'lmaydigan, tasavvurdagi o'tmish haqida.
p.ru: Обе части описывают воображаемое прошлое, которое уже нельзя изменить.

p.uz: 'would have' o'rniga could have (imkoniyat/qobiliyat) yoki might have (ehtimoliy natija) ishlating.
p.ru: Вместо 'would have' используйте could have (возможность/способность) или might have (возможный результат).

p.uz: 'I'd' — 'I had' yoki 'I would' bo'lishi mumkin. If qismida bu 'had', natija qismida — 'would'.
p.ru: 'I'd' может означать 'I had' или 'I would'. В if-части это 'had', в части результата — 'would'.

p.uz: Tugagan vaziyat haqida afsus, tanqid yoki yengil tortishni bildiradi.
p.ru: Выражает сожаление, критику или облегчение по поводу завершённой ситуации.

grammar.title: Mixed conditionals
grammar.lead: Mixed conditionals combine two time frames. The most common type links a past condition to a present result, or a present condition to a past result.

leadTr.uz: Aralash shart gaplari ikki vaqtni birlashtiradi: eng ko'p uchraydigani — o'tmishdagi shartning hozirgi natijasi: If I had studied medicine, I would be a doctor now.
leadTr.ru: Смешанные кондиционалы соединяют два времени: чаще всего прошлое условие с настоящим результатом: If I had studied medicine, I would be a doctor now.

ex: If I had taken the job, I would be rich now.
If I were more careful, I wouldn’t have made that error.

p: if + past perfect, would + base. A past action affects the present.
ex: If I had taken the job, I would be rich now.

p: if + past simple, would have + past participle. A present (general) fact affects the past.
ex: If I were more careful, I wouldn’t have made that mistake.

p: Words like now, today, still often signal a present result from a past cause.
ex: If she hadn’t missed the flight, she would be here now.

p: Mixed conditionals are unreal in both clauses; only the time frames differ.
ex: If I spoke French (now), I would have understood them (then).

grammar.tip: Decide the time of each clause separately: if the cause is past, use past perfect; if the result is present, use ‘would + base’ (not ‘would have’).
examples: "If I had saved money, I would be on holiday now."
"If she were taller, she would have joined the team."
"If we hadn’t moved, we would still live in Leeds."
"If he weren’t so shy, he would have spoken to her."
"If I had learnt to drive, life would be easier now."
"If you liked sport, you would have come with us."
"If I had slept well, I wouldn’t be tired now."
"If they had invested earlier, they would be rich today."

mistakes.x: If I had studied medicine, I would have been a doctor now.
mistakes.v: …I would be a doctor now. (present result → would + base)

mistakes.x: If I’d booked, we would have been there now.
mistakes.v: …we would be there now.

tip.ru: Определяйте время каждой части отдельно: если причина в прошлом — past perfect; если результат в настоящем — 'would + начальная форма' (не 'would have').

grammar.title: Wish & if only
grammar.lead: We use ‘wish’ and ‘if only’ to talk about things we would like to be different. The tense we choose shows whether we mean the present, the past, or an annoying situation we want to change.

leadTr.uz: 'Wish' va 'if only' narsalar boshqacha bo'lishini istaganda ishlatiladi. Tanlangan zamon hozirgi, o'tmish yoki bezovta qiluvchi odat haqida ekanini ko'rsatadi.
leadTr.ru: Wish и if only выражают желание, чтобы всё было иначе. Выбранное время показывает: речь о настоящем, прошлом или раздражающей привычке.

ex: I wish I knew. (now)
I wish I had studied. (past regret)
I wish you would stop shouting.
I wish it would stop raining.

p: For present situations we want to be different, use the past simple (or ‘were’).
ex: I wish I had more time. · I wish I were taller.

p: For regrets about the past, use the past perfect.
ex: I wish I had studied harder.

p: For another person’s annoying behaviour, or a change we want, use would.
ex: I wish you would stop shouting. · I wish it would stop raining.

p: if only works like ‘wish’ but is more emphatic.
ex: If only I hadn’t said that!

grammar.tip: Don’t use ‘wish + would’ about yourself. Say ‘I wish I could…’, not ‘I wish I would…’. Use ‘would’ for other people’s behaviour.
examples: "I wish I hadn’t eaten so much."
"I wish you would listen to me."
"If only I were on holiday now."
"She wishes she had taken the job."
"He wishes he hadn’t sold his car."

mistakes.x: I wish I would be on holiday now.
mistakes.v: I wish I were on holiday now. (don’t use wish + would about yourself)

mistakes.x: I wish I would have studied harder.
mistakes.v: I wish I had studied harder.

tip.ru: Не используйте 'wish + would' о себе. Говорите 'I wish I could…', а не 'I wish I would…'. 'would' — о поведении других людей.

p.ru: Для настоящих ситуаций, которые хотим изменить, используется past simple (или 'were').

p.ru: О раздражающем поведении другого человека или желаемом изменении — would.

grammar.title: The passive: advanced
grammar.lead: At B2 we use the passive across all tenses and in impersonal reporting structures, which are common in news and academic writing to report opinions without naming a source.

leadTr.uz: B2 darajasida passiv barcha zamonlarda hamda 'It is said that…' kabi shaxssiz konstruksiyalarda ishlatiladi — bu yangiliklar va akademik uslubda keng tarqalgan.
leadTr.ru: На B2 пассив используется во всех временах и в безличных оборотах вроде It is said that… — это типично для новостей и академического стиля.

grammar.situation: “The painting is thought to be a fake.” / “It is said that he is very rich.” — Impersonal passive structures report opinions without naming who says them.

ex: It is said that he is rich.
It was believed that the Earth was flat.
He is said to be rich.
She is thought to have left.

p: Form the passive with the correct tense of be + past participle, including perfect and continuous forms.
ex: The road is being repaired. · The work had been finished. · It will have been done.

p: Use It + is/was + reporting verb + that… to report general opinions.
ex: It is said that he is very rich. · It was believed that the Earth was flat.

p: A second pattern: Subject + is/was + said/thought + to + infinitive.
ex: He is said to be rich. · She is thought to have left the country.

p: Use have/get + object + past participle when someone does a service for you (see causatives).
ex: I had my car repaired.

grammar.tip: In ‘He is said to have left’, use the perfect infinitive (to have + pp) when the action is earlier than the reporting.
examples: "The bridge is being rebuilt at the moment."
"The results had been announced before we arrived."
"It is believed that prices will rise."
"The painting is thought to be a fake."
"He is said to have made a fortune."
"The decision will have been made by Friday."
"It was reported that no one was hurt."
"She is known to have left the country."

mistakes.v: …he has left. (past participle)

grammar.title: Reported speech: reporting verbs
grammar.lead: Beyond ‘say’ and ‘tell’, English uses many reporting verbs that summarise the function of what was said — such as offer, promise, suggest, admit and refuse — each with its own grammar pattern.

leadTr.uz: 'Say' va 'tell'dan tashqari aytilgan gapning MAQSADINI ifodalovchi fe'llar bor: offer, promise, suggest, admit, refuse — har biri o'z grammatik qolipiga ega.
leadTr.ru: Кроме say и tell есть глаголы, передающие ЦЕЛЬ сказанного: offer, promise, suggest, admit, refuse — у каждого своя грамматическая модель.

ex: offered to help
advised me to wait
refused to answer
suggested leaving
admitted breaking it
apologised for being late

p: offer, promise, agree, refuse, threaten, decide.
ex: He offered to help. · She refused to answer.

p: advise, ask, tell, warn, remind, encourage, invite.
ex: They advised me to wait. · He warned us not to go.

p: suggest, admit, deny, recommend, mention.
ex: She suggested leaving early. · He admitted breaking it.

p: apologise for, insist on, accuse sb of, congratulate sb on.
ex: He apologised for being late. · She insisted on paying.

grammar.tip: Match the verb to its pattern: ‘suggest’ takes -ing or ‘that…’, never ‘to’. ‘He suggested to go’ is wrong → ‘He suggested going’.
examples: "They warned us not to swim there."

grammar.title: Past modals of deduction
grammar.lead: To make guesses about the past, we use a modal verb + have + past participle. These show how certain we are that something happened, based on present evidence.

leadTr.uz: O'tmish haqidagi taxminlar uchun modal + have + V3 ishlatiladi: must have left — aniq ketgan; can't have known — bilgan bo'lishi mumkin emas.
leadTr.ru: Для догадок о прошлом: модальный глагол + have + V3. Must have left — точно ушёл; can't have known — не мог знать.

ex: It must have rained — the ground’s wet.
He can’t have seen us.
She might have missed the bus.
You should have called me. (regret)

p: Use must have + past participle when you are sure something happened.
ex: The ground is wet — it must have rained.

p: Use can’t/couldn’t have + pp when you are sure it did not happen.
ex: He can’t have finished already; it’s too soon.

p: Use these for things that possibly happened but you’re not sure.
ex: She might have missed the bus. · They could have got lost.

p: Use should have + pp for the right thing that didn’t happen (regret or criticism).
ex: You should have told me. · I shouldn’t have eaten so much.

grammar.tip: For deduction the opposite of ‘must have’ is ‘can’t have’, not ‘mustn’t have’. ‘Mustn’t have’ is not used for deduction in standard English.
examples: "The lights are off — they must have gone out."
"She can’t have seen us; she didn’t wave."
"They could have taken the wrong road."
"The ground’s wet — it must have rained."
"He can’t have seen us; he didn’t wave."
"He can’t have studied — he failed badly."

mistakes.x: He mustn’t have heard the bell.
mistakes.v: He can’t have heard the bell. (negative deduction → can’t have)

mistakes.x: You should have call me.
mistakes.v: You should have called me.

quiz.e: Sure it happened → must have rained.

quiz.e: Possible → might have gone.

quiz.q: The cake is gone. Someone ___ it.
quiz.e: Sure → must have eaten.

quiz.e: Sure not → can't have studied.

quiz.q: They're late. They ___ stuck in traffic.
quiz.e: Possible → might have been.

quiz.q: I feel ill. I ___ that fish.
quiz.e: Regret → shouldn't have eaten.

quiz.q: Choose the 'impossible' deduction.
quiz.e: can't have = sure it didn't happen.

quiz.q: Find the mistake: 'He mustn't have heard the bell.'
quiz.e: For negative deduction use ‘can't have’.

quiz.q: Complete: 'The door's open — someone ___ in, or you ___ to lock it.'
o: must have broken / might have forgotten
quiz.e: must have broken in (sure) + might have forgotten (possible).

quiz.e: should have = regret.

quiz.e: Sure it wasn't hard → can't have been.

quiz.q: Choose the correct sentence.
quiz.e: should have + past participle: should have called.

tip.uz: Xulosa chiqarishda 'must have'ning aksi — 'can't have', 'mustn't have' emas. Standart ingliz tilida xulosa uchun 'mustn't have' ishlatilmaydi.
tip.ru: Противоположность 'must have' при умозаключении — 'can't have', а не 'mustn't have'. 'Mustn't have' в этом значении не используется.

p.uz: Biror narsa bo'lganiga ishonchingiz komil bo'lsa, must have + sifatdosh ishlating.
p.ru: Когда вы уверены, что что-то произошло: must have + причастие.

p.uz: Bo'lmaganiga ishonchingiz komil bo'lsa, can't/couldn't have + sifatdosh ishlating.
p.ru: Когда вы уверены, что этого не было: can't/couldn't have + причастие.

p.uz: Ehtimol bo'lgan, lekin aniq bilmagan narsalar uchun shularni ishlating.
p.ru: Для того, что возможно произошло, но вы не уверены.

p.uz: Bo'lishi kerak bo'lgan, lekin bo'lmagan to'g'ri ish uchun should have + sifatdosh (afsus yoki tanqid).
p.ru: Для правильного действия, которое не произошло: should have + причастие (сожаление или критика).

quiz.ru: Уверенность, что произошло → must have rained.
Уверенность, что не было → can't have seen.
Уверенность, что не было → can't have studied.
can't have = уверенность, что не произошло.

quiz.uz: must have broken in (ishonch) + might have forgotten (ehtimol).
quiz.ru: must have broken in (уверенность) + might have forgotten (возможно).

quiz.uz: Qiyin bo'lmaganiga ishonch → can't have been.
quiz.ru: Уверенность, что не был сложным → can't have been.

quiz.uz: should have + sifatdosh: should have called.
quiz.ru: should have + причастие: should have called.

grammar.title: Relative clauses: advanced
grammar.lead: At B2 we use more formal relative structures: prepositions before the relative pronoun, ‘whose’ for possession, and quantifiers like ‘some of whom’ and ‘both of which’ in non-defining clauses.

leadTr.uz: B2 da rasmiyroq nisbiy tuzilmalar o'rganiladi: predlog + relative pronoun (in which), egalik uchun 'whose' hamda 'some of whom', 'both of which' kabi birikmalar.
leadTr.ru: На B2 — более формальные относительные конструкции: предлог + местоимение (in which), whose для принадлежности, some of whom, both of which.

ex: the man to whom I spoke
the house in which they live
the man I spoke to
the house they live in

p: In formal English the preposition can go before the relative pronoun (which/whom).
ex: The man to whom I spoke… · The house in which they live…

p: In everyday English we usually move the preposition to the end and may drop the pronoun.
ex: The man (who) I spoke to… · The house (that) they live in…

p: In non-defining clauses use all/some/many/none/both + of whom/which.
ex: I have three sisters, all of whom are doctors.

p: whose shows possession for people and things.
ex: A company whose products are famous… · The author, whose books I love…

grammar.tip: After a preposition use whom (not ‘who’) and which (not ‘that’): ‘the person to whom…’, ‘the tool with which…’. ‘To that’ and ‘to who’ are wrong here.
examples: "The colleague with whom I work is brilliant."
"This is the book about which we spoke."
"She has many friends, most of whom live abroad."
"They sell phones, none of which are cheap."
"He’s an artist whose work sells worldwide."
"The reason for which he left is unclear."
"I have three sisters, all of whom are doctors."
"That’s the house in which she was born."

mistakes.x: The client to that I wrote replied.
mistakes.v: …to whom I wrote… (preposition + whom)

mistakes.x: I have two cousins, both of who are nurses.
mistakes.v: …both of whom are nurses.

quiz.q: The person ___ I spoke was helpful. (formal)
quiz.e: Preposition + whom: to whom.

quiz.q: That's the house ___ which they were born.
quiz.e: born in a house → in which.

quiz.q: He's a writer ___ novels are famous.
quiz.e: Possession → whose.

quiz.q: Informal: 'The man I spoke ___.'
quiz.e: speak to → preposition at the end: to.

quiz.q: I have two cousins, both ___ whom are nurses.
quiz.e: both of whom.

quiz.q: The tool ___ which we cut it was sharp.
quiz.e: cut with → with which.

quiz.q: She has many fans, some ___ whom waited all night.
quiz.e: some of whom.

quiz.q: The company ___ products we use is British.
quiz.e: Possession (company's) → whose.

quiz.q: This is the issue ___ which we must decide.
quiz.e: decide on → on which.

quiz.q: Choose the formal version of 'the man I work with'.
o: the man with who I work
the man with whom I work
the man with that I work
quiz.e: with whom I work.

quiz.q: Find the mistake: 'The client to that I wrote replied.'
quiz.e: After a preposition use ‘whom’, not ‘that’.

quiz.q: Complete: 'He owns three shops, ___ are in London.'
quiz.e: Things → all of which.

quiz.q: Which is correct and formal?
o: The report on which it is based is here.
The report on that it is based is here.
The report which it is based on which…
The report based which on it…
quiz.e: based on → on which.

quiz.q: Complete: 'She interviewed ten people, ___ had experience.'
quiz.e: People → none of whom.

quiz.q: Choose the correct 'whose' sentence.
o: The painter who paintings sell well is here.
The painter whose paintings sell well is here.
The painter which paintings sell well is here.
The painter whom paintings sell well is here.
quiz.e: Possession → whose paintings.

tip.uz: Predlogdan keyin whom ('who' emas) va which ('that' emas) ishlatiladi: 'the person to whom…', 'the tool with which…'. 'To that' va 'to who' bu yerda xato.
tip.ru: После предлога используйте whom (не 'who') и which (не 'that'): 'the person to whom…', 'the tool with which…'. 'To that' и 'to who' здесь ошибочны.

p.uz: Rasmiy ingliz tilida predlog nisbiy olmoshdan (which/whom) oldin kelishi mumkin.
p.ru: В формальном английском предлог может стоять перед относительным местоимением (which/whom).

p.uz: Kundalik nutqda predlog odatda gap oxiriga ko'chadi, olmosh esa tushib qolishi mumkin.
p.ru: В повседневной речи предлог обычно уходит в конец, а местоимение может опускаться.

p.uz: Ajratuvchi bo'lmagan gaplarda all/some/many/none/both + of whom/which ishlatiladi.
p.ru: В неограничительных придаточных: all/some/many/none/both + of whom/which.

p.uz: whose odamlar va narsalar uchun egalikni bildiradi.
p.ru: whose выражает принадлежность для людей и предметов.

quiz.uz: born in a house → in which.
quiz.ru: born in a house → in which.
speak to → предлог в конце: to.

grammar.title: Causative: have/get something done
grammar.lead: We use the causative when we arrange for someone else to do a service for us, rather than doing it ourselves. The structure focuses on the result, not on who does the work.

leadTr.uz: Kauzativ (have/get something done) xizmatni o'zimiz emas, boshqa birov bajarishini bildiradi: I had my phone repaired — telefonimni tuzattirdim.
leadTr.ru: Каузатив (have/get something done) означает, что услугу выполняет кто-то другой: I had my phone repaired — мне починили телефон.

grammar.situation: “I don’t cut my own hair — I have it cut.” — The causative shows that someone does a service for you. The focus is on the result, not who does the work.

ex: I painted the door.
I repaired my car.
I had the door painted.
I got my car repaired.

p: The standard structure: have + thing + past participle.
ex: I had my hair cut. · We had the house painted.

p: get is a more informal alternative to ‘have’.
ex: I got my car repaired. · She got her photo taken.

p: Change the tense of ‘have/get’ as needed.
ex: I’m having my eyes tested tomorrow. · He’s had his phone fixed.

p: The same structure can describe something bad that happened to you.
ex: She had her bag stolen. · They had their flight cancelled.

grammar.tip: The order is have + OBJECT + past participle, not ‘have + past participle + object’. Say ‘I had my car washed’, not ‘I had washed my car’ (that means you did it yourself).
examples: "I had my suit cleaned for the wedding."
"I need to have my passport renewed."
"You should get that checked by a doctor."
"We had the house painted last summer."

mistakes.x: I had repaired my bike at the shop.
mistakes.v: I had my bike repaired. (have + object + past participle)

mistakes.x: I’ll have fix the roof.
mistakes.v: I’ll have the roof fixed.

quiz.q: I ___ my hair cut yesterday.
quiz.e: Causative past: had my hair cut.

quiz.q: We're going to ___ the house painted.
quiz.e: have the house painted.

quiz.q: She ___ her car repaired last week.
quiz.e: got her car repaired.

quiz.q: Choose the correct order.
quiz.e: have + object + past participle.

quiz.q: He needs to have his eyes ___.
quiz.e: Past participle: tested.

quiz.q: I'm ___ my photo taken tomorrow.
quiz.e: Present continuous: having.

quiz.q: They ___ their windows cleaned every month.
quiz.e: Habit, present simple: get.

quiz.q: She ___ her bag stolen on the train. (bad event)
quiz.e: had her bag stolen.

quiz.q: We've just ___ the carpet cleaned.
quiz.e: Present perfect: have had → 'have just had'... here 'had' completes 'have just had'.

quiz.q: Choose the causative meaning 'someone did it for me'.
quiz.e: Causative: had the door painted.

quiz.q: Find the mistake: 'I had repaired my bike at the shop.'
o: had repaired → had my bike repaired
quiz.e: Causative needs object + pp: had my bike repaired.

quiz.q: Complete: 'You should ___ that tooth ___.'
quiz.e: get + object + past participle: get it looked at.

quiz.q: Which describes an unpleasant event?
quiz.e: had his car stolen = bad event.

quiz.q: Complete: 'They ___ their flight ___ because of the storm.'
quiz.e: had + object + past participle: had it cancelled.

quiz.q: Choose the correct future causative.
o: I'll have fixed the roof for me.
quiz.e: have + object + past participle: have the roof fixed.

tip.uz: Tartib: have + OBYEKT + sifatdosh, 'have + sifatdosh + obyekt' emas. 'I had my car washed' deng, 'I had washed my car' emas (bu o'zingiz yuvganingizni bildiradi).
tip.ru: Порядок: have + ОБЪЕКТ + причастие, а не 'have + причастие + объект'. Говорите 'I had my car washed', а не 'I had washed my car' (это значит, что вы сделали это сами).

p.uz: Standart qolip: have + narsa + sifatdosh.
p.ru: Стандартная структура: have + предмет + причастие.

p.uz: get — 'have'ning norasmiyroq muqobili.
p.ru: get — более разговорная альтернатива 'have'.

p.uz: 'have/get' fe'lining zamonini kerak bo'lganda o'zgartiring.
p.ru: Меняйте время глагола 'have/get' по необходимости.

p.uz: Xuddi shu qolip boshingizga tushgan yomon hodisani ham tasvirlashi mumkin.
p.ru: Та же структура может описывать неприятность, случившуюся с вами.

quiz.uz: Causative o'tgan zamon: had my hair cut.
quiz.ru: Каузатив в прошедшем: had my hair cut.

quiz.uz: Present perfect: 'have just had' shaklini 'had' to'ldiradi.
quiz.ru: Present perfect: 'had' завершает форму 'have just had'.

quiz.uz: Causative uchun obyekt + sifatdosh kerak: had my bike repaired.
quiz.ru: Каузативу нужен объект + причастие: had my bike repaired.

quiz.uz: get + obyekt + sifatdosh: get it looked at.
quiz.ru: get + объект + причастие: get it looked at.

quiz.uz: had his car stolen = yomon hodisa.
quiz.ru: had his car stolen = неприятное событие.

quiz.uz: had + obyekt + sifatdosh: had it cancelled.
quiz.ru: had + объект + причастие: had it cancelled.

quiz.uz: have + obyekt + sifatdosh: have the roof fixed.
quiz.ru: have + объект + причастие: have the roof fixed.

grammar.title: Gerunds & infinitives: advanced
grammar.lead: Some verbs are followed by either a gerund or an infinitive, but with a clear change of meaning. Knowing the difference lets you say exactly what you mean.

leadTr.uz: Ayrim fe'llardan keyin gerund ham, infinitiv ham keladi, lekin ma'no aniq o'zgaradi: remember doing (eslash) / remember to do (unutmaslik).
leadTr.ru: После некоторых глаголов возможны обе формы, но смысл меняется: remember doing (помнить, как делал) / remember to do (не забыть сделать).

ex: remember to lock (a duty)
stop to rest (pause in order to)
try to open (attempt)
remember locking (a memory)
stop smoking (quit)
try adding salt (experiment)

p: + to = the duty comes after; + -ing = the memory comes before.
ex: Remember to lock the door. (do it) · I remember locking it. (memory)

p: stop + -ing = end the activity; stop + to = pause in order to do something.
ex: He stopped smoking. (quit) · He stopped to smoke. (paused)

p: try + -ing = experiment; try + to = attempt something difficult.
ex: Try adding salt. (experiment) · I tried to open it. (attempt)

p: regret + -ing = be sorry about the past; regret + to = be sorry to announce. mean + -ing = involve; mean + to = intend.
ex: I regret saying it. · I regret to inform you… · This job means travelling. · I meant to call.

grammar.tip: With ‘remember/forget’: use the infinitive for a task you must do, and the -ing form for a memory of something already done.
examples: "He stopped to rest for a minute."
"Try turning it off and on again."
"I regret to tell you the news is bad."
"He stopped to rest for a minute. (paused)"
"I regret to inform you the news is bad."

mistakes.x: I regret to tell him the truth; now he’s angry.
mistakes.v: I regret telling him… (regret + -ing = sorry about the past)

mistakes.x: On the walk we stopped taking photos. (meaning: paused to take)
mistakes.v: …we stopped to take photos. (pause in order to)

quiz.q: Remember ___ the door when you leave.
quiz.e: Duty to do → to lock.

quiz.q: I remember ___ him at the party last year.
quiz.e: Memory → meeting.

quiz.q: He stopped ___ because his lungs hurt. (quit)
quiz.e: Ended the activity → stopped smoking.

quiz.q: On the walk, we stopped ___ photos.
quiz.e: Paused in order to → to take.

quiz.q: I regret ___ that I can't help.
quiz.e: Sorry to announce → regret to say.

quiz.q: The recipe didn't work. Try ___ more sugar.
quiz.e: Experiment → try adding.

quiz.q: I tried ___ the window, but it was stuck.
quiz.e: Attempt at something hard → tried to open.

quiz.q: This new job means ___ to another city.
quiz.e: mean = involve → moving.

quiz.q: I'm sorry, I meant ___ you earlier.
quiz.e: mean = intend → to call.

quiz.q: Don't forget ___ your medicine tonight.
quiz.e: Duty → to take.

quiz.q: Find the mistake: 'I regret to tell him the truth; now he's angry.'
quiz.e: Sorry about the past → regret telling.

quiz.q: Complete: 'I'll never forget ___ the Pyramids, but please remember ___ the tickets.'
quiz.e: Memory ‘seeing’ + duty ‘to buy’.

quiz.q: Which means 'he paused his walk to make a call'?
quiz.e: stop + to = pause in order to.

quiz.q: Complete: 'We regret ___ you that the flight ___, so we tried ___ another route.'
o: to inform / has been cancelled / to find
quiz.e: regret to inform + passive + tried to find.

quiz.q: Choose the correct pair.
o: Remember posting it (do it now) / I stopped to smoke (quit).
Remember to post it (do it) / I stopped smoking (quit).
Remember to post it / I stopped to smoke means I quit.
Remember posting it means do it now.
quiz.e: to-infinitive = task; stop + -ing = quit.

tip.uz: 'remember/forget' bilan: bajarilishi kerak bo'lgan vazifa uchun infinitive, allaqachon bo'lib o'tgan narsaning xotirasi uchun -ing shakli ishlatiladi.
tip.ru: С 'remember/forget': инфинитив — для задачи, которую нужно сделать, форма -ing — для воспоминания об уже сделанном.

p.uz: + to = vazifa keyin bajariladi; + -ing = xotira oldin bo'lgan voqea haqida.
p.ru: + to = обязанность идёт после; + -ing = воспоминание о том, что было раньше.

p.uz: stop + -ing = harakatni tugatish; stop + to = biror narsa qilish uchun to'xtash.
p.ru: stop + -ing = прекратить действие; stop + to = остановиться, чтобы что-то сделать.

p.uz: try + -ing = sinab ko'rish (tajriba); try + to = qiyin narsaga urinish.
p.ru: try + -ing = поэкспериментировать; try + to = попытаться сделать трудное.

p.uz: regret + -ing = o'tmishdan afsuslanish; regret + to = aytishdan afsusda bo'lish. mean + -ing = talab qilmoq; mean + to = niyat qilmoq.
p.ru: regret + -ing = сожалеть о прошлом; regret + to = с сожалением сообщать. mean + -ing = подразумевать/требовать; mean + to = намереваться.

quiz.uz: Bajarilishi kerak bo'lgan vazifa → to lock.
quiz.ru: Задача, которую нужно сделать → to lock.
С сожалением сообщать → regret to say.

quiz.uz: Qiyin narsaga urinish → tried to open.
regret to inform + passiv + tried to find.
quiz.ru: regret to inform + пассив + tried to find.

grammar.title: Future perfect & continuous
grammar.lead: To talk about the future in detail, we use the future continuous for actions in progress at a future time, and the future perfect for actions that will be completed before a future point.

leadTr.uz: Kelajakni batafsil ifodalash uchun: future continuous — kelajakdagi paytda davom etadigan harakat; future perfect — muayyan muddatgacha tugaydigan harakat.
leadTr.ru: Для детального будущего: future continuous — действие в процессе в будущий момент; future perfect — действие, завершённое к сроку.

timeline.note: Continuous = happening AT a future moment · Perfect = finished BEFORE it.

ex: At 8pm I ’ll be having dinner.
This time tomorrow I’ll be flying.
By Friday I’ll have finished.
By 2030 they’ll have built it.

p: An action that will be in progress at a specific future time.
ex: This time tomorrow I will be flying to Rome.

blocks.h: Future perfect: will have + past participle
p: An action that will be finished before a future time, often with ‘by’.
ex: By 2030 they will have built the bridge.

p: Use by + time or by the time + clause with the future perfect.
ex: By the time you arrive, I will have left.

p: will have been + -ing stresses the duration up to a future point.
ex: By June I will have been working here for ten years.

grammar.tip: Use the future continuous for something happening at a future moment, and the future perfect for something completed before that moment.
examples: "By Friday we ’ll have finished the report."
"This time next week she ’ll be lying on a beach."
"By the time he’s 30, he ’ll have travelled the world."
"In May I ’ll have been studying here for three years."
"Don’t call at six — I’ll be driving."
"Don’t call at six — I ’ll be driving."
"They ’ll have left by the time we arrive."
"This time tomorrow we ’ll be flying to Rome."

mistakes.x: By next month I will finish the course.
mistakes.v: By next month I will have finished… (completed before → future perfect)

mistakes.x: Don’t call at six — I will drive.
mistakes.v: …I’ll be driving. (in progress → future continuous)

quiz.q: This time tomorrow I ___ to Spain.
quiz.e: In progress at a future time → will be flying.

quiz.q: By next year, they ___ the new road.
quiz.e: Completed before a future time → will have built.

quiz.q: At 9 pm tonight, we ___ the match.
quiz.e: In progress → will be watching.

quiz.q: By the time you arrive, I ___.
quiz.e: Finished before → will have left.

quiz.q: Don't phone at six; I ___.
quiz.e: In progress → will be driving.

quiz.q: By Friday she ___ the project.
quiz.e: Completed by a deadline → will have finished.

quiz.q: This time next week, they ___ on holiday.
quiz.e: In progress → will be relaxing.

quiz.q: In June I ___ here for five years.
quiz.e: Duration up to a future point → will have been working.

quiz.q: By 2040, scientists ___ a cure, perhaps.
quiz.e: Completed before → will have found.

quiz.q: Choose the action in progress at a future time.
quiz.e: will be eating = in progress.

quiz.q: Find the mistake: 'By next month I will finish the course.'
quiz.e: Completed before a future time → will have finished.

quiz.q: Complete: 'At noon we ___ the test; by 2 pm we ___ it.'
o: will be taking / will have finished
will have taken / will be finishing
quiz.e: In progress ‘will be taking’ + completed ‘will have finished’.

quiz.q: Which stresses duration up to a future point?
o: By May I'll have been writing for a year.
quiz.e: will have been writing = duration.

quiz.q: Complete: 'By the time the film ends, we ___ here for three hours.'
quiz.e: Duration up to a point → will have been sitting.

quiz.q: Choose the correct future perfect.
quiz.e: will have + past participle: will have left.

tip.uz: Kelajakdagi aniq paytda davom etadigan harakat uchun future continuous, o'sha paytgacha tugaydigan harakat uchun future perfect ishlatiladi.
tip.ru: Future continuous — для действия в процессе в будущий момент, future perfect — для действия, завершённого до этого момента.

p.uz: Kelajakdagi aniq vaqtda davom etib turadigan harakat.
p.ru: Действие, которое будет в процессе в конкретный момент будущего.

p.uz: Kelajakdagi vaqtdan oldin tugaydigan harakat, ko'pincha 'by' bilan.
p.ru: Действие, которое завершится до будущего момента, часто с 'by'.

p.uz: Future perfect bilan by + vaqt yoki by the time + gap ishlatiladi.
p.ru: С future perfect используйте by + время или by the time + придаточное.

p.uz: will have been + -ing kelajakdagi nuqtagacha bo'lgan davomiylikni ta'kidlaydi.
p.ru: will have been + -ing подчёркивает длительность до будущего момента.

quiz.ru: В процессе в будущем → will be flying.

quiz.uz: Kelajakdagi vaqtdan oldin tugaydi → will have built.
quiz.ru: Завершено до будущего момента → will have built.

quiz.uz: Oldin tugagan bo'ladi → will have left.

quiz.ru: Завершено к сроку → will have finished.

quiz.uz: Kelajakdagi nuqtagacha davomiylik → will have been working.
quiz.ru: Длительность до будущей точки → will have been working.

Kelajakdagi vaqtdan oldin tugaydi → will have finished.

grammar.title: Past perfect continuous
grammar.lead: The past perfect continuous shows that an activity had been in progress for a period before another point in the past. It emphasises duration and often explains a past situation.

leadTr.uz: Past perfect continuous o'tmishdagi nuqtadan OLDIN ma'lum muddat davom etgan faoliyatni bildiradi va ko'pincha sababni tushuntiradi: He was tired because he had been working.
leadTr.ru: Past perfect continuous — действие, длившееся ДО момента в прошлом; часто объясняет причину: He was tired because he had been working.

grammar.situation: “She had been waiting for an hour when the bus finally came.” — The past perfect continuous shows how long an activity had gone on up to a past moment.

timeline.note: A long activity continuing up to a point in the past.

p: Use had been + verb-ing for an action that continued up to a point in the past.
ex: She had been waiting for an hour when the bus came.

p: It often explains why something was the case at a past moment.
ex: His eyes were red because he had been crying.

p: Use for + period and since + starting point.
ex: They had been living there for years before they moved.

p: The continuous stresses the activity/duration; the simple stresses the completed result.
ex: I had been reading. (activity) · I had read the book. (finished)

grammar.tip: Don’t use the continuous with state verbs. Say ‘I had known her for years’, not ‘I had been knowing’.
examples: "He was tired because he had been working all night."
"We had been driving for hours when the car broke down."
"She had been studying French before she moved to Paris."
"The ground was wet; it had been raining."
"They had been arguing before we arrived."
"I had been waiting for ages when she finally called."
"I had been waiting for ages when she called."
"His eyes were red because he had been crying."
"By noon they had been walking for six hours."

mistakes.x: I had been knowing him for years before he left.
mistakes.v: I had known him for years… (state verb → simple)

mistakes.x: They had been lived there for years.
mistakes.v: They had been living there for years.

quiz.q: She ___ for an hour when the bus arrived.
quiz.e: Duration up to a past point → had been waiting.

quiz.e: Explains the past result → had been crying.

quiz.q: They ___ for hours before they stopped.
quiz.e: Duration → had been driving.

quiz.e: had been + -ing.

quiz.q: It was wet outside; it ___.
quiz.e: Earlier activity → had been raining.

quiz.q: We ___ for the train when it was cancelled.
quiz.e: Duration before a past event → had been waiting.

quiz.q: She was out of breath because she ___.
quiz.e: Explains the state → had been running.

quiz.q: How long ___ they ___ before they got married?
quiz.e: Duration → had they been dating.

quiz.q: Which verb is WRONG in this form?
quiz.e: ‘know’ is a state verb.

quiz.q: Choose the duration form.
o: I had been reading for hours.
quiz.e: Duration → had been reading.

quiz.q: Find the mistake: 'I had been knowing him for years before he left.'
quiz.e: State verb: had known.

quiz.q: Complete: 'By the time help arrived, they ___ for three hours.'
quiz.e: Duration up to a past point → had been swimming.

quiz.q: Which stresses the completed result?
o: She had been painting the room.

quiz.e: Completed → past perfect simple: had painted.

quiz.e: Ongoing activity explaining the result → had been playing.

o: They had been lived there for years.
They had been living there for years.

tip.uz: Holat fe'llari bilan continuous ishlatmang. 'I had known her for years' deng, 'I had been knowing' emas.
tip.ru: Не используйте continuous с глаголами состояния. Говорите 'I had known her for years', а не 'I had been knowing'.

p.uz: O'tmishdagi nuqtagacha davom etgan harakat uchun had been + fe'l-ing ishlatiladi.
p.ru: had been + глагол-ing — для действия, длившегося до момента в прошлом.

p.uz: Ko'pincha o'tmishdagi paytda nima uchun shunday bo'lganini izohlaydi.
p.ru: Часто объясняет, почему в прошлый момент дело обстояло так.

p.uz: for + davr va since + boshlanish nuqtasi ishlatiladi.
p.ru: for + период и since + точка отсчёта.

p.uz: Continuous harakat/davomiylikni, simple esa tugallangan natijani ta'kidlaydi.
p.ru: Continuous подчёркивает процесс/длительность, simple — завершённый результат.

quiz.uz: O'tmishdagi nuqtagacha davomiylik → had been waiting.
quiz.ru: Длительность до момента в прошлом → had been waiting.

quiz.uz: O'tmishdagi natijani izohlaydi → had been crying.
quiz.ru: Объясняет прошлый результат → had been crying.

quiz.uz: O'tmishdagi nuqtagacha davomiylik → had been swimming.
quiz.ru: Длительность до момента в прошлом → had been swimming.

quiz.uz: Tugallangan → past perfect simple: had painted.
quiz.ru: Завершено → past perfect simple: had painted.

quiz.uz: Natijani izohlagan davomiy harakat → had been playing.
quiz.ru: Длительное действие, объясняющее результат → had been playing.

grammar.title: Inversion
grammar.lead: In formal or emphatic English, certain negative or limiting adverbials at the start of a sentence force inversion — the auxiliary verb comes before the subject, as in a question.

leadTr.uz: Rasmiy va ta'sirli uslubda gap boshidagi inkor iboralar (never, rarely, not only) inversiyani talab qiladi — yordamchi fe'l egadan oldin keladi: Never have I seen…
leadTr.ru: В формальном стиле отрицательные обороты в начале предложения (never, rarely, not only) требуют инверсии: Never have I seen…

grammar.situation: “Never have I seen such a mess.” — In formal or emphatic English, a negative word at the start pushes the auxiliary in front of the subject, like a question.

p: After never, rarely, seldom, hardly, no sooner, not only, little at the start, invert subject and auxiliary.
ex: Never have I seen such a mess. · Rarely does she complain.

p: Used for one event quickly following another.
ex: Hardly had we arrived when it started to rain. · No sooner had he spoken than she left.

p: Not only + auxiliary + subject, … but also …
ex: Not only did he apologise, but he also paid.

p: After only then / only after / only when / not until, invert.
ex: Only when she left did I realise. · Not until midnight did they finish.

grammar.tip: Inversion uses the same auxiliary you’d use in a question: ‘Never have I…’, ‘Rarely does he…’, ‘Not only did she…’. Don’t use normal word order after these openers.
examples: "Hardly had I sat down when the phone rang."
"No sooner had they left than it snowed."
"Not only is she clever, but she’s kind too."
"Only after the test did he relax."
"Little did he know what was coming."

mistakes.x: Never I have eaten such good food.
mistakes.v: Never have I eaten such good food. (invert: aux + subject)

mistakes.x: Not only she sings, but she dances.
mistakes.v: Not only does she sing, but she also dances.

mistakes.x: No sooner he had left when it rained.
mistakes.v: No sooner had he left than it rained.

quiz.q: Never ___ such a beautiful view.
quiz.e: Inversion: have I seen.

quiz.e: Inversion: does she go.

quiz.e: Inversion: was he.

quiz.e: Inversion: had I sat.

quiz.q: No sooner had we left ___ it started to rain.
quiz.e: No sooner … than.

quiz.q: Little ___ that he was being watched.
quiz.e: Inversion: did he know.

quiz.e: Inversion: did I feel.

quiz.q: Not until the next day ___ the news.
quiz.e: Inversion: did they hear.

quiz.q: Hardly had I arrived ___ the trouble began.
quiz.e: Hardly … when.

quiz.q: Find the mistake: 'Never I have eaten such good food.'
quiz.e: Inversion: Never have I eaten.

quiz.q: Complete: 'No sooner ___ the door ___ the alarm rang.'
quiz.e: No sooner had he opened … than.

quiz.q: Which is correct?
o: Not only she sings, but she dances.
Not only does she sing, but she also dances.
Not only sings she, but she dances.
Not only she does sing, but dances.
quiz.e: Not only does she sing, but she also dances.

quiz.q: Complete: 'Only after he left ___ how rude he had been.'
quiz.e: Inversion after ‘Only after’: did I realise.

quiz.q: Rewrite with inversion: 'I had rarely felt so happy.'
o: Rarely I had felt so happy.
Rarely had I felt so happy.
Rarely did I had felt so happy.
quiz.e: Rarely had I felt so happy.

tip.uz: Inversion'da savoldagi kabi yordamchi fe'l ishlatiladi: 'Never have I…', 'Rarely does he…', 'Not only did she…'. Bu so'zlardan keyin oddiy so'z tartibini ishlatmang.
tip.ru: В инверсии используется тот же вспомогательный глагол, что в вопросе: 'Never have I…', 'Rarely does he…', 'Not only did she…'. После таких слов обычный порядок слов не подходит.

p.uz: Gap boshidagi never, rarely, seldom, hardly, no sooner, not only, little so'zlaridan keyin ega va yordamchi fe'l o'rin almashadi.
p.ru: После never, rarely, seldom, hardly, no sooner, not only, little в начале предложения подлежащее и вспомогательный глагол меняются местами.

p.uz: Bir voqea ketidan tez keladigan ikkinchi voqea uchun ishlatiladi.
p.ru: Для одного события, быстро следующего за другим.

p.uz: Not only + yordamchi fe'l + ega, … but also …
p.ru: Not only + вспомогательный глагол + подлежащее, … but also …

p.uz: only then / only after / only when / not until dan keyin inversion qilinadi.
p.ru: После only then / only after / only when / not until — инверсия.

quiz.uz: No sooner had he opened … than.
quiz.ru: No sooner had he opened … than.

quiz.uz: Not only does she sing, but she also dances.
quiz.ru: Not only does she sing, but she also dances.

quiz.ru: Инверсия после 'Only after': did I realise.

quiz.ru: Rarely had I felt so happy.

grammar.title: Cleft sentences
grammar.lead: Cleft (‘divided’) sentences split one idea into two clauses to emphasise a particular part. They are very common in speech for adding focus and contrast.

leadTr.uz: Cleft gaplar bitta fikrni ikki qismga bo'lib, kerakli joyga urg'u beradi: It was Aziz who called. / What I need is time. Og'zaki nutqda juda ko'p uchraydi.
leadTr.ru: Расщеплённые предложения делят мысль надвое ради акцента: It was Aziz who called. / What I need is time. Очень частотны в речи.

ex: It was Tom who broke it.
It was in 2010 that we met.
What I need is a holiday.
What he did was (to) call the police.

p: Emphasise a person, thing, time or place.
ex: It was Tom who broke it. · It was in 2010 that we met.

p: Emphasise the whole idea, often an action or need.
ex: What I need is a holiday. · What he did was (to) call the police.

blocks.h: The thing / the reason / the place
p: Other openers add focus too.
ex: The reason (why) I’m late is the traffic. · The place where we stayed was lovely.

p: All can mean ‘the only thing’.
ex: All I want is peace and quiet.

grammar.tip: In a What-cleft, the verb ‘be’ is singular even before a plural idea if ‘what’ is the subject: ‘What I need is answers’ (not ‘are’).
examples: "It was my sister who called, not me."
"What we did was book another flight."
"The reason I left was the noise."
"It was in 2010 that we first met."
"The place where we stayed was lovely."

mistakes.x: What I want are answers.
mistakes.v: What I want is answers. (“what” as subject → singular verb)

mistakes.x: It was John which sent the email.
mistakes.v: It was John who sent the email.

quiz.q: ___ Tom who broke the window.
quiz.e: It-cleft: It was Tom who…

quiz.q: What I need ___ a long rest.
quiz.e: What-cleft, singular: is.

quiz.q: It was in Paris ___ they got married.
quiz.e: Place/time it-cleft: that.

quiz.q: ___ I want is some peace.
quiz.e: All = the only thing.

quiz.q: It was Sarah ___ helped me.
quiz.e: Person → who.

quiz.q: What he did ___ apologise.
quiz.e: What-cleft: was (to) apologise.

quiz.q: The reason ___ I called was to thank you.
quiz.e: The reason why.

quiz.q: It's not the money ___ matters.
quiz.e: It-cleft: that matters.

quiz.q: What surprised everyone ___ his decision.
quiz.e: Singular ‘what’ → was.

quiz.q: Choose the cleft emphasising the place.
o: We stayed in a lovely hotel.
It was the hotel that we loved.
The place where we stayed was lovely.
quiz.e: The place where… = focus on place.

quiz.q: Find the mistake: 'What I want are answers.'
quiz.e: ‘What’ as subject → singular: is.

quiz.q: Rewrite to emphasise 'John': 'John sent the email.'
o: It was John who sent the email.
It was the email who John sent.
John it was sent the email.
quiz.e: It was John who sent the email.

quiz.q: Complete: '___ we should do ___ tell the truth.'
quiz.e: What we should do is tell the truth.

quiz.q: Which correctly emphasises the reason?
o: The reason why he left was the noise.
The reason what he left was the noise.
It was the reason the noise left.
Why the reason he left noise.
quiz.e: The reason why he left was the noise.

quiz.q: Complete: '___ that I admire ___ her honesty.'
quiz.e: The thing that I admire is her honesty.

tip.uz: What-cleft'da 'what' ega bo'lsa, 'be' fe'li ko'plik g'oyasidan oldin ham birlikda bo'ladi: 'What I need is answers' ('are' emas).
tip.ru: В What-cleft глагол 'be' стоит в единственном числе, даже перед множественной идеей, если 'what' — подлежащее: 'What I need is answers' (не 'are').

p.uz: Shaxs, narsa, vaqt yoki joyni ta'kidlash uchun.
p.ru: Для выделения человека, предмета, времени или места.

p.uz: Butun g'oyani, ko'pincha harakat yoki ehtiyojni ta'kidlaydi.
p.ru: Выделяет целую идею, часто действие или потребность.

h.uz: The thing / the reason / the place
h.ru: The thing / the reason / the place

p.uz: Boshqa boshlovchi so'zlar ham urg'u qo'shadi.
p.ru: Другие вводные конструкции тоже добавляют фокус.

p.uz: All 'yagona narsa' ma'nosini berishi mumkin.
p.ru: All может означать 'единственное, что'.

quiz.ru: The place where… = фокус на месте.

quiz.uz: It was John who sent the email.
quiz.ru: It was John who sent the email.

quiz.uz: What we should do is tell the truth.
quiz.ru: What we should do is tell the truth.

quiz.uz: The reason why he left was the noise.
quiz.ru: The reason why he left was the noise.

grammar.title: Linking & contrast
grammar.lead: Linkers of contrast and concession join ideas that seem to conflict. The right choice depends on whether the linker is followed by a noun, an -ing form, or a full clause.

leadTr.uz: Qarama-qarshilik bog'lovchilari zid fikrlarni birlashtiradi. To'g'ri tanlov bog'lovchidan keyin ot, -ing shakli yoki to'liq gap kelishiga bog'liq: despite + ot, although + gap.
leadTr.ru: Союзы контраста и уступки соединяют противоречащие идеи. Выбор зависит от того, что идёт после: despite + сущ., although + предложение.

ex: Although it was late, we worked.
Even though she tried, she failed.
Despite the rain, we went out.
In spite of being tired, he worked.

p: Followed by a subject + verb.
ex: Although it was late, we kept working. · Even though she tried, she failed.

p: Followed by a noun or -ing form, not a clause. Add ‘the fact that’ to use a clause.
ex: Despite the rain, we went out. · In spite of being tired, he worked. · Despite the fact that it rained…

p: Link two sentences; usually start a new sentence with a comma after.
ex: It was expensive. However, we bought it.

p: Show a direct contrast between two ideas.
ex: He likes tea, whereas she prefers coffee.

grammar.tip: Use ‘although’ before a clause and ‘despite / in spite of’ before a noun or -ing. ‘Despite it was raining’ is wrong → ‘Despite the rain’ or ‘Although it was raining’.
examples: "Although he was rich, he wasn’t happy."
"Despite the traffic, we arrived on time."
