"In spite of feeling ill, she came."
"The plan was risky. Nevertheless, it worked."
"I love cities, whereas my brother prefers the countryside."
"Even though it costs more, it’s worth it."
"It was expensive. However, we bought it."
"Despite the fact that it rained, the match went ahead."

mistakes.x: Despite it was cold, we swam.
mistakes.v: Although it was cold… / Despite the cold… (despite + noun, not a clause)

mistakes.x: Although it was hard but he tried.
mistakes.v: Although it was hard, he tried. (no “but” with although)

quiz.q: ___ it was raining, we went out.
quiz.e: + clause → Although.

quiz.q: ___ the rain, we went out.
quiz.e: + noun → Despite.

quiz.q: He likes coffee, ___ she prefers tea.
quiz.e: Contrast two facts → whereas.

quiz.q: It was expensive. ___, we bought it.
quiz.e: Links two sentences → However.

quiz.q: In spite ___ the cost, they travelled.
quiz.e: in spite of + noun.

quiz.q: ___ being tired, she finished the race.
quiz.e: + -ing → Despite being tired.

quiz.q: ___ he studied hard, he didn't pass.
quiz.e: + clause → Even though.

quiz.q: Choose the linker + clause.
quiz.e: Although + clause.

quiz.q: The food was cold. ___, it tasted fine.
quiz.e: Adverb linking sentences → Nevertheless.

quiz.q: Despite ___ that it was late, they continued.
quiz.e: despite the fact that + clause.

quiz.q: Find the mistake: 'Despite it was cold, we swam.'
quiz.e: Despite + noun/-ing; before a clause use ‘Although’.

quiz.q: Complete: '___ his wealth, he was unhappy, ___ his brother, who had little, was content.'
quiz.e: Despite + noun ‘his wealth’ + whereas (contrast).

quiz.q: Which is correct?
o: In spite the danger, they climbed.
In spite of the danger, they climbed.
In spite of they were in danger, they climbed.
In spite that the danger, they climbed.
quiz.e: in spite of + noun.

quiz.q: Complete: '___ being cheaper, the second option is better, ___ the first looks nicer.'
quiz.e: Despite + -ing ‘being cheaper’ + whereas (contrast).

quiz.q: Choose the sentence that links two contrasting sentences.
o: Although it was hard, however we tried.
It was hard. However, we tried.
However it was hard we tried.
quiz.e: However links two separate sentences.

tip.uz: Gapdan oldin 'although', ot yoki -ing dan oldin 'despite / in spite of' ishlatiladi. 'Despite it was raining' — xato → 'Despite the rain' yoki 'Although it was raining'.
tip.ru: Перед придаточным — 'although', перед существительным или -ing — 'despite / in spite of'. 'Despite it was raining' — ошибка → 'Despite the rain' или 'Although it was raining'.

p.uz: Keyin ega + fe'l keladi.
p.ru: После них идёт подлежащее + глагол.

p.uz: Keyin ot yoki -ing shakli keladi, gap emas. Gap ishlatish uchun 'the fact that' qo'shing.
p.ru: После них — существительное или -ing, а не придаточное. Для придаточного добавьте 'the fact that'.

p.uz: Ikkita gapni bog'laydi; odatda yangi gapni boshlab, keyin vergul qo'yiladi.
p.ru: Связывают два предложения; обычно начинают новое предложение, после — запятая.

p.uz: Ikki g'oya o'rtasidagi to'g'ridan-to'g'ri qarama-qarshilikni ko'rsatadi.
p.ru: Показывают прямой контраст между двумя идеями.

grammar.title: Articles & determiners: advanced
grammar.lead: At B2, article choice depends on shades of meaning: specific vs. general, the use of ‘the’ with unique reference, and fixed patterns with quantifiers and abstract nouns.

leadTr.uz: B2 da artikl tanlash ma'no nozikliklariga bog'liq: aniq va umumiy ma'no, yagona narsalar bilan 'the' hamda mavhum otlar bilan turg'un qoliplar.
leadTr.ru: На B2 выбор артикля зависит от оттенков: конкретное против общего, the с уникальными объектами, устойчивые модели с абстрактными существительными.

ex: The book you lent me was great.
He’s the first to arrive.
Knowledge is power.
The government helps the poor.

p: Use the when context makes the noun specific, after superlatives, and with ‘the only/same/first’.
ex: The book you lent me was great. · He’s the best. · It’s the only way.

p: Use no article for plural and uncountable nouns talking in general.
ex: Happiness matters. · Children learn fast. · I study history.

p: the + adjective can mean a whole group of people.
ex: The rich get richer. · The government helps the unemployed.

p: Use of with the/my/these: ‘most of the students’, ‘none of my friends’; without ‘of’ for general: ‘most students’.
ex: Most of the water was gone. · Most water is recycled here.

grammar.tip: Use ‘the’ when the noun is made specific by context (‘the book you lent me’), but no article for general statements with plurals/uncountables (‘books are useful’).
examples: "The information you gave me was helpful."

mistakes.x: I’m interested in the nature.
mistakes.v: …in nature. (general uncountable → no article)

mistakes.x: He gave me an useful advice.
mistakes.v: He gave me useful advice. (advice is uncountable)

quiz.q: ___ book you recommended was excellent.
quiz.e: Specified by context → The book you recommended.

quiz.q: ___ is important for everyone. (general)
quiz.e: General uncountable → no article.

quiz.q: The government should help ___.
quiz.e: the + adjective = the group: the poor.

quiz.q: ___ of the students passed.
quiz.e: + the → Most of the students.

quiz.q: She's ___ only person who knows.
quiz.e: ‘only’ → the only person.

quiz.q: I love ___ in general. (plural, general)
quiz.e: General plural → no article: dogs.

quiz.q: ___ water in this bottle is dirty.
quiz.e: Specified ‘in this bottle’ → The water.

quiz.q: ___ students learn at different speeds. (general)
quiz.e: General plural → no article.

quiz.q: He was ___ first to finish.
quiz.e: Ordinal → the first.

quiz.q: Choose the general statement.
quiz.e: Abstract general → Life is hard.

quiz.q: Find the mistake: 'I'm interested in the nature.'
quiz.e: General uncountable → nature (no article).

quiz.q: Complete: '___ rich should pay more tax, and ___ advice you gave was wise.'
quiz.e: the rich (group) + the advice (specified).

quiz.q: Which is correct?
o: Most of the people hard work.
quiz.e: General → Most people (no ‘of’ without the).

quiz.q: Complete: 'She studies ___ history of ___ art.'
quiz.e: ‘the history of art’: specified ‘the history’, general ‘art’.

quiz.q: Choose the correct sentence.
o: He gave me an useful advice.
He gave me a useful advice.
He gave me the useful advices.
quiz.e: ‘advice’ is uncountable → no article, no plural.

tip.uz: Ot kontekst orqali aniq bo'lsa 'the' ishlatiladi ('the book you lent me'), ko'plik/sanoqsiz otlar bilan umumiy gaplarda esa artikl ishlatilmaydi ('books are useful').
tip.ru: Используйте 'the', когда существительное конкретизировано контекстом ('the book you lent me'), и нулевой артикль в общих утверждениях с множественными/неисчисляемыми ('books are useful').

p.uz: Kontekst otni aniq qilganda, superlativlardan keyin va 'the only/same/first' bilan the ishlatiladi.
p.ru: the — когда контекст делает существительное конкретным, после превосходной степени и с 'the only/same/first'.

p.uz: Umumiy ma'nodagi ko'plik va sanoqsiz otlar bilan artikl ishlatilmaydi.
p.ru: Без артикля — множественные и неисчисляемые существительные в общем смысле.

p.uz: the + sifat butun bir guruh odamlarni bildirishi mumkin.
p.ru: the + прилагательное может обозначать целую группу людей.

p.uz: the/my/these bilan of ishlatiladi: 'most of the students', 'none of my friends'; umumiy ma'noda 'of'siz: 'most students'.
p.ru: of — с the/my/these: 'most of the students', 'none of my friends'; в общем смысле без 'of': 'most students'.

quiz.uz: Kontekst orqali aniqlangan → The book you recommended.
quiz.ru: Конкретизировано контекстом → The book you recommended.

quiz.uz: 'in this bottle' bilan aniqlangan → The water.
'the history of art': aniqlangan 'the history', umumiy 'art'.
quiz.ru: 'the history of art': конкретное 'the history', общее 'art'.
'advice' неисчисляемое → без артикля и множественного числа.

grammar.title: Participle clauses
grammar.lead: 'Feeling tired, she went home early.' Participle clauses compress two sentences into one elegant line — a hallmark of good written English.

leadTr.uz: 'Feeling tired, she went home early.' Participle clauses ikki gapni bitta nafis qatorga siqadi — bu yaxshi yozma ingliz tilining belgisidir.
leadTr.ru: 'Feeling tired, she went home early.' Причастные обороты сжимают два предложения в одну изящную строку — признак хорошего письменного английского.

grammar.situation: From a company report: "Founded in 2019, the startup now employs forty people. Having secured new investment, it plans to open an office in Samarkand, creating dozens of new jobs."

p: An -ing clause can replace a clause about reason, time, or result when both parts share the same subject: 'Because she felt tired, she left' → 'Feeling tired, she left.'
The -ing form here has active meaning and can refer to present or past — the tense is understood from the main clause.
ex: Knowing the city well, Rustam offered to be our guide.
She sat by the window, watching the rain.
The road was closed, causing long delays.

p: A past participle clause has passive meaning: 'Built in the 15th century, the madrasa attracts thousands of visitors' = 'which was built…'. It often replaces a passive relative clause.
ex: Written in simple English, the report was easy to follow.
The products sold in this shop are all handmade. (= which are sold)
Shocked by the news, Kamola couldn't speak.

p: Use 'having + past participle' to make clear that one action finished before another began: 'Having finished the report, she emailed it to the client.'
Compare: 'Finishing the report, she noticed a mistake' (during) vs 'Having finished the report, she went home' (after). Use the perfect form when the sequence matters.
ex: Having lived in Tashkent for years, he knows every street.
Having passed IELTS, Kamola applied to a university abroad.
Having been warned twice, the driver finally slowed down.

p: The unspoken subject of the participle must be the subject of the main clause. 'Walking to work, the rain started' is wrong — the rain was not walking. Fix it by changing the subject or restoring a full clause: 'Walking to work, I got caught in the rain.'
Participle clauses are common after conjunctions too: 'while waiting', 'when asked', 'if necessary', 'although exhausted'.
ex: Walking to work, I saw an accident. (I was walking)
When asked about the delay, the manager apologised.
While living in Bukhara, she learned to weave carpets.

grammar.tip: Ask: who is doing the -ing action? If it is not the subject of the main clause, the sentence collapses — that is the famous 'dangling participle'.
examples: Founded in 2019, the company has grown rapidly.
Having checked the figures twice, the accountant signed the report.
Students taking the exam tomorrow should arrive by 8:30.

mistakes.x: Driving to Samarkand, the mountains looked beautiful.
mistakes.v: Driving to Samarkand, we thought the mountains looked beautiful. — the participle's subject must match the main clause

mistakes.x: Having finish the project, the team celebrated.
mistakes.v: Having finished the project, the team celebrated. — perfect participle is having + past participle

mistakes.x: The letter sending yesterday arrived today.
mistakes.v: The letter sent yesterday arrived today. — passive meaning needs the past participle

quiz.q: ___ tired after the flight, Kamola went straight to bed.
quiz.e: Same subject, active meaning → present participle: Feeling tired.

quiz.q: ___ in the 15th century, the madrasa is now a museum.
quiz.e: Passive meaning ('it was built') → past participle: Built.

quiz.q: ___ the report, she sent it to her manager.
quiz.e: One action completed before another → having + past participle.

quiz.q: Which sentence contains a dangling participle?
o: Opening the window, I let in some air.
Opening the window, the room felt cooler.
Having opened the window, I sat down.
I opened the window, letting in some air.
quiz.e: The room did not open the window — the participle's subject does not match.

quiz.q: The candidates ___ for the interview should wait in room 4.
quiz.e: The candidates were selected (passive) → past participle: selected.

quiz.q: 'Having been warned twice, the driver slowed down.' The participle form is…
quiz.e: 'Having been + past participle' is the perfect passive participle.

quiz.q: While ___ in Bukhara, she learned to weave carpets.
quiz.e: After conjunctions like while, use the -ing participle: while living.

quiz.q: The bridge collapsed, ___ traffic chaos across the city.
quiz.e: A result of the main clause → -ing clause: causing chaos.

quiz.q: Which is the best one-sentence version of 'Because he knew the answer, he raised his hand'?
o: Known the answer, he raised his hand.
Knowing the answer, he raised his hand.
Having knowing the answer, he raised his hand.
The answer knowing, he raised his hand.
quiz.e: Reason + same subject + active → Knowing the answer, ….

quiz.q: When ___ about the project's delay, the director refused to comment.
quiz.e: The director was asked (passive) → when asked.

situation.uz: Kompaniya hisobotidan: "Founded in 2019, the startup now employs forty people. Having secured new investment, it plans to open an office in Samarkand." — participle clauses rasmiy yozuvni ixcham qiladi.
situation.ru: Из отчёта компании: «Founded in 2019, the startup now employs forty people. Having secured new investment, it plans to open an office in Samarkand.» — причастные обороты делают деловой текст компактным.

tip.uz: So'rang: -ing harakatini kim bajaryapti? Agar bu bosh gapning egasi bo'lmasa, gap buziladi — bu mashhur 'dangling participle' xatosi.
tip.ru: Спросите себя: кто выполняет действие с -ing? Если это не подлежащее главного предложения, конструкция рушится — это и есть знаменитый 'dangling participle'.

p.uz: -ing qurilma sabab, vaqt yoki natija ergash gapining o'rnini bosa oladi, agar ikkala qismning egasi bir xil bo'lsa: 'Because she felt tired, she left' → 'Feeling tired, she left.'
p.ru: Оборот с -ing может заменить придаточное причины, времени или следствия, если у обеих частей одно подлежащее: 'Because she felt tired, she left' → 'Feeling tired, she left.'

p.uz: Bu yerda -ing shakli faol ma'noga ega va hozirgi yoki o'tgan zamonga tegishli bo'lishi mumkin — zamon bosh gapdan anglashiladi.
p.ru: Форма -ing здесь имеет активное значение и может относиться к настоящему или прошлому — время понятно из главного предложения.

p.uz: O'tgan zamon sifatdoshli qurilma majhul (passiv) ma'noga ega: 'Built in the 15th century, the madrasa attracts thousands of visitors' = 'which was built…'. U ko'pincha passiv relative clause o'rnini bosadi.
p.ru: Оборот с past participle имеет пассивное значение: 'Built in the 15th century, the madrasa attracts thousands of visitors' = 'which was built…'. Он часто заменяет пассивное относительное придаточное.

p.uz: Bir harakat ikkinchisidan oldin tugaganini aniq ko'rsatish uchun 'having + past participle' ishlating: 'Having finished the report, she emailed it to the client.'
p.ru: Чтобы ясно показать, что одно действие завершилось до начала другого, используйте 'having + past participle': 'Having finished the report, she emailed it to the client.'

p.uz: Solishtiring: 'Finishing the report, she noticed a mistake' (jarayonda) va 'Having finished the report, she went home' (tugagandan keyin). Ketma-ketlik muhim bo'lsa, perfect shaklni ishlating.
p.ru: Сравните: 'Finishing the report, she noticed a mistake' (в процессе) и 'Having finished the report, she went home' (после завершения). Когда важна последовательность — используйте перфектную форму.

p.uz: Sifatdoshning aytilmagan egasi bosh gapning egasi bo'lishi shart. 'Walking to work, the rain started' — xato: yomg'ir yurmaydi. Egani o'zgartirib yoki to'liq gapni qaytarib tuzating: 'Walking to work, I got caught in the rain.'
p.ru: Невысказанное подлежащее причастия должно совпадать с подлежащим главного предложения. 'Walking to work, the rain started' — ошибка: дождь не шёл на работу. Исправьте, поменяв подлежащее или вернув полное придаточное: 'Walking to work, I got caught in the rain.'

p.uz: Participle qurilmalar bog'lovchilardan keyin ham keng tarqalgan: 'while waiting', 'when asked', 'if necessary', 'although exhausted'.
p.ru: Причастные обороты часто идут и после союзов: 'while waiting', 'when asked', 'if necessary', 'although exhausted'.

quiz.uz: Bir xil ega, faol ma'no → hozirgi zamon sifatdoshi: Feeling tired.
quiz.ru: Одно подлежащее, активное значение → причастие настоящего времени: Feeling tired.

quiz.uz: Majhul ma'no ('it was built') → past participle: Built.
quiz.ru: Пассивное значение ('it was built') → past participle: Built.

quiz.uz: Bir harakat ikkinchisidan oldin tugagan → having + past participle.
quiz.ru: Одно действие завершилось до другого → having + past participle.

quiz.uz: Xona derazani ochmagan — sifatdoshning egasi mos kelmaydi.
quiz.ru: Комната не открывала окно — подлежащее причастия не совпадает.

quiz.uz: Nomzodlar tanlab olingan (passiv) → past participle: selected.
'Having been + past participle' — perfect passiv sifatdosh.
quiz.ru: 'Having been + past participle' — перфектное пассивное причастие.

quiz.uz: While kabi bog'lovchilardan keyin -ing sifatdosh keladi: while living.
quiz.ru: После союзов вроде while используется причастие на -ing: while living.

quiz.uz: Bosh gapning natijasi → -ing qurilma: causing chaos.
quiz.ru: Следствие главного предложения → оборот с -ing: causing chaos.

quiz.uz: Sabab + bir xil ega + faol ma'no → Knowing the answer, ….
quiz.ru: Причина + одно подлежащее + актив → Knowing the answer, ….

grammar.title: Future in the past
grammar.lead: 'I was going to call you, but my phone died.' Learn to talk about the future as it looked from a point in the past — plans, promises and near-misses.

leadTr.uz: 'I was going to call you, but my phone died.' O'tmishdagi nuqtadan qaraganda kelajak qanday ko'ringanini aytishni o'rganing — rejalar, va'dalar va amalga oshmagan niyatlar.
leadTr.ru: 'I was going to call you, but my phone died.' Научитесь говорить о будущем, каким оно виделось из прошлого — планы, обещания и несбывшиеся намерения.

grammar.situation: Rustam: "You missed the meeting yesterday!" Kamola: "I know, I'm sorry. I was going to join online, but just as the call was about to start, the electricity went off. I knew you would manage without me, though."

p: English shifts future forms into the past to describe what was still ahead at a past moment. Will becomes would, is going to becomes was going to, is about to becomes was about to.
You need this constantly in storytelling and reported speech: 'She said she would call' reports 'I will call' from the past.
ex: In 2015 nobody knew the area would become IT Park.
He promised he would help us move house.
We were sure the plan was going to work.

blocks.h: was/were going to: past plans and intentions
p: 'Was/were going to + verb' describes a plan that existed in the past. Very often the plan did NOT happen, and the sentence continues with but: 'I was going to study abroad, but my visa was refused.'
It can also describe a past prediction that came true: 'I knew it was going to rain — and it did.'
ex: We were going to drive to Samarkand, but the car broke down.
Kamola was going to resign; luckily, her manager offered her a new role.
The sky was dark — it was clearly going to storm.

blocks.h: would: the future seen from a narrative past
p: In stories and reports, 'would' marks events that were still in the future at that point: 'At twenty he moved to Tashkent, where he would spend the rest of his life.'
This is common in biographies and history writing — the narrator already knows the outcome and looks forward from a past moment.
ex: She joined the startup in 2020; two years later she would become its CEO.
They said the results would be announced on Friday.
He didn't realise then how important that decision would be.

blocks.h: was about to / was to / was due to
p: 'Was about to + verb' = on the point of doing something: 'I was about to leave when the phone rang.' Add 'just' for extra immediacy.

'Was to + verb' (formal) marks a destined or officially arranged event: 'The president was to visit the region in May.' 'Was due to' is similar for schedules: 'The train was due to arrive at six, but it was late.'
ex: I was just about to email you when you called.
The two leaders were to meet again the following year.
The flight was due to depart at 9:40, but it was delayed by fog.

grammar.tip: 'Was going to' very often signals a broken plan — listeners expect a 'but'. If the plan actually happened, past simple is usually enough: 'I visited Bukhara', not 'I was going to visit Bukhara.'
examples: I was going to text you, but I fell asleep.
Nobody guessed the small company would grow so fast.
The conference was due to start at nine, but the speaker was about to cancel.

mistakes.x: She said she will call me yesterday evening.
mistakes.v: She said she would call me. — in past reporting, will shifts to would

mistakes.x: I was going to called you.
mistakes.v: I was going to call you. — after 'going to', use the base form of the verb

mistakes.x: I was about leaving when he arrived.
mistakes.v: I was about to leave when he arrived. — the pattern is 'be about to + infinitive'

quiz.q: I ___ call you, but my phone died.
quiz.e: A past intention that failed → was going to + verb.

quiz.q: She promised she ___ help us with the move.
quiz.e: Reported from the past: will → would.

quiz.q: I was just ___ leave when the phone rang.
quiz.e: 'Be about to + verb' = on the point of doing something.

quiz.q: He moved to Tashkent in 1998, where he ___ the next twenty years.
quiz.e: Narrative future in the past → would spend.

quiz.q: The train ___ arrive at six, but it was forty minutes late.
quiz.e: Scheduled past event → was due to + verb.

quiz.q: Which sentence most strongly suggests the plan did NOT happen?
o: We drove to Samarkand last weekend.
We were going to drive to Samarkand.
We would often drive to Samarkand.
quiz.e: 'Was/were going to' typically introduces an unfulfilled plan.

quiz.q: 'The ceremony was to take place in Registan Square.' 'Was to' expresses…
quiz.e: Formal 'was to + verb' marks an official or destined arrangement.

quiz.q: Direct: 'The results will be published on Friday.' → They said the results ___ on Friday.
quiz.e: Shift will → would and keep the passive: would be published.

quiz.q: Looking at the black clouds, we knew it ___ rain.
quiz.e: A past prediction from evidence → was going to rain.

quiz.q: Which sentence is wrong?
o: I was about to call you.
I was going to call you.
I would call you the next day, I promised.
I was going to called you.
quiz.e: After 'going to' the verb stays in the base form: going to call.

situation.uz: Rustam: "You missed the meeting yesterday!" Kamola: "I was going to join online, but the electricity went off." — o'tmishdagi reja amalga oshmadi, buni 'was going to' ko'rsatadi.
situation.ru: Rustam: «You missed the meeting yesterday!» Kamola: «I was going to join online, but the electricity went off.» — план из прошлого не сбылся, на это указывает 'was going to'.

tip.uz: 'Was going to' ko'pincha buzilgan rejani bildiradi — tinglovchi 'but' kutadi. Reja amalga oshgan bo'lsa, odatda past simple kifoya: 'I visited Bukhara', 'I was going to visit Bukhara' emas.
tip.ru: 'Was going to' чаще всего сигнализирует о сорвавшемся плане — слушатель ждёт 'but'. Если план осуществился, обычно достаточно past simple: 'I visited Bukhara', а не 'I was going to visit Bukhara'.

p.uz: Ingliz tili o'tmishdagi paytda hali oldinda turgan voqealarni aytish uchun kelasi zamon shakllarini o'tgan zamonga suradi. Will — would, is going to — was going to, is about to — was about to bo'ladi.
p.ru: Английский сдвигает будущие формы в прошлое, чтобы описать то, что ещё было впереди в прошлый момент. Will становится would, is going to — was going to, is about to — was about to.

p.uz: Bu hikoya qilishda va reported speech'da doim kerak: 'She said she would call' o'tmishdan turib 'I will call' ni yetkazadi.
p.ru: Это постоянно нужно в повествовании и в reported speech: 'She said she would call' передаёт 'I will call' из прошлого.

h.uz: was/were going to: o'tmishdagi rejalar va niyatlar
h.ru: was/were going to: планы и намерения в прошлом

p.uz: 'Was/were going to + fe'l' o'tmishda mavjud bo'lgan rejani bildiradi. Ko'pincha reja amalga OSHMAGAN bo'ladi va gap but bilan davom etadi: 'I was going to study abroad, but my visa was refused.'
p.ru: 'Was/were going to + глагол' описывает план, существовавший в прошлом. Очень часто план НЕ осуществился, и предложение продолжается с but: 'I was going to study abroad, but my visa was refused.'

p.uz: U amalga oshgan o'tmish bashoratini ham bildira oladi: 'I knew it was going to rain — and it did.'
p.ru: Он может описывать и сбывшийся прогноз из прошлого: 'I knew it was going to rain — and it did.'

h.ru: would: будущее, увиденное из повествовательного прошлого

p.uz: Hikoya va hisobotlarda 'would' o'sha paytda hali kelajakda bo'lgan voqealarni belgilaydi: 'At twenty he moved to Tashkent, where he would spend the rest of his life.'
p.ru: В рассказах и отчётах 'would' отмечает события, которые в тот момент были ещё впереди: 'At twenty he moved to Tashkent, where he would spend the rest of his life.'

p.uz: Bu biografiya va tarixiy matnlarda keng tarqalgan — hikoyachi natijani allaqachon biladi va o'tmishdagi nuqtadan oldinga qaraydi.
p.ru: Это типично для биографий и исторических текстов — рассказчик уже знает исход и смотрит вперёд из прошлого момента.

h.uz: was about to / was to / was due to
h.ru: was about to / was to / was due to

p.uz: 'Was about to + fe'l' = biror ishni qilish arafasida bo'lmoq: 'I was about to leave when the phone rang.' Yana ham yaqinlik uchun 'just' qo'shing.
p.ru: 'Was about to + глагол' = быть на грани действия: 'I was about to leave when the phone rang.' Для большей непосредственности добавьте 'just'.

p.uz: 'Was to + fe'l' (rasmiy) taqdir qilingan yoki rasmiy belgilangan voqeani bildiradi: 'The president was to visit the region in May.' Jadval uchun 'was due to' o'xshash: 'The train was due to arrive at six, but it was late.'
p.ru: 'Was to + глагол' (формально) отмечает предначертанное или официально запланированное событие: 'The president was to visit the region in May.' Для расписаний похоже работает 'was due to': 'The train was due to arrive at six, but it was late.'

quiz.uz: Amalga oshmagan o'tmish niyati → was going to + fe'l.
quiz.ru: Несбывшееся намерение в прошлом → was going to + глагол.

quiz.uz: 'Be about to + fe'l' = biror ishni qilish arafasida bo'lmoq.
quiz.ru: 'Be about to + глагол' = быть на грани действия.

quiz.uz: Hikoyada o'tmishdan ko'ringan kelajak → would spend.
quiz.ru: Повествовательное будущее в прошлом → would spend.

quiz.uz: O'tmishdagi jadval bo'yicha voqea → was due to + fe'l.
quiz.ru: Событие по расписанию в прошлом → was due to + глагол.

quiz.uz: 'Was/were going to' odatda amalga oshmagan rejani kiritadi.
quiz.ru: 'Was/were going to' обычно вводит несбывшийся план.

quiz.uz: Rasmiy 'was to + fe'l' rasmiy yoki taqdir qilingan kelishuvni bildiradi.
quiz.ru: Формальное 'was to + глагол' отмечает официальную или предначертанную договорённость.

quiz.uz: Will → would ga suriladi, passiv saqlanadi: would be published.
quiz.ru: Will сдвигается в would, пассив сохраняется: would be published.

quiz.uz: Dalilga asoslangan o'tmish bashorati → was going to rain.
quiz.ru: Прогноз в прошлом на основе признаков → was going to rain.

quiz.uz: 'Going to' dan keyin fe'l asosiy shaklda qoladi: going to call.
quiz.ru: После 'going to' глагол остаётся в начальной форме: going to call.

grammar.title: Unreal past: it's time, would rather, as if
grammar.lead: 'It's time we left.' 'I'd rather you didn't.' English uses past forms with present meaning to sound diplomatic, critical or hypothetical — master this hidden system.

leadTr.uz: 'It's time we left.' 'I'd rather you didn't.' Ingliz tili diplomatik, tanqidiy yoki farazli ohang uchun hozirgi ma'noda o'tgan zamon shakllarini ishlatadi — bu yashirin tizimni egallang.
leadTr.ru: 'It's time we left.' 'I'd rather you didn't.' Английский использует прошедшие формы с настоящим значением, чтобы звучать дипломатично, критично или гипотетично — освойте эту скрытую систему.

grammar.situation: It's 11 p.m. at the office. Kamola: "It's high time we went home — you look as if you hadn't slept for days." Rustam: "One more email…" Kamola: "I'd rather you finished it tomorrow. Suppose the system crashed right now — you'd lose it all anyway."

p: After 'It's time + subject', use the past simple with present or future meaning: 'It's time we left' = we should leave now. Adding 'high' or 'about' adds impatience: 'It's high time the government fixed these roads.'
Compare the neutral infinitive version: 'It's time to leave' simply states the time; 'It's time we left' hints that we are already late.
ex: It's time you found your own apartment.
It's high time this old bridge was repaired.
It's time to go. / It's time we went.

p: When you prefer that ANOTHER person do something, use 'would rather + subject + past simple': 'I'd rather you didn't smoke here.' The past form refers to now or the future.
When the same person is the subject of both, use the bare infinitive instead: 'I'd rather stay home tonight.' Do not mix the two patterns up.
ex: I'd rather you paid me in cash.
She'd rather her son studied medicine, but he loves design.
I'd rather walk than take the bus. (same subject → infinitive)

blocks.h: as if / as though + unreal past
p: Use a past form after 'as if / as though' when the comparison is unreal or doubtful: 'He talks as if he owned the company' — he doesn't. For an unreal past comparison, use the past perfect: 'She looked as if she had seen a ghost.'
If the comparison may well be true, a present form is fine: 'It looks as if it's going to rain.'
ex: He spends money as if he were a millionaire.
You look as though you hadn't slept at all.
It sounds as if the meeting went well. (probably real)

p: 'Suppose', 'supposing', 'what if' and 'imagine' also take the unreal past for hypothetical situations now or in the future: 'Suppose you lost your job — what would you do?'
With the past perfect they reach back to unreal past situations: 'Imagine we had never met.' In all these patterns, formal English prefers 'were' for all persons: 'as if he were', 'suppose she were'.
ex: What if we moved the launch to September?
Suppose Kamola were the team lead — would anything change?
Imagine you had grown up in Samarkand.

grammar.tip: Past form ≠ past time. In all these structures the past simple points at the present or future; only the past perfect points at the past: 'as if he knew' (now) vs 'as if he had known' (then).
examples: It's high time we booked the tickets — prices keep rising.
I'd rather you told me the truth now than apologised later.
He gives orders as if he were the director.

mistakes.x: It's time we go home.
mistakes.v: It's time we went home. — after 'it's time + subject', use the past simple

mistakes.x: I'd rather you don't call me after 10 p.m.
mistakes.v: I'd rather you didn't call me after 10 p.m. — 'would rather + subject' takes the past form

mistakes.x: She acts as if she knows everything about it. (she clearly doesn't)
mistakes.v: She acts as if she knew everything about it. — unreal comparisons take the past form

quiz.q: It's high time we ___ home — it's almost midnight.
quiz.e: 'It's (high) time + subject' takes the past simple with present meaning.

quiz.q: I'd rather you ___ me tomorrow, not tonight.
quiz.e: 'Would rather + different subject' takes the past simple.

quiz.q: He talks as if he ___ the company. (he doesn't)
quiz.e: Unreal present comparison after 'as if' → past simple: owned.

quiz.q: She looked as if she ___ a ghost.
quiz.e: Unreal comparison about an earlier moment → past perfect: had seen.

quiz.q: I'd rather ___ at home tonight. (same subject)
quiz.e: Same subject after 'would rather' → bare infinitive: stay.

quiz.q: Suppose you ___ your job — what would you do?
quiz.e: 'Suppose' + hypothetical present/future → past simple: lost.

quiz.q: Which sentence suggests we are already late?
o: It will be time to leave.
quiz.e: 'It's time we left' (past form) implies the action is overdue.

quiz.q: 'It looks as if it ___ going to rain.' (a real possibility)
quiz.e: When the comparison is probably true, use a present form: it looks as if it is going to rain.

quiz.q: Choose the most formal version: 'He behaves as if he ___ the boss.'
quiz.e: Formal English prefers 'were' for all persons in unreal comparisons.

quiz.q: Imagine we ___ in Samarkand instead of Tashkent. (unreal past)
quiz.e: An unreal situation in the past → past perfect: had grown up.

situation.uz: Kechki soat 11, ofis. Kamola: "It's high time we went home — you look as if you hadn't slept for days." — o'tgan zamon shakllari bu yerda hozirgi vaziyat haqida.
situation.ru: 11 вечера, офис. Kamola: «It's high time we went home — you look as if you hadn't slept for days.» — прошедшие формы здесь говорят о настоящем.

tip.uz: O'tgan zamon shakli ≠ o'tgan vaqt. Bu qurilmalarning barchasida past simple hozirgi yoki kelajakka ishora qiladi; faqat past perfect o'tmishga qaraydi: 'as if he knew' (hozir) va 'as if he had known' (o'shanda).
tip.ru: Прошедшая форма ≠ прошедшее время. Во всех этих конструкциях past simple указывает на настоящее или будущее; только past perfect — на прошлое: 'as if he knew' (сейчас) и 'as if he had known' (тогда).

p.uz: 'It's time + ega' dan keyin hozirgi yoki kelajak ma'nosida past simple ishlatiladi: 'It's time we left' = hozir ketishimiz kerak. 'High' yoki 'about' qo'shilsa, sabrsizlik ohang qo'shiladi: 'It's high time the government fixed these roads.'
p.ru: После 'It's time + подлежащее' используется past simple со значением настоящего или будущего: 'It's time we left' = нам пора уходить. 'High' или 'about' добавляют нетерпение: 'It's high time the government fixed these roads.'

p.uz: Neytral infinitivli variant bilan solishtiring: 'It's time to leave' shunchaki vaqtni aytadi; 'It's time we left' allaqachon kechikayotganimizga ishora qiladi.
p.ru: Сравните с нейтральным инфинитивным вариантом: 'It's time to leave' просто констатирует время; 'It's time we left' намекает, что мы уже опаздываем.

p.uz: BOSHQA odam biror ish qilishini istasangiz, 'would rather + ega + past simple' ishlating: 'I'd rather you didn't smoke here.' O'tgan shakl hozirgi yoki kelajakka tegishli.
p.ru: Когда вы предпочитаете, чтобы что-то сделал ДРУГОЙ человек, используйте 'would rather + подлежащее + past simple': 'I'd rather you didn't smoke here.' Прошедшая форма относится к настоящему или будущему.

p.uz: Ikkala qismda ham bir kishi bo'lsa, to'siqsiz infinitiv ishlatiladi: 'I'd rather stay home tonight.' Ikki qolipni aralashtirib yubormang.
p.ru: Если субъект один и тот же, используется инфинитив без to: 'I'd rather stay home tonight.' Не путайте эти два шаблона.

h.uz: as if / as though + noreal o'tgan zamon
h.ru: as if / as though + нереальное прошедшее

p.uz: Qiyoslash noreal yoki shubhali bo'lsa, 'as if / as though' dan keyin o'tgan shakl ishlating: 'He talks as if he owned the company' — aslida egasi emas. Noreal o'tmish qiyosi uchun past perfect: 'She looked as if she had seen a ghost.'
p.ru: Используйте прошедшую форму после 'as if / as though', когда сравнение нереально или сомнительно: 'He talks as if he owned the company' — компанией он не владеет. Для нереального сравнения о прошлом — past perfect: 'She looked as if she had seen a ghost.'

p.uz: Qiyoslash haqiqatga yaqin bo'lsa, hozirgi shakl ham bo'laveradi: 'It looks as if it's going to rain.'
p.ru: Если сравнение вполне может быть правдой, допустима форма настоящего: 'It looks as if it's going to rain.'

h.uz: suppose / what if / imagine + o'tgan zamon
h.ru: suppose / what if / imagine + прошедшее время

p.uz: 'Suppose', 'supposing', 'what if' va 'imagine' ham hozirgi yoki kelajakdagi farazlar uchun noreal o'tgan zamonni oladi: 'Suppose you lost your job — what would you do?'
p.ru: 'Suppose', 'supposing', 'what if' и 'imagine' тоже берут нереальное прошедшее для гипотез о настоящем или будущем: 'Suppose you lost your job — what would you do?'

p.uz: Past perfect bilan ular noreal o'tmish vaziyatlariga qaytadi: 'Imagine we had never met.' Bu qoliplarning barchasida rasmiy ingliz tili barcha shaxslar uchun 'were' ni afzal ko'radi: 'as if he were', 'suppose she were'.
p.ru: С past perfect они обращаются к нереальным ситуациям прошлого: 'Imagine we had never met.' Во всех этих шаблонах формальный английский предпочитает 'were' для всех лиц: 'as if he were', 'suppose she were'.

quiz.uz: 'It's (high) time + ega' hozirgi ma'noda past simple oladi.
quiz.ru: 'It's (high) time + подлежащее' берёт past simple со значением настоящего.

quiz.uz: 'Would rather + boshqa ega' past simple oladi.
quiz.ru: 'Would rather + другое подлежащее' берёт past simple.

quiz.uz: 'As if' dan keyingi noreal hozirgi qiyos → past simple: owned.
quiz.ru: Нереальное сравнение о настоящем после 'as if' → past simple: owned.

quiz.uz: Oldinroq bo'lgan noreal qiyos → past perfect: had seen.
quiz.ru: Нереальное сравнение о более раннем моменте → past perfect: had seen.

quiz.uz: 'Would rather' dan keyin bir xil ega → to'siqsiz infinitiv: stay.
quiz.ru: После 'would rather' при одном субъекте → инфинитив без to: stay.
'Suppose' + гипотеза о настоящем/будущем → past simple: lost.

quiz.uz: 'It's time we left' (o'tgan shakl) ish kechikkanini bildiradi.
quiz.ru: 'It's time we left' (прошедшая форма) намекает, что действие запаздывает.

quiz.uz: Qiyos haqiqatga yaqin bo'lsa, hozirgi shakl ishlatiladi: it looks as if it is going to rain.
quiz.ru: Если сравнение правдоподобно, используется форма настоящего: it looks as if it is going to rain.

quiz.uz: Rasmiy ingliz tili noreal qiyoslarda barcha shaxslar uchun 'were' ni afzal ko'radi.
quiz.ru: Формальный английский предпочитает 'were' для всех лиц в нереальных сравнениях.

quiz.uz: O'tmishdagi noreal vaziyat → past perfect: had grown up.
quiz.ru: Нереальная ситуация в прошлом → past perfect: had grown up.

grammar.title: Subject–verb agreement in long sentences
grammar.lead: When the subject and the verb are separated by long phrases, it becomes easy to match the verb to the wrong noun. Train yourself to find the true subject first — then choose the verb form.

leadTr.uz: Ega va kesim orasida uzun iboralar bo'lsa, fe'lni noto'g'ri otga moslashtirish oson. Avval haqiqiy egani toping — keyin fe'l shaklini tanlang.
leadTr.ru: Когда подлежащее и сказуемое разделены длинными оборотами, легко согласовать глагол не с тем словом. Сначала найдите настоящее подлежащее — затем выбирайте форму глагола.

grammar.situation: "The box of old photographs were in the attic... or was it?" An editor pauses: what is actually in the attic — the box or the photographs? The box. So: 'The box of old photographs WAS in the attic.'

blocks.h: Find the true subject — cross out the middle
p: Long sentences hide the subject behind prepositional phrases ('of...', 'from...', 'in...') and interrupters ('along with...', 'together with...'). None of these change the number of the subject. Mentally cross them out, and the agreement becomes obvious.
The noun closest to the verb is often NOT the subject — that is exactly the trap test writers set.
ex: The collection of handwritten letters HAS been donated. (subject = collection)
The report, together with its appendices, WAS submitted. (subject = the report)
The policy changes announced by the administration HAVE sparked debate. (subject = changes)

blocks.h: Collective nouns: committee, team, jury, series
p: In American English, collective nouns that act as a single unit — committee, team, jury, government, series — take a SINGULAR verb. The group votes, decides, or deliberates as one body.
ex: The committee HAS voted to adopt stricter regulations.
The jury WAS still deliberating when the judge called a recess.
There IS a series of unresolved questions. (a series = singular)

blocks.h: 'A number of' vs. 'the number of' — and each/every
p: 'A number of X' means 'many X' and is PLURAL. 'The number of X' refers to the quantity itself and is SINGULAR. Meanwhile 'each' and 'every' are always singular — even before a long compound like 'every student, teacher, and administrator.'
ex: A number of studies HAVE produced alarming results.
The number of species HAS grown dramatically.
Each of the participating countries HAS agreed to the target.

p: With 'neither...nor' (and 'either...or'), the verb agrees with the CLOSEST subject. In sentences starting with 'There is/are', the subject comes AFTER the verb — find it before you choose.
ex: Neither the budget nor the alternative plans HAVE received support. (closest = plans)
There IS a series of questions about its safety. (subject = a series)

grammar.tip: Cross out everything between the subject and the verb. If the sentence still makes sense, you have found the true subject — now match the verb to it and nothing else.
examples: The quality of the applicants' essays varies enormously.
A number of residents have complained about the noise.
Every laptop, tablet, and phone in the building is encrypted.
Neither the manager nor her assistants were aware of the change.

mistakes.x: The box of old photographs were in the attic.
mistakes.v: The box of old photographs was in the attic. — subject is 'box', not 'photographs'.

mistakes.x: A number of studies has confirmed the effect.
mistakes.v: A number of studies have confirmed the effect. — 'a number of' is plural.

mistakes.x: The team, along with its coaches, were celebrating.
mistakes.v: The team, along with its coaches, was celebrating. — 'along with...' does not make the subject plural.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The collection of handwritten letters from the early twentieth century [___] recently been donated to the university library.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: Cross out 'of handwritten letters from the early twentieth century.' Subject = 'collection' (singular) → has.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The committee on environmental standards [___] voted to adopt stricter regulations on industrial emissions.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: 'Committee' is a collective noun — singular in American English. It acts as a unit → has.

quiz.q:
Text: 'A number of studies examining the long-term effects of sleep deprivation on cognitive function [___] produced alarming results.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: 'A number of X' = PLURAL → have. (Contrast: 'The number of studies HAS grown' — 'the number' = singular.)

quiz.q:
Text: 'The team of researchers, along with several graduate students, [___] presented findings at last month's conference.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: 'Along with several graduate students' is an intervening phrase — cross it out. Subject = 'The team' (singular collective noun) → has.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The number of species affected by climate change [___] grown dramatically since the 1980s.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: 'The number of X' = SINGULAR → has. Cross out 'of species affected by climate change.' Subject = 'the number' → has.

quiz.q:
Text: 'Every student, teacher, and administrator in the district [___] required to complete the new training module.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: When 'every' or 'each' precedes a compound subject joined by 'and,' the subject is still treated as SINGULAR. 'Every student, teacher, and administrator' → singular → is.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The report, together with its supporting appendices, [___] submitted to the board last Friday.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: 'Together with its supporting appendices' is an intervening phrase (cross it out). Subject = 'The report' (singular) → was.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The policy changes announced by the administration [___] sparked widespread debate among educators.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: Cross out the intervening phrase 'announced by the administration.' Subject = 'changes' (plural) → have.

quiz.q:
Text: 'There [___] a series of unresolved questions about the long-term safety of the compound.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: Inverted sentence — find the subject after 'There ___.' Subject = 'a series' (singular collective noun) → is. 'A series of X' = singular.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The jury [___] still deliberating when the judge called for a recess.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: 'Jury' = collective noun, singular in American English → was. The jury acts as a unified body.

quiz.q:
Text: 'Neither the proposed budget nor the alternative plans [___] received sufficient support from the full council.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: 'Neither...nor': verb agrees with the CLOSEST subject. Closest = 'plans' (plural) → have.

quiz.q:
Text: 'Each of the participating countries [___] agreed to reduce carbon emissions by at least 30 percent by 2030.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: 'Each' is always SINGULAR regardless of the following noun. Cross out 'of the participating countries.' Subject = 'each' → has.

situation.uz: "The box of old photographs were in the attic..." — to'g'rimi? Chodirda aslida nima bor — box yoki photographs? Box. Demak: 'The box ... WAS in the attic.' Ega bilan fe'lni to'g'ri moslashtirish uchun avval haqiqiy egani toping.
situation.ru: «The box of old photographs were in the attic...» — верно ли? Что на самом деле на чердаке — box или photographs? Box. Значит: 'The box ... WAS in the attic.' Сначала найдите настоящее подлежащее, затем выбирайте форму глагола.

tip.uz: Ega bilan fe'l orasidagi hamma narsani o'chirib tashlang. Gap ma'nosini saqlasa — haqiqiy egani topdingiz; fe'lni faqat unga moslang.
tip.ru: Вычеркните всё между подлежащим и глаголом. Если смысл сохранился — вы нашли настоящее подлежащее; согласуйте глагол только с ним.

p.uz: Uzun gaplarda ega predlogli iboralar ('of...', 'from...', 'in...') va oradagi qo'shimchalar ('along with...', 'together with...') orqasiga yashirinadi. Ular eganing sonini o'zgartirmaydi — ularni xayolan o'chirsangiz, moslashuv oson ko'rinadi.
p.ru: В длинных предложениях подлежащее прячется за предложными оборотами ('of...', 'from...', 'in...') и вставками ('along with...', 'together with...'). Они не меняют число подлежащего — мысленно вычеркните их, и согласование станет очевидным.

p.uz: Fe'lga eng yaqin ot ko'pincha ega EMAS — testlar aynan shu tuzoqni qo'yadi.
p.ru: Существительное, стоящее ближе всего к глаголу, часто НЕ является подлежащим — именно на этом строится ловушка в тестах.

h.uz: Jamlovchi otlar: committee, team, jury, series
h.ru: Собирательные существительные: committee, team, jury, series

p.uz: Amerika inglizchasida bir butun sifatida harakat qiladigan jamlovchi otlar — committee, team, jury, government, series — BIRLIKDAGI fe'l oladi.
p.ru: В американском английском собирательные существительные, действующие как единое целое — committee, team, jury, government, series — принимают глагол в ЕДИНСТВЕННОМ числе.

h.uz: 'A number of' va 'the number of' — hamda each/every
h.ru: 'A number of' и 'the number of' — а также each/every

p.uz: 'A number of X' — 'ko'p X' degani, KO'PLIK. 'The number of X' — miqdorning o'zi, BIRLIK. 'Each' va 'every' esa doim birlik — hatto uzun qo'shma egadan oldin kelsa ham.
p.ru: 'A number of X' значит «много X» — МНОЖЕСТВЕННОЕ число. 'The number of X' — само количество, ЕДИНСТВЕННОЕ число. 'Each' и 'every' всегда единственное число — даже перед длинным составным подлежащим.

p.uz: 'Neither...nor' (va 'either...or') bilan fe'l ENG YAQIN egaga mos keladi. 'There is/are' bilan boshlangan gaplarda ega fe'ldan KEYIN keladi — avval uni toping.
p.ru: С 'neither...nor' (и 'either...or') глагол согласуется с БЛИЖАЙШИМ подлежащим. В предложениях с 'There is/are' подлежащее стоит ПОСЛЕ глагола — сначала найдите его.

quiz.uz: 'of handwritten letters...' ni o'chiring: ega — 'collection' (birlik) → has.
quiz.ru: Вычеркните 'of handwritten letters...': подлежащее — 'collection' (ед. ч.) → has.

quiz.uz: 'Committee' — jamlovchi ot, Amerika inglizchasida birlik → has.
quiz.ru: 'Committee' — собирательное существительное, в американском английском ед. ч. → has.

quiz.uz: 'A number of X' — KO'PLIK → have ('the number of' esa birlik bo'lardi).
quiz.ru: 'A number of X' — МНОЖЕСТВЕННОЕ число → have (а 'the number of' было бы ед. ч.).

quiz.uz: 'Along with...' — oradagi ibora, o'chiring; ega — 'the team' (birlik) → has.
quiz.ru: 'Along with...' — вставка, вычеркните; подлежащее — 'the team' (ед. ч.) → has.

quiz.uz: 'The number of X' — BIRLIK → has; 'of species...' ni o'chiring.
quiz.ru: 'The number of X' — ЕДИНСТВЕННОЕ число → has; вычеркните 'of species...'.

quiz.uz: 'Every' bilan kelgan qo'shma ega baribir BIRLIK hisoblanadi → is.
quiz.ru: Составное подлежащее с 'every' всё равно считается ЕДИНСТВЕННЫМ числом → is.

quiz.uz: 'Together with...' — oradagi ibora; ega — 'the report' (birlik) → was.
quiz.ru: 'Together with...' — вставка; подлежащее — 'the report' (ед. ч.) → was.

quiz.uz: Teskari tartib: ega 'there' dan keyin — 'a series' (birlik) → is.
quiz.ru: Инверсия: подлежащее после 'there' — 'a series' (ед. ч.) → is.

quiz.uz: 'Neither...nor': fe'l eng yaqin egaga mos — 'plans' (ko'plik) → have.
quiz.ru: 'Neither...nor': глагол согласуется с ближайшим — 'plans' (мн. ч.) → have.

quiz.uz: 'Each' doim birlik → has; 'of the participating countries' ni o'chiring.
quiz.ru: 'Each' всегда ед. ч. → has; вычеркните 'of the participating countries'.

grammar.title: Pronouns: agreement & clear reference
grammar.lead: A pronoun must match its noun in number and refer to it unambiguously. These exercises train both: choosing the right pronoun and keeping the reference clear.

leadTr.uz: Olmosh o'z oti bilan son jihatdan mos kelishi va unga aniq ishora qilishi kerak. Bu mashqlar ikkalasini ham rivojlantiradi: to'g'ri olmoshni tanlash va ishorani aniq saqlash.
leadTr.ru: Местоимение должно совпадать с существительным в числе и однозначно на него указывать. Эти упражнения тренируют и выбор местоимения, и ясность ссылки.

grammar.situation: "The company revised their policy." A careful editor stops: a company is ONE thing, so it needs 'its'. — 'The company revised ITS policy.' Small word, big difference in formal writing.

blocks.h: Match the pronoun to its antecedent in number
p: A pronoun must agree with the noun it replaces (its antecedent). Singular antecedent → singular pronoun; plural antecedent → plural pronoun. The most tested case: institutions and organizations — company, government, university, corporation — are SINGULAR and take 'its', not 'their'.
ex: The government announced ITS intention to reform the tax code.
The university updated ITS admissions policy.
Both the director and the lead actor acknowledged THEIR debt to the playwright.

blocks.h: Indefinite pronouns: each, every, no one, neither
p: 'Each', 'every', 'no one', 'anyone', 'neither' are grammatically SINGULAR. In formal written English they take 'his or her' (or a rewritten plural sentence), not 'their'. Informal English increasingly accepts singular 'they', but exam-style formal writing still expects the singular form.
ex: Each candidate must prepare HIS OR HER own statement.
No one should compromise HIS OR HER principles.
Neither of the researchers would retract HIS OR HER findings.

p: When a committee, team, or board acts as one unit — publishing a report, approving a merger — it takes 'its'. Only when members act separately as individuals does plural phrasing become natural, and formal tests almost always frame the group as a unit.
ex: The committee published ITS annual report.
The board of directors voiced ITS concerns about the valuation.

blocks.h: Keep the reference clear — and don't confuse its/it's
p: A pronoun should point to exactly one noun. If 'it' or 'they' could refer to two different things, rewrite. And remember: 'its' = possessive; 'it's' = 'it is' — never a possessive.
ex: The company and ITS subsidiary both reported strong earnings.
It's clear that the plan failed. (= it is)

grammar.tip: Ask: is the antecedent ONE thing or MANY? Companies, committees, and countries are one thing — 'its'. 'Each', 'every', 'no one', 'neither' are also one — 'his or her' in formal writing.
examples: The corporation restructured its operations to cut costs.
Every employee must badge in with his or her ID card.
Both partners defended their decision to sell.
Each country pledged to increase its defense budget.

mistakes.x: The company revised their policy.
mistakes.v: The company revised its policy. — a company is singular.

mistakes.x: Each student must bring their own laptop. (formal writing)
mistakes.v: Each student must bring his or her own laptop. — 'each' is singular in formal register.

mistakes.x: The committee published it's report.
mistakes.v: The committee published its report. — 'it's' means 'it is'.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The government announced [___] intention to reform the tax code before the end of the fiscal year.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: 'The government' is a singular collective noun → 'its.' A (their) treats it as plural.

quiz.q:
Text: 'Each candidate must prepare [___] own statement of purpose before the interview.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: 'Each' = singular. In formal written English, 'each candidate' takes 'his or her.' C is correct.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The research team, frustrated by the lack of funding, decided to publish [___] preliminary findings independently.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: 'Research team' is a collective noun acting as a unit → singular → 'its.' But as members sharing intellectual agency, 'their' is also increasingly accepted. In this context — 'publish findings' as a unified act — B (its) is more formally precise.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The corporation restructured [___] operations to reduce overhead costs in the wake of declining revenues.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: 'The corporation' = singular → 'its.' A (their) incorrectly treats it as plural.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The company and [___] subsidiary both reported strong earnings for the third quarter.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: 'The company' is singular. 'Its subsidiary' — the subsidiary belongs to the singular company → 'its.' A is correct.

quiz.q:
Text: 'No one should be forced to compromise [___] principles simply to advance a career.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: 'No one' = SINGULAR indefinite pronoun → 'his or her' in formal register. C is correct.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The committee published [___] annual report outlining the progress made toward achieving sustainability goals.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: 'The committee' = singular collective noun → 'its.' D is correct. A (their) is incorrect for a singular noun. B (it's) = 'it is' — wrong word.

quiz.q:
Text: 'Both the director and the lead actor acknowledged [___] debt to the playwright's original vision.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: 'Both X and Y' = plural → 'their.' C is correct. They share a collective debt.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The university updated [___] admissions policy to consider a wider range of socioeconomic factors.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: 'The university' = singular → 'its.' C is correct. A (their) is plural. B (it's) = 'it is.'

quiz.q:
Text: 'Each country in the alliance pledged to increase [___] defense budget by two percent over the next decade.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: 'Each country' — 'each' modifies 'country' (singular) → 'its.' B is correct. Though 'their' is increasingly used informally, 'its' is more formally precise for a singular noun.

quiz.q:
Text: 'Neither of the lead researchers was willing to retract [___] published findings without further evidence.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: 'Neither of the lead researchers' — 'neither' is singular → 'his or her.' B is correct.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The board of directors voted to approve the merger despite [___] concerns about the valuation.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: 'The board of directors' = singular collective noun → 'its.' A is correct. The board as a unified body has 'its' concerns.

situation.uz: "The company revised their policy." Diqqatli muharrir to'xtaydi: kompaniya — BITTA narsa, demak 'its' kerak: 'The company revised ITS policy.' Kichkina so'z, lekin rasmiy yozuvda katta farq.
situation.ru: «The company revised their policy.» Внимательный редактор останавливается: компания — ОДНА, значит нужно 'its': 'The company revised ITS policy.' Маленькое слово — большая разница в формальном письме.

tip.uz: So'rang: oldingi ot BITTAMI yoki KO'PMI? Kompaniya, qo'mita, davlat — bitta narsa → 'its'. 'Each', 'every', 'no one', 'neither' ham birlik → rasmiy yozuvda 'his or her'.
tip.ru: Спросите себя: антецедент — ОДИН или МНОГО? Компания, комитет, страна — одно целое → 'its'. 'Each', 'every', 'no one', 'neither' тоже ед. ч. → в формальном письме 'his or her'.

h.uz: Olmoshni oldingi ot bilan sonda moslang
h.ru: Согласуйте местоимение с антецедентом в числе

p.uz: Olmosh o'zi almashtirayotgan otga (antecedent) mos kelishi kerak: birlik ot → birlik olmosh, ko'plik → ko'plik. Eng ko'p tekshiriladigan holat: tashkilotlar — company, government, university, corporation — BIRLIK va 'their' emas, 'its' oladi.
p.ru: Местоимение должно согласовываться с существительным, которое оно заменяет (антецедентом): ед. ч. → ед. ч., мн. ч. → мн. ч. Самый частый тестовый случай: организации — company, government, university, corporation — ЕДИНСТВЕННОЕ число и берут 'its', а не 'their'.

h.uz: Noaniq olmoshlar: each, every, no one, neither
h.ru: Неопределённые местоимения: each, every, no one, neither

p.uz: 'Each', 'every', 'no one', 'anyone', 'neither' grammatik jihatdan BIRLIK. Rasmiy yozma inglizchada ular 'their' emas, 'his or her' oladi. Norasmiy tilda singular 'they' tobora ko'p qabul qilinadi, lekin imtihon uslubidagi rasmiy yozuv hali ham birlik shaklni kutadi.
p.ru: 'Each', 'every', 'no one', 'anyone', 'neither' грамматически ЕДИНСТВЕННОЕ число. В формальном письменном английском они требуют 'his or her', а не 'their'. В неформальной речи всё чаще допустимо singular 'they', но экзаменационный формальный стиль по-прежнему ожидает форму ед. ч.

p.uz: Qo'mita, jamoa yoki kengash bir butun sifatida harakat qilsa — hisobot chiqarsa, qo'shilishni tasdiqlasa — 'its' oladi. Rasmiy testlar deyarli har doim guruhni bir butun sifatida ko'rsatadi.
p.ru: Когда комитет, команда или совет действуют как единое целое — публикуют отчёт, одобряют сделку — используется 'its'. Формальные тесты почти всегда подают группу как единое целое.

h.uz: Havolani aniq saqlang — its/it's ni adashtirmang
h.ru: Сохраняйте ясность ссылки — не путайте its/it's

p.uz: Olmosh aynan bitta otga ishora qilishi kerak; 'it' yoki 'they' ikki narsaga tegishli bo'lishi mumkin bo'lsa, gapni qayta yozing. Va esda tuting: 'its' — egalik, 'it's' — 'it is'.
p.ru: Местоимение должно указывать ровно на одно существительное; если 'it' или 'they' могут относиться к двум вещам — перепишите. И помните: 'its' — притяжательное, 'it's' — это 'it is'.

quiz.ru: 'Each' — ед. ч.; в формальном письме 'his or her'.

quiz.uz: 'Research team' bir butun sifatida harakat qiladi → 'its'.

quiz.ru: Дочерняя компания принадлежит компании в ед. ч. → 'its'.

quiz.uz: 'No one' — birlikdagi noaniq olmosh → rasmiy uslubda 'his or her'.
quiz.ru: 'No one' — неопределённое местоимение ед. ч. → в формальном стиле 'his or her'.
'The committee' — ед. ч. → 'its'; 'it's' = 'it is' — не то слово.
'Each country' — 'each' определяет существительное в ед. ч. → 'its'.

quiz.uz: 'The board of directors' — jamlovchi ot, birlik → 'its'.
quiz.ru: 'The board of directors' — собирательное существительное, ед. ч. → 'its'.

grammar.title: Commas & semicolons
grammar.lead: The comma and the semicolon are where most writing mistakes live. Learn when two ideas need a semicolon, when a comma is enough, and when neither belongs.

leadTr.uz: Vergul va nuqtali vergul — yozuvdagi xatolarning ko'pchiligi shu yerda. Ikki fikr qachon nuqtali vergul talab qilishini, qachon vergul yetarli ekanini o'rganing.
leadTr.ru: Запятая и точка с запятой — где живёт большинство ошибок письма. Учитесь понимать, когда двум идеям нужна точка с запятой, когда достаточно запятой, а когда не нужно ничего.

grammar.situation: "The results were clear, the team celebrated." Something feels off — two complete sentences glued with only a comma. Either write '...clear; the team celebrated' or '...clear, and the team celebrated.'

blocks.h: Semicolon: two independent clauses, no conjunction
p: A semicolon joins two complete sentences that are closely related. A comma alone in that position is the classic 'comma splice' error. Test: can each side stand alone as a sentence? If yes, you need a semicolon, a period, or a comma PLUS a conjunction.
ex: The experiment produced unexpected results; the team redesigned the protocol.
Scientists have long studied sleep deprivation; researchers continue to find new consequences.

p: When two independent clauses are joined by a coordinating conjunction (for, and, nor, but, or, yet, so — FANBOYS), put a comma before it. An introductory dependent clause or phrase ('Although...', 'After analyzing the data...') is always followed by a comma.
ex: The architect designed the museum, but the city lacked funding.
Although the forecast predicted rain, the ceremony proceeded as planned.
After analyzing three years of data, the researchers published their conclusions.

blocks.h: Restrictive vs. nonrestrictive: commas in pairs
p: Nonrestrictive elements — extra information that could be deleted — take commas on BOTH sides: 'The bridge, which was built in 1923, still stands.' Restrictive elements identify WHICH one you mean and take NO commas: 'The students who complete the coursework will graduate.'
The most common exam trap: the opening comma is given, and you must supply the CLOSING comma of the pair.
ex: Dr. Chen, the lead researcher, presented her findings. (nonrestrictive appositive)
The students who complete all coursework will graduate. (restrictive — no commas)
The novel, written over ten years, draws on her life abroad.

p: Separate three or more items with commas, including before the final 'and' (the Oxford comma, standard in American academic style). Use semicolons between items only when the items themselves contain commas.
ex: The park features hiking trails, a botanical garden, and an amphitheater.
The bill was praised by economists, criticized by unions, and debated in the press.

grammar.tip: Two complete sentences can NEVER be joined by a comma alone. Your options: period, semicolon, comma + FANBOYS, or making one clause dependent (because, although, when...).
examples: The data was incomplete; the committee postponed its decision.
Although the trial was small, the results were striking.
Her latest book, published last spring, has already been translated twice.
We packed water, sunscreen, and a map.

mistakes.x: The results were clear, the team celebrated.
mistakes.v: The results were clear; the team celebrated. — comma splice: use a semicolon.

mistakes.x: The bridge, which was built in 1923 has withstood earthquakes.
mistakes.v: The bridge, which was built in 1923, has withstood earthquakes. — nonrestrictive clauses need commas on both sides.

mistakes.x: The students, who complete all coursework, will graduate in May.
mistakes.v: The students who complete all coursework will graduate in May. — restrictive clause: no commas.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The experiment produced unexpected results[___] the team immediately redesigned the protocol.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: Two independent clauses. C (semicolon) correctly joins them.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The bridge, which was built in 1923[___] has withstood numerous earthquakes without significant structural damage.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: 'Which was built in 1923' is a NONRESTRICTIVE clause — it adds information but doesn't identify which bridge. Nonrestrictive elements need commas on BOTH sides. The opening comma is present; a closing comma is needed here. A (,) is correct.

quiz.q:
Text: 'After carefully analyzing three years of climate data[___] the researchers concluded that temperatures had risen faster than projected.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: An introductory participial phrase ('After carefully analyzing...') must be followed by a comma before the main clause. C (,) is correct.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The students who complete all required coursework[___] will be eligible to graduate in May.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: 'Who complete all required coursework' is RESTRICTIVE — it identifies WHICH students (not all students, only those who complete coursework). No commas around restrictive clauses. B (no punctuation) is correct.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The novel, written over a period of ten years[___] draws on the author's experiences living in three different countries.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: 'Written over a period of ten years' is a nonrestrictive participial phrase providing extra information about the novel. It needs commas on BOTH sides. The opening comma is already there; a closing comma is needed. B (,) is correct.

quiz.q:
Text: 'Scientists have long studied the effects of sleep deprivation[___] researchers continue to discover new neurological consequences.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: Two independent clauses. A comma alone = comma splice (A wrong). C (semicolon) correctly joins two independent clauses. B adds 'and' with a comma — also grammatically correct, but since we're choosing from four options, C (semicolon) is the clean correct punctuation choice.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The park features hiking trails, a botanical garden[___] and a small amphitheater for outdoor performances.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: Series of three items: 'hiking trails, a botanical garden, and a small amphitheater.' Standard comma before 'and' in a series (Oxford comma). C (,) is correct. A semicolon would only be needed if the items had internal commas.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The proposal was rejected[___] the board felt it lacked sufficient financial justification.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: "Because" makes the second clause dependent: "rejected because the board felt..." C is natural and correct.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The architect designed the museum[___] but the city lacked funding to build it for another decade.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: Two independent clauses joined by 'but' (FANBOYS) require a comma before 'but.' C (,) is correct.

quiz.q:
Text: 'Dr. Chen, the lead researcher on the project[___] presented her findings at the international conference.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: 'The lead researcher on the project' is a NONRESTRICTIVE appositive (renames Dr. Chen). It needs commas on both sides. The opening comma is present; a closing comma is needed. C (,) is correct.

quiz.q:
Text: 'Although the weather forecast predicted rain[___] the outdoor ceremony proceeded as planned.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: 'Although the weather forecast predicted rain' is an introductory dependent clause. Must be followed by a comma before the main clause. C (,) is correct.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The legislation was praised by economists[___] criticized by labor unions, and debated extensively in the press.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: This is a series: 'praised by economists, criticized by labor unions, and debated...' The comma after 'economists' is needed to separate the first and second items in the series. B (,) is correct.

situation.uz: "The results were clear, the team celebrated." Nimadir noto'g'ri — ikkita to'liq gap faqat vergul bilan yopishtirilgan. To'g'risi: '...clear; the team celebrated' yoki '...clear, and the team celebrated.'
situation.ru: «The results were clear, the team celebrated.» Что-то не так — два полных предложения склеены одной запятой. Правильно: '...clear; the team celebrated' или '...clear, and the team celebrated.'

tip.uz: Ikkita to'liq gapni faqat vergul bilan bog'lab BO'LMAYDI. Variantlar: nuqta, nuqtali vergul, vergul + FANBOYS, yoki bir gapni ergash gapga aylantirish (because, although, when...).
tip.ru: Два полных предложения НЕЛЬЗЯ соединить одной запятой. Варианты: точка, точка с запятой, запятая + FANBOYS или превращение одного из них в придаточное (because, although, when...).

h.uz: Nuqtali vergul: ikkita mustaqil gap, bog'lovchisiz
h.ru: Точка с запятой: два независимых предложения без союза

p.uz: Nuqtali vergul o'zaro yaqin ikkita to'liq gapni bog'laydi. Bu o'rinda faqat vergul — mashhur 'comma splice' xatosi. Tekshiruv: har ikki tomon alohida gap bo'la oladimi? Ha bo'lsa — nuqtali vergul, nuqta yoki vergul + bog'lovchi kerak.
p.ru: Точка с запятой соединяет два тесно связанных полных предложения. Одна запятая в этой позиции — классическая ошибка 'comma splice'. Проверка: может ли каждая часть быть отдельным предложением? Если да — нужна точка с запятой, точка или запятая + союз.

p.uz: Ikkita mustaqil gap muvofiqlashtiruvchi bog'lovchi (for, and, nor, but, or, yet, so — FANBOYS) bilan bog'lansa, bog'lovchidan oldin vergul qo'yiladi. Kirish ergash gap yoki ibora ('Although...', 'After analyzing...') dan keyin doim vergul keladi.
p.ru: Если два независимых предложения соединены сочинительным союзом (for, and, nor, but, or, yet, so — FANBOYS), перед союзом ставится запятая. После вводного придаточного или оборота ('Although...', 'After analyzing...') всегда идёт запятая.

h.uz: Restrictive va nonrestrictive: vergullar juft bo'ladi

p.uz: Nonrestrictive elementlar — olib tashlansa ham gap buzilmaydigan qo'shimcha ma'lumot — IKKI tomondan vergul oladi. Restrictive elementlar QAYSI birini nazarda tutayotganingizni aniqlaydi va vergul OLMAYDI.
p.ru: Nonrestrictive элементы — дополнительная информация, которую можно убрать — выделяются запятыми с ОБЕИХ сторон. Restrictive элементы определяют, О КАКОМ именно предмете речь, и запятых НЕ получают.

p.uz: Eng keng tarqalgan imtihon tuzog'i: ochuvchi vergul berilgan, siz juftlikning YOPUVCHI vergulini qo'yishingiz kerak.
p.ru: Самая частая экзаменационная ловушка: открывающая запятая уже стоит, а вам нужно поставить ЗАКРЫВАЮЩУЮ запятую пары.

p.uz: Uch va undan ortiq elementni vergul bilan ajrating, oxirgi 'and' dan oldin ham (Oxford comma — Amerika akademik uslubida standart). Elementlar ichida vergul bo'lsagina ular orasida nuqtali vergul ishlatiladi.
p.ru: Три и более элемента разделяются запятыми, включая запятую перед финальным 'and' (Oxford comma — стандарт американского академического стиля). Точки с запятой между элементами нужны только когда сами элементы содержат запятые.

quiz.ru: Два независимых предложения → точка с запятой.

quiz.uz: Nonrestrictive gap ikki tomondan vergul oladi — yopuvchi vergul kerak.
quiz.ru: Nonrestrictive оборот выделяется запятыми с двух сторон — нужна закрывающая запятая.

quiz.uz: Kirish iborasidan keyin asosiy gapdan oldin vergul kerak.
quiz.ru: После вводного оборота перед главным предложением нужна запятая.

quiz.uz: Restrictive gap — qaysi talabalar ekanini aniqlaydi → vergul yo'q.
quiz.ru: Restrictive оборот определяет, какие именно студенты → без запятых.

quiz.uz: Nonrestrictive ibora — juftlikning yopuvchi verguli kerak.
quiz.ru: Nonrestrictive оборот — нужна закрывающая запятая пары.

quiz.uz: Ikkita mustaqil gap: faqat vergul — comma splice; nuqtali vergul to'g'ri.
quiz.ru: Два независимых предложения: одна запятая — comma splice; верна точка с запятой.

quiz.uz: Uchta elementli sanash: 'and' dan oldin standart vergul.
quiz.ru: Перечисление из трёх элементов: стандартная запятая перед 'and'.

quiz.uz: 'Because' ikkinchi gapni ergash gapga aylantiradi — tabiiy va to'g'ri.
quiz.ru: 'Because' делает вторую часть придаточной — естественно и правильно.

quiz.uz: 'But' (FANBOYS) bilan bog'langan ikki mustaqil gap → 'but' dan oldin vergul.
quiz.ru: Два независимых предложения с 'but' (FANBOYS) → запятая перед 'but'.

quiz.uz: Nonrestrictive appositive — ikki tomondan vergul; yopuvchisi kerak.
quiz.ru: Nonrestrictive приложение — запятые с двух сторон; нужна закрывающая.

quiz.uz: 'Although...' — kirish ergash gap → undan keyin vergul.
Sanash: birinchi va ikkinchi elementni ajratish uchun vergul kerak.
quiz.ru: Перечисление: запятая отделяет первый элемент от второго.

grammar.title: Verb tense in context
grammar.lead: Real texts mix tenses constantly. These items give you a sentence with surrounding context — your job is to keep the timeline consistent.

leadTr.uz: Haqiqiy matnlarda zamonlar doim aralashadi. Bu mashqlarda kontekstli gap beriladi — vazifangiz voqealar chizig'ini izchil saqlash.
leadTr.ru: В настоящих текстах времена постоянно смешиваются. Здесь дано предложение с контекстом — ваша задача сохранить хронологию последовательной.

grammar.situation: "By the time the ambulance arrived, the crowd had already moved the injured cyclist." One sentence, two past events — and the earlier one is marked with past perfect. Context decides the tense.

blocks.h: Ordering past events: simple past, past progressive, past perfect
p: Simple past narrates completed events in sequence ('excavated... found'). Past progressive shows an action in progress at a past moment ('mold WAS KILLING the bacteria when Fleming noticed'). Past perfect ('had dropped') marks the EARLIER of two past events — the signal phrase 'by the time + past event' almost always demands it.
ex: When the archaeologists excavated the site, they found older ruins.
Fleming noticed that mold was killing the bacteria.
By the time the team reached them, temperatures had dropped for eighteen hours.

blocks.h: Present perfect and future perfect: linking to a reference point
p: Present perfect ('have concluded') connects a past action to NOW — current scientific understanding, results that still matter. Future perfect ('will have converted') looks back from a future deadline: 'by 2030' + will have + past participle.
ex: Researchers have concluded that the species went extinct 65 million years ago.
Scientists have estimated a rise of 1.1°C since pre-industrial times.
By 2030, the company will have converted all operations to renewables.

p: After 'recommend that', 'require that', 'insist that', 'suggest that', formal English uses the BASE form of the verb for all subjects — no -s, no tense marking: 'recommended that the facilities BE accessible', 'required that every employee COMPLETE the training'.
ex: The committee recommended that the facilities be accessible.
The policy required that every employee complete the course.
The judge insisted that the witness read the entire transcript.

p: Present unreal: 'If the treatment WERE more affordable, patients WOULD benefit' — 'were' for all subjects. Past unreal: 'If the proposal HAD BEEN submitted, it WOULD HAVE BEEN considered' — had + past participle in the if-clause, would have + past participle in the result.
ex: If the treatment were cheaper, more patients would benefit.
If renewable energy had become cheaper faster, the transition would have occurred earlier.

grammar.tip: Scan for time anchors before choosing: 'by the time + past' → had done; 'by + future year' → will have done; 'recommend/require/insist that' → base verb; 'if... would have' → had done.
examples: By the time the votes were counted, the challenger had conceded.
The board demanded that the CEO resign immediately.
If the dam had been reinforced, the flood would have caused far less damage.
By next June, she will have completed her residency.

mistakes.x: By the time we arrived, the lecture already started.
mistakes.v: By the time we arrived, the lecture had already started. — the earlier past event needs past perfect.

mistakes.x: The committee recommended that the report is published.
mistakes.v: The committee recommended that the report be published. — subjunctive: base verb after 'recommended that'.

mistakes.x: If the proposal was submitted on time, it would have been funded.
mistakes.v: If the proposal had been submitted on time, it would have been funded. — past unreal condition takes 'had been'.

quiz.q:
Text: 'In 1928, Alexander Fleming noticed that mold [___] the bacteria in his petri dish, leading to the discovery of penicillin.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: The passage describes events in 1928 (past). 'Was killing' = past progressive, showing the ongoing action at the time of his observation. D is correct.

quiz.q:
Text: 'By the time the rescue team reached the stranded climbers, temperatures [___] below freezing for over eighteen hours.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: 'By the time [past event]' requires PAST PERFECT to show the temperature drop preceded the rescue. B (had dropped) is correct.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The committee recommended that the new facilities [___] accessible to all students with disabilities.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: 'Recommended that' + SUBJECT + BASE VERB (subjunctive). C (be) is correct.

quiz.q:
Text: 'If the treatment [___] more affordable, many patients who currently cannot access it would benefit significantly.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: Contrary-to-fact condition (treatment is NOT currently affordable). 'Were' for all subjects in hypothetical conditions. C is correct.

quiz.q:
Text: 'Researchers studying the fossilized remains [___] that the species went extinct approximately 65 million years ago.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: Present perfect (have concluded) shows ongoing/current relevance — researchers have concluded (and this is the current scientific understanding). A is correct.

quiz.q:
Text: 'If the proposal [___] submitted before the deadline, it would have been considered for funding.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: Contrary-to-fact past (it was NOT submitted): 'If it HAD BEEN submitted' + 'would have been considered.' C (had been) is correct.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The policy required that every employee [___] a mandatory safety training course before beginning work.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: 'Required that' + subjunctive: BASE VERB. C (complete) is correct.

quiz.q:
Text: 'By 2030, the company [___] all of its operations to renewable energy sources.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: 'By 2030' (a future deadline) + FUTURE PERFECT to show completion by that point. C (will have converted) is correct.

quiz.q:
Text: 'When the archaeologists [___] the site, they found evidence of a civilization far older than previously thought.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: Sequential past events: 'excavated...found.' Both in simple past since they happened at roughly the same time (the finding was part of the excavation). D is correct.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The judge insisted that the witness [___] the entire transcript without interruption.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: 'Insisted that' + subjunctive: BASE VERB. B (read) is correct.

quiz.q:
Text: 'Scientists [___] that the average global temperature has risen by approximately 1.1°C since pre-industrial times.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
