quiz.e: Current scientific consensus with past-to-present relevance → PRESENT PERFECT. C (have estimated) is correct.

quiz.q:
Text: 'If renewable energy [___] cheaper faster, the transition from fossil fuels would have occurred decades earlier.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: Contrary-to-fact past: 'If it HAD BECOME cheaper' + 'would have occurred.' B is correct.

situation.uz: "By the time the ambulance arrived, the crowd had already moved the injured cyclist." Bitta gap, ikkita o'tgan voqea — oldinroq bo'lgani past perfect bilan belgilanadi. Zamonni kontekst hal qiladi.
situation.ru: «By the time the ambulance arrived, the crowd had already moved the injured cyclist.» Одно предложение, два прошлых события — более раннее отмечено past perfect. Время выбирает контекст.

tip.uz: Tanlashdan oldin vaqt belgilarini qidiring: 'by the time + o'tgan zamon' → had done; 'by + kelasi yil' → will have done; 'recommend/require/insist that' → asosiy shakl; 'if... would have' → had done.
tip.ru: Перед выбором ищите временные ориентиры: 'by the time + прошедшее' → had done; 'by + будущий год' → will have done; 'recommend/require/insist that' → базовая форма; 'if... would have' → had done.

h.uz: O'tgan voqealar tartibi: simple past, past progressive, past perfect
h.ru: Порядок прошлых событий: simple past, past progressive, past perfect

p.uz: Simple past ketma-ket tugagan voqealarni bayon qiladi. Past progressive o'tgan paytdagi davom etayotgan harakatni ko'rsatadi. Past perfect ikki o'tgan voqeadan OLDINROQ bo'lganini belgilaydi — 'by the time + o'tgan zamon' iborasi deyarli har doim uni talab qiladi.
p.ru: Simple past описывает завершённые события по порядку. Past progressive показывает действие в процессе в прошлый момент. Past perfect отмечает БОЛЕЕ РАННЕЕ из двух прошлых событий — сигнал 'by the time + прошедшее' почти всегда требует его.

h.uz: Present perfect va future perfect: tayanch nuqtaga bog'lash
h.ru: Present perfect и future perfect: привязка к опорной точке

p.uz: Present perfect ('have concluded') o'tgan harakatni HOZIR bilan bog'laydi — hozirgi ilmiy xulosa, hali ham muhim natijalar. Future perfect ('will have converted') kelajakdagi muddatdan orqaga qaraydi: 'by 2030' + will have + past participle.
p.ru: Present perfect ('have concluded') связывает прошлое действие с НАСТОЯЩИМ — текущий научный вывод, всё ещё значимые результаты. Future perfect ('will have converted') смотрит назад от будущего срока: 'by 2030' + will have + past participle.

p.uz: 'Recommend that', 'require that', 'insist that', 'suggest that' dan keyin rasmiy inglizchada barcha egalar uchun fe'lning ASOSIY shakli ishlatiladi — -s siz, zamon belgisisiz.
p.ru: После 'recommend that', 'require that', 'insist that', 'suggest that' формальный английский использует БАЗОВУЮ форму глагола для всех лиц — без -s и без показателей времени.

p.uz: Hozirgi noreal: 'If the treatment WERE more affordable...' — hamma egalar uchun 'were'. O'tgan noreal: if-gapda had + past participle, natijada would have + past participle.
p.ru: Нереальное настоящее: 'If the treatment WERE more affordable...' — 'were' для всех лиц. Нереальное прошлое: в if-части had + past participle, в результате would have + past participle.

quiz.uz: 1928-yildagi voqea: kuzatuv paytida davom etayotgan harakat → past progressive 'was killing'.
quiz.ru: Событие 1928 года: действие в процессе в момент наблюдения → past progressive 'was killing'.

quiz.uz: 'By the time + o'tgan voqea' → oldinroq bo'lgan harakat past perfect: 'had dropped'.
quiz.ru: 'By the time + прошлое событие' → более раннее действие в past perfect: 'had dropped'.

quiz.uz: Haqiqatga zid hozirgi shart → hamma egalar uchun 'were'.
quiz.ru: Нереальное условие в настоящем → 'were' для всех лиц.

quiz.uz: Hozirgi ilmiy xulosa → present perfect 'have concluded'.
quiz.ru: Текущий научный вывод → present perfect 'have concluded'.

quiz.uz: O'tgan noreal shart: 'if it HAD BEEN submitted' + 'would have been considered'.
quiz.ru: Нереальное прошлое: 'if it HAD BEEN submitted' + 'would have been considered'.

quiz.uz: 'By 2030' — kelajak muddati → future perfect 'will have converted'.
quiz.ru: 'By 2030' — будущий срок → future perfect 'will have converted'.

quiz.uz: Ketma-ket o'tgan voqealar → ikkalasi simple past: 'excavated... found'.
quiz.ru: Последовательные прошлые события → оба в simple past: 'excavated... found'.

quiz.uz: O'tmishdan hozirgacha dolzarb xulosa → present perfect 'have estimated'.
quiz.ru: Вывод, актуальный от прошлого до настоящего → present perfect 'have estimated'.

quiz.uz: O'tgan noreal shart: 'had become' + 'would have occurred'.

grammar.title: Transitions between ideas
grammar.lead: However, therefore, meanwhile, in contrast… The right connector shows the logical relationship between two sentences. Read both sides of the blank before choosing.

leadTr.uz: However, therefore, meanwhile… To'g'ri bog'lovchi ikki gap orasidagi mantiqiy aloqani ko'rsatadi. Tanlashdan oldin bo'sh joyning ikkala tomonini ham o'qing.
leadTr.ru: However, therefore, meanwhile… Правильная связка показывает логическую связь между предложениями. Прочитайте обе стороны пропуска, прежде чем выбирать.

grammar.situation: "The lab results were promising. However, the clinical trial failed." Change 'However' to 'Therefore' and the paragraph stops making sense. The connector IS the logic of the text.

blocks.h: Contrast: however, nevertheless, yet, by contrast
p: 'However' and 'yet' signal a simple reversal of direction. 'Nevertheless' is stronger: something happens DESPITE what the first sentence established. 'By contrast' sets two different subjects or views side by side (internal causes vs. external causes, proponents vs. critics).
ex: The drug worked in the lab. However, human trials revealed side effects.
The harms are well documented. Nevertheless, sleep deprivation keeps rising.
Some blame internal corruption. By contrast, others emphasize external pressures.

p: Use addition connectors when the second sentence points in the SAME direction as the first — another benefit, another piece of confirming evidence. If sentence two supports or extends sentence one, do not reach for a contrast word.
ex: The pottery suggests 3000 BCE. Moreover, carbon dating confirms the early date.
Transit cut commute times. Additionally, it lowered carbon emissions.

blocks.h: Cause and effect: consequently, as a result, therefore
p: When sentence one is the cause and sentence two is its outcome, use a result connector. Check the direction: the cause must come first for 'consequently / as a result / therefore' to fit.
ex: Costs fell 40%. Consequently, retail prices dropped.
The libraries lost funding. As a result, many branches reduced their hours.

blocks.h: Clarification: that is, in other words
p: Sometimes sentence two neither contrasts nor results — it RESTATES or explains the mechanism behind sentence one. 'That is' and 'in other words' introduce this reformulation. Confusing clarification with cause/effect is a favorite distractor.
ex: Moderate pressure improves decisions. That is, some deadline stress focuses attention.
The signal is costly. In other words, only a fit bird can afford the tail.

grammar.tip: Read the sentence BEFORE the blank and the sentence AFTER it, and ask: same direction (addition), opposite direction (contrast), cause → effect (result), or a restatement (that is)? Choose the relationship, then the word.
examples: Sales rose steadily. Meanwhile, profits barely moved.
The theory was elegant. However, the data refused to cooperate.
Rainfall doubled. As a result, the reservoirs refilled within months.
The design is minimalist; that is, every element serves a function.

mistakes.x: The study found no effect. Therefore, real-world data suggested benefits.
mistakes.v: The study found no effect. Nevertheless, real-world data suggested benefits. — the second sentence defies the first, so contrast, not result.

mistakes.x: The system cut commutes. However, it also lowered emissions.
mistakes.v: The system cut commutes. Additionally, it also lowered emissions. — both sentences point the same way: addition.

mistakes.x: Costs fell sharply. By contrast, prices for consumers dropped.
mistakes.v: Costs fell sharply. Consequently, prices for consumers dropped. — this is cause and effect, not contrast.

quiz.q:
Text: 'Early research on the drug showed promising results in laboratory settings. _____, clinical trials involving human subjects revealed serious side effects that had not appeared in animal models.'

Which transition most logically completes the text?
quiz.e: S1 (promising results) CONTRASTS with S2 (serious side effects). This is a CONTRAST relationship → However.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The archaeologist found pottery suggesting settlement dating to 3000 BCE. _____, carbon dating of charcoal found in the same stratum confirmed the site was occupied during the early Bronze Age.'

Which transition most logically completes the text?
quiz.e: S1 (pottery suggests early date) and S2 (carbon dating confirms similar date) are pointing in the SAME direction — S2 adds confirming evidence. ADDITION → Moreover.

quiz.q:
Text: 'Researchers have documented that people sleeping fewer than six hours show impaired reaction times and reduced working memory. _____, the prevalence of chronic sleep deprivation in industrialized nations continues to rise.'

Which transition most logically completes the text?
quiz.e: S1 (documented harms) vs. S2 (deprivation is RISING despite this knowledge). Something continues DESPITE evidence against it. CONTRAST-DESPITE → Nevertheless.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The new manufacturing technique reduced production costs by 40%. _____, the savings were passed on to consumers in the form of lower retail prices.'

Which transition most logically completes the text?
quiz.e: Lower costs (cause) → lower prices for consumers (effect). CAUSE/EFFECT → Consequently.

quiz.q:
Text: 'Some historians argue the decline of Rome was primarily due to internal political corruption. _____, other scholars emphasize the role of external pressures, including migrations and military defeats along the empire's borders.'

Which transition most logically completes the text?
quiz.e: S1 (internal factors) is contrasted with S2 (external factors — 'other scholars emphasize DIFFERENT causes'). CONTRAST → By contrast.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The new public transit system reduced average commute times significantly. _____, it lowered carbon emissions by reducing the number of private vehicles on major roadways.'

Which transition most logically completes the text?
quiz.e: S1 (reduced commutes) and S2 (also reduced emissions) — the second ADDS another benefit of the same system. ADDITION → Additionally.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The medication showed no improvement over placebo in the controlled study. _____, subsequent real-world data collected from thousands of patients suggested meaningful benefits in the general population.'

Which transition most logically completes the text?
quiz.e: S1 (no improvement over placebo) vs. S2 (real-world data shows benefits). Something positive happens DESPITE the controlled study finding. CONTRAST-DESPITE → Nevertheless.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The company invested heavily in employee training programs. _____, staff turnover rates fell sharply over the following three years, saving considerable recruitment and onboarding costs.'

Which transition most logically completes the text?
quiz.e: Investment in training (cause) → lower turnover (direct effect). CAUSE/EFFECT → As a result.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The prime minister had campaigned on a platform of fiscal restraint. _____, the budget she presented in her first year in office included the largest spending increase in a decade.'

Which transition most logically completes the text?
quiz.e: The PM campaigned on restraint (expectation) but her budget was the opposite (largest spending increase). Clear reversal. CONTRAST → Yet.

quiz.q:
Text: 'Several studies have found that people make better decisions under moderate rather than extreme time pressure. _____, some amount of deadline stress appears to focus attention productively.'

Which transition most logically completes the text?
quiz.e: S2 explains/clarifies the MECHANISM behind S1's finding. 'That is' introduces a reformulation or explanation in other words. 'Therefore' would be wrong if S2 is a result but here it elaborates why.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The city's public library system has faced severe budget cuts over the past decade. _____, many branches have reduced their hours and eliminated programs for children and seniors.'

Which transition most logically completes the text?
quiz.e: Budget cuts (cause) → reduced hours and eliminated programs (effect). CAUSE/EFFECT → As a result.

quiz.q:
Text: 'Proponents of nuclear energy argue it produces reliable, low-carbon electricity at scale. _____, critics point to unresolved questions about waste storage and the safety of aging reactor infrastructure.'

Which transition most logically completes the text?
quiz.e: Proponents' view (positive) vs. critics' view (concerns). Two opposing perspectives. CONTRAST → However.

situation.uz: "The lab results were promising. However, the clinical trial failed." 'However' ni 'Therefore' ga almashtirsangiz — abzats ma'nosini yo'qotadi. Bog'lovchi — matnning mantig'i.
situation.ru: «The lab results were promising. However, the clinical trial failed.» Замените 'However' на 'Therefore' — и абзац потеряет смысл. Коннектор — это логика текста.

tip.uz: Bo'sh joydan OLDINGI va KEYINGI gapni o'qing va so'rang: bir xil yo'nalishmi (addition), qarama-qarshimi (contrast), sabab → natijami (result) yoki qayta ifodami (that is)? Avval munosabatni, keyin so'zni tanlang.
tip.ru: Прочитайте предложение ДО пропуска и ПОСЛЕ него и спросите: то же направление (addition), противоположное (contrast), причина → следствие (result) или переформулировка (that is)? Сначала выберите отношение, потом слово.

h.uz: Qarama-qarshilik: however, nevertheless, yet, by contrast
h.ru: Противопоставление: however, nevertheless, yet, by contrast

p.uz: 'However' va 'yet' oddiy yo'nalish o'zgarishini bildiradi. 'Nevertheless' kuchliroq: birinchi gap o'rnatgan narsaga QARAMAY nimadir yuz beradi. 'By contrast' ikki xil mavzu yoki qarashni yonma-yon qo'yadi.
p.ru: 'However' и 'yet' обозначают простой разворот направления. 'Nevertheless' сильнее: что-то происходит ВОПРЕКИ сказанному в первом предложении. 'By contrast' ставит рядом два разных предмета или взгляда.

p.uz: Ikkinchi gap birinchisi bilan BIR yo'nalishda bo'lsa — yana bir foyda, yana bir tasdiqlovchi dalil — qo'shimcha bog'lovchilarini ishlating. Ikkinchi gap birinchisini qo'llab-quvvatlasa, contrast so'ziga qo'l urmang.
p.ru: Если второе предложение идёт в ТОМ ЖЕ направлении, что и первое — ещё одна выгода, ещё одно подтверждение — используйте коннекторы добавления. Если второе поддерживает первое, слово контраста не подходит.

h.uz: Sabab va natija: consequently, as a result, therefore
h.ru: Причина и следствие: consequently, as a result, therefore

p.uz: Birinchi gap sabab, ikkinchisi natija bo'lsa — natija bog'lovchisini ishlating. Yo'nalishni tekshiring: 'consequently / as a result / therefore' mos kelishi uchun sabab oldin kelishi kerak.
p.ru: Когда первое предложение — причина, а второе — её результат, используйте коннектор следствия. Проверьте направление: причина должна идти первой, чтобы подошли 'consequently / as a result / therefore'.

h.uz: Izohlash: that is, in other words
h.ru: Пояснение: that is, in other words

p.uz: Ba'zan ikkinchi gap qarshilik ham, natija ham emas — birinchisining mexanizmini QAYTA IFODALAB beradi. 'That is' va 'in other words' shu qayta ifodani kiritadi; buni sabab-natija bilan adashtirish testlarning sevimli chalg'ituvchisi.
p.ru: Иногда второе предложение — не контраст и не следствие, а ПЕРЕФОРМУЛИРОВКА механизма первого. 'That is' и 'in other words' вводят такое пояснение; спутать его с причиной-следствием — любимый дистрактор тестов.

quiz.uz: Umidli natijalar va jiddiy nojo'ya ta'sirlar — qarama-qarshilik → However.
quiz.ru: Обнадёживающие результаты против серьёзных побочных эффектов — контраст → However.

quiz.uz: Ikkinchi gap tasdiqlovchi dalil qo'shadi — ADDITION → Moreover.
quiz.ru: Второе предложение добавляет подтверждающее свидетельство — ADDITION → Moreover.

quiz.uz: Dalillarga QARAMAY holat davom etmoqda → Nevertheless.
Ichki omillar va tashqi omillar — ikki qarash yonma-yon → By contrast.
quiz.ru: Внутренние и внешние факторы — два взгляда рядом → By contrast.

quiz.uz: Ikkinchi gap yana bir foydani qo'shadi → Additionally.
quiz.ru: Второе предложение добавляет ещё одну выгоду → Additionally.

quiz.uz: Nazorat tadqiqotiga QARAMAY real foydali natijalar → Nevertheless.
quiz.ru: Польза в реальных данных ВОПРЕКИ контролируемому исследованию → Nevertheless.

quiz.uz: Treningga sarmoya (sabab) → kam ketish (natija) → As a result.
quiz.ru: Инвестиции в обучение (причина) → низкая текучесть (следствие) → As a result.

quiz.uz: Va'da va aksincha harakat — aniq burilish → Yet.
quiz.ru: Обещание и противоположное действие — явный разворот → Yet.

quiz.uz: Ikkinchi gap birinchisining mexanizmini izohlaydi → That is.
quiz.ru: Второе предложение поясняет механизм первого → That is.

quiz.uz: Byudjet qisqarishi (sabab) → soatlar qisqarishi (natija) → As a result.
quiz.ru: Сокращение бюджета (причина) → сокращение часов (следствие) → As a result.

quiz.uz: Tarafdorlar va tanqidchilar — qarama-qarshi qarashlar → However.
quiz.ru: Сторонники против критиков — противоположные взгляды → However.

grammar.title: Subject-Verb Agreement — Finding the Real Subject
grammar.lead: Subject-verb agreement questions present a sentence with a blank and ask which verb form 'conforms to the conventions of Standard English.' The rule is simple: singular subjects take singular verbs; plural subjects take plural verbs. The challenge is finding the REAL subject when the sentence tries to hide it. The most common trap: an INTERVENING PHRASE between the subject and verb. Prepositional phrases beginning with of, in, with, among, along with, together with, as well as, including, and excluding do NOT change the number of the subject. Always locate the main noun before the verb, ignoring everything between them.

leadTr.uz: Subject-verb agreement savollarida bo'sh joyli gap beriladi va qaysi fe'l shakli Standard English qoidalariga mos kelishi so'raladi. Qoida oddiy: birlikdagi ega — birlikdagi fe'l, ko'plikdagi ega — ko'plikdagi fe'l. Qiyinchilik — gap HAQIQIY egani yashirganda uni topishda. Eng keng tarqalgan tuzoq: ega bilan fe'l orasidagi ORALIQ IBORA (intervening phrase). of, in, with, among, along with, together with, as well as, including, excluding bilan boshlanadigan predlogli iboralar eganing sonini O'ZGARTIRMAYDI. Har doim fe'ldan oldingi asosiy otni toping, ular orasidagi hamma narsani e'tiborsiz qoldiring.
leadTr.ru: Вопросы на subject-verb agreement дают предложение с пропуском и спрашивают, какая форма глагола соответствует нормам Standard English. Правило простое: единственное число подлежащего — глагол в единственном числе, множественное — во множественном. Трудность — найти НАСТОЯЩЕЕ подлежащее, когда предложение его прячет. Самая частая ловушка: ВСТАВНАЯ ФРАЗА между подлежащим и глаголом. Предложные обороты с of, in, with, among, along with, together with, as well as, including, excluding НЕ меняют число подлежащего. Всегда находите главное существительное перед глаголом, игнорируя всё, что стоит между ними.

p: INTERVENING PHRASE strategy: cross out everything between the subject and verb. 'The collection of rare manuscripts [was/were] donated' → cross out 'of rare manuscripts' → 'The collection ___ donated' → singular → was. 'A team of engineers [has/have] designed' → cross out 'of engineers' → 'A team ___ designed' → singular → has. The noun closest to the verb is NOT necessarily the subject — the subject is the MAIN noun that the verb is describing an action of.

Three key patterns: (1) 'The number of X' = SINGULAR ('The number of applicants has increased'). (2) 'A number of X' = PLURAL ('A number of applicants have applied'). (3) Subjects joined by AND = PLURAL, EXCEPT when they refer to a single unit ('peanut butter and jelly IS my favorite sandwich'). Memorize: 'the number' = singular; 'a number' = plural. This distinction appears on almost every exam.
Intervening phrase trick: cross out everything between subject and verb
'The number of X' = SINGULAR | 'A number of X' = PLURAL
Prepositional phrases (of, in, with, among) do NOT affect subject number
AND joins subjects → plural (unless referring to one unit)
Neither/either as subject → SINGULAR
Collective nouns (team, committee, jury) → SINGULAR in American English
Who/that/which: verb agrees with the ANTECEDENT (what who/that/which refers to)

quiz.q:
Text: 'The discovery of new antibiotic compounds [___] offered hope in the battle against drug-resistant infections.'

Which choice is correct?
quiz.e: ' What remains: 'The discovery ___ offered hope.' Subject = 'discovery' (singular). Singular verb → 'has.' A (have), C (having), D (are) are all wrong. Key: 'of new antibiotic compounds' is just a descriptor — it doesn't change the subject.

quiz.q:
Text: 'A number of researchers studying the effects of climate change on Arctic ecosystems [___] published findings suggesting accelerated ice loss.'

Which choice is correct?
quiz.e: B (have) is correct. Compare: 'The number of researchers has grown' — 'the number' = singular. The distinction 'a number' (plural) vs. 'the number' (singular) is a classic exam trap. Always check which article precedes 'number.'

quiz.q:
Text: 'The jury, after deliberating for three days, [___] reached a unanimous verdict of not guilty.'

Which choice is correct?
quiz.e: Here, the jury as a whole reached ONE verdict. C (has) is correct. A (have), B (were), D (are) treat 'jury' as plural, which is British English usage but not standard American English.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The committee includes several members who [___] backgrounds in environmental science.'

Which choice is correct?
quiz.e: The verb must agree with 'members,' not with 'committee.' Several members → plural → 'have.' B is correct. Trap: you might think the subject is 'committee' (singular) — but 'who' introduces a relative clause modifying 'members,' not 'committee.'

quiz.q:
Text: 'The influence of social media platforms on political discourse in democratic societies [___] been the subject of intense scholarly debate.'

Which choice is correct?
quiz.e: ' What remains: 'The influence ___ been the subject.' Subject = 'influence' (singular). B (has) is correct. The long intervening phrase is a typical exam distractor designed to make you forget the real subject.

p.uz: ORALIQ IBORA strategiyasi: ega bilan fe'l orasidagi hamma narsani chizib tashlang. 'The collection of rare manuscripts [was/were] donated' → 'of rare manuscripts'ni o'chiring → 'The collection ___ donated' → birlik → was. 'A team of engineers [has/have] designed' → 'of engineers'ni o'chiring → 'A team ___ designed' → birlik → has. Fe'lga eng yaqin ot har doim ham ega EMAS — ega bu fe'l harakatini bajarayotgan ASOSIY ot.
p.ru: Стратегия ВСТАВНОЙ ФРАЗЫ: вычеркните всё между подлежащим и глаголом. 'The collection of rare manuscripts [was/were] donated' → убираем 'of rare manuscripts' → 'The collection ___ donated' → ед. число → was. 'A team of engineers [has/have] designed' → убираем 'of engineers' → 'A team ___ designed' → ед. число → has. Ближайшее к глаголу существительное — НЕ обязательно подлежащее; подлежащее — это ГЛАВНОЕ существительное, действие которого описывает глагол.

p.uz: Uchta asosiy naqsh: (1) 'The number of X' = BIRLIK ('The number of applicants has increased'). (2) 'A number of X' = KO'PLIK ('A number of applicants have applied'). (3) AND bilan bog'langan egalar = KO'PLIK, faqat bir butunlikni anglatganda emas ('peanut butter and jelly IS my favorite sandwich'). Yodlang: 'the number' = birlik; 'a number' = ko'plik. Bu farq deyarli har bir imtihonda uchraydi.
p.ru: Три ключевых шаблона: (1) 'The number of X' = ЕДИНСТВЕННОЕ число ('The number of applicants has increased'). (2) 'A number of X' = МНОЖЕСТВЕННОЕ ('A number of applicants have applied'). (3) Подлежащие, соединённые AND, = множественное число, КРОМЕ случаев, когда они образуют одно целое ('peanut butter and jelly IS my favorite sandwich'). Запомните: 'the number' = ед. число; 'a number' = мн. число. Это различие встречается почти на каждом экзамене.

p.uz: Oraliq ibora usuli: ega bilan fe'l orasidagi hamma narsani chizib tashlang
p.ru: Приём вставной фразы: вычеркните всё между подлежащим и глаголом

p.uz: 'The number of X' = BIRLIK | 'A number of X' = KO'PLIK
p.ru: 'The number of X' = ЕД. число | 'A number of X' = МН. число

p.uz: Predlogli iboralar (of, in, with, among) eganing soniga TA'SIR QILMAYDI
p.ru: Предложные обороты (of, in, with, among) НЕ влияют на число подлежащего

p.uz: AND bilan bog'langan egalar → ko'plik (bir butunlikni bildirmasa)
p.ru: Подлежащие с AND → мн. число (если это не одно целое)

p.uz: Neither/either ega bo'lsa → BIRLIK
p.ru: Neither/either как подлежащее → ЕД. число

p.ru: Собирательные существительные (team, committee, jury) → ЕД. число в американском английском

p.ru: Who/that/which: глагол согласуется с АНТЕЦЕДЕНТОМ (тем, к чему отсылает who/that/which)

quiz.uz: 'of new antibiotic compounds'ni o'chiring: 'The discovery ___ offered' — ega 'discovery' (birlik) → has.
quiz.ru: Уберите 'of new antibiotic compounds': 'The discovery ___ offered' — подлежащее 'discovery' (ед. число) → has.

quiz.uz: 'A number of X' = ko'plik → have; 'the number of X' esa birlik bo'lardi.
quiz.ru: 'A number of X' = мн. число → have; а 'the number of X' было бы ед. числом.

quiz.uz: Jury bir butun sifatida BITTA hukm chiqardi → Amerika inglizchasida birlik → has.
quiz.ru: Jury как единое целое вынесло ОДИН вердикт → в американском английском ед. число → has.
'who' отсылает к 'members' (мн. число), а не к 'committee' → have.

quiz.uz: Uzun oraliq iborani o'chiring: ega 'influence' (birlik) → has.
quiz.ru: Вычеркните длинную вставную фразу: подлежащее 'influence' (ед. число) → has.

grammar.title: Tricky Agreement — Compound, Inverted & Indefinite Subjects
grammar.lead: COMPOUND SUBJECTS with OR / NOR: the verb agrees with the subject CLOSEST to it. 'Either the manager or the employees are responsible' (employees = plural → are). 'Either the employees or the manager is responsible' (manager = singular → is). With AND: nearly always plural. Exception: 'bread and butter IS expensive' (treated as one item). INVERTED SENTENCES: when the verb comes before the subject (sentences beginning with 'here,' 'there,' or starting with a prepositional phrase), find the real subject after the verb. 'There are several problems' (problems = plural → are). 'There is a problem' (problem = singular → is).

leadTr.uz: OR / NOR bilan MURAKKAB EGALAR: fe'l o'ziga ENG YAQIN ega bilan moslashadi. 'Either the manager or the employees are responsible' (employees = ko'plik → are). 'Either the employees or the manager is responsible' (manager = birlik → is). AND bilan: deyarli har doim ko'plik. Istisno: 'bread and butter IS expensive' (bir narsa sifatida qaraladi). TESKARI TARTIBLI GAPLAR: fe'l egadan oldin kelganda ('here', 'there' bilan yoki predlogli ibora bilan boshlanadigan gaplar), haqiqiy egani fe'ldan KEYIN toping. 'There are several problems' (problems = ko'plik → are). 'There is a problem' (problem = birlik → is).
leadTr.ru: СОСТАВНЫЕ ПОДЛЕЖАЩИЕ с OR / NOR: глагол согласуется с БЛИЖАЙШИМ подлежащим. 'Either the manager or the employees are responsible' (employees = мн. число → are). 'Either the employees or the manager is responsible' (manager = ед. число → is). С AND: почти всегда мн. число. Исключение: 'bread and butter IS expensive' (воспринимается как одно целое). ИНВЕРСИЯ: когда глагол стоит перед подлежащим (предложения с 'here', 'there' или начинающиеся с предложного оборота), ищите настоящее подлежащее ПОСЛЕ глагола. 'There are several problems' (problems = мн. число → are). 'There is a problem' (problem = ед. число → is).

p: INDEFINITE PRONOUNS: memorize these groups. ALWAYS SINGULAR: each, every, either, neither, one, anyone, everyone, someone, no one, anybody, everybody, somebody, nobody, anything, everything, something, nothing, another, much. ALWAYS PLURAL: both, few, many, others, several. CAN BE EITHER (depends on the 'of' phrase that follows): all, any, more, most, none, some. 'Some of the water IS contaminated' (water = singular → is). 'Some of the samples ARE contaminated' (samples = plural → are).

WHO/THAT/WHICH RELATIVE CLAUSES: these pronouns introduce clauses where the verb must agree with the antecedent. 'She is one of the scientists who HAVE published on this topic' — 'who' refers to 'scientists' (plural) → have. Compare: 'She is the only one of the scientists who HAS published on this topic' — 'the only one' constrains it to a single person → has. The 'one of those who' vs. 'the only one who' distinction is a recurring exam item.
Or/nor: verb matches the CLOSEST subject ('manager or employees ARE')
There is/are: find the subject AFTER 'there'
SINGULAR indefinites: each, every, either, neither, everyone, anyone, no one
PLURAL indefinites: both, few, many, several
FLEXIBLE indefinites (all, some, none, most): agree with the 'of X' noun
'One of the X who' → PLURAL verb | 'The only one of the X who' → SINGULAR
Every/each + compound subject: still SINGULAR ('Each student and teacher IS present')

quiz.q:
Text: 'Neither the principal nor the teachers [___] been informed of the schedule change before it was announced.'

Which choice is correct?
quiz.e: ..nor,' the verb agrees with the CLOSEST subject. The closest subject to the verb is 'teachers' (plural). Plural → 'have.' B is correct. If the sentence were reversed: 'Neither the teachers nor the principal has been informed' — closest = 'principal' (singular) → has.

quiz.q:
Text: 'There [___] a number of compelling reasons to reconsider the current approach to urban planning.'

Which choice is correct?
quiz.e: 'There ___ a number of compelling reasons.' Subject = 'a number of compelling reasons.' 'A number of X' = PLURAL → are. A is correct. Note: if the sentence had 'There ___ one compelling reason,' the answer would be 'is' (one = singular).

quiz.q:
Text: 'Each of the proposed solutions [___] strengths and weaknesses that must be weighed carefully.'

Which choice is correct?
quiz.e: Cross out 'of the proposed solutions.' Subject = 'each' (singular). Singular → 'has.' B is correct. This is a very common exam trap: the plural noun 'solutions' immediately follows 'each,' tempting you to use 'have.'

quiz.q:
Text: 'Most of the evidence supporting the new hypothesis [___] been collected from deep-sea observation sites.'

Which choice is correct?
quiz.e: 'Most of the evidence' → 'evidence' is singular (uncountable noun) → singular verb → 'has.' B is correct. Compare: 'Most of the samples HAVE been collected' → 'samples' is plural → have. The key is always checking the noun after 'of.'

quiz.q:
Text: 'She is one of the few scientists who [___] consistently challenged the prevailing model of dark matter.

Which choice is correct?
quiz.e: ' Several scientists have challenged the model; she is one of them. Plural 'scientists' → 'have.' B is correct. Compare: 'She is THE ONLY one of the scientists who HAS challenged...' — 'the only one' makes it singular.

p.uz: NOANIQ OLMOSHLAR: bu guruhlarni yodlang. HAR DOIM BIRLIK: each, every, either, neither, one, anyone, everyone, someone, no one, anybody, everybody, somebody, nobody, anything, everything, something, nothing, another, much. HAR DOIM KO'PLIK: both, few, many, others, several. IKKALASI HAM BO'LISHI MUMKIN (keyingi 'of' iborasiga bog'liq): all, any, more, most, none, some. 'Some of the water IS contaminated' (water = birlik → is). 'Some of the samples ARE contaminated' (samples = ko'plik → are).
p.ru: НЕОПРЕДЕЛЁННЫЕ МЕСТОИМЕНИЯ: выучите группы. ВСЕГДА ЕД. ЧИСЛО: each, every, either, neither, one, anyone, everyone, someone, no one, anybody, everybody, somebody, nobody, anything, everything, something, nothing, another, much. ВСЕГДА МН. ЧИСЛО: both, few, many, others, several. МОГУТ БЫТЬ И ТЕМ И ДРУГИМ (зависит от последующей фразы с 'of'): all, any, more, most, none, some. 'Some of the water IS contaminated' (water = ед. число → is). 'Some of the samples ARE contaminated' (samples = мн. число → are).

p.uz: WHO/THAT/WHICH NISBIY GAPLAR: bu olmoshlar kiritadigan gapda fe'l antetsedent bilan moslashishi kerak. 'She is one of the scientists who HAVE published on this topic' — 'who' 'scientists'ga (ko'plik) ishora qiladi → have. Solishtiring: 'She is the only one of the scientists who HAS published on this topic' — 'the only one' bitta odamga cheklaydi → has. 'One of those who' va 'the only one who' farqi imtihonda tez-tez uchraydi.
p.ru: ОТНОСИТЕЛЬНЫЕ ПРИДАТОЧНЫЕ с WHO/THAT/WHICH: в них глагол согласуется с антецедентом. 'She is one of the scientists who HAVE published on this topic' — 'who' отсылает к 'scientists' (мн. число) → have. Сравните: 'She is the only one of the scientists who HAS published on this topic' — 'the only one' ограничивает до одного человека → has. Различие 'one of those who' и 'the only one who' — регулярный экзаменационный пункт.

p.uz: Or/nor: fe'l ENG YAQIN ega bilan moslashadi ('manager or employees ARE')
p.ru: Or/nor: глагол согласуется с БЛИЖАЙШИМ подлежащим ('manager or employees ARE')

p.uz: There is/are: egani 'there'dan KEYIN toping
p.ru: There is/are: ищите подлежащее ПОСЛЕ 'there'

p.uz: BIRLIKDAGI noaniq olmoshlar: each, every, either, neither, everyone, anyone, no one
p.ru: Неопределённые местоимения ЕД. числа: each, every, either, neither, everyone, anyone, no one

p.uz: KO'PLIKDAGI noaniq olmoshlar: both, few, many, several
p.ru: Неопределённые местоимения МН. числа: both, few, many, several

p.ru: ГИБКИЕ местоимения (all, some, none, most): согласуются с существительным в 'of X'

p.uz: 'One of the X who' → KO'PLIK fe'l | 'The only one of the X who' → BIRLIK
p.ru: 'One of the X who' → глагол МН. числа | 'The only one of the X who' → ЕД. число

p.uz: Every/each + murakkab ega: baribir BIRLIK ('Each student and teacher IS present')
p.ru: Every/each + составное подлежащее: всё равно ЕД. число ('Each student and teacher IS present')

quiz.uz: 'Neither...nor'da fe'l eng yaqin egaga qaraydi: 'teachers' (ko'plik) → have.
quiz.ru: При 'neither...nor' глагол согласуется с ближайшим подлежащим: 'teachers' (мн. число) → have.
'A number of reasons' = мн. число → are.

quiz.uz: 'of the proposed solutions'ni o'chiring: ega 'each' (birlik) → has.
quiz.ru: Уберите 'of the proposed solutions': подлежащее 'each' (ед. число) → has.

quiz.uz: 'Most of the evidence' — 'evidence' sanalmaydigan ot (birlik) → has.
quiz.ru: 'Most of the evidence' — 'evidence' неисчисляемое (ед. число) → has.

quiz.uz: 'one of the few scientists who' → 'who' 'scientists'ga (ko'plik) ishora qiladi → have.
quiz.ru: 'one of the few scientists who' → 'who' отсылает к 'scientists' (мн. число) → have.

grammar.title: Pronoun-Antecedent Agreement
grammar.lead: Pronoun agreement questions test whether a pronoun correctly matches its antecedent (the noun it refers to) in NUMBER (singular/plural) and PERSON. The question format is typically: a passage with a blank where a pronoun or pronoun phrase goes. The most common agreement error on the exam is using a PLURAL pronoun ('they/their/them') when the antecedent is SINGULAR. This is especially tricky with: (1) indefinite pronouns ('everyone left their bag' — 'everyone' is singular, so 'their' is technically wrong; use 'his or her'), (2) collective nouns, and (3) singular nouns that feel plural because of context.

leadTr.uz: Pronoun agreement savollari olmosh o'z antetsedenti (u ishora qiladigan ot) bilan SON (birlik/ko'plik) va SHAXS jihatidan to'g'ri moslashganini tekshiradi. Savol formati odatda: olmosh yoki olmoshli ibora tushirilgan bo'sh joyli matn. Imtihondagi eng keng tarqalgan xato — antetsedent BIRLIK bo'lganda KO'PLIKDAGI olmosh ('they/their/them') ishlatish. Bu ayniqsa quyidagilarda qiyin: (1) noaniq olmoshlar ('everyone left their bag' — 'everyone' birlik, shuning uchun 'their' rasman xato; 'his or her' ishlating), (2) jamlovchi otlar va (3) kontekst tufayli ko'plikdek tuyuladigan birlikdagi otlar.
leadTr.ru: Вопросы на pronoun agreement проверяют, согласуется ли местоимение со своим антецедентом (существительным, к которому оно отсылает) в ЧИСЛЕ (ед./мн.) и ЛИЦЕ. Формат обычно такой: отрывок с пропуском на месте местоимения. Самая частая ошибка на экзамене — местоимение МН. числа ('they/their/them') при антецеденте в ЕД. числе. Особенно коварны: (1) неопределённые местоимения ('everyone left their bag' — 'everyone' ед. числа, поэтому 'their' формально неверно; используйте 'his or her'), (2) собирательные существительные и (3) существительные ед. числа, которые из-за контекста кажутся множественными.

p: THE SINGULAR THEY: The exam has updated its conventions to accept 'they/their/them' as singular pronouns when the gender of the person is unknown or when referring to a person who uses they/them pronouns. However, when the antecedent is an indefinite pronoun (everyone, each, neither) or a clearly singular noun in a formal register, the exam still tests the traditional rule. Read the passage carefully: if a specific person is described, use the gender-specific pronoun or 'they' if the person's gender is unspecified. For a generic/indefinite antecedent, 'his or her' is the traditional formal option.

KEY AGREEMENT PATTERNS: (1) Collective nouns (company, government, team) are singular → its, not their. 'The company increased its revenue.' (2) Indefinite pronouns (everyone, each, neither, anyone) → singular pronoun. 'Each student must bring his or her own materials.' (3) When a noun refers to both objects and people — 'the jury' refers to people but takes singular 'its verdict.' (4) Antecedent-pronoun agreement must match across the entire sentence, not just the nearest noun.
Pronoun must match antecedent in NUMBER (singular/plural) and PERSON
Collective nouns (company, team, committee) → its (singular)
Everyone/each/neither/anyone → his or her / their (singular)
Two antecedents joined by AND → their (plural)
Two antecedents joined by OR/NOR → match the CLOSEST antecedent
exam accepts singular 'they' for unspecified gender; still tests agreement
Find the antecedent FIRST, then check: does the pronoun match its number?

quiz.q:
Text: 'After months of negotiation, the company finally announced [___] decision to relocate its headquarters to a smaller city.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: ' A (their) treats the company as plural. C (his or her) is for a person, not an organization. D doesn't fit. B is correct.

quiz.q:
Text: 'Each of the astronauts was required to submit [___] medical records before the mission could be approved.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: The antecedent is 'each of the astronauts.' In formal written English, the singular indefinite 'each' requires a singular pronoun → 'his or her.' A (their) is the informal plural usage. B is the formally correct option. C is awkward and repetitive. D is wrong person.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The university announced that [___] will expand the financial aid program to cover more low-income students beginning next academic year.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: B (it) is correct. A (they) would treat the university as plural — this is a common informal usage, but on the exam, a singular organization takes 'it.' C (we) introduces a first-person perspective not established. D (one) is impersonal and awkward here.

quiz.q:
Text: 'Neither the CEO nor the board members were willing to reveal [___] reasoning for the unexpected decision.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: Closest = 'board members' (plural) → their. C is correct. If the sentence were 'Neither the board members nor the CEO was willing to reveal HIS OR HER reasoning,' the closest would be 'CEO' (singular). The proximity rule applies to pronouns as well as verbs.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The team of scientists published a paper in which [___] argued for a fundamental revision of the standard model.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: The exam accepts 'they' for a team acting as individuals. B (they) is most natural and correct. A (it) would be correct for a purely organizational statement. C (one) is impersonal. D (the scientists) is repetitive but grammatically acceptable — however B is more concise and natural.

p.uz: BIRLIKDAGI THEY: imtihon qoidalari yangilangan — shaxsning jinsi noma'lum bo'lganda yoki they/them olmoshlarini ishlatadigan odam haqida gap ketganda 'they/their/them' birlik sifatida qabul qilinadi. Biroq antetsedent noaniq olmosh (everyone, each, neither) yoki rasmiy uslubda aniq birlikdagi ot bo'lsa, imtihon hali ham an'anaviy qoidani tekshiradi. Matnni diqqat bilan o'qing: aniq shaxs tasvirlansa, jinsga mos olmosh yoki jinsi ko'rsatilmagan bo'lsa 'they' ishlating. Umumiy/noaniq antetsedent uchun an'anaviy rasmiy variant — 'his or her'.
p.ru: СИНГУЛЯРНОЕ THEY: экзамен обновил нормы и принимает 'they/their/them' как местоимения ед. числа, когда пол человека неизвестен или человек использует местоимения they/them. Однако если антецедент — неопределённое местоимение (everyone, each, neither) или явно единственное существительное в формальном стиле, экзамен по-прежнему проверяет традиционное правило. Читайте внимательно: если описан конкретный человек, используйте местоимение его пола или 'they', если пол не указан. Для обобщённого/неопределённого антецедента традиционный формальный вариант — 'his or her'.

p.uz: ASOSIY MOSLASHUV NAQSHLARI: (1) Jamlovchi otlar (company, government, team) birlik → its, their emas. 'The company increased its revenue.' (2) Noaniq olmoshlar (everyone, each, neither, anyone) → birlikdagi olmosh. 'Each student must bring his or her own materials.' (3) Ot ham narsalar, ham odamlarga tegishli bo'lganda — 'the jury' odamlarni bildiradi, lekin birlikdagi 'its verdict' oladi. (4) Antetsedent-olmosh moslashuvi eng yaqin ot bilan emas, butun gap bo'ylab mos kelishi kerak.
p.ru: КЛЮЧЕВЫЕ ШАБЛОНЫ СОГЛАСОВАНИЯ: (1) Собирательные существительные (company, government, team) — ед. число → its, а не their. 'The company increased its revenue.' (2) Неопределённые местоимения (everyone, each, neither, anyone) → местоимение ед. числа. 'Each student must bring his or her own materials.' (3) Когда существительное обозначает и людей, и организацию — 'the jury' обозначает людей, но берёт единственное 'its verdict'. (4) Согласование должно выдерживаться по всему предложению, а не только с ближайшим существительным.

p.uz: Olmosh antetsedent bilan SON (birlik/ko'plik) va SHAXSda mos kelishi shart
p.ru: Местоимение должно совпадать с антецедентом в ЧИСЛЕ (ед./мн.) и ЛИЦЕ

quiz.ru: 'The company' — собирательное существительное, ед. число → its; 'their' трактует его как мн. число.

quiz.ru: 'Each' — ед. число, в формальном стиле нужно местоимение ед. числа → his or her.

grammar.title: Pronoun Reference — Clarity & Who vs. Whom
grammar.lead: Pronoun REFERENCE questions test whether a pronoun's antecedent is CLEAR and UNAMBIGUOUS. If a pronoun could logically refer to more than one noun in the sentence or surrounding context, it is ambiguous and must be replaced with the specific noun. This is the same issue we saw in Sentence Revision (Day 10), now tested as a stand-alone grammar convention. The test typically presents a sentence with 'it,' 'they,' 'this,' or 'that' where the referent is not clear, and asks you to identify the clearest revision.

leadTr.uz: Pronoun REFERENCE savollari olmoshning antetsedenti ANIQ va BIR MA'NOLI ekanini tekshiradi. Agar olmosh gapdagi yoki kontekstdagi bir nechta otga mantiqan ishora qilishi mumkin bo'lsa, u noaniq hisoblanadi va aniq ot bilan almashtirilishi kerak. Bu Sentence Revision (10-kun)da ko'rgan muammomizning o'zi, endi alohida grammatik qoida sifatida tekshiriladi. Testda odatda 'it', 'they', 'this' yoki 'that' ishlatilgan, lekin nimaga ishora qilishi noaniq gap beriladi va eng aniq tahrirni topish so'raladi.
leadTr.ru: Вопросы на pronoun REFERENCE проверяют, ЯСЕН и ОДНОЗНАЧЕН ли антецедент местоимения. Если местоимение может логически отсылать к нескольким существительным в предложении или контексте, оно двусмысленно и должно быть заменено конкретным существительным. Это та же проблема, что и в Sentence Revision (день 10), но теперь как отдельное грамматическое правило. Тест обычно даёт предложение с 'it', 'they', 'this' или 'that', где референт неясен, и просит выбрать самую ясную правку.

p: WHO vs. WHOM: 'Who' is a subject pronoun (replaces he/she/they); 'whom' is an object pronoun (replaces him/her/them). The trick: mentally substitute 'he/she' vs. 'him/her.' 'Who called?' → 'He called' (subject) → who. 'Whom did you call?' → 'You called him' (object) → whom. In relative clauses: 'the scientist who won the prize' (who = subject of 'won') vs. 'the scientist whom we interviewed' (whom = object of 'interviewed'). On the exam, 'who' errors are more common than 'whom' errors — most people over-correct by using 'whom' when 'who' is correct.

PRONOUN CASE — SUBJECT vs. OBJECT: 'I/he/she/we/they' are subject pronouns used as sentence subjects or subject complements. 'Me/him/her/us/them' are object pronouns used as objects of verbs or prepositions. Tricky pattern: 'between you and me' (not 'between you and I') — 'between' is a preposition, so it takes object pronouns. 'She and I went' (subjects). 'He invited her and me' (objects). When in doubt: remove one of the two nouns and see which pronoun sounds right. 'He invited I' → wrong → 'He invited me' → correct.
Ambiguous pronoun: if 'it/they/this' could refer to 2+ nouns → replace with specific noun
Who = subject (replace with he/she/they) | Whom = object (replace with him/her/them)
Test: substitute 'he/she' or 'him/her' — whichever sounds right determines who/whom
Prepositions take OBJECT pronouns: 'between you and ME' (not I)
Compound subject: 'She and I went' | Compound object: 'He called her and me'
Remove one person from compound to test: 'He called I' vs 'He called me' → me
Who/whom in relative clause: is the pronoun doing the action (who) or receiving it (whom)?

quiz.q:
Text: 'The award was given to the researcher [___] developed the most innovative solution to the problem.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: ' 'He developed' (subject) → WHO. B is correct. 'Whom' would be correct if the researcher were the object: 'the researcher whom we recognized' (we recognized him → object → whom).

quiz.q:
Text: 'The committee must decide [___] to recommend for the directorship.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: ' 'Recommend him' (object of 'recommend') → WHOM. C is correct. Compare: 'The committee must decide WHO should be recommended' — here 'who' is the subject of 'should be recommended.'

quiz.q:
Text: 'When the scientists reviewed the data with the programmers, they discovered several critical errors that could have invalidated the results.'

The pronoun 'they' is ambiguous. Which revision most clearly identifies who made the discovery?
o: When the scientists reviewed the data with the programmers, they discovered several critical errors.
During the review, the scientists discovered several critical errors in the data that could have invalidated the results.
When reviewing the data, they found several critical errors.
The scientists and the programmers, they discovered several critical errors.
quiz.e: 'They' could refer to either the scientists or the programmers — ambiguous. B rewrites to make the scientists clearly the subject and eliminates the ambiguity while preserving the meaning. A keeps the ambiguous 'they.' C is still ambiguous ('they' still unclear). D is grammatically awkward.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The conflict between the department head and [___] has created tension throughout the organization.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: Test by removing 'the department head and': 'The conflict between [I/me]...' → 'Between me' sounds right because 'me' is the object form. C (me) is correct. A (I) is a subject pronoun, which doesn't follow prepositions. B (myself) is a reflexive, used only when the subject and object are the same person.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The dean invited Professor Chen and [___] to present our research findings at the annual symposium.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: ' Remove 'Professor Chen and' to test: 'The dean invited [I/me].' → 'The dean invited me.' 'Me' is the object of 'invited.' B (me) is correct. A (I) is wrong because 'invited I' is incorrect. C (myself) is reflexive — only correct if the dean is also 'me.' D (we) is wrong — we isn't an object.

p.uz: WHO va WHOM: 'Who' — ega olmoshi (he/she/they o'rnida); 'whom' — to'ldiruvchi olmoshi (him/her/them o'rnida). Usul: xayolan 'he/she' yoki 'him/her' qo'yib ko'ring. 'Who called?' → 'He called' (ega) → who. 'Whom did you call?' → 'You called him' (to'ldiruvchi) → whom. Nisbiy gaplarda: 'the scientist who won the prize' (who = 'won'ning egasi) va 'the scientist whom we interviewed' (whom = 'interviewed'ning to'ldiruvchisi). Imtihonda 'who' xatolari 'whom' xatolaridan ko'proq uchraydi — ko'pchilik 'who' to'g'ri bo'lganda ham 'whom' ishlatib, ortiqcha tuzatadi.
p.ru: WHO и WHOM: 'Who' — местоимение-подлежащее (заменяет he/she/they); 'whom' — местоимение-дополнение (заменяет him/her/them). Приём: мысленно подставьте 'he/she' или 'him/her'. 'Who called?' → 'He called' (подлежащее) → who. 'Whom did you call?' → 'You called him' (дополнение) → whom. В придаточных: 'the scientist who won the prize' (who = подлежащее 'won') и 'the scientist whom we interviewed' (whom = дополнение 'interviewed'). На экзамене ошибки с 'who' чаще, чем с 'whom' — многие «переисправляют», ставя 'whom' там, где верно 'who'.

p.uz: OLMOSH KELISHIGI — EGA va TO'LDIRUVCHI: 'I/he/she/we/they' — ega olmoshlari, gap egasi yoki ega komplementi sifatida ishlatiladi. 'Me/him/her/us/them' — to'ldiruvchi olmoshlari, fe'l yoki predlog to'ldiruvchisi sifatida keladi. Qiyin naqsh: 'between you and me' ('between you and I' emas) — 'between' predlog, shuning uchun to'ldiruvchi olmoshi talab qiladi. 'She and I went' (egalar). 'He invited her and me' (to'ldiruvchilar). Ikkilanganingizda: ikki otdan birini olib tashlab, qaysi olmosh to'g'ri eshitilishini tekshiring. 'He invited I' → xato → 'He invited me' → to'g'ri.
p.ru: ПАДЕЖ МЕСТОИМЕНИЙ — СУБЪЕКТ и ОБЪЕКТ: 'I/he/she/we/they' — субъектные местоимения, употребляются как подлежащее или именная часть сказуемого. 'Me/him/her/us/them' — объектные, идут как дополнения глаголов и предлогов. Коварный шаблон: 'between you and me' (не 'between you and I') — 'between' предлог, значит нужны объектные местоимения. 'She and I went' (подлежащие). 'He invited her and me' (дополнения). Сомневаетесь — уберите одно из двух и проверьте на слух: 'He invited I' → неверно → 'He invited me' → верно.

p.uz: Noaniq olmosh: 'it/they/this' 2+ otga ishora qilishi mumkin bo'lsa → aniq ot bilan almashtiring
p.ru: Двусмысленное местоимение: если 'it/they/this' может отсылать к 2+ существительным → замените конкретным существительным

p.uz: Who = ega (he/she/they bilan almashtiring) | Whom = to'ldiruvchi (him/her/them bilan)
p.ru: Who = подлежащее (заменяется he/she/they) | Whom = дополнение (him/her/them)

p.uz: Test: 'he/she' yoki 'him/her' qo'yib ko'ring — qaysi to'g'ri eshitilsa, who/whom shu
p.ru: Тест: подставьте 'he/she' или 'him/her' — что звучит верно, то и определяет who/whom

p.uz: Predloglar TO'LDIRUVCHI olmoshlarini oladi: 'between you and ME' (I emas)
p.ru: Предлоги требуют ОБЪЕКТНЫХ местоимений: 'between you and ME' (не I)

p.uz: Murakkab ega: 'She and I went' | Murakkab to'ldiruvchi: 'He called her and me'
p.ru: Составное подлежащее: 'She and I went' | Составное дополнение: 'He called her and me'

p.uz: Tekshirish uchun bir kishini olib tashlang: 'He called I' yoki 'He called me' → me
p.ru: Уберите одного для проверки: 'He called I' или 'He called me' → me

p.uz: Nisbiy gapda who/whom: olmosh harakatni bajaryaptimi (who) yoki qabul qilyaptimi (whom)?
p.ru: Who/whom в придаточном: местоимение выполняет действие (who) или принимает его (whom)?

reading.title: The Remote Working Debate
reading.text:
Since the pandemic, working from home has become normal for millions of people. Supporters argue that it offers a better work-life balance: employees save hours that would otherwise be wasted commuting, and many report feeling less stressed and more productive.
Not everyone is convinced, however. Some managers worry that staff who work remotely are harder to supervise and less connected to their colleagues. Younger workers, in particular, may miss the informal learning that happens in an office, where they can pick up skills simply by watching experienced people.
The truth probably lies somewhere in between. A growing number of companies in Manchester and London now offer a 'hybrid' model, in which employees spend part of the week at home and part in the office. Had this option been available ten years ago, it might have seemed strange. Today, it is increasingly seen as the best of both worlds.

quiz.e: Part of the week at home, part in the office.

quiz.e: It is increasingly seen as the best of both worlds.

reading.title: Living with Artificial Intelligence
reading.text:
Artificial intelligence is no longer science fiction. It already recommends the films we watch, filters our emails, and helps doctors read medical scans. For many, these developments are exciting; for others, they are a cause for concern.
Those who welcome AI point to its potential to save lives and time. A computer can examine thousands of images far faster than a human, spotting patterns that might otherwise be missed. In industries from farming to finance, AI is helping people make better decisions.
Yet the same technology raises difficult questions. If a self-driving car causes an accident, who is responsible? As machines take over more tasks, some jobs will certainly disappear. Supporters argue that new jobs will be created, just as they were during the Industrial Revolution. Critics are less sure. What seems clear is that AI is here to stay, and societies will need to decide carefully how to use it.

reading.title: Why We Put Things Off
reading.text:
Almost everyone procrastinates. We delay important tasks, choosing instead to check our phones, tidy a drawer, or make yet another cup of tea. We know we are wasting time, and yet we do it anyway. Why?
Psychologists suggest that procrastination is not really about laziness. It is more often about emotion. When a task makes us feel anxious or bored, our brain looks for an escape, and a quick, pleasant distraction provides instant relief. The problem, of course, is that the relief never lasts, and the task only grows more stressful.
The good news is that procrastination can be managed. Experts recommend breaking a large task into small steps, so that it feels less frightening. It also helps to forgive yourself for past delays; research has shown that students who stopped criticising themselves actually procrastinated less in future. In other words, being kinder to ourselves may be the first step towards getting things done.

reading.title: Report: Improving the Town Library
reading.text:
Introduction
The purpose of this report is to assess the current state of Brighton Central Library and to recommend improvements. The findings are based on a survey of 200 users and interviews with staff.

Findings
The majority of users praised the library's wide selection of books. However, several problems were identified. Firstly, the opening hours were felt to be too limited, particularly for those who work full-time. Secondly, the building's Wi-Fi was described as slow and unreliable. Finally, a number of younger visitors complained that there was nowhere quiet to study.

Recommendations
In light of these findings, it is recommended that the library extend its opening hours into the evening. Furthermore, the Wi-Fi system should be upgraded as a priority. Were a quiet study area to be created on the upper floor, it would almost certainly attract more students.

Conclusion
With relatively modest investment, the library could serve the community far more effectively.

reading.title: The Cost of Cheap Travel
reading.text:
Never before has travel been so affordable. Budget airlines now offer flights across Europe for the price of a meal, and millions of us take advantage every year. Yet this golden age of cheap travel comes at a price that does not appear on the ticket.
The most obvious cost is environmental. Aviation produces a significant share of carbon emissions, and a single long flight can undo months of careful recycling. Less visible, but no less serious, is the impact on popular destinations. Cities such as Venice and Barcelona have become so crowded with visitors that local residents are being pushed out of their own neighbourhoods.
None of this means we should stop travelling altogether. Travel broadens the mind and supports countless livelihoods. What it does suggest is that we should travel more thoughtfully — flying less often, staying longer, and respecting the places we visit. Only if tourists and governments act together will the benefits of travel be preserved for future generations.

quiz.e: We should travel more thoughtfully, not stop.

reading.title: A Startup Story from IT Park
reading.text:
When Dilnoza left her stable accounting job to join a three-person startup at Tashkent's IT Park, her relatives were sceptical. 'They thought I had lost my mind,' she laughs. 'In their world, a good job meant a desk you kept for thirty years.' Four years later, her company employs sixty people and sells education software to schools in five countries.

Her story reflects a wider shift. A decade ago, ambitious graduates in Uzbekistan generally faced a narrow choice: a government position, a bank, or emigration. The growth of the IT sector has added a fourth path, one in which fluency in English matters more than family connections. Companies serving foreign clients conduct interviews, meetings and code reviews in English, and salaries at successful firms can rival those abroad — without the cost of leaving home.

Yet Dilnoza warns against romanticising the sector. 'People see the beanbags and the free coffee, not the deadlines,' she says. Roughly half of new startups fail within two years, and the pressure to keep learning never stops. Her advice to students is unglamorous: master English first, learn to write clearly, and treat failure as tuition. 'My first startup collapsed in eight months,' she admits. 'It was the most expensive and most useful course I ever took.'

quiz.q: How did Dilnoza's relatives react to her career change?
o: They thought it was a mistake
quiz.e: They were sceptical — 'they thought I had lost my mind'.

quiz.q: What 'wider shift' does the text describe?
o: The IT sector has created a new career path
Government jobs pay more than before
quiz.e: The growth of the IT sector added a fourth path beyond government, banks or emigration.

quiz.q: Why does English matter in this sector, according to the text?
o: Companies work with foreign clients in English
quiz.e: Companies serving foreign clients hold interviews, meetings and code reviews in English.

quiz.q: What does Dilnoza mean by calling failure 'tuition'?
o: Failure is expensive but teaches valuable lessons
quiz.e: Her failed startup was 'the most expensive and most useful course' — failure teaches like a paid course.

quizTr.uz: Ular ishonqiramay qarashdi — 'meni aqldan ozgan deb o'ylashdi'.
quizTr.ru: Они отнеслись скептически — «думали, что я сошла с ума».

quizTr.uz: IT sohasining o'sishi davlat ishi, bank yoki emigratsiyadan tashqari to'rtinchi yo'lni ochdi.
quizTr.ru: Рост IT-сектора добавил четвёртый путь помимо госслужбы, банка или эмиграции.

quizTr.uz: Xorijiy mijozlar bilan ishlaydigan kompaniyalar suhbat va yig'ilishlarni ingliz tilida o'tkazadi.
quizTr.ru: Компании с иностранными клиентами проводят собеседования и встречи на английском.

quizTr.uz: Muvaffaqiyatsizlik — pullik kursdek saboq beradi: qimmat, lekin juda foydali.
quizTr.ru: Неудача учит, как платный курс: дорого, но очень полезно.

reading.title: Reading set: Ideas & evidence I
reading.text:
Each task below contains its own short passage. Read it closely, then answer — this trains exactly the kind of reading you will meet in real academic texts and exams.

Quyida har bir topshiriqning o'z qisqa matni bor. Diqqat bilan o'qing, so'ng javob bering.

quiz.q:
Passage: Recent archaeological discoveries along the ancient Silk Road reveal that the exchange of goods was accompanied by an equally significant transfer of agricultural knowledge. Crop varieties, farming techniques, and irrigation methods all traveled alongside silk and spices, fundamentally reshaping food production across Eurasia.

Which best states the main idea?
o: The Silk Road facilitated trade in goods AND the spread of agricultural knowledge across Eurasia
Irrigation methods developed in Asia were superior to those used in Europe
Silk Road sites contain artifacts related to farming and food production
The Silk Road was primarily a route for luxury goods between Asia and Europe
quiz.e: The passage argues the Silk Road transferred BOTH goods AND agricultural knowledge. C covers the full argument. A and B are too narrow. D is not stated.

quiz.q:
Passage: The assumption that digital technology has uniformly shortened human attention spans is not supported by evidence. While social media correlates with brief engagement, long-form video streaming and e-reading involve sustained attention comparable to traditional media.

Which best states the central claim?
o: Digital technology has significantly shortened the average human attention span
Long-form streaming requires greater attention than reading physical books
The relationship between digital technology and attention is more complex than a simple decline narrative
Social media platforms are specifically designed to capture user attention
quiz.e: The passage challenges the 'uniformly shortened' assumption — not all digital activities reduce attention. C captures this nuance. A is what the passage contradicts. B and D are too narrow.

quiz.q:
Passage: Biologist E.O. Wilson coined 'biophilia' to describe an innate human affinity for other living systems. He argued that millions of years of evolution hardwired humans to find beauty and meaning in nature — a connection he believed modern urban life systematically erodes.

The text is primarily about
o: Wilson's argument that humans have an evolutionarily rooted connection to nature that urbanization threatens
The psychological effects of city living without access to natural environments
The scientific debate surrounding Wilson's hypothesis
Wilson's career contributions to evolutionary science
quiz.e: The passage presents Wilson's specific argument: humans are hardwired for nature AND urbanization erodes this. B captures both parts. A implies debate (not stated). C and D are too narrow.

quiz.q:
Passage: The narrative that the printing press single-handedly caused the Protestant Reformation oversimplifies history. While Gutenberg's invention accelerated Luther's ideas, religious discontent had been building for over a century before 1517, driven by clerical corruption and economic grievances.

The central claim is that
o: The Reformation was caused primarily by economics rather than religion
The press was one factor in the Reformation, but tensions had deeper roots that preceded it
Gutenberg's press was not invented until after Luther's 95 Theses
Luther's ideas would have spread even without the printing press
quiz.e: The passage argues the press-caused-Reformation narrative is oversimplified because discontent predated print. C captures this. A is factually wrong. B distorts. D is speculative.

quizTr.uz: Matn Silk Road tovarlarni HAM, dehqonchilik bilimini HAM tarqatgan deydi — C to'liq argumentni qamraydi; A va B juda tor, D aytilmagan.
quizTr.ru: Текст утверждает, что Silk Road передавал И товары, И аграрные знания — C охватывает весь аргумент; A и B слишком узки, D не заявлено.

quizTr.uz: Matn 'bir xilda qisqargan' degan taxminni rad etadi — C shu nozik ma'noni qamraydi; A matn rad etayotgan fikr, B va D juda tor.
quizTr.ru: Текст оспаривает допущение о «равномерном снижении» — C передаёт этот нюанс; A — то, что текст опровергает, B и D слишком узки.

quizTr.uz: B Wilson argumentining ikkala qismini qamraydi: insonning tabiatga tug'ma bog'liqligi VA urbanizatsiya bunga xavf solishi; A bahs borligini nazarda tutadi, C va D juda tor.
quizTr.ru: B охватывает обе части аргумента Wilson: врождённую связь человека с природой И угрозу от урбанизации; A предполагает спор, C и D слишком узки.

quizTr.uz: Matn 'matbaa Reformatsiyani keltirib chiqardi' degan hikoyani soddalashtirilgan deb hisoblaydi, chunki norozilik matbaadan oldin bo'lgan — C buni beradi; A faktik xato, B buzadi, D taxminiy.
quizTr.ru: Текст считает тезис «печать вызвала Реформацию» упрощением, поскольку недовольство существовало раньше — C это передаёт; A фактически неверен, B искажает, D спекулятивен.

reading.title: Reading set: Ideas & evidence II
reading.text:
Each task below contains its own short passage. Read it closely, then answer — this trains exactly the kind of reading you will meet in real academic texts and exams.

Quyida har bir topshiriqning o'z qisqa matni bor. Diqqat bilan o'qing, so'ng javob bering.

quiz.q:
Passage: As Arctic permafrost thaws, it releases stored carbon dioxide and methane, which accelerate warming, which causes more thawing. What makes this alarming is that permafrost contains roughly twice as much carbon as is currently in the atmosphere.

The main idea is
o: Climate change poses threats to Arctic ecosystems that scientists are only beginning to understand
Arctic permafrost stores large quantities of carbon accumulated over thousands of years
The thawing of permafrost creates a self-reinforcing cycle that could dramatically amplify climate change
Scientists have recently discovered that permafrost contains methane in addition to carbon dioxide
quiz.e: The key argument is the feedback loop PLUS the alarming carbon quantity. B captures both. A and C are individual details. D is too vague.

quiz.q:
Passage: Scholar Nancy Armstrong argues that the rise of the Victorian novel was inseparable from the rise of middle-class femininity. The idealized domestic woman depicted in these novels was not merely a reflection of social reality but an active construct that helped produce it — shaping how readers understood desire and virtue.

What is the central claim?
o: Victorian heroines demonstrated virtues that real women were expected to emulate
Victorian novels were primarily written by and for middle-class women
Armstrong argues domestic fiction both reflected and actively shaped Victorian ideals of femininity
Victorian domestic fiction was more concerned with class than gender
quiz.e: Armstrong's argument has two parts: novels were part of the rise of femininity AND they actively produced that femininity. B captures both. A is not stated. C misses 'actively constructed.' D contradicts the text.

quiz.q:
Passage: Traditional economics treats humans as rational actors who maximize self-interest. However, behavioral economics research demonstrates that human decision-making is systematically shaped by cognitive biases, emotional states, and social influences that often lead people to act against their own stated preferences.

The passage primarily argues that
o: Behavioral economics has replaced traditional economics as the dominant framework
Human beings are fundamentally irrational and incapable of sound economic decisions
Cognitive biases can occasionally cause people to deviate from economically rational behavior
Traditional economic models fail to accurately capture how humans actually make decisions
quiz.e: The passage says traditional models assume rationality BUT behavioral economics shows systematic biases. B captures this. A is too strong. C is too extreme. D is too weak — 'occasionally' vs. 'systematically.'

quiz.q:
Passage: Standardized testing was justified by the need for objective measures. Yet critics argue these tests measure a narrow band of skills, create incentives to 'teach to the test,' and systematically disadvantage lower-income students who lack access to test preparation resources.

The main idea is
o: Test preparation resources give wealthier students an unfair advantage
Despite their stated purpose of objective measurement, standardized tests have several significant shortcomings
Standardized testing was introduced to American schools in the 1980s
Academic performance has declined since the adoption of standardized testing
quiz.e: The passage presents the purpose AND multiple criticisms. B captures this full structure. A is background only. C is one specific criticism. D is not stated.

quizTr.uz: Asosiy argument — o'z-o'zini kuchaytiruvchi sikl VA xavotirli uglerod miqdori; B ikkalasini qamraydi, A va C alohida detallar, D juda noaniq.
quizTr.ru: Ключевой аргумент — самоусиливающийся цикл ПЛЮС тревожный объём углерода; B охватывает оба, A и C — отдельные детали, D слишком расплывчат.

quizTr.uz: Armstrong argumenti ikki qismli: romanlar Viktoriya ayollik ideallarini aks ettirgan VA faol shakllantirgan — B ikkalasini qamraydi; A aytilmagan, C 'faol yaratish'ni o'tkazib yuboradi, D matnga zid.
quizTr.ru: Аргумент Armstrong двойной: романы отражали И активно формировали викторианские идеалы женственности — B охватывает оба; A не заявлено, C упускает «активное создание», D противоречит тексту.

quizTr.uz: An'anaviy modellar ratsionallikni taxmin qiladi, LEKIN xulq-atvor iqtisodiyoti tizimli xatolarni ko'rsatadi — B shuni qamraydi; A juda kuchli, C haddan tashqari, D juda zaif ('vaqti-vaqti bilan' emas, 'tizimli').
quizTr.ru: Традиционные модели предполагают рациональность, НО поведенческая экономика показывает системные искажения — B это передаёт; A слишком силён, C чрезмерен, D слишком слаб («иногда» вместо «системно»).

quizTr.uz: Matn maqsadni VA bir nechta tanqidni keltiradi — B shu to'liq tuzilmani qamraydi; A faqat fon, C bitta aniq tanqid, D aytilmagan.
quizTr.ru: Текст излагает цель И ряд критических замечаний — B охватывает всю структуру; A — лишь фон, C — одна конкретная претензия, D не заявлено.

reading.title: Reading set: Author's craft
reading.text:
Each task below contains its own short passage. Read it closely, then answer — this trains exactly the kind of reading you will meet in real academic texts and exams.

Quyida har bir topshiriqning o'z qisqa matni bor. Diqqat bilan o'qing, so'ng javob bering.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The architect's early sketches were rough and provisional, but they captured the essential character of the building she would eventually construct.'

As used in the text, 'provisional' most nearly means
quiz.e: The sketches are 'rough' and not final — they are preliminary. 'Provisional' = temporary, not yet final. 'Legally authorized' and 'provided as a benefit' are other senses of 'provision.'

quiz.q:
Text: 'Anthropologists studying the remote community found that its social structures were remarkably resilient, having persisted through centuries of external disruption and internal conflict.'

As used in the text, 'resilient' most nearly means
o: resistant to all forms of change
able to withstand and recover from difficulties
quiz.e: The structures 'persisted through' disruption — they survived and endured. 'Resilient' = able to withstand and recover. 'Elastic' is a physical sense. 'Resistant to all change' is too absolute.

quiz.q:
Text: 'Though the two theories appear superficially similar, closer examination reveals they rest on fundamentally incompatible assumptions about the nature of consciousness.'

As used in the text, 'incompatible' most nearly means
o: unable to coexist or be reconciled
quiz.e: The assumptions 'cannot coexist' — they can't both be right simultaneously. 'Incompatible' = unable to be reconciled. 'Difficult to understand' changes the meaning entirely.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The documentary draws on extensive archival footage to illuminate aspects of the artist's life that were previously unknown.'

As used in the text, 'illuminate' most nearly means
quiz.e: The footage 'sheds light on' previously unknown aspects — makes them clear and understandable. The physical lighting sense doesn't apply here.

quizTr.uz: Eskizlar 'rough' va yakuniy emas — 'provisional' bu yerda vaqtinchalik degani; boshqa variantlar 'provision' so'zining boshqa ma'nolari.
quizTr.ru: Наброски «rough» и не окончательны — «provisional» здесь значит «временный»; остальные варианты — другие значения слова «provision».

quizTr.uz: Tuzilmalar buzilishlardan omon qolib chidagan — 'resilient' bardosh berib tiklana olishni bildiradi; 'elastic' jismoniy ma'no, 'barcha o'zgarishga chidamli' juda mutlaq.
quizTr.ru: Структуры «пережили» потрясения — «resilient» значит «способный выстоять и восстановиться»; «elastic» — физический смысл, «устойчивый к любым изменениям» слишком абсолютен.

quizTr.uz: Taxminlar bir vaqtda to'g'ri bo'la olmaydi — 'incompatible' kelishtirib bo'lmaslikni bildiradi; 'tushunish qiyin' ma'noni butunlay o'zgartiradi.
quizTr.ru: Допущения не могут быть верны одновременно — «incompatible» значит «непримиримый»; «трудный для понимания» полностью меняет смысл.

quizTr.uz: 'Sheds light on' — ilgari noma'lum jihatlarni aniq va tushunarli qilishni bildiradi; jismoniy yoritish ma'nosi bu yerda mos kelmaydi.
quizTr.ru: «Sheds light on» — делает ранее неизвестные стороны ясными и понятными; физический смысл освещения здесь не подходит.

reading.title: Drawing Inferences from Text
reading.text:
Inference questions ask you to determine what is MOST REASONABLY CONCLUDED from the passage — not what is directly stated, but what logically FOLLOWS from the information given. The question stems typically read: 'Based on the passage, it can most reasonably be inferred that...' or 'The passage most strongly suggests which of the following?' The key constraint: the correct answer must be SUPPORTED by the passage — not merely consistent with it, not something you personally believe is true, but something the passage's information REQUIRES or STRONGLY IMPLIES.

The most important rule for inference questions: the correct answer cannot go BEYOND what the passage supports. If the passage says a drug reduced symptoms in 60% of patients in one study, you cannot infer the drug is generally effective for all patients. You can infer it reduced symptoms in that study's population. The exam frequently tests whether students over-infer: the trap answers are often things that seem logical and may even be true in the real world, but the passage doesn't actually provide enough information to support them.

Elimination strategy for inference questions: (1) ELIMINATE answers that are directly stated in the passage — inference means reading BETWEEN the lines, not restating what's already there. (2) ELIMINATE answers that require information not in the passage. (3) ELIMINATE answers where the logical jump is too large. (4) ELIMINATE answers that contradict any part of the passage. The correct answer will be the one most tightly and logically supported by the passage's actual content.

Key points:
• Inference = what FOLLOWS logically from the passage (not what's stated directly)
• Correct answer: tightly supported by passage content, not beyond it
• Eliminate: answers that are directly stated (not inferences)
• Eliminate: answers requiring information NOT in the passage
• Eliminate: answers where the logical jump is too large
• Eliminate: answers that contradict any part of the passage
• Over-inference trap: may be true in real life but passage doesn't support it

quiz.q:
Passage: 'The introduction of rabbits to Australia in the 1850s led to a population explosion, with rabbits consuming native vegetation that many endemic species depended on. Within decades, several native mammal species had declined precipitously in affected regions.'

From the passage, it can be most reasonably inferred that
o: All invasive species cause ecological damage wherever they are introduced
Rabbits were intentionally introduced to Australia by settlers who wanted them for food
The native Australian mammal species that declined were competing with rabbits for the same vegetation
Rabbits are now extinct in Australia due to control measures
quiz.e: C is directly supported. A over-generalizes (all invasive species). B adds a motivation not in the passage. D contradicts the passage (rabbits thrived — a population explosion).

quiz.q:
Passage: 'A study of 300 adults found that those who regularly journaled about stressful events reported lower levels of perceived stress after six weeks. The researchers noted that the act of writing may help individuals process emotional experiences more systematically.'

Which inference is MOST supported by the passage?
o: Journaling eliminates stress for everyone who tries it consistently
For the adults in this study, regular journaling was associated with lower self-reported stress levels
Writing in a journal is superior to all other stress-management techniques
Journaling works by activating specific neurological pathways associated with emotional regulation
quiz.e: A over-claims ('eliminates stress for everyone'). C requires comparative data with other techniques — not in the passage. D claims neurological pathways — not supported (researchers only 'noted' the writing may help with systematic processing).

quiz.q:
Passage: 'The invention of the printing press fundamentally transformed European literacy rates. Before Gutenberg, books were hand-copied and affordable only to monasteries, noble households, and the very wealthy. Within a century of the press's invention, affordable books were available to artisans, merchants, and the growing middle class.'

From the passage, it can most reasonably be inferred that
o: The printing press was the only factor responsible for rising European literacy rates
Before the printing press, literacy in Europe was largely confined to wealthy and religious elites
Gutenberg personally ensured that affordable books reached all social classes
The majority of Europeans could read and write before the printing press was invented
quiz.e: B captures this inference. A says 'only factor' (not stated). C attributes distribution to Gutenberg personally (not stated). D is directly contradicted by the passage.

quiz.q:
Passage: 'The tech industry's self-regulatory approach to data privacy has produced a decade of recurring scandals, massive data breaches affecting hundreds of millions of users, and terms of service that no ordinary user reads or understands. Advocates continue to argue that government regulation would stifle innovation.'

The passage most strongly implies that the author
o: Believes the tech industry's self-regulatory approach has been successful
Is skeptical that self-regulation has adequately protected user privacy, and finds the innovation argument insufficient
Fully supports government regulation of the tech industry
Believes data breaches are an inevitable feature of digital technology
