quiz.e: This implies the author finds self-regulation inadequate and the innovation argument insufficient. B is most accurate. A contradicts the evidence presented. C over-infers (author implies problems, doesn't advocate specific government regulation). D is not stated.

quiz.q:
Passage: 'In countries with universal healthcare, individuals rarely delay seeking medical treatment due to cost concerns. In the United States, surveys consistently find that approximately 30% of adults report skipping recommended medical care because of cost.'

From the passage, it can most reasonably be inferred that
o: Universal healthcare systems always provide better medical outcomes than the US system
In countries with universal healthcare, financial barriers to accessing care are largely absent
The United States has the worst healthcare system among developed nations
US doctors recommend more medical care than doctors in countries with universal healthcare
quiz.e: B captures this precisely. A requires 'better outcomes' data — not provided. C requires a ranking against all developed nations. D attributes the difference to different recommendation rates — not what the passage says (it's about patient decisions in response to cost).

quizTr.uz: C bevosita asoslangan: A barcha invaziv turlarga umumlashtiradi, B matnda yo'q motiv qo'shadi, D matnga zid (quyonlar juda ko'payib ketgan).
quizTr.ru: C прямо подтверждается: A обобщает на все инвазивные виды, B добавляет мотив, которого нет, D противоречит тексту (кролики резко размножились).

quizTr.uz: A haddan tashqari da'vo qiladi ('hammada stressni yo'qotadi'), C boshqa usullar bilan taqqoslashni talab qiladi, D esa matnda asoslanmagan neyrologik da'vo.
quizTr.ru: A преувеличивает («устраняет стресс у всех»), C требует сравнения с другими техниками, D заявляет о нейронных механизмах без опоры на текст.

quizTr.uz: B shu xulosani qamraydi: A 'yagona omil' deydi (aytilmagan), C tarqatishni shaxsan Gutenbergga bog'laydi (aytilmagan), D matnga to'g'ridan-to'g'ri zid.
quizTr.ru: B передаёт этот вывод: A говорит «единственный фактор» (не заявлено), C приписывает распространение лично Gutenberg (не заявлено), D прямо противоречит тексту.

quizTr.uz: Muallif o'z-o'zini tartibga solishni yetarli emas va innovatsiya argumentini ishonarsiz deb biladi — B eng aniq; A dalillarga zid, C ortiqcha xulosa chiqaradi, D aytilmagan.
quizTr.ru: Автор считает саморегулирование недостаточным, а довод об инновациях неубедительным — B точнее всех; A противоречит фактам, C делает лишний вывод, D не заявлено.

quizTr.uz: B buni aniq qamraydi: A 'yaxshiroq natijalar' ma'lumotini talab qiladi (berilmagan), C barcha rivojlangan davlatlar reytingini, D esa farqni matn aytmagan sababga bog'laydi.
quizTr.ru: B передаёт это точно: A требует данных о «лучших исходах» (их нет), C — рейтинга среди всех развитых стран, D приписывает разницу не той причине, что названа в тексте.

reading.title: Implications & What the Author Suggests
reading.text:
IMPLICATION questions ask what the author SUGGESTS without directly stating — what attitude, assumption, or conclusion is implied by the author's word choice, structure, or argument. These questions often use stems like: 'The author of the passage would most likely agree that...' or 'The passage implies that...' or 'The information in the passage suggests which of the following?' Unlike pure inference questions, implication questions often require you to detect the author's TONE or ATTITUDE toward the subject.

Key techniques for implication questions: (1) Look for EVALUATIVE language — adjectives and adverbs that signal the author's attitude ('unfortunately,' 'remarkably,' 'merely,' 'despite'). (2) Pay attention to what the author EMPHASIZES versus what is mentioned briefly or with qualifications. (3) Note the STRUCTURE of the argument — does the author present one view before refuting it? This implies the author disagrees with the first view. (4) The author's implication is always grounded in the TEXT — if you can't point to specific textual evidence for the implication, it's probably not the correct answer.

Common traps in implication questions: (1) Statements that are CONSISTENT with the author's position but not actually IMPLIED — the author might not disagree with them but doesn't suggest them. (2) Extreme statements that take the author's position further than the text warrants ('the author would NEVER' or 'the author believes ALL cases...'). (3) Statements that come from your EXTERNAL KNOWLEDGE about the topic rather than from the passage's own argument.

Key points:
• Implication = what the author SUGGESTS, not directly states
• Look for evaluative language: 'unfortunately,' 'remarkably,' 'merely,' 'despite'
• Emphasis signals agreement; brief/qualified mention signals skepticism or reservation
• Author refutes View A = author disagrees with View A
• Implication must be grounded in specific textual evidence
• Trap: consistent-with-author's-position ≠ implied by author
• Trap: extreme versions of the author's view ('always,' 'never,' 'all')

quiz.q:
Passage: 'The housing voucher program, despite modest funding increases over the past decade, serves only about one in four eligible families. The remaining three-quarters are left to navigate a private rental market increasingly dominated by institutional investors whose profit-driven decisions have accelerated rent increases well beyond wage growth. Defenders of the status quo insist that market forces will eventually correct these imbalances.'

The passage most strongly implies the author believes
o: The housing voucher program is adequately funded and should be maintained
The current approach to housing affordability is insufficient and leaves most eligible families without adequate support
Market forces will eventually solve the housing affordability problem
Institutional investors should be prohibited from participating in residential real estate markets
quiz.e: The defenders of the status quo are presented neutrally — the author's language consistently implies inadequacy. B is correct. A contradicts the 'only one in four' framing. C is what the 'defenders' argue, not the author. D is not stated.

quiz.q:
Passage: 'Proponents of homeschooling cite studies showing that homeschooled students perform above average on standardized tests. Critics argue that these studies suffer from selection bias: families who choose homeschooling tend to be more educated, more financially stable, and more engaged with their children's education regardless of schooling format. When controlling for these factors, the homeschooling advantage largely disappears.'

The passage implies that the author's view on the standardized test advantage of homeschooling is that
o: The test advantage clearly demonstrates homeschooling's superiority as an educational method
The test advantage is likely explained by the characteristics of families who choose homeschooling rather than by the homeschooling method itself
Homeschooling should be promoted as a superior alternative to traditional schooling
Both homeschooling and traditional schooling produce equivalent academic outcomes for all students
quiz.e: This structure implies the author finds the critics' point convincing. B captures this. A accepts the proponents' view uncritically. C is a policy recommendation not in the passage. D overstates ('equivalent for all students').

quiz.q:
Passage: 'Gene drives — genetic modifications that spread through wild populations — could theoretically eliminate malaria-carrying mosquito species entirely. The prospect is genuinely exciting for global health advocates, who point to millions of annual malaria deaths. Ecologists, however, note that eliminating an entire species from complex ecosystems could trigger cascading consequences we have limited ability to predict or reverse.'

The author's attitude toward gene drives is best described as
o: Enthusiastically in favor of deploying them as quickly as possible
Fully opposed, believing the risks outweigh any potential health benefits
Cautiously interested but concerned that the ecological risks warrant careful deliberation before deployment
Neutral, providing both perspectives without indicating any view
quiz.e: The structure — present the appeal, then the serious concern — without resolving the tension suggests the author finds the excitement legitimate but the caution equally warranted. C (cautiously interested but concerned) is precisely calibrated. A ignores the ecological concern. B ignores the health benefit acknowledgment. D is wrong — the framing of ecological concern as an important qualification reveals the author's own concern.

quiz.q:
Passage: 'The pharmaceutical company announced it had identified a promising new antibiotic. Company executives noted that the drug would not be brought to market because, given that antibiotics are taken for short periods and must be kept in reserve to prevent resistance, it would not generate adequate returns for shareholders. They expressed hope that public funding or government incentives might encourage the development of the drug they had discovered but declined to produce.'

The author's attitude toward the company's decision is best described as
o: Sympathetic to the financial constraints faced by pharmaceutical companies
Implicitly critical, using the company's own logic to expose the misalignment between market incentives and public health needs
Neutral, describing a business decision without evaluation
Alarmed that antibiotic resistance has become a serious public health crisis
quiz.e: The accumulation of these details, without editorial comment, creates implicit critique through juxtaposition. B is correct. A would require sympathetic language (absent). C is wrong (the selection of these specific ironic details is evaluative). D is not the focus of the passage.

quiz.q:
Passage: 'Large language models can now produce text that is indistinguishable from human writing in many contexts. This capability has obvious benefits — it can democratize access to well-written communication. At the same time, the same capability could be used to produce disinformation at unprecedented scale. Most proposed safeguards rely on detecting AI-generated content, but detection methods have consistently lagged behind generation capabilities.'

The author's perspective on large language model capabilities is best described as
o: Alarmist, predicting inevitable misuse and catastrophic societal harm
Fully optimistic about the democratizing benefits while dismissing safety concerns
Ambivalent — acknowledging genuine benefits while expressing substantive concern about risks and the inadequacy of current safeguards
Neutral, presenting the technology's capabilities without taking a position on their implications
quiz.e: ' The final note about lagging safeguards shows the author's concern has substance beyond abstract risk acknowledgment. C — ambivalent with substantive concern — is most precise. A over-weights the concern. B ignores the safety concern. D is wrong (the 'at the same time' structure and the critical final note reveal the author's concern).

quizTr.uz: Muallif tili izchil ravishda yetarli emaslikni bildiradi — B to'g'ri; A 'to'rtdan faqat biri' faktiga zid, C himoyachilarning fikri, muallifniki emas, D aytilmagan.
quizTr.ru: Язык автора последовательно указывает на недостаточность — B верен; A противоречит факту «лишь один из четырёх», C — позиция защитников, а не автора, D не заявлено.

quizTr.uz: Tuzilma muallif tanqidchilar fikrini ishonarli topishini bildiradi — B shuni qamraydi; A tarafdorlar qarashini tanqidsiz qabul qiladi, C matnda yo'q siyosiy tavsiya, D bo'rttiradi.
quizTr.ru: Структура показывает, что автор находит довод критиков убедительным — B это передаёт; A некритично принимает позицию сторонников, C — рекомендация не из текста, D преувеличивает.

quizTr.uz: Jozibani keltirib, so'ng jiddiy xavotirni hal qilmasdan qoldirish — C ('ehtiyotkor qiziqish, ammo xavotir bilan') aynan mos; A ekologik xavotirni, B esa foyda e'tirofini e'tiborsiz qoldiradi, D xato.
quizTr.ru: Изложить привлекательность, затем серьёзное опасение, не разрешая напряжения — C («осторожный интерес с опасением») точен; A игнорирует экологический риск, B — признание пользы, D неверен.

quizTr.uz: Sharhsiz keltirilgan detallar to'plami yonma-yon qo'yish orqali yashirin tanqid yaratadi — B to'g'ri; A xayrixoh til talab qiladi (matnda yo'q), C xato (istehzoli detallar tanlovi baholovchi), D matn fokusida emas.
quizTr.ru: Накопление деталей без комментария создаёт скрытую критику через сопоставление — B верен; A требует сочувственного языка (его нет), C неверен (отбор иронических деталей оценочен), D не в фокусе текста.

quizTr.uz: Orqada qolayotgan himoya choralari haqidagi yakuniy eslatma xavotir jiddiy ekanini ko'rsatadi — C ('ikkilanuvchan, jiddiy xavotir bilan') eng aniq; A xavotirni bo'rttiradi, B xavfsizlik masalasini e'tiborsiz qoldiradi, D xato.
quizTr.ru: Финальное замечание об отстающих мерах показывает основательность опасений — C («амбивалентный, с существенным опасением») точнее всех; A перевешивает опасение, B игнорирует его, D неверен.

reading.title: Reading Charts, Tables & Graphs
reading.text:
The exam regularly includes questions where a short passage is paired with a table, bar chart, line graph, or scatterplot. These questions test whether you can accurately READ the data and INTEGRATE it with a written claim. The question types include: (1) 'Which choice most accurately represents the data in the table/graph?' (2) 'Which choice uses data from the graph to most effectively support/complete the student's argument?' (3) 'A student studying X claims Y. Which choice best describes the data that supports this claim?'

Critical reading rules for data: (1) READ THE AXES AND LABELS FIRST before looking at the data. What is being measured? What are the units? What time period? (2) For comparison questions, identify the DIRECTION (which is higher/lower) AND the MAGNITUDE (by how much). (3) For 'supports the argument' questions, read the argument claim precisely and find the data point that SPECIFICALLY MATCHES the claim. (4) NEVER bring outside knowledge — your answer must be based entirely on what the data shows, not what you know about the topic.

Common traps in data questions: (1) The answer describes data that EXISTS in the graph but does NOT support the specific argument. (2) The answer accurately describes one part of the data but misrepresents another part. (3) The answer describes what the data would show IF a different variable were measured. (4) The answer describes a TREND correctly but from the WRONG time period or category. Always verify every word of the correct answer against the actual data presented.

Key points:
• Step 1: Read axes, labels, units, and title BEFORE the data
• Step 2: Identify what is being compared and in what units
• Step 3: For 'supports argument' — match data to the EXACT claim
• Trap: data exists in the graph but doesn't support the specific claim
• Trap: describes trend from wrong time period or wrong category
• Trap: correct direction but wrong magnitude
• Never use outside knowledge — answer only from what the data shows

quiz.q:
Bar chart: Average hours of sleep per night by age group
Teens (13-17): 7.0 hrs | Young adults (18-25): 6.8 hrs | Adults (26-64): 6.9 hrs | Seniors (65+): 7.3 hrs

A student argues: 'Sleep duration decreases with age among adults.'

Which choice most accurately evaluates this claim using the data?
o: Supported — younger groups sleep less than older groups
Not supported — the data shows no consistent decrease with age; seniors sleep more than all younger groups
Partially supported — working-age adults sleep less, but the trend reverses for seniors
Supported — the differences are too small to be meaningful
quiz.e: The data shows: Teens 7.0 → Young adults 6.8 → Adults 6.9 (slight increase) → Seniors 7.3 (further increase). The trend reverses — working-age adults do sleep somewhat less, but seniors sleep the MOST. C accurately describes the partial pattern. A describes the opposite. B overstates ('no consistent decrease' is partially right, but the middle does decrease). D avoids the evaluation.

quiz.q:
Table: Water usage by sector (billion gallons/day, US)
Agriculture: 322 | Thermoelectric power: 161 | Industrial: 18 | Public supply: 39 | Other: 14

A student argues: 'Agriculture is by far the dominant consumer of water in the United States.'

Which choice most effectively uses this data to support the argument?
o: Agriculture uses 322 billion gallons per day in the United States.
Agriculture accounts for 322 billion gallons per day — more than twice the next largest sector (thermoelectric power at 161) and representing approximately 58% of total water use.
Water usage varies significantly across sectors in the United States.
All sectors combined use approximately 554 billion gallons per day.
quiz.e: The argument is about agriculture being 'BY FAR' the dominant consumer — this requires showing HOW MUCH larger it is than others. B provides the comparison (more than twice thermoelectric) AND the proportional share (58%) — both establishing 'by far.' A gives only the raw number without comparison. C is vague. D gives a total without comparison.

quiz.q:
Scatterplot showing a positive correlation between number of hospitals in a region and number of deaths in that region (r = 0.78).

A student concludes: 'The data proves that hospitals cause death — more hospitals means more deaths.'

Which response most accurately evaluates this conclusion?
o: The student is correct — the strong positive correlation proves hospitals are dangerous

The correlation exists because regions with more hospitals tend to be more densely populated and/or have sicker patients — the correlation reflects population and illness, not a causal effect of hospitals
The data is insufficient to draw any conclusions about hospitals
A negative correlation would have proven the opposite
quiz.e: More hospitals → denser, sicker populations → more deaths. The hospital count and death count both reflect an underlying variable (population size and illness burden). B correctly identifies this confound. A claims correlation = causation. C is too dismissive (the data does show something — just not what the student concluded). D is irrelevant.

quiz.q:
Table: Streaming revenue as percentage of total music industry revenue
2015: 22% | 2017: 38% | 2019: 56% | 2021: 65% | 2023: 71%

Which statement most accurately describes the data?
o: Streaming revenue has exceeded physical media revenue every year since 2015
Streaming has grown as a share of total music revenue in every period shown, though the rate of growth has slowed in recent years
The music industry's total revenue has increased since 2015
By 2023, streaming had completely replaced all other music formats
quiz.e: A requires data about physical media separately — not provided. C requires total revenue data — only percentages are given. D says 'completely replaced' — 29% is still non-streaming in 2023.

quiz.q:
A student writes: 'Renewable energy's share of global electricity generation has grown substantially, though fossil fuels still dominate. _____'

Table: Global electricity by source (2022)
Coal: 36% | Natural gas: 23% | Nuclear: 10% | Hydro: 15% | Wind: 7% | Solar: 4% | Other renewables: 5%

Which choice most effectively uses the data to complete the argument?
o: Coal alone generates 36% of global electricity.
All renewables combined — hydro (15%), wind (7%), solar (4%), and other (5%) — account for 31% of global electricity, still well below coal's 36% and fossil fuels' combined 59%.
Solar energy is growing rapidly and will soon surpass coal.
The data shows that nuclear energy generates 10% of global electricity.
quiz.e: The argument states renewable growth BUT fossil fuel dominance. B supports this precisely: calculates all renewables (31%) AND explicitly compares to coal (36%) and all fossil fuels (59%) — showing fossil fuel dominance. A gives only one fossil fuel figure. C adds a prediction not in the data. D gives a single non-renewable figure without the comparison.

quizTr.uz: Mehnat yoshidagilar biroz kamroq uxlaydi, lekin keksalarda tendensiya teskari (7.3 — eng ko'p) — C shu qisman naqshni to'g'ri tasvirlaydi; A teskarisini aytadi, B bo'rttiradi, D bahodan qochadi.
quizTr.ru: Работающие возрасты спят чуть меньше, но у пожилых тренд разворачивается (7.3 — больше всех) — C точно описывает частичную закономерность; A — обратное, B преувеличивает, D уходит от оценки.

quizTr.uz: 'By far' ustunlikni ko'rsatish uchun taqqoslash kerak — B buni beradi: thermoelectric'dan ikki baravar ko'p VA 58% ulush; A faqat yalang'och raqam, C noaniq, D taqqoslashsiz jami.
quizTr.ru: Для «by far» нужно сравнение — B даёт его: более чем вдвое больше thermoelectric И доля 58%; A — лишь голое число, C расплывчат, D — итог без сравнения.

quizTr.uz: Kasalxonalar soni ham, o'limlar soni ham aholi zichligi va kasallik yukini aks ettiradi — B shu chalkashtiruvchi omilni to'g'ri aniqlaydi; A korrelyatsiyani sabab deb biladi, C juda inkor etadi, D aloqasiz.
quizTr.ru: И число больниц, и число смертей отражают население и уровень заболеваемости — B верно определяет этот искажающий фактор; A приравнивает корреляцию к причинности, C чрезмерно отрицает, D нерелевантен.

quizTr.uz: A jismoniy tashuvchilar bo'yicha alohida ma'lumot, C esa umumiy daromad ma'lumotini talab qiladi (faqat foizlar berilgan); D 'butunlay almashtirdi' deydi — 2023 da hali 29% streaming emas.
quizTr.ru: A требует отдельных данных о физических носителях, C — об общей выручке (даны только проценты); D говорит «полностью заменил», хотя 29% в 2023 — не streaming.

quizTr.uz: B argumentni aniq qo'llab-quvvatlaydi: barcha qayta tiklanuvchilarni (31%) hisoblab, ko'mir (36%) va qazilma yoqilg'i (59%) bilan taqqoslaydi; A bitta raqam, C ma'lumotlarda yo'q bashorat qo'shadi, D taqqoslashsiz.
quizTr.ru: B точно подтверждает аргумент: суммирует возобновляемые (31%) и сравнивает с углём (36%) и ископаемым топливом (59%); A — одна цифра, C добавляет прогноз не из данных, D без сравнения.

reading.title: Integrating Data with Textual Arguments
reading.text:
The most challenging data questions ask you to COMPLETE a student's argument by selecting which data best fills a specific logical gap. The student's passage will make a claim, then say something like 'as shown in the data' or 'the data supports this because...' — and you must choose which specific data point or description MOST SPECIFICALLY supports the argument being made. The key: do not choose data that is merely RELATED to the topic — choose data that SPECIFICALLY PROVES the exact assertion.

For COMPLETING A CLAIM with data: (1) Identify the EXACT assertion the student is making (not the general topic). (2) Ask: 'What specific number or comparison would prove THIS assertion?' (3) Find the data that provides exactly that proof. Wrong answers typically describe real data that supports a RELATED but DIFFERENT point than the one being made.

For INTERPRETING WHAT THE DATA SHOWS: Be careful about (1) CORRELATIONS vs. CAUSES — data showing A and B together does not mean A causes B. (2) RELATIVE vs. ABSOLUTE — a category can be the 'fastest growing' while still being the smallest in absolute terms. (3) AVERAGES vs. DISTRIBUTIONS — an average says nothing about individual variation. (4) PARTIAL DATA — a trend in the data for years 2015-2020 does not necessarily represent a trend for all years.

Key points:
• Completing a claim: find data that proves THE EXACT ASSERTION, not just the topic
• Wrong answer: related data that proves a DIFFERENT point
• Correlation ≠ causation — data shows association, not cause
• Relative vs. absolute: fastest-growing category may still be smallest
• Average hides distribution: average can be high while most values are low
• Partial data: a trend over selected years doesn't mean a universal trend
• Always check: does this data support THIS claim or a SIMILAR claim?

quiz.q:
Table: Electric vehicle sales (thousands of units)
         | 2018  | 2023
Norway:  | 72    | 138
Germany: | 36    | 524
USA:     | 361   | 1,189

A student argues: 'Norway is the world leader in the EV transition.'

Which response most accurately evaluates this claim using only the data provided?
o: Supported — Norway had the highest growth rate between 2018 and 2023
The data cannot support or refute this claim as stated, since absolute sales units don't account for population size, and the table doesn't include market share percentages
Contradicted — the USA sold far more EVs than Norway in 2023
Supported — Norway was first to adopt EVs, starting in 2018
quiz.e: Norway's small absolute numbers might represent a very high market share (which it does in reality), but the DATA ALONE doesn't show this. B correctly identifies the data's limitation. A says 'growth rate' — but Norway grew from 72 to 138 (92%) while Germany grew from 36 to 524 (>1,000%). C uses absolute sales — but total car market size matters for 'leadership.' D misreads the timing.

quiz.q:
Line graph: US college tuition (inflation-adjusted, thousands USD/year)
2000: $8,000 | 2005: $9,500 | 2010: $11,000 | 2015: $13,500 | 2020: $15,000

Which conclusion is NOT supported by the data?
o: Tuition increased in every five-year period shown
The rate of tuition increase has accelerated over time
By 2020, inflation-adjusted tuition was nearly double what it was in 2000
Financial aid offset the tuition increases shown, making college no more expensive for students
quiz.e: 5→11→13.5→15 — increases in every period. SUPPORTED. B: Increases per period: +1.5, +1.5, +2.5, +1.5 — not clearly accelerating but the overall trend shows faster growth after 2005. ARGUABLY SUPPORTED. C: $15K / $8K = 1.875 — nearly double. SUPPORTED. D: Financial aid data is NOT in the graph. The graph shows tuition cost, not net cost after aid. D cannot be determined from this data. NOT SUPPORTED.

quiz.q:
Table: Average annual salary by education level
High school: $40,000 | Associate's: $50,000 | Bachelor's: $70,000 | Master's: $85,000

A student concludes: 'Getting a bachelor's degree guarantees you will earn at least $70,000 per year.'

Which response most accurately evaluates this conclusion?
o: The student's conclusion is supported by the data
The data shows an AVERAGE, so many bachelor's degree holders earn significantly less than $70,000; the conclusion confuses average with minimum
The data proves that advanced degrees are not worth pursuing
Every bachelor's degree holder will earn exactly $70,000
quiz.e: The student confuses average with minimum/guarantee. B is correct. A accepts the flawed reasoning. C is an unsupported extreme conclusion. D confuses average with an exact amount.

quiz.q:
Bar chart: % of adults who trust news from each source in 2023
Local TV: 52% | National newspapers: 48% | Online news: 41% | Cable TV: 37% | Social media: 18%

A student argues: 'Traditional news sources are trusted more than digital ones.'

Which response most accurately evaluates this claim?
o: Fully supported — traditional sources rank higher than digital in every comparison

Partially supported — traditional sources (local TV, national newspapers) do rank higher than social media and cable news, but online news sites occupy a middle position, making the traditional/digital divide less clear than claimed
Not supported — no sources are trusted by a majority of adults
Fully contradicted — digital news is more accessible than traditional news
quiz.e: But cable TV (traditionally distributed but 24-hour 'cable news' is arguably less traditional) at 37% is below online news at 41%. The picture is more nuanced than a clean traditional > digital pattern. B is most accurate. A overstates — cable TV (arguable traditional source) is below online news. C ignores local TV's 52% majority. D is unrelated to trust.

quiz.q:
Table: Countries ranked by happiness score (0-10) vs. GDP per capita (USD)
Finland: 7.8 happiness / $53K GDP | Denmark: 7.6 / $68K | Iceland: 7.5 / $73K | Netherlands: 7.4 / $57K | Switzerland: 7.5 / $93K | Australia: 7.1 / $63K | USA: 6.9 / $80K | Japan: 5.9 / $42K

A student argues: 'Higher GDP per capita causes greater happiness.'

Which response most accurately evaluates this claim?
o: Fully supported — every wealthier country is happier

The data shows a rough positive relationship but notable exceptions (Switzerland is the wealthiest shown yet not the happiest; Japan has a lower GDP and lower happiness, consistent with the claim), suggesting wealth correlates with but does not clearly cause happiness
The data proves that GDP has no relationship to happiness
USA's lower happiness score proves that GDP is irrelevant to happiness
quiz.e: 5 vs Finland's 7.8). This complicates a simple 'higher GDP → higher happiness' pattern. The overall trend is positive (generally wealthier countries are happier) but exceptions exist. B accurately describes: rough positive relationship WITH notable exceptions, correlation ≠ causation. A says 'every wealthier country' — Switzerland disproves this. C says 'no relationship' — clearly there's some. D draws too strong a conclusion from one country.

quizTr.uz: Mutlaq sotuv raqamlari aholi va bozor hajmini hisobga olmaydi — B ma'lumotlarning shu cheklovini to'g'ri aniqlaydi; A o'sish sur'atini noto'g'ri o'qiydi, C mutlaq raqamlarga tayanadi, D vaqtni noto'g'ri o'qiydi.
quizTr.ru: Абсолютные продажи не учитывают население и размер рынка — B верно определяет это ограничение данных; A путает темпы роста, C опирается на абсолютные цифры, D неверно читает сроки.

quizTr.uz: Moliyaviy yordam ma'lumotlari grafikda YO'Q — grafik yordamdan keyingi emas, o'qish narxini ko'rsatadi, shuning uchun D ni bu ma'lumotlardan aniqlab bo'lmaydi.
quizTr.ru: Данных о финансовой помощи на графике НЕТ — он показывает стоимость обучения, а не чистую цену после помощи, поэтому D нельзя вывести из этих данных.

quizTr.uz: Talaba o'rtacha qiymatni minimum yoki kafolat bilan chalkashtiradi — B to'g'ri; A xato mulohazani qabul qiladi, C asossiz keskin xulosa, D o'rtachani aniq summa deb biladi.
quizTr.ru: Студент путает среднее с минимумом или гарантией — B верен; A принимает ошибочную логику, C — необоснованно резкий вывод, D путает среднее с точной суммой.

quizTr.uz: Kabel TV (37%) onlayn yangiliklardan (41%) past, shuning uchun manzara sof 'an'anaviy > raqamli' emas — B eng aniq; A bo'rttiradi, C mahalliy TVning 52% ko'pchiligini e'tiborsiz qoldiradi, D ishonchga aloqasiz.
quizTr.ru: Кабельное ТВ (37%) ниже онлайн-новостей (41%), поэтому картина не сводится к «традиционные > цифровые» — B точнее всех; A преувеличивает, C игнорирует 52% местного ТВ, D не о доверии.

quizTr.uz: Umumiy tendensiya ijobiy, lekin istisnolar bor (eng boy Switzerland eng baxtli emas) — B to'g'ri tasvirlaydi: taxminiy ijobiy bog'liqlik, korrelyatsiya ≠ sabab; A ni Switzerland rad etadi, C da 'aloqa yo'q' xato, D bitta davlatdan kuchli xulosa chiqaradi.
quizTr.ru: Общий тренд положительный, но есть исключения (богатейшая Switzerland не самая счастливая) — B описывает верно: примерная связь, корреляция ≠ причинность; A опровергается Switzerland, C («связи нет») неверен, D делает сильный вывод из одной страны.

reading.title: Words in Context
reading.text:
Words in Context questions appear on every exam test and are among the most frequent question type. The question asks: 'As used in the text, what does the word [X] most nearly mean?' The critical rule: you are NOT tested on the word's most common meaning. You are tested on how the author uses the word in THIS specific context.

Best strategy: (1) COVER the answer choices. (2) Read the sentence with the target word PLUS the surrounding sentences. (3) Substitute your own word or phrase. (4) Match your substitution to the closest answer choice. (5) Plug it back in and verify. Wrong answers are usually the word's most common everyday meaning — the exam often uses words in more specialized or metaphorical senses.

Three trap patterns: (1) COMMON vs. CONTEXT — 'address' commonly means a home location; in academic text it means 'to deal with or tackle.' (2) REGISTER SHIFT — the correct answer often matches the formal or technical register of the surrounding text. (3) NEAR-SYNONYM TRAP — the exam often includes a word that is close to correct but subtly wrong in tone or precision. Always prioritize what fits the passage over what you know the word means in daily life.

Key points:
• Cover choices → read context → substitute your own word → match → verify
• Target: the author's USE here, not the word's most common meaning
• Trap 1: most common everyday meaning (usually wrong on exam)
• Trap 2: a meaning the word CAN have, but doesn't fit this context
• Trap 3: near-synonym that is subtly off in tone or precision
• If the word is positive/negative, check the surrounding tone first
• Multiple meanings: choose the one fitting the ENTIRE surrounding context

quiz.q:
Text: 'The committee reviewed the budget proposal and identified several areas where spending could be addressed without compromising core programs.'

As used in the text, 'addressed' most nearly means
o: written as a formal letter to
quiz.e: Substitute: what would the committee DO with areas of spending — not write to them or speak about them (those use 'address' differently). They would 'reduce' or 'control' or 'tackle' the spending. C matches. A and D use the noun/acknowledgment sense. B uses the speech sense.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The geological record documents several mass extinction events in which environmental disruption precipitated the collapse of dominant species.

As used in the text, 'precipitated' most nearly means
quiz.e: ' Environmental disruption 'triggered' the collapse. The weather/rain sense (A) doesn't apply. 'Predicted' (B) changes the meaning. 'Prevented' (D) is the opposite.

quiz.q:
Text: 'Critics found the director's latest film earnest to the point of naivety — its sincerity felt unearned, more like sentimentality than genuine emotional insight.'

As used in the text, 'earnest' most nearly means
o: seriously sincere in a way the critics found excessive
highly original in theme and style
quiz.e: ' B — seriously sincere in a way the critics found excessive — captures this ambivalent sense. A is financial. C and D are unrelated meanings.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The enzyme's catalytic function was significantly attenuated when researchers reduced the temperature of the reaction environment below 15°C.'

As used in the text, 'attenuated' most nearly means
quiz.e: The context (reduced temperature reduces enzyme function) confirms B. A is the opposite. C overstates ('completely destroyed'). D is a different process (transformation).

quiz.q:
Text: 'The senator's measured response neither confirmed nor denied the allegations, allowing her to preserve optionality without committing to a position that might prove untenable.'

As used in the text, 'untenable' most nearly means
quiz.e: The senator avoids committing to something she couldn't defend later. B is correct. A applies to financial positions. C is legal. D is about information disclosure, not the position's defensibility.

quizTr.uz: Qo'mita xarajatlarni 'kamaytiradi' yoki 'nazorat qiladi' — C mos; A va D 'address'ning ot/murojaat ma'nosi, B nutq ma'nosi.
quizTr.ru: Комитет «сократит» или «возьмёт под контроль» расходы — подходит C; A и D — значение обращения/адреса у «address», B — смысл речи.

quizTr.uz: Ekologik buzilish inqirozni 'keltirib chiqargan' — ob-havo/yomg'ir ma'nosi (A) mos emas, 'bashorat qildi' (B) ma'noni o'zgartiradi, 'oldini oldi' (D) teskarisi.
quizTr.ru: Экологический сдвиг «спровоцировал» коллапс — погодный смысл (A) не подходит, «предсказал» (B) меняет смысл, «предотвратил» (D) — противоположность.

quizTr.uz: B — tanqidchilar ortiqcha deb bilgan jiddiy samimiylik — aynan shu ikkilangan ma'noni qamraydi; A moliyaviy ma'no, C va D aloqasiz ma'nolar.
quizTr.ru: B — серьёзная искренность, показавшаяся критикам чрезмерной — передаёт именно этот двойственный смысл; A — финансовое значение, C и D не связаны.

quizTr.uz: Kontekst (past harorat ferment faoliyatini pasaytiradi) B ni tasdiqlaydi; A teskarisi, C bo'rttiradi ('butunlay yo'q qilingan'), D boshqa jarayon (aylanish).
quizTr.ru: Контекст (снижение температуры ослабляет работу фермента) подтверждает B; A — противоположность, C преувеличивает («полностью разрушен»), D — другой процесс (превращение).

quizTr.uz: Senator keyinchalik himoya qilib bo'lmaydigan pozitsiyaga bog'lanishdan qochadi — B to'g'ri; A moliyaviy pozitsiyalarga oid, C yuridik ma'no, D pozitsiya emas, ma'lumot oshkor qilish haqida.
quizTr.ru: Сенатор избегает позиции, которую не сможет потом отстоять — B верен; A — о финансовых позициях, C — юридический смысл, D — о раскрытии информации, а не о позиции.

reading.title: Logical Transitions
reading.text:
Transition questions ask you to select the word or phrase that best connects two sentences or ideas. The question presents a sentence with a blank and asks which transition 'most logically' completes it. These questions test your understanding of LOGICAL RELATIONSHIPS between ideas, not grammar.

The five essential logical relationships: (1) CONTRAST: however, nevertheless, although, while, despite, yet, on the other hand. (2) ADDITION/SUPPORT: furthermore, moreover, additionally, in fact, indeed, also. (3) CAUSE/EFFECT: therefore, consequently, as a result, thus, hence. (4) CONCESSION: admittedly, granted, to be sure. (5) EXEMPLIFICATION: for example, for instance, specifically, in particular.

The most common exam traps: (a) 'However' vs. 'Moreover' — however=contrast, moreover=addition. The sentences look similar but their logical direction is opposite. (b) 'Therefore' vs. 'Nevertheless' — therefore=result, nevertheless=contrast-despite-something. (c) Subtle contrast vs. strong contrast — 'while' signals a mild contrast; 'however' signals a clear break. Always read BOTH sentences fully before choosing.

Key points:
• Contrast: however, nevertheless, yet, while, despite, although, on the other hand
• Addition: furthermore, moreover, additionally, in fact, indeed, also, similarly
• Cause/Effect: therefore, consequently, thus, as a result, hence
• Concession: admittedly, granted, to be sure, it is true that
• Example: for example, for instance, specifically, in particular, namely
• Test step 1: Does sentence 2 ADD to, CONTRAST with, or RESULT from sentence 1?
• Test step 2: Choose the transition that precisely matches that relationship

quiz.q:
'A series of poor harvests depleted the region's grain reserves. _____, food prices rose sharply, triggering widespread unrest among urban workers.'

Which transition most logically completes the text?
quiz.e: CAUSE/EFFECT → Consequently. 'Furthermore' adds information. 'However' signals contrast. 'For instance' introduces an example.

quiz.q:
'Early versions of the vaccine showed limited effectiveness in clinical trials. _____, real-world data collected after broad rollout revealed substantially higher protection rates than the trials had suggested.'

Which transition most logically completes the text?
quiz.e: Something positive happens DESPITE the negative trial result. CONTRAST-DESPITE → Nevertheless. 'Therefore' and 'Consequently' are cause/effect. 'Similarly' suggests sameness.

quiz.q:
'Research shows that students who read for pleasure perform better on standardized tests. _____, they tend to demonstrate stronger writing skills and a larger active vocabulary than non-readers.'

Which transition most logically completes the text?
quiz.e: S2 (also stronger writing and vocabulary — additional benefits). The second sentence ADDS more benefits to the first. ADDITION → Furthermore. 'However' would signal contrast. 'Therefore' would signal a result. 'For example' would introduce an illustration.

quiz.q:
'Many natural materials have been repurposed in innovative ways by contemporary designers. _____, one furniture company uses mushroom mycelium grown in custom molds to produce biodegradable packaging that is stronger than polystyrene.'

Which transition most logically completes the text?
quiz.e: S2 provides a SPECIFIC CASE (mushroom mycelium furniture). EXEMPLIFICATION → For instance. 'Nevertheless' is contrast. 'As a result' is cause/effect. 'Furthermore' could add another general point, but 'for instance' introduces a specific example.

quiz.q:
'The documentary presents compelling evidence for its central thesis. _____, several historians have noted that the filmmakers selectively omitted sources that complicate their argument.'

Which transition most logically completes the text?
quiz.e: S2 (historians note selective omission — qualification/complication). The second sentence concedes a problem with something that was just praised. CONCESSION → Admittedly (signals acknowledging a flaw). 'Moreover' would add another positive. 'Consequently' would suggest the historians' note is a result. 'For example' would introduce an illustration.

quizTr.uz: SABAB/OQIBAT → Consequently; 'Furthermore' qo'shimcha ma'lumot kiritadi, 'However' qarama-qarshilikni bildiradi, 'For instance' misol keltiradi.
quizTr.ru: ПРИЧИНА/СЛЕДСТВИЕ → Consequently; «Furthermore» добавляет информацию, «However» противопоставляет, «For instance» вводит пример.

quizTr.uz: Salbiy sinov natijasiga QARAMAY ijobiy narsa yuz beradi → Nevertheless; 'Therefore' va 'Consequently' sabab-oqibat, 'Similarly' o'xshashlikni bildiradi.
quizTr.ru: Позитивное происходит ВОПРЕКИ неудачному результату испытания → Nevertheless; «Therefore» и «Consequently» — следствие, «Similarly» — сходство.

quizTr.uz: Ikkinchi jumla birinchisiga yana foydalar QO'SHADI → Furthermore; 'However' qarama-qarshilik, 'Therefore' natija, 'For example' esa misol bo'lardi.
quizTr.ru: Второе предложение ДОБАВЛЯЕТ к первому новые плюсы → Furthermore; «However» дал бы контраст, «Therefore» — результат, «For example» — иллюстрацию.

quizTr.uz: Ikkinchi jumla ANIQ MISOL keltiradi (mushroom mycelium mebeli) → For instance; 'Nevertheless' qarama-qarshilik, 'As a result' sabab-oqibat, 'Furthermore' umumiy fikr qo'shardi.
quizTr.ru: Второе предложение даёт КОНКРЕТНЫЙ пример (мебель из mushroom mycelium) → For instance; «Nevertheless» — контраст, «As a result» — следствие, «Furthermore» добавил бы общий тезис.

quizTr.uz: Ikkinchi jumla endigina maqtalgan narsadagi kamchilikni TAN OLADI → Admittedly; 'Moreover' yana ijobiy fikr qo'shardi, 'Consequently' natija qilardi, 'For example' misol kiritardi.
quizTr.ru: Второе предложение ПРИЗНАЁТ изъян в только что похваленном → Admittedly; «Moreover» добавил бы позитив, «Consequently» сделал бы это следствием, «For example» ввёл бы пример.

reading.title: Identifying Text Structure & Organization
reading.text:
Text structure questions ask HOW a passage is organized — what overall pattern the author uses to present information. The exam tests six major text structures: (1) CHRONOLOGICAL — events or ideas presented in time order. (2) COMPARE AND CONTRAST — discusses similarities and/or differences between two or more things. (3) CAUSE AND EFFECT — explains why something happened and what resulted. (4) PROBLEM AND SOLUTION — identifies a challenge and proposes how to address it. (5) DESCRIPTION/CLASSIFICATION — presents characteristics of a topic or organizes things into categories. (6) CLAIM AND COUNTERCLAIM — presents a position, then acknowledges and responds to opposing views.

The key to identifying structure is to look at the RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN PARAGRAPHS or sentences, not just the content. Ask: 'Why does sentence 2 come after sentence 1? What logical relationship connects them?' Compare/contrast passages use signal words like 'similarly,' 'in contrast,' 'whereas,' 'on the other hand.' Problem-solution uses 'however,' 'to address this,' 'one solution is.' Cause-effect uses 'because,' 'as a result,' 'consequently.' Claim-counterclaim uses 'while some argue,' 'critics contend,' 'proponents assert.'

On the exam, structure questions often appear as: 'Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?' or 'Which choice most accurately describes what happens in the text?' The answer choices will describe the structure using verbs like 'introduces and then counters,' 'presents a problem and proposes a solution,' 'contrasts two perspectives,' or 'traces the development of.' Match these structural descriptions against the actual organization you observe in the passage.

Key points:
• Chronological: time order — first, then, next, finally, in [year]
• Compare/contrast: similarities AND/OR differences — similarly, whereas, on the other hand
• Cause/effect: reasons AND/OR consequences — because, therefore, as a result
• Problem/solution: issue identified THEN addressed — however, one approach, to remedy this
• Claim/counterclaim: position stated THEN challenged/defended — critics argue, proponents contend
• Description: characteristics or categories — consists of, is defined by, can be classified as
• Key test: what is the RELATIONSHIP between the sections, not just the content?

quiz.q:
Passage: 'In the 1940s, computer programming meant manually wiring physical connections. The development of punch cards in the 1950s allowed programs to be stored separately from the machine. Assembly languages in the late 1950s introduced symbolic commands that abstracted away from direct hardware control. By the 1960s and 70s, high-level languages like FORTRAN and COBOL enabled programmers to write instructions closer to human language. Today's Python and JavaScript continue this trajectory toward greater abstraction.'

Which best describes the overall structure of this passage?
o: A comparison of modern programming languages with historical ones
A chronological account of programming languages' evolution toward increasing abstraction
A problem-solution analysis of the limitations of early computing
A classification of different types of programming languages by complexity
quiz.e: This is CHRONOLOGICAL structure, and the thread connecting all periods is increasing abstraction. B is correct. A (comparison) requires side-by-side contrast of languages. C (problem-solution) would require identifying a problem and proposing a solution. D (classification) would organize by type without the temporal progression.

quiz.q:
Passage: 'The Roman Republic and the United States share a similar constitutional architecture: both divided power among executive, legislative, and judicial functions to prevent tyranny. However, the Roman system concentrated executive power in two annually elected consuls who could veto each other, while the American system distributes executive power in a single president. Where Rome used a Senate of hereditary aristocrats, America used an elected Senate. The Roman system ultimately proved unstable and collapsed into empire; the American system has so far endured for nearly two and a half centuries.'

Which best describes the overall structure?
o: A chronological account of both democratic systems
A comparison of the Roman Republic and the United States across shared structural features and key differences
A problem-solution analysis of what caused the fall of the Roman Republic
A description of how the Roman Republic influenced the American founding
quiz.e: president, hereditary vs. elected Senate, stability vs. collapse). Signal words: 'however,' 'while,' 'where.' B accurately identifies the COMPARE/CONTRAST structure. A is wrong — no time progression through events. C is wrong — the fall of Rome is mentioned as an outcome, not the focus. D is wrong — influence is not what's being analyzed.

quiz.q:
Passage: 'Antibiotic resistance now kills approximately 700,000 people annually, and without intervention, this toll could reach 10 million per year by 2050. The primary drivers are overprescription in medical settings, routine prophylactic use in agriculture, and patients failing to complete treatment courses. Addressing this crisis will require coordinated action: stewardship programs that restrict antibiotic prescription to confirmed bacterial infections, phasing out agricultural use except for treating illness, and global investment in developing new antibiotic classes.'

The overall structure of this passage is best described as
o: A chronological history of antibiotic development and resistance
A comparison between medical and agricultural contributions to antibiotic resistance
A presentation of a serious public health problem, its causes, and proposed solutions
A classification of the different types of antibiotic-resistant bacteria
quiz.e: C is correct. A has no chronological progression through time. B partially fits (medical vs. agricultural causes are mentioned) but 'comparison' misses the problem-solution arc. D is wrong — no classification of bacteria types.

quiz.q:
Passage: 'Proponents of free trade argue that it increases efficiency, lowers consumer prices, and raises global living standards through comparative advantage. Critics counter that free trade destroys manufacturing employment in wealthier nations and exploits workers in developing ones. Advocates respond that adjustment programs can address displacement while preserving the gains. Skeptics rejoin that adjustment assistance has historically been underfunded and workers rarely recovered their previous incomes.'

The structure is best described as
o: A chronological account of international trade policy
A classification of different types of economic agreements
A series of alternating claims and counterclaims about free trade policy
A description of how free trade works and its effects on global markets
quiz.e: This is classic CLAIM AND COUNTERCLAIM structure. C is correct. A is wrong — no time progression. B is wrong — no categorization of trade types. D is wrong — the passage is about the policy debate, not a neutral description of how free trade works.

quiz.q:
Passage: 'Clouds are classified by both altitude and form. High clouds (above 20,000 feet) include cirrus, which are wispy and ice-crystal-based. Middle clouds (6,500–20,000 feet) include altostratus, which appear as a gray sheet, and altocumulus, which form rounded masses. Low clouds include stratus, which form uniform flat layers, and cumulus, which develop vertical mass from updrafts. Cumulonimbus clouds span all altitude levels and are associated with thunderstorms.'

The overall structure of this passage is best described as
o: A chronological account of cloud formation and dissipation
A comparison of dangerous and non-dangerous cloud types
A hierarchical classification of cloud types by altitude and form
A problem-solution analysis of how clouds affect weather patterns
quiz.e: ), defining each type and its characteristics. C (hierarchical classification) is correct. A is wrong — no time progression. B is wrong — no danger/non-danger comparison. D is wrong — no problem-solution framing.

quizTr.uz: Bu XRONOLOGIK tuzilma, barcha davrlarni bog'lovchi ip — abstraksiyaning oshib borishi; B to'g'ri, A yonma-yon taqqoslashni, C muammo-yechimni, D vaqtsiz tasniflashni talab qilardi.
quizTr.ru: Это ХРОНОЛОГИЧЕСКАЯ структура, сквозная нить — рост абстракции; B верен, A требовал бы сравнения бок о бок, C — проблемы-решения, D — классификации без временной оси.

quizTr.uz: 'However', 'while', 'where' signal so'zlari TAQQOSLASH/QARAMA-QARSHI QO'YISH tuzilmasini ko'rsatadi — B to'g'ri; A da voqealar bo'ylab vaqt izchilligi yo'q, C xato (Rim qulashi fokus emas), D xato (ta'sir tahlil qilinmaydi).
quizTr.ru: Сигнальные слова «however», «while», «where» указывают на СРАВНЕНИЕ/ПРОТИВОПОСТАВЛЕНИЕ — B верен; A — нет хода по времени, C неверен (падение Рима не фокус), D неверен (влияние не анализируется).

quizTr.uz: C to'g'ri — muammo, sabablar va taklif etilgan yechimlar arki; A da xronologik rivojlanish yo'q, B dagi 'taqqoslash' muammo-yechim tuzilmasini o'tkazib yuboradi, D da bakteriya turlari tasnifi yo'q.
quizTr.ru: C верен — дуга «проблема, причины, предложенные решения»; в A нет хронологии, «сравнение» в B упускает арку проблема-решение, в D нет классификации бактерий.

quizTr.uz: Bu klassik DA'VO VA QARSHI DA'VO tuzilmasi — C to'g'ri; A da vaqt izchilligi yo'q, B da savdo turlari tasnifi yo'q, D xato — matn erkin savdo qanday ishlashining neytral tavsifi emas, siyosat bahsi.
quizTr.ru: Это классическая структура «ТЕЗИС — КОНТРТЕЗИС» — C верен; в A нет хронологии, в B нет категорий торговли, D неверен — это спор о политике, а не нейтральное описание.

quizTr.uz: Har bir tur va uning xususiyatlari ta'riflanadi — C (iyerarxik tasniflash) to'g'ri; A da xronologiya yo'q, B da xavfli/xavfsiz taqqoslashi yo'q, D da muammo-yechim tuzilmasi yo'q.
quizTr.ru: Каждый тип и его признаки определяются — верна C (иерархическая классификация); в A нет хронологии, в B нет сравнения по опасности, в D нет схемы проблема-решение.

reading.title: How Structure Supports Argument
reading.text:
Beyond identifying WHAT the structure is, advanced exam questions ask WHY the author chose that structure — how the organizational choices SUPPORT the argument being made. These questions might ask: 'Why does the author begin with X before moving to Y?' or 'What is the effect of presenting the counterargument before the main claim?' Understanding the RHETORICAL PURPOSE of structural choices requires you to think about what the author ACHIEVES by organizing the passage as they did.

Common rhetorical effects of structural choices: (1) ACKNOWLEDGING A COUNTERARGUMENT before presenting your own strengthens credibility by showing you have considered other views. (2) PRESENTING BACKGROUND BEFORE ARGUMENT establishes context that makes the argument more compelling or understandable. (3) MOVING FROM SPECIFIC EXAMPLE TO GENERAL PRINCIPLE (or vice versa) builds the argument inductively or deductively. (4) ENDING WITH A CALL TO ACTION or recommendation signals that the author's purpose is persuasive. (5) USING PARALLEL STRUCTURE (presenting multiple items the same way) creates emphasis and makes comparisons clearer.

For these questions, the answer must do two things: accurately describe WHAT the structural move is AND correctly identify WHY it serves the argument. A common trap: answers that correctly describe what a section does but misidentify its PURPOSE. Another trap: answers that correctly state a purpose but inaccurately describe what actually happens in the text. Always check both components of the answer.

Key points:
• Counterargument first = strengthens credibility by showing awareness of other views
• Background before argument = establishes context for the argument
• Specific → General = inductive reasoning (builds up to a principle)
• General → Specific = deductive reasoning (applies a principle to examples)
• Parallel structure = creates emphasis and clarity in comparisons
• Call to action at end = signals persuasive intent
• Check BOTH: what the structural move IS and what it ACHIEVES

quiz.q:
Passage structure: 'Many assume that raising the minimum wage primarily helps low-income workers. In fact, research shows that the majority of minimum wage earners are not in households below the poverty line — many are secondary earners in middle-income families. [The passage then argues for more targeted anti-poverty interventions.]'

Why does the author begin by presenting the common assumption before challenging it?
o: To concede that the common assumption is correct
To establish what the argument is pushing against, making the subsequent evidence more impactful by contrast with what readers likely believe
To prove that minimum wage workers are not poor
To introduce the topic of poverty policy in general
quiz.e: The surprise of having a common belief overturned makes the evidence more memorable and impactful. B captures this rhetorical function. A says the author concedes (wrong — the author challenges). C misidentifies the purpose as proving a single claim. D is too broad.

quiz.q:
Passage structure: [Para 1: Describes a specific case — a fishing community in Indonesia whose livelihoods collapsed after coral reef bleaching.] [Para 2: Shows that 500 million people worldwide depend on coral reefs for food and income.] [Para 3: Argues for international funding to protect coral reefs as a global economic and humanitarian priority.]

What is the effect of beginning with the Indonesian community before presenting the global statistics?
o: It proves that Indonesia is more affected than other countries
Opening with a specific human case creates emotional engagement that makes readers more receptive to the subsequent global statistics and policy argument
The specific case contradicts the global statistics presented in Para 2
It introduces an exception to the argument made in Para 3
quiz.e: The Indonesian case makes the abstract problem concrete and emotionally resonant before the scale is established (500 million). B is correct — emotional engagement is the rhetorical function. A is wrong — no comparison with other countries is implied. C and D are wrong — the specific case supports, not contradicts, the broader argument.

quiz.q:
A student argues that nuclear energy should be reconsidered for climate change. The student uses this structure: [Para 1: New technology X was feared as dangerous and economically unviable when introduced.] [Para 2: Regulation and engineering advances made technology X safe and economical.] [Para 3: Nuclear energy is currently viewed the same way X was — as too dangerous and costly.] [Para 4: Argues nuclear could similarly become viable with the right investment.]

What is the rhetorical function of the historical analogy (Paras 1-2)?
o: To prove that nuclear energy is already safe
To establish a precedent showing that feared technologies can become viable through investment — making the nuclear argument feel consistent with historical pattern rather than utopian
To demonstrate that all new technologies are initially opposed
To provide evidence that nuclear energy's risks have been exaggerated
quiz.e: This makes the argument feel less radical. B is correct. A is wrong — the analogy is about technology X, not nuclear energy directly. C overgeneralizes. D makes a specific claim about nuclear risk that the analogy doesn't directly support.

quiz.q:
Passage structure: [Para 1: Describes the severity of urban food deserts.] [Para 2: Explains why conventional grocery stores don't enter these neighborhoods (low profit margins).] [Para 3: Documents the health consequences.] [Para 4: Proposes mobile markets and community-owned cooperatives as solutions.]

Why does the author place the proposed solutions (Para 4) after the cause analysis (Para 2) rather than introducing them in Para 1?
o: The author doesn't know the solutions until the problem is fully analyzed

By establishing the structural CAUSE of food deserts (low profit margins) before the solutions, the author ensures readers understand why solutions must address economic incentives, not just physical access
The solutions are less important than the health consequences
Para 1 is too short to contain both the problem and the solutions
quiz.e: B is correct. A is naive. C reverses the importance hierarchy (the author clearly values the solutions — they form the conclusion). D is a mechanical observation that misses the rhetorical logic.

quiz.q:
Passage: 'The candidate's record shows a consistent pattern: she voted to cut education funding when districts needed support; she voted to expand tax incentives when corporations sought relief; she voted to weaken environmental protections when industry requested flexibility.'

What is the rhetorical effect of the parallel 'she voted to...' structure?
o: It proves the candidate is corrupt

The parallel structure creates emphasis through repetition — the similar grammatical form for three different policy areas reinforces the author's claim of a consistent pattern by making the pattern visually and rhythmically apparent
It introduces a chronological account of her voting record
It provides three separate arguments, each of which can stand independently
quiz.e: The three parallel 'she voted to X when Y needed Z' clauses don't just present facts — their identical form makes the PATTERN feel inevitable and undeniable. B is correct. A adds a corruption inference not made. C is wrong (no chronological order). D is wrong — they work together as a unified argument for a pattern, not independently.

quizTr.uz: Umumiy e'tiqodning ag'darilishi dalillarni esda qolarli va ta'sirli qiladi — B shu ritorik funksiyani qamraydi; A muallif yon bosadi deydi (xato — muallif e'tiroz bildiradi), C maqsadni noto'g'ri aniqlaydi, D juda keng.
quizTr.ru: Опровержение расхожего мнения делает доказательства запоминающимися и сильными — B передаёт эту риторическую функцию; A говорит об уступке (неверно — автор оспаривает), C путает цель, D слишком широк.

quizTr.uz: Indoneziya misoli mavhum muammoni konkret va hissiy jihatdan yaqin qiladi — B to'g'ri: emotsional jalb qilish aynan ritorik funksiya; A da davlatlar taqqoslanmaydi, C va D xato — misol argumentni qo'llab-quvvatlaydi, unga zid emas.
quizTr.ru: Индонезийский случай делает абстрактную проблему конкретной и эмоционально близкой — B верен: эмоциональное вовлечение и есть функция; A — сравнения стран нет, C и D неверны — пример поддерживает аргумент, а не противоречит ему.

quizTr.uz: Qo'rqilgan texnologiya sarmoya bilan hayotiy bo'lgani haqidagi pretsedent argumentni kamroq radikal ko'rsatadi — B to'g'ri; A xato (analogiya bevosita yadro energiyasi haqida emas), C haddan tashqari umumlashtiradi, D analogiya asoslamaydigan da'vo qiladi.
quizTr.ru: Прецедент «пугающая технология стала жизнеспособной благодаря инвестициям» делает аргумент менее радикальным — B верен; A неверен (аналогия не о ядерной энергии напрямую), C чрезмерно обобщает, D делает не подкреплённое аналогией заявление.

quizTr.uz: Sababni (past foyda marjasi) yechimlardan oldin berish o'quvchini tayyorlaydi — B to'g'ri; A sodda qarash, C ahamiyat ierarxiyasini teskari qiladi (yechimlar xulosani tashkil etadi), D ritorik mantiqni o'tkazib yuboradigan mexanik kuzatuv.
quizTr.ru: Причина (низкая маржа) перед решениями готовит читателя — B верен; A наивен, C переворачивает иерархию значимости (решения образуют вывод), D — механическое наблюдение без риторической логики.

quizTr.uz: Uch parallel jumlaning bir xil grammatik shakli naqshni muqarrar va inkor etib bo'lmaydigan qilib his qildiradi — B to'g'ri; A matnda yo'q korruptsiya xulosasini qo'shadi, C xato (xronologik tartib yo'q), D xato — ular yagona argument sifatida birga ishlaydi.
quizTr.ru: Одинаковая грамматическая форма трёх параллельных фраз делает закономерность неизбежной и неоспоримой — B верен; A добавляет вывод о коррупции, которого нет, C неверен (нет хронологии), D неверен — они работают вместе как единый аргумент.

reading.title: Author's Purpose — Why Was This Written?
reading.text:
Author's Purpose questions ask WHY the author wrote the passage — what they are trying to accomplish. The question stems are: 'Which choice best describes the overall purpose of the text?' or 'What is the main purpose of the passage?' There are six core purposes on the exam: (1) INFORM/EXPLAIN — present factual information, describe how something works; (2) PERSUADE/ARGUE — advocate for a position, change the reader's mind; (3) ANALYZE/CRITIQUE — examine a topic critically, evaluate strengths and weaknesses; (4) DESCRIBE — create a vivid picture of a scene, person, or object (common in literary excerpts); (5) COUNTER — challenge an existing assumption, claim, or argument; (6) SYNTHESIZE — combine perspectives or evidence to reach a conclusion.

The critical skill is distinguishing between purposes that look similar. INFORM vs. ARGUE: an informative passage presents facts without taking sides; an argumentative passage takes a clear position and marshals evidence for it. Look for words like 'should,' 'must,' 'ought to,' 'is wrong,' 'is essential' — these signal argument. ANALYZE vs. COUNTER: an analytical passage examines something without necessarily trying to change anyone's mind; a counter passage specifically sets up an existing view and challenges it. Watch for 'contrary to popular belief,' 'this assumption is wrong,' 'the conventional view overlooks.'

For questions about the PURPOSE OF A SPECIFIC SENTENCE or PARAGRAPH within the passage, you must identify the sentence's ROLE IN THE ARGUMENT or narrative — not just what it says. Ask: 'Why is this sentence here? What does it do for the passage?' Common sentence-level purposes: introduces the topic, provides background context, gives supporting evidence, acknowledges a counterargument, transitions between ideas, or states the conclusion. The POSITION of the sentence in the passage (opening, middle, end) is a reliable clue about its purpose.

Key points:
• Inform: presents facts neutrally, no clear position taken
• Argue: takes a position, uses 'should/must/ought/is wrong'
• Analyze: examines strengths AND weaknesses without necessarily advocating
• Counter: sets up an existing view THEN challenges it directly
• Describe: creates vivid detail, sensory language, often literary
• Sentence purpose: ask WHY the sentence is there, not just WHAT it says
• Position clue: opening sentence often introduces; final sentence often concludes

quiz.q:
Passage: 'The human gut contains approximately 38 trillion bacteria — nearly equal to the number of human cells in the body. These microorganisms, collectively called the gut microbiome, play critical roles in digestion, immune regulation, and the synthesis of certain vitamins. Recent research has also linked microbiome composition to mental health, with disruptions associated with increased rates of depression and anxiety.'

Which choice best describes the overall purpose of this text?
o: To argue that doctors should prescribe probiotics for patients with depression
To explain the composition and significance of the gut microbiome
To counter the common belief that bacteria are harmful to human health
To describe the experience of living with a disrupted gut microbiome
quiz.e: It does not take a position ('should' or 'must'), does not counter a specific argument, and does not describe a personal experience. B is correct — the purpose is INFORMATIVE/EXPLANATORY. A is wrong (no recommendation about probiotics). C is wrong (no specific belief is being countered). D is wrong (no personal description).

quiz.q:
Passage: 'Popular accounts of the Middle Ages routinely depict it as a period of intellectual stagnation — a 'Dark Age' between the brilliance of classical antiquity and the Renaissance. This characterization is deeply misleading. Medieval scholars translated, preserved, and extended classical knowledge. Institutions like the University of Bologna (founded 1088) and the University of Paris represent genuine intellectual centers that directly enabled Renaissance humanism. Dismissing the medieval period as intellectually barren is not only inaccurate but reflects a Renaissance-era propaganda that later historians have too uncritically inherited.'

Which choice best describes the overall purpose of this text?
o: To analyze the major intellectual achievements of the medieval period
To persuade readers to study medieval history more seriously
To counter the characterization of the Middle Ages as intellectually stagnant
To describe the founding of medieval universities like Bologna and Paris
quiz.e: It provides evidence against this view and ends by attributing the misconception to Renaissance propaganda. C is correct — this is a COUNTER purpose. A is wrong (the passage doesn't systematically analyze medieval achievements; it refutes a specific claim). B is wrong (no explicit recommendation to study medieval history). D is wrong (universities are mentioned as evidence, not the focus).

quiz.q:
Passage: 'Many parents choose to enroll their children in after-school coding programs, believing this will prepare them for the technology-driven economy. [Sentence X: In 2023 alone, the US technology sector laid off over 260,000 workers.] This statistic suggests that the assumption of stable, growing tech employment underlying these enrollment decisions may be more fragile than parents recognize.'

Which choice best describes the function of Sentence X in the passage?
o: To argue that parents should not enroll their children in coding programs
To provide evidence that complicates the assumption that technology careers offer stable employment
To counter the claim that the technology sector is an important part of the economy
To introduce the topic of the passage by establishing its economic context
quiz.e: ' The statistic's purpose is to provide concrete evidence supporting the argument that parental assumptions about tech employment may be unreliable. B is correct. A is wrong — the passage questions assumptions, but Sentence X itself doesn't argue 'don't enroll.' C is wrong — the passage doesn't dispute tech's importance to the economy. D is wrong — the passage has already introduced its topic before Sentence X.

quiz.q:
Passage: 'For decades, conservation policy in Africa was dominated by the 'fortress conservation' model, which established protected areas from which local communities were excluded. This approach was predicated on the assumption that human presence is inherently incompatible with wildlife preservation. Ethnographic and ecological research has since undermined this assumption: communities living alongside wildlife for generations have developed sophisticated management practices that maintain biodiversity, and exclusion has often led to resentment and poaching that undermines conservation goals.'

Which choice best describes the overall purpose of this text?
o: To describe the history of wildlife conservation in Africa
To argue that the fortress conservation model should be immediately abolished
To challenge the assumption underlying fortress conservation by presenting contrary evidence
To analyze the strengths and weaknesses of multiple conservation approaches
quiz.e: ' The explicit structure — assumption presented, then challenged with evidence — makes this a COUNTER passage. C is correct. A is wrong (it's not a historical narrative; it's an argument). B is wrong (the passage questions the assumption but doesn't call for 'immediate abolition'). D is wrong (the passage critiques one approach, not multiple approaches comparatively).

quiz.q:
Passage: 'Current environmental regulations in the United States require companies to disclose certain pollutants in public databases. However, these databases use different formats, are hosted on separate agency websites, and require technical expertise to interpret. Environmental scientists and legal scholars have consistently found that this fragmentation prevents both regulators and the public from identifying patterns of violation. Congress should establish a unified, publicly accessible environmental data portal that allows non-experts to search, visualize, and compare pollution data across regions and time periods.'

Which choice best describes the overall purpose of this text?
o: To describe the current state of environmental data disclosure in the United States
To analyze the structural challenges facing environmental regulatory agencies
To argue for a specific policy reform to improve public access to environmental data
To counter the claim that environmental regulations are ineffective
quiz.e: ..portal.' The word 'should' signals an ARGUMENT/PERSUASION purpose. The passage identifies a problem (fragmented databases) and advocates for a specific solution. C is correct. A is partially true (the current state is described) but only as background for the argument. B is partially true but 'analyze' misses the advocacy element — the author isn't just examining the problem but calling for action. D is wrong — the author doesn't counter a claim that regulations are ineffective; the author accepts the value of regulations and wants them improved.

quizTr.uz: Matn pozitsiya bildirmaydi, aniq argumentga qarshi chiqmaydi va shaxsiy tajribani tasvirlamaydi — B to'g'ri: maqsad AXBOROT BERISH/TUSHUNTIRISH; A, C va D matnda yo'q vazifalarni ko'rsatadi.
quizTr.ru: Текст не занимает позицию, не спорит с конкретным мнением и не описывает личный опыт — B верен: цель ИНФОРМАТИВНАЯ/объяснительная; A, C и D называют отсутствующие задачи.

quizTr.uz: Matn qarashga qarshi dalil keltirib, noto'g'ri tasavvurni Renessans targ'ibotiga bog'laydi — C to'g'ri: bu QARSHI CHIQISH maqsadi; A tizimli tahlil emas, B da o'rganish tavsiyasi yo'q, D da universitetlar dalil, fokus emas.
quizTr.ru: Текст приводит контрдоказательства и возводит заблуждение к пропаганде Ренессанса — C верен: цель ОПРОВЕРГНУТЬ; A — не системный анализ, B — рекомендации изучать нет, D — университеты лишь довод, а не фокус.

quizTr.uz: Statistika ota-onalarning tech bandligi haqidagi taxminlari ishonchsiz bo'lishi mumkinligiga konkret dalil beradi — B to'g'ri; A 'o'qimang' demaydi, C tech'ning iqtisodiy ahamiyatini inkor qilmaydi, D xato — mavzu allaqachon kiritilgan.
quizTr.ru: Статистика даёт конкретное свидетельство ненадёжности родительских допущений о занятости в tech — B верен; A не говорит «не поступайте», C не оспаривает важность tech для экономики, D неверен — тема уже введена.

quizTr.uz: Aniq tuzilma — taxmin keltiriladi, so'ng dalil bilan rad etiladi — buni QARSHI matn qiladi; C to'g'ri, A tarixiy hikoya emas, B 'darhol bekor qilish'ga chaqirmaydi, D bitta yondashuv tanqid qilinadi, bir nechtasi taqqoslanmaydi.
quizTr.ru: Явная структура — допущение, затем опровержение доказательствами — делает текст ОПРОВЕРГАЮЩИМ; C верен, A — не историческое повествование, B — призыва к «немедленной отмене» нет, D — критикуется один подход, а не сравниваются несколько.

quizTr.uz: 'Should' so'zi ARGUMENT/ISHONTIRISH maqsadini bildiradi: muammo (tarqoq bazalar) aniqlanadi va aniq yechim taklif etiladi — C to'g'ri; A va B faqat qisman to'g'ri (harakatga chaqiriqni o'tkazib yuboradi), D xato.
quizTr.ru: Слово «should» сигнализирует цель УБЕДИТЬ: названа проблема (разрозненные базы) и предложено конкретное решение — C верен; A и B верны лишь отчасти (упускают призыв к действию), D неверен.

listening.title: A University Lecture
listening.script: Good morning, everyone. Today we're looking at the psychology of decision-making. Now, we like to think we make choices logically, weighing up the facts. But research suggests otherwise. In fact, most of our decisions are driven by emotion and by mental shortcuts the brain uses to save effort. These shortcuts are usually helpful, but they can lead to predictable mistakes. For example, people tend to fear losing something far more than they value gaining the same thing. This is called loss aversion, and we'll explore it in detail after the break. For now, I'd like you to read chapter four before next week's seminar.

quiz.q: What is the lecture about?
quiz.e: It is about the psychology of decision-making.

quiz.q: What does research suggest about our decisions?
o: They are driven by emotion and mental shortcuts.
quiz.e: Most decisions are driven by emotion and shortcuts.

quiz.q: What are the mental shortcuts usually like?
o: usually helpful but sometimes lead to mistakes
quiz.e: Usually helpful, but can cause predictable mistakes.

quiz.q: What is 'loss aversion'?
o: fearing loss more than valuing an equal gain
quiz.e: Fearing loss more than valuing the same gain.

quiz.q: What must students do before the seminar?
quiz.e: Read chapter four before next week's seminar.

quizTr.uz: U qaror qabul qilish psixologiyasi haqida.
quizTr.ru: Она посвящена психологии принятия решений.

quizTr.uz: Ko'pchilik qarorlarni hissiyot va aqliy yo'l-yo'riqlar boshqaradi.
quizTr.ru: Большинство решений определяются эмоциями и ментальными сокращениями.

quizTr.uz: Odatda foydali, lekin bashorat qilsa bo'ladigan xatolarga olib kelishi mumkin.
quizTr.ru: Обычно полезны, но могут приводить к предсказуемым ошибкам.

quizTr.uz: Yo'qotishdan qo'rqish xuddi shunday yutuqni qadrlashdan kuchliroq.
quizTr.ru: Страх потери сильнее, чем ценность равного выигрыша.

quizTr.uz: Kelasi haftadagi seminardan oldin to'rtinchi bobni o'qish.
quizTr.ru: Прочитать четвёртую главу до семинара на следующей неделе.

listening.title: A Job Interview
listening.script: So, thank you for coming in. Could you tell me why you applied for this marketing role? Of course. I've followed your company for years, and I really admire your creative campaigns. I felt my experience would be a good fit. Tell me about a challenge you've faced. In my last job, we lost a major client unexpectedly. Rather than panic, I led a small team to win back three smaller clients within a month. That's impressive. And where do you see yourself in five years? Honestly, I'd like to be managing my own team here, helping to develop the kind of campaigns that first attracted me to you. Excellent. We'll be in touch by the end of the week.

quiz.q: What role is the candidate applying for?
quiz.e: It is a marketing role.

quiz.q: Why did she apply?
o: she admires the company's creative campaigns
quiz.e: She admires their creative campaigns and felt it fit.

quiz.q: What challenge did she describe?
o: losing a major client and winning back smaller ones
quiz.e: Losing a major client, then winning back three smaller ones.

quiz.q: Where does she see herself in five years?
quiz.e: Managing her own team at the company.

quiz.q: When will she hear back?
o: by the end of the week
quiz.e: By the end of the week.

quizTr.uz: Bu marketing sohasidagi lavozim.
quizTr.ru: Это должность в маркетинге.

quizTr.uz: U ularning ijodiy kampaniyalariga qoyil qoladi va bu o'ziga mos deb hisoblagan.
quizTr.ru: Она восхищается их креативными кампаниями и почувствовала, что это ей подходит.

quizTr.uz: Yirik mijozni yo'qotib, keyin uchta kichikroq mijozni qaytarib olish.
quizTr.ru: Потеря крупного клиента и возвращение трёх клиентов поменьше.

quizTr.uz: Shu kompaniyada o'z jamoasini boshqarish.
quizTr.ru: Руководить собственной командой в этой компании.

quizTr.uz: Hafta oxirigacha.
quizTr.ru: До конца недели.

listening.title: A Discussion on Social Media
listening.script: Welcome back. Today we're debating whether social media does more harm than good. Sarah, you start. Well, I think the benefits are huge. It keeps families connected across the world and gives a voice to people who would otherwise be ignored. But James, you disagree? I do. I'm not denying the benefits, but we can't ignore the harm. Studies link heavy use to anxiety, especially among teenagers. People compare their real lives to others' perfect online images, and they feel worse. Sarah, a response? I'd say the problem isn't the technology itself, but how we use it. With better education, we could enjoy the good and avoid the worst. That's a fair point. We'll take some calls after this.

quiz.q: What is the debate about?
o: whether social media does more harm than good
quiz.e: Whether social media does more harm than good.

quiz.q: What benefit does Sarah mention?
o: it keeps families connected and gives a voice
quiz.e: It connects families and gives people a voice.

quiz.q: What harm does James describe?
o: a link to anxiety, especially in teenagers
quiz.e: Heavy use is linked to anxiety in teenagers.

quiz.q: Why do people feel worse, according to James?
o: they compare their lives to others' perfect images
quiz.e: They compare real lives to perfect online images.

quiz.q: What is Sarah's final point?
o: The problem is how we use it, not the technology.
