quiz.e: The problem is how we use it; education could help.

quizTr.uz: Ijtimoiy tarmoqlar foydadan ko'ra ko'proq zarar keltiradimi degan savol.
quizTr.ru: Вопрос о том, приносят ли соцсети больше вреда, чем пользы.

quizTr.uz: U oilalarni bog'laydi va odamlarga ovoz beradi.
quizTr.ru: Они соединяют семьи и дают людям голос.

quizTr.uz: Ko'p foydalanish o'smirlarda xavotir bilan bog'liq.
quizTr.ru: Активное использование связано с тревожностью у подростков.

quizTr.uz: Ular real hayotni internetdagi mukammal tasvirlar bilan solishtirishadi.
quizTr.ru: Они сравнивают реальную жизнь с идеальными картинками в сети.

quizTr.uz: Muammo undan qanday foydalanishimizda; ta'lim yordam berishi mumkin.
quizTr.ru: Проблема в том, как мы им пользуемся; образование могло бы помочь.

listening.title: A Climate News Report
listening.script: In environmental news, a major report published today warns that global temperatures are rising faster than previously expected. Scientists say that without urgent action, many coastal cities could face serious flooding within decades. However, the report is not entirely negative. It notes that the cost of renewable energy, such as solar and wind power, has fallen dramatically, making clean energy cheaper than coal in much of the world. The authors argue that the technology to solve the crisis already exists; what is missing is political will. A global summit will be held in Leeds next month, where world leaders will be under pressure to agree on stronger targets. Critics, however, fear that promises will once again be broken.

quiz.q: What does the new report warn about?
quiz.e: Global temperatures are rising faster than expected.

quiz.q: What could happen to coastal cities?
quiz.e: They could face serious flooding within decades.

quiz.q: What positive point does the report make?
o: renewable energy has become much cheaper
quiz.e: Renewable energy costs have fallen dramatically.

quiz.q: According to the authors, what is missing?
quiz.e: The technology exists; political will is missing.

quiz.q: What do critics fear about the summit?
quiz.e: They fear promises will once again be broken.

quizTr.uz: Global harorat kutilganidan tezroq ko'tarilmoqda.
quizTr.ru: Глобальные температуры растут быстрее, чем ожидалось.

quizTr.uz: Ular bir necha o'n yil ichida jiddiy suv toshqiniga duch kelishi mumkin.
quizTr.ru: Им может грозить серьёзное затопление в ближайшие десятилетия.

quizTr.uz: Qayta tiklanadigan energiya narxi keskin tushdi.
quizTr.ru: Стоимость возобновляемой энергии резко упала.

quizTr.uz: Texnologiya bor; siyosiy iroda yetishmayapti.
quizTr.ru: Технологии есть; не хватает политической воли.

quizTr.uz: Ular va'dalar yana buziladi, deb qo'rqishadi.
quizTr.ru: Они опасаются, что обещания снова будут нарушены.

listening.title: Radio: Tourism Boom in Uzbekistan
listening.script: Good evening. Tonight we look at tourism in Uzbekistan, a sector that has grown dramatically since visa-free travel was introduced for dozens of countries. Before the reforms, visitors faced paperwork that could take weeks; today, most European tourists simply board a plane. The results are visible in the arrival numbers, which have multiplied several times over, and in the hotels of Samarkand, where finding a room in high season has become a challenge. But rapid growth brings dilemmas. Preservation experts warn that historic monuments were never designed for millions of feet, and some restoration work has been criticised for prioritising appearance over authenticity — fresh tiles where worn ones told a story. There is also the question of who benefits. Large hotels are often owned by international chains, while family guesthouses fight for visibility on booking platforms. Still, most economists agree the boom is an opportunity rather than a threat, provided the country invests revenue in training, infrastructure, and — crucially — in the language skills of the young people who will welcome the world.

quiz.q: What triggered the tourism boom, according to the report?
quiz.e: The sector has grown dramatically since visa-free travel was introduced.

quiz.q: What do preservation experts warn about?
o: Monuments were not designed for mass tourism
quiz.e: Historic monuments were never designed for millions of feet.

quiz.q: What criticism is made of some restoration work?
quiz.e: Fresh tiles replaced worn ones that 'told a story' — appearance over authenticity.

quiz.q: Under what condition do economists see the boom positively?
o: If revenue is invested in training, infrastructure and language skills
quiz.e: An opportunity — provided revenue is invested in training, infrastructure and language skills.

quizTr.uz: Soha ko'plab davlatlar uchun vizasiz rejim joriy etilgach keskin o'sdi.
quizTr.ru: Сектор резко вырос после введения безвизового режима для многих стран.

quizTr.uz: Tarixiy obidalar millionlab odamlar uchun mo'ljallanmagan.
quizTr.ru: Исторические памятники не рассчитаны на миллионы посетителей.

quizTr.uz: Eskirgan koshinlar o'rniga yangilari qo'yilgan — haqiqiylikdan ko'ra tashqi ko'rinish ustun qo'yilgan.
quizTr.ru: Старые изразцы заменили новыми — внешний вид поставили выше подлинности.

quizTr.uz: Imkoniyat — agar daromad ta'lim, infratuzilma va til ko'nikmalariga sarflansa.
quizTr.ru: Возможность — при условии инвестиций в обучение, инфраструктуру и языковые навыки.

listening.title: Talk: The Bilingual Brain
listening.script: Thank you all for coming. As a neuroscientist who grew up speaking two languages, I'm often asked whether bilingualism makes you smarter. The honest answer is: not exactly — but it changes how your brain works in fascinating ways. Every time a bilingual person speaks, both languages are active simultaneously. The brain must constantly select one and suppress the other, and this invisible workout strengthens what we call executive control — the ability to focus, switch between tasks, and ignore distractions. Studies also suggest that lifelong bilingualism may delay the symptoms of dementia by several years, although researchers still debate the size of the effect. What I find most striking, however, is the flexibility argument. Bilinguals report that each language carries its own personality, its own humour, even its own way of apologising. Switching languages is not just translation — it is a slight change of perspective. And in a world that rewards those who can see problems from more than one angle, that may be the real advantage — greater than any test score could show.

quiz.q: What happens in the brain when a bilingual person speaks?
o: Both languages are active at the same time
The brain translates word by word
quiz.e: Both languages are active simultaneously; the brain selects one and suppresses the other.

quiz.q: What is 'executive control'?
o: The ability to focus, switch tasks and ignore distractions
quiz.e: Executive control is defined as focusing, switching between tasks, and ignoring distractions.

quiz.q: What do researchers still debate about dementia?
o: Whether bilinguals get dementia at all
The size of the delay effect
quiz.e: Bilingualism may delay symptoms by several years, but researchers debate the size of the effect.

quiz.q: What does the speaker consider the 'real advantage' of bilingualism?
o: Seeing problems from more than one perspective
quiz.e: Switching languages is a change of perspective — valuable in a world that rewards multiple angles.

quizTr.uz: Ikkala til bir vaqtda faol bo'ladi; miya birini tanlab, ikkinchisini bosib turadi.
quizTr.ru: Оба языка активны одновременно; мозг выбирает один и подавляет другой.

quizTr.uz: Executive control — diqqatni jamlash, vazifalar orasida almashish va chalg'ituvchi narsalarni e'tiborsiz qoldirish qobiliyati.
quizTr.ru: Executive control — способность концентрироваться, переключаться между задачами и игнорировать отвлечения.

quizTr.uz: Bilingvizm alomatlarni bir necha yilga kechiktirishi mumkin, ammo olimlar ta'sir hajmi haqida bahslashadi.
quizTr.ru: Билингвизм может отсрочить симптомы на несколько лет, но учёные спорят о размере эффекта.

quizTr.uz: Tillarni almashtirish — nuqtai nazarni o'zgartirish; muammoga bir necha tomondan qaray olish — asosiy afzallik.
quizTr.ru: Смена языка — смена перспективы; главное преимущество — видеть проблему с разных сторон.

speaking.title: Arguing a position
speaking.prompt: Should social media be regulated? Argue your position for 90 seconds.
tips: State your thesis in one sentence.
Concede one opposing point, then refute it.

speaking.title: Describing change
speaking.prompt: How has your country changed in the last ten years?
tips: Trends: there has been a steady rise in…

speaking.title: Job interview
speaking.prompt: Answer: 'Tell me about a challenge you overcame.'

speaking.title: Hypothetical
speaking.prompt: If you could change one law, what would it be and why?

speaking.title: Explaining a process
speaking.prompt: Explain how something you know well works, to a beginner.
tips: Passive voice: it is heated / it gets stored…

speaking.title: Culture
speaking.prompt: What should a visitor know about your culture before arriving?

writing.prompt: Write a magazine article (140–180 words): 'Three habits that changed my life.'
hints: Hook the reader in line one.

grammar.title: Inversion for emphasis
grammar.lead: Advanced English uses inversion — putting the auxiliary before the subject — to add drama and formality. It is common in writing, speeches, and formal speaking.

leadTr.uz: Ilg'or ingliz tilida urg'u berish uchun inversiya ishlatiladi — yordamchi fe'l egadan oldin keladi. Bu yozma nutq va rasmiy uslubda ko'p uchraydi.
leadTr.ru: В продвинутом английском для усиления используется инверсия — вспомогательный глагол ставится перед подлежащим. Это характерно для письменной и формальной речи.

p: After never, rarely, seldom, little, no sooner, not only — invert subject and auxiliary.
ex: Never have I seen such dedication.
Not only did she win, but she also broke the record.

p: Had / Should / Were can replace 'if' in formal conditionals.
ex: Had I known, I would have called.
Should you need anything, ask.

p: So + adjective and Such + noun phrase can open the sentence with inversion.
ex: So intense was the storm that flights stopped.
Such was the noise that nobody slept.

grammar.tip: Inversion is a spice, not a staple — one per paragraph is plenty.
examples: Rarely does a film capture a book so well.
Little did they know what awaited them.
No sooner had we arrived than it started to rain.

mistakes.x: Never I have seen such a thing.
mistakes.v: Never have I seen such a thing — auxiliary before subject.

mistakes.x: Not only she sings, but she dances.
mistakes.v: Not only does she sing, but she also dances.

quiz.q: ___ had the meeting started when the fire alarm rang.
quiz.e: No sooner had X happened than Y — paired with 'than'.

quiz.q: ___ you require assistance, our team is available around the clock.
quiz.e: Should = if, in formal conditionals: Should you require…

quiz.q: Not only ___ the deadline, she exceeded every target.
quiz.e: After 'not only' use auxiliary + subject + verb: did she meet.

quiz.q: ___ was the demand that the servers crashed.
quiz.e: Such + was + noun phrase: Such was the demand that…

quiz.q: Had I known about the traffic, I ___ earlier.
quiz.e: Had I known = If I had known → would have left (third conditional).

tip.uz: Inversiya — ziravor, asosiy taom emas: har bir xatboshiga bittasi yetarli.
tip.ru: Инверсия — приправа, а не основное блюдо: одной на абзац вполне достаточно.

p.uz: never, rarely, seldom, little, no sooner, not only dan keyin ega va yordamchi fe'l o'rin almashadi.
p.ru: После never, rarely, seldom, little, no sooner, not only подлежащее и вспомогательный глагол меняются местами.

p.uz: Rasmiy shart gaplarda Had / Should / Were 'if' o'rnini bosa oladi.
p.ru: В формальных условных Had / Should / Were могут заменять 'if'.

p.uz: So + sifat va Such + ot birikmasi gapni inversiya bilan boshlashi mumkin.
p.ru: So + прилагательное и Such + именная группа могут открывать предложение с инверсией.

quiz.uz: No sooner had X happened than Y — 'than' bilan juftlikda keladi.
quiz.ru: No sooner had X happened than Y — в паре с 'than'.

quiz.uz: Should = if, rasmiy shart gaplarda: Should you require…
quiz.ru: Should = if в формальных условных: Should you require…

quiz.uz: 'Not only' dan keyin yordamchi fe'l + ega + fe'l: did she meet.
quiz.ru: После 'not only': вспомогательный глагол + подлежащее + глагол: did she meet.

quiz.uz: Such + was + ot birikmasi: Such was the demand that…
quiz.ru: Such + was + именная группа: Such was the demand that…

quiz.uz: Had I known = If I had known → would have left (uchinchi shart mayli).
quiz.ru: Had I known = If I had known → would have left (третий кондиционал).

grammar.title: Cleft sentences
grammar.lead: Cleft sentences (It was… that…, What I need is…) split one message into two clauses to control emphasis — a hallmark of fluent, natural English.

leadTr.uz: Cleft gaplar (It was… that…, What I need is…) bitta fikrni ikki qismga bo'lib, urg'uni boshqaradi — bu ravon ingliz tilining belgisi.
leadTr.ru: Расщеплённые предложения (It was… that…, What I need is…) делят одну мысль на две части, управляя акцентом — признак свободного владения языком.

p: Emphasise who, what, when or where with It + be + focus + that/who.
ex: It was Maria who solved it.
It was in 2019 that everything changed.

p: What + clause + be + focus emphasises the thing itself.
ex: What I need is a long holiday.
What annoyed me was the silence afterwards.

p: All + clause + be + focus means 'the only thing'.
ex: All I asked for was five minutes.
All it takes is practice.

grammar.tip: In speech, wh-clefts buy you thinking time while sounding sophisticated.
examples: It's the small details that matter.
What makes her different is her patience.
All we can do is wait.

mistakes.x: It was Maria which solved it.
mistakes.v: Use who for people: It was Maria who solved it.

mistakes.x: What I need it is a holiday.
mistakes.v: No extra pronoun: What I need is a holiday.

quiz.q: ___ the ending that ruined the film for me.
quiz.e: It-cleft: It was + focus + that…

quiz.q: What impressed the panel ___ her honesty.
quiz.e: Wh-cleft takes singular be: What impressed them was…

quiz.q: ___ I'm saying is that we need more time.
quiz.e: What I'm saying is… — emphasising the message.

quiz.q: It was only when I reread the letter ___ I understood.
quiz.e: It-cleft closes with that: …that I understood.

tip.uz: Og'zaki nutqda wh-cleft o'ylab olish uchun vaqt beradi va nutqni jozibali qiladi.
tip.ru: В устной речи wh-клефт даёт время подумать и звучит изысканно.

p.uz: Kim, nima, qachon yoki qayerdaligini It + be + urg'u + that/who bilan ta'kidlang.
p.ru: Подчёркивайте кто, что, когда или где с помощью It + be + фокус + that/who.

p.uz: What + gap + be + urg'u narsaning o'zini ta'kidlaydi.
p.ru: What + придаточное + be + фокус подчёркивает саму вещь.

p.uz: All + gap + be + urg'u 'yagona narsa' degan ma'noni beradi.
p.ru: All + придаточное + be + фокус означает «единственное».

quiz.uz: Wh-cleft birlikdagi be oladi: What impressed them was…
quiz.ru: Wh-клефт берёт be в единственном числе: What impressed them was…

quiz.uz: What I'm saying is… — asosiy fikrni ta'kidlash.
quiz.ru: What I'm saying is… — подчёркивание сути сказанного.

quiz.uz: It-cleft that bilan yopiladi: …that I understood.
quiz.ru: It-клефт закрывается словом that: …that I understood.

grammar.title: The subjunctive & formal structures
grammar.lead: Formal English preserves the subjunctive after verbs like suggest, demand, insist — and fixed phrases like 'be that as it may'. Mastering it lifts your writing register instantly.

leadTr.uz: Rasmiy ingliz tilida suggest, demand, insist kabi fe'llardan keyin subjunktiv saqlanadi. Uni egallash yozuv uslubingizni darhol ko'taradi.
leadTr.ru: Формальный английский сохраняет сослагательное наклонение после глаголов suggest, demand, insist. Владение им сразу повышает регистр письма.

p: After suggest/recommend/demand/insist + that, use the base form for all persons.
ex: They insisted that she be present.
We recommend that he take the earlier train.

p: Some subjunctives survive only in set expressions.
ex: Be that as it may…
Suffice it to say…
Far be it from me to judge.

p: Use 'were' for all persons in hypotheticals.
ex: If I were in your position…
I wish it were simpler.

grammar.tip: In American English the mandative subjunctive is standard; British English often uses 'should' instead — both are correct.
examples: The board demanded that the report be rewritten.
It is essential that every voice be heard.
If he were honest, he'd admit it.

mistakes.x: They suggested that he goes home.
mistakes.v: Base form after suggest: …that he go home.

mistakes.x: If I was you, I'd wait.
mistakes.v: Hypothetical: If I were you, I'd wait.

quiz.q: The committee insisted that the policy ___ reviewed annually.
quiz.e: Mandative subjunctive: insisted that it be reviewed.

quiz.q: It is vital that she ___ informed immediately.
quiz.e: It is vital that + base form: …that she be informed.

quiz.q: I wish it ___ possible to be in two places at once.
quiz.e: Wish + were-subjunctive: I wish it were possible.

tip.uz: Amerika inglizchasida mandativ subjunktiv odatiy; Britaniya inglizchasida ko'pincha 'should' ishlatiladi — ikkalasi ham to'g'ri.
tip.ru: В американском английском мандативный субжунктив — норма; в британском чаще 'should' — оба варианта верны.

p.uz: suggest/recommend/demand/insist + that dan keyin barcha shaxslar uchun fe'lning asosiy shakli ishlatiladi.
p.ru: После suggest/recommend/demand/insist + that используется базовая форма глагола для всех лиц.

p.uz: Ba'zi subjunktivlar faqat turg'un iboralarda saqlanib qolgan.
p.ru: Некоторые формы субжунктива сохранились только в устойчивых выражениях.

p.uz: Faraziy gaplarda barcha shaxslar uchun 'were' ishlatiladi.
p.ru: В гипотетических предложениях 'were' используется для всех лиц.

quiz.uz: Mandativ subjunktiv: insisted that it be reviewed.
quiz.ru: Мандативный субжунктив: insisted that it be reviewed.

quiz.uz: It is vital that + asosiy shakl: …that she be informed.
quiz.ru: It is vital that + базовая форма: …that she be informed.

quiz.uz: Wish + were-subjunktiv: I wish it were possible.
quiz.ru: Wish + were-субжунктив: I wish it were possible.

grammar.title: Hedging & distancing language
grammar.lead: Present claims without full commitment: seem, appear, reportedly, and passive reporting structures let you sound cautious, objective and professionally careful.

leadTr.uz: Fikrni to'liq zimmangizga olmasdan bayon qiling: seem, appear, reportedly va passiv reporting tuzilmalari ehtiyotkor, xolis va professional ohang beradi.
leadTr.ru: Излагайте утверждения без полной ответственности за них: seem, appear, reportedly и пассивные конструкции сообщения придают осторожный, объективный тон.

grammar.situation: A journalist writes: 'The minister is believed to have approved the deal, which allegedly took place last spring.' Not a single claim is stated as bare fact — every statement is carefully distanced from the writer.

p: In academic and professional English, stating everything as certain fact sounds naive — or legally risky. Hedging places your claim on a scale from full commitment ('X causes Y') down to cautious suggestion ('X may contribute to Y').

Compare the registers: neutral speech says 'This proves the drug works'; a careful paper says 'These results would suggest that the drug is effective.' The second writer can still be right — and can never be accused of overclaiming.
ex: The data suggest a link between screen time and sleep quality.
There would seem to be a flaw in this argument.
This is arguably the most significant finding of the decade.

p: Both verbs take three main patterns: subject + seem/appear + to-infinitive ('He seems to know'); It seems/appears + that-clause ('It appears that prices will fall'); and There seems/appears to be + noun ('There seems to be a problem').
To refer to the past, use the perfect infinitive: 'She seems to have left early' = it looks as though she left early. 'It would seem/appear that…' is one degree more tentative than 'It seems that…'.
ex: The committee appears to have ignored the warning.
It would appear that the files were deleted deliberately.
There seems to be no record of the payment.

p: Formal writing distances a claim by attributing it to unnamed sources. Pattern A: It + passive reporting verb + that-clause — 'It is said/thought/believed/reported that the company is in trouble.'

Pattern B moves the person into subject position: subject + passive verb + to-infinitive — 'He is said to be in trouble.' For past reference, use the perfect infinitive: 'He is believed to have left the country.'
ex: It is widely believed that the talks have stalled.
The painting is thought to be worth two million pounds.
The suspects are reported to have crossed the border on Friday.

p: Distancing adverbs compress a whole reporting structure into one word: reportedly (= it is reported that), allegedly (= it is claimed, but unproven — essential in journalism), apparently, presumably, seemingly.

Other common hedges: 'tend to' for cautious generalisations ('Reviewers tend to favour longer papers'), 'may well' / 'could well' for likely possibilities, and 'is likely/unlikely to' for predictions without promises.
ex: The CEO has reportedly resigned, though the company has not confirmed it.
The defendant allegedly transferred the funds to an offshore account.
Interest rates may well rise again before December.

grammar.tip: For past reference inside seem/appear and passive reporting patterns, switch to the perfect infinitive: 'She is thought to have resigned' (past), not 'She is thought to resign.' The tense of the reporting verb stays present.
examples: It would seem that the original estimate was far too optimistic.
The virus is believed to have originated in wild bird populations.
The two ministers allegedly met in private, and the government has presumably known about it for weeks.

mistakes.x: It seems that he to be tired.
mistakes.v: It seems that he is tired — after 'It seems that', use a normal finite clause, not an infinitive.

mistakes.x: He is said that he lives abroad.
mistakes.v: He is said to live abroad — with a personal subject, the pattern is passive verb + to-infinitive.

mistakes.x: She is thought to resign last month.
mistakes.v: She is thought to have resigned last month — past reference needs the perfect infinitive.

quiz.q: Choose the most distanced version: '___ the CEO has resigned.'
quiz.e: The passive reporting verb 'It is believed that' detaches the claim from the writer.

quiz.q: The company is reported ___ heavy losses last year.
quiz.e: Past reference ('last year') after a reporting passive needs the perfect infinitive.

quiz.q: There ___ to be a mistake in these figures.
quiz.e: 'There appears to be' — a fixed hedging pattern; appear is a state verb here, so no continuous.

quiz.q: Which adverb marks an accusation as unproven?
quiz.e: 'Allegedly' flags a claim as unverified — standard in careful journalism.

quiz.q: He ___ said to live somewhere in Scotland.
quiz.e: Personal-subject pattern: subject + is said + to-infinitive.

quiz.q: Most natural academic hedge: 'The results ___ that the drug is effective.'
quiz.e: 'Suggest' keeps the claim cautious; 'prove' commits the writer completely.

quiz.q: It would ___ that the samples were contaminated.
quiz.e: 'It would seem that…' — the bare infinitive after would; an extra-tentative version of 'it seems'.

quiz.q: The minister is thought ___ the meeting yesterday, though nothing is confirmed.
quiz.e: 'Yesterday' points to the past, so the perfect infinitive 'to have attended' is required.

quiz.q: Which sentence contains a hedge?
o: The plan tends to attract criticism.
quiz.e: 'Tends to' turns a blunt claim into a cautious generalisation.

quiz.q: 'She didn't reply to my email.' Choose the most distanced, diplomatic rewrite.
o: She appears not to have received my email.
quiz.e: 'Appears not to have received' offers an innocent explanation instead of an accusation.

situation.uz: Jurnalist yozadi: 'The minister is believed to have approved the deal, which allegedly took place last spring.' Birorta ham fikr quruq fakt sifatida aytilmagan — har bir gap muallifdan ehtiyotkorlik bilan uzoqlashtirilgan.
situation.ru: Журналист пишет: 'The minister is believed to have approved the deal, which allegedly took place last spring.' Ни одно утверждение не подано как голый факт — каждое аккуратно отстранено от автора.

tip.uz: seem/appear va passiv reporting qoliplarida o'tgan zamonga ishora uchun perfect infinitive ishlating: 'She is thought to have resigned' (o'tgan), 'She is thought to resign' emas. Reporting fe'lning zamoni hozirgi bo'lib qolaveradi.
tip.ru: Для отсылки к прошлому внутри seem/appear и пассивных конструкций используйте перфектный инфинитив: 'She is thought to have resigned' (прошлое), а не 'She is thought to resign'. Время самого глагола сообщения остаётся настоящим.

p.uz: Akademik va professional ingliz tilida hamma narsani aniq fakt sifatida aytish sodda — yoki huquqiy jihatdan xavfli — eshitiladi. Hedging fikringizni to'liq ishonchdan ('X causes Y') ehtiyotkor taxmin darajasigacha ('X may contribute to Y') joylashtiradi.
p.ru: В академическом и профессиональном английском подавать всё как несомненный факт звучит наивно — или юридически рискованно. Хеджирование помещает утверждение на шкалу от полной уверенности ('X causes Y') до осторожного предположения ('X may contribute to Y').

p.uz: Registrlarni solishtiring: oddiy nutqda 'This proves the drug works' deyiladi; ehtiyotkor maqolada esa 'These results would suggest that the drug is effective.' Ikkinchi muallif baribir haq bo'lishi mumkin — lekin uni hech qachon mubolag'ada ayblab bo'lmaydi.
p.ru: Сравните регистры: в нейтральной речи — 'This proves the drug works'; в аккуратной статье — 'These results would suggest that the drug is effective.' Второй автор может быть прав — и его никогда не обвинят в преувеличении.

p.uz: Ikkala fe'l uchta asosiy qolipda keladi: ega + seem/appear + to-infinitive ('He seems to know'); It seems/appears + that-gap ('It appears that prices will fall'); There seems/appears to be + ot ('There seems to be a problem').
p.ru: Оба глагола употребляются в трёх основных моделях: подлежащее + seem/appear + to-инфинитив ('He seems to know'); It seems/appears + придаточное с that ('It appears that prices will fall'); There seems/appears to be + существительное ('There seems to be a problem').

p.uz: O'tgan zamonga ishora uchun perfect infinitive ishlatiladi: 'She seems to have left early' = u erta ketganga o'xshaydi. 'It would seem/appear that…' — 'It seems that…' dan yana bir daraja ehtiyotkorroq.
p.ru: Для отсылки к прошлому используется перфектный инфинитив: 'She seems to have left early' = похоже, она рано ушла. 'It would seem/appear that…' — ещё на ступень осторожнее, чем 'It seems that…'.

p.uz: Rasmiy matn fikrni noma'lum manbalarga bog'lab uzoqlashtiradi. A qolip: It + passiv reporting fe'l + that-gap — 'It is said/thought/believed/reported that the company is in trouble.'
p.ru: Формальный текст отстраняет утверждение, приписывая его неназванным источникам. Модель A: It + пассивный глагол сообщения + придаточное с that — 'It is said/thought/believed/reported that the company is in trouble.'

p.uz: B qolipda shaxs ega o'rniga chiqadi: ega + passiv fe'l + to-infinitive — 'He is said to be in trouble.' O'tgan zamon uchun perfect infinitive: 'He is believed to have left the country.'
p.ru: В модели B лицо становится подлежащим: подлежащее + пассивный глагол + to-инфинитив — 'He is said to be in trouble.' Для прошлого — перфектный инфинитив: 'He is believed to have left the country.'

p.uz: Distancing ravishlari butun reporting tuzilmani bitta so'zga siqadi: reportedly (= it is reported that), allegedly (= da'vo qilinadi, lekin isbotlanmagan — jurnalistikada zarur), apparently, presumably, seemingly.
p.ru: Дистанцирующие наречия сжимают целую конструкцию сообщения в одно слово: reportedly (= it is reported that), allegedly (= утверждается, но не доказано — необходимо в журналистике), apparently, presumably, seemingly.

p.uz: Boshqa keng tarqalgan hedgelar: ehtiyotkor umumlashtirish uchun 'tend to' ('Reviewers tend to favour longer papers'), ehtimoli yuqori holatlar uchun 'may well' / 'could well', va'dasiz bashorat uchun 'is likely/unlikely to'.
p.ru: Другие частые хеджи: 'tend to' для осторожных обобщений ('Reviewers tend to favour longer papers'), 'may well' / 'could well' для вероятных возможностей, 'is likely/unlikely to' для прогнозов без обещаний.

quiz.uz: Passiv reporting fe'li 'It is believed that' fikrni muallifdan uzoqlashtiradi.
quiz.ru: Пассивная конструкция 'It is believed that' отстраняет утверждение от автора.

quiz.uz: O'tgan zamonga ishora ('last year') reporting passivdan keyin perfect infinitive talab qiladi: to have suffered.
quiz.ru: Отсылка к прошлому ('last year') после пассива сообщения требует перфектного инфинитива: to have suffered.

quiz.uz: 'There appears to be' — turg'un hedging qolipi; appear holat fe'li, continuous ishlatilmaydi.
quiz.ru: 'There appears to be' — устойчивая модель хеджирования; appear — глагол состояния, continuous не нужен.

quiz.uz: 'Allegedly' ayblovni isbotlanmagan deb belgilaydi — ehtiyotkor jurnalistikaning standarti.
quiz.ru: 'Allegedly' помечает обвинение как недоказанное — стандарт аккуратной журналистики.

quiz.uz: Shaxs-ega qolipi: ega + is said + to-infinitive.
quiz.ru: Модель с личным подлежащим: подлежащее + is said + to-инфинитив.

quiz.uz: 'Suggest' fikrni ehtiyotkor saqlaydi; 'prove' muallifni to'liq majburiyatga soladi.
quiz.ru: 'Suggest' сохраняет осторожность; 'prove' полностью связывает автора обязательством.

quiz.uz: 'It would seem that…' — would dan keyin yalang'och infinitiv; 'it seems' ning yanada ehtiyotkor varianti.
quiz.ru: 'It would seem that…' — после would голый инфинитив; ещё более осторожный вариант 'it seems'.

quiz.uz: 'Yesterday' o'tgan zamonni ko'rsatadi, shuning uchun perfect infinitive 'to have attended' kerak.
quiz.ru: 'Yesterday' указывает на прошлое, поэтому нужен перфектный инфинитив 'to have attended'.

quiz.uz: 'Tends to' keskin da'voni ehtiyotkor umumlashtirishga aylantiradi.
quiz.ru: 'Tends to' превращает резкое заявление в осторожное обобщение.

quiz.uz: 'Appears not to have received' ayblash o'rniga begunoh izoh taklif qiladi.
quiz.ru: 'Appears not to have received' предлагает невинное объяснение вместо обвинения.

grammar.title: Nominalisation & academic style
grammar.lead: Turn verbs and adjectives into nouns — 'we analysed the data' becomes 'our analysis of the data' — to write the dense, impersonal prose of reports and academic papers.

leadTr.uz: Fe'l va sifatlarni otga aylantiring — 'we analysed the data' 'our analysis of the data' bo'ladi — hisobot va ilmiy maqolalarning zich, shaxssiz uslubida yozish uchun.
leadTr.ru: Превращайте глаголы и прилагательные в существительные — 'we analysed the data' становится 'our analysis of the data' — так пишется плотная, безличная проза отчётов и научных статей.

grammar.situation: A colleague's email says: 'We decided to expand quickly, and this caused problems.' The annual report renders the same idea as: 'The decision to expand rapidly gave rise to a number of difficulties.' Same facts — entirely different register, built on nouns.

p: Nominalisation converts a verb or adjective into a noun: decide → decision, grow → growth, fail → failure, refuse → refusal, accurate → accuracy, reluctant → reluctance. The action or quality becomes a 'thing' you can then describe, measure and connect.
Once nominalised, the idea takes adjectives instead of adverbs: 'prices grew rapidly' → 'the rapid growth in prices'. The grammar of the whole sentence reorganises itself around the new noun.
ex: They refused to cooperate. → Their refusal to cooperate surprised us.
The engine failed. → The failure of the engine delayed the launch.
She argued persuasively. → Her persuasive argument won the debate.

p: Nominalisation packs a full clause into a noun phrase, freeing the verb slot for a new claim: 'The growth in exports [whole previous idea] has masked a decline in quality [new idea].' It also removes people, making prose impersonal: 'we analysed' → 'the analysis'.
This is why official and academic English feels noun-heavy: each sentence stands on the compressed shoulders of the previous one.
ex: The committee's rejection of the proposal ended the negotiations.
A further reduction in staff numbers is expected.
The investigation revealed serious shortcomings in the process.

p: The commonest frame is the + noun + of/in/to + noun: 'the introduction of the tax', 'the rise in unemployment', 'the response to the crisis'. Choose the preposition the noun demands — it often differs from the verb's.

Nominalisations also pair with specific 'light' verbs: make a decision/an assessment, reach a conclusion/an agreement, hold a discussion, undergo a transformation, give rise to problems. The light verb carries the grammar; the noun carries the meaning.
ex: The board reached an agreement on the merger terms.
The industry has undergone a profound transformation.
Management held a discussion about the restructuring.

blocks.h: Cohesion — and knowing when to stop
p: A powerful cohesive trick: summarise the previous sentence with this + nominalisation. 'Many staff refused to relocate. This refusal forced a rethink of the whole plan.' The noun bundles the old information and pushes the text forward.

But over-nominalisation kills prose: 'We carried out an investigation into the causes of the failure of the engine' says nothing that 'We investigated why the engine failed' doesn't say better. In plain, direct writing — emails, instructions — prefer strong verbs; save dense noun style for formal reports.
ex: Sales fell sharply in March. This decline alarmed investors.
Heavy: The implementation of the improvement of the process… → Better: Improving the process…
The minister resigned. Her resignation triggered a leadership contest.

grammar.tip: Use 'this + nominalisation' to link sentences: '…they refused to sign. This refusal…' — it compresses the previous clause into given information and keeps the new information at the end of the sentence, where English wants it.
examples: The rapid expansion of the company masked a steady erosion of its margins.
Her appointment as director came as no surprise; her subsequent resignation did.
Any reduction in funding would have serious implications for the project.

mistakes.x: The improve of the results was clear.
mistakes.v: The improvement in the results was clear — use the noun form 'improvement', not the bare verb.

mistakes.x: There has been a significant grow in exports.
mistakes.v: a significant growth in exports — 'grow' is the verb; the noun is 'growth'.

mistakes.x: The government made a discussion about taxes.
mistakes.v: The government held a discussion — each nominalisation takes its own light verb; 'discussion' pairs with hold, not make.

quiz.q: Choose the nominalised version of 'They decided to close the plant.'
o: The decision to close the plant
They were deciding on the plant.
quiz.e: 'Decision' is the noun form of 'decide' — the clause becomes a noun phrase.

quiz.q: The noun form of 'fail' is ___.
quiz.e: fail → failure; the -ure suffix, like press → pressure.

quiz.q: Formal register: 'Prices grew quickly, which surprised analysts.' →
o: The rapid growth in prices surprised analysts.
That prices grew quick surprised analysts.
quiz.e: Verb 'grew' becomes the noun 'growth'; the adverb 'quickly' becomes the adjective 'rapid'.

quiz.q: Which light verb collocates: '___ an assessment of the risks'?
quiz.e: 'Make an assessment' — nominalisations pair with fixed light verbs.

quiz.q: Cohesive follow-up to 'Many staff refused to relocate.':
quiz.e: 'This + nominalisation' ('this refusal') summarises the previous clause and links forward.

quiz.q: The noun form of 'accurate' is ___.
quiz.e: accurate → accuracy, like private → privacy.

quiz.q: Which sentence is over-nominalised (worst style)?
o: We investigated why the engine failed.
We carried out an investigation into the causes of the failure of the engine.
The investigation focused on the engine.
quiz.e: Three stacked nominalisations bury the meaning — plain verbs say it more clearly.

quiz.q: 'The company expanded into Asia' → formal noun phrase:
o: the expanding of company into Asia
quiz.e: expand → expansion; possessive + noun + preposition is the standard frame.

quiz.q: Which verb typically pairs with 'a transformation'?
quiz.e: 'Undergo a transformation' — a fixed formal collocation.

quiz.q: Impersonal academic style prefers:
o: I think we should analyse the data again.
You must analyse the data again.
A further analysis of the data is required.
quiz.e: The nominalisation 'a further analysis' removes the personal subject entirely.

situation.uz: Hamkasbning emailida: 'We decided to expand quickly, and this caused problems.' Yillik hisobotda xuddi shu fikr: 'The decision to expand rapidly gave rise to a number of difficulties.' Faktlar bir xil — registr butunlay boshqa, va u otlar ustiga qurilgan.
situation.ru: В письме коллеги: 'We decided to expand quickly, and this caused problems.' В годовом отчёте та же мысль: 'The decision to expand rapidly gave rise to a number of difficulties.' Факты те же — регистр совершенно иной, и построен он на существительных.

tip.uz: Gaplarni bog'lash uchun 'this + nominalisation' ishlating: '…they refused to sign. This refusal…' — u oldingi gapni ma'lum axborotga siqadi va yangi axborotni gap oxirida qoldiradi — ingliz tili aynan shuni xohlaydi.
tip.ru: Связывайте предложения через 'this + номинализация': '…they refused to sign. This refusal…' — она сжимает предыдущую мысль в данное и оставляет новую информацию в конце предложения, как того требует английский.

p.uz: Nominalisation fe'l yoki sifatni otga aylantiradi: decide → decision, grow → growth, fail → failure, refuse → refusal, accurate → accuracy, reluctant → reluctance. Harakat yoki xususiyat 'narsa'ga aylanadi — endi uni tasvirlash, o'lchash va bog'lash mumkin.
p.ru: Номинализация превращает глагол или прилагательное в существительное: decide → decision, grow → growth, fail → failure, refuse → refusal, accurate → accuracy, reluctant → reluctance. Действие или качество становится «предметом», который можно описывать, измерять и связывать.

p.uz: Otga aylangach, fikr ravish o'rniga sifat oladi: 'prices grew rapidly' → 'the rapid growth in prices'. Butun gapning grammatikasi yangi ot atrofida qayta quriladi.
p.ru: После номинализации идея берёт прилагательные вместо наречий: 'prices grew rapidly' → 'the rapid growth in prices'. Грамматика всего предложения перестраивается вокруг нового существительного.

h.uz: Nega rasmiy matn otlarni afzal ko'radi

p.uz: Nominalisation butun gapni ot iborasiga siqadi va fe'l o'rnini yangi fikr uchun bo'shatadi: 'The growth in exports [oldingi fikr] has masked a decline in quality [yangi fikr].' U odamlarni ham olib tashlaydi va matnni shaxssiz qiladi: 'we analysed' → 'the analysis'.
p.ru: Номинализация сжимает целое предложение в именную группу, освобождая позицию глагола для нового утверждения: 'The growth in exports [прежняя мысль] has masked a decline in quality [новая мысль].' Она также убирает людей, делая текст безличным: 'we analysed' → 'the analysis'.

p.uz: Shuning uchun rasmiy va akademik ingliz tili otlarga boy tuyuladi: har bir gap oldingisining siqilgan yelkasida turadi.
p.ru: Поэтому официальный и академический английский кажется перегруженным существительными: каждое предложение стоит на сжатых плечах предыдущего.

p.uz: Eng keng tarqalgan qolip: the + ot + of/in/to + ot — 'the introduction of the tax', 'the rise in unemployment', 'the response to the crisis'. Ot talab qiladigan predlogni tanlang — u ko'pincha fe'lnikidan farq qiladi.
p.ru: Самая частая рамка: the + существительное + of/in/to + существительное — 'the introduction of the tax', 'the rise in unemployment', 'the response to the crisis'. Выбирайте предлог, которого требует существительное — он часто отличается от глагольного.

p.uz: Nominalisationlar maxsus 'light' fe'llar bilan juftlashadi: make a decision/an assessment, reach a conclusion/an agreement, hold a discussion, undergo a transformation, give rise to problems. Light verb grammatikani, ot esa ma'noni ko'taradi.
p.ru: Номинализации сочетаются с определёнными «лёгкими» глаголами: make a decision/an assessment, reach a conclusion/an agreement, hold a discussion, undergo a transformation, give rise to problems. Лёгкий глагол несёт грамматику, существительное — смысл.

p.uz: Kuchli bog'lash usuli: oldingi gapni this + nominalisation bilan umumlashtiring. 'Many staff refused to relocate. This refusal forced a rethink of the whole plan.' Ot eski axborotni o'raydi va matnni oldinga suradi.
p.ru: Мощный приём связности: обобщите предыдущее предложение через this + номинализация. 'Many staff refused to relocate. This refusal forced a rethink of the whole plan.' Существительное упаковывает старую информацию и двигает текст вперёд.

p.uz: Lekin ortiqcha nominalisation matnni o'ldiradi: 'We carried out an investigation into the causes of the failure of the engine' — 'We investigated why the engine failed' dan yaxshiroq hech narsa demaydi. Oddiy, to'g'ridan-to'g'ri matnda — email, ko'rsatmalarda — kuchli fe'llarni tanlang; zich ot uslubini rasmiy hisobotlarga qoldiring.
p.ru: Но избыточная номинализация убивает текст: 'We carried out an investigation into the causes of the failure of the engine' не говорит ничего, что 'We investigated why the engine failed' не сказало бы лучше. В простом прямом письме — email, инструкциях — предпочитайте сильные глаголы; плотный именной стиль оставьте для формальных отчётов.

quiz.uz: 'Decision' — 'decide' fe'lining ot shakli; gap ot iborasiga aylanadi.
quiz.ru: 'Decision' — именная форма глагола 'decide'; предложение становится именной группой.

quiz.uz: fail → failure; -ure qo'shimchasi, press → pressure kabi.
quiz.ru: fail → failure; суффикс -ure, как press → pressure.

quiz.uz: 'Make an assessment' — nominalisationlar turg'un light verblar bilan keladi.
quiz.ru: 'Make an assessment' — номинализации идут с фиксированными light verbs.

quiz.uz: 'This + nominalisation' ('this refusal') oldingi gapni umumlashtirib, matnni bog'laydi.
quiz.ru: 'This + номинализация' ('this refusal') обобщает предыдущее предложение и связывает текст.

quiz.uz: Uchta ustma-ust nominalisation ma'noni ko'mib yuboradi — oddiy fe'llar aniqroq aytadi.
quiz.ru: Три нагромождённые номинализации хоронят смысл — простые глаголы яснее.

quiz.uz: expand → expansion; egalik + ot + predlog — standart qolip.
quiz.ru: expand → expansion; притяжательная форма + существительное + предлог — стандартная рамка.

quiz.uz: 'A further analysis' nominalisationi shaxsiy egani butunlay olib tashlaydi.
quiz.ru: Номинализация 'a further analysis' полностью убирает личное подлежащее.

grammar.title: Participle clauses & reduced relatives
grammar.lead: Tighten your sentences: 'anyone wishing to attend', 'the issues raised', 'Having finished the report, she…' — participle clauses do the work of full clauses in half the words.

leadTr.uz: Gaplaringizni ixchamlashtiring: 'anyone wishing to attend', 'the issues raised', 'Having finished the report, she…' — participle gaplar to'liq gaplarning ishini ikki barobar kam so'z bilan bajaradi.
leadTr.ru: Сжимайте предложения: 'anyone wishing to attend', 'the issues raised', 'Having finished the report, she…' — причастные обороты выполняют работу полных придаточных вдвое меньшим числом слов.

grammar.situation: A conference notice reads: 'Delegates arriving after 9 a.m. should register at the main desk. Having collected your badge, please proceed to the hall. Any documents left unattended will be removed.' Three participle structures, not a single relative pronoun.

p: When the relative pronoun is the subject of its clause, you can delete it and reduce the verb: active meaning takes -ing — 'the man who is standing there' → 'the man standing there'; passive meaning takes the past participle — 'the issues that were raised' → 'the issues raised'.

The -ing form works even for state verbs and other tenses: 'anyone who wants a refund' → 'anyone wanting a refund'. But if the pronoun is the object ('the book that she wrote'), no reduction is possible — you can only drop the pronoun: 'the book she wrote'.
ex: Passengers travelling with children may board first.
The proposals put forward by the committee were rejected.
Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

blocks.h: Participle clauses for time and reason
p: A fronted -ing clause can replace a time or reason clause: 'Feeling exhausted, she cancelled the meeting' (= because she felt); 'Opening the letter, he began to smile' (= when/as he opened). The reader infers the connector from context.
One iron rule: the unstated subject of the participle must be the subject of the main clause. That is what makes the shortcut safe — and what breaks it when ignored.
ex: Realising her mistake, she apologised at once.
Living so far from town, we rarely get visitors.
Not knowing the password, he couldn't open the file.

p: Having + past participle marks an action clearly earlier than the main verb: 'Having signed the contract, they celebrated.' The negative puts not first: 'Not having received a reply, I wrote again.'
For passive meaning, use having been + past participle or a bare past participle: 'Having been warned twice, he was finally dismissed'; 'Seen from above, the island resembles a bird.'
ex: Having spent all the budget, the team asked for more funding.
Having been translated into forty languages, the novel needs no introduction.
Built in the 1890s, the bridge still carries daily traffic.

blocks.h: After conjunctions — and the dangling trap
p: Participles follow time conjunctions and prepositions directly: 'after checking the figures', 'while waiting for the results', 'before signing anything', 'on entering the room' (formal: = as soon as). This is the backbone of instructions and formal notices.

The classic error is the dangling participle: 'Walking down the street, the trees looked beautiful' — grammatically, the trees are walking. Fix it by matching the subjects ('Walking down the street, I admired the trees') or by restoring a full clause ('As I walked down the street…').
ex: After reviewing the evidence, the panel dismissed the claim.
On hearing the verdict, the family burst into tears.
When using this device, always wear protective gloves.

grammar.tip: Test every fronted participle: ask 'who is doing this?' — the answer must be the subject of the main clause. 'Having read the report, the plan seemed weak' fails the test (the plan didn't read anything); 'Having read the report, I found the plan weak' passes.
examples: Anyone wishing to speak at the meeting should notify the chair in advance.
Having been delayed twice already, the project is now under intense scrutiny.
The figures quoted in the article, taken from last year's report, are already out of date.

mistakes.x: Walking down the street, the trees looked beautiful.
mistakes.v: Walking down the street, I thought the trees looked beautiful — the participle's implied subject must be the main-clause subject.

mistakes.x: The report publishing last week caused a stir.
mistakes.v: The report published last week — passive meaning ('which was published') needs the past participle.

mistakes.x: After to finish the meeting, we went for lunch.
mistakes.v: After finishing the meeting — after a conjunction or preposition, use the -ing form, never the infinitive.

quiz.q: Reduce: 'The people who are waiting outside are getting impatient.'
quiz.e: Active meaning with a subject pronoun → the -ing participle replaces 'who are waiting'.

quiz.q: The questions ___ at the meeting were difficult to answer.
quiz.e: Passive meaning ('which were raised') → past participle.

quiz.q: ___ the report, she emailed it to the board.
quiz.e: 'Having + past participle' clearly marks the earlier of two actions.

quiz.q: Which sentence has a dangling participle?
o: Driving to work, Tom saw an accident.
Having eaten, we left the restaurant.
Opening the box, the smell was awful.
While cooking, she cut her finger.
quiz.e: The smell didn't open the box — the participle has no matching subject in the main clause.

quiz.q: ___ twice about the deadline, he still submitted late.
quiz.e: Passive meaning plus earlier action → 'Having been warned'.

quiz.q: After ___ the contract, read the appendix carefully.
quiz.e: After a conjunction or preposition, use the -ing form.

quiz.q: Which reduction is impossible?
o: the man who lives next door → the man living next door
the book that she wrote → the book she writing
anyone who wants tickets → anyone wanting tickets
the money that was stolen → the money stolen
quiz.e: Participle reduction only works when the relative pronoun is the subject; here 'she' is the subject, so only pronoun-dropping is possible.

quiz.q: ___ received no reply, I wrote to them again.
quiz.e: Earlier active action → 'Having received no reply'.

quiz.q: Formal notice: 'Passengers ___ to change trains should alight here.'
quiz.e: 'Wishing' reduces 'who wish' — the typical style of formal notices.

quiz.q: 'On ___ at the hotel, guests are asked to present ID.'
quiz.e: 'On + -ing' = 'as soon as' in formal style; a preposition needs the -ing form.

situation.uz: Konferensiya e'lonida: 'Delegates arriving after 9 a.m. should register at the main desk. Having collected your badge, please proceed to the hall. Any documents left unattended will be removed.' Uchta participle tuzilma — birorta ham nisbiy olmosh yo'q.
situation.ru: В объявлении конференции: 'Delegates arriving after 9 a.m. should register at the main desk. Having collected your badge, please proceed to the hall. Any documents left unattended will be removed.' Три причастные конструкции — и ни одного относительного местоимения.

tip.uz: Har bir gap boshidagi participle ni tekshiring: 'buni kim qilyapti?' deb so'rang — javob bosh gapning egasi bo'lishi shart. 'Having read the report, the plan seemed weak' testdan o'tmaydi (plan hech narsa o'qimagan); 'Having read the report, I found the plan weak' — o'tadi.
tip.ru: Проверяйте каждое начальное причастие вопросом «кто это делает?» — ответом должно быть подлежащее главного предложения. 'Having read the report, the plan seemed weak' тест не проходит (план ничего не читал); 'Having read the report, I found the plan weak' — проходит.

p.uz: Nisbiy olmosh o'z gapining egasi bo'lsa, uni tushirib, fe'lni qisqartirish mumkin: faol ma'no -ing oladi — 'the man who is standing there' → 'the man standing there'; passiv ma'no past participle oladi — 'the issues that were raised' → 'the issues raised'.
p.ru: Если относительное местоимение — подлежащее своего придаточного, его можно убрать и свернуть глагол: активное значение берёт -ing — 'the man who is standing there' → 'the man standing there'; пассивное — причастие прошедшего времени: 'the issues that were raised' → 'the issues raised'.

p.uz: -ing shakli holat fe'llari va boshqa zamonlar uchun ham ishlaydi: 'anyone who wants a refund' → 'anyone wanting a refund'. Lekin olmosh to'ldiruvchi bo'lsa ('the book that she wrote'), qisqartirish mumkin emas — faqat olmoshni tushirish mumkin: 'the book she wrote'.
p.ru: Форма -ing работает и для глаголов состояния, и для других времён: 'anyone who wants a refund' → 'anyone wanting a refund'. Но если местоимение — дополнение ('the book that she wrote'), редукция невозможна — можно лишь опустить местоимение: 'the book she wrote'.

h.uz: Vaqt va sabab uchun participle gaplar

p.uz: Gap boshidagi -ing gap vaqt yoki sabab ergash gapini almashtira oladi: 'Feeling exhausted, she cancelled the meeting' (= chunki charchagan edi); 'Opening the letter, he began to smile' (= ochganida). O'quvchi bog'lovchini kontekstdan topadi.
p.ru: Начальный оборот с -ing может заменять придаточное времени или причины: 'Feeling exhausted, she cancelled the meeting' (= потому что устала); 'Opening the letter, he began to smile' (= когда открыл). Связку читатель выводит из контекста.

p.uz: Temir qoida: participle ning aytilmagan egasi bosh gapning egasi bo'lishi shart. Aynan shu qoida qisqartmani xavfsiz qiladi — unga rioya qilinmasa, gap buziladi.
p.ru: Железное правило: невыраженное подлежащее причастия должно совпадать с подлежащим главного предложения. Именно это делает сокращение безопасным — и ломает его при нарушении.

p.uz: Having + past participle harakat bosh fe'ldan aniq oldin bo'lganini bildiradi: 'Having signed the contract, they celebrated.' Inkorda not oldin keladi: 'Not having received a reply, I wrote again.'
p.ru: Having + причастие прошедшего времени показывает действие, явно предшествующее главному: 'Having signed the contract, they celebrated.' В отрицании not ставится первым: 'Not having received a reply, I wrote again.'

p.uz: Passiv ma'no uchun having been + past participle yoki yolg'iz past participle ishlatiladi: 'Having been warned twice, he was finally dismissed'; 'Seen from above, the island resembles a bird.'
p.ru: Для пассивного значения — having been + причастие или одиночное причастие прошедшего времени: 'Having been warned twice, he was finally dismissed'; 'Seen from above, the island resembles a bird.'

h.ru: После союзов — и ловушка висячего причастия

p.uz: Participle lar vaqt bog'lovchilari va predloglardan keyin to'g'ridan-to'g'ri keladi: 'after checking the figures', 'while waiting for the results', 'before signing anything', 'on entering the room' (rasmiy: = kirishi bilanoq). Bu ko'rsatmalar va rasmiy e'lonlarning asosiy usuli.
p.ru: Причастия идут сразу после временных союзов и предлогов: 'after checking the figures', 'while waiting for the results', 'before signing anything', 'on entering the room' (формально: = как только вошёл). Это основа инструкций и официальных объявлений.

p.uz: Klassik xato — dangling participle: 'Walking down the street, the trees looked beautiful' — grammatik jihatdan daraxtlar yurmoqda. Egalarni moslashtirib ('Walking down the street, I admired the trees') yoki to'liq gapni qaytarib ('As I walked down the street…') tuzating.
p.ru: Классическая ошибка — висячее причастие: 'Walking down the street, the trees looked beautiful' — грамматически идут деревья. Исправьте, согласовав подлежащие ('Walking down the street, I admired the trees') или вернув полное придаточное ('As I walked down the street…').

quiz.uz: Faol ma'no, olmosh ega bo'lgani uchun -ing participle 'who are waiting' ni almashtiradi.
quiz.ru: Активное значение при местоимении-подлежащем → причастие -ing заменяет 'who are waiting'.

quiz.uz: Passiv ma'no ('which were raised') → past participle.
quiz.ru: Пассивное значение ('which were raised') → причастие прошедшего времени.

quiz.uz: 'Having + past participle' ikki harakatdan oldingisini aniq belgilaydi.
quiz.ru: 'Having + причастие' чётко отмечает более раннее из двух действий.

quiz.uz: Hid qutini ochmagan — participle ning bosh gapda mos egasi yo'q.
quiz.ru: Запах не открывал коробку — у причастия нет соответствующего подлежащего в главном предложении.

quiz.uz: Passiv ma'no + oldingi harakat → 'Having been warned'.
quiz.ru: Пассивное значение + предшествующее действие → 'Having been warned'.

quiz.uz: Bog'lovchi yoki predlogdan keyin -ing shakli ishlatiladi.
quiz.ru: После союза или предлога используется форма -ing.

quiz.uz: Qisqartirish faqat nisbiy olmosh ega bo'lganda ishlaydi; bu yerda ega 'she', shuning uchun faqat olmoshni tushirish mumkin.
quiz.ru: Редукция работает только когда относительное местоимение — подлежащее; здесь подлежащее 'she', возможно лишь опустить местоимение.

quiz.uz: Oldingi faol harakat → 'Having received no reply'.
quiz.ru: Предшествующее активное действие → 'Having received no reply'.

quiz.uz: 'Wishing' — 'who wish' ning qisqargan shakli; rasmiy e'lonlarning odatiy uslubi.
quiz.ru: 'Wishing' — редукция 'who wish'; типичный стиль официальных объявлений.

quiz.uz: 'On + -ing' rasmiy uslubda = 'as soon as'; predlogdan keyin -ing kerak.
quiz.ru: 'On + -ing' в формальном стиле = 'as soon as'; после предлога нужна форма -ing.

grammar.title: Colons & dashes
grammar.lead: Colons introduce and dashes interrupt — both add sophistication when used precisely, and both are tested mercilessly in formal writing. Master the exact rules.

leadTr.uz: Ikki nuqta kiritadi, tire esa to'xtatadi — ikkalasi ham aniq ishlatilganda uslubni boyitadi. Aniq qoidalarni o'zlashtiring.
leadTr.ru: Двоеточие вводит, тире прерывает — оба знака делают стиль изящнее при точном использовании. Освойте точные правила.

grammar.situation: "Her thesis needed one thing: evidence." The colon promises an explanation and delivers it. Swap it for a dash — "Her thesis needed one thing — evidence." — and the register shifts from formal to dramatic.

blocks.h: The colon: a complete clause, then the payoff
p: A colon may only follow a COMPLETE independent clause. What comes after it — a list, an explanation, a single word — answers the expectation the clause creates: 'The study identified three risk factors: poor diet, sedentary lifestyle, and chronic stress.'
ex: Three cities were considered for the summit: Geneva, Singapore, and Nairobi.
Her conclusion was simple: the current model was fundamentally flawed.
The finding had one major implication: the treatment needed revision.

p: Never place a colon after a preposition or a verb that flows directly into its object: 'The success depended on: innovation...' is wrong because 'depended on' is not a complete clause. If the words before the colon cannot stand alone as a sentence, use no punctuation at all.
ex: The company's success depended on innovation, partnerships, and timing. (no colon)
The panel consists of three economists and a historian. (no colon after 'consists of')

blocks.h: Em dashes come in pairs mid-sentence
p: A parenthetical interruption in the middle of a sentence takes an em dash on BOTH sides — never a dash on one side and a comma on the other. Delete the material between the dashes and the sentence must still work.
ex: The scientist — who had spent 30 years on the topic — finally announced her breakthrough.
The award — never before given to a non-citizen — recognized her contributions.

p: Both can introduce an explanation after a complete clause. The colon is the formal, academic choice; the single dash is more dramatic and conversational. On formal-writing questions where both appear as options, the colon is usually the intended answer.
ex: Formal: The data pointed to one culprit: the cooling system.
Dramatic: The data pointed to one culprit — the cooling system.

grammar.tip: Cover everything after the colon: do the remaining words form a complete sentence? If not, the colon is illegal there. For dashes mid-sentence, count them — interruptions always need two.
examples: The recipe requires three things: patience, butter, and more patience.
The verdict — reached after nine hours of deliberation — surprised everyone.
One question remained: who would fund the second phase?
The committee was divided: half supported the proposal, and half opposed it.

mistakes.x: The success depended on: innovation and timing.
mistakes.v: The success depended on innovation and timing. — no colon after a preposition.

mistakes.x: The scientist — who led the study, announced the result.
mistakes.v: The scientist — who led the study — announced the result. — mid-sentence dashes come in pairs.

mistakes.x: Included in the kit: a manual and two cables.
mistakes.v: The kit includes two things: a manual and two cables. — a colon needs a complete clause before it.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The study identified three major risk factors[___] poor diet, sedentary lifestyle, and chronic stress.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: An independent clause ('The study identified three major risk factors') followed by a list. D (:) correctly introduces the list. Both colon and dash would work, but in formal writing a colon is preferred.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The scientist[___]who had spent 30 years researching the topic[___]finally announced her breakthrough.'

Which choice correctly uses dashes?
quiz.e: 'Who had spent 30 years researching the topic' is parenthetical information. Em dashes must appear in PAIRS: 'The scientist—who had spent 30 years...—finally announced.' D is correct.

quiz.q:
Text: 'Her conclusion was simple[___] the current model was fundamentally flawed.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: 'Her conclusion was simple' is an independent clause. A colon or dash can introduce the explanation that follows. D (:) is correct (formal). C (—) also works. Both D and C are valid — D is preferred in formal contexts.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The award[___]which had never before been given to a non-citizen[___]recognized her lifetime contributions.'

Which choice correctly uses dashes?
quiz.e: Em dashes must appear in PAIRS around parenthetical information. B (dash and dash) is correct: 'The award—which had never...non-citizen—recognized...'

quiz.q:
Text: 'The new policy accomplished one crucial thing[___]it gave low-income families access to affordable healthcare.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: 'The new policy accomplished one crucial thing' is a complete independent clause. A colon introduces the explanation. C (:) is correct. D (em dash) would also work. Both are valid; C is the formal choice.

quiz.q:
Text: 'Three cities were considered for the summit[___]Geneva, Singapore, and Nairobi.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: Complete independent clause followed by a list. D (:) is correct. C (—) would also work but the colon is more formal.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The expedition[___]the first of its kind in over fifty years[___]attracted international media attention.'

Which choice correctly uses dashes?
quiz.e: Parenthetical information in the middle of a sentence requires em dashes in PAIRS. C (dash and dash) is correct.

quiz.q:
Text: 'One conclusion emerged from the data[___]the intervention was only effective for adolescents.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: Complete clause + explanation. C (:) is correct. B (—) also works. C preferred in formal writing.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The architect designed three landmark buildings[___]the concert hall, the public library, and the civic center.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: Complete clause followed by a list of explanatory items. C (:) is correct. B (—) also works.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The company's success depended on[___]innovation, strategic partnerships, and market timing.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: Colon CANNOT follow a preposition ('on'). D (no punctuation) is correct: 'depended on innovation, strategic partnerships, and market timing.'

quiz.q:
Text: 'The finding had one major implication[___]the standard treatment needed to be revised.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: Complete clause + implication explained. C (:) is correct. B (—) also valid. C is formal choice.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The committee was divided[___]half supported the proposal, and half opposed it.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: 'The committee was divided' is a complete clause. A colon introduces an explanation. B (:) is correct. A (em dash) would also work.

situation.uz: "Her thesis needed one thing: evidence." Ikki nuqta izoh va'da qiladi va uni beradi. Uni tirega almashtirsangiz — "...one thing — evidence." — ohang rasmiylikdan dramatiklikka o'tadi.
situation.ru: «Her thesis needed one thing: evidence.» Двоеточие обещает пояснение и даёт его. Замените его на тире — «...one thing — evidence.» — и регистр сместится с формального на драматичный.

tip.uz: Ikki nuqtadan keyingi hamma narsani yoping: qolgan so'zlar to'liq gap bo'ladimi? Bo'lmasa — ikki nuqta u yerda mumkin emas. Gap o'rtasidagi tirelerni sanang — uzilishlar doim ikkitasini talab qiladi.
tip.ru: Закройте всё после двоеточия: образуют ли оставшиеся слова полное предложение? Если нет — двоеточие там недопустимо. Тире в середине предложения считайте — вставке всегда нужны два.

h.uz: Ikki nuqta: to'liq gap, keyin javob

p.uz: Ikki nuqta faqat TO'LIQ mustaqil gapdan keyin kela oladi. Undan keyingisi — ro'yxat, izoh yoki bitta so'z — gap yaratgan kutishga javob beradi.
p.ru: Двоеточие может стоять только после ПОЛНОГО независимого предложения. То, что идёт после — список, пояснение или одно слово — отвечает на ожидание, созданное предложением.

p.uz: Predlogdan yoki to'ldiruvchisiga bevosita o'tadigan fe'ldan keyin hech qachon ikki nuqta qo'ymang: 'depended on: innovation...' xato, chunki 'depended on' to'liq gap emas. Ikki nuqtadan oldingi so'zlar alohida gap bo'la olmasa — umuman tinish belgisi kerak emas.
p.ru: Никогда не ставьте двоеточие после предлога или глагола, переходящего прямо в дополнение: 'depended on: innovation...' — ошибка, потому что 'depended on' не полное предложение. Если слова перед двоеточием не образуют предложение — знак не нужен вовсе.

h.uz: Em dash gap o'rtasida juft keladi
h.ru: Em dash в середине предложения парой

p.uz: Gap o'rtasidagi kirish ma'lumot IKKI tomondan em dash oladi — bir tomonda tire, ikkinchisida vergul bo'lishi mumkin emas. Tireler orasidagi qismni o'chirsangiz, gap baribir ishlashi kerak.
p.ru: Вставка в середине предложения выделяется em dash с ОБЕИХ сторон — нельзя с одной стороны тире, а с другой запятая. Удалите часть между тире — предложение должно остаться корректным.

h.uz: Ikki nuqta yoki tire? Uslub hal qiladi

p.uz: Ikkalasi ham to'liq gapdan keyin izoh kirita oladi. Ikki nuqta — rasmiy, akademik tanlov; yakka tire — dramatikroq va so'zlashuvga yaqin. Rasmiy yozuv savollarida ikkalasi ham variant bo'lsa, odatda ikki nuqta kutiladi.
p.ru: Оба могут вводить пояснение после полного предложения. Двоеточие — формальный, академический выбор; одиночное тире — более драматичное и разговорное. В вопросах о формальном письме, где есть оба варианта, обычно ожидается двоеточие.

quiz.uz: To'liq gap + ro'yxat → ikki nuqta; rasmiy yozuvda u afzal.
quiz.ru: Полное предложение + список → двоеточие; в формальном письме оно предпочтительно.

quiz.uz: Kirish ma'lumot — em dash JUFT bo'lishi kerak.
quiz.ru: Вставка — em dash должны идти ПАРОЙ.

quiz.uz: To'liq gap + izoh → ikki nuqta (rasmiy tanlov).
Kirish ma'lumot atrofida em dash juft keladi.
quiz.ru: Вокруг вставки em dash ставятся парой.

quiz.uz: To'liq gap + izoh → ikki nuqta; tire ham mumkin, lekin ikki nuqta rasmiyroq.
quiz.ru: Полное предложение + пояснение → двоеточие; тире тоже возможно, но двоеточие формальнее.

quiz.uz: To'liq gap + shaharlar ro'yxati → ikki nuqta.
Gap o'rtasidagi kirish ma'lumot → juft em dash.
quiz.ru: Вставка в середине предложения → парные em dash.

quiz.uz: Predlog ('on') dan keyin ikki nuqta qo'yib BO'LMAYDI → tinish belgisisiz.
quiz.ru: После предлога ('on') двоеточие ставить НЕЛЬЗЯ → без знака.

quiz.uz: To'liq gap + xulosa izohi → ikki nuqta.
'The committee was divided' — to'liq gap; izohni ikki nuqta kiritadi.
quiz.ru: 'The committee was divided' — полное предложение; пояснение вводит двоеточие.

grammar.title: Apostrophes & possession
grammar.lead: Its or it's? Students' or student's? The apostrophe is small but ruthless. These exercises cover possession, contractions and the classic traps.

leadTr.uz: Its yoki it's? Students' yoki student's? Apostrof kichik, lekin shafqatsiz. Bu mashqlar egalik, qisqartma va klassik tuzoqlarni qamrab oladi.
leadTr.ru: Its или it's? Students' или student's? Апостроф мал, но беспощаден. Здесь — принадлежность, сокращения и классические ловушки.

grammar.situation: "The dogs bowl" — whose bowl? One dog ('the dog's bowl') or several ('the dogs' bowl')? Without the apostrophe the sentence cannot say. That is the entire job of this small mark.

p: One owner: add 's — 'the government's initiative'. Multiple owners whose plural ends in -s: add only the apostrophe AFTER the s — 'the professors' lectures', 'both departments' offices'. Never double the s into 'professors's'.
ex: The government's new initiative targets emissions. (one government)
The professors' lectures drew huge crowds. (several professors)
The two departments' offices share one building.

p: Plurals that do NOT end in -s form the possessive like singulars: add 's. 'The children's responses', 'women's rights', 'people's choices'. The same logic covers -ies plurals: 'the factories' impact' (apostrophe after the s).
ex: The children's responses varied by age group.
The factories' impact on the ecosystem was studied for years.

p: 'Its', 'hers', 'theirs', 'yours', 'whose' are already possessive — adding an apostrophe creates a different word or a non-word. 'It's' = it is; 'who's' = who is; 'they're' = they are. 'Her's' and 'hers'' simply do not exist.
ex: The company released its report. / It's been a decade since the discovery.
The scientist whose research won the prize gave a lecture.
Despite their best efforts, the results never replicated.

p: Whenever you hesitate between its/it's or whose/who's, expand the contraction and reread: 'It's been a decade' → 'It has been a decade' — works, so keep the apostrophe. 'The company released it's report' → 'released it is report' — nonsense, so use 'its'.
ex: It's expanding into three new markets. (= it is — correct)
The scientist who's presenting today studies deep-sea life. (= who is)

grammar.tip: Apostrophe decision in two questions: (1) Contraction? Expand it and check. (2) Possessive noun? Find how many owners: one → 's; plural in -s → s'; irregular plural → 's.
examples: The candidates' proposals were reviewed by the committee. (six candidates)
It's been raining since the ceremony's opening minutes.
The women's team broke the men's record.
Whose thesis is this — and who's supervising it?

mistakes.x: The company released it's annual report.
mistakes.v: The company released its annual report. — 'it's' = 'it is'; the possessive is 'its'.

mistakes.x: The professors's lectures were popular.
mistakes.v: The professors' lectures were popular. — plural in -s takes only the apostrophe.

mistakes.x: The childrens' responses were recorded.
mistakes.v: The children's responses were recorded. — irregular plural: apostrophe before the s.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The company released [___] annual sustainability report last month.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: 'Its' = possessive (belonging to the company). Expand test: 'released it is annual report' → nonsense → use 'its' (no apostrophe). B is correct.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The professors [___] lectures on quantum mechanics attracted students from across the university.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: Multiple professors → plural → plural possessive: 'professors'' (apostrophe after the s). B is correct. A would mean one professor. C doubles the s — never correct.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The researcher presented [___] findings to a panel of international experts.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: 'Hers' is already a possessive pronoun — no apostrophe needed. C is correct. 'Her's' and 'hers'' are not real words.

quiz.q:
Text: 'Despite [___] best efforts, the team could not replicate the original experiment's results.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: 'Their' = possessive pronoun (belonging to them). B is correct. A = they are. C = location. D is the expanded form of A.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The study examined the [___] responses to the new curriculum across three age groups.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: 'Children' is an irregular plural (does not end in s). Possessive = add 's: 'children's.' A is correct.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The committee reviewed all six [___] proposals before making its final decision.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: Multiple candidates (all six) → plural possessive: 'candidates'' (apostrophe after s). B is correct.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The [___] new initiative focuses on reducing carbon emissions.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: One government → singular possessive: 'government's.' A is correct.

quiz.q:
Text: '[___] been over a decade since the discovery was first announced.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: 'It's been...' = 'It has been...' — a contraction. B (it's) is correct. A (its) is possessive, not a contraction.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The scientist [___] research on deep-sea organisms earned her international recognition.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: 'Whose' = possessive relative pronoun (the scientist's research). B is correct. A (who's) = 'who is' — expand test: 'the scientist who is research...' → nonsense.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The two [___] offices share the same building but operate completely independently.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: Two departments → plural → plural possessive: 'departments'' (apostrophe after s). B is correct.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The [___] impact on the local ecosystem was studied for three years.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: Multiple factories (implied by context) → plural possessive: 'factories'' (apostrophe after s, irregular plural formed with -ies). A is correct.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The company announced that [___] expanding operations to three new markets.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: 'It's expanding' = 'it is expanding' — a contraction. B (it's) is correct.

situation.uz: "The dogs bowl" — kimning idishi? Bitta itnikimi ('the dog's bowl') yoki bir nechtanikimi ('the dogs' bowl')? Apostrofsiz gap buni ayta olmaydi. Bu kichkina belgining butun vazifasi shu.
situation.ru: «The dogs bowl» — чья миска? Одной собаки ('the dog's bowl') или нескольких ('the dogs' bowl')? Без апострофа предложение не может этого сказать. В этом вся работа маленького знака.

tip.uz: Apostrof qarori ikki savolda: (1) Qisqartmami? Yoyib tekshiring. (2) Egalik otimi? Egalar sonini toping: bitta → 's; -s bilan tugagan ko'plik → s'; noto'g'ri ko'plik → 's.
tip.ru: Решение об апострофе в два вопроса: (1) Сокращение? Разверните и проверьте. (2) Притяжательное существительное? Определите число владельцев: один → 's; мн. ч. на -s → s'; неправильное мн. ч. → 's.

p.uz: Bitta ega: 's qo'shiladi — 'the government's initiative'. -s bilan tugagan ko'plikdagi egalar: faqat s dan KEYIN apostrof — 'the professors' lectures'. Hech qachon 'professors's' deb s ni ikkilantirmang.
p.ru: Один владелец: добавьте 's — 'the government's initiative'. Владельцы во мн. ч. на -s: только апостроф ПОСЛЕ s — 'the professors' lectures'. Никогда не удваивайте s в 'professors's'.

h.ru: Неправильные формы мн. ч.: children's, women's, people's

p.uz: -s bilan tugamaydigan ko'pliklar egalikni birlik kabi yasaydi: 's qo'shiladi — 'the children's responses'. -ies ko'pliklari uchun esa apostrof s dan keyin: 'the factories' impact'.
p.ru: Множественные числа, не оканчивающиеся на -s, образуют притяжательную форму как ед. ч.: добавляется 's — 'the children's responses'. А у форм на -ies апостроф после s: 'the factories' impact'.

h.uz: Egalik olmoshlari hech qachon apostrof olmaydi
h.ru: Притяжательные местоимения никогда не берут апостроф

p.uz: 'Its', 'hers', 'theirs', 'yours', 'whose' allaqachon egalik shakllari — apostrof qo'shsangiz boshqa so'z yoki mavjud bo'lmagan so'z hosil bo'ladi. 'It's' = it is; 'who's' = who is; 'they're' = they are. 'Her's' degan so'z yo'q.
p.ru: 'Its', 'hers', 'theirs', 'yours', 'whose' уже притяжательные — апостроф даст другое слово или несуществующее. 'It's' = it is; 'who's' = who is; 'they're' = they are. Слова 'her's' не существует.

p.uz: Its/it's yoki whose/who's orasida ikkilansangiz, qisqartmani yoyib qayta o'qing: 'It's been a decade' → 'It has been a decade' — ishlaydi, apostrof qoladi. 'released it's report' → 'released it is report' — bema'ni, demak 'its'.
p.ru: Сомневаетесь между its/it's или whose/who's — разверните сокращение и перечитайте: 'It's been a decade' → 'It has been a decade' — работает, апостроф остаётся. 'released it's report' → 'released it is report' — бессмыслица, значит 'its'.

quiz.ru: Притяжательное → 'its' (без апострофа); разворот 'it is' дал бы бессмыслицу.

quiz.uz: Bir nechta professor → ko'plik egalik: professors' (s dan keyin apostrof).
quiz.ru: Несколько профессоров → притяжательное мн. ч.: professors' (апостроф после s).

quiz.uz: 'Hers' — tayyor egalik olmoshi, apostrof kerak emas.
quiz.ru: 'Hers' — готовое притяжательное местоимение, апостроф не нужен.
Шесть кандидатов → притяжательное мн. ч.: candidates'.
Одно правительство → притяжательное ед. ч.: government's.

quiz.uz: 'It's been' = 'It has been' — qisqartma → apostrof kerak.
quiz.ru: 'It's been' = 'It has been' — сокращение → нужен апостроф.

quiz.uz: 'Whose' — egalik nisbiy olmoshi; 'who's' = who is bema'ni bo'lardi.
quiz.ru: 'Whose' — притяжательное относительное местоимение; 'who's' = who is дало бы бессмыслицу.
Два отдела → притяжательное мн. ч.: departments'.

quiz.uz: Bir nechta zavod (-ies ko'pligi) → factories' (s dan keyin apostrof).
quiz.ru: Несколько фабрик (мн. ч. на -ies) → factories' (апостроф после s).

grammar.title: Sentence boundaries
grammar.lead: Run-ons and fragments are the two ways a sentence can fail. Learn to detect where one complete thought ends and the next must begin.

leadTr.uz: Qo'shilib ketgan gaplar va chala gaplar — gap buzilishining ikki yo'li. Bitta to'liq fikr qayerda tugashini va keyingisi qayerda boshlanishi kerakligini aniqlashni o'rganing.
leadTr.ru: Слипшиеся предложения и фрагменты — два способа сломать предложение. Учитесь видеть, где заканчивается одна законченная мысль и должна начаться следующая.

grammar.situation: "Having analyzed all available data." A reviewer writes in the margin: 'And then what?' The phrase promises a sentence that never arrives — a fragment. The opposite failure: two sentences fused with nothing between them.

p: An independent clause has a subject and a main verb and expresses a complete thought. Every sentence needs at least one. The two boundary errors are mirror images: a RUN-ON jams two independent clauses together (with no punctuation, or with only a comma — the comma splice); a FRAGMENT punctuates less than a full clause as if it were a sentence.
ex: Run-on: The weather delayed the launch engineers rescheduled for next week.
Comma splice: The data was compelling, the board approved the project.
Complete: The test results were inconclusive, but the study continued.

blocks.h: Four legal ways to join two independent clauses
p: (1) A period — two sentences. (2) A semicolon. (3) A comma plus a coordinating conjunction (FANBOYS). (4) Subordination — turn one clause into a dependent clause with 'because', 'although', 'when'. A conjunctive adverb like 'however' or 'nevertheless' needs the pattern '; however,' — semicolon before, comma after.
ex: Solar panels became cheaper; many households can now afford them.
The novel got mixed reviews; however, it is now considered a masterpiece.
The population is declining; yet, conservationists cannot find the cause.

p: Typical fragments: a participial phrase ('Having analyzed all available data.'), a prepositional opener ('After years of painstaking research.'), or a relative clause cut loose ('Which proved the hypothesis was correct.'). The fix is always attachment: connect the fragment to the main clause it belongs to, or give it its own subject and verb.
ex: The paintings, discovered in a remote cave, date back 30,000 years.
