The experiment was a success, which proved the hypothesis was correct.
After years of research, the team finally published.

grammar.tip: Read each candidate 'sentence' alone and ask: subject? main verb? complete thought? All three yes — independent clause. Then check every junction between two independent clauses for one of the four legal connectors.
examples: The funding fell through; nevertheless, the lab stayed open.
Because the survey sample was tiny, the findings were treated with caution.
The mayor promised reform, and the council delivered it.
Exhausted but satisfied, the crew docked the ship. (participial opener attached — not a fragment)

mistakes.x: The results were published. Which surprised the reviewers.
mistakes.v: The results were published, which surprised the reviewers. — a relative clause cannot stand alone.

mistakes.x: The trial ended, the verdict shocked everyone.
mistakes.v: The trial ended; the verdict shocked everyone. — comma splice: use a semicolon or a conjunction.

mistakes.x: The storm intensified overnight the city closed all schools.
mistakes.v: The storm intensified overnight, so the city closed all schools. — fused run-on: add punctuation plus a connector.

quiz.q: Which version is a comma splice?
o: The data was compelling, so the board approved the project immediately.
The data was compelling; the board approved the project immediately.
The data was compelling, the board approved the project immediately.
Because the data was compelling, the board approved the project immediately.
quiz.e: B joins two independent clauses with only a comma — a comma splice.

quiz.q: Which version is a run-on?
o: The weather delayed the launch, and engineers rescheduled for the following week.
The weather delayed the launch engineers rescheduled for the following week.
Although the weather delayed the launch, engineers rescheduled for the following week.
The weather delayed the launch; engineers rescheduled for the following week.
quiz.e: B has two independent clauses with no punctuation or connector — a fused run-on.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The novel received mixed reviews upon publication[___] it is now considered a masterpiece of twentieth-century literature.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: Two contrasting independent clauses. '; however,' correctly shows contrast with semicolon before and comma after.

quiz.q: Which version is a sentence fragment?
o: The scientist published her findings last month.
The board reviewed all proposals carefully.
quiz.e: B — 'After years of painstaking research' — is a dependent clause with no main clause. Fragment.

quiz.q:
Text: 'Solar panels have become significantly cheaper over the past decade[___] many households that previously could not afford them can now install them.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: Two independent clauses. C (semicolon) correctly joins them. A = comma splice. D = run-on.

quiz.q: Which version correctly fixes the fragment 'Discovered in a remote cave in southern France'?
o: The paintings, discovered in a remote cave in southern France, date back 30,000 years.
Discovered in a remote cave in southern France the paintings date back 30,000 years.
Discovered in a remote cave in southern France, to date back 30,000 years.
Discovered in a remote cave in southern France; the paintings date back 30,000 years.
quiz.e: B attaches the participial phrase to the main sentence: 'The paintings... date back 30,000 years.' Correct sentence structure.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The researchers worked around the clock[___] they were determined to publish before the competing team.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: Two independent clauses. C (semicolon) is correct. A = comma splice. D = run-on.

quiz.q: Which version is a fragment?
o: After the team analyzed all available data, it reached a conclusion.
The team analyzed all available data and reached a conclusion.
Having analyzed all available data, the team reached a definitive conclusion.
quiz.e: B is only a participial phrase — no subject, no main verb. Fragment.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The population has been declining for years[___] conservationists have been unable to determine the primary cause.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: Contrast: declining but cause unknown. '; yet,' shows contrast with proper semicolon + comma punctuation.

quiz.q: Which version is NOT a fragment?
o: Although the researchers worked for three years.
The test results were inconclusive, but the study continued.
To determine the cause of the anomaly.
Because the test results were inconclusive.
quiz.e: C has a subject ('the study') and a main verb ('continued'). A, B are dependent clauses alone. D is an infinitive phrase alone.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The bridge was structurally sound[___] city engineers ordered it closed after residents reported unusual vibrations.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: Sound but still closed — contrast. '; nevertheless,' correctly shows the contrast.

quiz.q: Which version correctly rewrites 'The experiment was a success. Which proved that the hypothesis was correct.' to eliminate the fragment?
o: The experiment was a success; which proved that the hypothesis was correct.
The experiment was a success, it proved that the hypothesis was correct.
The experiment was a success. That proved that the hypothesis was correct.
The experiment was a success, which proved that the hypothesis was correct.
quiz.e: A attaches 'which proved...' as a nonrestrictive relative clause — no longer a fragment. B incorrectly uses semicolon before a relative clause (not an independent clause). D is a comma splice.

situation.uz: "Having analyzed all available data." Muharrir chetiga yozadi: 'Xo'sh, keyin nima?' Ibora gap va'da qiladi, lekin gap kelmaydi — bu fragment. Teskari xato: ikkita gap orasiga hech narsa qo'ymay yopishtiriladi.
situation.ru: «Having analyzed all available data.» Рецензент пишет на полях: «И что дальше?» Оборот обещает предложение, которое так и не приходит — это fragment. Противоположная ошибка: два предложения слиты вообще без знака.

tip.uz: Har bir 'gap'ni alohida o'qib so'rang: ega bormi? asosiy fe'l bormi? fikr tugalmi? Uchalasi ham ha — mustaqil gap. Keyin ikki mustaqil gap orasidagi har bir tutashuvda to'rt qonuniy bog'lagichdan biri borligini tekshiring.
tip.ru: Прочитайте каждое «предложение» отдельно и спросите: подлежащее? главный глагол? законченная мысль? Три «да» — независимое предложение. Затем проверьте каждый стык двух независимых предложений на один из четырёх законных соединителей.

p.uz: Mustaqil gapda ega, asosiy fe'l va tugal fikr bor. Ikki chegara xatosi bir-birining aksi: RUN-ON ikkita mustaqil gapni belgisiz (yoki faqat vergul bilan — comma splice) yopishtiradi; FRAGMENT esa to'liq gapdan kamroq narsani gap kabi rasmiylashtiradi.
p.ru: У независимого предложения есть подлежащее, главный глагол и законченная мысль. Две ошибки границ зеркальны: RUN-ON слепляет два независимых предложения без знака (или только запятой — comma splice); FRAGMENT оформляет как предложение то, что предложением не является.

h.uz: Ikki mustaqil gapni bog'lashning to'rt qonuniy yo'li
h.ru: Четыре законных способа соединить два независимых предложения

p.uz: (1) Nuqta — ikkita gap. (2) Nuqtali vergul. (3) Vergul + muvofiqlashtiruvchi bog'lovchi (FANBOYS). (4) Ergashtirish — 'because', 'although', 'when' bilan. 'However' yoki 'nevertheless' kabi bog'lovchi ravishlar '; however,' qolipini talab qiladi — oldin nuqtali vergul, keyin vergul.
p.ru: (1) Точка — два предложения. (2) Точка с запятой. (3) Запятая + сочинительный союз (FANBOYS). (4) Подчинение — с 'because', 'although', 'when'. Союзные наречия вроде 'however' и 'nevertheless' требуют схемы '; however,' — точка с запятой до, запятая после.

p.uz: Odatiy fragmentlar: participial ibora ('Having analyzed...'), predlogli boshlanish ('After years of research.') yoki uzilib qolgan nisbiy gap ('Which proved...'). Yechim doim biriktirish: fragmentni tegishli asosiy gapga ulang yoki unga o'z egasi va fe'lini bering.
p.ru: Типичные фрагменты: причастный оборот ('Having analyzed...'), предложное начало ('After years of research.') или оторванное относительное придаточное ('Which proved...'). Решение всегда одно — присоединение: прикрепите фрагмент к главному предложению или дайте ему своё подлежащее и глагол.

quiz.uz: Ikki mustaqil gap faqat vergul bilan — comma splice.
quiz.ru: Два независимых предложения с одной запятой — comma splice.

quiz.uz: Ikki mustaqil gap belgisiz yopishtirilgan — fused run-on.
quiz.ru: Два независимых предложения без знака — слитный run-on.

quiz.uz: Qarama-qarshi ikki mustaqil gap → '; however,' qolipi.
quiz.ru: Два контрастных независимых предложения → схема '; however,'.

quiz.uz: 'After years of painstaking research' — asosiy gapi yo'q → fragment.
quiz.ru: 'After years of painstaking research' — нет главного предложения → фрагмент.

quiz.uz: Ikki mustaqil gap → nuqtali vergul; vergul splice, hech narsa run-on bo'lardi.
quiz.ru: Два независимых предложения → точка с запятой; запятая — splice, ничего — run-on.

quiz.uz: Participial ibora asosiy gapga biriktiriladi — fragment yo'qoladi.
quiz.ru: Причастный оборот присоединяется к главному предложению — фрагмент исчезает.
Два независимых предложения → точка с запятой.

quiz.uz: Faqat participial ibora — ega ham, fe'l ham yo'q → fragment.
quiz.ru: Только причастный оборот — ни подлежащего, ни глагола → фрагмент.
Контраст → '; yet,' — точка с запятой + запятая.

quiz.uz: Ega va asosiy fe'l bor variantgina to'liq gap.
quiz.ru: Только вариант с подлежащим и главным глаголом — полное предложение.

quiz.uz: Mustahkam, lekin baribir yopilgan — qarama-qarshilik → '; nevertheless,'.
quiz.ru: Мост прочный, но всё же закрыт — контраст → '; nevertheless,'.

quiz.uz: 'Which proved...' nonrestrictive nisbiy gap sifatida biriktiriladi — endi fragment emas.
quiz.ru: 'Which proved...' присоединяется как nonrestrictive придаточное — больше не фрагмент.

grammar.title: Modifiers & parallelism
grammar.lead: 'Walking to work, the rain started' — who was walking? Dangling modifiers and broken parallel structures are subtle errors that mark the difference between B2 and C1 writing.

leadTr.uz: 'Walking to work, the rain started' — kim yurayotgan edi? Noto'g'ri bog'langan aniqlovchilar va buzilgan parallel tuzilmalar B2 va C1 yozuvini ajratib turadigan nozik xatolardir.
leadTr.ru: 'Walking to work, the rain started' — кто шёл? Висячие обороты и нарушенный параллелизм — тонкие ошибки, отличающие письмо C1 от B2.

grammar.situation: "Walking to work, the rain started." So the rain was walking to work? The opening phrase grabs the nearest subject — and finds the wrong one. C1 writing is where these ghosts get exorcised.

blocks.h: Dangling modifiers: the doer must follow the comma
p: An opening participial or infinitive phrase ('Returning from the field,...', 'Having examined the patient,...', 'To pass the course,...') silently claims the subject of the main clause as its doer. If that subject did not perform the action, the modifier dangles. Fix it by making the true doer the subject, or by rewriting the phrase as a full clause.
ex: Returning from the field, the team labeled the samples. (the team returned)
Having examined the patient, the doctor made a diagnosis.
To pass the course, students must attend regularly.

blocks.h: Misplaced modifiers: keep them next to what they modify
p: Modifiers attach to the nearest plausible word, so position changes meaning: 'The storm NEARLY destroyed every home' (came close, destroyed none) vs. 'The storm destroyed NEARLY every home' (destroyed most). Phrases behave the same way — 'She served cake on paper plates to the children' puts the cake, not the children, on the plates.
ex: The storm destroyed nearly every home in the neighborhood.
She served cake on paper plates to the children.
Using a high-powered microscope, the scientist observed the samples.

p: Items in a series must share one grammatical shape: all nouns, all adjectives, or all matching verb phrases. 'Talented, dedicated, and works very hard' breaks the pattern — two adjectives and a verb phrase. Repeating a marker word ('her vision, her work ethic, her willingness') makes the parallelism audible.
ex: The CEO was praised for her vision, her work ethic, and her willingness to take risks.
He is talented, dedicated, and hardworking.

p: 'Not only... but also' and 'both... and' must frame grammatically identical pieces: 'not only PREVENTS the disease but also REDUCES its severity.' Comparisons must match like with like: compare Tokyo's population with New York's population — not with New York itself.
ex: The vaccine not only prevents the disease but also reduces its severity.
The policy is both controversial and widely criticized.
Tokyo's population is larger than New York's.

grammar.tip: After any opening phrase with a comma, point at the next noun and ask: 'Did YOU do this?' If it couldn't have, the modifier is dangling. For lists and correlatives, read each item against the same frame word.
examples: Hoping to win the grant, the lab submitted three proposals.
The committee wants a plan that is bold, feasible, and fundable.
The course covers not only theory but also practice.
Her salary is higher than her manager's.

mistakes.x: Having examined the patient, the diagnosis was made.
mistakes.v: Having examined the patient, the doctor made a diagnosis. — the doctor, not the diagnosis, did the examining.

mistakes.x: He is talented, dedicated, and works very hard.
mistakes.v: He is talented, dedicated, and hardworking. — keep all three items adjectives.

mistakes.x: Tokyo's population is larger than New York.
mistakes.v: Tokyo's population is larger than New York's. — compare population with population.

quiz.q: Which version correctly fixes the dangling modifier?
o: The samples, returning from the field, were carefully labeled.
Returning from the field, the samples were carefully labeled by the team.
The team's samples returning from the field were carefully labeled.
Returning from the field, the team carefully labeled the samples.
quiz.e: 'Returning from the field' — who returned? The team. Subject after comma must be 'the team.' B is correct.

quiz.q: Which version is correctly parallel?
o: The CEO was praised for her vision, her work ethic, and her willingness to take bold risks.
The CEO was praised for having vision, her work ethic, and taking bold risks.
The CEO was praised for her vision, her work ethic, and taking bold risks.
The CEO was praised for vision, her work ethic, and that she took bold risks.
quiz.e: B: three parallel noun phrases — 'her vision, her work ethic, her willingness.' All possessive noun phrases. A mixes nouns and a gerund. C and D mix forms.

quiz.q: Which version corrects the dangling modifier 'Having examined the patient, the diagnosis was made'?
o: Having examined the patient, the diagnosis was made.
The patient, having been examined, the diagnosis was made.
A diagnosis was made, having examined the patient.
Having examined the patient, the doctor made a diagnosis.
quiz.e: 'Having examined the patient' — the doctor examined. B: subject after comma = 'the doctor.' Correct.

quiz.q: Which version is NOT correctly parallel?
o: She enjoys reading novels, watching films, and hiking trails.
He is talented, dedicated, and works very hard.
The course covers theory, practice, and application.
The study was comprehensive, rigorous, and well-documented.
quiz.e: B mixes adjectives (talented, dedicated) with a verb phrase (works very hard). Should be: 'talented, dedicated, and hardworking.'

quiz.q: Which placement of 'nearly' gives the meaning that almost all homes were affected?
o: The storm destroyed every home nearly in the neighborhood.
Nearly the storm destroyed every home in the neighborhood.
The storm nearly destroyed every home in the neighborhood.
The storm destroyed nearly every home in the neighborhood.
quiz.e: B: 'nearly every home' — 'nearly' directly modifies 'every home.' A: 'nearly destroyed' means the storm came close to destroying. B is correct for the intended meaning.

quiz.q: Which version uses 'not only...but also' correctly?
o: The vaccine not only preventing the disease but also reduces its severity.
The vaccine not only prevents the disease but also it reduces severity.
The vaccine not only prevents the disease but also reducing its severity.
The vaccine not only prevents the disease but also reduces its severity.
quiz.e: B: 'not only PREVENTS...but also REDUCES' — both base verbs, parallel. A ends with a gerund. C begins with a gerund. D adds 'it' unnecessarily.

quiz.q: Which version corrects the misplaced modifier?
o: On paper plates, she served cake to the children.
She served to the children cake on paper plates.
She served cake on paper plates to the children.
She served cake to the children on paper plates.
quiz.e: 'On paper plates' should modify 'cake' (the cake was on paper plates, not the children). C: 'cake on paper plates to the children' — modifier is adjacent to 'cake.' Correct.

quiz.q: Which version corrects the dangling modifier 'Written during the Great Depression, readers found the novel deeply moving'?
o: Readers found the novel, written during the Great Depression, deeply moving.
Written during the Great Depression, readers found the novel deeply moving.
Written during the Great Depression, the novel was found deeply moving by readers.
The novel, written during the Great Depression, readers found deeply moving.
quiz.e: 'Written during the Great Depression' modifies 'the novel.' C places the modifier immediately after 'the novel' as a nonrestrictive element — correct. B also works. C is cleaner.

quiz.q: Which version makes a correct parallel comparison?
o: Both B and C are correct.
The population of Tokyo is larger than New York's.
The population of Tokyo is larger than New York.
The population of Tokyo is larger than the population of New York.
quiz.e: B (Tokyo's population vs. New York's) and C (Tokyo's population vs. New York's population) both correctly compare population to population. D is correct.

quiz.q: Which correctly fixes the dangling modifier 'To pass the course, regular attendance is required'?
o: Both B and C are correct.
To pass the course, students must attend regularly.
To pass the course, regular attendance is required.
Regular attendance is required to pass the course.
quiz.e: A is a dangling modifier (attendance doesn't pass courses; students do). B fixes the subject. C restructures. Both B and C are correct. D is the answer.

quiz.q: 'The scientist observed the samples using a high-powered microscope.' The modifier 'using a high-powered microscope' is ambiguous. Which revision is clearest?
o: Using a high-powered microscope, the scientist observed the samples.
Using a high-powered microscope, the samples were observed by the scientist.
The scientist, using a high-powered microscope, observed the samples.
Both B and C are correct.
quiz.e: B and C both correctly attach 'using a high-powered microscope' to 'the scientist' (the person using the microscope). Both are clear and grammatically correct. D is the answer.

quiz.q: Which version uses 'both...and' correctly?
o: The policy is both controversial and wide criticism has followed.
The policy is both controversial and widely criticized.
The policy is both controversial and it has been widely criticized.
The policy both is controversial and widely criticized.
quiz.e: B: 'both CONTROVERSIAL and WIDELY CRITICIZED' — both adjective phrases parallel. A mixes adjective and clause. C is awkward. D mixes adjective and clause.

situation.uz: "Walking to work, the rain started." Demak, yomg'ir ishga piyoda ketayotgan ekanmi? Boshlovchi ibora eng yaqin egani o'ziniki qilib oladi — va noto'g'risini topadi. C1 yozuvida ana shu 'sharpalar' tuzatiladi.
situation.ru: «Walking to work, the rain started.» Выходит, дождь шёл на работу пешком? Начальный оборот присваивает себе ближайшее подлежащее — и находит не то. Именно на уровне C1 эти «призраки» изгоняются.

tip.uz: Vergulli boshlovchi iboradan keyin keyingi otga ishora qilib so'rang: 'Buni SEN qildingmi?' Qila olmagan bo'lsa — modifier osilib qolgan. Ro'yxat va korrelativlarda har bir elementni bir xil qolipga solib o'qing.
tip.ru: После любого начального оборота с запятой укажите на следующее существительное и спросите: «Это сделал ТЫ?» Если не мог — модификатор повис. В списках и коррелятивах читайте каждый элемент через одну и ту же рамку.

h.uz: Osilgan modifierlar: verguldan keyin bajaruvchi kelishi kerak
h.ru: Висячие модификаторы: после запятой должен идти деятель

p.uz: Boshlovchi participial yoki infinitive ibora asosiy gapning egasini o'z bajaruvchisi deb biladi. Ega bu harakatni bajarmagan bo'lsa, modifier osilib qoladi. Tuzatish: haqiqiy bajaruvchini ega qiling yoki iborani to'liq gapga aylantiring.
p.ru: Начальный причастный или инфинитивный оборот молча объявляет подлежащее главного предложения своим деятелем. Если подлежащее действие не выполняло — модификатор повисает. Исправление: сделайте настоящего деятеля подлежащим или перепишите оборот полным предложением.

h.uz: Noto'g'ri joylashgan modifierlar: aniqlanayotgan so'z yonida saqlang
h.ru: Смещённые модификаторы: держите их рядом с определяемым словом

p.uz: Modifier eng yaqin mos so'zga yopishadi, shuning uchun o'rin ma'noni o'zgartiradi: 'NEARLY destroyed every home' (deyarli vayron qildi, lekin qilmadi) va 'destroyed NEARLY every home' (deyarli hammasini vayron qildi) — butunlay boshqa gaplar. Iboralar ham xuddi shunday ishlaydi.
p.ru: Модификатор цепляется к ближайшему подходящему слову, поэтому позиция меняет смысл: 'NEARLY destroyed every home' (чуть не разрушил) и 'destroyed NEARLY every home' (разрушил почти все) — совсем разные предложения. Обороты ведут себя так же.

p.uz: Sanashdagi elementlar bitta grammatik shaklda bo'lishi kerak: hammasi ot, hammasi sifat yoki hammasi mos fe'l iborasi. Belgi so'zni takrorlash ('her vision, her work ethic, her willingness') parallelizmni yaqqol qiladi.
p.ru: Элементы перечисления должны иметь одну грамматическую форму: все существительные, все прилагательные или все одинаковые глагольные группы. Повтор опорного слова ('her vision, her work ethic, her willingness') делает параллелизм наглядным.

p.uz: 'Not only... but also' va 'both... and' grammatik jihatdan bir xil bo'laklarni qamrashi shart: 'not only PREVENTS... but also REDUCES...'. Qiyoslashda o'xshash narsalar solishtiriladi: Tokioning aholisi Nyu-Yorkning AHOLISI bilan — Nyu-Yorkning o'zi bilan emas.
p.ru: 'Not only... but also' и 'both... and' должны обрамлять грамматически одинаковые части: 'not only PREVENTS... but also REDUCES...'. В сравнении сопоставляют подобное с подобным: население Токио — с НАСЕЛЕНИЕМ Нью-Йорка, а не с самим городом.

quiz.uz: 'Returning from the field' — kim qaytdi? Jamoa; verguldan keyin 'the team' kelishi kerak.
quiz.ru: 'Returning from the field' — кто вернулся? Команда; после запятой должно идти 'the team'.

quiz.uz: Uchta parallel egalik ot iborasi: 'her vision, her work ethic, her willingness'.
quiz.ru: Три параллельные притяжательные группы: 'her vision, her work ethic, her willingness'.

quiz.uz: Bemorni shifokor ko'rdi → verguldan keyin ega 'the doctor'.
quiz.ru: Пациента осматривал врач → после запятой подлежащее 'the doctor'.

quiz.uz: Ikki sifat + fe'l iborasi — parallelizm buzilgan.
quiz.ru: Два прилагательных + глагольная группа — параллелизм нарушен.

quiz.uz: 'Nearly every home' — 'nearly' to'g'ridan-to'g'ri 'every home' ni aniqlaydi.
'not only PREVENTS... but also REDUCES' — ikkala fe'l parallel.
quiz.ru: 'not only PREVENTS... but also REDUCES' — оба глагола параллельны.

quiz.uz: 'On paper plates' tort yonida turishi kerak — bolalar emas, tort likopchada.
quiz.ru: 'On paper plates' должно стоять рядом с 'cake' — на тарелках торт, а не дети.

quiz.uz: 'Written during the Great Depression' romanni aniqlaydi — modifier 'the novel' yoniga qo'yiladi.
quiz.ru: 'Written during the Great Depression' определяет роман — модификатор ставится рядом с 'the novel'.

quiz.uz: Ikkala variant ham aholini aholi bilan qiyoslaydi — ikkalasi to'g'ri.
quiz.ru: Оба варианта сравнивают население с населением — верны оба.

quiz.uz: Kursdan talabalar o'tadi, davomat emas — ikkala qayta yozuv ham to'g'ri.
quiz.ru: Курс сдают студенты, а не посещаемость — обе переработки верны.

quiz.uz: Ikkala variant ham mikroskopni olimga bog'laydi — ikkalasi aniq va to'g'ri.
quiz.ru: Оба варианта относят микроскоп к учёному — оба ясны и верны.

quiz.uz: 'both CONTROVERSIAL and WIDELY CRITICIZED' — ikkala sifat ibora parallel.
quiz.ru: 'both CONTROVERSIAL and WIDELY CRITICIZED' — обе адъективные группы параллельны.

grammar.title: Words in context
grammar.lead: Advanced texts choose words for precision, not decoration. Use the logic of the passage — contrast, cause, tone — to select the word that fits exactly.

leadTr.uz: Murakkab matnlar so'zni bezak uchun emas, aniqlik uchun tanlaydi. Matn mantig'idan — qarama-qarshilik, sabab, ohang — foydalanib, aynan mos so'zni tanlang.
leadTr.ru: Сложные тексты выбирают слова ради точности, а не украшения. Опирайтесь на логику текста — контраст, причину, тон — чтобы выбрать точное слово.

grammar.situation: "The speaker's tone was measured." Measured — with a ruler? No: in this sentence the word means 'carefully controlled'. Advanced vocabulary questions test the sense a word carries HERE, not its dictionary headline.

p: Most sophisticated words have several senses, and 'as used in the text' questions ask which one is active. The passage always contains the evidence: 'measured' next to 'neither contempt nor enthusiasm' must mean restrained; 'costly' next to 'metabolically expensive' must mean resource-intensive, not pricey.
ex: The speaker's tone was measured — carefully controlled and restrained.
The peacock's tail is a costly signal — requiring significant biological resources.

p: Wrong answers love the most familiar sense of the word: 'measured' = quantified, 'synthesize' = produce chemically, 'harbored' = sheltered a ship, 'articulate' = speak clearly. Substitute the candidate meaning back into the sentence — if it produces nonsense or the wrong register, it is the distractor.
ex: Secondary sources synthesize primary materials — combine them into a coherent whole.
The president harbored reservations — held them privately within himself.
Gift-giving articulates social hierarchies — expresses and gives form to them.

blocks.h: Use the passage's logic: contrast, cause, definition
p: Passages often define the word for you: an appositive ('primary sources — documents produced at the time'), a contrast ('broad support BUT entrenched resistance'), or an elaboration ('austere, stripped of ornamentation'). Read the frame before the options.
Also check intensity: 'tarnished' means damaged, not destroyed; 'tentative' means not yet certain, not temporary. The right answer matches the strength of the original word.
ex: The novelist's prose is austere — severely simple, without decoration.
Her reputation was tarnished — diminished, but not destroyed.
The findings were tentative — not fully committed or certain.

grammar.tip: Treat the tested word as a blank. Read the sentence, predict your own word for the blank, THEN look at the options — the answer closest to your prediction wins, and the flashy dictionary-first sense loses.
examples: Profitability remained elusive — not yet achieved despite record revenues.
Entrenched interests resisted the reform — firmly established and resistant to change.
The canon was codified in the nineteenth century — arranged into a systematic body.
The findings warrant replication — they justify and necessitate it.

mistakes.x: Reading 'The tone was measured' as 'the tone was quantified'.
mistakes.v: 'Measured' here means carefully controlled — the context of restraint, not numbers, decides.

mistakes.x: Reading 'harbored reservations' as 'concealed them from the authorities'.
mistakes.v: 'Harbored' means held privately within oneself — no illegality is implied.

mistakes.x: Choosing 'completely destroyed' for 'tarnished'.
mistakes.v: 'Tarnished' means damaged or diminished — match the word's intensity, not the strongest option.

quiz.q:
Text: 'Critics have questioned whether canonical works of Western literature adequately represent human diversity, or whether the canon merely reflects the prejudices of those who codified it.'

As used in the text, 'codified' most nearly means
o: arranged into a systematic body of rules or standards
quiz.e: The canon was 'codified' — established and systematized into a recognized body of works. 'Codified' = arranged into a formal system or set of standards.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The speaker's tone was measured throughout the debate, conveying neither the contempt her critics expected nor the enthusiasm her supporters hoped for.'

As used in the text, 'measured' most nearly means
quiz.e: The tone was moderate — neither contemptuous nor enthusiastic. 'Measured' here = carefully controlled and restrained. 'Quantified' is a different sense entirely.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The proposed reforms enjoyed broad popular support but faced sustained resistance from entrenched interests in the legislature who stood to lose influence if the changes were implemented.'

As used in the text, 'entrenched' most nearly means
o: firmly established and resistant to change
quiz.e: 'Entrenched interests' = deeply established and resistant to change. They've long held their positions. 'Recently installed' is the opposite meaning.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The novelist's prose style has been described as austere, stripped of ornamentation and reliant on plain declarative sentences that place the weight of meaning on individual words.'

As used in the text, 'austere' most nearly means
quiz.e: 'Austere' prose is stripped of ornamentation — severely simple. B captures this. 'Morally rigorous' applies to people or conduct, not prose style.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The startup's rapid expansion was celebrated, but observers who scrutinized its financial filings noted that profitability remained elusive despite record revenue growth.'

As used in the text, 'elusive' most nearly means
quiz.e: Profitability 'remained elusive' despite efforts — it was not yet obtained. 'Elusive' = difficult to achieve or attain. 'Secretive' is wrong. 'Present in small amounts' is wrong.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The historian carefully distinguished between primary sources — documents produced at the time of the events — and secondary sources, which interpret and synthesize primary materials.'

As used in the text, 'synthesize' most nearly means
o: combine elements into a coherent whole
quiz.e: 'Synthesize primary materials' = combine and integrate them into a unified analysis. The chemistry meaning (produce artificially) doesn't apply in this academic writing context.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The administration's position on the treaty was ambiguous: official statements seemed to support ratification, but unnamed officials suggested the president harbored significant reservations.'

As used in the text, 'harbored' most nearly means
quiz.e: The president 'harbored reservations' = held or maintained them internally, without expressing them publicly. 'Concealed from authorities' implies illegality, which doesn't fit.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The peacock's elaborate tail is described as a 'costly signal' — a feature so metabolically expensive to produce that its very existence demonstrates the fitness of the individual bearing it.'

As used in the text, 'costly' most nearly means
quiz.e: 'Metabolically expensive' is the context — the passage itself clarifies the sense. 'Costly' here means requiring significant biological/metabolic resources, not money.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The scientist's reputation, once sterling, was tarnished by the revelation that several of her most celebrated findings could not be replicated by independent researchers.'

As used in the text, 'tarnished' most nearly means
quiz.e: 'Tarnished reputation' = damaged, made less bright — a metaphor from metal tarnishing. 'Completely destroyed' is too strong; the passage says 'tarnished,' not 'destroyed.'

quiz.q:
Text: 'The committee's findings were tentative, acknowledging that available data was insufficient to support definitive conclusions and calling for further investigation.'

As used in the text, 'tentative' most nearly means
quiz.e: 'Tentative findings' = preliminary, not fully established, open to revision. 'Not fully committed or certain' captures this. 'Intended as temporary' misses the certainty/confidence aspect.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The anthropologist argued that gift-giving in this culture was not merely ceremonial but served to articulate and reinforce complex social hierarchies among participants.'

As used in the text, 'articulate' most nearly means
o: express or give form to something
quiz.e: Gift-giving 'articulates' social hierarchies — expresses and makes them manifest. 'Speak clearly' is the adjective/adverb meaning applied to a person, not to a cultural practice.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The researcher noted that the initial findings were suggestive but not conclusive, warranting replication before they could be incorporated into clinical guidelines.'

As used in the text, 'warranting' most nearly means
quiz.e: The findings 'warrant replication' = require/justify replication before clinical use. 'Legally authorizing' is the legal warranty sense, which doesn't fit an academic context.

situation.uz: "The speaker's tone was measured." Measured — chizg'ich bilan o'lchanganmi? Yo'q: bu gapda so'z 'ehtiyotkorona jilovlangan' degani. Yuqori darajadagi lug'at savollari so'zning SHU YERDAGI ma'nosini tekshiradi, lug'atdagi birinchi ma'nosini emas.
situation.ru: «The speaker's tone was measured.» Measured — измерен линейкой? Нет: в этом предложении слово значит «тщательно сдержанный». Продвинутые вопросы по лексике проверяют смысл слова ЗДЕСЬ, а не заглавное словарное значение.

tip.uz: Tekshirilayotgan so'zni bo'sh joy deb hisoblang. Gapni o'qing, bo'sh joyga o'z so'zingizni bashorat qiling, KEYIN variantlarga qarang — bashoratingizga eng yaqini yutadi, lug'atdagi 'yaltiroq' birinchi ma'no esa yutqazadi.
tip.ru: Считайте проверяемое слово пропуском. Прочитайте предложение, предскажите своё слово для пропуска, ПОТОМ смотрите варианты — побеждает ближайший к вашему прогнозу, а броское первое словарное значение проигрывает.

p.uz: Aksariyat murakkab so'zlarning bir nechta ma'nosi bor, 'as used in the text' savollari qaysi biri faol ekanini so'raydi. Dalil doim matnning o'zida: 'measured' 'neither contempt nor enthusiasm' yonida — demak jilovlangan; 'costly' 'metabolically expensive' yonida — demak resurs talab qiladigan.
p.ru: У большинства сложных слов несколько значений, и вопросы 'as used in the text' спрашивают, какое из них активно. Доказательство всегда в тексте: 'measured' рядом с 'neither contempt nor enthusiasm' — значит сдержанный; 'costly' рядом с 'metabolically expensive' — значит ресурсозатратный.

p.uz: Noto'g'ri javoblar so'zning eng tanish ma'nosini yaxshi ko'radi: 'measured' = o'lchangan, 'synthesize' = kimyoviy ishlab chiqarish, 'articulate' = ravon gapirish. Nomzod ma'noni gapga qaytarib qo'yib ko'ring — bema'nilik chiqsa, bu chalg'ituvchi.
p.ru: Неверные ответы обожают самое привычное значение слова: 'measured' = измеренный, 'synthesize' = синтезировать химически, 'articulate' = чётко говорить. Подставьте значение-кандидат обратно в предложение — если выходит бессмыслица, это дистрактор.

h.uz: Matn mantig'idan foydalaning: qarama-qarshilik, sabab, ta'rif
h.ru: Используйте логику текста: контраст, причина, определение

p.uz: Matn ko'pincha so'zni o'zi ta'riflab beradi: appositive ('primary sources — documents produced at the time'), qarama-qarshilik yoki kengaytma ('austere, stripped of ornamentation'). Variantlardan oldin shu ramkani o'qing.
p.ru: Текст часто сам определяет слово: приложение ('primary sources — documents produced at the time'), контраст или уточнение ('austere, stripped of ornamentation'). Прочитайте эту рамку до вариантов.

p.uz: Kuchni ham tekshiring: 'tarnished' — shikastlangan, vayron qilingan emas; 'tentative' — hali aniq emas, vaqtinchalik emas. To'g'ri javob asl so'zning kuchiga mos keladi.
p.ru: Проверяйте и силу слова: 'tarnished' — повреждённый, а не уничтоженный; 'tentative' — ещё не окончательный, а не временный. Правильный ответ соответствует силе исходного слова.

quiz.uz: Kanon tartibga solingan tizimga aylantirilgan — 'codified' = qoidalar tizimiga keltirilgan.
quiz.ru: Канон превращён в упорядоченную систему — 'codified' = сведён в систему норм.

quiz.uz: Ohang mo''tadil — 'measured' = ehtiyotkorona jilovlangan; 'o'lchangan' boshqa ma'no.
quiz.ru: Тон умеренный — 'measured' = тщательно сдержанный; «измеренный» — другой смысл.

quiz.uz: Bezaklardan xoli uslub — 'austere' = qat'iy sodda, bezaksiz.
quiz.ru: Стиль без украшений — 'austere' = строго простой, без декора.

quiz.uz: Foyda harakatlarga qaramay qo'lga kirmadi — 'elusive' = hali erishilmagan.
quiz.ru: Прибыль не достигнута несмотря на усилия — 'elusive' = ещё не достигнутый.

quiz.uz: 'Synthesize' = elementlarni yaxlit butunlikka birlashtirish; kimyoviy ma'no mos emas.
quiz.ru: 'Synthesize' = соединять элементы в связное целое; химический смысл не подходит.
'Harbored' = держал внутри себя, не выражая публично.

quiz.uz: Matnning o'zi izohlaydi: 'metabolically expensive' — biologik resurs talab qiladigan.
quiz.ru: Текст сам поясняет: 'metabolically expensive' — требующий биологических ресурсов.

quiz.uz: 'Tentative' = dastlabki, hali aniq emas, qayta ko'rishga ochiq.
quiz.ru: 'Tentative' = предварительный, ещё не окончательный, открытый для пересмотра.

quiz.uz: Sovg'a berish ierarxiyalarni ifodalaydi — 'articulate' = ifodalash, shakl berish.
quiz.ru: Дарение выражает иерархии — 'articulate' = выражать, придавать форму.

quiz.uz: Natijalar takrorlashni talab qiladi — 'warranting' = asoslaydigan, zarur qiladigan.
quiz.ru: Результаты требуют репликации — 'warranting' = обосновывающий, делающий необходимым.

grammar.title: Concision & precision
grammar.lead: Strong English says more with fewer words. Spot redundancy, cut empty phrases, and keep the sentence's full meaning intact.

leadTr.uz: Kuchli ingliz tili kam so'z bilan ko'p ma'no beradi. Ortiqchalikni toping, bo'sh iboralarni olib tashlang, gapning to'liq ma'nosini saqlang.
leadTr.ru: Сильный английский говорит больше меньшим числом слов. Находите избыточность, убирайте пустые фразы, сохраняя полный смысл.

grammar.situation: "The council decided to postpone and delay the vote until a later date in the future." Cross out everything the sentence already said once: 'The council decided to postpone the vote.' Nothing was lost — nine words were.

p: English test sentences love doubled synonyms: 'postpone and delay', 'unexpected and surprising', 'document and record', 'important and significant', 'unique and one-of-a-kind'. Each pair carries one idea — keep one word, cut the twin.
ex: Scientists made a surprising discovery. (not 'unexpected and surprising')
Researchers should document all observations. (not 'document and record')
The findings were significant. (not 'important and significant')

p: Multi-word constructions often collapse into one word with no loss: 'due to the fact that' → 'because'; 'in the event that' → 'if'; 'has the ability to' → 'can'; 'help facilitate the improvement of' → 'help improve'. Formal does not mean wordy — the compressed version is usually MORE formal.
ex: Because the medication can cause side effects, patients should consult their doctors.
If the experiment produces unexpected results, document them.
The new policy will help improve working conditions.

blocks.h: Cut what the sentence already implies
p: 'Was able to successfully complete' — completing IS succeeding, and doing it proves ability: 'completed' says everything. Likewise 'crossed the finish line at the end of the race', 'future advancement', 'ancient ruins which were old'. If deleting a phrase changes nothing, the phrase was noise.
ex: The athlete completed the marathon in under three hours.
The exhausted runners crossed the finish line.
The findings were significant for the advancement of the field.

blocks.h: One structural trap: 'the reason is that'
p: 'The reason... was because' doubles the cause marker — 'because' already means 'for the reason that'. Formal English requires 'the reason... was THAT': 'The reason the project failed was that the team lacked resources.' Or simpler still: 'The project failed because the team lacked resources.'
ex: The reason the project failed was that the team lacked resources.
The project failed because the team lacked resources.

grammar.tip: For every candidate revision, run the deletion test: remove the suspect words and reread. If the meaning is fully intact, the shorter version is the answer — concision questions almost never reward added words.
examples: The board approved the merger. (not 'made the decision to approve')
The design incorporates several unique features.
If demand rises, prices will follow.
The report is significant for the field's advancement.

mistakes.x: The reason the launch slipped was because the vendor was late.
mistakes.v: The reason the launch slipped was that the vendor was late. — 'the reason... was because' doubles the cause marker.

mistakes.x: The athlete was able to successfully complete the race.
mistakes.v: The athlete completed the race. — 'was able to' and 'successfully' are implied by 'completed'.

mistakes.x: We will revisit this at a later date in the future.
mistakes.v: We will revisit this later. — 'a later date' and 'in the future' say the same thing.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The council decided to postpone and delay the vote until a later date in the future.'

Which choice most effectively revises the sentence to eliminate unnecessary repetition?
o: The council decided to postpone the vote.
The council decided to later postpone and delay the vote.
The council decided to postpone and delay the vote to a future date.
The council decided to postpone and delay the vote until a later date in the future.
quiz.e: 'Postpone' and 'delay' are synonyms (redundant pair). 'Until a later date in the future' — 'later date' and 'in the future' both mean the same thing, and 'postpone' already implies moving to a future time. B keeps only the essential meaning.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The reason the project failed was because the team lacked adequate resources.'

Which choice most effectively revises the underlined portion?
o: The reason the project failed was that the team lacked adequate resources.
The reason for which the project failed was because the team lacked in adequate resources.
The reason the project failed was because the team lacked adequate resources.
The project failed due to the fact that there was a lack of adequate resources on the team.
quiz.e: 'The reason was because' is redundant — 'because' already introduces a reason. The correct form is 'the reason was that.' B makes this correction. A keeps the error. C adds 'due to the fact that' (wordy). D is grammatically awkward and keeps 'because.'

quiz.q:
Text: 'The completely exhausted marathon runners finally crossed the finish line at the end of the race.'

Which revision most effectively eliminates redundancy?
o: The marathon runners, who were exhausted, finally crossed the finish line at the end of the race.
The completely exhausted marathon runners finally crossed the finish line at the end of the race.
The completely exhausted and very tired marathon runners finally crossed the finish line at the end of the race.
The exhausted marathon runners crossed the finish line.
quiz.e: 'Completely exhausted' — 'completely' is a meaningless intensifier (you're either exhausted or you're not). 'At the end of the race' is implied by 'crossing the finish line.' B removes both. A keeps both. C adds 'and very tired' (redundant with exhausted). D keeps 'at the end of the race.'

quiz.q:
Text: 'Due to the fact that the medication has the ability to cause serious side effects, patients should consult their doctors.'

Which revision is most concise without losing meaning?
o: Because the medication can cause serious side effects, patients should consult their doctors.
Due to the fact that the medication has the ability to cause serious side effects, patients should consult their doctors.
As a result of the fact that the medication possesses the ability to cause serious side effects, patients should consult with their doctors.
The medication has the ability to cause serious side effects, which is the reason why patients should consult their doctors.
quiz.e: 'Due to the fact that' → 'because' | 'has the ability to' → 'can.' B applies both concisions. A keeps both wordy phrases. C replaces one wordy phrase with an even wordier one. D keeps 'has the ability to' and adds 'which is the reason why.'

quiz.q:
Text: 'Scientists made an unexpected and surprising discovery about the origins of the universe.'

Which revision eliminates the redundancy?
o: Scientists made a surprising discovery about the origins of the universe.
Scientists made an unexpected and surprising discovery about the origins of the universe.
Scientists made a very unexpected discovery that was surprising about the origins of the universe.
Scientists made a discovery that was both unexpected and also surprising about the origins of the universe.
quiz.e: 'Unexpected' and 'surprising' are synonyms when describing a discovery — a redundant pair. B keeps just 'surprising.' A keeps both. C adds 'very' and rephrases awkwardly. D adds 'both...and also' (more words, same redundancy).

quiz.q:
Text: 'The new policy will help facilitate the improvement of working conditions for employees at the company.'

Which is the most concise revision?
o: The new policy has the ability to help in the facilitation of improvements to employee working conditions.
The new policy will facilitate the improvement and betterment of working conditions for all employees at the company.
The new policy will help improve working conditions for employees.
The new policy will help facilitate the improvement of working conditions for employees at the company.
quiz.e: 'Help facilitate the improvement of' → 'help improve' (three words become two). 'At the company' is contextually implied when talking about a company policy. B is maximally concise. A is wordy. C adds 'betterment' (redundant with improvement). D is much wordier.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The ancient ruins, which were old and dated back thousands of years, attracted tourists from around the world.'

Which revision is most effective?
o: The ancient ruins, which were old and dated back thousands of years, attracted tourists from around the world.
The ancient ruins, which dated back thousands of years, attracted tourists from around the world.
The old, ancient ruins, which were thousands of years old, attracted tourists from around the world.
The ruins, which were ancient and dated back many thousands of years into the past, attracted tourists from around the world.
quiz.e: 'Ancient ruins which were old' — 'ancient' and 'old' are redundant. 'Dated back thousands of years' shows age, making 'which were old' doubly redundant. B removes 'which were old' and 'ancient' (keeping 'ancient' in the main noun is actually better than the clause). A keeps all redundancies. C has 'old, ancient' (redundant pair). D has 'many thousands of years into the past' ('into the past' is redundant with 'dated back').

quiz.q:
Text: 'In the event that the experiment produces unexpected results, researchers should document and record all observations.'

Which revision is most concise?
o: In the event that the experiment produces unexpected results, researchers need to make documentation and recordings of all observations.
Should the experiment produce results that are unexpected in nature, researchers ought to document and record their observations.
If the experiment produces unexpected results, researchers should document all observations.
In the event that the experiment produces unexpected results, researchers should document and record all observations.
quiz.e: 'In the event that' → 'if' (4 words → 1). 'Document and record' — redundant pair; 'document' includes recording. B applies both concisions. A keeps both. C adds 'in nature' and 'ought to document and record.' D keeps 'in the event that' and adds 'make documentation and recordings.'

quiz.q:
Text: 'The athlete was able to successfully complete the marathon in under three hours.'

Which revision eliminates the redundancy?
o: The athlete was able to and did successfully complete the marathon in under three hours.
The athlete was able to successfully complete the marathon in under three hours.
The athlete completed the marathon in under three hours.
The athlete was successful in being able to complete the marathon in a time under three hours.
quiz.e: 'Was able to' and 'successfully' are both implied by 'complete' — if you complete something, you were able to do it and you did it successfully. B strips both. A keeps both. C adds 'in a time under' (wordy). D adds 'and did.'

quiz.q:
Text: 'The report's findings were both important and significant to the future advancement of the field.'

Which is the most effective revision?
o: The report's findings were significant for the advancement of the field.
The report's findings were important, significant, and consequential for the future of the field.
The report's findings were both important and significant to the future advancement of the field.
The report's findings were very important and quite significant for the future advancement of the field.
quiz.e: 'Important and significant' — redundant pair. 'Future advancement' — 'advancement' implies moving forward (future is redundant). B removes the redundant pair and 'future.' A keeps both. C adds a third synonym ('consequential'). D adds intensifiers ('very,' 'quite').

quiz.q:
Text: 'The new bridge design incorporates several different features that are unique and one-of-a-kind.'

Which revision is most effective?
o: The new bridge design incorporates features that are unique, one-of-a-kind, and unlike any other.
The new bridge design, which is new, incorporates several different and varied unique features.
The new bridge design incorporates several unique features.
The new bridge design incorporates several different features that are unique and one-of-a-kind.
quiz.e: 'Different' is redundant with 'several' (several already implies differences). 'Unique' and 'one-of-a-kind' are synonyms. 'That are' is a wordy relative clause replaceable by an adjective. B strips all: 'several unique features.' A keeps all redundancies. C triples the synonyms. D adds 'which is new' (already in 'new bridge design') and 'different and varied.'

quiz.q:
Text: 'The novel is widely considered one of the greatest and most celebrated achievements in American literature.'

Which choice eliminates the redundancy most effectively?
o: one of the greatest, most celebrated, and most acclaimed achievements in American literature
one of the greatest achievements in American literature
one of the very greatest and widely celebrated achievements in American literature
one of the greatest and most celebrated achievements in American literature
quiz.e: 'Greatest' and 'most celebrated' overlap in meaning as superlative praise — using both is redundant. B keeps only 'greatest.' A keeps both. C adds a third ('most acclaimed'). D adds 'very' and 'widely.'

situation.uz: "The council decided to postpone and delay the vote until a later date in the future." Gap bir marta aytgan hamma narsani o'chiring: 'The council decided to postpone the vote.' Ma'no yo'qolmadi — to'qqizta so'z yo'qoldi.
situation.ru: «The council decided to postpone and delay the vote until a later date in the future.» Вычеркните всё, что предложение уже сказало один раз: 'The council decided to postpone the vote.' Смысл не потерян — потеряны девять слов.

tip.uz: Har bir taklif qilingan tahrir uchun o'chirish testini o'tkazing: shubhali so'zlarni olib tashlab qayta o'qing. Ma'no to'liq saqlansa — qisqa varianti javob; concision savollari deyarli hech qachon qo'shimcha so'zlarni mukofotlamaydi.
tip.ru: Для каждой предложенной правки проведите тест удаления: уберите подозрительные слова и перечитайте. Если смысл полностью цел — ответ короче; вопросы на лаконичность почти никогда не вознаграждают добавленные слова.

p.uz: Test gaplari ikkilangan sinonimlarni yaxshi ko'radi: 'postpone and delay', 'unexpected and surprising', 'document and record', 'unique and one-of-a-kind'. Har bir juftlik bitta fikrni tashiydi — bittasini qoldiring, egizagini o'chiring.
p.ru: Тестовые предложения любят удвоенные синонимы: 'postpone and delay', 'unexpected and surprising', 'document and record', 'unique and one-of-a-kind'. Каждая пара несёт одну мысль — оставьте одно слово, уберите близнеца.

p.uz: Ko'p so'zli qurilmalar ko'pincha bitta so'zga yig'iladi: 'due to the fact that' → 'because'; 'in the event that' → 'if'; 'has the ability to' → 'can'. Rasmiylik ko'p so'zlilik degani emas — siqilgan variant odatda RASMIYROQ.
p.ru: Многословные конструкции часто сворачиваются в одно слово: 'due to the fact that' → 'because'; 'in the event that' → 'if'; 'has the ability to' → 'can'. Формальность — не многословие: сжатый вариант обычно ФОРМАЛЬНЕЕ.

h.ru: Уберите то, что предложение уже подразумевает

p.uz: 'Was able to successfully complete' — tugatishning o'zi muvaffaqiyat va qobiliyat isboti: 'completed' hammasini aytadi. Xuddi shunday 'future advancement', 'ancient ruins which were old'. Iborani o'chirish hech narsani o'zgartirmasa — u shovqin edi.
p.ru: 'Was able to successfully complete' — само завершение и есть успех и доказательство способности: 'completed' говорит всё. Так же 'future advancement', 'ancient ruins which were old'. Если удаление оборота ничего не меняет — это был шум.

h.uz: Bitta tuzilma tuzog'i: 'the reason is that'
h.ru: Одна структурная ловушка: 'the reason is that'

p.uz: 'The reason... was because' sabab belgisini ikkilantiradi — 'because' allaqachon 'shu sababdan' degani. Rasmiy inglizcha 'the reason... was THAT' ni talab qiladi; yoki yanada sodda: 'The project failed because...'.
p.ru: 'The reason... was because' удваивает показатель причины — 'because' уже значит «по той причине, что». Формальный английский требует 'the reason... was THAT'; или ещё проще: 'The project failed because...'.

quiz.uz: 'Postpone' va 'delay' — sinonimlar; 'later date in the future' ham takror — faqat mohiyat qoladi.
quiz.ru: 'Postpone' и 'delay' — синонимы; 'later date in the future' тоже повтор — остаётся только суть.

quiz.uz: 'The reason was because' — takror; to'g'ri shakl: 'the reason was that'.
quiz.ru: 'The reason was because' — избыточно; правильная форма: 'the reason was that'.

quiz.uz: 'Completely' — bo'sh kuchaytirgich; 'at the end of the race' marra chizig'ida yotadi — ikkalasi o'chadi.
quiz.ru: 'Completely' — пустой усилитель; 'at the end of the race' уже в финишной черте — оба убираются.

quiz.uz: 'Due to the fact that' → 'because'; 'has the ability to' → 'can'.
quiz.ru: 'Due to the fact that' → 'because'; 'has the ability to' → 'can'.

quiz.uz: 'Help facilitate the improvement of' → 'help improve'; 'at the company' kontekstdan ma'lum.
quiz.ru: 'Help facilitate the improvement of' → 'help improve'; 'at the company' ясно из контекста.

quiz.uz: 'Ancient' bilan 'old' takror; yoshni 'dated back thousands of years' ko'rsatib turibdi.
quiz.ru: 'Ancient' и 'old' — повтор; возраст уже показывает 'dated back thousands of years'.

quiz.uz: 'In the event that' → 'if'; 'document and record' — takroriy juftlik.
quiz.ru: 'In the event that' → 'if'; 'document and record' — избыточная пара.

quiz.uz: 'Was able to' va 'successfully' — 'completed' ichida allaqachon bor.
quiz.ru: 'Was able to' и 'successfully' уже содержатся в 'completed'.

quiz.uz: 'Important and significant' — sinonim juftlik; 'future advancement' dagi 'future' ortiqcha.
quiz.ru: 'Important and significant' — пара синонимов; 'future' в 'future advancement' лишнее.

quiz.uz: 'Several different', 'unique and one-of-a-kind', 'that are' — hammasi qisqaradi: 'several unique features'.
quiz.ru: 'Several different', 'unique and one-of-a-kind', 'that are' — всё сжимается до 'several unique features'.

quiz.uz: 'Greatest' va 'most celebrated' ma'no jihatdan ustma-ust tushadi — 'greatest' yetarli.
quiz.ru: 'Greatest' и 'most celebrated' пересекаются по смыслу — достаточно 'greatest'.

grammar.title: Run-Ons & Comma Splices
grammar.lead: A RUN-ON sentence occurs when two independent clauses are joined without any punctuation or connecting word. A COMMA SPLICE is a specific type of run-on where only a comma (no conjunction) joins two independent clauses. Both are errors the exam tests directly. The four ways to fix a run-on or comma splice: (1) Add a PERIOD — make two sentences. (2) Add a SEMICOLON between the clauses. (3) Add a COMMA + FANBOYS (for, and, nor, but, or, yet, so). (4) Add a SUBORDINATING CONJUNCTION (although, because, since, while, when, after, before, if, unless) to make one clause dependent.

leadTr.uz: RUN-ON gap — ikkita mustaqil gap hech qanday tinish belgisi yoki bog'lovchisiz qo'shilganda paydo bo'ladi. COMMA SPLICE — run-onning bir turi: ikkita mustaqil gapni faqat vergul (bog'lovchisiz) bog'laydi. Ikkalasi ham imtihonda to'g'ridan-to'g'ri tekshiriladigan xatolar. Run-on yoki comma splice'ni tuzatishning to'rt yo'li: (1) NUQTA qo'ying — ikkita gap qiling. (2) Gaplar orasiga NUQTALI VERGUL qo'ying. (3) VERGUL + FANBOYS (for, and, nor, but, or, yet, so) qo'shing. (4) ERGASHTIRUVCHI BOG'LOVCHI (although, because, since, while, when, after, before, if, unless) qo'shib, bir gapni ergash gapga aylantiring.
leadTr.ru: RUN-ON — это два независимых предложения, соединённые без знаков препинания и без союза. COMMA SPLICE — разновидность run-on, где два независимых предложения соединяет только запятая (без союза). Обе ошибки экзамен проверяет напрямую. Четыре способа исправления: (1) ТОЧКА — сделать два предложения. (2) ТОЧКА С ЗАПЯТОЙ между частями. (3) ЗАПЯТАЯ + FANBOYS (for, and, nor, but, or, yet, so). (4) ПОДЧИНИТЕЛЬНЫЙ СОЮЗ (although, because, since, while, when, after, before, if, unless), делающий одну часть придаточной.

p: RECOGNIZING THE ERROR: the key skill is identifying whether each clause before and after the connection point could stand alone as a sentence. 'The study was flawed, the researchers retracted it' — test each part: 'The study was flawed' ✓ complete. 'The researchers retracted it' ✓ complete. Two complete sentences joined by a comma only = comma splice. On the exam, answer choices will offer different punctuation options and sometimes different connecting words. Always check that the chosen connector is appropriate for the relationship between the ideas.

CHOOSING THE RIGHT FIX: not all fixes are equally good. The connection word signals the relationship. 'The experiment failed; however, the data was valuable' (contrast). 'The experiment failed because the temperature was too high' (cause). 'The experiment failed, but the data was valuable' (contrast with FANBOYS). The exam sometimes presents multiple grammatically valid options — in that case, choose the one that best reflects the logical relationship between the two ideas as expressed in context.
Run-on: [clause][clause] — no connector at all
Comma splice: [clause], [clause] — comma alone, no conjunction
Fix 1: Period → two sentences | Fix 2: Semicolon
Fix 3: Comma + FANBOYS | Fix 4: Subordinating conjunction
Subordinating conjunctions: although, because, since, while, when, if, unless, after
Test each side: can it stand alone? If yes × 2 → must connect properly
Choose connector that fits the LOGICAL relationship (contrast/cause/concession)

quiz.q:
Text: 'The medication effectively reduced inflammation[___] it caused significant liver damage in long-term users.'

Which choice correctly and most logically completes the text?
quiz.e: A ('; however,') correctly uses a semicolon + conjunctive adverb showing contrast. B (because) would make it a cause-effect — 'reduced inflammation because it caused damage' — illogical. C has no connector (run-on). D (and) adds without contrasting.

quiz.q: Which version is a run-on (fused sentence)?
o: The study lasted three years, yet it produced inconclusive results.
The study lasted three years; it produced inconclusive results.
The study lasted three years it produced inconclusive results.
Although the study lasted three years, it produced inconclusive results.
quiz.e: C has two independent clauses with NO connector and NO punctuation — a fused run-on. A (comma + yet) is correct. B (semicolon) is correct. D (subordinating conjunction) is correct.

quiz.q:
Text: 'Researchers had expected a gradual decline in the population[___] the collapse happened suddenly and without warning.'

Which choice most effectively completes the text?
quiz.e: B ('; instead,') uses semicolon + 'instead' to show the contrast precisely. A (', and') just adds, missing the contrast. C (because) creates an illogical cause. D creates a run-on.

p.uz: XATONI TANISH: asosiy ko'nikma — bog'lanish nuqtasidan oldingi va keyingi qism mustaqil gap bo'la oladimi, aniqlash. 'The study was flawed, the researchers retracted it' — har qismni tekshiring: 'The study was flawed' ✓ to'liq. 'The researchers retracted it' ✓ to'liq. Faqat vergul bilan qo'shilgan ikki to'liq gap = comma splice. Imtihonda javob variantlari turli tinish belgilari va ba'zan turli bog'lovchi so'zlarni taklif qiladi. Tanlangan bog'lovchi g'oyalar orasidagi munosabatga mos kelishini har doim tekshiring.
p.ru: РАСПОЗНАВАНИЕ ОШИБКИ: ключевой навык — определить, может ли каждая часть до и после точки соединения стоять как отдельное предложение. 'The study was flawed, the researchers retracted it' — проверяем: 'The study was flawed' ✓ полное. 'The researchers retracted it' ✓ полное. Два полных предложения только с запятой = comma splice. На экзамене варианты предлагают разную пунктуацию и иногда разные связки. Всегда проверяйте, что выбранный коннектор соответствует отношению между идеями.

p.uz: TO'G'RI TUZATISHNI TANLASH: hamma tuzatishlar bir xil yaxshi emas. Bog'lovchi so'z munosabatni bildiradi. 'The experiment failed; however, the data was valuable' (qarama-qarshilik). 'The experiment failed because the temperature was too high' (sabab). 'The experiment failed, but the data was valuable' (FANBOYS bilan qarama-qarshilik). Imtihon ba'zan bir nechta grammatik jihatdan to'g'ri variant beradi — bunda ikki g'oya orasidagi mantiqiy munosabatni kontekstga ko'ra eng yaxshi aks ettiruvchisini tanlang.
p.ru: ВЫБОР ПРАВИЛЬНОГО ИСПРАВЛЕНИЯ: не все исправления одинаково хороши. Связующее слово сигнализирует об отношении. 'The experiment failed; however, the data was valuable' (контраст). 'The experiment failed because the temperature was too high' (причина). 'The experiment failed, but the data was valuable' (контраст с FANBOYS). Иногда экзамен даёт несколько грамматически верных вариантов — тогда выбирайте тот, что лучше всего отражает логическую связь идей в контексте.

p.uz: Run-on: [gap][gap] — hech qanday bog'lovchi yo'q
p.ru: Run-on: [часть][часть] — вообще без связки

p.uz: Comma splice: [gap], [gap] — faqat vergul, bog'lovchisiz
p.ru: Comma splice: [часть], [часть] — только запятая, без союза

p.uz: 1-tuzatish: Nuqta → ikkita gap | 2-tuzatish: Nuqtali vergul
p.ru: Исправление 1: точка → два предложения | Исправление 2: точка с запятой

p.uz: 3-tuzatish: Vergul + FANBOYS | 4-tuzatish: Ergashtiruvchi bog'lovchi
p.ru: Исправление 3: запятая + FANBOYS | Исправление 4: подчинительный союз

p.uz: Ergashtiruvchi bog'lovchilar: although, because, since, while, when, if, unless, after
p.ru: Подчинительные союзы: although, because, since, while, when, if, unless, after

p.uz: Har tomonni tekshiring: mustaqil tura oladimi? Ikkalasi ham ha bo'lsa → to'g'ri bog'lash shart
p.ru: Проверьте каждую часть: стоит ли отдельно? Если да × 2 → нужна правильная связка

p.uz: MANTIQIY munosabatga (qarama-qarshilik/sabab/yon berish) mos bog'lovchini tanlang
p.ru: Выбирайте коннектор по ЛОГИЧЕСКОЙ связи (контраст/причина/уступка)

quiz.uz: Nuqtali vergul + 'however' qarama-qarshilikni to'g'ri ko'rsatadi; 'because' mantiqsiz sabab yaratadi.
quiz.ru: Точка с запятой + 'however' верно передаёт контраст; 'because' создало бы нелогичную причину.

quiz.uz: Ikkita mustaqil gap bog'lovchisiz va tinish belgisisiz — fused run-on.
quiz.ru: Два независимых предложения без связки и пунктуации — fused run-on.

quiz.uz: '; instead,' kutilgan va yuz bergan narsa orasidagi qarama-qarshilikni aniq ifodalaydi.
quiz.ru: '; instead,' точно передаёт контраст между ожиданием и случившимся.

grammar.title: Fragments — Recognizing & Fixing Incomplete Sentences
grammar.lead: A FRAGMENT is a group of words that lacks a subject, a main verb, or both — it cannot stand alone as a complete sentence. The exam tests three types of fragments: (1) MISSING SUBJECT: 'Discovered a new species in the rainforest.' (who discovered?) (2) MISSING VERB or only a PARTICIPLE: 'The researchers studying the effects of sleep deprivation.' (studying is a participle, not a main verb — no action is completed). (3) DEPENDENT CLAUSE ALONE: 'Although the results were promising.' (begins with a subordinating conjunction but has no main clause).

leadTr.uz: FRAGMENT — ega, asosiy fe'l yoki ikkalasi ham yetishmaydigan so'zlar guruhi; u mustaqil gap bo'la olmaydi. Imtihon fragmentning uch turini tekshiradi: (1) EGA YO'Q: 'Discovered a new species in the rainforest.' (kim kashf qildi?) (2) FE'L YO'Q yoki faqat SIFATDOSH bor: 'The researchers studying the effects of sleep deprivation.' (studying — sifatdosh, asosiy fe'l emas — harakat tugallanmagan). (3) YOLG'IZ ERGASH GAP: 'Although the results were promising.' (ergashtiruvchi bog'lovchi bilan boshlanadi, lekin bosh gap yo'q).
leadTr.ru: FRAGMENT — группа слов без подлежащего, основного глагола или того и другого; она не может стоять как полное предложение. Экзамен проверяет три типа фрагментов: (1) НЕТ ПОДЛЕЖАЩЕГО: 'Discovered a new species in the rainforest.' (кто открыл?) (2) НЕТ ГЛАГОЛА или только ПРИЧАСТИЕ: 'The researchers studying the effects of sleep deprivation.' (studying — причастие, не основной глагол — действие не завершено). (3) ПРИДАТОЧНОЕ ОТДЕЛЬНО: 'Although the results were promising.' (начинается с подчинительного союза, но без главного предложения).

p: IDENTIFYING FRAGMENTS: ask two questions. (1) Is there a subject? (2) Is there a complete verb — not just a participle (-ing, -ed without a helping verb) or an infinitive? 'Running through the park' has a subject? No. Fragment. 'The team running through the park' has a verb? No — 'running' is a participle. Fragment. 'The team was running through the park' — subject (team) + complete verb (was running). Sentence. On the exam, answer choices that create fragments are always wrong.

FIXING FRAGMENTS: (1) Add the missing subject or verb. (2) Attach the fragment to an adjacent sentence. (3) Remove the subordinating conjunction to make the dependent clause independent. 'Although the results were promising. Researchers continued.' → 'Although the results were promising, researchers continued.' On the exam, fragments usually appear as answer choices that begin with participial phrases or dependent clauses that are cut off from the main sentence.
Fragment test: does it have a SUBJECT and a complete MAIN VERB?
-ing alone is NOT a complete verb: 'The team working...' = fragment
Dependent clause alone = fragment: 'Because the data showed...' alone = fragment
Fix: attach to adjacent clause or add missing subject/verb
Participial phrase opener: '[Participle phrase], SUBJECT VERB' = complete sentence
Never choose an answer that creates a fragment
Infinitives (to + verb) are NOT main verbs: 'To solve the problem' = fragment

quiz.q: Which of the following is a sentence fragment?
o: The committee approved the new proposal unanimously.
Having reviewed all the evidence carefully.
The researchers published their findings last month.
Although the trial was short, the results were significant.
quiz.e: B — 'Having reviewed all the evidence carefully' — has no subject and no main verb. 'Having reviewed' is a participial phrase. It cannot stand alone. A, C, and D all have subjects and complete verbs.

quiz.q: Which version correctly fixes the fragment?
o: Because the satellite lost communication. Mission control improvised a solution.
Because the satellite lost communication, mission control improvised a solution.
Because the satellite lost communication; mission control improvised a solution.
Because the satellite lost communication and mission control improvised a solution.
quiz.e: A has a fragment ('Because the satellite lost communication' alone) followed by a separate sentence. B correctly attaches the dependent clause to the main clause with a comma. C incorrectly uses a semicolon after a dependent clause. D creates a run-on with unclear structure.

quiz.q: Which version is a complete sentence (not a fragment)?
o: The professor, having spent thirty years studying migration patterns.
Having spent thirty years studying migration patterns, the professor published her definitive account.
Having spent thirty years studying migration patterns.
The professor spending thirty years studying migration patterns.
quiz.e: B: 'Having spent thirty years...' is an introductory participial phrase, followed by 'the professor published her definitive account' (subject + complete verb). It is a complete sentence. A has no main verb after 'the professor.' C is only the participial phrase. D has no main verb.

quiz.q:
A student writes: 'Climate change poses significant risks to coastal communities. Particularly those in low-lying areas vulnerable to storm surges and sea-level rise.'

The second sentence is a fragment. Which is the best fix?
o: Climate change poses significant risks to coastal communities; particularly those in low-lying areas.
Climate change poses significant risks to coastal communities, particularly those in low-lying areas vulnerable to storm surges and sea-level rise.
Climate change poses significant risks. To coastal communities particularly those in low-lying areas.
Climate change poses significant risks to coastal communities. Those are in low-lying areas vulnerable.
quiz.e: B attaches the fragment to the preceding sentence with a comma, creating one complete sentence. A uses a semicolon before a fragment. C creates two fragments. D changes meaning and is still awkward.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The ancient temple [___] for over two thousand years before archaeologists uncovered it in 1987.'

Which choice makes this a complete sentence?
quiz.e: Subject = 'The ancient temple,' verb = 'stood.' Complete sentence. A ('standing') = participial — no complete verb. B ('which stood') = relative clause — 'which' makes it dependent. D ('having stood') = participial — no complete verb.

p.uz: FRAGMENTNI ANIQLASH: ikki savol bering. (1) Ega bormi? (2) To'liq fe'l bormi — yordamchi fe'lsiz sifatdosh (-ing, -ed) yoki infinitiv emas? 'Running through the park' — ega bormi? Yo'q. Fragment. 'The team running through the park' — fe'l bormi? Yo'q — 'running' sifatdosh. Fragment. 'The team was running through the park' — ega (team) + to'liq fe'l (was running). Gap. Imtihonda fragment hosil qiladigan javob variantlari har doim noto'g'ri.
p.ru: ВЫЯВЛЕНИЕ ФРАГМЕНТОВ: задайте два вопроса. (1) Есть подлежащее? (2) Есть полный глагол — а не просто причастие (-ing, -ed без вспомогательного) или инфинитив? 'Running through the park' — подлежащее есть? Нет. Фрагмент. 'The team running through the park' — глагол есть? Нет — 'running' причастие. Фрагмент. 'The team was running through the park' — подлежащее (team) + полный глагол (was running). Предложение. На экзамене варианты, создающие фрагмент, всегда неверны.

p.uz: FRAGMENTNI TUZATISH: (1) Yetishmayotgan ega yoki fe'lni qo'shing. (2) Fragmentni qo'shni gapga qo'shing. (3) Ergashtiruvchi bog'lovchini olib tashlab, ergash gapni mustaqil qiling. 'Although the results were promising. Researchers continued.' → 'Although the results were promising, researchers continued.' Imtihonda fragmentlar odatda sifatdoshli ibora yoki bosh gapdan uzilgan ergash gap bilan boshlanadigan javob variantlari sifatida keladi.
p.ru: ИСПРАВЛЕНИЕ ФРАГМЕНТОВ: (1) Добавьте недостающее подлежащее или глагол. (2) Присоедините фрагмент к соседнему предложению. (3) Уберите подчинительный союз, сделав придаточное независимым. 'Although the results were promising. Researchers continued.' → 'Although the results were promising, researchers continued.' На экзамене фрагменты обычно появляются как варианты, начинающиеся с причастных оборотов или придаточных, оторванных от главного предложения.

p.uz: Fragment testi: EGA va to'liq ASOSIY FE'L bormi?
p.ru: Тест на фрагмент: есть ли ПОДЛЕЖАЩЕЕ и полный ОСНОВНОЙ ГЛАГОЛ?

p.uz: Yolg'iz -ing to'liq fe'l EMAS: 'The team working...' = fragment
p.ru: -ing в одиночку — НЕ полный глагол: 'The team working...' = фрагмент

p.uz: Yolg'iz ergash gap = fragment: 'Because the data showed...' o'zi = fragment
p.ru: Придаточное отдельно = фрагмент: 'Because the data showed...' само по себе = фрагмент

p.uz: Tuzatish: qo'shni gapga biriktiring yoki yetishmayotgan ega/fe'lni qo'shing
p.ru: Исправление: присоедините к соседнему предложению или добавьте подлежащее/глагол

p.uz: Sifatdoshli ibora bilan boshlanish: '[Sifatdosh ibora], EGA FE'L' = to'liq gap
p.ru: Причастный оборот в начале: '[оборот], ПОДЛЕЖАЩЕЕ ГЛАГОЛ' = полное предложение

p.uz: Fragment hosil qiladigan javobni hech qachon tanlamang
p.ru: Никогда не выбирайте вариант, создающий фрагмент

p.uz: Infinitivlar (to + fe'l) asosiy fe'l EMAS: 'To solve the problem' = fragment
p.ru: Инфинитивы (to + глагол) — НЕ основные глаголы: 'To solve the problem' = фрагмент

quiz.uz: 'Having reviewed all the evidence carefully' — ega ham, asosiy fe'l ham yo'q → fragment.
quiz.ru: 'Having reviewed all the evidence carefully' — нет ни подлежащего, ни основного глагола → фрагмент.

quiz.uz: Ergash gap vergul bilan bosh gapga to'g'ri biriktirilgan.
quiz.ru: Придаточное правильно присоединено к главному через запятую.

quiz.uz: Kirish sifatdoshli iboradan keyin ega + to'liq fe'l bor → to'liq gap.
quiz.ru: После вводного причастного оборота идёт подлежащее + полный глагол → полное предложение.

quiz.uz: Fragment oldingi gapga vergul bilan biriktirilib, bitta to'liq gap hosil bo'ladi.
quiz.ru: Фрагмент присоединяется к предыдущему предложению запятой, образуя одно полное предложение.

quiz.uz: 'Stood' — to'liq fe'l; 'standing'/'having stood' sifatdosh, 'which stood' ergash gap qiladi.
quiz.ru: 'Stood' — полный глагол; 'standing'/'having stood' — причастия, а 'which stood' делает часть придаточной.

grammar.title: Modifiers — Placement & Dangling Modifiers
grammar.lead: A MODIFIER is a word, phrase, or clause that describes something else. The exam tests two modifier errors. (1) MISPLACED MODIFIER: the modifier is in the wrong position — too far from what it modifies, making the sentence ambiguous or illogical. 'She almost drove her children to school every day' (almost modifies drove — she nearly drove but didn't?) vs. 'She drove her children to almost every school' (correct placement). (2) DANGLING MODIFIER: the thing being modified is not in the sentence at all, or is not the subject of the main clause. 'Walking down the street, the trees were beautiful.' — the trees were not walking. Fix: 'Walking down the street, I noticed the trees were beautiful.'

leadTr.uz: MODIFIER — boshqa narsani tasvirlaydigan so'z, ibora yoki gap. Imtihon ikki xil modifier xatosini tekshiradi. (1) NOTO'G'RI JOYLASHGAN MODIFIER (misplaced): modifier noto'g'ri o'rinda — tasvirlanayotgan narsadan uzoq, bu gapni noaniq yoki mantiqsiz qiladi. 'She almost drove her children to school every day' (almost 'drove'ni aniqlaydi — deyarli haydadi, lekin haydamadimi?) va 'She drove her children to almost every school' (to'g'ri joylashuv). (2) OSILIB QOLGAN MODIFIER (dangling): tasvirlanayotgan narsa gapda umuman yo'q yoki bosh gapning egasi emas. 'Walking down the street, the trees were beautiful.' — daraxtlar yurmagan. Tuzatish: 'Walking down the street, I noticed the trees were beautiful.'
leadTr.ru: MODIFIER — слово, оборот или придаточное, описывающее что-то другое. Экзамен проверяет две ошибки. (1) НЕВЕРНО РАЗМЕЩЁННЫЙ MODIFIER (misplaced): модификатор стоит не там — слишком далеко от определяемого, делая предложение двусмысленным или нелогичным. 'She almost drove her children to school every day' (almost относится к drove — почти повезла, но не повезла?) и 'She drove her children to almost every school' (верное размещение). (2) ВИСЯЧИЙ MODIFIER (dangling): определяемое вообще отсутствует в предложении или не является подлежащим главной части. 'Walking down the street, the trees were beautiful.' — деревья не гуляли. Исправление: 'Walking down the street, I noticed the trees were beautiful.'

p: IDENTIFYING DANGLING MODIFIERS: when a sentence opens with a participial phrase (-ing or -ed), the subject of the main clause MUST be the thing performing or experiencing the action in the phrase. Test: who is doing the -ing? That entity must be the subject immediately after the comma. 'Exhausted after the long hike, the tent was pitched' — the tent isn't exhausted. Correct: 'Exhausted after the long hike, the hikers pitched their tent.' The subject ('hikers') must immediately follow the introductory phrase.

ONLY, ALMOST, NEARLY, JUST, EVEN: these limiting modifiers must immediately precede the word they modify because their placement changes meaning. 'Only I told him the truth' (no one else told him). 'I only told him the truth' (I merely told him, did nothing else). 'I told only him the truth' (I told him and no one else). 'I told him only the truth' (I told the truth and nothing else). On the exam, pay careful attention to where these words are placed in answer choices.
Modifier must be ADJACENT to what it modifies
Dangling modifier: opening phrase must match the SUBJECT of the main clause
'Opening phrase, SUBJECT VERB' — subject must be performing the phrase's action
Only/almost/just/nearly: place immediately before the word they limit
Test dangling: ask 'WHO is [verb]-ing?' — that entity must be the subject
Misplaced: ambiguous | Dangling: illogical (impossible for subject to do the action)
Fix dangling: change subject OR restructure the phrase

quiz.q:
Which version correctly places the modifier 'only'?

Original: 'The study only found evidence of improvement in patients who exercised for at least 30 minutes.'

If the intended meaning is that improvement was found exclusively in patients who exercised (not in those who did not), which version is best?
o: The study only found evidence of improvement in patients who exercised.
The study found evidence only of improvement in patients who exercised.
The study found evidence of improvement only in patients who exercised.
Only the study found evidence of improvement in patients who exercised.
quiz.e: 'Only in patients who exercised' limits WHERE improvement was found. C places 'only' immediately before 'in patients who exercised,' correctly specifying that the improvement was exclusive to the exercising group. A places 'only' before 'found' (modifies the finding, not the location). B limits to improvement (vs. other effects). D implies no other studies found evidence.

quiz.q: Which version correctly uses the opening participial phrase?
o: Designed to withstand extreme weather, engineers tested the bridge for three years.
