Designed to withstand extreme weather, the bridge was tested for three years.
Designed to withstand extreme weather, the bridge's testing took three years.
The bridge, designed to withstand extreme weather, engineers tested for three years.
quiz.e: 'Designed to withstand extreme weather' modifies the bridge (the bridge was designed). The subject after the comma must be 'the bridge.' B is correct. A makes 'engineers' the subject (engineers weren't designed for weather). C uses 'the bridge's testing' — a gerund as subject, not the bridge itself. D misplaces the phrase.

quiz.q:
Original sentence: 'Researchers almost documented every species in the rainforest.'

If the intended meaning is that researchers documented nearly all (but not quite all) species, which revision is best?
o: Researchers almost documented every species in the rainforest.
Researchers documented almost every species in the rainforest.
Almost researchers documented every species in the rainforest.
Researchers documented every species almost in the rainforest.
quiz.e: To convey that nearly all species were documented, 'almost' must modify 'every species.' B: 'documented almost every species' — 'almost' directly precedes 'every species.' A places 'almost' before 'documented' — meaning researchers came close to doing the documentation but didn't. C is ungrammatical. D misplaces 'almost.'

p.uz: DANGLING MODIFIERNI ANIQLASH: gap sifatdoshli ibora (-ing yoki -ed) bilan boshlansa, bosh gapning egasi shu iboradagi harakatni bajarayotgan yoki boshdan kechirayotgan narsa BO'LISHI SHART. Test: -ing harakatini kim bajaryapti? O'sha shaxs verguldan keyin darhol ega bo'lishi kerak. 'Exhausted after the long hike, the tent was pitched' — chodir charchamagan. To'g'ri: 'Exhausted after the long hike, the hikers pitched their tent.' Ega ('hikers') kirish iborasidan keyin darhol kelishi kerak.
p.ru: ВЫЯВЛЕНИЕ ВИСЯЧИХ МОДИФИКАТОРОВ: если предложение открывается причастным оборотом (-ing или -ed), подлежащее главной части ОБЯЗАНО быть тем, кто выполняет или испытывает действие оборота. Тест: кто делает действие на -ing? Именно эта сущность должна стоять сразу после запятой. 'Exhausted after the long hike, the tent was pitched' — палатка не устала. Верно: 'Exhausted after the long hike, the hikers pitched their tent.' Подлежащее ('hikers') должно идти сразу за вводным оборотом.

p.uz: ONLY, ALMOST, NEARLY, JUST, EVEN: bu cheklovchi modifierlar aniqlanayotgan so'zdan bevosita oldin turishi kerak, chunki joylashuvi ma'noni o'zgartiradi. 'Only I told him the truth' (boshqa hech kim aytmadi). 'I only told him the truth' (faqat aytdim, boshqa hech narsa qilmadim). 'I told only him the truth' (faqat unga aytdim). 'I told him only the truth' (faqat haqiqatni aytdim). Imtihonda bu so'zlarning javob variantlaridagi o'rniga alohida e'tibor bering.
p.ru: ONLY, ALMOST, NEARLY, JUST, EVEN: эти ограничительные модификаторы должны стоять непосредственно перед определяемым словом, поскольку их позиция меняет смысл. 'Only I told him the truth' (никто другой не сказал). 'I only told him the truth' (я лишь сказал, больше ничего не делал). 'I told only him the truth' (сказал только ему). 'I told him only the truth' (сказал только правду). На экзамене внимательно смотрите, где эти слова стоят в вариантах ответа.

p.uz: Modifier tasvirlanayotgan narsaga YONMA-YON turishi kerak
p.ru: Модификатор должен стоять РЯДОМ с тем, что он описывает

p.uz: Dangling modifier: kirish iborasi bosh gap EGASIga mos kelishi shart
p.ru: Висячий модификатор: вводный оборот должен соответствовать ПОДЛЕЖАЩЕМУ главной части

p.uz: 'Kirish ibora, EGA FE'L' — ega iboradagi harakatni bajarayotgan bo'lishi kerak
p.ru: 'Вводный оборот, ПОДЛЕЖАЩЕЕ ГЛАГОЛ' — подлежащее должно выполнять действие оборота

p.uz: Only/almost/just/nearly: cheklaydigan so'zdan bevosita oldin qo'ying
p.ru: Only/almost/just/nearly: ставьте непосредственно перед ограничиваемым словом

p.uz: Dangling testi: 'kim [fe'l]-ing qilyapti?' deb so'rang — o'sha shaxs ega bo'lishi kerak
p.ru: Тест на dangling: спросите «КТО делает действие на -ing?» — эта сущность должна быть подлежащим

p.uz: Misplaced: noaniq | Dangling: mantiqsiz (ega bu harakatni bajara olmaydi)
p.ru: Misplaced: двусмысленно | Dangling: нелогично (подлежащее не может выполнить действие)

p.uz: Danglingni tuzatish: egani o'zgartiring YOKI iborani qayta tuzing
p.ru: Исправление dangling: смените подлежащее ИЛИ перестройте оборот

quiz.uz: 'only' 'in patients who exercised'dan bevosita oldin turibdi — yaxshilanish faqat shu guruhda topilgan.
quiz.ru: 'only' стоит прямо перед 'in patients who exercised' — улучшение найдено только в этой группе.

quiz.uz: 'Designed to withstand extreme weather' ko'prikni tasvirlaydi → verguldan keyingi ega 'the bridge' bo'lishi kerak.
quiz.ru: 'Designed to withstand extreme weather' описывает мост → подлежащим после запятой должен быть 'the bridge'.

quiz.uz: 'almost' 'every species'dan oldin turishi kerak — deyarli barcha turlar hujjatlashtirilgan.
quiz.ru: 'almost' должно стоять перед 'every species' — задокументированы почти все виды.

grammar.title: Parallel Structure
grammar.lead: PARALLEL STRUCTURE (parallelism) requires that words, phrases, or clauses in a series or comparison have the same grammatical form. When a sentence lists or compares items, all items must match in form: all nouns, all infinitives, all -ing phrases, all clauses, etc. 'She likes swimming, hiking, and to run' violates parallelism — mix of gerunds and infinitive. Correct: 'She likes swimming, hiking, and running' OR 'She likes to swim, to hike, and to run.' The exam tests parallelism in lists (and/or), correlative conjunctions (both/and, either/or, not only/but also, neither/nor), and comparative structures.

leadTr.uz: PARALLEL STRUCTURE (parallelizm) qatordagi yoki qiyoslashdagi so'zlar, iboralar yoki gaplar bir xil grammatik shaklda bo'lishini talab qiladi. Gap narsalarni sanasa yoki qiyoslasa, hammasi shaklan mos bo'lishi kerak: hammasi ot, hammasi infinitiv, hammasi -ing ibora, hammasi gap va h.k. 'She likes swimming, hiking, and to run' parallelizmni buzadi — gerundiy va infinitiv aralashgan. To'g'ri: 'She likes swimming, hiking, and running' YOKI 'She likes to swim, to hike, and to run.' Imtihon parallelizmni ro'yxatlarda (and/or), juft bog'lovchilarda (both/and, either/or, not only/but also, neither/nor) va qiyosiy tuzilmalarda tekshiradi.
leadTr.ru: PARALLEL STRUCTURE (параллелизм) требует, чтобы слова, обороты или части в перечислении или сравнении имели одинаковую грамматическую форму. Если предложение перечисляет или сравнивает, все элементы должны совпадать по форме: все существительные, все инфинитивы, все -ing формы, все придаточные и т.д. 'She likes swimming, hiking, and to run' нарушает параллелизм — смесь герундиев и инфинитива. Верно: 'She likes swimming, hiking, and running' ИЛИ 'She likes to swim, to hike, and to run.' Экзамен проверяет параллелизм в перечислениях (and/or), парных союзах (both/and, either/or, not only/but also, neither/nor) и сравнительных конструкциях.

p: CORRELATIVE CONJUNCTIONS require strict parallelism: whatever comes after the first conjunction must match grammatically with whatever comes after the second. 'Both working late AND to skip lunch' — wrong. 'Both working late AND skipping lunch' — correct (both are gerunds). 'Not only DID she win the competition BUT ALSO received a standing ovation' — wrong. 'Not only DID she win the competition BUT ALSO DID she receive a standing ovation' or 'Not only did she win but also receive...' The structures on both sides must match.

COMPARING LIKE WITH LIKE: parallelism also requires that comparisons be made between grammatically equivalent and logically comparable things. 'The climate in Norway is colder than Spain' — wrong (comparing climate to Spain). 'The climate in Norway is colder than the climate in Spain' or 'The climate in Norway is colder than Spain's.' 'She worked harder than her colleague did' or 'than her colleague.' Both comparing people's work. This type of error is especially common in academic writing on the exam.
All items in a series must have the same grammatical form
Gerunds: swimming, hiking, running (not 'to run')
Infinitives: to swim, to hike, to run (not 'running')
Correlatives: both X and Y | not only X but also Y | neither X nor Y
Both sides of correlative must match grammatically
Comparisons: compare LIKE with LIKE (climate to climate, not climate to country)
Fix: identify the pattern, then make all items match

quiz.q: Which version is correctly parallel?
o: The program requires reading, writing, and to solve mathematical problems.
The program requires reading, writing, and solving mathematical problems.
The program requires to read, writing, and solving mathematical problems.
The program requires reading, to write, and solving mathematical problems.
quiz.e: B uses three gerunds: reading, writing, solving. All in the same -ing form. A mixes gerunds and an infinitive. C mixes infinitive and gerunds. D mixes gerund, infinitive, and gerund.

quiz.q: Which version is correctly parallel?
o: The new policy will not only reduce emissions but also improving air quality.
The new policy will not only reduce emissions but also improve air quality.
The new policy will not only reducing emissions but also improve air quality.
The new policy not only will reduce emissions but will also improving air quality.
quiz.e: 'Not only X but also Y' — both sides must match. B: 'not only REDUCE (bare infinitive) but also IMPROVE (bare infinitive)' — parallel. A: 'reduce' (infinitive) vs. 'improving' (gerund) — not parallel. C: 'reducing' vs. 'improve' — not parallel. D is structurally awkward.

quiz.q: Which version is correctly parallel?
o: The study examined how poverty affects education, what happens to health outcomes, and the implications of housing instability.
The study examined how poverty affects education, how it affects health outcomes, and how housing instability creates long-term consequences.
The study examined how poverty affects education, health outcomes, and implications of housing instability.
The study examined the effects of poverty on education, health outcomes, and what housing instability does.
quiz.e: B: three parallel 'how' clauses — 'how poverty affects education / how it affects health outcomes / how housing instability creates consequences.' All three have the same structure. A mixes two 'how' clauses and a noun phrase. C is partially parallel. D mixes noun phrases and a clause.

quiz.q: Which version makes a correct parallel comparison?
o: The average salary of engineers in Germany is higher than France.
The average salary of engineers in Germany is higher than in France.
The average salary of engineers in Germany is higher than France's engineers.
The average salary of engineers in Germany is higher than the average salary of engineers in France.
quiz.e: D clearly compares 'average salary of engineers in Germany' with 'average salary of engineers in France' — salary to salary. B is also acceptable ('higher than in France' is idiomatic). A incorrectly compares salary to France (a country). C compares salary to 'France's engineers' (illogical). D is the most explicit.

quiz.q: Which version correctly uses neither/nor?
o: The report was neither thoroughly researched nor did it present its conclusions clearly.
The report was neither thoroughly researched nor clearly presented.
The report neither was thoroughly researched nor presenting its conclusions clearly.
Neither the research was thorough nor the conclusions clearly.
quiz.e: B: 'neither THOROUGHLY RESEARCHED (adjective phrase) nor CLEARLY PRESENTED (adjective phrase)' — both are adjective phrases describing 'the report.' Parallel. A mixes adjective phrase and clause. C mixes 'was' and gerund. D is incomplete and awkward.

p.uz: JUFT BOG'LOVCHILAR qat'iy parallelizmni talab qiladi: birinchi bog'lovchidan keyin kelgan narsa ikkinchisidan keyin kelgani bilan grammatik jihatdan mos bo'lishi kerak. 'Both working late AND to skip lunch' — xato. 'Both working late AND skipping lunch' — to'g'ri (ikkalasi ham gerundiy). 'Not only DID she win the competition BUT ALSO received a standing ovation' — xato. 'Not only DID she win the competition BUT ALSO DID she receive a standing ovation' yoki 'Not only did she win but also receive...' Ikki tomondagi tuzilmalar mos kelishi shart.
p.ru: ПАРНЫЕ СОЮЗЫ требуют строгого параллелизма: то, что стоит после первого союза, должно грамматически совпадать с тем, что после второго. 'Both working late AND to skip lunch' — неверно. 'Both working late AND skipping lunch' — верно (оба герундии). 'Not only DID she win the competition BUT ALSO received a standing ovation' — неверно. 'Not only DID she win the competition BUT ALSO DID she receive a standing ovation' или 'Not only did she win but also receive...' Структуры по обе стороны должны совпадать.

p.uz: O'XSHASHNI O'XSHASH BILAN QIYOSLASH: parallelizm qiyoslashlar grammatik jihatdan teng va mantiqan qiyoslanadigan narsalar orasida bo'lishini ham talab qiladi. 'The climate in Norway is colder than Spain' — xato (iqlim Ispaniya bilan qiyoslanyapti). 'The climate in Norway is colder than the climate in Spain' yoki 'The climate in Norway is colder than Spain's.' 'She worked harder than her colleague did' yoki 'than her colleague.' Ikkalasida ham odamlarning ishi qiyoslanadi. Bu turdagi xato imtihondagi akademik matnlarda ayniqsa ko'p uchraydi.
p.ru: СРАВНИВАТЬ ПОДОБНОЕ С ПОДОБНЫМ: параллелизм требует, чтобы сравнивались грамматически эквивалентные и логически сопоставимые вещи. 'The climate in Norway is colder than Spain' — неверно (климат сравнивается с Испанией). 'The climate in Norway is colder than the climate in Spain' или 'The climate in Norway is colder than Spain's.' 'She worked harder than her colleague did' или 'than her colleague.' В обоих случаях сравнивается работа людей. Этот тип ошибки особенно част в академических текстах на экзамене.

p.uz: Qatordagi barcha elementlar bir xil grammatik shaklda bo'lishi kerak
p.ru: Все элементы перечисления должны иметь одну грамматическую форму

p.uz: Gerundiylar: swimming, hiking, running ('to run' emas)
p.ru: Герундии: swimming, hiking, running (не 'to run')

p.uz: Infinitivlar: to swim, to hike, to run ('running' emas)
p.ru: Инфинитивы: to swim, to hike, to run (не 'running')

p.uz: Juft bog'lovchilar: both X and Y | not only X but also Y | neither X nor Y
p.ru: Парные союзы: both X and Y | not only X but also Y | neither X nor Y

p.uz: Juft bog'lovchining ikki tomoni grammatik jihatdan mos bo'lishi shart
p.ru: Обе части парного союза должны грамматически совпадать

p.uz: Qiyoslash: O'XSHASHNI O'XSHASH bilan qiyoslang (iqlimni iqlim bilan, mamlakat bilan emas)
p.ru: Сравнения: сравнивайте ПОДОБНОЕ с ПОДОБНЫМ (климат с климатом, а не со страной)

p.uz: Tuzatish: naqshni aniqlang, keyin barcha elementlarni unga moslang
p.ru: Исправление: определите шаблон, затем приведите все элементы к нему

quiz.uz: Uchta gerundiy bir xil -ing shaklida: reading, writing, solving — parallel.
quiz.ru: Три герундия в одной -ing форме: reading, writing, solving — параллельно.

quiz.uz: 'not only REDUCE but also IMPROVE' — ikkala tomonda ham yalang'och infinitiv, parallel.
quiz.ru: 'not only REDUCE but also IMPROVE' — с обеих сторон голый инфинитив, параллельно.

quiz.uz: Uchta bir xil tuzilishdagi 'how' gapi — to'liq parallel.
quiz.ru: Три однотипных придаточных с 'how' — полностью параллельно.

quiz.uz: Maosh maosh bilan qiyoslanadi: 'average salary...in Germany' va 'average salary...in France'.
quiz.ru: Зарплата сравнивается с зарплатой: 'average salary...in Germany' и 'average salary...in France'.

quiz.uz: 'neither thoroughly researched nor clearly presented' — ikkala tomonda ham sifat ibora, parallel.
quiz.ru: 'neither thoroughly researched nor clearly presented' — обе части адъективные, параллельно.

grammar.title: Verb Tense — Consistency & Sequence
grammar.lead: VERB TENSE tells the reader WHEN an action occurs. The exam tests two main tense skills: (1) TENSE CONSISTENCY — don't shift tenses unnecessarily within a passage. If a passage describes historical events in the past tense, all verbs should stay in the past tense unless there is a clear reason to shift (e.g., describing a current truth vs. a historical event). 'Galileo observed the moons of Jupiter. He publishes his findings' — wrong shift from past to present. (2) TENSE SEQUENCE — when events happen at different times, verbs must reflect the correct time relationship using perfect tenses.

leadTr.uz: VERB TENSE o'quvchiga harakat QACHON sodir bo'lishini aytadi. Imtihon ikkita asosiy zamon ko'nikmasini tekshiradi: (1) ZAMON IZCHILLIGI — matn ichida zamonlarni sababsiz almashtirmang. Matn tarixiy voqealarni o'tgan zamonda tasvirlasa, aniq sabab bo'lmaguncha (masalan, hozirgi haqiqat va tarixiy voqea farqi) barcha fe'llar o'tgan zamonda qolishi kerak. 'Galileo observed the moons of Jupiter. He publishes his findings' — o'tgandan hozirgiga noto'g'ri o'tish. (2) ZAMONLAR KETMA-KETLIGI — voqealar turli vaqtlarda sodir bo'lganda, fe'llar perfect zamonlar yordamida to'g'ri vaqt munosabatini aks ettirishi kerak.
leadTr.ru: VERB TENSE сообщает читателю, КОГДА происходит действие. Экзамен проверяет два навыка: (1) СОГЛАСОВАННОСТЬ ВРЕМЁН — не меняйте время без необходимости внутри отрывка. Если текст описывает исторические события в прошедшем времени, все глаголы должны оставаться в прошедшем, если нет ясной причины для сдвига (например, текущая истина против исторического факта). 'Galileo observed the moons of Jupiter. He publishes his findings' — неверный сдвиг из прошедшего в настоящее. (2) ПОСЛЕДОВАТЕЛЬНОСТЬ ВРЕМЁН — когда события происходят в разное время, глаголы должны отражать временные отношения с помощью перфектных времён.

p: PERFECT TENSES: PAST PERFECT ('had + past participle') shows that one past action occurred BEFORE another past action. 'By the time the rescue team arrived, the survivors had built a shelter.' (building happened before arriving). PRESENT PERFECT ('have/has + past participle') shows a past action with present relevance, or an action that began in the past and continues. 'Scientists have discovered three new species this year.' FUTURE PERFECT ('will have + past participle') shows an action that will be complete before a future point. 'By 2050, renewables will have replaced most fossil fuels.'

COMMON TENSE ERRORS on the exam: (1) Unnecessary tense shift mid-passage. (2) Using simple past when past perfect is needed to show prior occurrence. 'When the inspector arrived, someone already removed the evidence' — should be 'someone had already removed' (removal before arrival). (3) Mixing present and past in historical or narrative passages. Strategy: find the BASE TENSE of the passage. All verbs should be in that tense unless a time signal (before, after, already, by the time, since) requires a different tense.
Tense consistency: establish base tense, stay in it throughout
Past perfect (had + PP): earlier past action before another past action
Present perfect (have/has + PP): past with present relevance, or ongoing since past
Signal words → past perfect: before, after, already, by the time, when (two past events)
Future perfect (will have + PP): completed before a future point
Present tense for CURRENT TRUTHS even in historical passages: 'Water freezes at 0°C'
Avoid: simple past when sequence requires past perfect

quiz.q: Which version correctly shows that the evidence was removed BEFORE the inspector arrived?
o: When the inspector arrived, someone already removed the evidence.
When the inspector arrived, someone had already removed the evidence.
When the inspector had arrived, someone already removed the evidence.
When the inspector arrived, someone has already removed the evidence.
quiz.e: 'Already removed' = happened before 'arrived.' For an earlier past event, use PAST PERFECT: 'had already removed.' B is correct. A uses simple past — doesn't show the sequence. C wrongly uses past perfect for arrival (the arrival isn't the earlier event). D uses present perfect — wrong tense entirely.

quiz.q:
Text: 'The archaeologists discovered that an ancient civilization occupied the site for centuries before mysteriously disappearing.'

Which is the error and how should it be fixed?
o: There is no error in this sentence.
quiz.e: 'Occupied' should be 'had occupied' to show the occupation preceded the discovery. B is correct. 'Discovered' is the reference point in the past (simple past is fine). 'Disappearing' is a participial modifier — it can stay.

quiz.q:
Text: 'By the time the infrastructure project is complete in 2028, engineers [___] over a decade on its design.'

Which choice correctly completes the text?
quiz.e: D: 'will have spent' correctly expresses that the spending will be completed by 2028. A (present) and B (past) are wrong tenses. C (simple future) doesn't convey the completion by 2028.

p.uz: PERFECT ZAMONLAR: PAST PERFECT ('had + past participle') bir o'tgan harakat boshqa o'tgan harakatdan OLDIN sodir bo'lganini ko'rsatadi. 'By the time the rescue team arrived, the survivors had built a shelter.' (qurish kelishdan oldin bo'lgan). PRESENT PERFECT ('have/has + past participle') hozirgiga aloqador o'tgan harakatni yoki o'tmishda boshlanib davom etayotgan harakatni bildiradi. 'Scientists have discovered three new species this year.' FUTURE PERFECT ('will have + past participle') kelajakdagi nuqtadan oldin tugallanadigan harakatni ko'rsatadi. 'By 2050, renewables will have replaced most fossil fuels.'
p.ru: ПЕРФЕКТНЫЕ ВРЕМЕНА: PAST PERFECT ('had + past participle') показывает, что одно прошедшее действие произошло ДО другого прошедшего. 'By the time the rescue team arrived, the survivors had built a shelter.' (постройка была до прибытия). PRESENT PERFECT ('have/has + past participle') — прошедшее действие с актуальностью в настоящем или действие, начавшееся в прошлом и продолжающееся. 'Scientists have discovered three new species this year.' FUTURE PERFECT ('will have + past participle') — действие завершится до момента в будущем. 'By 2050, renewables will have replaced most fossil fuels.'

p.uz: Imtihondagi KENG TARQALGAN ZAMON XATOLARI: (1) Matn o'rtasida sababsiz zamon almashinuvi. (2) Oldinroq sodir bo'lganini ko'rsatish uchun past perfect kerak bo'lganda simple past ishlatish. 'When the inspector arrived, someone already removed the evidence' — 'someone had already removed' bo'lishi kerak (olib tashlash kelishdan oldin). (3) Tarixiy yoki hikoya matnlarida hozirgi va o'tgan zamonni aralashtirish. Strategiya: matnning ASOSIY ZAMONINI toping. Vaqt signali (before, after, already, by the time, since) boshqa zamonni talab qilmaguncha barcha fe'llar shu zamonda bo'lishi kerak.
p.ru: ЧАСТЫЕ ОШИБКИ ВРЕМЁН на экзамене: (1) Немотивированный сдвиг времени посреди текста. (2) Simple past там, где нужен past perfect для более раннего события. 'When the inspector arrived, someone already removed the evidence' — должно быть 'someone had already removed' (удаление до прибытия). (3) Смешение настоящего и прошедшего в исторических или повествовательных текстах. Стратегия: определите БАЗОВОЕ ВРЕМЯ отрывка. Все глаголы должны стоять в нём, пока сигнал времени (before, after, already, by the time, since) не потребует другого.

p.uz: Zamon izchilligi: asosiy zamonni aniqlang va oxirigacha unda qoling
p.ru: Согласованность: установите базовое время и держитесь его до конца

p.uz: Past perfect (had + PP): boshqa o'tgan harakatdan oldingi harakat
p.ru: Past perfect (had + PP): более раннее прошедшее действие перед другим прошедшим

p.uz: Present perfect (have/has + PP): hozirgiga aloqador o'tmish yoki o'tmishdan davom etayotgan
p.ru: Present perfect (have/has + PP): прошлое с актуальностью сейчас или длящееся с прошлого

p.uz: Signal so'zlar → past perfect: before, after, already, by the time, when (ikki o'tgan voqea)
p.ru: Сигнальные слова → past perfect: before, after, already, by the time, when (два прошедших события)

p.uz: Future perfect (will have + PP): kelajakdagi nuqtadan oldin tugallangan
p.ru: Future perfect (will have + PP): завершено до точки в будущем

p.uz: HOZIRGI HAQIQATLAR uchun tarixiy matnda ham hozirgi zamon: 'Water freezes at 0°C'
p.ru: Настоящее время для ТЕКУЩИХ ИСТИН даже в исторических текстах: 'Water freezes at 0°C'

grammar.title: Subjunctive Mood & Conditional Structures
grammar.lead: MOOD refers to the form a verb takes to indicate the attitude toward the action. The INDICATIVE mood states facts ('She is a scientist'). The SUBJUNCTIVE mood expresses wishes, doubts, hypotheticals, recommendations, or conditions contrary to fact. The exam tests two subjunctive patterns: (1) PRESENT SUBJUNCTIVE in 'that' clauses after verbs of recommendation, demand, suggestion, request, or requirement: 'The committee recommended that she PRESENT her findings' (not 'presents'). Always base form (no -s, no -ed, no -ing). Common triggers: recommend, suggest, require, demand, insist, propose, ask, request, urge.

leadTr.uz: MOOD — fe'lning harakatga munosabatni bildiruvchi shakli. INDICATIVE mayl faktlarni bayon qiladi ('She is a scientist'). SUBJUNCTIVE mayl istak, shubha, faraz, tavsiya yoki haqiqatga zid shartlarni ifodalaydi. Imtihon ikkita subjunctive naqshini tekshiradi: (1) tavsiya, talab, taklif, iltimos yoki majburiyat fe'llaridan keyingi 'that' gaplarida PRESENT SUBJUNCTIVE: 'The committee recommended that she PRESENT her findings' ('presents' emas). Har doim asosiy shakl (-s siz, -ed siz, -ing siz). Keng tarqalgan trigger fe'llar: recommend, suggest, require, demand, insist, propose, ask, request, urge.
leadTr.ru: MOOD (наклонение) — форма глагола, выражающая отношение к действию. INDICATIVE констатирует факты ('She is a scientist'). SUBJUNCTIVE выражает желания, сомнения, гипотезы, рекомендации или условия, противоречащие фактам. Экзамен проверяет два шаблона: (1) PRESENT SUBJUNCTIVE в придаточных с 'that' после глаголов рекомендации, требования, предложения, просьбы: 'The committee recommended that she PRESENT her findings' (не 'presents'). Всегда базовая форма (без -s, -ed, -ing). Частые глаголы-триггеры: recommend, suggest, require, demand, insist, propose, ask, request, urge.

p: PAST SUBJUNCTIVE for CONTRARY-TO-FACT conditions: use 'were' (not 'was') for all subjects. 'If I were president...' (not 'if I was') — this is a hypothetical, not a real condition. 'If she were taller...' 'If the data were complete...' 'As if he were an expert...' The test: is the condition FALSE or HYPOTHETICAL? If yes → 'were.' If the condition might be TRUE → use normal 'was.' 'If the report was accurate, we can proceed' (it might be accurate) vs. 'If the report were accurate, we could proceed' (it's not accurate — hypothetical).

CONDITIONAL STRUCTURES: 'If...would' patterns. Real/possible conditions use simple present + simple future: 'If she studies, she will pass.' Hypothetical conditions use past + would: 'If she studied, she would pass.' Contrary-to-fact past conditions use past perfect + would have: 'If she had studied, she would have passed.' The exam error: mixing the conditional tiers. 'If she studies, she would pass' mixes real condition (present) with hypothetical result (would) — wrong. Match the tier consistently.
Subjunctive: recommend/require/insist/suggest + that + SUBJECT + BASE VERB
'Recommend that she GO' (not 'goes') | 'Require that he BE' (not 'is')
Contrary-to-fact: 'If I WERE...' (not 'was') for all subjects
Real condition: If + present → will + base verb
Hypothetical: If + past → would + base verb
Contrary-to-fact past: If + past perfect → would have + past participle
Never: 'If she would study' — never 'would' in the 'if' clause

quiz.q: Which version correctly uses the subjunctive?
o: The board required that all members submits a disclosure form.
The board required that all members submit a disclosure form.
The board required that all members submitted a disclosure form.
The board required that all members are submitting a disclosure form.
quiz.e: 'Required that' + SUBJECT + BASE VERB (subjunctive). B: 'submit' — base form, no -s. Correct. A uses third-person singular ('submits') — wrong in subjunctive. C uses past tense. D uses present progressive.

quiz.q: Which version correctly uses the subjunctive?
o: If the population was larger, the city would receive more federal funding.
If the population were larger, the city would receive more federal funding.
If the population would be larger, the city would receive more federal funding.
If the population has been larger, the city would receive more federal funding.
quiz.e: 'If the population were larger' is CONTRARY-TO-FACT (the population is NOT larger). Use 'were' for all subjects in hypothetical conditions. B is correct. A uses 'was' — acceptable in informal English but not the formal exam standard. C uses 'would be' in the 'if' clause — never allowed. D uses present perfect — wrong.

quiz.q: Which version best expresses a REAL/POSSIBLE condition?
o: If the funding were approved, the research will begin next month.
If the funding is approved, the research will begin next month.
If the funding was approved, the research would begin next month.
If the funding would be approved, the research will begin next month.
quiz.e: Real/possible condition (funding might be approved): 'If + present → will + base.' B: 'If the funding IS approved, the research WILL begin.' Correct. A mixes subjunctive 'were' with 'will' (hypothetical + real = inconsistent). C uses past tense (hypothetical). D uses 'would be' in the if-clause (never correct).

quiz.q: Which version correctly expresses: the project failed because the team didn't plan properly — and the speaker is reflecting on what would have been different.
o: If the team planned better, the project would succeed.
If the team had planned better, the project would have succeeded.
If the team were to plan better, the project will succeed.
If the team plans better, the project would have succeeded.
quiz.e: Contrary-to-fact PAST (the team DID NOT plan well, the project DID fail): use PAST PERFECT in 'if' clause + 'would have' in result. B: 'If they HAD planned...the project WOULD HAVE succeeded.' Correct. A is a hypothetical present-to-future (not past). C uses were-to + will (mixed). D mixes real condition (plans) with past result (would have succeeded).

quiz.q: Which version correctly uses the subjunctive after a trigger verb?
o: The professor suggested that the student revises her thesis.
The professor suggested that the student revised her thesis.
The professor suggested that the student revise her thesis.
The professor suggested that the student is revising her thesis.
quiz.e: 'Suggested that' + subjunctive: SUBJECT + BASE VERB. C: 'suggested that the student REVISE' — base form. Correct. A uses third-person 's' ('revises'). B uses past tense ('revised'). D uses present progressive.

p.uz: HAQIQATGA ZID shartlar uchun PAST SUBJUNCTIVE: barcha egalar bilan 'were' ('was' emas) ishlating. 'If I were president...' ('if I was' emas) — bu faraz, real shart emas. 'If she were taller...' 'If the data were complete...' 'As if he were an expert...' Test: shart YOLG'ONMI yoki FARAZIYMI? Ha bo'lsa → 'were'. Shart ROST bo'lishi mumkin bo'lsa → oddiy 'was'. 'If the report was accurate, we can proceed' (rost bo'lishi mumkin) va 'If the report were accurate, we could proceed' (rost emas — faraz).
p.ru: PAST SUBJUNCTIVE для условий, ПРОТИВОРЕЧАЩИХ ФАКТАМ: используйте 'were' (не 'was') со всеми подлежащими. 'If I were president...' (не 'if I was') — это гипотеза, не реальное условие. 'If she were taller...' 'If the data were complete...' 'As if he were an expert...' Тест: условие ЛОЖНО или ГИПОТЕТИЧНО? Если да → 'were'. Если условие может быть ИСТИННЫМ → обычное 'was'. 'If the report was accurate, we can proceed' (может быть точным) и 'If the report were accurate, we could proceed' (не точен — гипотеза).

p.uz: SHART TUZILMALARI: 'If...would' naqshlari. Real/mumkin shartlar: simple present + simple future: 'If she studies, she will pass.' Faraziy shartlar: past + would: 'If she studied, she would pass.' O'tmishdagi haqiqatga zid shartlar: past perfect + would have: 'If she had studied, she would have passed.' Imtihondagi xato: darajalarni aralashtirish. 'If she studies, she would pass' — real shart (hozirgi) faraziy natija (would) bilan aralashgan — xato. Darajani izchil moslang.
p.ru: УСЛОВНЫЕ КОНСТРУКЦИИ: шаблоны 'If...would'. Реальные/возможные условия: simple present + simple future: 'If she studies, she will pass.' Гипотетические: past + would: 'If she studied, she would pass.' Противоречащие фактам в прошлом: past perfect + would have: 'If she had studied, she would have passed.' Экзаменационная ошибка — смешение уровней. 'If she studies, she would pass' смешивает реальное условие (настоящее) с гипотетическим результатом (would) — неверно. Выдерживайте уровень последовательно.

p.uz: Subjunctive: recommend/require/insist/suggest + that + EGA + ASOSIY FE'L
p.ru: Subjunctive: recommend/require/insist/suggest + that + ПОДЛЕЖАЩЕЕ + БАЗОВЫЙ ГЛАГОЛ

reading.title: Reading set: Inference & implication
reading.text:
Each task below contains its own short passage. Read it closely, then answer — this trains exactly the kind of reading you will meet in real academic texts and exams.

Quyida har bir topshiriqning o'z qisqa matni bor. Diqqat bilan o'qing, so'ng javob bering.

quiz.q:
Passage: 'Countries that have legalized and regulated cannabis markets have seen declines in cannabis purchases from illegal dealers in those regions. However, cross-border trafficking to neighboring areas where cannabis remains illegal has increased significantly in some cases.'

The passage most strongly suggests that
o: Cannabis legalization is ineffective as a policy because illegal activity increases
Cannabis legalization reduces domestic illegal sales but may shift rather than eliminate some illegal trafficking
Legalizing cannabis eliminates all illegal drug trade activity
The effects of cannabis legalization on illegal markets vary depending on whether neighboring jurisdictions have also legalized
quiz.e: The passage shows: legal markets → fewer local illegal sales BUT MORE cross-border trafficking where it's illegal elsewhere. D accurately captures both effects: reduces domestic illegal sales but shifts (not eliminates) trafficking. A is an over-inference. B mischaracterizes (legal markets DO reduce local illegal sales). C is about what would happen with neighboring legalization — not directly stated.

quiz.q:
Passage: 'The reintroduction of wolves to Yellowstone in 1995 produced cascading ecological effects. Elk populations declined and changed their grazing behavior, which allowed riverbank vegetation to recover. The returning vegetation stabilized banks, changed river flow patterns, and attracted beavers, whose dams created wetland habitats. Songbird and fish populations subsequently increased.'

It can most reasonably be inferred from the passage that
o: Wolves directly improved water quality in Yellowstone's rivers
Beaver populations were zero in Yellowstone before wolf reintroduction
The removal of wolves had previously triggered a chain of ecological changes throughout the park
Elk are the primary threat to ecological balance in all natural parks
quiz.e: Since the REINTRODUCTION of wolves triggered positive cascading changes (elk behavior changed, vegetation recovered, rivers changed, beavers returned), it can be inferred that the REMOVAL of wolves had previously triggered the REVERSE chain — elk overgrazed, banks eroded, rivers changed, etc. B captures this logical reversal. A is not supported (water quality not mentioned). C is too broad. D is an over-inference (beavers may have been reduced, not necessarily zero).

quiz.q:
Passage: 'Antibiotic resistance has emerged as a major threat to global health, with drug-resistant infections killing an estimated 700,000 people annually. Much of this resistance has developed because antibiotics have been prescribed for viral infections — against which they are entirely ineffective — or because patients fail to complete their full course of treatment.'

The passage most strongly implies that
o: Completing a full course of antibiotics guarantees that resistance will not develop
Viruses will eventually become resistant to antibiotics as well
All antibiotic prescriptions are unnecessary and should be eliminated
Reducing inappropriate antibiotic use could help slow the development of resistance
quiz.e: The passage identifies two causes of resistance: prescribing for viruses AND incomplete courses. It follows logically that reducing these practices could slow resistance development. B directly follows. A is extreme (passage doesn't say all prescriptions are inappropriate). C is a biological misunderstanding (viruses can't develop antibiotic resistance). D over-infers (completion helps but doesn't guarantee resistance prevention).

quiz.q:
Passage: 'Observations of chimpanzee groups in the wild have documented tool use, strategic deception, cultural transmission of behaviors across generations, and even rudimentary forms of political coalition-building. These findings have required researchers to revise earlier assumptions about what distinguishes human cognition from that of other primates.'

From the passage, it can be inferred that researchers previously believed
o: Observations of wild primates were not scientifically valid before these studies
Chimpanzees were incapable of any form of intelligent behavior
Chimpanzees and humans share a common ancestor but diverged significantly in cognitive ability
The behaviors observed in chimpanzees — tool use, deception, culture, and political behavior — were thought to be exclusively human
quiz.e: The passage says the findings 'required researchers to REVISE EARLIER ASSUMPTIONS about what distinguishes human cognition' — implying the earlier assumption was that these specific behaviors (tool use, deception, culture, coalition-building) DISTINGUISHED humans and were thought to be uniquely human. B captures this. A is too extreme (they didn't think chimps had NO intelligence). C is about ancestry (not mentioned). D is unsupported.

quizTr.uz: Matn ikkala effektni ko'rsatadi: mahalliy noqonuniy sotuvlar kamayadi, LEKIN u noqonuniy bo'lgan joylarga chegara orqali kontrabanda ko'chadi — D ikkalasini aniq qamraydi; A ortiqcha xulosa, B noto'g'ri tavsiflaydi, C bevosita aytilmagan.
quizTr.ru: Текст показывает оба эффекта: локальные нелегальные продажи падают, НО трафик смещается туда, где это нелегально — D точно передаёт оба; A — сверхвывод, B искажает, C прямо не заявлено.

quizTr.uz: Bo'rilarning QAYTARILISHI ijobiy zanjirni boshlaganidan, ularning YO'Q QILINISHI ilgari teskari zanjirni boshlagani kelib chiqadi — B shu mantiqiy teskarilikni qamraydi; A asoslanmagan (suv sifati aytilmagan), C juda keng, D ortiqcha xulosa.
quizTr.ru: Раз ВОЗВРАЩЕНИЕ волков запустило позитивную цепочку изменений, их ИСТРЕБЛЕНИЕ ранее запустило обратную — B передаёт этот логический разворот; A не подтверждено (качество воды не упомянуто), C слишком широк, D — сверхвывод.

quizTr.uz: Matn rezistentlikning ikki sababini ko'rsatadi — bu amaliyotlarni kamaytirish rezistentlikni sekinlatishi mantiqan kelib chiqadi; B bevosita, A keskin, C biologik xato (viruslar antibiotikka chidamlilik hosil qilmaydi), D ortiqcha xulosa.
quizTr.ru: Текст называет две причины резистентности — логически следует, что их сокращение замедлит её развитие; B прямо вытекает, A чрезмерен, C — биологическая ошибка (вирусы не вырабатывают резистентность к антибиотикам), D — сверхвывод.

quizTr.uz: 'Oldingi taxminlarni qayta ko'rish' bu xatti-harakatlar (asbob ishlatish, aldash, madaniyat, koalitsiya) ilgari faqat insonga xos deb hisoblanganini bildiradi — B shuni qamraydi; A haddan tashqari, C ajdodlar haqida (aytilmagan), D asoslanmagan.
quizTr.ru: «Пересмотр прежних допущений» означает, что эти формы поведения (орудия, обман, культура, коалиции) считались уникально человеческими — B это передаёт; A чрезмерен, C — о предках (не упомянуто), D не подтверждён.

reading.title: Reading set: Tone & perspective
reading.text:
Each task below contains its own short passage. Read it closely, then answer — this trains exactly the kind of reading you will meet in real academic texts and exams.

Quyida har bir topshiriqning o'z qisqa matni bor. Diqqat bilan o'qing, so'ng javob bering.

quiz.q:
Passage: 'Renewable energy capacity has grown dramatically in recent years. Solar installations increased globally by 45% in 2023 alone, while wind capacity additions reached a new record. These developments are genuinely encouraging. Nevertheless, fossil fuels still account for approximately 80% of global energy consumption, and emissions continue to rise. The pace of the energy transition, impressive in absolute terms, remains deeply insufficient relative to what climate science indicates is necessary to limit warming to 1.5°C.'

The author's attitude toward the renewable energy transition is best described as
o: Neutral, presenting both positive and negative data without taking a position
Enthusiastically celebratory of renewable energy's rapid growth
Deeply pessimistic that the energy transition will ever succeed
Cautiously concerned — acknowledging genuine progress while emphasizing that the pace remains inadequate for climate goals
quiz.e: Evaluative language: 'genuinely encouraging' (positive) + 'deeply insufficient relative to what climate science indicates is necessary' (concern). The structure — acknowledge progress, then emphasize inadequacy — produces CAUTIOUS CONCERN. C is correct. A is wrong (the author doesn't stop at encouragement). B is wrong (the progress is genuine). D is wrong (the passage is not neutral — it takes a clear position on adequacy).

quiz.q:
Passage: 'Dr. Semmelweis published his findings demonstrating that handwashing reduced maternal mortality by more than 80%. His colleagues dismissed his work, continued their contaminated practices, and Semmelweis died in an asylum — ironically, from an infection. The medical establishment he had sought to enlighten took another generation to accept what he had already proven. When we speak of 'evidence-based medicine' today, we would do well to remember that the evidence can be readily available and the medicine still catastrophically wrong.'

The author's attitude toward the medical establishment's rejection of Semmelweis's findings is best described as
o: Sharply critical, with the irony of Semmelweis's death used to intensify the critique
Sympathetically understanding of why doctors might resist new evidence
Cautiously optimistic that modern medicine has learned from this mistake
Neutral and objective, presenting the historical facts without judgment
quiz.e: 'The medical establishment he had sought to enlighten took another generation to accept' is already critical. 'Ironically, from an infection' uses irony to sharpen the critique dramatically. The final sentence ('evidence can be readily available and the medicine still catastrophically wrong') maintains the critical tone. B is correct. A is wrong (no sympathy for the establishment). C is wrong (the language is evaluative and critical, not neutral). D is wrong (the final sentence warns that the problem persists, not that it's been learned from).

quiz.q:
Passage: 'It has become fashionable in some quarters to argue that the humanities are in 'crisis' — that declining enrollments, reduced funding, and employer skepticism signal their irrelevance in a technology-driven economy. This narrative is overdrawn. Humanities graduates demonstrate strong performance in critical thinking, written communication, and ethical reasoning — skills that employers consistently rank among their highest priorities. The crisis, to the extent it is real, is one of perception and marketing, not of value.'

The author's perspective on the humanities 'crisis' is best described as
o: Neutral, presenting arguments both for and against the relevance of the humanities
Alarmed by the genuine decline in humanities enrollment and funding
Nostalgic for an era when the humanities were more central to university education
Skeptical of the crisis narrative, arguing that the humanities' value remains intact even if their public perception has suffered
quiz.e: The author directly dismisses the 'crisis' narrative as 'overdrawn' and provides evidence for humanities graduates' value. The final characterization — crisis of 'perception and marketing, not of value' — shows the author believes the value is real but the image is damaged. B is correct. A is wrong (the author rejects the alarm). C is wrong (the author takes a clear position). D is wrong (no nostalgia is expressed).

quiz.q:
Passage: 'The global ocean conveyor belt — the system of deep and surface currents that redistributes heat around the planet — has shown measurable signs of slowing. Computer models have long predicted this as a consequence of freshwater input from melting glaciers. The potential consequences of significant slowdown include dramatic temperature changes in Northern Europe, disruption of monsoon systems, and sea level rise along certain coastlines. Scientists are careful to note that the current evidence, while concerning, does not indicate imminent collapse — but the direction of change is unambiguous.'

The author's attitude toward ocean conveyor belt slowdown is best described as
o: Dismissive of the evidence, noting that scientists themselves are not alarmed
Enthusiastically reporting that the science on this issue is now settled
Measured concern — noting the signs and potential consequences while accurately reflecting scientific caution about overstatement
quiz.e: The passage notes 'measurable signs' and 'potential consequences' (expressing concern) but explicitly notes scientists say 'evidence... does not indicate imminent collapse' (reflecting appropriate caution). The tone precisely mirrors scientific epistemic standards: concerned but not alarmist. B is correct. A is wrong (the author explicitly says scientists don't predict imminent collapse). C is wrong (the evidence is presented as 'concerning'). D is wrong (the author presents ongoing uncertainty, not settled science).

quizTr.uz: 'Genuinely encouraging' (ijobiy) + 'deeply insufficient' (xavotir) tuzilmasi EHTIYOTKOR XAVOTIRNI beradi — C to'g'ri; A rag'batlantirishda to'xtab qolmaydi, B xato (taraqqiyot haqiqiy), D xato (matn neytral emas).
quizTr.ru: Структура «genuinely encouraging» (позитив) + «deeply insufficient» (тревога) даёт ОСТОРОЖНУЮ ОБЕСПОКОЕННОСТЬ — C верен; A — автор не останавливается на одобрении, B неверен (прогресс реален), D неверен (текст не нейтрален).

quizTr.uz: 'Ironically, from an infection' ironiyasi tanqidni keskin kuchaytiradi, yakuniy jumla tanqidiy ohangni saqlaydi — B to'g'ri; A da establishment'ga hamdardlik yo'q, C xato (til baholovchi), D xato (yakun muammo davom etayotganidan ogohlantiradi).
quizTr.ru: Ирония «Ironically, from an infection» резко заостряет критику, финальная фраза сохраняет критический тон — B верен; A — сочувствия истеблишменту нет, C неверен (язык оценочный), D неверен (финал предупреждает, что проблема жива).

quizTr.uz: Muallif 'inqiroz' hikoyasini 'overdrawn' deb rad etadi: qiymat haqiqiy, zarar ko'rgan — imidj va marketing; B to'g'ri, A xato (muallif vahimani rad etadi), C xato (pozitsiya aniq), D xato (nostalgiya yo'q).
quizTr.ru: Автор отвергает нарратив «кризиса» как «overdrawn»: ценность реальна, пострадали имидж и маркетинг — B верен, A неверен (автор отвергает тревогу), C неверен (позиция ясна), D неверен (ностальгии нет).

quizTr.uz: Matn 'measurable signs' va potensial oqibatlarni qayd etadi, lekin olimlar 'imminent collapse'ni bashorat qilmasligini ham aniq aytadi — ohang xavotirli, ammo vahimasiz; B to'g'ri.
quizTr.ru: Текст отмечает «measurable signs» и возможные последствия, но подчёркивает, что учёные не предрекают «imminent collapse» — тон обеспокоенный, но не паникёрский; B верен.

reading.title: Reading set: Cross-text analysis
reading.text:
Each task below contains its own short passage. Read it closely, then answer — this trains exactly the kind of reading you will meet in real academic texts and exams.

Quyida har bir topshiriqning o'z qisqa matni bor. Diqqat bilan o'qing, so'ng javob bering.

quiz.q:
Text 1: 'The human memory is fundamentally reconstructive, not reproductive. Each time a memory is retrieved, it is rebuilt from fragments and can be altered by subsequent experience, suggestion, and expectation. This means eyewitness testimony is inherently unreliable as legal evidence.'

Text 2: 'While memory is subject to distortion, the degree of unreliability varies considerably with conditions. Highly distinctive, emotionally salient events are encoded and retained more accurately than ordinary ones. Eyewitness testimony for peripheral details is indeed unreliable, but testimony about the central action in a violent crime may be quite accurate.'

How would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the argument in Text 1?
o: By agreeing that eyewitness testimony should never be used as legal evidence
By arguing that legal reforms have already addressed the problem of unreliable eyewitness testimony
By disputing the claim that human memory is reconstructive rather than reproductive
By arguing that Text 1 overgeneralizes — the reliability of eyewitness testimony varies by emotional significance and detail type
quiz.e: Text 2 acknowledges memory distortion ('while memory is subject to distortion') but argues reliability VARIES — emotionally salient events are more accurate, and central actions more reliable than peripheral details. This directly challenges Text 1's blanket conclusion that eyewitness testimony is 'inherently unreliable.' B is correct. A is wrong (Text 2 argues testimony CAN be reliable). C is wrong (Text 2 doesn't dispute reconstruction — it accepts it but argues it varies). D is wrong (legal reforms not mentioned).

quiz.q:
Text 1: 'The concept of 'natural' in food marketing has no scientific basis. 'Natural' flavors can be chemically identical to 'artificial' ones; the difference lies in source, not structure. Regulatory agencies in most countries have declined to define the term, making 'natural' on a food label legally meaningless.'

Text 2: 'Consumer preference for 'natural' products, however scientifically unfounded, is a real and powerful market signal. Companies that ignore it do so at commercial risk. The interesting question is not whether 'natural' is scientifically meaningful but why consumers have developed such strong preferences for naturalness — what psychological and cultural functions the concept serves.'

How would the author of Text 1 most likely respond to the focus of Text 2?
o: By conceding that the scientific meaninglessness of 'natural' is less important than its cultural significance
By suggesting that regulatory agencies should study consumer psychology before defining 'natural'
By arguing that Text 2's acceptance of consumer preferences as a 'market signal' ignores the harm caused by misleading marketing that exploits those preferences
By agreeing that consumer psychology is the most important lens for understanding 'natural' food labeling
quiz.e: Text 1's concern is that 'natural' is misleading and scientifically meaningless. If Text 2 accepts consumer preference as a 'market signal' to be catered to, Text 1's author would argue: this ignores the problem that companies are exploiting a psychologically real but scientifically false belief. B captures this response. A is wrong (Text 1 is critical of the 'natural' concept, not interested in its psychology). C is wrong (Text 1 doesn't concede cultural significance trumps scientific accuracy). D is wrong (not stated).

quiz.q:
Text 1: 'Long-form journalism — deeply reported, book-length magazine features — is in crisis. Digital platforms reward brevity and engagement metrics. Advertisers follow eyeballs. The economic incentives that once sustained thousand-word investigations have largely dissolved.'

Text 2: 'The apparent crisis of long-form journalism is a crisis of the legacy advertising model, not of audience appetite. Newsletter platforms, reader-supported journalism, and podcast adaptations of long-form reporting have found substantial audiences willing to pay directly for in-depth work. The business model has changed; the form may survive.'

Based on Text 2, how would its author most likely respond to the argument in Text 1?
o: By suggesting that brief content is preferable to long-form journalism for modern audiences
By arguing that Text 1 conflates the crisis of the advertising model with the fate of long-form journalism as a form, and that direct-support models suggest the form can persist
By arguing that government subsidy is the only path to saving long-form journalism
By agreeing that long-form journalism is disappearing because of digital platforms
quiz.e: Text 2 explicitly says the crisis is 'of the legacy advertising model, not of audience appetite' — directly responding to Text 1's claim that 'economic incentives have dissolved.' Text 2 argues new models (newsletters, direct support) can sustain the form. B accurately captures this reframe. A is wrong (Text 2 argues the form can survive). C is wrong (Text 2 says audience appetite for long-form remains). D is wrong (Text 2 doesn't mention government subsidy).

quizTr.uz: Text 2 xotira buzilishini tan oladi, lekin ishonchlilik hissiy ahamiyatga qarab FARQ QILISHINI aytib, Text 1 ning 'tabiatan ishonchsiz' degan umumiy xulosasini rad etadi — B to'g'ri.
quizTr.ru: Text 2 признаёт искажения памяти, но утверждает, что надёжность ВАРЬИРУЕТСЯ по эмоциональной значимости, оспаривая общий вывод Text 1 о «принципиальной ненадёжности» — B верен.

quizTr.uz: Text 1 muallifi javob berardi: iste'molchi xohishini 'bozor signali' sifatida qabul qilish kompaniyalar ilmiy asossiz e'tiqodni suiiste'mol qilayotgan zararni e'tiborsiz qoldiradi — B shu javobni qamraydi.
quizTr.ru: Автор Text 1 ответил бы: принятие предпочтений как «рыночного сигнала» игнорирует вред от эксплуатации научно ложного убеждения — B передаёт этот ответ.

quizTr.uz: Text 2 inqiroz 'legacy advertising model'da, auditoriya ishtiyoqida emasligini aytadi va yangi modellar janrni saqlab qolishini ta'kidlaydi — B shu qayta talqinni aniq qamraydi.
quizTr.ru: Text 2 говорит, что кризис — у «legacy advertising model», а не у аудитории, и новые модели сохранят жанр — B точно передаёт этот рефрейминг.

reading.title: Reading set: Rhetorical synthesis
reading.text:
Each task below contains its own short passage. Read it closely, then answer — this trains exactly the kind of reading you will meet in real academic texts and exams.

Quyida har bir topshiriqning o'z qisqa matni bor. Diqqat bilan o'qing, so'ng javob bering.

quiz.q:
Notes:
• Coffee was first cultivated in Ethiopia around the 9th century CE
• Coffee spread to the Arabian Peninsula by the 15th century
• First European coffeehouses opened in the 17th century
• Coffee is now the second most traded commodity globally after crude oil
• Approximately 2 billion cups of coffee are consumed worldwide each day

The student wants to introduce the topic by establishing the global significance of coffee consumption.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes?
o: With approximately 2 billion cups consumed daily, coffee is the second most traded commodity in the world after crude oil, making it one of the most globally significant agricultural products.
Coffee was first cultivated in Ethiopia around the 9th century CE before spreading to the Arabian Peninsula and then Europe.
European coffeehouses, which first opened in the 17th century, played an important role in the development of intellectual and commercial culture.
Coffee has a rich history spanning more than a thousand years, from its origins in Ethiopia to its current global presence.
quiz.e: The goal is to establish GLOBAL SIGNIFICANCE. B uses the two most impactful statistics: 2 billion cups daily AND second most traded commodity — both directly establish significance. A only covers the historical spread (not significance). C focuses on coffeehouses (historical context, not global significance). D is vague and doesn't use specific data to establish significance.

quiz.q:
Notes:
• Polar ice sheets contain approximately 68% of Earth's fresh water
• If all polar ice melted, sea levels would rise approximately 70 meters
• Current sea level rise: about 3.6 mm per year
• 2023 was the hottest year on record globally
• Arctic sea ice extent hit a record low in September 2023

The student wants to support the claim that recent climate data reflects accelerating change.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes?
o: The record global temperatures of 2023 and the concurrent record low Arctic sea ice extent represent evidence of accelerating change in Earth's climate systems.
If all polar ice melted, sea levels would rise approximately 70 meters — a scenario that would threaten most coastal cities worldwide.
Polar ice sheets hold approximately 68% of Earth's fresh water, meaning their complete melting would raise sea levels by approximately 70 meters.
Sea levels are currently rising at approximately 3.6 millimeters per year, and polar ice sheets contain approximately 68% of Earth's fresh water.
quiz.e: The goal is to support 'accelerating change' using RECENT DATA. B uses 2023 record temperatures and record low Arctic sea ice — both from 2023 and explicitly described as 'accelerating change.' A uses the ice volume and sea level rise potential — not recent trend data. C uses current sea level rise rate and ice volume — not the most recent record-breaking data. D projects the total melt scenario — future speculation, not recent trend evidence.

quiz.q:
Notes:
• Library of Congress holds approximately 173 million items
• Founded in 1800; originally served US Congress
• Now open to the public — no library card required for on-site research
• Holds the first map to use the name 'America' (1507)
• Holds Stradivari violins and active string quartet performances

The student wants to emphasize the Library of Congress's unexpected breadth — that it holds far more than books and documents.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes?
o: Founded in 1800, the Library of Congress holds approximately 173 million items and has evolved from a congressional resource to a public institution.

While the Library of Congress holds the historic 1507 map that first named 'America,' its collections extend far beyond historical documents to include Stradivari violins — instruments still used in active performances hosted by the institution.
The Library of Congress holds 173 million items and is open to the public without requiring a library card for on-site research.
The Library of Congress, founded in 1800 to serve the US Congress, has grown into a public research institution holding approximately 173 million items.
quiz.e: The goal is to emphasize 'unexpected breadth — far more than books and documents.' B presents a progression from a historical document (expected) to Stradivari violins used in live performances (unexpected, non-documentary) — the contrast shows the unexpected breadth perfectly. A focuses on history and size but doesn't show the non-documentary breadth. C mentions size and public access but not the surprising range of collections. D is historical but doesn't show the unexpected breadth.

quiz.q:
Notes:
• Bees pollinate approximately 1/3 of the world's food supply
• Global bee populations have declined 30% in the last decade
• Neonicotinoid pesticides are linked to bee disorientation and colony collapse
• Urban beekeeping has increased 200% in the past five years
• Some urban environments have higher bee health than rural agricultural areas

The student wants to present a surprising finding that complicates the narrative of universal bee decline.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes?
o: Counterintuitively, some urban environments now support healthier bee populations than adjacent rural agricultural areas — a finding that complicates the narrative of universal decline.
Urban beekeeping has increased by 200% in the past five years, reflecting growing public awareness of the importance of pollinators.
Bees pollinate approximately one-third of the world's food supply, making their documented 30% population decline over the past decade a serious concern for global agriculture.
Neonicotinoid pesticides, widely used in agricultural settings, have been linked to the bee disorientation and colony collapse that have contributed to the 30% population decline.
quiz.e: The goal is to present a SURPRISING FINDING that COMPLICATES the universal decline narrative. C uses the urban/rural health comparison and explicitly frames it as counterintuitive — directly serving the 'complicates the narrative' goal. A presents the decline narrative rather than complicating it. B explains causes of the decline — doesn't complicate the narrative. D notes urban beekeeping growth but doesn't present the surprising health finding.

quizTr.uz: Maqsad — GLOBAL AHAMIYATNI ko'rsatish; B eng ta'sirli ikki statistikani ishlatadi: kuniga 2 milliard piyola VA savdo bo'yicha ikkinchi o'rin; boshqalari ahamiyatni bevosita asoslamaydi.
quizTr.ru: Цель — установить ГЛОБАЛЬНУЮ значимость; B использует две сильнейшие цифры: 2 млрд чашек в день И второе место в мировой торговле; остальные значимость прямо не устанавливают.

quizTr.uz: Maqsad — 'tezlashayotgan o'zgarish'ni ENG YANGI ma'lumotlar bilan asoslash; B 2023-yilgi rekord harorat va rekord past Arktika muzini ishlatadi; boshqalari yaqin trend ma'lumoti emas.
quizTr.ru: Цель — подкрепить «ускоряющиеся изменения» СВЕЖИМИ данными; B берёт рекордные температуры 2023 и рекордно малый арктический лёд; остальные — не свежие трендовые данные.

quizTr.uz: Maqsad — 'kutilmagan kenglik'ni ta'kidlash; B tarixiy 1507 xaritadan jonli ijrolarda ishlatiladigan Stradivari skripkalarigacha kontrast beradi — bu kutilmagan kenglikni mukammal ko'rsatadi.
quizTr.ru: Цель — подчеркнуть «неожиданную широту»; B ведёт от исторической карты 1507 года к скрипкам Stradivari, звучащим на концертах, — контраст идеально показывает неожиданную широту.

quizTr.uz: Maqsad — umumiy pasayish hikoyasini MURAKKABLASHTIRUVCHI KUTILMAGAN topilma; C shahar/qishloq salomatlik taqqoslamasini counterintuitive deb aniq keltiradi — boshqalari hikoyani murakkablashtirmaydi.
quizTr.ru: Цель — НЕОЖИДАННЫЙ факт, УСЛОЖНЯЮЩИЙ нарратив всеобщего упадка; C приводит сравнение здоровья город/село и прямо называет его контринтуитивным — остальные нарратив не усложняют.

reading.title: Author's Perspective & Tone
reading.text:
Perspective and tone questions ask about the AUTHOR'S ATTITUDE toward the subject. The question stems are: 'The author's attitude toward X can best be described as...' or 'Which choice best describes the author's perspective on Y?' Unlike purpose questions (which ask WHAT the author is doing), perspective questions ask HOW the author FEELS about the topic. The range of possible tones includes: critical, skeptical, alarmed, cautious, neutral/objective, celebratory, admiring, nostalgic, ironic, satirical, reluctantly accepting, cautiously optimistic.

The key strategy is to find EVALUATIVE LANGUAGE — adjectives, adverbs, and verbs that signal the author's feelings. 'Unfortunately,' 'remarkably,' 'troublingly,' 'merely,' 'only,' 'despite,' 'yet' — these small words carry tonal weight. Also look for WHAT THE AUTHOR CHOOSES TO EMPHASIZE: if an author describes both positive and negative aspects of something but devotes more space and stronger language to the negatives, the overall tone is critical. If the author acknowledges flaws but concludes with praise, the tone is measured admiration.

Common traps in tone questions: (1) CONFUSING TOPIC TONE with AUTHOR'S TONE — a passage about a tragic event can be written in a clinical, detached tone. The author's attitude is not necessarily emotional just because the topic is emotional. (2) TOO EXTREME vs. TOO MILD — if the author expresses concern, 'alarmed' may be too strong and 'interested' too mild. Look for the precision of fit. (3) SINGLE-SENTENCE BIAS — don't identify the tone from one sentence. Read the complete passage before committing. (4) CONFUSING REPORTED ATTITUDE with AUTHOR'S ATTITUDE — if the author says 'critics argue X is wrong,' the CRITICS' view is negative, but the author may be neutral or even supportive of X.

Key points:
• Evaluative language: 'unfortunately,' 'remarkably,' 'merely,' 'troublingly,' 'despite'
• Emphasis = attitude: more space + stronger words on X = author values/criticizes X
• Tone precision: 'concerned' vs. 'alarmed' vs. 'distressed' — choose the best fit
• Reported attitude ≠ author's attitude: critics say X is wrong ≠ author says X is wrong
• Conclusion matters: how does the passage END? That often reveals final attitude
• Neutral: facts presented without evaluative language, no clear position
• Ironic: says one thing but means another, often via understatement or paradox

quiz.q:
Passage: 'The speed at which artificial intelligence systems are being deployed across critical sectors — healthcare, criminal justice, financial lending — has dramatically outpaced the development of oversight frameworks. Regulators, themselves often lacking technical expertise, are attempting to govern technologies they do not fully understand, while the companies deploying these systems have minimal incentives to slow their own expansion. The result has been a troubling series of documented failures: biased medical diagnostic tools, racially skewed criminal sentencing algorithms, and discriminatory lending models deployed to millions of users before their flaws were identified.'

The author's attitude toward the current deployment of AI systems can best be described as
o: Cautiously optimistic about AI's long-term potential
Deeply concerned about the gap between deployment speed and adequate oversight
Neutral and objective in presenting both benefits and risks of AI
Nostalgic for a time before AI systems were used in critical decisions
quiz.e: ' The author presents NO positive aspects of AI deployment in this passage — only failures and oversight gaps. B is correct. A is wrong (no optimism is expressed). C is wrong (the author is not neutral — the language is strongly critical). D is wrong (no nostalgic longing for a pre-AI time is expressed).

quiz.q:
Passage: 'Gene therapy — the technique of correcting defective genes to treat disease — has made remarkable strides in recent years. Several previously untreatable genetic conditions now have approved therapies, and clinical trials for dozens more are underway. Yet the field remains young, the cost of treatments prohibitively expensive for most patients globally, and the long-term durability of corrections in many conditions is still being established. The promise of gene therapy is genuine, but the distance between current capabilities and the transformative medicine its advocates envision remains considerable.'

The author's perspective on gene therapy can best be described as
o: Enthusiastically supportive of gene therapy's achievements
Skeptical that gene therapy will ever achieve its promise
Cautiously optimistic, acknowledging both genuine achievements and significant remaining limitations
Neutral and detached, presenting information without evaluation
quiz.e: .. remains considerable'). The structure — achievements then limitations, ending with a note of remaining challenge — produces CAUTIOUS OPTIMISM. C is correct. A is wrong (the author's final note is about the 'considerable distance' remaining — not pure enthusiasm). B is wrong (the author does say the promise is 'genuine,' not that it will never be achieved). D is wrong (the language 'remarkable strides,' 'genuine promise' is evaluative, not neutral).

quiz.q:
Passage: 'Tech industry executives frequently describe their platforms as neutral conduits for information, arguing that they merely provide infrastructure for human communication and bear no more responsibility for their content than a telephone company bears for conversations on its lines. Legal scholars and regulators, however, increasingly argue that this analogy is false: unlike telephone companies, platforms actively curate, recommend, and algorithmically amplify content, shaping what users see in ways that traditional common carrier models were never designed to address.'

The author's own attitude toward the tech industry's 'neutral conduit' claim is best described as
o: Supportive of the tech industry's position that platforms should not be regulated
Skeptical of the claim, as shown by the author's framing and the final contrast
Neutral, presenting both positions without indicating a preference
Alarmed that tech platforms are actively censoring communication
quiz.e: The executives' position is described as their own claim ('describe,' 'arguing'). The legal scholars' counterargument is introduced as 'however,' and the refutation is specific: 'this analogy is false' and 'platforms ACTIVELY curate' — the word 'actively' contrasted with the 'neutral conduit' claim shows the author sides with the critics. B is correct. A is wrong (the author doesn't support the industry position). C is wrong (the framing is not neutral — 'this analogy is false' is a strong evaluative statement). D is wrong (the passage is about algorithmic amplification/curation, not censorship).

quiz.q:
Passage: 'The discovery that RNA could catalyze biochemical reactions — once thought to be the exclusive province of proteins — opened up entirely new research directions in molecular biology. The 'RNA world' hypothesis that followed offered an elegant potential solution to the chicken-and-egg problem of life's origins: which came first, the DNA that stores genetic information or the proteins that act on that information? RNA could, in principle, do both. The hypothesis remains controversial, with competing models and unresolved questions, but it has inspired decades of productive experimental work and fundamentally changed how scientists think about the origins of life.'

The author's attitude toward the RNA world hypothesis can best be described as
o: Fully convinced that the RNA world hypothesis correctly explains life's origins
Critical of the hypothesis for remaining unresolved after decades of research
Appreciative of the hypothesis's intellectual contribution despite its unresolved status
Alarmed that scientists have not yet resolved the question of life's origins
quiz.e: ' Simultaneously, the author acknowledges that it 'remains controversial, with competing models and unresolved questions.' This combination — genuine appreciation for a hypothesis's intellectual contribution + honest acknowledgment of its limitations — is APPRECIATIVE/ADMIRING DESPITE LIMITATIONS. C is the most precise. A is wrong ('remains controversial' shows the author doesn't claim full conviction). B is wrong (the author does not criticize it for being unresolved — the decades of inspired work are presented positively). D is wrong (no alarm is expressed about unresolved questions).

quiz.q:
Passage: 'The consulting firm's 400-page report on improving organizational communication at the company arrived six months late, was distributed only to senior executives who had already left the organization, and concluded — after extensive interviews, surveys, and data collection — that the primary obstacle to effective communication was that employees felt their concerns were not heard by senior management. The report recommended forming a working group to study the issue further.'

The author's attitude toward the consulting report can best be described as
o: Admiring of the thoroughness and rigor of the consulting process
Ironically critical, using the report's own outcomes to expose its absurdity
Alarmed by the specific findings about employee concerns
Neutral and objective in describing what happened
quiz.e: The accumulation of absurdities — without the author ever directly saying 'this was useless' — creates sharp ironic critique. B is correct. A is wrong (no admiration is expressed — the details mock the process). C is wrong (the specific finding about employees is presented as part of the irony, not as something alarming). D is wrong (the selection of these specific absurd details is not neutral — the author is clearly critiquing).

quizTr.uz: Muallif AI joriy etishning birorta ijobiy jihatini keltirmaydi — faqat muvaffaqiyatsizliklar va nazorat bo'shliqlari; B to'g'ri: optimizm ham, neytrallik ham, nostalgiya ham yo'q.
quizTr.ru: Автор не приводит ни одного плюса внедрения AI — только провалы и пробелы надзора; B верен: ни оптимизма, ни нейтральности, ни ностальгии нет.

quizTr.uz: Yutuqlar, so'ng cheklovlar va qolgan 'katta masofa' haqidagi yakun EHTIYOTKOR OPTIMIZMNI beradi — C to'g'ri; A sof ishtiyoq emas, B 'genuine promise'ga zid, D xato (til baholovchi, neytral emas).
quizTr.ru: Структура «достижения, затем ограничения и оставшийся путь» даёт ОСТОРОЖНЫЙ ОПТИМИЗМ — C верен; A — не чистый энтузиазм, B противоречит «genuine promise», D неверен (язык оценочный, не нейтральный).

quizTr.uz: 'This analogy is false' va 'platforms ACTIVELY curate' iboralari muallif tanqidchilar tomonida ekanini ko'rsatadi — B to'g'ri; A sanoat pozitsiyasini qo'llamaydi, C xato (bayon neytral emas), D senzura haqida emas.
quizTr.ru: «This analogy is false» и «platforms ACTIVELY curate» показывают, что автор на стороне критиков — B верен; A — автор не поддерживает индустрию, C неверен (подача не нейтральна), D — не о цензуре.

quizTr.uz: Gipotezaning intellektual hissasiga samimiy hurmat + hal etilmagan holatini halol tan olish — C ('cheklovlariga qaramay qadrlaydi') eng aniq; A xato ('remains controversial' to'liq ishonchni istisno qiladi), B da tanqid yo'q, D da xavotir yo'q.
quizTr.ru: Искреннее признание интеллектуального вклада гипотезы + честное признание её нерешённости — C («ценит вопреки ограничениям») точнее всех; A неверен («remains controversial» исключает полную убеждённость), B — критики нет, D — тревоги нет.

quizTr.uz: Muallif 'bu befoyda edi' demasdan absurdlarni to'plab, o'tkir istehzoli tanqid yaratadi — B to'g'ri; A da hayrat yo'q (detallar jarayonni masxara qiladi), C xato (topilma ironiyaning qismi), D xato (detallar tanlovi neytral emas).
quizTr.ru: Накопление абсурдов без прямых слов «это было бесполезно» создаёт острую ироническую критику — B верен; A — восхищения нет (детали высмеивают процесс), C неверен (факт — часть иронии), D неверен (отбор деталей не нейтрален).

reading.title: Paired Passages — Understanding the Relationship
reading.text:
Cross-text questions present TWO SHORT PASSAGES by different authors and ask about the relationship between them. The exam includes several paired passage sets per test. The most important first step: before answering any question, identify the RELATIONSHIP between the two texts. The four main relationships are: (1) AGREEMENT — both authors share the same position; (2) DISAGREEMENT/CONTRAST — the authors take opposing views on the same topic; (3) COMPLEMENTARY — the texts address different aspects of the same topic without directly contradicting each other; (4) EXTENSION — Text 2 builds on, develops, or applies what Text 1 establishes.

The most common cross-text question type asks: 'How would the author of Text 1 most likely respond to the argument in Text 2?' or 'Based on the texts, both authors would most likely agree that...' For these questions, you must first identify each author's POSITION and then determine whether they would AGREE, DISAGREE, or have MIXED views. The trap: texts on the same topic can share vocabulary and examples while taking very different positions. Always identify the central CLAIM of each text before comparing them.

For AGREEMENT questions: find a statement that BOTH authors would endorse — not something one says explicitly and the other might possibly support, but something both clearly imply or argue. For DISAGREEMENT questions: find the exact point of divergence — on WHAT SPECIFIC ISSUE do the authors disagree? Two authors can agree on the facts but disagree on interpretation; agree on the problem but disagree on the solution; or disagree on fundamental assumptions.

Key points:
• Step 1: Identify each author's central CLAIM before comparing
• Step 2: Map the relationship (agree / disagree / complement / extend)
• Agreement: both clearly support — not just 'might possibly support'
• Disagreement: find the EXACT point of divergence, not just different topics
• How would Author 1 respond? = find the overlap/gap between their positions
• Trap: same topic + same vocabulary ≠ same position
• Trap: authors can agree on facts but disagree on interpretation or implications

quiz.q:
Text 1: 'Social media platforms should be regulated like public utilities because they have become essential infrastructure for public discourse. Just as telephone companies cannot discriminate in providing service, social media companies should be required to host all legal speech without algorithmic discrimination.'

Text 2: 'Treating social media platforms as public utilities misunderstands their nature. Unlike telephone networks, which passively transmit communication, social media platforms actively curate and amplify content. This editorial function is itself constitutionally protected expression — requiring platforms to host all speech regardless of content would effectively compel speech, which the First Amendment prohibits.'

Based on these texts, the authors would most likely disagree about which of the following?
o: Whether social media has become an important part of public life
Whether social media platforms actively curate the content they display
Whether the public utility model is appropriate for regulating social media platforms
Whether telephone companies are regulated in the United States
quiz.e: Text 2 ARGUES AGAINST it, specifically because platforms curate content (unlike passive telephone networks). Their disagreement is directly about whether the public utility regulatory model is appropriate for social media. C is correct. A is not a point of disagreement (both imply social media matters). B is actually a point of AGREEMENT (Text 2 explicitly says platforms 'actively curate,' while Text 1 implies editorial function by saying 'algorithmic discrimination'). D is not discussed as a point of disagreement.

quiz.q:
Text 1: 'Standardized tests like the exam were originally designed to identify talented students from non-elite backgrounds who lacked access to prestigious preparation. In practice, however, test scores correlate strongly with family income, primarily because wealthier families can afford test preparation courses, tutors, and multiple retakes. The test has become a mechanism for reproducing the privilege it was designed to disrupt.'

Text 2: 'Research consistently shows that exam scores, when combined with high school GPA, predict college performance better than either measure alone. The test provides colleges with a standardized metric that supplements the varying standards of thousands of high schools nationwide. Eliminating the exam from admissions without an equally valid alternative would reduce predictive accuracy.'

Based on Text 1, how would its author most likely respond to the argument in Text 2?
o: By agreeing that the exam's predictive validity justifies its continued use in admissions
