By arguing that even if the exam predicts college performance, this predictive validity does not address the concern that it reproduces economic inequality in admissions
By suggesting that high school GPA is a more reliable predictor than the exam
By conceding that no alternative to standardized testing currently exists
quiz.e: Text 2 argues the exam predicts college performance. The Author of Text 1 would most likely say: 'Even if the exam predicts performance, this doesn't address my concern about inequality.' B captures this response perfectly. A is wrong (Text 1 is clearly critical of the exam). C is wrong (Text 1 doesn't mention GPA). D is wrong (Text 1 doesn't discuss alternatives).

quiz.q:
Text 1: 'The global decline in insect populations poses an existential threat to agricultural systems. Insects pollinate approximately 75% of flowering crops; without them, yields would collapse. The primary drivers — pesticide use, habitat loss, and climate change — are all human-caused and could be addressed through policy reform.'

Text 2: 'While much attention has focused on iconic endangered species like polar bears and tigers, the quieter collapse of insect biodiversity may ultimately prove more consequential for human welfare. Insects sit at the base of most terrestrial food chains. Their decline cascades upward, affecting birds, mammals, and ultimately the agricultural systems that feed eight billion people.'

Based on both texts, what would both authors most likely agree on?
o: That polar bears and tigers receive too much attention relative to insects
That pesticide use is the primary cause of insect population decline
That the decline of insect populations poses a serious threat to human food systems
That policy reform is the most effective solution to insect population collapse
quiz.e: ' C is correct. A is only from Text 2 and is not in Text 1. B is only from Text 1 (Text 2 doesn't identify pesticides specifically). D is only from Text 1 (Text 2 makes no policy claim).

quiz.q:
Text 1: 'Research on expert performance consistently challenges the intuition that talent is innate. Studies of musicians, chess players, and athletes show that practice hours — specifically deliberate, goal-directed practice — predict performance far better than any measured trait present at birth. The 10,000-hour figure, while an oversimplification, captures something real: expertise takes sustained effort.'

Text 2: 'The 'deliberate practice explains everything' model now faces significant pushback. Subsequent meta-analyses of the original studies found that deliberate practice explains approximately 26% of the variance in expert performance in games, 21% in music, and only 18% in sports. Something else — likely including domain-specific aptitude, early developmental exposure, and motivational factors — accounts for the majority of variance.'

Which choice best describes the relationship between the two texts?
o: Text 2 fully confirms and extends the argument made in Text 1
Text 2 challenges the strength of the central claim in Text 1 by presenting subsequent research that shows deliberate practice is less explanatory than originally claimed
The two texts address completely different topics and cannot be directly compared
Text 2 presents the same argument as Text 1 but focuses specifically on sports performance
quiz.e: Text 2 presents later research showing practice explains only 18-26% of variance — CHALLENGING the 'practice explains everything' model. B correctly describes Text 2 as challenging Text 1's claim using subsequent research. A is wrong (Text 2 challenges, not confirms). C is wrong (both address expert performance). D is wrong (they present different arguments).

quiz.q:
Text 1: 'The Roman Empire's engineering achievements — roads, aqueducts, sewage systems — enabled the remarkable administrative efficiency that sustained a polity spanning three continents. Without reliable infrastructure, the communication and supply chains that held the empire together could not have functioned.'

Text 2: 'Roman military dominance rested not only on tactical innovation but on institutional design: the professional legionary system created disciplined, standardized fighting forces that could be deployed reliably across diverse terrain. The empire conquered and held territory through organizational excellence as much as battlefield prowess.'

Which choice best describes the relationship between the two texts?
o: The texts disagree about whether Roman engineering or military power was more important
Text 2 directly counters the central claim in Text 1
The texts complement each other, both arguing that Roman success depended on systematic organization rather than any single genius or advantage
Text 1 provides the historical context for the argument Text 2 makes about Roman military tactics
quiz.e: Neither contradicts the other — they address different domains (civil vs. military) but share a common thesis about systematic excellence. C is correct. A is wrong (neither text makes a comparative 'more important' claim). B is wrong (Text 2 doesn't counter Text 1 — they address different aspects). D is wrong (Text 1 doesn't provide context for Text 2's argument).

quizTr.uz: Kelishmovchilik aynan public utility modeli ijtimoiy tarmoqlarni tartibga solishga mosligi haqida — C to'g'ri; A kelishmovchilik nuqtasi emas, B aslida KELISHUV nuqtasi, D muhokama qilinmaydi.
quizTr.ru: Спор именно о том, уместна ли модель public utility для регулирования соцсетей — C верен; A — не предмет спора, B — на деле точка СОГЛАСИЯ, D не обсуждается.

quizTr.uz: Text 1 muallifi aytardi: 'imtihon natijani bashorat qilsa ham, bu mening tengsizlik haqidagi xavotirimni hal qilmaydi' — B shu javobni aniq qamraydi; A xato, C GPA aytilmagan, D muqobillar muhokama qilinmagan.
quizTr.ru: Автор Text 1 сказал бы: «даже если экзамен предсказывает успеваемость, это не снимает моей претензии о неравенстве» — B точно передаёт этот ответ; A неверен, C — GPA не упомянут, D — альтернативы не обсуждаются.

quizTr.uz: C to'g'ri — ikkala matn hasharotlar sonining kamayishi oziq-ovqat tizimlariga jiddiy xavf ekaniga qo'shiladi; A faqat Text 2 da, B va D faqat Text 1 da.
quizTr.ru: C верен — оба текста согласны, что сокращение насекомых серьёзно угрожает продовольственным системам; A — только в Text 2, B и D — только в Text 1.

quizTr.uz: Text 2 keyingi tadqiqotni keltiradi (mashq atigi 18-26% farqni tushuntiradi) va Text 1 ning markaziy da'vosini SHUBHA OSTIGA oladi — B buni to'g'ri tasvirlaydi; A xato (tasdiqlamaydi), C xato, D xato.
quizTr.ru: Text 2 приводит позднейшие исследования (практика объясняет лишь 18-26% дисперсии), ОСПАРИВАЯ центральный тезис Text 1 — B описывает это верно; A неверен (не подтверждает), C и D неверны.

quizTr.uz: Matnlar bir-birini to'ldiradi: turli sohalarni (fuqarolik va harbiy) yoritsa-da, muvaffaqiyat tizimli tashkilotchilikka bog'liq degan umumiy tezisni baham ko'radi — C to'g'ri.
quizTr.ru: Тексты дополняют друг друга: освещая разные сферы (гражданскую и военную), они разделяют общий тезис о системной организации как основе успеха — C верен.

reading.title: Answering Cross-Text Questions Precisely
reading.text:
For 'How would Author 1 respond to Text 2?' questions, follow a strict three-step process: (1) IDENTIFY Author 1's central position precisely — not just the topic, but the specific claim. (2) IDENTIFY what Text 2 actually argues — again, the specific claim, not just the topic. (3) Apply Author 1's position to Text 2's argument: would Author 1 agree, partially agree, or disagree, and on what specific grounds? The answer must be grounded in BOTH texts — not in general knowledge about the topic.

Common traps in 'How would Author 1 respond?' questions: (1) The answer accurately describes Author 1's position but doesn't actually respond to Text 2's specific argument. (2) The answer correctly identifies a disagreement but mischaracterizes the REASON for it. (3) The answer has Author 1 agreeing with an element of Text 2 that Author 1 never actually addresses. (4) The answer describes what AUTHOR 2 would say, not Author 1. Always re-read the question to confirm which author you're being asked about.

For 'Both authors would agree that...' questions: eliminate answers that are from only ONE author. The correct answer must be something that BOTH texts independently support — not just something consistent with one and not contradicted by the other. 'Not contradicted by' is weaker than 'supported by.' The correct answer should be something you could point to evidence for in BOTH texts.

Key points:
• Step 1: Author 1's exact claim | Step 2: Text 2's exact claim | Step 3: Match/clash
• Trap: answer describes Author 1's position but doesn't respond to Text 2's SPECIFIC argument
• Trap: confuses which author you're asked about (re-read the question!)
• Agreement: find evidence in BOTH texts — not just 'not contradicted by one'
• Partial agreement: one author endorses the facts but disputes the interpretation
• Point the specific line in each text that supports your answer choice
• Wrong: Author 1 agrees with something Text 2 says that Author 1 never addresses

quiz.q:
Text 1: 'The growing use of facial recognition technology by law enforcement agencies presents a serious civil liberties threat. Current systems misidentify Black individuals at rates up to 34% higher than white individuals, creating systematic racial bias in policing. Until this accuracy gap is closed, facial recognition should not be used in any law enforcement context.'

Text 2: 'Facial recognition technology, properly deployed, can significantly improve law enforcement efficiency and accuracy. When used to generate investigative leads — not as standalone proof of identity — and when combined with human review, it can help solve serious crimes that would otherwise go unpunished. The question is not whether to use the technology but how to regulate its use appropriately.'

Based on Text 1, how would its author most likely respond to the argument in Text 2?
o: By agreeing that facial recognition is useful for generating investigative leads
By arguing that even properly regulated use of facial recognition cannot address the underlying accuracy disparity that disproportionately harms Black individuals
By suggesting that human review is sufficient to overcome the technology's accuracy problems
By conceding that facial recognition has legitimate uses but calling for stronger privacy regulations
quiz.e: Text 2 argues for regulated, human-reviewed use. Author of Text 1 would say: even regulated use doesn't fix the accuracy disparity that creates racial bias. B directly applies Text 1's specific concern (accuracy gap + racial harm) to Text 2's proposal. A is wrong (Text 1 calls for no law enforcement use at all). C is wrong (Text 1 doesn't accept human review as a sufficient fix). D is wrong (Text 1 doesn't endorse 'legitimate uses with regulation').

quiz.q:
Text 1: 'Universal basic income would provide workers with genuine bargaining power: knowing they have an income floor, they could leave exploitative employment rather than endure it. This freedom from economic coercion would improve wages and conditions across the economy through market competition rather than regulation.'

Text 2: 'A universal basic income could provide economic security for individuals facing job displacement from automation. However, the amount required to replace existing welfare programs and provide a genuine living floor would cost trillions annually — a fiscal reality that makes truly universal and adequate UBI politically and economically impractical in most nations in the near term.'

Based on both texts, what would both authors most likely agree on?
o: That UBI would be economically sustainable with appropriate fiscal planning
That UBI could provide beneficial economic security for individuals in certain circumstances
That UBI should replace existing welfare programs
That automation is the primary justification for implementing a UBI
quiz.e: Text 2 says UBI 'could provide economic security for individuals facing job displacement.' Both acknowledge UBI's potential to provide beneficial economic security. B is the shared point. A is wrong (only Text 1 implies sustainability; Text 2 argues it's fiscally impractical). C is wrong (only Text 2 mentions replacing welfare programs — and questions it). D is wrong (only Text 2 mentions automation; Text 1 focuses on labor bargaining power).

quiz.q:
Text 1: 'Ancient Greek democracy was profoundly limited by modern standards: it excluded women, enslaved people, and non-citizens — the majority of the resident population. To call Athenian democracy a 'democracy' without qualification is to accept the Greeks' own self-description uncritically.'

Text 2: 'Whatever its exclusions, Athenian democracy represented a genuine conceptual breakthrough: the idea that a political community could be self-governing, that citizens had both the right and the obligation to participate directly in decisions affecting them. The exclusions were real but were features of their time, not of the democratic concept itself.'

Based on Text 2, how would its author most likely respond to the argument in Text 1?
o: By agreeing that Athenian democracy should not be called a democracy at all
By conceding that the exclusions were severe while arguing that they don't negate the genuine conceptual innovation of democratic self-governance
By arguing that women and enslaved people had more political influence than Text 1 acknowledges
By suggesting that modern democracy has also failed to include all people equally
quiz.e: B precisely captures this 'concede the facts, defend the concept' response. A is wrong (Text 2 defends calling it democracy). C is wrong (Text 2 doesn't make this argument). D is wrong (Text 2 doesn't mention modern democracy).

quizTr.uz: Text 1 muallifi aytardi: tartibga solingan foydalanish ham irqiy zarar keltiruvchi aniqlik farqini tuzatmaydi — B Text 1 ning aynan shu xavotirini Text 2 taklifiga qo'llaydi; A, C va D Text 1 pozitsiyasiga mos emas.
quizTr.ru: Автор Text 1 сказал бы: даже регулируемое применение не устраняет разрыв в точности, порождающий расовый вред — B применяет именно это возражение к предложению Text 2; A, C и D не соответствуют его позиции.

quizTr.uz: Ikkala matn ham UBI ma'lum sharoitlarda foydali iqtisodiy xavfsizlik berishi mumkinligini tan oladi — B umumiy nuqta; A faqat Text 1 da, C va D faqat Text 2 da.
quizTr.ru: Оба текста признают, что UBI может дать полезную экономическую защищённость в определённых условиях — B и есть общая точка; A — только Text 1, C и D — только Text 2.

quizTr.uz: B 'faktlarni tan ol, konsepsiyani himoya qil' javobini aniq qamraydi: istisnolar og'ir edi, lekin ular haqiqiy konseptual yangilikni bekor qilmaydi; A, C va D Text 2 ga mos emas.
quizTr.ru: B точно передаёт ход «признать факты, защитить концепцию»: исключения были суровы, но не отменяют подлинного концептуального новшества; A, C и D не соответствуют Text 2.

reading.title: Rhetorical Effectiveness — Adding, Deleting & Placement
reading.text:
Some of the exam's hardest questions ask whether a sentence SHOULD BE ADDED or DELETED, or WHERE a sentence should be placed. For ADDING: a sentence should be added only if it directly supports the paragraph's central purpose — not if it's merely related to the general topic. Ask: does this sentence provide specific support for the argument being made, or does it introduce a tangential idea? Adding tangential information, no matter how interesting, weakens a focused paragraph.

For DELETING: a sentence should be deleted if it (a) contradicts the paragraph's point, (b) introduces information already covered elsewhere, (c) digresses from the focus, or (d) is too general to serve as evidence. The question usually asks 'Should this sentence be kept or deleted? Why?' The correct answer identifies the SPECIFIC FUNCTION the sentence serves (or fails to serve) in its paragraph. Vague answers like 'it adds detail' are usually wrong — the detail must be the RIGHT KIND.

For PLACEMENT: a sentence fits best where (a) the content logically follows what precedes it, (b) the transition words connect to the surrounding context, and (c) it leads naturally into what follows. Look for CONTENT BRIDGES — the new sentence's subject or key terms should connect to terms introduced just before the target location. Also check whether the sentence's transition signals (however, furthermore, for example) match the logical relationship needed at that point.

Key points:
• Add only if: directly supports the paragraph's specific argument
• Delete if: tangential, contradicts, repeats, or too general to serve as evidence
• Placement: where content bridges are strongest (key terms connect before and after)
• Transition test: does 'however/furthermore/for example' fit the relationship needed?
• Wrong add answer: 'it provides interesting information' — must be RELEVANT information
• Correct delete reason: 'it shifts focus from X to Y' — specific, not vague
• Always consider the PARAGRAPH'S PURPOSE before evaluating a sentence

quiz.q:
Paragraph: 'Urban heat islands occur when cities trap heat due to pavement, buildings, and reduced vegetation. Studies show they can raise urban temperatures by 2-5°C above surrounding rural areas. [Proposed addition: The history of city planning dates back to ancient Mesopotamia.] This temperature difference increases energy demand for cooling and worsens air quality.'

Should the proposed sentence be added?
o: Yes — it provides useful background context about urban development
Yes — it explains why cities have become more vulnerable to heat islands
No — it shifts focus from the specific problem being discussed (heat islands) to a broadly related but irrelevant historical topic
No — it contradicts the claim that heat islands are caused by modern development
quiz.e: The history of ancient city planning does not support or advance this argument — it's merely topically adjacent to 'cities.' C correctly identifies the reason: it shifts focus to an irrelevant topic. A and B are wrong because relevance requires direct support, not just general connection.

quiz.q:
Paragraph: '[1] Citizen science projects have expanded dramatically in the past decade. [2] Thousands of volunteers contribute observations to research on bird migration, water quality, and galaxy classification. [3] However, data quality concerns have limited their use in peer-reviewed research. [4] Some studies have found error rates significantly higher than in professionally collected data.'

Where should the following sentence be inserted: 'These accuracy concerns have prompted researchers to develop new verification protocols'?
quiz.e: After S4 is most logical. C (after S3) would place it before the specific error rate evidence.

quiz.q:
Paragraph: 'The Amazon rainforest stores approximately 150-200 billion tons of carbon, making it critical to global climate stability. Deforestation releases this stored carbon and simultaneously eliminates the forest's future carbon absorption capacity. [Sentence X: The Amazon basin also contains the world's largest river by discharge volume.] Both effects compound over time, accelerating the pace of climate change.'

Should Sentence X be kept or deleted?
o: Kept — it provides important geographical context for the Amazon's global significance
Kept — it explains why the Amazon river contributes to carbon storage
Deleted — it introduces a geographical fact that does not connect to the paragraph's focus on carbon and climate
Deleted — it contradicts the paragraph's claim about the Amazon's size
quiz.e: The Amazon river's discharge volume is a geographical fact that doesn't connect to carbon, deforestation, or climate change. C correctly identifies the reason: it doesn't connect to the paragraph's focus. A is wrong — geographic significance doesn't serve the carbon/climate argument. B is wrong — the river discharge doesn't explain carbon storage.

quiz.q:
Passage: 'Traditional economic models assume that consumers make rational decisions to maximize utility. [___], behavioral economics has demonstrated that humans consistently make predictable irrational choices — influenced by framing, loss aversion, and cognitive biases.'

Which transition best completes the text?
quiz.e: CONTRAST → However. C is correct. A (furthermore) adds; doesn't contrast. B (therefore) shows a result — but behavioral economics isn't a result of traditional models. D (for example) introduces an example.

quiz.q:
Paragraph: 'The gig economy has created flexible employment for millions but also introduced new forms of economic precarity. Without benefits like health insurance, workers bear greater individual risk. Income volatility makes long-term financial planning difficult. [Proposed conclusion: These challenges suggest that existing labor regulations, designed for traditional employment relationships, may be inadequate for the gig economy.]

Should this concluding sentence be added?
o: No — the paragraph already makes a conclusion about the gig economy
Yes — it explicitly connects the specific problems described to a broader policy implication, providing the paragraph a meaningful conclusion
No — it introduces new information about labor regulations that is outside the scope of the paragraph
Yes — any concluding sentence improves a paragraph's structure
quiz.e: ' The proposed sentence connects these specific observations to a broader, relevant implication — inadequacy of existing labor law. B correctly identifies this function. A is wrong — the paragraph has no current conclusion. C is wrong — connecting to labor regulations is directly relevant to the problems described. D is too generic.

quizTr.uz: Qadimgi shahar rejalashtirish tarixi argumentni qo'llab-quvvatlamaydi — u faqat 'shaharlar' mavzusiga yaqin; C sababni to'g'ri ko'rsatadi: diqqat ahamiyatsiz mavzuga ko'chadi, umumiy bog'liqlik yetarli emas.
quizTr.ru: История древнего градостроительства не продвигает аргумент — она лишь тематически смежна с «городами»; C верно называет причину: фокус уходит на нерелевантную тему, общей связи недостаточно.

quizTr.uz: Eng mantiqiy joy — 4-jumladan keyin; C (3-jumladan keyin) uni xato darajasi haqidagi aniq dalildan oldin joylashtirgan bo'lardi.
quizTr.ru: Логичнее всего — после предложения 4; C (после 3-го) поставил бы его до конкретных данных об уровне ошибок.

quizTr.uz: Amazon daryosining suv oqimi — uglerod, o'rmon kesish va iqlim o'zgarishiga bog'lanmaydigan geografik fakt; C to'g'ri sababni ko'rsatadi: jumla paragraf fokusiga ulanmaydi.
quizTr.ru: Объём стока Amazon — географический факт, не связанный с углеродом, вырубкой и климатом; C верно указывает причину: предложение не связано с фокусом абзаца.

quizTr.uz: QARAMA-QARSHILIK → However; C to'g'ri, A ('furthermore') qo'shadi, qarama-qarshi qo'ymaydi, B ('therefore') natijani bildiradi, D ('for example') misol kiritadi.
quizTr.ru: КОНТРАСТ → However; C верен, A («furthermore») добавляет, а не противопоставляет, B («therefore») выражает следствие, D («for example») вводит пример.

quizTr.uz: Taklif etilgan jumla tasvirlangan aniq muammolarni kengroq siyosiy xulosaga — mavjud mehnat qonunchiligining yetarli emasligiga bog'laydi; B shu funksiyani to'g'ri aniqlaydi, A xato (paragrafda xulosa yo'q), C xato (mavzu bevosita tegishli), D juda umumiy.
quizTr.ru: Предложение связывает описанные проблемы с более широким политическим выводом — неадекватностью трудового права; B верно определяет функцию, A неверен (вывода в абзаце нет), C неверен (тема прямо релевантна), D слишком общий.

reading.title: Rhetorical Purpose & Word Choice at the 800 Level
reading.text:
At the 750-800 level, the exam tests subtle word choice distinctions within a rhetorical context. Words that are nearly synonymous may differ in CONNOTATION (positive, negative, neutral), REGISTER (formal, informal, technical), PRECISION (specific vs. vague), and IMPLICATION (what the word signals about the author's perspective). 'The policy FAILED' vs. 'The policy UNDERPERFORMED' vs. 'The policy DID NOT ACHIEVE ITS STATED GOALS' — each signals a different level of judgment and a different relationship between the author and the subject.

RHETORICAL PURPOSE questions ask: which word or phrase best accomplishes the writer's apparent purpose in this context? The answer depends on understanding: (1) the passage's overall tone (academic/neutral, critical, sympathetic, ironic), (2) the audience (general public, specialists, policymakers), and (3) the paragraph's specific argumentative purpose at this moment. A word appropriate for a personal essay may be wrong in an academic paper. A hedging word ('may suggest') may be wrong when the evidence is conclusive.

TRANSITIONS AS RHETORICAL SIGNALS: beyond grammar, transitions signal the logical structure of the argument. On the exam, transitions are tested not only for grammatical correctness but for RHETORICAL FIT — does this transition accurately signal the logical relationship that exists between the two ideas? 'The evidence is weak; nevertheless, the conclusion is strong' vs. 'The evidence is weak; therefore, the conclusion is strong' — both are grammatically correct; only one is logically accurate. Always check the relationship.

Key points:
• Word choice: consider connotation, register, precision, and implication
• Stronger judgment words: failed, flawed, inadequate vs. underperformed, limited
• Hedging language: may suggest, appears to, could indicate — for uncertain evidence
• Definitive language: demonstrates, confirms, establishes — for strong evidence
• Register: academic paper = formal; op-ed = more direct; technical audience = precise
• Rhetorical purpose: what is this paragraph trying to DO at this moment?
• Transition fit: does the transition accurately reflect the logical relationship?

quiz.q:
Context: A scientific paper discussing a study with mixed results.

Text: 'The intervention [___] the expected outcomes in approximately half the test conditions.'

Which word best fits the formal, measured tone of a scientific report?
quiz.e: B ('did not achieve') is the most formally neutral — it states the outcome without judgment. A ('failed') implies a more definitive negative judgment. C ('bombed') is informal slang. D ('fell disappointingly short') introduces emotional evaluation inappropriate for scientific reporting.

quiz.q:
Context: A passage presenting preliminary research findings.

Text: 'The correlation between screen time and attention deficits [___] a causal relationship.'

Which phrase is most appropriate given that only a correlation (not causation) has been established?
quiz.e: D ('may suggest') appropriately hedges — acknowledging the correlation without claiming causation. A ('proves') and B ('establishes') both overclaim for correlational data. C ('does not indicate') is too dismissive — the correlation does suggest something, just not causation.

quiz.q:
Context: An op-ed arguing for criminal justice reform.

Text: 'The current system [___] those who are most economically disadvantaged, perpetuating cycles of poverty and incarceration.'

Which phrase best fits an op-ed's direct, persuasive register?
o: has been shown in some studies to negatively impact
quiz.e: B ('disproportionately targets') is strong, direct, and uses precise language ('disproportionately' is accurate; 'targets' suggests deliberate structural effect). A and C hedge unnecessarily. D is overly academic and passive for an op-ed.

quiz.q:
Text: 'Historical data shows that economic growth often slows during periods of high inflation. The central bank raised interest rates last month.'

Which transition most accurately connects these sentences?
o: Moreover, the central bank raised interest rates last month.
For example, the central bank raised interest rates last month.
In response to these inflationary pressures, the central bank raised interest rates last month.
Nevertheless, the central bank raised interest rates last month.
quiz.e: The relationship is CAUSE AND EFFECT or CONTEXT TO ACTION: inflation (established in S1) prompted the central bank to act. C ('In response to these inflationary pressures') directly connects the cause to the effect. A ('moreover') adds, doesn't connect cause/effect. B ('for example') makes the rate increase an example of slowing growth — illogical. D ('nevertheless') implies contrast — the bank acted despite the trend.

quiz.q:
Context: A paragraph concluding an argument about the inadequacy of plastic bag bans.

Text: 'The evidence reviewed here [___] that single-use plastic bag bans, while symbolically significant, have not substantially reduced total plastic pollution.'

Which phrase best fits the conclusion of a well-supported argument?
quiz.e: D ('demonstrates') is appropriate for a conclusion where the evidence is presented as definitive. C ('suggests') is appropriate for preliminary or incomplete evidence. A and B are overly hedged for a paragraph presenting its conclusion. Given that the passage says 'evidence reviewed here,' D is appropriately confident.

quizTr.uz: B ('did not achieve') eng rasmiy-neytral — natijani bahosiz bayon qiladi; A ('failed') keskinroq salbiy hukm, C ('bombed') og'zaki sleng, D ilmiy hisobotga mos kelmaydigan hissiy baho kiritadi.
quizTr.ru: B («did not achieve») формально нейтральнее всех — констатирует результат без оценки; A («failed») — более жёсткое суждение, C («bombed») — сленг, D вносит эмоциональную оценку, неуместную в научном отчёте.

quizTr.uz: D ('may suggest') to'g'ri ehtiyotkorlik qiladi: korrelyatsiyani tan olib, sababiyat da'vo qilmaydi; A ('proves') va B ('establishes') korrelyatsion ma'lumot uchun ortiqcha da'vo, C juda inkor etadi.
quizTr.ru: D («may suggest») корректно хеджирует: признаёт корреляцию, не заявляя причинность; A («proves») и B («establishes») переоценивают корреляционные данные, C чрезмерно отрицает.

quizTr.uz: B ('disproportionately targets') kuchli, to'g'ridan-to'g'ri va aniq — op-ed uchun mos; A va C keraksiz yumshatadi, D op-ed uchun ortiqcha akademik va passiv.
quizTr.ru: B («disproportionately targets») — сильно, прямо и точно, как нужно для op-ed; A и C излишне смягчают, D слишком академичен и пассивен.

quizTr.uz: Bog'lanish — SABAB VA HARAKAT: inflyatsiya markaziy bankni harakatga undagan; C ('In response to these inflationary pressures') sababni oqibatga bevosita bog'laydi; A qo'shadi, B mantiqsiz misol qiladi, D qarama-qarshilikni bildiradi.
quizTr.ru: Связь — ПРИЧИНА И ДЕЙСТВИЕ: инфляция побудила центробанк действовать; C («In response to these inflationary pressures») прямо соединяет причину со следствием; A добавляет, B делает нелогичный пример, D подразумевает контраст.

quizTr.uz: D ('demonstrates') dalillar yakuniy sifatida taqdim etilgan xulosa uchun mos; C ('suggests') dastlabki dalillar uchun, A va B esa o'z xulosasini taqdim etayotgan paragraf uchun ortiqcha ehtiyotkor.
quizTr.ru: D («demonstrates») уместен для вывода, где доказательства поданы как весомые; C («suggests») — для предварительных данных, A и B слишком осторожны для абзаца, представляющего своё заключение.

reading.title: Rhetorical Synthesis — What the Question Is Actually Asking
reading.text:
Rhetorical Synthesis questions present a set of bulleted notes and ask you to combine the relevant information to accomplish a specific RHETORICAL GOAL. The question stem tells you exactly what goal the student is trying to achieve: 'The student wants to introduce the topic by presenting a surprising contrast,' or 'The student wants to provide evidence supporting the claim that...,' or 'The student wants to emphasize X while acknowledging Y.' Your job is to find the answer choice that accomplishes that SPECIFIC GOAL using information from the notes.

The most important skill: READ THE GOAL CAREFULLY before looking at the answer choices. The notes give you the raw material; the goal tells you what to BUILD from that material. A note might contain five facts, but the goal might only require one specific fact, presented in a specific way. Wrong answers often: (1) use correct information but fail to accomplish the stated goal; (2) accomplish a DIFFERENT goal than the one stated; (3) use information NOT in the notes; (4) combine information in a way that creates a DIFFERENT emphasis than the goal requires.

Common rhetorical goals on the exam include: INTRODUCE with surprising or interesting detail; SUPPORT a specific claim with evidence from the notes; EMPHASIZE a contrast or comparison; ACKNOWLEDGE a limitation or counterpoint; CONCLUDE by connecting a specific detail to a broader point. For each goal type, you must identify which specific pieces of note information are RELEVANT to the goal and which answer choice BEST SERVES the goal. Often two answer choices use correct information, but only one accomplishes the specific goal stated.

Key points:
• Step 1: Read the GOAL before reading the answer choices
• Step 2: Identify which notes are RELEVANT to the goal
• Step 3: Find the choice that accomplishes the goal (not just uses correct info)
• Trap: uses correct information but serves a DIFFERENT goal
• Trap: uses information NOT in the notes
• Trap: two choices use correct info — only one achieves the SPECIFIC goal
• Goal types: introduce, support, contrast, acknowledge, conclude, emphasize

quiz.q:
Notes:
• Monarch butterflies migrate up to 3,000 miles annually
• Migration is guided by a sun compass and circadian clock
• Population has declined 80% in 30 years
• Main causes: milkweed habitat loss and climate change
• Some populations now overwinter in California, not just Mexico

The student wants to support the claim that monarch butterfly migration requires sophisticated navigation mechanisms.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes?
o: Monarch butterflies migrate up to 3,000 miles annually, and their population has declined by 80% over the past 30 years.

Their migration is guided by a sun compass that uses the position of the sun in combination with an internal circadian clock to maintain directional orientation — a navigation system of remarkable complexity.
Because milkweed habitat loss and climate change have caused population decline, some monarchs now overwinter in California rather than Mexico.
Monarch butterflies travel up to 3,000 miles each year, making their journey one of the longest insect migrations in the world.
quiz.e: The goal is to support the claim about SOPHISTICATED NAVIGATION MECHANISMS. B directly addresses this: it describes the sun compass + circadian clock system and explicitly calls it 'a navigation system of remarkable complexity' — supporting the 'sophisticated' claim. A uses the distance and population decline facts — neither supports the navigation claim. C describes habitat/climate causes and range shifts — not navigation. D uses distance only, not the navigation mechanism.

quiz.q:
Notes:
• James Watson and Francis Crick won 1962 Nobel Prize for DNA structure
• Their discovery was based on X-ray diffraction data produced by Rosalind Franklin
• Franklin was not credited in their 1953 paper
• Franklin died in 1958, four years before the Nobel was awarded
• Nobel Prize cannot be awarded posthumously

The student wants to introduce the topic by highlighting an irony in the Nobel Prize story.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes?
o: James Watson and Francis Crick won the Nobel Prize in 1962 for determining the structure of DNA, a discovery with profound implications for biology and medicine.
Rosalind Franklin produced the X-ray diffraction data that Watson and Crick relied upon to determine DNA's structure, yet she was not credited in their original 1953 paper.

The scientists whose X-ray data made possible the 1962 Nobel Prize-winning discovery of DNA's structure died four years before the award was given — and the Nobel Prize cannot be awarded posthumously, making recognition impossible regardless of committee decisions.
Rosalind Franklin worked at King's College London, while Watson and Crick worked at Cambridge.
quiz.e: The goal is to highlight an IRONY in the Nobel Prize story. C presents the irony precisely: Franklin's data enabled the prize-winning discovery, but she died four years before the award — and the Nobel cannot be given posthumously, making the irony complete (she couldn't have won even if alive, because she died before the prize was awarded). A introduces Watson and Crick's Nobel without any irony. B presents the uncredited data problem but without the Nobel Prize irony specifically. D is a factual detail with no ironic contrast.

quiz.q:
Notes:
• Average CEO pay at S&P 500 companies: $16.7 million in 2022
• Average worker pay at same companies: $55,000 in 2022
• CEO-to-worker pay ratio: ~300:1
• In 1965, the ratio was approximately 21:1
• Japan's CEO-to-worker ratio averages approximately 10:1

The student wants to emphasize how dramatically the CEO-to-worker pay gap has changed over time.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes?
o: American CEOs earn approximately 300 times more than their average workers, and CEOs at comparable Japanese companies earn approximately 10 times more than their workers.
The CEO-to-worker pay ratio at major American companies has grown from approximately 21:1 in 1965 to approximately 300:1 in 2022, a more than fourteenfold increase over six decades.
Average CEO pay at S&P 500 companies was $16.7 million in 2022, while the average worker at the same companies earned $55,000.
The growing gap between executive and worker compensation reflects broader trends toward income inequality in the American economy.
quiz.e: The goal is to emphasize how dramatically the gap has CHANGED OVER TIME. B uses the historical comparison (21:1 in 1965 → 300:1 in 2022) and explicitly quantifies the change ('more than fourteenfold increase over six decades') — directly serving the 'change over time' goal. A uses the US-Japan comparison (not the historical change). C presents current pay figures without any historical comparison. D is a vague general statement not from the notes.

quiz.q:
Notes:
• Exercise has been shown to reduce symptoms of mild-to-moderate depression
• Meta-analysis of 41 studies showed exercise as effective as antidepressants for this group
• Most studies used self-reported outcomes (subjective)
• Studies typically lasted 8-12 weeks; long-term effects less studied
• Exercise may be less effective for severe depression

The student wants to support the claim that exercise is a promising treatment for depression while acknowledging a methodological limitation of the current research.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes?
o: A meta-analysis of 41 studies found exercise to be as effective as antidepressants for mild-to-moderate depression, though most of these studies relied on self-reported outcomes rather than objective clinical measures.
Exercise reduces symptoms of mild-to-moderate depression, making it a promising alternative to pharmaceutical treatment for all patients.
Studies show that exercise is effective for mild-to-moderate depression over periods of 8-12 weeks, and its effectiveness for severe depression and over longer timeframes remains less studied.
Because exercise may be less effective for severe depression, it cannot be recommended as a primary treatment.
quiz.e: The goal requires BOTH supporting the claim (exercise is promising) AND acknowledging a methodological limitation. A does both: cites the 41-study meta-analysis (support) while noting the self-reported outcomes limitation (methodological concern). B supports the claim but overstates ('all patients' is not in the notes) and doesn't acknowledge a limitation. C mentions timeframe limitations (not a methodological flaw but a scope limitation) and doesn't include the meta-analysis support. D only mentions the limitation and doesn't support the main claim.

quiz.q:
Notes:
• The Great Pacific Garbage Patch is not a solid island of plastic
• It consists of tiny plastic particles (microplastics) suspended in water
• It covers approximately 1.6 million km² — twice the size of Texas
• The particles are invisible to satellites
• Ocean currents concentrate plastic waste in five major 'gyres' worldwide

The student wants to conclude a paragraph about plastic pollution by connecting a specific detail about the Garbage Patch to the broader challenge of addressing ocean plastic.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes?
o: The Great Pacific Garbage Patch covers approximately 1.6 million square kilometers and consists of microplastic particles suspended in water.

Because the microplastic particles composing the Great Pacific Garbage Patch are invisible to satellites, accurately measuring — and therefore addressing — the full extent of ocean plastic pollution remains a fundamental challenge.
The five major ocean gyres concentrate plastic waste, and the Great Pacific Garbage Patch is the largest of these concentrations.
The Great Pacific Garbage Patch is often incorrectly described as a solid island of plastic, when in fact it consists of suspended microplastic particles.
quiz.e: The goal is to CONCLUDE by connecting a specific detail to the BROADER CHALLENGE of addressing ocean plastic. B uses the satellite-invisibility detail (specific) and explicitly connects it to the broader challenge ('accurately measuring — and therefore addressing — the full extent of ocean plastic pollution'). A states facts but makes no connection to a broader challenge. C describes the gyre system but doesn't connect to a challenge. D corrects a misconception but doesn't connect to a broader challenge.

quizTr.uz: Maqsad — MURAKKAB navigatsiya mexanizmlari haqidagi da'voni asoslash; B sun compass + ichki soat tizimini tasvirlab, uni 'a navigation system of remarkable complexity' deb ataydi; boshqalari navigatsiya da'vosini asoslamaydi.
quizTr.ru: Цель — подтвердить тезис о СЛОЖНЫХ механизмах навигации; B описывает систему sun compass + внутренние часы и прямо называет её «a navigation system of remarkable complexity»; остальные тезис о навигации не подтверждают.

quizTr.uz: C ironiyani aniq beradi: Franklin ma'lumotlari Nobel kashfiyotini ta'minladi, lekin u mukofotdan to'rt yil oldin vafot etdi — Nobel esa vafotdan keyin berilmaydi; boshqalarida ironik kontrast yo'q.
quizTr.ru: C передаёт иронию точно: данные Franklin обеспечили нобелевское открытие, но она умерла за четыре года до премии, а посмертно Нобеля не вручают; в остальных иронического контраста нет.

quizTr.uz: Maqsad — farq VAQT DAVOMIDA qanchalik keskin o'zgarganini ta'kidlash; B tarixiy taqqoslashni (1965: 21:1 → 2022: 300:1) ishlatib, o'sishni aniq ifodalaydi ('fourteenfold increase'); boshqalari tarixiy taqqoslashsiz.
quizTr.ru: Цель — подчеркнуть, как резко разрыв ИЗМЕНИЛСЯ во времени; B даёт историческое сравнение (1965: 21:1 → 2022: 300:1) и количественно оценивает рост («fourteenfold increase»); остальные — без исторического сравнения.

quizTr.uz: Maqsad da'voni qo'llab-quvvatlashni HAM metodologik cheklovni tan olishni talab qiladi; A ikkalasini bajaradi: 41 tadqiqot meta-tahlili (dalil) + self-reported natijalar cheklovi; boshqalari yo dalilsiz, yo cheklovsiz.
quizTr.ru: Цель требует И поддержать тезис, И признать методологическое ограничение; A делает оба: мета-анализ 41 исследования (довод) + оговорка о self-reported результатах; остальные — либо без довода, либо без оговорки.

quizTr.uz: Maqsad — aniq detalni okean plastigi bilan kurashning KENGROQ muammosiga bog'lab yakunlash; B sun'iy yo'ldoshga ko'rinmaslik detalini o'lchash va hal qilish muammosiga aniq bog'laydi; boshqalari bunday bog'lanish qilmaydi.
quizTr.ru: Цель — завершить, связав конкретную деталь с БОЛЕЕ ШИРОКОЙ проблемой океанского пластика; B связывает невидимость частиц для спутников с проблемой измерения и решения; остальные такой связи не делают.

reading.title: Advanced Synthesis — Emphasis, Precision & Avoiding Traps
reading.text:
At the 700+ level, rhetorical synthesis questions become challenging because two or three answer choices will use CORRECT INFORMATION from the notes. The difference lies in precision: which choice BEST accomplishes the stated goal? For emphasis questions, the correct answer must place the emphasized element in the most prominent position — typically the main clause, not a subordinate clause. For contrast questions, the correct answer must use appropriate contrast signal words (while, although, despite, however) and place the contrast in the right order.

STRUCTURAL PRECISION matters. 'Although X, Y' puts Y in the main clause (emphasized). 'X, although Y' puts X in the main clause. If the goal says 'emphasize X while acknowledging Y,' the correct answer must have X in the main clause and Y in the subordinate clause — not the reverse. If the goal says 'introduce X by noting the surprising contrast with Y,' the structure should acknowledge Y first (the setup/context) before introducing X (the surprise).

OVER-CLAIMING and UNDER-CLAIMING traps: the correct answer must match the scope of the notes exactly. If the notes say a treatment is effective for 'mild-to-moderate' depression, an answer saying it works for 'all patients' is an over-claim. If the notes provide strong evidence for a clear conclusion, an answer that hedges too cautiously ('may possibly suggest') is an under-claim. The correct answer should be as strong or as qualified as the evidence in the notes warrants — no more, no less.

Key points:
• Main clause = emphasized element | Subordinate clause = acknowledged/secondary element
• 'Although X, Y' = Y emphasized | 'X, although Y' = X emphasized
• Correct structure: goal says 'emphasize X while acknowledging Y' → X in main clause
• Over-claim: broader than what notes support (all patients vs. some patients)
• Under-claim: weaker than what notes clearly show
• Two correct-info choices: ask 'which one BEST achieves the goal's specific structure?'
• Contrast signals: while, although, despite, however, yet, whereas

quiz.q:
Notes:
• Processed meat consumption linked to increased colorectal cancer risk
• WHO classifies processed meat as a Group 1 carcinogen
• Risk increase: ~18% higher with each 50g daily serving
• Red meat classified as Group 2A (probably carcinogenic)
• Overall cancer risk from typical processed meat consumption is still small in absolute terms

The student wants to emphasize the official scientific classification of processed meat while acknowledging that absolute risk remains small for typical consumers.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes?
o: Although the absolute cancer risk from typical processed meat consumption remains small, the World Health Organization has classified processed meat as a Group 1 carcinogen — the same category as tobacco and asbestos.
While the WHO classifies processed meat as a Group 1 carcinogen, the absolute risk to typical consumers from normal consumption levels remains small.
Processed meat consumption increases colorectal cancer risk by approximately 18% per 50g daily serving, though this translates to a small absolute risk for typical consumers.
The WHO classifies both processed meat (Group 1) and red meat (Group 2A) as carcinogens, though at different levels of certainty.
quiz.e: The goal is to EMPHASIZE the official classification while acknowledging the small absolute risk. Correct structure: classification in main clause, risk smallness in subordinate/acknowledging position. A has the classification as the main clause ('WHO has classified') and puts the small risk first as the 'although' qualifier — the main clause carries the emphasis. B reverses this: the classification is in the 'while' subordinate clause and the small risk is in the main clause — this EMPHASIZES the small risk, not the classification. C focuses on the specific percentage, not the official classification. D adds the red meat comparison, not in the notes.

quiz.q:
Notes:
• Mindfulness meditation reduces cortisol levels in stressed adults
• Multiple RCTs show reduced anxiety in adults with generalized anxiety disorder
• Effects appear strongest when practiced 20+ minutes per day
• Some studies show modest effects; effect sizes vary considerably
• Long-term effects (beyond 1 year) less studied

The student wants to support the claim that mindfulness meditation has demonstrated benefits for anxiety.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes?
o: Mindfulness meditation eliminates anxiety in adults who practice it consistently for at least 20 minutes per day.

Multiple randomized controlled trials have found that mindfulness meditation reduces anxiety in adults with generalized anxiety disorder, with stronger effects observed when practiced 20 or more minutes daily.
Mindfulness meditation reduces cortisol and eliminates anxiety, making it a superior alternative to medication for all mental health conditions.
Studies show mindfulness meditation has modest and inconsistent benefits that are probably insufficient for most anxiety patients.
quiz.e: The goal is to support the claim that mindfulness has 'demonstrated benefits for anxiety.' B accurately uses the RCT evidence (demonstrated) for anxiety specifically, with appropriate qualification (20+ minutes). A over-claims: 'eliminates anxiety' — notes say 'reduces.' C over-claims wildly: 'superior alternative to medication for all mental health conditions' — not in the notes. D under-claims: 'modest and inconsistent...insufficient for most' — the notes show real RCT evidence of benefits.

quiz.q:
Notes:
• Roman Colosseum construction began 72 CE under Emperor Vespasian
• Completed 80 CE under Emperor Titus
• Could hold 50,000–80,000 spectators
• Featured 80 entrances for crowd management
• Seating was segregated by social class
• Modern stadiums use similar crowd management principles

The student wants to introduce the Colosseum as an example of sophisticated ancient engineering that remains relevant to modern design.

Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes?
o: The Roman Colosseum, completed in 80 CE, could hold up to 80,000 spectators and featured 80 entrances for rapid crowd distribution — crowd management principles that continue to inform the design of modern sports venues.
The Roman Colosseum was built between 72 CE and 80 CE under the emperors Vespasian and Titus, and its seating was segregated by social class.
The Colosseum featured 80 entrances and could hold 50,000 to 80,000 spectators, making it one of the largest entertainment venues in the ancient world.
Modern stadium designers have been influenced by ancient Roman architecture, particularly the Colosseum's capacity for large crowds.
quiz.e: The goal requires two things: (1) show sophisticated ancient engineering AND (2) connect to modern design relevance. A uses capacity + 80 entrances (sophisticated engineering) AND explicitly connects to 'crowd management principles that continue to inform modern sports venues' — achieving both goal elements. B mentions dates and seating segregation (historical facts that don't connect to modern design). C shows scale but doesn't connect to modern relevance. D mentions modern influence vaguely without the specific engineering detail.

quizTr.uz: Ta'kidni bosh gap ko'taradi: A rasmiy tasnifni bosh gapga, kichik xavfni 'although' bo'lagiga qo'yadi — aynan maqsadga mos; B buni teskari qilib kichik xavfni ta'kidlaydi, C foizga e'tibor qaratadi, D yozuvlarda yo'q taqqoslash qo'shadi.
quizTr.ru: Акцент несёт главное предложение: A ставит официальную классификацию в главную часть, а малый риск — в уступку «although», что и требуется; B делает наоборот и подчёркивает малый риск, C — про процент, D добавляет сравнение не из заметок.

quizTr.uz: B RCT dalillarini aynan anxiety uchun mos ehtiyotkorlik bilan to'g'ri ishlatadi; A ('eliminates') ortiqcha da'vo — yozuvlarda 'reduces', C yovvoyi darajada bo'rttiradi, D dalillarni kamsitadi.
quizTr.ru: B корректно использует данные RCT именно для тревожности с уместной оговоркой; A («eliminates») переоценивает — в заметках «reduces», C дико преувеличивает, D недооценивает доказательства.

quizTr.uz: Maqsad ikki narsani talab qiladi: qadimgi muhandislik mahoratini ko'rsatish VA zamonaviy dizaynga bog'lash; A 80 000 tomoshabin + 80 kirishni keltirib, buni zamonaviy sport inshootlari tamoyillariga aniq bog'laydi — ikkala elementga erishadi.
quizTr.ru: Цель требует двух вещей: показать инженерное мастерство древних И связать с современным дизайном; A приводит 80 000 зрителей + 80 входов и прямо связывает их с принципами современных арен — оба элемента достигнуты.

reading.title: Wordiness, Redundancy & Concision
reading.text:
Sentence revision questions ask you to select the MOST EFFECTIVE version of a sentence or underlined portion. The most frequent target on the exam is WORDINESS and REDUNDANCY — using more words than necessary to express an idea, or repeating the same information twice in different words. The correct answer expresses the complete meaning as concisely as possible without losing any necessary information. The golden rule: every word must earn its place.

The four types of wordiness the exam tests: (1) REDUNDANT PAIRS — words that mean the same thing used together ('important and significant,' 'basic and fundamental,' 'final and conclusive'); (2) MEANINGLESS INTENSIFIERS — words that add no information ('very unique,' 'absolutely essential,' 'completely eliminated' — something either is or isn't unique/essential/eliminated); (3) WORDY PHRASES — phrases with simpler one-word equivalents ('at this point in time' → 'now'; 'due to the fact that' → 'because'; 'in the event that' → 'if'; 'has the ability to' → 'can'); (4) IMPLICIT MEANING — stating something that is already implied ('the reason is because' → 'the reason is that'; 'return back' → 'return'; 'advance planning' → 'planning').

When two or more choices express the same information, the SHORTER choice is almost always correct — unless shortness comes at the cost of losing required information. To check: read each answer choice and ask 'Does this version include everything the original says that needs to be said?' If yes, and it's shorter, it's likely correct. The exam does not reward brevity that sacrifices necessary content — but it consistently penalizes unnecessary verbosity.

Key points:
• Redundant pairs: 'important and significant' → pick one
• 'at this point in time' → 'now' | 'due to the fact that' → 'because'
• 'has the ability to' → 'can' | 'in the event that' → 'if'
• 'return back / advance planning / end result' → just 'return / planning / result'
• 'very unique / absolutely essential' → 'unique / essential'
• When two choices express same info: shorter is almost always correct
• Check: does the shorter choice lose any REQUIRED information? If no → choose it

quiz.q:
Sentence: 'The merger created a new and novel approach to corporate governance that had not been seen in the industry before.'

Which choice most effectively revises the underlined sentence to eliminate unnecessary repetition?
o: The merger created a new and novel approach to corporate governance that had not been seen in the industry before.
The merger created a novel approach to corporate governance not previously seen in the industry.
The merger created an approach to corporate governance that was entirely new and had never been seen before.
The merger created a very new and quite novel approach to corporate governance.
quiz.e: 'New and novel' is a redundant pair — both mean the same thing. 'That had not been seen in the industry before' and 'not previously seen' are equivalent. B eliminates both redundancies: 'novel' (one word instead of 'new and novel') and 'not previously seen' (shorter than 'not seen in the industry before'). A keeps both redundancies. C adds 'entirely' and 'had never been seen before' — more words, same meaning. D adds 'very' and 'quite' — intensifiers that weaken, not strengthen.

quiz.q:
Sentence: 'Due to the fact that the funding was cut, the research team was forced to terminate their ongoing project before its completion.'

Which choice most effectively revises the sentence?
o: Due to the fact that the funding was cut, the research team was forced to terminate their ongoing project before its completion.
Because the funding was cut, the research team had to end their project before completion.
As a result of the reason that funding was cut, the research team found themselves in the position of having to terminate their ongoing project.
The research team was forced to terminate their ongoing project due to the fact that there was a cut in their funding.
quiz.e: 'Due to the fact that' → 'because' (4 words → 1). 'Was forced to terminate' → 'had to end' (shorter, same meaning). 'Their ongoing project before its completion' → 'their project before completion' ('ongoing' is implied; 'its' is unnecessary). B applies all three improvements. A keeps the wordiness. C adds 'as a result of the reason that' — even worse. D reorders but keeps 'due to the fact that.'

quiz.q:
Sentence: 'The committee will first begin the review process in January, starting with the oldest submitted applications.'

Which choice most effectively revises the sentence?
o: The committee will first begin the review process in January, starting with the oldest submitted applications.
The committee will begin its review in January, starting with the oldest applications.
The committee will begin to start the review process beginning in January with the oldest applications that have been submitted.
The committee will first and foremost begin the review process in January, initially starting with the oldest submitted applications.
quiz.e: 'Will first begin' — 'first' is redundant since 'begin' already means starting for the first time. 'Review process' → 'review' (process is implied). 'Submitted applications' → 'applications' in context (submitted is implied when talking about reviewing applications). B eliminates 'first' and 'process' and 'submitted.' A keeps 'first begin.' C adds 'beginning' and 'that have been submitted' — worse. D adds 'first and foremost' and 'initially starting' — much worse.

quiz.q:
Passage context: A student is writing about ocean plastics.
Sentence: 'Microplastics, which are tiny plastic fragments measuring less than five millimeters in their size, have been found in the tissues of marine animals.'

Which choice most effectively revises the underlined portion?
o: which are tiny plastic fragments measuring less than five millimeters in their size,
which are tiny plastic fragments less than five millimeters in size,
which are small, tiny plastic fragments that measure less than five millimeters,
which are plastic fragments that are very tiny in size and measure less than five millimeters,
quiz.e: B removes 'measuring' and 'their.' A keeps 'measuring' and 'their size' (redundant). C keeps 'small' and 'tiny' (redundant pair) and adds 'that measure.' D adds 'very tiny in size' and 'measure' — multiple redundancies.

quiz.q:
Passage: A student is describing a scientific study.
Original sentence: 'Researchers who study this phenomenon have published results.'
Proposed revision: 'Researchers published results.'

A third student argues the original sentence should instead read:
'Scientists specializing in the study of this phenomenon have released their research findings.'

Which version is the most effective?
o: Researchers who study this phenomenon have published results.
Scientists specializing in the study of this phenomenon have released their research findings.
Researchers studying this phenomenon published results.
quiz.e: The context requires telling readers WHICH researchers (those studying the phenomenon) — so 'researchers published results' (option B) is too brief and loses necessary information. 'Scientists specializing in the study of this phenomenon have released their research findings' (option C) is wordy: 'specializing in the study of' → 'studying'; 'research findings' → 'results' (findings is implied). D — 'researchers studying this phenomenon published results' — provides the necessary specification ('studying this phenomenon') with no unnecessary words. D is both complete and concise.

quizTr.uz: 'New and novel' — bir xil ma'noli ortiqcha juftlik; B ikkala takrorni yo'q qiladi ('novel' va qisqaroq 'not previously seen'); A ikkala takrorni saqlaydi, C va D so'z qo'shib faqat yomonlashtiradi.
quizTr.ru: «New and novel» — избыточная пара с одним смыслом; B убирает оба повтора («novel» и более короткое «not previously seen»); A сохраняет оба, C и D лишь добавляют слов.

quizTr.uz: 'Due to the fact that' → 'because', 'was forced to terminate' → 'had to end', ortiqcha 'ongoing' olib tashlanadi — B uchala yaxshilanishni qo'llaydi; A so'zchanlikni saqlaydi, C yanada yomon, D 'due to the fact that'ni saqlaydi.
quizTr.ru: «Due to the fact that» → «because», «was forced to terminate» → «had to end», лишнее «ongoing» убирается — B применяет все три правки; A сохраняет многословие, C ещё хуже, D оставляет «due to the fact that».

quizTr.uz: 'Begin' allaqachon boshlashni bildirgani uchun 'first' ortiqcha, 'process' va 'submitted' nazarda tutiladi — B uchalasini olib tashlaydi; A 'first begin'ni saqlaydi, C va D yanada so'zchan.
quizTr.ru: «First» избыточно, так как «begin» уже значит начало, «process» и «submitted» подразумеваются — B убирает все три; A сохраняет «first begin», C и D ещё многословнее.

quizTr.uz: B 'measuring' va 'their'ni olib tashlaydi; A ortiqcha 'their size'ni saqlaydi, C ortiqcha 'small'/'tiny' juftligini saqlab 'that measure' qo'shadi, D bir nechta takror qo'shadi.
quizTr.ru: B убирает «measuring» и «their»; A сохраняет избыточное «their size», C сохраняет пару «small»/«tiny» и добавляет «that measure», D добавляет несколько повторов.

quizTr.uz: Kontekst QAYSI tadqiqotchilar ekanini aytishni talab qiladi — B juda qisqa bo'lib zarur ma'lumotni yo'qotadi, C so'zchan; D zarur aniqlikni ('studying this phenomenon') ortiqcha so'zlarsiz beradi — ham to'liq, ham qisqa.
quizTr.ru: Контекст требует уточнить, КАКИЕ исследователи — B слишком краток и теряет нужную информацию, C многословен; D даёт нужное уточнение («studying this phenomenon») без лишних слов — полно и кратко.

reading.title: Precision, Clarity & Structural Revision
reading.text:
Beyond wordiness, revision questions also test PRECISION (choosing the most specific/accurate word or phrase), CLARITY (eliminating ambiguous pronoun references and misplaced modifiers), and STRUCTURAL EFFECTIVENESS (choosing the sentence structure that best achieves the passage's purpose). These are harder than simple wordiness questions because all choices may be grammatically correct — you must judge which is BEST, not just which is acceptable.

PRECISION questions: choose the answer that most specifically and accurately describes what the passage means. Vague language ('things,' 'aspects,' 'various') often signals a wrong answer when the passage supports a more specific description. Watch for: (a) answers that are too vague when specificity is possible; (b) answers that over-specify beyond what the passage supports; (c) answers that use imprecise synonyms ('happy' instead of 'enthusiastic' when enthusiasm is what the context supports).

CLARITY questions target ambiguous pronoun reference (when 'it' or 'they' could refer to more than one thing) and misplaced modifiers (when the modifier is too far from what it describes). The revision should make clear which noun the pronoun refers to, or place the modifier immediately next to what it modifies. For STRUCTURAL REVISION: consider how the sentence serves the paragraph. The best revision maintains the needed information, achieves the appropriate emphasis (main clause = most important idea), and connects smoothly to surrounding sentences.

Key points:
• Precision: avoid vague words when specific ones are supported by context
• Clarity: a pronoun is unclear if it could refer to more than one noun
• Fix ambiguous pronoun: replace 'it/they' with the specific noun
• Misplaced modifier: must immediately precede/follow what it modifies
• Structural revision: main clause should contain the most important idea
• Wrong: too vague when context supports specific | Wrong: over-specifies beyond context
• Smooth transition: revision should connect naturally to surrounding sentences

quiz.q:
Passage: 'Scientists placed the bacteria samples in the nutrient solution. After 48 hours, they had tripled in volume.'

The pronoun 'they' is ambiguous — it could refer to the bacteria samples or the scientists. Which revision most effectively clarifies the sentence?
o: After 48 hours, they had tripled in volume.
After 48 hours, the bacteria samples had tripled in volume.
After 48 hours, both they and the solution had tripled in volume.
After 48 hours, it had tripled in volume.
quiz.e: 'They' is ambiguous because it could refer to either the scientists or the bacteria samples. B replaces the ambiguous 'they' with the specific noun 'the bacteria samples,' eliminating the ambiguity. A keeps the ambiguous 'they.' C changes the meaning by adding 'and the solution.' D replaces 'they' with 'it' — 'it' is even less clear here.

quiz.q:
Passage: 'Written in 1848 during the revolutionary upheavals across Europe, Marx and Engels published the Communist Manifesto.'

Which revision corrects the misplaced modifier?
o: Written in 1848 during the revolutionary upheavals across Europe, Marx and Engels published the Communist Manifesto.
Marx and Engels published the Communist Manifesto, written in 1848 during the revolutionary upheavals across Europe.
Marx and Engels, written in 1848 during the revolutionary upheavals across Europe, published the Communist Manifesto.
Written during the revolutionary upheavals, Marx and Engels published the Communist Manifesto in 1848 across Europe.
quiz.e: 'Written in 1848 during the revolutionary upheavals' modifies the Manifesto, not Marx and Engels (who were not 'written'). The modifier must be placed next to 'the Communist Manifesto.' B places 'written in 1848 during the revolutionary upheavals' as a modifier immediately after 'Communist Manifesto.' A is the problematic original. C places 'written' to modify Marx and Engels (wrong). D misplaces 'across Europe' to modify 'published.'

quiz.q:
Passage: 'The new vaccine produced a strong reaction in the body's defensive system, leading to significantly better outcomes in clinical trials.'

Which choice provides the most precise revision?
o: a strong reaction in the body's defensive system
a very good reaction in the body
a strong and powerful response in the immune system
quiz.e: ' 'Strong reaction' is less precise than 'robust immune response' — in medical writing, 'response' is the standard term for how the immune system reacts to a vaccine. B is both precise ('immune response' is the technical term) and concise. A is the original vague version. C is vaguer ('very good reaction'). D has 'strong and powerful' (redundant pair) and correctly says 'immune system' but keeps 'response' after a redundant pair.

quiz.q:
Passage context: The paragraph argues that the printing press was the most transformative technology of the second millennium.
Sentence: 'The printing press, which historians regard as the most transformative technology of the second millennium, was invented by Gutenberg around 1440.'

Which revision best emphasizes the main point of the paragraph?
o: The printing press, which historians regard as the most transformative technology of the second millennium, was invented by Gutenberg around 1440.
Invented by Gutenberg around 1440, the printing press is widely regarded by historians as the most transformative technology of the second millennium.
Gutenberg invented the printing press around 1440, a technology which is regarded by historians as quite transformative.
The printing press was invented around 1440 by a man named Gutenberg, who made a very transformative contribution to history.
quiz.e: The paragraph argues the printing press was the MOST TRANSFORMATIVE technology. The sentence's main clause should carry this claim. A buries the key claim in a relative clause and emphasizes the date of invention. B puts the historical significance claim in the main clause ('is widely regarded as the most transformative technology') and moves the invention date to a subordinate opening phrase. C uses 'quite transformative' (imprecise) and puts Gutenberg as the subject. D is wordy and vague ('a man named,' 'very transformative').

quiz.q:
Passage context: A student is writing about ocean acidification affecting coral reefs.

Version 1: 'Ocean acidification, which is the process by which oceans absorb carbon dioxide and become more acidic, is causing coral reefs to bleach.'
Version 2: 'As oceans absorb atmospheric CO₂ and acidify, coral reefs bleach.'
Version 3: 'Coral reefs are being caused to bleach by the process of ocean acidification.'
Version 4: 'Ocean acidification is causing coral reefs to bleach.'

Which version is most effective for a science essay that assumes readers know what ocean acidification is?
quiz.e: ..') is unnecessary — a good revision removes known information. Version 2 is concise but buries 'coral reefs bleach' (the key point) as the main clause. Version 3 uses passive voice awkwardly ('are being caused to bleach by the process of'). Version 4 — 'Ocean acidification is causing coral reefs to bleach' — is direct, active, clear, and appropriately concise for an audience that knows the term. D (Version 4) is correct.

quizTr.uz: 'They' noaniq — olimlarga ham, bakteriya namunalariga ham tegishli bo'lishi mumkin; B uni aniq ot ('the bacteria samples') bilan almashtirib noaniqlikni yo'q qiladi; A noaniqlikni saqlaydi, C ma'noni o'zgartiradi, D dagi 'it' yanada noaniq.
quizTr.ru: «They» двусмысленно — может относиться и к учёным, и к образцам бактерий; B заменяет его на конкретное «the bacteria samples», устраняя двусмысленность; A сохраняет её, C меняет смысл, «it» в D ещё неяснее.

quizTr.uz: 'Written in 1848...' aniqlovchisi Manifestoni izohlashi kerak, Marx va Engelsni emas; B uni 'Communist Manifesto'dan keyin joylashtiradi; A muammoli asl variant, C aniqlovchini odamlarga bog'laydi, D 'across Europe'ni noto'g'ri joylashtiradi.
quizTr.ru: Оборот «written in 1848...» должен определять Манифест, а не Marx и Engels; B ставит его сразу после «Communist Manifesto»; A — проблемный оригинал, C относит оборот к людям, D смещает «across Europe».

quizTr.uz: Tibbiy matnda 'immune response' — standart atama, shuning uchun B ham aniq, ham qisqa; A noaniq asl variant, C yanada noaniq, D ortiqcha 'strong and powerful' juftligini saqlaydi.
quizTr.ru: В медицинском тексте «immune response» — стандартный термин, поэтому B точен и краток; A — расплывчатый оригинал, C ещё расплывчатее, D содержит избыточную пару «strong and powerful».

quizTr.uz: Asosiy da'vo ('eng transformatsion texnologiya') bosh gapda turishi kerak — B shunday qiladi va ixtiro sanasini kirish bo'lagiga ko'chiradi; A da'voni nisbiy gapga ko'mib sanani ta'kidlaydi, C va D noaniq va so'zchan.
quizTr.ru: Главный тезис («самая преобразующая технология») должен стоять в главном предложении — B делает так и уводит дату изобретения в оборот; A хоронит тезис в придаточном и подчёркивает дату, C и D расплывчаты и многословны.

quizTr.uz: Version 4 — 'Ocean acidification is causing coral reefs to bleach' — to'g'ridan-to'g'ri, faol va atamani biladigan auditoriya uchun mos darajada qisqa; 1 keraksiz izoh beradi, 2 asosiy fikrni ko'madi, 3 passivni noqulay ishlatadi.
quizTr.ru: Version 4 — «Ocean acidification is causing coral reefs to bleach» — прямая, активная и уместно краткая для знающей термин аудитории; 1 даёт лишнее пояснение, 2 хоронит главную мысль, 3 неуклюже пассивна.

listening.title: Lecture: The Aral Sea
listening.script: Good afternoon, everyone. Today I want to talk about one of the most dramatic environmental transformations of the twentieth century: the shrinking of the Aral Sea. Once the fourth-largest lake in the world, it lost over ninety percent of its volume within two generations, after the rivers that fed it were diverted to irrigate cotton fields. The consequences reached far beyond the shoreline. Fishing towns like Moynaq found themselves dozens of kilometres from the water, and dust storms began carrying salt across the region, affecting agriculture and public health. Yet the story is not only one of loss. In recent years, cooperation on the Kazakh side led to the construction of a dam that has partially revived the northern basin, and fish have returned to some waters. Scientists now treat the Aral as a case study — a warning about short-term planning, but also evidence that determined intervention can reverse at least part of the damage.

quiz.q: What caused the Aral Sea to shrink?
quiz.e: The lecturer says the rivers that fed it were diverted to irrigate cotton fields.

quiz.q: What does the speaker say about Moynaq?
o: It was flooded by the sea
It ended up far from the water
quiz.e: Fishing towns like Moynaq found themselves dozens of kilometres from the water.

quiz.q: Why does the speaker mention the northern dam?
o: To show partial recovery is possible
quiz.e: The dam partially revived the northern basin — evidence that intervention can reverse damage.

quiz.q: The speaker's overall tone is best described as…
quiz.e: The story is 'not only one of loss': a warning, but also evidence of recovery.

quizTr.uz: Ma'ruzachi aytadi: uni to'ydiradigan daryolar paxta dalalarini sug'orish uchun burib yuborilgan.
quizTr.ru: Лектор говорит: питавшие его реки отвели на орошение хлопковых полей.

quizTr.uz: Mo'ynoq kabi baliqchi shaharlar suvdan o'nlab kilometr uzoqda qolib ketdi.
quizTr.ru: Рыбацкие города вроде Муйнака оказались в десятках километров от воды.

quizTr.uz: To'g'on shimoliy havzani qisman tikladi — aralashuv zararni qaytarishi mumkinligiga dalil.
quizTr.ru: Дамба частично возродила северную часть — доказательство, что вмешательство может обратить ущерб.

quizTr.uz: Hikoya 'faqat yo'qotish haqida emas': ogohlantirish, ammo tiklanish dalili ham.
quizTr.ru: История «не только о потере»: предупреждение, но и свидетельство восстановления.

listening.title: Interview: Studying abroad
listening.script: Interviewer: You spent four years studying in another country. What surprised you most? — Speaker: Honestly, it wasn't the language or the weather. It was how differently people approached disagreement. In my first seminar, a student openly challenged the professor's interpretation, and instead of taking offence, the professor thanked him and adjusted her argument. Where I grew up, questioning a teacher in public would have felt disrespectful. It took me a full semester to realise that debate was not an attack but a form of participation — and another semester to actually join in. — Interviewer: And did that change you? — Speaker: Completely. I still value politeness, but I no longer confuse silence with respect. If I disagree now, I say so — carefully, with evidence, but I say so. I think that skill has helped my career more than any single course I took.

quiz.q: What surprised the speaker most abroad?
quiz.e: It wasn't language or weather — it was how differently people approached disagreement.

quiz.q: How did the professor react to being challenged?
o: She thanked him and adjusted her argument
quiz.e: Instead of taking offence, the professor thanked him.

quiz.q: What does the speaker mean by 'I no longer confuse silence with respect'?
o: Staying quiet is not the only way to show respect
quiz.e: He still values politeness but now expresses disagreement carefully — silence isn't the only respectful option.

quiz.q: Which skill does the speaker say helped his career most?
quiz.e: "That skill has helped my career more than any single course" — voicing disagreement with evidence.

quizTr.uz: Til yoki ob-havo emas — odamlarning kelishmovchilikka munosabati hayratlantirgan.
quizTr.ru: Не язык и не погода — удивило отношение людей к несогласию.

quizTr.uz: Professor xafa bo'lish o'rniga unga rahmat aytdi.
quizTr.ru: Вместо обиды профессор поблагодарила его.

quizTr.uz: U hali ham xushmuomalalikni qadrlaydi, lekin jim turish hurmatning yagona yo'li emasligini tushundi.
quizTr.ru: Он по-прежнему ценит вежливость, но понял: молчание — не единственный способ уважения.

quizTr.uz: Dalil bilan ehtiyotkorona e'tiroz bildirish ko'nikmasi kareraga eng ko'p yordam berdi.
quizTr.ru: Навык аргументированно возражать больше всего помог карьере.

listening.title: Podcast: How polyglots learn
listening.script: Welcome back to the show. Our topic today: what do successful language learners actually do differently? We interviewed thirty people who each speak five or more languages, and three patterns kept appearing. First, none of them waited to feel ready. They started speaking from day one, tolerating mistakes that would make most learners blush. Second, they built the language into their routine instead of adding it on top: podcasts while commuting, shopping lists in the target language, a diary of three sentences every night. The effort felt almost invisible, which is precisely why it survived busy weeks. And third — this one surprised us — they were selective about vocabulary. Rather than memorising long lists, they tracked words they had personally needed and missed in real conversations. One participant put it beautifully: a word you needed yesterday is worth twenty words you might need someday.

quiz.q: How many patterns did the researchers identify?
quiz.e: Three patterns kept appearing.

quiz.q: What did polyglots do 'from day one'?
quiz.e: None of them waited to feel ready — they started speaking from day one.

quiz.q: Why did routine-based learning survive busy weeks?
quiz.e: Built into the routine, the effort felt almost invisible — so it survived.

quiz.q: Which words did polyglots prioritise?
o: Words they personally needed and missed
Words that are easy to spell
quiz.e: They tracked words they had needed and missed in real conversations.

quizTr.uz: Uchta umumiy xususiyat aniqlangan.
quizTr.ru: Выявили три общие закономерности.

quizTr.uz: Hech biri tayyor bo'lishni kutmadi — birinchi kundanoq gapira boshlashdi.
quizTr.ru: Никто не ждал готовности — заговорили с первого дня.

quizTr.uz: Kundalik odatlarga singdirilgani uchun harakat deyarli sezilmasdi — shuning uchun davom etdi.
quizTr.ru: Встроенное в рутину усилие почти не ощущалось — потому и сохранилось.

quizTr.uz: Ular haqiqiy suhbatlarda o'zlariga kerak bo'lgan va yetishmagan so'zlarni kuzatib borishdi.
quizTr.ru: Они отслеживали слова, которых им реально не хватило в разговорах.

listening.title: Panel: Should Universities Teach in English?
listening.script: Moderator: Our topic tonight: the growing number of universities in non-English-speaking countries that teach entirely in English. Professor Rahimova, you're in favour? — Rahimova: With reservations, yes. Science today is published overwhelmingly in English. If we teach our brightest students in a language the global research community cannot read, we are, in effect, building them a beautiful room with no doors. — Moderator: Dr Bennett, you've called this trend 'linguistic outsourcing'. — Bennett: Because that's what it often is. When a country stops developing academic vocabulary in its own language, entire fields become unthinkable in that language within a generation. Medicine, law, engineering — if these can only be discussed in English, the national language is slowly demoted to the kitchen and the market. That has consequences for democracy: citizens cannot debate what they cannot name. — Rahimova: I'd push back on the fatalism. Bilingual academia is possible — publish internationally in English, teach and popularise in the national language. The real failure is not English-medium instruction; it is neglecting translation and terminology work at home. — Bennett: On that, at least, we agree entirely: the danger is not learning English. It is forgetting to keep the other language growing.

quiz.q: What does Rahimova's 'room with no doors' metaphor describe?
quiz.e: Teaching in a language the global research community cannot read isolates students — a beautiful room with no doors.

quiz.q: What does Bennett mean by 'linguistic outsourcing'?
o: Letting another language take over entire academic fields
quiz.e: When academic vocabulary stops developing, whole fields become discussable only in English.

quiz.q: Why does Bennett link the issue to democracy?
o: Citizens cannot debate what they cannot name
English is the language of politics
Laws must be written in English
quiz.e: If law or medicine can't be discussed in the national language, citizens are excluded from those debates.

quiz.q: On what do both speakers finally agree?
o: The national language must be kept growing
Translation work is a waste of resources
quiz.e: The danger is not learning English — it is forgetting to keep the other language growing.

quizTr.uz: Jahon ilmiy jamoasi o'qiy olmaydigan tilda o'qitish talabalarni yakkalab qo'yadi — eshiksiz chiroyli xona.
quizTr.ru: Обучение на языке, который мировое научное сообщество не читает, изолирует студентов — красивая комната без дверей.

quizTr.uz: Ilmiy lug'at rivojlanishdan to'xtasa, butun sohalar faqat ingliz tilida muhokama qilinadigan bo'lib qoladi.
quizTr.ru: Когда научная лексика перестаёт развиваться, целые области можно обсуждать только по-английски.

quizTr.uz: Huquq yoki tibbiyotni milliy tilda muhokama qilib bo'lmasa, fuqarolar bu bahslardan chetda qoladi.
quizTr.ru: Если право или медицину нельзя обсуждать на родном языке, граждане исключены из этих дебатов.

quizTr.uz: Xavf ingliz tilini o'rganishda emas — boshqa tilning o'sishini unutishda.
quizTr.ru: Опасность не в изучении английского, а в том, чтобы забыть развивать другой язык.

tips: Cite an example or study you know.
